003a23579000d7402129.days.0.move: Sendai ↔ Matsushima-Kaigan: about 40 minutes on the JR Senseki Line
003a23579000d7402129.days.0.title: Sendai and Matsushima
003a23579000d7402129.days.1.move: Sendai → Ichinoseki: just over 30 minutes by Shinkansen; Ichinoseki → Hiraizumi: about 8 minutes by JR
003a23579000d7402129.days.1.title: Hiraizumi World Heritage sites
003a23579000d7402129.days.2.move: Ichinoseki → Morioka → Kakunodate by Shinkansen; then take a bus from Tazawako Station into the mountains for about 50 minutes
003a23579000d7402129.days.2.title: Kakunodate and Nyuto Onsen
003a23579000d7402129.days.3.items.0.note: Enjoy one more soak in the morning, then take the bus back to Tazawako Station
003a23579000d7402129.days.3.move: Tazawako → Morioka → Shin-Aomori: about 2 hours by Shinkansen, then transfer to a JR train to Aomori Station
003a23579000d7402129.days.3.title: North to Aomori
003a23579000d7402129.days.4.items.2.note: Return to Shin-Aomori in the evening, then take the Shinkansen back to Tokyo in about 3 hours
003a23579000d7402129.days.4.move: Take the JR bus from Aomori Station to Oirase. Services are infrequent, so check the return schedule in advance
003a23579000d7402129.days.4.title: Oirase autumn foliage
003a23579000d7402129.for: Travelers who have already visited Tokyo and Kansai and want to see autumn foliage and enjoy hot springs without the crowds
003a23579000d7402129.summary: Enter via Sendai and head north along the Tohoku Shinkansen: see Matsushima Bay, visit Chusonji's Golden Hall and take a gorge cruise in Hiraizumi, then detour to Kakunodate and Nyuto Onsen for a soak in milky-white secluded hot springs. Finish in Aomori with autumn foliage along the Oirase Stream. The Shinkansen portion fits the 5-day JR EAST PASS perfectly. This route also works in winter—replace Oirase with Hakkoda's rime ice.
003a23579000d7402129.title: Tohoku autumn foliage and hot springs · 5 days

003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.0.move: Take JR from Okayama Station to Uno in about 1 hour, then take a ferry to Naoshima in about 20 minutes
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.0.title: From Okayama to Naoshima
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.1.items.2.note: Avoid Naoshima on Mondays and Teshima on Tuesdays. Book tickets online in advance
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.1.move: Take a ferry from Naoshima to Ieura Port on Teshima, then an evening ferry from Teshima to Takamatsu. Sailings are limited, so check the schedule in advance
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.1.title: Chichu Art Museum and Teshima
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.2.move: Take JR or Kotoden around the city, then take a bus up Yashima
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.2.title: Takamatsu gardens and udon
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.3.items.1.note: Have a bowl of udon for lunch along the approach
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.3.move: Takamatsu to Kotohira takes about 1 hour; Kotohira to Matsuyama via Tadotsu takes about 2.5 hours by limited express
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.3.title: Climb Konpira and head to Dogo
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.4.move: Take trams around the city; take a local JR train to Shimonada Station in about 1 hour
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.4.title: Matsuyama Castle and a seaside station
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.5.items.3.note: If you’re not in strong shape, cycle only part of the route and take a bus for the rest
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.5.move: Take a JR limited express from Matsuyama to Imabari, then cycle or take a bus across the bridges to Onomichi
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.days.5.title: Cross the Shimanami Kaido back to Honshu
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.for: Travelers who love art, architecture, and a slower pace, and are visiting Japan for the second time
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.season: March–November; avoid the island museums’ winter closures
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.summary: Start in Okayama and spend the first night on Naoshima. Visit Chichu Art Museum on day 2, then continue to Teshima and take an evening ferry to Takamatsu. Explore gardens and eat udon in Takamatsu, climb Kotohira-gu, then take a limited express to Matsuyama for Dogo Onsen. Finally, cross the sea along the Shimanami Kaido and return to Honshu at Onomichi.
003e37d7fccd6d717c49.title: Setouchi art islands + Shikoku · 6 days

0084cbb63ede7f21b20a.location: Naha Airport Station → Asahibashi Station → Kokusai-dori / Makishi Public Market
0084cbb63ede7f21b20a.paragraphs.0: Naha Airport is compact and painless: exit the international terminal and follow the covered walkway straight to Naha Airport Monorail Station. Tap Apple Pay, a physical Suica/ICOCA card (Okinawa's Yui Rail accepts Japan's nationwide IC transit cards plus select contactless Visa cards), and ride 5 stops—just 11 minutes—to Asahibashi Station. Why stay right here? Its footbridge links directly into the modern Naha Bus Terminal, where buses to Churaumi Aquarium, American Village, and southern Gyokusendo Cave all originate with plenty of open seats.
0084cbb63ede7f21b20a.paragraphs.1: After dropping your bags, stroll 10 minutes down leafy boulevards to Kokusai-dori and wander into the newly renovated First Makishi Public Market: pick fresh turban shell or Ishigaki beef downstairs and have upstairs kitchens cook it to order. Or duck north off the main strip into Tsuboya Yachimun Street for hand-thrown Okinawan pottery before sipping a frosty Orion draft beer in the 20°C evening breeze.
0084cbb63ede7f21b20a.phase: Step 01 · Day 1 Land in Naha & set up base
0084cbb63ede7f21b20a.photo.alt: Okinawa's elevated Yui Rail monorail gliding above palm-lined Naha streets under winter sun
0084cbb63ede7f21b20a.photo.caption: Naha's elevated Yui Rail carries you from the airport to Asahibashi Bus Terminal in 11 minutes—the stress-free backbone of a car-free Okinawa trip.
0084cbb63ede7f21b20a.tip: The Yui Rail 1-day pass runs for a rolling 24 hours from activation, not a calendar day. Activate it at 16:00 on Day 1 and it stays valid until 15:59 on Day 2—4 rides in a single day pays it off.
0084cbb63ede7f21b20a.title: Ride the Yui Rail 11 minutes to Asahibashi Station, then explore Kokusai-dori & Makishi Market

01b95bef2a11d690bf77.location: Kizu Market Dining Row · Uoichi Shokudo / Kawakami Shoten
01b95bef2a11d690bf77.paragraphs.0: Arrive hungry. Kizu Uoichi Shokudo's signature kaisendon and uni-ikura bowls routinely sell out before 10:00 AM—sourced thirty meters away from the fish stalls, the fatty otoro melts cleanly, sweet shrimp snaps, and the sea urchin has zero bitter alum taste, all at just over half of Kuromon's prices.
01b95bef2a11d690bf77.paragraphs.1: If you're traveling as a pair, split forces: one orders a seafood bowl while the other walks next door to 200-year-old Kawakami Shoten for Kansai-style charcoal-grilled unagi. Unlike Tokyo's steamed eel, Kansai unagi goes straight over glowing charcoal with repeated tare glazes until the skin turns crisp and smoky—unreal over hot white rice.
01b95bef2a11d690bf77.photo.alt: Overflowing sea urchin, salmon roe, and fatty tuna kaisendon bowl
01b95bef2a11d690bf77.photo.caption: Digging into freshly sliced uni and fatty tuna kaisendon at a worn wooden Kizu Market counter at 8 AM wakes up your appetite better than any coffee.
01b95bef2a11d690bf77.tip: Lines at Uoichi Shokudo stay reasonable between 07:30 and 09:00 (around 15–25 minutes). Past 10:00 the wait doubles and top uni and prime tuna bowls often sell out.
01b95bef2a11d690bf77.title: Kizu Uoichi Shokudo Seafood Bowl + 200-Year-Old Kawakami Shoten Charcoal-Grilled Eel

0218adee958efabc57cd.access.0.how: The monorail takes about 13 minutes to Kencho-mae Station (Kokusai Street) and costs about ¥290. Contactless credit card payment is accepted.
0218adee958efabc57cd.access.1.how: All have direct flights to Naha, taking about 1.5–2.5 hours.
0218adee958efabc57cd.access.2.how: Flights to Naha take about 2–3 hours. Low-cost carriers offer many flights, usually making this much more convenient than combining the Shinkansen with a ferry.
0218adee958efabc57cd.access.3.how: Flights from Naha to Ishigaki and Miyako each take about 1 hour. There are also direct flights from Tokyo and Osaka.
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.0.name: Okinawa soba
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.0.text: Despite its name, this is a thick wheat noodle rather than buckwheat soba. The broth combines pork bones and bonito, topped with tender braised pork belly or pork ribs. Locals season it with a few drops of awamori infused with chili peppers.
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.0.where: Noodle shops and diners in central Naha and around the main island
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.1.name: Goya champuru
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.1.text: Bitter melon stir-fried with tofu, eggs, and luncheon meat. The eggs and tofu soften the bitterness, making it a satisfying dish with rice. In Okinawan, champuru means stir-fried together.
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.1.where: Okinawan restaurants and izakayas in Naha
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.2.name: Taco rice
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.2.text: A fusion dish born near the U.S. military bases: seasoned ground meat, cheese, lettuce, and tomatoes from a Mexican taco are served over white rice, then topped with salsa. Portions are large, and the dish is cheap and quick when you are short on time.
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.2.where: Fast-food restaurants and diners in Kin Town and central Naha
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.3.name: Agu pork
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.3.text: A local Okinawan breed of black pig. It has plenty of fat without being greasy, with a slightly sweet flavor. It is excellent in hot pot or grilled, and menus marked アグー feature it.
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.3.where: Yakiniku and hot-pot restaurants in Naha and around the main island
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.4.name: Sata andagi
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.4.text: Okinawan fried doughnuts with a crisp outside and dense center. The cracks formed during frying look like a smiling face. They are best fresh, but keep well after cooling and make a good souvenir.
0218adee958efabc57cd.foods.4.where: Snack shops and souvenir stores around Kokusai Street and Makishi Market
0218adee958efabc57cd.intro.0: Okinawa is Japan's southernmost prefecture, made up of more than 100 islands. It was once the independent Ryukyu Kingdom, so its architecture, food, and music are quite different from mainland Japan. Naha and Ryukyu Kingdom sites are in the south of the main island. The central area has U.S. military bases and resort hotels, while the north is home to Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium and clearer water.
0218adee958efabc57cd.intro.1: For a first visit, stay in Naha. Use the monorail and buses to explore the south, then join one or two day tours to the north. Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your licence and the required documents, so check the official rules; many online self-drive guides may not apply. For even bluer water, fly about 1 hour from Naha to Ishigaki Island or Miyakojima. From Ishigaki, you can also take a ferry to Taketomi Island.
0218adee958efabc57cd.name: Okinawa
0218adee958efabc57cd.seasons.note: April and October–November are the most comfortable months. The swimming season runs roughly from April–October. Typhoons are common from July–October, and you can see Taiwan cherry blossoms in January–February.
0218adee958efabc57cd.sources.0.title: Shuri Castle Park: Price changes and advance reservations for the Seiden's reopening
0218adee958efabc57cd.sources.1.title: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium admission fees
0218adee958efabc57cd.sources.2.title: Nanjo City: Notice of revised admission fees for Sefa-utaki
0218adee958efabc57cd.sources.3.title: Yui Rail: Ticket types and fares
0218adee958efabc57cd.sources.4.title: An-ei Kanko: Timetables and fares
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.0.name: Shuri Castle
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.0.text: The royal castle of the Ryukyu Kingdom. A fire destroyed the Seiden in 2019, and the reconstructed main hall will reopen on November 23, 2026. The red palace blends Chinese and Japanese styles, while the castle walls curve along the hillside. Shuri Castle Ruins and Sonohyan-utaki Ishimon are part of a World Heritage Site.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.0.tip: Online reservations are required for a 30-minute time slot inside the main hall. Same-day tickets may be available if there are openings. Shuri Station is about a 15–20-minute walk away.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.1.name: Kokusai Street and Makishi Market
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.1.text: Naha's liveliest street stretches for about 1.6 kilometers, lined with souvenir shops, restaurants, and bars. Turn onto Market Main Street, where the First Makishi Public Market sells fish and meat on the first floor. You can take your purchases upstairs and have a vendor cook them for an additional fee. For many visitors, this is their first meal in Okinawa.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.1.tip: Walk from Kencho-mae Station to Makishi Station to cover the full length of the street. Before buying seafood at the market, ask how it is priced.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.2.name: Sefa-utaki
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.2.text: The most sacred site of the Ryukyu Kingdom and a World Heritage Site. Follow a stone path through the forest and giant rocks to a triangular opening formed by two leaning boulders. From inside, you can look out toward Kudaka Island, known as the island of the gods. People still come here to pray, so keep quiet during your visit.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.2.tip: Buy a ticket at the Nanjo City Regional Products Center, then walk about 10 minutes to the entrance. The site closes for two periods each year, so check before you go.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.3.name: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.3.text: The main attraction is the massive Kuroshio Sea tank, where whale sharks and giant manta rays glide slowly past. You can sit and watch for a long time. The aquarium is inside Ocean Expo Park, which is free to enter and also has dolphin shows and Emerald Beach. It is more than 2 hours by car from Naha, so combine it with Kouri Island and Nakijin Castle Ruins in one day.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.3.tip: Highway buses run directly from Naha Airport and take about 2.5 hours. The main tank has scheduled feeding talks, so check the times when you enter.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.4.name: Kouri Island
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.4.text: This small island is linked to the main island by a bridge nearly 2 kilometers long. As you cross, clear pale-blue water stretches out on both sides. It is one of Okinawa's classic views. A beach on the north side has a heart-shaped rock, and the island has plenty of seaside cafés and food trucks. Half a day is enough to drive around it.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.4.tip: Public transportation is inconvenient. Whether you can drive depends on your licence and the required documents, so joining a northern Okinawa day tour is the easiest option. Most tours stop here.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.5.name: Cape Manzamo
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.5.text: A flat coral plateau on the coast of Onna Village. Legend says that a Ryukyu king praised it as a place where 10,000 people could sit. At the tip, a cliff resembling an elephant's trunk reaches into the sea. From above, the water changes color in layers. With many resort hotels nearby, it is best visited at sunset.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.5.tip: Many northern Okinawa day tours stop here. If you are staying in Onna Village, walk over in the evening for sunset.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.6.name: Nakijin Castle Ruins
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.6.text: The castle of the king of Hokuzan before the Ryukyu Kingdom was unified. Its limestone walls rise and curve along the hillside, with views of the distant sea. No buildings remain inside, only the walls and sacred sites. It is a World Heritage Site. From late January to early February, deep-pink Taiwan cherry blossoms fill the area in front of the gate.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.6.tip: It is close to Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium, so visit both on the same day. Weekends are crowded during cherry blossom season, so try to go in the morning.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.7.name: Kabira Bay, Ishigaki
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.7.text: A bay in northern Ishigaki Island, with white sand and layers of blue-green water. The colors are brightest in good sunlight. Swimming is prohibited in the bay, but you can take a glass-bottom boat to see coral and tropical fish. Each trip takes about 30 minutes, making it suitable for non-swimmers.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.7.tip: Buses run from central Ishigaki to Kabira, but services are infrequent. The water looks best around midday on sunny days.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.8.name: Taketomi Island
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.8.text: A small island just over 10 minutes by ferry from Ishigaki Port. Red-tile roofs, low coral-stone walls, and white-sand paths preserve the traditional Yaeyama village landscape. Take a slow water buffalo cart ride around the village, or rent a bicycle to visit Nishi Pier at sunset and search for star sand on the beach. It works as a half-day or full-day trip.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.8.tip: There are many ferries, but confirm the last return sailing in advance. The white-sand paths can be slippery by bicycle, so ride slowly.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.9.name: Yonaha Maehama Beach, Miyakojima
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.9.text: A roughly 7-kilometer white-sand beach on the south side of Miyakojima. Its water is famous as Miyako blue and is often ranked among Japan's most beautiful beaches. Nearby, the 3.5-kilometer Irabu Bridge links Miyakojima and Irabu Island. It is Japan's longest toll-free bridge, with shades of blue stretching all the way across.
0218adee958efabc57cd.spots.9.tip: Buses are infrequent on the island. Whether you can drive depends on your licence and the required documents, so consider hiring a car with a driver, renting an electric-assist bicycle, or joining an island day tour.
0218adee958efabc57cd.stay: For a first visit, stay around Kokusai Street or Kencho-mae in Naha. The monorail makes it easy to reach the airport and Shuri. For more time by the sea, spend one or two nights at a resort hotel in Onna Village or Motobu. On the outlying islands, stay near Ishigaki Port for easy ferry access.
0218adee958efabc57cd.tagline: Ryukyu heritage and blue islands, even without a car
0218adee958efabc57cd.tips.0: Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your licence and the required documents. Okinawa can also be explored by monorail, bus, hired car with a driver, or day tour.
0218adee958efabc57cd.tips.1: For Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium and Kouri Island, a northern Okinawa day tour is the easiest option and can cover four or five spots in one day.
0218adee958efabc57cd.tips.2: Typhoons are common from July–October, and flights and ferries to the outlying islands may be suspended. Leave one buffer day after island trips.
0218adee958efabc57cd.tips.3: The monorail 1-day pass costs about ¥1,000 and is valid for 24 hours after purchase. A round trip to Shuri plus one additional ride makes it worthwhile.
0218adee958efabc57cd.tips.4: Okinawa's UV levels are very high. Use sun protection in spring and fall, too, and wear a rash guard when snorkeling.

023f2b87ec381ca1624b.cost: Grounds free; Sanmon Gate ¥600 / Hojo Garden ¥600
023f2b87ec381ca1624b.location: Nanzen-ji · about 700 meters on foot from Eikando
023f2b87ec381ca1624b.paragraphs.0: Putting Nanzen-ji second is deliberate: its sprawling, open grounds are largely free to enter, so even as late-morning crowds build past 10:00, it still feels airy rather than claustrophobic. Follow the quiet stone-walled lane south from Eikando for 10 minutes into the heart of the complex, starting beneath the towering wooden Sanmon Gate—climb to the upper balcony for a cinematic maple-framed panorama.
023f2b87ec381ca1624b.paragraphs.1: Two minutes past Sanmon Gate to the rear right stands Suirokaku, a Meiji-era red-brick aqueduct. Against blazing autumn leaves, the weathered arches look straight out of vintage film. Skip fighting ten people at the first pillar—walk a few steps up along the canal path above, or drop low to emphasize the repeating depth of the brick arches for a far cleaner shot.
023f2b87ec381ca1624b.photo.alt: Historic red-brick arches of Nanzen-ji's Suirokaku aqueduct framed by vivid autumn maple foliage
023f2b87ec381ca1624b.photo.caption: Nanzen-ji's Meiji-era red-brick aqueduct strikes a warm vintage contrast against fiery maples—shoot down the corridor of arches to leave the crowds out of frame.
023f2b87ec381ca1624b.tip: Next door, Tenju-an pairs crimson maples with a jewel-box white-gravel rock garden—stunning, though lines build fast after 10:30. If the wait tops 15 minutes, skip it and head straight to lunch.
023f2b87ec381ca1624b.title: Walk over to Nanzen-ji for the monumental Sanmon Gate, brick Suirokaku aqueduct, and open maple groves

033c6ece5d3ba727b08d.location: Osaka Kizu Wholesale Market · 3 min walk from Daikokucho Station Exit 1 (Midosuji / Yotsubashi Line)
033c6ece5d3ba727b08d.paragraphs.0: Ride the Midosuji Line one stop south from Namba to Daikokucho Station and walk 3 minutes out of Exit 1—vintage eaves and unloading delivery vans mark the 300-year-old Kizu Wholesale Market. Unlike touristified Kuromon, at 7:15 AM you'll still watch sushi chefs and kaiseki owners pushing handcarts past live sea bream, sea urchin, and seasonal melons.
033c6ece5d3ba727b08d.paragraphs.1: Stay clear of electric tug-cart lanes as you loop through the seafood and produce aisles. Boxes of strawberries, Shine Muscat grapes, or Shizuoka musk melons here often run 30–40% cheaper than department-store basements. Tucked at the back is the massive ODA Gyomu Supermarket, where locals load up on matcha powder, Rishiri kombu, sauces, and snacks—an effortless souvenir stop.
033c6ece5d3ba727b08d.photo.alt: Early-morning wholesale fish stalls at Osaka's Kizu Market
033c6ece5d3ba727b08d.photo.caption: At 7:30 AM Kizu Market's seafood hall is still in full wholesale swing—crushed ice, glistening fish, and brisk banter make up Osaka's real morning soundtrack.
033c6ece5d3ba727b08d.tip: The easiest way to whiff at Kizu Market is showing up on a closed day: it normally closes Wednesdays and Sundays (while the last Saturday morning each month hosts the public Kizu Morning Fair). Confirm the calendar the night before.
033c6ece5d3ba727b08d.title: Walk into Osaka's Real Wholesale Morning Market (Kizu) While the Fish Halls Are Still Buzzing

03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.gateways.0.how: The airport bus takes about 50 minutes to Hiroshima Station and costs about ¥1,500; international flights include Seoul and Taipei
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.gateways.0.name: Hiroshima Airport (HIJ)
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.gateways.1.how: The airport bus takes about 30 minutes to Okayama Station and costs about ¥1,000; flights include Shanghai, Hong Kong, and Taipei
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.gateways.1.name: Okayama Airport (OKJ)
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.gateways.2.how: Shin-Osaka to Okayama takes about 45 minutes–1 hour, and Hiroshima about 1.5 hours; the most flexible option when entering or leaving via Kansai
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.gateways.2.name: Take the Shinkansen from Kansai
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.gateways.3.how: Hakata to Hiroshima takes about 1 hour, and Shin-Shimonoseki about 15–20 minutes, making it easy to combine with Kyushu
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.gateways.3.name: Take the Shinkansen from Fukuoka
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.intro.0: Chugoku is a region in western Honshu, Japan—not China. It includes Okayama, Hiroshima, and Yamaguchi on the Seto Inland Sea (the Sanyo side), and Tottori and Shimane on the Sea of Japan (the San'in side). The Sanyo side is connected by the Shinkansen, making it easy to visit the Atomic Bomb Dome and Miyajima in Hiroshima, Okayama Korakuen, and Kurashiki's historic quarter. The San'in side is less crowded, with Izumo Taisha, Matsue Castle, and the Tottori Sand Dunes.
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.intro.1: For a first visit, take the Shinkansen west from Kansai and spend two nights in Hiroshima and one night in Okayama—a classic route. On a second visit, take a limited express north from Okayama into San'in, or cycle from Onomichi across the islands on the Shimanami Kaido to Shikoku. The Chugoku Mountains separate Sanyo and San'in, and JR limited express trains take more than 2 hours, so don't plan on a day trip there and back.
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.name: Chugoku
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.passes.0.name: JR Okayama–Hiroshima–Yamaguchi Area Pass
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.passes.0.text: About ¥17,000 for 5 days. It includes reserved seats on the Sanyo Shinkansen from Okayama to Hakata and the ferry to Miyajima. It pays off if you spend 3 days or more west of Okayama.
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.passes.1.name: JR Sanyo–San'in Area Pass
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.passes.1.text: About ¥23,000 for 7 days. It includes the Sanyo Shinkansen from Shin-Osaka to Hakata (excluding Nozomi and Mizuho trains) and San'in limited express trains. It's the best choice for combining Sanyo and San'in on a trip from Kansai.
03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.passes.2.name: JR Tottori–Matsue Area Pass

03d3b0bc5aa4ab12709c.season: Spring and fall are best. In winter, eat oysters on the Sanyo side and Matsuba crab in San'in. The islands are very sunny in summer.

05aa01b32bc84be07b89.access.0.how: Air China operates about 2 nonstop flights a week from Beijing to Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD), taking about 13–14 hours. Many travelers come by train from New York or connect through another city.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.access.1.how: The Silver Line runs directly to the airport and takes about 50–60 minutes to downtown. From Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA), the Metro takes about 15–20 minutes into the city.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.access.2.how: Amtrak takes about 3–3.5 hours to Union Station. Buses take about 4–5 hours and are cheaper, but travel time depends on traffic.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.cover.alt: Washington Monument reflected in the Reflecting Pool at sunrise
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.0.name: Half-Smoke
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.0.text: Washington’s signature hot dog is a thick smoked sausage made from a pork-and-beef blend. It is spicier and chewier than a regular hot dog and is usually topped with chili, onions, and mustard. A longtime shop on U Street that opened in 1958 is a popular late-night stop for locals.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.0.where: Long-running hot dog shops and stadium stands around U Street.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.1.name: Ethiopian cuisine
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.1.text: Washington is home to the largest Ethiopian community in the United States, making Ethiopian food one of the city’s specialties. Various stews are served on a large, tangy flatbread: spicy chicken, lentils, sautéed beef, and vegetables. There are plenty of vegetarian options.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.1.where: Around U Street and Shaw, as well as Silver Spring to the north.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.2.name: Maryland crab cake
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.2.text: The nearby Chesapeake Bay is known for blue crabs. Crab cakes are made almost entirely from crab meat, held together with just a little breading, then fried until crisp outside and tender inside. A good crab cake falls apart with the first bite and tastes sweet and rich with crab. It is served with tartar sauce and lemon.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.2.where: Seafood markets and restaurants along the Wharf on Washington’s Southwest Waterfront.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.3.name: Jumbo slice
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.3.text: A late-night staple in Adams Morgan’s bar district, a jumbo slice is so large that it takes two paper plates to hold. It is cheap and filling, and a standard stop for Washington’s young crowd after a night out. The flavor is average, but it is worth trying once.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.foods.3.where: The 18th Street bar district in Adams Morgan, open at night.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.intro.0: Washington is the U.S. capital and the city with the most free museums in the country. More than a dozen Smithsonian museums line both sides of the National Mall, covering air and space, natural history, American history, African American history, and art. Three days is enough to see the Mall and the museums you most want to visit.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.intro.1: The National Mall stretches about 3 km from the United States Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial, with the Washington Monument in the middle. Walking the full length, plus the Jefferson Memorial and the World War II and Vietnam Veterans Memorials around the Tidal Basin, takes some effort. You can rent a shared bike or electric scooter.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.intro.2: Tours of the United States Capitol, the Washington Monument elevator, the Library of Congress, and some museums require free timed-entry tickets. Book them on the official websites about a month before your trip.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.name: Washington, D.C.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.seasons.note: Peak cherry blossom season usually runs from the last week of March through the first week of April, but it varies each year. September–October is cool. July–August is hot and humid, with frequent thunderstorms.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.sources.6.title: China–U.S. nonstop flight roundup (U.S. credit card guide)
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.0.fee: Free; a small booking fee applies online
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.0.name: National Mall and Washington Monument
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.0.text: This long lawn runs from the United States Capitol in the east to the Lincoln Memorial in the west and is the backbone of sightseeing in Washington. The white obelisk in the middle, about 169 meters high, is the Washington Monument. The elevator takes you to an observation level with views of the entire Mall and the White House. The World War II Memorial and Reflecting Pool are within walking distance. An evening loop is especially pleasant.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.0.tip: A timed-entry ticket is required for the monument. Tickets are released on recreation.gov 30 days ahead, and a small number are also available on-site at 8:45 a.m. the same day.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.1.name: Lincoln Memorial
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.1.text: This white marble temple was modeled on a Greek temple. Inside is a huge seated statue of Lincoln, with two of his famous speeches carved into the walls. Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his “I Have a Dream” speech on the steps here. From the steps, the Reflecting Pool, Washington Monument, and Capitol line up to the east. The view is even better after the lights come on at night.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.1.tip: Open 24 hours. Visit at night for fewer people and good lighting, and stop by the Korean War and Vietnam Veterans Memorials nearby.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.2.name: Smithsonian museums on the National Mall
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.2.text: Most museums along the National Mall are free. First-time visitors should prioritize three: the National Museum of Natural History for the Hope Diamond and dinosaur hall; the National Air and Space Museum for the Wright brothers’ plane and Apollo spacecraft; and the National Museum of African American History and Culture, whose galleries rise floor by floor from the underground. The National Gallery of Art is also free but is not part of the Smithsonian.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.2.tip: The National Air and Space Museum requires a free timed-entry ticket booked in advance. Most museums are open from about 10 a.m. to 17:30.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.3.name: United States Capitol
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.3.text: The white-domed United States Capitol is where Congress meets. Enter through the underground Visitor Center, where a guide leads you through the Rotunda’s dome murals and the National Statuary Hall. Tours are free, but timed-entry tickets must be booked on the official website. Afterward, take the underground tunnel to the Library of Congress’s Thomas Jefferson Building across the street. Its Main Reading Room has an especially ornate ceiling.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.3.tip: Security is strict. Food, drinks, sprays, and similar items are not allowed. The Library of Congress also requires a separate free timed-entry ticket.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.4.name: Tidal Basin cherry blossoms
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.4.text: More than a thousand cherry trees, gifted by Japan, grow around the Tidal Basin. When they bloom, the entire shoreline turns pink and white, with the Jefferson Memorial’s dome across the water. Peak bloom lasts only a few days, and the National Park Service forecasts the date each year based on the flower buds. The area is worth visiting outside cherry blossom season too. A walk around the basin can include the Franklin Delano Roosevelt Memorial and Martin Luther King, Jr. Memorial.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.4.tip: Go at sunrise during cherry blossom season for fewer people and better light. Hotels raise their rates early during those weeks.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.5.name: Georgetown
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.5.text: This historic neighborhood predates Washington itself. Its brick row houses, cobblestone sidewalks, and 19th-century canal path feel completely different from the formal government district. M Street and Wisconsin Avenue are lined with shops and restaurants. Waterfront Park is to the south, and Georgetown University is to the north. There is no Metro station here, but you can take a bus or walk from Dupont Circle.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.5.tip: Go to the waterfront at sunset, then have dinner on M Street.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.6.name: Smithsonian's National Zoo
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.6.text: This free Smithsonian zoo sits in Rock Creek Park, with paths winding up and down the hillsides. The giant pandas along the Asia Trail draw many visitors, and there are also elephants, lions, tigers, and orangutans. Families can spend half a day here. Get off at Woodley Park station on the Red Line and walk uphill for about 10 minutes.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.spots.6.tip: Admission is free, but everyone must reserve an entry pass on the official website, including babies.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.stay: Stay downtown north of the National Mall, around Pennsylvania Avenue, or in Dupont Circle. The sights are just a few Metro stops away. Rosslyn and Crystal City in Virginia are also on the Metro and are often somewhat cheaper.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.tagline: The capital with the highest concentration of monuments and free museums
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.tips.0: Most museums are free, but the National Air and Space Museum, United States Capitol, Library of Congress, and monument elevator require timed-entry tickets booked in advance.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.tips.1: Washington Metro uses SmarTrip. You can add it directly to an iPhone or Android mobile wallet. Fares vary by distance and time of day.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.tips.2: The District’s sales and dining taxes are not included in listed prices. The dining tax is higher than the general sales tax. Tip separately.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.tips.3: There is little shade on the Mall, so bring water, a hat, and sunscreen in summer. Most museums close around 17:30.
05aa01b32bc84be07b89.tips.4: Security is strict at federal buildings. Knives, sprays, selfie sticks, and similar items may be stopped at the entrance.

08a704e0a530c56ac283.access.0.how: The JR limited express HARUKA takes about 75–80 minutes to Kyoto Station. International visitors can buy a discounted one-way ticket in advance for about ¥2,700.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.access.1.how: The JR Special Rapid from Osaka Station takes about 30 minutes. The Hankyu line from Osaka-Umeda to Kyoto-Kawaramachi takes about 45 minutes and goes directly to the Shijo area.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.access.2.how: The Tokaido Shinkansen Nozomi takes about 2 hours 15 minutes to Kyoto Station.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.access.3.how: The Kintetsu line from Kintetsu-Nara Station to Kyoto Station takes about 35 minutes by limited express or about 45 minutes by express.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.0.name: Yudofu
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.0.text: Silken tofu gently warmed in kombu broth and eaten with soy sauce and condiments. The flavor is delicate, highlighting Kyoto's clean water and the fragrance of soybeans. It is especially comforting in winter. It is usually served as a set meal with tempura and small side dishes.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.0.where: Traditional restaurants around Nanzen-ji and Arashiyama, many with garden seating.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.1.name: Nishin soba
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.1.text: Hot soba topped with a whole herring simmered in a sweet-and-savory sauce. The fish's salty sweetness slowly blends into the broth, making it a warming winter meal.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.1.where: Traditional noodle shops around Gion-Shijo and Minamiza; also common around Kyoto Station.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.2.name: Obanzai
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.2.text: Everyday Kyoto home cooking: simmered pumpkin, braised daikon, and dressed greens made with seasonal vegetables and dashi. The flavors are light. Many small restaurants display a dozen or more dishes at the counter for you to choose from. Add a bowl of rice for a satisfying dinner.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.2.where: Small restaurants around Shijo-Karasuma, Nishiki Market, and Pontocho.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.3.name: Uji matcha sweets
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.3.text: Uji is one of Japan's best-known matcha-producing regions. You can try matcha parfaits, matcha ice cream, and fresh mochi with a strong tea flavor. The bitterness is more pronounced than in matcha desserts elsewhere. For a traditional drink, order usucha with wagashi.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.3.where: Tea shops along the approach to Byodo-in in Uji, as well as around Kyoto Station and Gion.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.4.name: Saba sushi
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.4.text: Mackerel from Wakasa Bay was once salted and transported to Kyoto, where it was made into thick pressed sushi. The flavor is moderately salty and tangy. It is a traditional dish for festivals and entertaining. A sliced piece also makes a good late-night snack back at your hotel.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.foods.4.where: Traditional sushi restaurants in Gion and the basement food halls of department stores.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.intro.0: Kyoto served as Japan's capital for more than a thousand years. It has so many temples, shrines, and old streets that you could not see them all in a lifetime. On your first visit, don't try to do too much. Exploring by area is easiest: spend one day in Higashiyama (Kiyomizu-dera, Gion, and Ginkaku-ji), one day in Arashiyama, half a day each at Kinkaku-ji and Fushimi Inari Taisha, and another half day in Uji or Kibune.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.intro.1: Crowds are Kyoto's biggest problem. Popular sights start to develop lines after 9 am, and city buses are often too packed to board. Leave early whenever possible. Take the subway, JR, or Keihan instead of waiting for a bus. During cherry blossom and fall foliage season, move popular sights to weekdays.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.intro.2: If you have an extra day or two, Amanohashidate and Ine in northern Kyoto Prefecture are worth an overnight stay. The scenery there is all bays, pine forests, and fishing villages. The pace is slower and the crowds are lighter—a completely different side of Kyoto from the temple-filled city center.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.name: Kyoto
08a704e0a530c56ac283.seasons.note: Cherry blossoms usually appear from late March to early April, and fall foliage peaks from mid-November to early December. These are also the most beautiful, crowded, and expensive periods. January–February is quieter, while summers are hot and humid.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.sources.0.title: Kyoto Tourism Navi: Notice on changes to Kyoto City accommodation tax
08a704e0a530c56ac283.sources.1.title: Kyoto City Transportation Bureau: Overview of the preferential city bus fare system for residents
08a704e0a530c56ac283.sources.2.title: Ginkaku-ji: Notice on revised admission fees (effective April 1, 2026)
08a704e0a530c56ac283.sources.3.title: Byodo-in: Visitor information
08a704e0a530c56ac283.sources.4.title: JR West: WEST QR HARUKA One-way Ticket
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.0.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.0.text: Thousands of vermilion torii form a tunnel through the hills, making this Kyoto's most photographed sight. The entrance is the busiest area, and the crowds thin out as you climb. From Yotsutsuji halfway up, you can look over Kyoto. The round trip to the summit takes about 2–3 hours. JR Inari Station is right outside the gate. The shrine is open 24 hours and admission is free.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.0.tip: Go before 8 am or in the evening if you want a people-free shot of the Senbon Torii.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.1.name: Kiyomizu-dera & Sannenzaka
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.1.text: The wooden Kiyomizu Stage, suspended over the hillside, is one of Kyoto's signature views. Cherry blossoms in spring and fall foliage in autumn spread out below. Walk downhill along the stone-paved lanes of Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka, lined with traditional shops and teahouses, then continue to Yasaka Shrine and Gion.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.1.tip: The slopes are packed during the day, so go early when the temple opens. Special evening visits are held in spring and fall.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.2.name: Gion & Hanamikoji
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.2.text: This is Kyoto's most atmospheric traditional neighborhood. Teahouses and ryotei line the stone-paved streets, which look their best when the lanterns come on at dusk. You can also walk along the Shirakawa River and visit Yasaka Shrine, which stays lively at night. This is where geiko and maiko live and work—not a staged tourist attraction.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.2.tip: Photography is prohibited on private lanes around Hanamikoji. Do not block the way or chase geiko and maiko for photos.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.3.name: Arashiyama & Tenryu-ji
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.3.text: This scenic district lies in western Kyoto. The garden at World Heritage-listed Tenryu-ji uses the mountains of Arashiyama as its backdrop. The north gate opens onto the bamboo grove, with smaller temples such as Jojakko-ji farther north. The fall colors are beautiful. Togetsukyo Bridge offers the broadest mountain views, and you can also rent a boat or ride the Sagano Romantic Train.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.3.tip: Visit the bamboo grove before 8 am. After 9 am, the path is usually packed.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.4.name: Kinkaku-ji
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.4.text: The Golden Pavilion, covered in gold leaf, is reflected in Kyokochi Pond. It is one of Kyoto's most famous postcard views. The route is one-way and takes 30–40 minutes. Nearby Ryoan-ji and Ninna-ji can be combined for a half-day northern Kyoto route. The pavilion covered in snow is a rare sight.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.4.tip: Arrive when it opens at 9 am. Tour groups usually start arriving after about 10 am.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.5.name: Ginkaku-ji & Philosopher's Path
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.5.text: Ginkaku-ji is not actually silver. The highlights are the white-sand Silver Sand Sea and the moss garden. From the entrance, follow the canal south to the Philosopher's Path, a flat route about 2 kilometers long. In spring it is lined with cherry blossoms, and in fall with colorful leaves. At the end, you can continue to Nanzen-ji and Eikando.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.5.tip: There are plenty of cafés along the way for a break. During blossom season, go in the morning, when it is much less crowded than in the afternoon.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.6.name: Tofuku-ji
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.6.text: One of Kyoto's top fall foliage spots. From the wooden Tsutenkyo Bridge, you can look down over a valley filled with maple trees. In late November, the colors are almost fiery. The abbot's square moss garden is a modern garden masterpiece. It is only one stop from Fushimi Inari, so you can see the foliage in the morning and walk through the torii in the afternoon.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.6.tip: People line up before opening during foliage season, and the crowds grow throughout the day. Photography is prohibited on Tsutenkyo Bridge during peak periods.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.7.name: Byodo-in, Uji
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.7.text: The Phoenix Hall depicted on the back of the ¥10 coin stands here. This original Heian-period building is especially beautiful reflected in the pond. Uji is also a major matcha-producing area. The approach is lined with tea shops where you can drink tea and try matcha desserts, then take a stroll along the Uji River. From Kyoto, the JR Nara Line takes about 20–30 minutes.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.7.tip: Entry to the Phoenix Hall interior costs about ¥300 extra. Visitors enter in timed groups, so register when you first arrive.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.8.name: Kurama & Kibune
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.8.text: A half-day hike in the mountains north of Kyoto. Climb from Kurama-dera through cedar forests and over the ridge to Kifune Shrine, a walk of about 1.5–2 hours. In summer, Kibune is known for kawadoko dining platforms built over the stream. The fall foliage is also beautiful, and temperatures are several degrees cooler than in the city. The Eizan Railway from Demachiyanagi takes about 30 minutes.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.8.tip: The trail has stairs and tree roots, so wear comfortable walking shoes. Reserve kawadoko dining in Kibune in advance.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.9.name: Amanohashidate & Ine
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.9.text: A coastal escape in northern Kyoto Prefecture. Amanohashidate is a pine-covered sandbar stretching across a bay and is considered one of Japan's Three Scenic Views. From the hilltop observatory, the famous view is to bend over and look at it upside down between your legs. Then take a bus to Ine to see its fishing village and rows of funaya built over the water. The limited express from Kyoto takes about 2 hours.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.spots.9.tip: A day trip is too rushed. Stay overnight in Amanohashidate or Ine.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.stay: For a first visit, stay near Kyoto Station, Shijo-Kawaramachi, or Karasuma. Kyoto Station is the most convenient for the airport, Nara, and Osaka. The Shijo area is good for dining and shopping, and Gion is within walking distance at night.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.tagline: A thousand-year-old capital, best explored one neighborhood at a time
08a704e0a530c56ac283.tips.0: From March 2026, Kyoto's accommodation tax will have 5 tiers based on the room rate per person per night, ranging from about ¥200–10,000. It is usually paid separately at check-in.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.tips.1: City buses toward Kiyomizu-dera and Kinkaku-ji are often too crowded to board. Take the subway, JR, or Keihan instead of waiting for a bus. For groups of 3–4, a taxi can also be cost-effective.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.tips.2: Arriving at popular sights before 8–9 am and after 10 am offer two completely different experiences. During blossom season, visit popular sights on weekdays.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.tips.3: Kyoto plans to raise city bus fares for nonresidents from fiscal 2027, with preferential prices for residents. Follow the announcement at the time.
08a704e0a530c56ac283.tips.4: Don't take large luggage on buses. Use the luggage storage or hotel delivery service at Kyoto Station.

08cc4024c6bdf4dcc717.cost: Sunday daily transit cap ~A$9.65; Scenic World pass ~A$58–65
08cc4024c6bdf4dcc717.duration: Full day (~2 hours each way by train)
08cc4024c6bdf4dcc717.location: Central Station → Katoomba Station → Echo Point → Scenic World
08cc4024c6bdf4dcc717.paragraphs.0: Reach Central Station around 08:15 and check the departure boards for the BMT Blue Mountains Line double-decker intercity train bound for Katoomba or Lithgow (download the TripView app ahead of time for live platform updates). Tap your phone through the gate and head straight for an upper-deck window seat—two hours of climbing through mountain ridges brings you to the town of Katoomba.
08cc4024c6bdf4dcc717.paragraphs.1: Right outside the station, tap the same phone onto the loop bus 686; in 10 minutes you're standing at Echo Point. Vast eucalyptus forests blanketing the Jamison Valley release a fine mist of eucalyptus oil that scatters sunlight into a dreamy pale blue—the real reason the Blue Mountains got their name. After photographing the Three Sisters rock formation, ride bus 686 two stops to Scenic World for its three signature rides: plunge into the valley on the world's steepest 52° red mine railway, walk the ancient rainforest boardwalk, and glide back across the canyon in a glass-floored cableway.
08cc4024c6bdf4dcc717.phase: Step 02 · Day 2 (strongly recommended on Sunday!) Blue Mountains escape
08cc4024c6bdf4dcc717.photo.alt: Australia's Blue Mountains Three Sisters and canyon veiled in soft blue mist
08cc4024c6bdf4dcc717.photo.caption: Morning mist and eucalyptus oil cast an unmistakable pale-blue haze over the valley—and the round-trip train on Sunday's cap costs under ten Australian dollars.
08cc4024c6bdf4dcc717.tip: From Echo Point toward the Three Sisters, the Giant Stairway plunges over nine hundred steep steps to the valley floor. If you have sensitive knees or are short on time, walk just the first couple hundred steps to Honeymoon Bridge for the thrill instead of going all the way down.
08cc4024c6bdf4dcc717.title: Ride a double-decker Blue Mountains train 2 hours from Central Station for the Three Sisters and the 52° cliff railway

091bc6790d7395c8717f.gateways.0.how: The Sendai Airport Line takes about 25 minutes to Sendai Station and costs about ¥680. International routes mainly serve East Asia, so check seasonal flights before departure.
091bc6790d7395c8717f.gateways.0.name: Sendai Airport (SDJ)
091bc6790d7395c8717f.gateways.1.how: Take the Tohoku Shinkansen north: about 1.5 hours to Sendai, 2 hours 13 minutes to Morioka, and 3 hours to Shin-Aomori.
091bc6790d7395c8717f.gateways.1.name: Tokyo Station
091bc6790d7395c8717f.gateways.2.how: Travel south from Hokkaido. The Shinkansen takes about 1 hour to Shin-Aomori, making this a good option for combining Hokkaido and Tohoku.
091bc6790d7395c8717f.gateways.2.name: Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto Station
091bc6790d7395c8717f.intro.0: Tohoku covers the six prefectures in northern Honshu: Aomori, Iwate, Miyagi, Akita, Yamagata, and Fukushima. It is large and sparsely populated, with far fewer visitors from China than Kansai. The Tohoku Shinkansen runs north to south. It takes about 1.5 hours from Tokyo to Sendai and about 3 hours to Shin-Aomori. Akita and Yamagata also have direct Shinkansen branch lines, so you can reach the main sights by train.
091bc6790d7395c8717f.intro.1: The region has four distinct seasons. In late April, the cherry blossoms in Hirosaki and Kakunodate bloom a month later than those in Tokyo. In early August, three major festivals take place: Aomori Nebuta, Akita Kanto, and Sendai Tanabata. From mid-October, Oirase, Naruko Gorge, and other areas turn bright with fall foliage. In winter, see the snow monsters at Zao and the snowy scenery at Ginzan Onsen and Nyuto Onsen. Mountain buses run infrequently, so leave extra time in your itinerary.
091bc6790d7395c8717f.name: Tohoku
091bc6790d7395c8717f.passes.0.text: The JR East Pass for the entire JR East area (including Tohoku, Kanto, and Nagano–Niigata) costs about ¥35,000 for 5 consecutive days. If your itinerary starts in Tokyo and includes three or more Shinkansen rides, compare the price with individual tickets first.
091bc6790d7395c8717f.passes.1.name: JR Tohoku-South Hokkaido Rail Pass
091bc6790d7395c8717f.passes.1.text: About ¥32,000 for 6 consecutive days, covering Tohoku and the Hakodate and Sapporo areas but not Tokyo. Good for combining Hokkaido and Tohoku.
091bc6790d7395c8717f.season: Late-April cherry blossoms, early-August summer festivals, mid-to-late October fall foliage, and January–February snowy hot springs.

123e2c48b827bc8c2942.access.0.how: The domestic terminal connects directly to the subway, and Hakata Station is about 5 minutes away; from the international terminal, take the free shuttle bus to the domestic terminal or a direct bus to Hakata Station in about 20 minutes
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.access.1.how: Sanyo Shinkansen: about 2.5 hours from Shin-Osaka to Hakata and about 5 hours from Tokyo to Hakata; flying is usually cheaper
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.access.2.how: Kyushu Shinkansen: about 35 minutes from Hakata to Kumamoto and from 1 hour 20 minutes to Kagoshima-Chuo
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.access.3.how: Take a limited express and transfer to the Nishi Kyushu Shinkansen at Takeo Onsen on the same platform; the fastest trips take about 1 hour 20 minutes
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.0.name: Hakata ramen
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.0.text: Thin, straight noodles in a milky pork-bone broth. You can choose how firm you want the noodles. If you still have broth left, order a side of noodles called kaedama. This refill is a classic Hakata ramen custom.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.0.where: All around Hakata Station, Nakasu, and Tenjin; yatai also serve it
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.1.name: Motsunabe
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.1.text: Beef offal simmered with plenty of garlic chives, cabbage, and sliced garlic. Common broths include soy sauce and miso. Finish with noodles or zosui rice porridge. It is especially comforting in winter.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.1.where: Izakaya around Hakata Station, Tenjin, and Nakasu
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.2.name: Mizutaki
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.2.text: A whole chicken is simmered for hours into a milky-white broth. Drink a bowl of the plain broth first, then add the chicken and vegetables. The flavor is mild and suits diners who prefer lighter food.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.2.where: Long-established specialty restaurants in Hakata, Nakasu, and Tenjin
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.3.name: Yatai street stalls
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.3.text: These stalls are set up along the streets in the evening and serve ramen, oden, skewers, and stir-fried noodles. Around ten people squeeze onto the seats. The atmosphere is the main attraction, so try one or two dishes and move on to the next stall.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.3.where: Along the Naka River in Nakasu, Tenjin, and the Nagahama area
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.4.name: Mentaiko
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.4.text: Pollock roe cured with spicy seasonings, and Fukuoka's most famous souvenir food. Eat it with white rice, use it in onigiri, or mix it into pasta. Many shops also sell mentaiko baguettes.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.foods.4.where: Souvenir areas at Hakata Station and Fukuoka Airport, plus department-store basements
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.intro.0: Fukuoka is Kyushu's largest city and the main gateway to the region. The airport is remarkably close to downtown, and the subway reaches Hakata Station in just a few minutes. You can land and be eating ramen or exploring yatai the same day. The city is compact and slower-paced than Tokyo or Osaka, making it a good choice for first-time visitors and anyone who wants an easier trip.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.intro.1: One day is enough for the city: visit shrines and parks by day, then eat around Nakasu and Tenjin at night. With more time, take day trips to Dazaifu, Yanagawa, or Mojiko. Farther afield, Yufuin, Nagasaki, and Kumamoto are all reachable from Hakata, so many travelers use Fukuoka as the starting and ending point of a Kyushu trip.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.name: Fukuoka
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.seasons.note: See cherry blossoms and wisteria in spring, and enjoy hot pot in the cool fall weather. The Hakata Gion Yamakasa takes place in early July. June is the rainy season, and typhoons are possible in summer and fall.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.sources.0.title: JR Kyushu Rail Pass official information
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.sources.1.title: Kawachi Fujien official website
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.sources.2.title: Dazaifu Tenmangu official website
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.0.name: Dazaifu Tenmangu
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.0.text: Dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane, the deity of learning, this shrine draws many visitors seeking good luck before exams. Plum blossoms fill the grounds in early spring, and the approach is lined with shops selling umegae mochi. Eating one as you walk is part of the experience. The Kyushu National Museum is right next door. Take the escalator through the tunnel behind the shrine to reach it, and you can see both in half a day.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.0.tip: Take the Nishitetsu train from Tenjin in about 30 minutes, changing at Nishitetsu Futsukaichi. Weekends get busy after 10 a.m., so go early.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.1.name: Kushida Shrine
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.1.text: Hakata's main guardian shrine and the starting point of the Hakata Gion Yamakasa festival. A decorative float more than ten meters high is displayed here year-round, so you can see one even outside the July festival. It is a short walk from Hakata Station and Nakasu, making it an easy stop while exploring downtown. Kawabata Shopping Arcade is just beyond it.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.1.tip: During the Yamakasa festival from July 1–15, the Oiyamanarashi race takes place early in the morning. Check the time in advance if you want to watch; crowds are very large.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.2.name: Ohori Park & Fukuoka Castle Ruins
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.2.text: A large lake fills the center of Ohori Park, where locals jog and walk their dogs. One lap around the lake is about 2 kilometers. Nearby Maizuru Park contains the ruins of Fukuoka Castle, including its stone walls. It is the city's most popular cherry blossom spot in spring, with evening illuminations. Rest at the lakeside Starbucks or Japanese garden when you need a break.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.2.tip: Get off at Ohori Koen Station and you are there. Weekend evenings during cherry blossom season are very crowded, so weekdays are more comfortable.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.3.name: Mojiko Retro
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.3.text: This former international trading port preserves a group of red-brick Western-style buildings and the restored Mojiko Station. The waterfront is great for photos, and a ferry takes about 5 minutes to reach Karato Market in Shimonoseki, across the strait, for sushi. Plan half a day to a full day. Go in the afternoon, stay for the night view, and then return to Fukuoka.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.3.tip: Take the shinkansen from Hakata to Kokura, then transfer to a local JR train to Mojiko. Karato Market is busiest around noon on weekends.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.4.fee: About ¥2,000–2,200; prices vary slightly by operator
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.4.name: Yanagawa River Cruise
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.4.text: Yanagawa is a small city threaded with canals. Boatmen slowly pole flat-bottomed boats past willows and old homes on a ride lasting about an hour, with commentary and songs along the way. After getting off, eat a serving of steamed eel over rice—the classic Yanagawa itinerary.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.4.tip: Take the Nishitetsu limited express from Tenjin in about 50 minutes. Boats have kotatsu heaters in winter; bring a hat and sun protection in summer.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.5.fee: Varies with bloom conditions; advance tickets required
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.5.name: Kawachi Fujien
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.5.text: This privately run wisteria garden is known for its seemingly endless wisteria tunnels during the bloom season, which draws many visitors to northern Kyushu. The flowers usually bloom from late April to early May. The garden also opens briefly for fall foliage. Admission varies with bloom conditions, and tickets are not sold at the gate.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.5.tip: You must buy a timed-entry ticket in advance through the official website or at a convenience store. There is no public transportation nearby, so a tour or private car is recommended.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.6.name: Sakurai Futamigaura, Itoshima
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.6.text: Two sacred rocks stand in the sea, joined by a shimenawa rope, with a white torii on the shore. The view is best around sunset. Itoshima's coast has many seaside cafés, making it a good half-day drive for ocean views. It is a popular weekend escape for Fukuoka residents.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.6.tip: Bus service is infrequent. Driving rules depend on your licence, so check the official requirements before renting a car. A day tour or private car is recommended; arrive before sunset.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.7.name: Akizuki
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.7.text: Known as the Little Kyoto of Chikuzen, this small castle town retains its stone walls, old homes, and moat. The Sugi-no-Baba area becomes a tunnel of cherry blossoms in spring, while the ruins of Akizuki Castle are famous for fall foliage. It is usually quiet and ideal for a leisurely walk.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.spots.7.tip: Take a bus from Amagi Station. Services are infrequent, so check the return schedule before setting out. Traffic can be heavy on fall foliage weekends.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.stay: Stay around Hakata Station or Tenjin. Hakata Station is best for shinkansen connections and the airport; Tenjin and Nakasu have more restaurants, bars, and shopping. The two areas are only a few subway stops apart, so either works well.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.tagline: The gateway to Kyushu: ramen, yatai, and easy connections everywhere
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.tips.0: Look for Nishitetsu sightseeing passes for Dazaifu and Yanagawa. They combine train fares with attraction discounts and cost less than buying everything separately.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.tips.1: Yatai generally open in the evening. They may not operate on rainy or very windy days.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.tips.2: The international terminal is separate from the subway station, so allow time for the shuttle bus when catching a flight.
123e2c48b827bc8c2942.tips.3: The shinkansen from Hakata to Kokura is operated by JR West and is not covered by the JR Kyushu Rail Pass.

14203a69ba6a49997b3f.0: If your last trip to Japan was in 2025, wipe your old tax-free muscle memory clean before you fly. 2026 brought Japan's densest wave of visitor policy changes in a decade: the International Tourist Tax (departure tax) jumped to ¥3,000 in July, shopping switched nationwide on November 1 to a pay-now, refund-at-departure model, and hot-spot cities like Kyoto rolled out steep tiered accommodation taxes.
14203a69ba6a49997b3f.1: In mid-November I field-tested the entire flow out of both Haneda and Kansai airports, and cross-checked two weeks of real traveler mishaps from Xiaohongshu (RedNote) and Reddit's r/JapanTravelTips. Below is the exact sequence broken into 6 practical steps—follow it in order and you'll enjoy ditching the sealed bags without accidentally handing back your 10% refund at the airport.

1425da54a113faa415d1.location: JR Noboribetsu → 15 min Donan Bus → Noboribetsu Onsen & Hell Valley
1425da54a113faa415d1.paragraphs.0: If your suitcase is bigger than 26 inches, leave it stored at your Sapporo hotel or forward it via Yamato Takkyubin and carry only a two-day backpack to Noboribetsu and Lake Toya—hauling a 20 kg trunk across deep snow while waiting for mountain buses is pure misery.
1425da54a113faa415d1.paragraphs.1: At JR Noboribetsu, step straight onto the waiting Donan Bus up to Onsen Town (ryokans allow early bag drop before 15:00 check-in). Walk the wooden trails of Jigokudani (Hell Valley) before 15:30 dark: sub-zero air meets boiling rust-red volcanic vents throwing towering clouds of sulfur steam over snowdrifts. Return at dusk for yukata, snow-dusted open-air sulfur baths, and a kaiseki or crab buffet dinner.
1425da54a113faa415d1.photo.alt: Snowy volcanic steam vents at Noboribetsu Hell Valley in Hokkaido
1425da54a113faa415d1.photo.caption: White volcanic steam roars into freezing air across snow-blanketed cliffs at Noboribetsu Jigokudani—walking the boardwalk feels like another planet.
1425da54a113faa415d1.tip: Jigokudani's boardwalks get slick in winter and deeper trails toward Oyunuma close during heavy snow—stick to the main overlook and Tessen-ike path and stay behind railings.
1425da54a113faa415d1.title: Travel Light on the Hokuto Express, Hike Steaming Jigokudani & Soak in Milky Sulfur Springs

176747677677b4641aac.days.5.title: The Rocky Steps to the Lincoln Memorial
176747677677b4641aac.days.6.move: Reserve free timed tickets in advance for the U.S. Capitol, the National Air and Space Museum and the monument elevators.
176747677677b4641aac.days.6.title: A full day on the National Mall
176747677677b4641aac.days.7.items.2.note: In the afternoon, take the Metro Silver Line to Dulles International Airport. Arrive 3 hours before your international flight.

176747677677b4641aac.days.7.title: Georgetown, then depart
176747677677b4641aac.for: First-time visitors to the U.S. who don't want to drive and want to see major cities and museums
176747677677b4641aac.summary: Arrive in New York and depart from Washington, D.C. Take trains throughout, with no driving. Spend 4 nights in New York, exploring downtown, the Upper East Side and Midtown by area. On day 5, take Amtrak to Philadelphia to visit Independence Hall. Continue to Washington, D.C. on day 6, then spend the final two days at the National Mall and its free museums. Reserve tickets in advance for Independence Hall, the U.S. Capitol and popular observation decks.

1a17260fc11e7d024a92.0: If you had to pick one global metropolis where you can skip the rental car completely and still pull off a dream coastal vacation on foot and public transit, Sydney easily lands in the top three. Trains, metro, light rail, harbor ferries, and beach buses all tie together seamlessly—and you can tap Apple Pay, Google Pay, or any contactless Visa/Mastercard straight at the gates without ever buying a physical Opal card.
1a17260fc11e7d024a92.1: The biggest money-saving trick in this field-tested 4-day, 3-night itinerary is stacking the longest rides—the round-trip Blue Mountains National Park train and the harbor ferry—onto Sunday. Thanks to New South Wales' low Sunday daily fare cap, you can travel from mountain canyons to ocean surf all day for under ten Australian dollars, alongside the Opera House's best sunset angle, the 6 km Bondi-to-Coogee cliff walk, and brunch spots locals happily line up for.

1dc74dc83a3607be6bbb.cost: Build in an extra 45–60 minutes of airport buffer
1dc74dc83a3607be6bbb.duration: 3 minutes for green light; 20–40 minutes in line for red light
1dc74dc83a3607be6bbb.location: Departure-level customs tax-free zones at Narita, Haneda, Kansai, New Chitose, and other international terminals
1dc74dc83a3607be6bbb.paragraphs.0: The moment you step off the train or bus into the terminal, resist the instinct to join your airline's check-in line. Look up for 'Tax-Free / Customs Verification' signs, wheel every suitcase containing tax-free goods to a self-service KIOSK, and scan your passport's photo page. The system pulls up every tax-free purchase tied to your stay automatically.
1dc74dc83a3607be6bbb.paragraphs.1: Only two outcomes appear on screen. Green (OK / Green) means you're cleared immediately—roll your bags to airline check-in, clear security, and your refund hits your linked card or e-wallet automatically after departure. Red (Red) means you've been selected for inspection: take the relevant bags and your passport straight to the adjacent staffed customs counter, show the physical goods, get the officer's digital sign-off, and then check in.
1dc74dc83a3607be6bbb.phase: Step 03 · Arrive at the airport 3 hours early
1dc74dc83a3607be6bbb.photo.alt: Self-service tax-free verification kiosk area inside a Japanese airport overlooking the tarmac at sunset
1dc74dc83a3607be6bbb.photo.caption: Never flip the airport order: self-service passport scan first → green clearance or red-light customs check → airline bag drop last.
1dc74dc83a3607be6bbb.tip: Between 14:00 and 17:00, Kansai T1 and Narita T2 see dense banks of flights to mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, backing up the red-light manual counters fast. While the new system settles in, arrive at least 3 hours before departure.
1dc74dc83a3607be6bbb.title: Head straight to the tax-free KIOSK: scan for green or red before checking bags

1eae7aa8084cab21deee.cost: Kanazawa → Shirakawa-go about ¥2,800; Shirakawa-go → Takayama about ¥2,600
1eae7aa8084cab21deee.duration: Register 1 day early; complete checkout in 5 minutes on release morning
1eae7aa8084cab21deee.location: Japan Bus Online / Highwaybus.com official websites
1eae7aa8084cab21deee.paragraphs.0: Never wait until you land in Japan to try your luck at the ticket counter. Exactly 31 days before travel, create an account on Japan Bus Online or Highwaybus.com, save an internationally enabled Visa or Mastercard, and run a practice search so you recognize the exact route names (Kanazawa → Shirakawa-go and Shirakawa-go → Takayama).
1eae7aa8084cab21deee.paragraphs.1: The sweet-spot connection is the 08:40 or 09:40 departure from Kanazawa Station East Exit Stop 2 (1 hour 15 minutes), giving you a relaxed 3–3.5 hours in Shirakawa-go before catching the 14:00 or 14:30 reserved bus on to Takayama (50 minutes). Grab both legs the instant sales open; a screenshot of your e-ticket QR code or booking name on your phone is all you need to board, and large suitcases ride free in the under-bus luggage bay.
1eae7aa8084cab21deee.phase: Step 01 · 30 days ahead at 08:55 UTC+8 (09:55 JST)
1eae7aa8084cab21deee.tip: If you log in late and the Shirakawa-go → Takayama reserved buses show sold out, don't panic: a small number of non-R unreserved local buses still run between Takayama and Shirakawa-go—just queue at the Shirakawa-go Bus Terminal 35–40 minutes early for a solid shot at boarding (the Kanazawa leg, however, is virtually all-reserved, so no seat means changing dates).
1eae7aa8084cab21deee.title: Book both reserved bus legs: Kanazawa → Shirakawa-go and Shirakawa-go → Takayama
