1f019f7c4d8ab252ecda.cost: Tsutenkyo autumn admission ~¥1,000; Gaunkyo Bridge free
1f019f7c4d8ab252ecda.location: Tofuku-ji · 10-minute walk from JR Nara Line / Keihan Tofukuji Station
1f019f7c4d8ab252ecda.paragraphs.0: Tofuku-ji's Sengyokukan ravine is one of Japan's grandest maple valleys, yet by 14:00 the bridge can get so jammed you can barely raise a camera. After testing it myself, only three painless strategies work. Option A: if you're staying near Kyoto Station, save Tofuku-ji for 08:15 the next morning to enter first (or reserve a 07:30 early-access slot via JR Central's EX service) and soak up crisp dawn light.
1f019f7c4d8ab252ecda.paragraphs.1: Option B: on a single-day itinerary, ride the Keihan Line south from eastern Kyoto to arrive around 15:15—low golden sunlight sweeps the ravine as tour buses pull out for dinner, and crowds ease noticeably right before last ticket entry at 15:30. Option C is the zero-stress move: walk the free neighboring Gaunkyo Bridge looking across at Tsutenkyo and the sea of red leaves—no lingering or tripods allowed, yet that iconic postcard angle costs nothing.
1f019f7c4d8ab252ecda.phase: Step 05 · 15:00 Cracking Tofuku-ji (or saving it for dawn)
1f019f7c4d8ab252ecda.photo.alt: Panoramic late-afternoon view from Kyoto's Tofuku-ji Tsutenkyo Bridge over a valley of fiery autumn maples
1f019f7c4d8ab252ecda.photo.caption: Late-afternoon sun raking across two thousand maples in Sengyokukan turns the view from Tsutenkyo Bridge into a glowing crimson sea.
1f019f7c4d8ab252ecda.tip: During peak foliage, selfie sticks and tripods are banned on both Gaunkyo and Tsutenkyo bridges, and guards keep foot traffic moving one way. Dial in your camera exposure beforehand so you can shoot smoothly on the move.
1f019f7c4d8ab252ecda.title: 3 tested ways to see Tofuku-ji's crimson valley without getting crushed on Tsutenkyo Bridge

1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.access.0.how: Take the JR Kusatsu-Shima limited express to Naganohara-Kusatsuguchi, about 2 hours 20 minutes, then a JR bus to Kusatsu Onsen, about 25 minutes. There are only a few departures a day.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.access.1.how: Direct highway buses run from Shinjuku Expressway Bus Terminal to Kusatsu Onsen Bus Terminal in about 4 hours. No transfers are needed, and fares are lower than the train.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.access.2.how: The Joetsu or Hokuriku Shinkansen reaches Takasaki in about 50–60 minutes. Transfer here for Tomioka and Ikaho.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.foods.0.name: Mizusawa udon
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.foods.0.text: Served around Mizusawa Kannon near Ikaho, these glossy, chewy noodles are slightly thinner than Sanuki udon. They usually come cold with a sesame or soy-based dipping sauce. Udon restaurants line the temple approach, making this a handy meal stop on the way to Ikaho.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.foods.0.where: The approach to Mizusawa Kannon near Ikaho Onsen
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.foods.1.name: Yaki manju
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.foods.1.text: This everyday Gunma snack consists of fluffy steamed buns threaded onto bamboo skewers, brushed with a sweet and spicy miso sauce, and grilled over charcoal. Crisp outside and soft inside, they are inexpensive and sold in hot spring towns and at temple festivals. Eat them hot, and watch for sauce dripping onto your clothes.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.foods.1.where: Long-established shops and temple festivals around Ikaho, Takasaki, and Maebashi
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.foods.2.name: Onsen manju
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.foods.2.text: Ikaho claims to be one of the birthplaces of these hot spring buns. Their thin brown skins enclose sweet red bean paste, with the color said to mimic the local spring water. Shops around Yubatake in Kusatsu also sell plenty, often freshly steamed at the storefront. Some offer samples.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.foods.2.where: Ikaho’s stone steps and around Yubatake in Kusatsu
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.intro.0: Gunma is a favorite hot spring getaway for Tokyo residents. Its best-known resort, Kusatsu Onsen, centers on the steaming Yubatake hot spring field. Ikaho has a hot spring street with hundreds of stone steps, while Shima Onsen is quieter. Beyond the baths, there is the World Heritage-listed Tomioka Silk Mill and mountain scenery to the north, including Mount Tanigawa and the Oze wetlands. Come for skiing in winter and hiking in summer.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.intro.1: Kusatsu is about 3 hours from Tokyo. Stay overnight to see Yubatake lit up after dark and visit a public bath in the morning. Ikaho and Tomioka are close to Takasaki, making them easy day trips from Tokyo or stops on a longer route. Buses in Gunma’s mountains are infrequent, so check schedules before you go.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.name: Gunma
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.seasons.note: Mountain foliage peaks from mid-October to early November. Winter is best for hot springs with snowy views. Flowers bloom in the Oze wetlands from late May to July.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.sources.0.title: Gunma tourism: Getting to Kusatsu
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.sources.1.title: japan-guide: Getting from Tokyo to Kusatsu
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.sources.2.title: japan-guide: Sainokawara Park
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.sources.3.title: japan-guide: Tomioka Silk Mill
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.sources.4.title: japan-guide: Getting from Tokyo to Ikaho
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.0.name: Yubatake, Kusatsu Onsen
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.0.text: At this hot spring source in central Kusatsu, steaming water flows down rows of wooden channels to cool, filling the air with the smell of sulfur. It is especially beautiful when lit up at night. Shops, inns, and several free public baths surround it. Next door, Netsunoyu stages yumomi performances, with performers stirring the hot water with long wooden paddles to cool it while singing and dancing.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.0.tip: The water is highly acidic, so avoid putting on silver jewelry right after bathing. The free public baths are very hot; rinse first and ease into the water.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.1.name: Sainokawara Rotenburo
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.1.text: Walk west from Yubatake for a little over 10 minutes through Sainokawara Park, past steaming streams and small pools. At the far end are two large outdoor baths, one for each gender, surrounded by wooded mountains. A soak is especially atmospheric when it snows. There is a free footbath by the entrance if you prefer to keep your clothes on.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.1.tip: Opening time is later in winter. Photography is not allowed in the bathing area; lock up your valuables.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.2.name: Ikaho Onsen
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.2.text: More than three hundred stone steps climb to Ikaho Shrine, lined with inns, shooting galleries, and onsen manju shops that give the street a nostalgic Showa-era feel. The iron-rich Kogane no Yu, or golden water, is brownish in color. Direct highway buses from Shinjuku take about 2 and a half hours. You can also travel via Takasaki and connect to a bus.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.2.tip: Kajika Bridge, beyond the top of the steps, is especially beautiful in fall and is lit up at night. Wear flat shoes for the climb.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.3.name: Tomioka Silk Mill
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.3.text: Built in 1872 by the Meiji government with help from French engineers, this state-run silk mill helped launch Japan’s modernization. Its long red-brick warehouses and silk-reeling workshop are well preserved, earning it World Heritage status. Tours and original machinery show how silk exports helped build Japan’s economy. Take the Joshin Railway from Takasaki for about 35 minutes, then walk 10–15 minutes from the station.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.3.tip: The Joshin Railway offers a discount package with round-trip train fare and admission. Buy it at Takasaki Station to save over separate tickets.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.4.name: Fukiware Falls
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.4.text: The river plunges into a long fissure carved into the rocky riverbed, earning these falls the nickname “Niagara of the East.” Riverside paths bring you close to the rushing water, with beautiful foliage on both banks in fall. Buses run from Jomo-Kogen Station on the Joetsu Shinkansen or from Numata Station.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.4.tip: The trails usually close in winter. Keep well back from the edge where there are no railings.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.5.name: Mount Tanigawa
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.5.text: This prominent mountain straddles Niigata and Gunma. A ropeway takes you straight to Tenjindaira for views of its rugged cliffs without a hike. The slopes turn red and yellow in fall, and Tenjindaira becomes a ski area in winter. Experienced hikers can climb to the summit from the ropeway station; allow well over half a day for the round trip. Weather changes quickly, so bring proper gear. Buses run to the ropeway station from Jomo-Kogen or Minakami Station.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.5.tip: Summit weather is changeable, so check conditions at the ropeway station first. Beginners can take the ropeway to Tenjindaira and enjoy a walk there.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.6.name: Ozegahara Marsh
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.6.text: Honshu’s largest alpine wetland has boardwalks stretching for several kilometers through open marshland, backed by Mount Shibutsu and Mount Hiuchigatake. Asian skunk cabbage blooms from late May to June, followed by Nikko daylilies in July. The grasses turn gold from late September to early October. From Gunma, the usual entry point is Hatomachitoge Pass. Allow a full day for the round trip.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.spots.6.tip: Private vehicles are restricted on the approach to Hatomachitoge during peak season, so transfer to a shuttle bus. The area closes in winter; check opening dates before you go.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.stay: An overnight stay at Kusatsu Onsen is the top choice; the town is easy to explore on foot. For Ikaho and Tomioka, staying near Takasaki Station is most convenient for transportation.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.tagline: Kanto’s hot spring heartland, home to Kusatsu and Ikaho
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.tips.0: Snow is common in Kusatsu in winter, so wear shoes with good traction. Heavy snow can delay or cancel highway buses.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.tips.1: Limited express trains from Ueno to Naganohara-Kusatsuguchi are infrequent. Missing one can mean a wait of several hours, so reserve a seat ahead.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.tips.2: Many public baths in hot spring towns do not accept cards. Bring coins and cash.
1f0d24d2b8bcdbec28cb.tips.3: Buses in Gunma’s mountains are infrequent. Driving requirements depend on where your license was issued; check official sources for the permits or translations you need to drive in Japan.

20562d9f436d0eb71f66.gateways.0.how: The JR limited express HARUKA takes about 75–80 minutes to Kyoto. Discounted one-way tickets for international visitors cost about ¥2,700. The Nankai Railway takes about 35–45 minutes to Namba.
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.gateways.0.name: Kansai International Airport (KIX)
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.gateways.1.how: The Tokaido Shinkansen Nozomi takes about 2.5 hours from Tokyo. Kyoto is about 15 minutes away by Shinkansen. Transfer to the subway for Umeda and Namba.
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.gateways.1.name: Shin-Osaka Station
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.gateways.2.how: It serves domestic flights only, making it convenient for flights from Tokyo, Hokkaido, and Okinawa. Airport buses run directly to Umeda and Kyoto Station.
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.gateways.2.name: Osaka Itami Airport (ITM)
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.gateways.3.how: It is closer to Ise-Shima in Mie: first travel to Nagoya, then take a Kintetsu limited express for about 1 hour 20 minutes to Ise.
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.gateways.3.name: Chubu Centrair International Airport (NGO)
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.intro.0: Kansai is one of the easiest regions to visit on your first trip to Japan: see temples and old streets in Kyoto, eat and shop in Osaka, feed the deer and see the Great Buddha in Nara, and enjoy Kobe's harbor views at night. Most cities are less than an hour apart by train. Choose one or two cities as your base and take day trips to the main sights without changing hotels every night.
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.intro.1: For a longer trip, add Himeji Castle, Kinosaki Onsen, Mount Koya, the Kumano Kodo, or Ise Jingu. These destinations take two or three hours each way, so staying overnight is best. Cherry blossom and fall foliage season are the busiest and most expensive times in Kansai, so book hotels one or two months ahead. Summers are hot and humid. Winter is quieter and better for taking your time at the temples.
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.name: Kansai
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.passes.0.name: JR Kansai WIDE Area Pass
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.passes.0.text: About ¥12,000 for 5 consecutive days. It covers the Shinkansen between Shin-Osaka and Okayama, the HARUKA, and limited express trains to Kinosaki Onsen, Amanohashidate, and Shirahama. It pays off only if you take longer trips.
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.passes.1.name: WEST QR Kansai Area Pass
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.passes.1.text: About ¥2,700–6,700 for 1–4 days. Sold only through overseas channels, it lets you enter stations by scanning a code on your phone. It covers JR trains only, not the Shinkansen. The paper version stopped being sold at the end of September 2026.
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.passes.2.name: HARUKA one-way ticket for international visitors
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.passes.2.text: About ¥2,700 from Kansai Airport to Kyoto and about ¥1,900 to Osaka/Shin-Osaka—much cheaper than regular fares. It is most useful when you are taking the airport train only once.
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.passes.3.name: ICOCA transportation IC card
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.passes.3.text: Kansai's transportation IC card. Use it on subways, private railways, buses, and at convenience stores. If you are mainly traveling around the cities, tapping an IC card is often easier than buying a pass.
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.season: Late March–early April for cherry blossoms and mid- to late November for fall foliage are the most beautiful—and busiest—times. Winter is quieter and cheaper, while summers are hot and humid.
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.sources.0.title: JR West: WEST QR HARUKA One-way Ticket
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.sources.1.title: JR West: Kansai WIDE Area Pass
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.sources.2.title: JR West: WEST QR Kansai Area Pass
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.sources.3.title: Nankai Electric Railway: New limited express fares from April 1, 2026
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.sources.4.title: Wikipedia: Kintetsu Limited Express
20562d9f436d0eb71f66.tagline: Historic cities, great food, and hot springs—the perfect introduction to Japan

20c67e32c9ef63cab131.0: Renting a winter car in Central Hokkaido with no snow-driving background—black ice, whiteouts, and left-side driving are a dangerous mix.
20c67e32c9ef63cab131.1: Underestimating winter restaurant queues—popular Sapporo Jingisukan, Kani Honke, and sushi counters require booking 2–4 weeks ahead around holidays.
20c67e32c9ef63cab131.2: Scheduling outdoor sights after 15:30—winter twilight ends around 16:00 and temperatures plunge fast.
20c67e32c9ef63cab131.3: Commuting from Toya or Noboribetsu on the morning of an international flight—always sleep in Sapporo or the airport on night 4.

212b6bcec4943740741c.s: Maps & Weather: Boundaries come from Natural Earth (public domain) for overview only; monthly temperature and rainfall come from Open-Meteo (ERA5 reanalysis, 1996–2025 averages). Use the map links next to each spot for turn-by-turn navigation.

21559d27eb12d5b76ed3.0: Almost every Tokyo itinerary carves out a day for Kamakura and Enoshima, and nearly every cookie-cutter guide tells you to grab an Odakyu pass from Shinjuku straight to Katase-Enoshima. If you're staying around Ueno, Tokyo Station, Ginza, or Shinagawa, detouring through Shinjuku wastes half an hour—and robs you of Japan's coolest commuter ride: the Shonan Monorail, whose cars dangle beneath overhead steel tracks and swoop across hillsides like a roller coaster.
21559d27eb12d5b76ed3.1: Here is the clockwise loop I've walked four times: ride JR to Ofuna, fly over the hills on the Shonan Monorail into Enoshima, hop east along the coast on the Enoden, and glide straight back to Tokyo Station or Shinagawa on the JR Yokosuka Line from Kamakura. Zero backtracking—plus the exact fare math comparing the Odakyu Freepass, Enoden 1-day pass, and plain Suica tap-and-go.

21608de721eac017582e.location: Ura-Namba · Alleys between Namba Sennichimae and Nipponbashi
21608de721eac017582e.paragraphs.0: Osaka's finest nightlife never happens on Shinsaibashi's main drag—it lives in Ura-Namba, the tangle of backstreets east of Nankai Namba Station between Doguyasuji and Kuromon. Tiny wooden counters hold eight to twelve standing guests behind half-parted noren curtains where chefs slice sashimi, grill chicken hearts over binchotan, or ladle steaming oden inches away.
21608de721eac017582e.paragraphs.1: Forget chasing one viral post: peek through foggy glass for a lively crowd of Kansai regulars and clear outside menus (most dishes ¥380–680), slide open the door, hold up one or two fingers, and order charcoal yakitori, torched mackerel, and a yuzu highball for the most relaxed finale in town.
21608de721eac017582e.tip: Seated Japanese izakayas often add a ¥300–500 otoshi appetizer cover charge—totally normal local etiquette, not a scam. Pure standing bars (tachinomi) usually skip cover charges altogether.
21608de721eac017582e.title: Wander East of Nankai Namba: Pick Any Standing Bar Packed with Local Regulars

21e2d7a2974cc245cf50.cost: Pay the 10% consumption tax upfront (8% on food)
21e2d7a2974cc245cf50.location: Tax-Free shops, drugstores, and department stores across Japan
21e2d7a2974cc245cf50.paragraphs.0: Under the new rules, shopping at Matsumoto Kiyoshi, Don Quijote, Uniqlo, or Ginza department stores only requires hitting ¥5,000 before tax in a single store on the same day. The old wall between consumables and general goods is gone—a ¥3,500 sweatshirt plus ¥1,600 of eye drops and snacks now combine smoothly to clear ¥5,000, making souvenir runs far simpler.
21e2d7a2974cc245cf50.paragraphs.1: At the register, staff charge the full tax-included price and log your passport in the tax-free system (many major stores and J-TaxRefund counters also print a QR code on the receipt). Connect to store Wi-Fi—or do it back at your hotel that night—to scan the code, confirm your passport, and bind your refund method: Visa/Mastercard credit card, e-wallet, or airport cash counter. Setting it up early saves frantic form-filling at the terminal.
21e2d7a2974cc245cf50.phase: Step 01 · Store checkout & mobile refund setup
21e2d7a2974cc245cf50.photo.alt: Japanese skincare, matcha tins, and folded clothes neatly packed inside an open suitcase on a hotel bed
21e2d7a2974cc245cf50.photo.caption: With bulky sealed plastic bags finally retired, cosmetics, snacks, and apparel can pack neatly wherever they fit—just keep every single item on your receipts unopened until departure.
21e2d7a2974cc245cf50.tip: Although the ¥500,000 cap and clear sealed bags are gone, tax-free goods must still leave Japan with you in person within 90 days of purchase. The old postal shipping (unaccompanied goods) tax-free option has been abolished—never mail tax-free purchases home.
21e2d7a2974cc245cf50.title: Spend ¥5,000+ at full tax-included price, then scan the QR code to link your payout

22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.access.0.how: JR Hida limited express to Takayama in about 2 hours 30 minutes, or Gero in about 1 hour 40 minutes
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.access.1.how: Nohi and other highway buses to Shirakawa-go in about 1 hour 30 minutes, or Takayama in about 2 hours 15 minutes; reservations required
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.access.2.how: JR Hida limited express or highway bus to Takayama, about 1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours 30 minutes
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.access.3.how: Meitetsu train to Nagoya in about 30 minutes, then transfer to the Hida limited express to Takayama
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.0.name: Hida beef
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.0.text: This wagyu from Gifu Prefecture has fine marbling and melts in your mouth. The most popular option in Takayama's old town is grilled Hida beef sushi served on rice crackers. You can also have it as yakiniku or steak.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.0.where: Yakiniku restaurants in Takayama Sanmachi Old Town and around Takayama Station
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.1.name: Takayama ramen
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.1.text: Locally called chuka soba, this dish combines thin, curly noodles with a clear soy-sauce and chicken-bone broth. It is light and not greasy, and the small portion is ideal for brunch.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.1.where: Ramen shops between Takayama Station and the old town
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.2.name: Hoba miso
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.2.text: Miso, green onions, and shiitake mushrooms are placed on a dried magnolia leaf and grilled over a small charcoal stove. The fragrant, slightly charred miso is eaten with white rice. It is common at ryokan breakfasts in Takayama, and adding Hida beef turns it into a main dish.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.2.where: Ryokan breakfasts and local-cuisine restaurants in Takayama's old town
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.3.name: Mitarashi dango
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.3.text: The Hida version of grilled dango is not covered in sweet sauce. It is brushed with soy sauce and grilled until savory and crisp, making it completely different from the sweet versions found elsewhere. A skewer is inexpensive, and you will find them in the old town and at the morning market.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.foods.3.where: Takayama Sanmachi Old Town and Miyagawa Morning Market
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.intro.0: The Hida region in northern Gifu is central to travel in central Japan. Takayama's old town preserves Edo-period merchant houses, Shirakawa-go's gassho-style villages are a World Heritage Site, and the Shinhotaka Ropeway climbs above 2,000 meters for views of the Northern Alps. Takayama is about 2.5 hours from Nagoya by limited express, followed by about 50 minutes by bus to Shirakawa-go. It fits best into the classic Nagoya–Takayama–Shirakawa-go–Kanazawa route.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.intro.1: The areas closer to Nagoya in the south have plenty to see as well. Gero Onsen is considered one of Japan's three great hot springs, Gujo Hachiman is a small town surrounded by water, and Magome-juku is a historic post town on the Nakasendo. From here, you can hike to Tsumago in Nagano. The Hida region gets heavy snow in winter, and Shirakawa-go is at its most beautiful then, but transportation and accommodations should be booked early.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.name: Gifu
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.seasons.note: Shirakawa-go's snowy scenery in January–February; the Takayama Festival on April 14–15 and October 9–10; fall foliage from late October to early November. Book accommodations early during peak season.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.sources.0.title: Nohi Bus Takayama–Shirakawa-go–Kanazawa Route
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.sources.1.title: Shirakawa-go Tourist Association
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.sources.2.title: Takayama Jinya official site
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.sources.3.title: Shinhotaka Ropeway fares
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.sources.4.title: JR Takayama–Hokuriku Area Tourist Pass
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.0.name: Shirakawa-go (Ogimachi)
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.0.text: This gassho-style village became a World Heritage Site in 1995. More than 100 old houses with steep thatched roofs are scattered among the fields, and people still live in many of them. You can enter some houses, such as Wada House, to see their three-story attics. The Ogimachi Castle Ruins viewpoint north of the village looks over the entire area and offers a classic postcard view. The bus ride from Takayama takes about 50 minutes.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.0.tip: The winter light-up takes place on only a few nights and requires reservations. In 2027, the dates are 1/11, 1/17, 1/24, and 1/31. Do not enter private homes or fields.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.1.name: Takayama Sanmachi Old Town
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.1.text: One traditional merchant house after another lines these streets, with lattice-fronted wooden buildings dating to the Edo period. Sake breweries have cedar-ball decorations, called sugidama, hanging by their entrances, and many offer paid tastings. The streets are packed with Hida beef sushi, dango, and miso shops, making it easy to spend two hours snacking as you walk. At the spring and fall Takayama Festivals, elaborate floats are pulled through the streets. The festival is one of Japan's three most beautiful.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.1.tip: Many shops close around 5 p.m. The easiest plan is to visit after exploring the morning market.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.2.name: Miyagawa Morning Market and Takayama Jinya
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.2.text: Every morning, farmers set up stalls along the Miyagawa River selling vegetables, pickles, apples, and handicrafts. There are also food stalls for snacks on the go. Another morning market is held in front of Takayama Jinya, the office used by the Edo shogunate to govern Hida. It is the only surviving building of its kind in Japan. Allow about 30 minutes inside.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.2.tip: The morning markets generally run from 7–8 a.m. until noon, and are liveliest early. Admission to Takayama Jinya is free for high school students and younger children.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.3.name: Hida-Furukawa
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.3.text: This town is about 15 minutes north of Takayama by JR train. White-walled sake breweries line the Seto River, whose canals are home to more than 1,000 colorful carp. It is much quieter than Takayama. The town also served as one of the models for the town in the anime film Your Name, and fans often take photos around the station and library. You can explore at a relaxed pace in half a day.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.3.tip: The carp are moved elsewhere for the winter, so you will not see them in the canals. JR trains are infrequent, so check the timetable in advance.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.4.name: Shinhotaka Ropeway
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.4.text: Two ropeway sections carry passengers from the hot-spring town to Nishihotakaguchi at about 2,156 meters. The second section is Japan's only double-decker ropeway. The summit observation deck faces Mount Yari and the Hotaka mountain range in the Northern Alps. In winter, the mountains are covered in snow; in fall, the slopes turn red. The Nohi bus ride from Takayama takes about 1 hour 30 minutes.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.4.tip: The summit is more than 10°C colder than the valley, so bring a down jacket. Clouds can hide the mountains; check the summit livestream before setting out.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.5.name: Gero Onsen
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.5.text: Gero Onsen was listed as one of Japan's three great hot springs as early as the Edo period. Its silky water is known as bijin-no-yu, or "beauty water." Cross the bridge from the station to reach the hot-spring district, where you will find several free foot baths and inns that offer paid bathing without an overnight stay. The town lies midway along the limited express route from Nagoya to Takayama, making it a good place to get off and spend a night.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.5.tip: Buy a Yumeguri Tegata wooden pass to bathe once at several participating inns.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.6.name: Gujo Hachiman
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.6.text: This small mountain town is surrounded by clear streams. Canals run beside the old streets, and residents still wash vegetables and dishes in shared tiered water basins called mizubune. Gujo Hachiman Castle on the hill is a reconstructed wooden keep that looks especially beautiful with fall foliage. From July–September, the Gujo Odori dance is held for dozens of nights, with all-night dancing during the Bon Festival. The town is also Japan's center for food replicas, and you can try making one yourself.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.6.tip: Highway buses from Nagoya or Gifu are the most convenient option. Visitors can join the Gujo Odori dances.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.7.name: Magome-juku
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.7.text: This post town on the Nakasendo was built along a slope, with wooden houses and waterwheels lining its stone-paved streets. It was the hometown of writer Shimazaki Toson. From here, the hike over Magome Pass to Tsumago-juku in Nagano is about 8 km and takes 2.5–3 hours. It is fairly easy because most of the route is downhill. The bus from JR Nakatsugawa Station takes about 25 minutes.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.spots.7.tip: You can send luggage between the two towns. Mountain paths may be icy in winter, so wear shoes with good traction.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.stay: Stay near Takayama Station. The old town is a 10-minute walk away, and limited express trains and buses to Shirakawa-go and Shinhotaka leave nearby. To stay in a gassho-style house, spend a night in Shirakawa-go, but rooms are limited and must be booked well in advance.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.tagline: Takayama's old town, Shirakawa-go's gassho-style village, and Gero Onsen
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.tips.0: Buses from Takayama to Shirakawa-go and Kanazawa have reserved seats only. Book online one month in advance during peak season.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.tips.1: Roads in Shirakawa-go can be icy and snow-covered in winter. Wear shoes with good traction, and crampons are recommended.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.tips.2: Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your driver's license and required translation or permit. The Hida region can be easily explored by limited express train and bus.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.tips.3: Accommodations sell out well in advance during the Takayama Festival (4/14–15 and 10/9–10). Book six months ahead.
22ff96bbf74123c12cbf.tips.4: Visitors from abroad can use the JR Takayama–Hokuriku Area Tourist Pass, which includes the limited express from Nagoya to Takayama and the bus to Shirakawa-go within 5 days.

23603178929de82e8fcd.s: An original travel guide to Japan’s 47 prefectures: interactive maps, {n} sights and local foods, seasonal themes, itinerary templates, and offline travel tools.

23f0d03095c387daa072.cost: SUMMIT ~$45–55; High Line free; Chelsea lunch ~$20
23f0d03095c387daa072.paragraphs.0: If you're doing a second observation deck, catch the 09:30 first wave at SUMMIT One Vanderbilt right next to Grand Central. Three mirrored, floor-to-ceiling glass levels refract the Chrysler Building and drifting clouds into infinity for showstopping photos (heads up: mirrored floors mean wear pants and bring sunglasses against the glare).
23f0d03095c387daa072.paragraphs.1: In the afternoon, ride the 7 train west to its Hudson Yards terminus, check out the honeycomb Vessel sculpture, and step straight onto the High Line—an abandoned elevated freight rail line reborn as a linear park. Stroll 2.3 km south amid wild grasses, public art, and sleek glass residences by star architects like Zaha Hadid before dropping seamlessly into Chelsea Market inside a historic biscuit factory. Make a beeline for Los Tacos No. 1: freshly pressed tortillas piled with charcoal-grilled beef and fiery salsa run only a few dollars each, and the long line moves in roughly 10 minutes.
23f0d03095c387daa072.phase: Step 02 · Day 2 modern architecture: SUMMIT + High Line + Chelsea Market
23f0d03095c387daa072.photo.alt: Autumn grasses swaying along Manhattan's elevated High Line park
23f0d03095c387daa072.photo.caption: Reborn from an abandoned elevated railway, the High Line gently stitches Hudson Yards' glass forest to Chelsea's red-brick historic blocks.
23f0d03095c387daa072.tip: Always check whether a New York subway entrance is marked Uptown (northbound) or Downtown (southbound)! Many older stations put opposite-direction platforms across the street with no underground crossover—tap into the wrong side and you'll pay another $3 to re-enter.
23f0d03095c387daa072.title: Hit SUMMIT's mirrored wonderland in the morning, then walk the elevated High Line to Chelsea Market's standout tacos

2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.access.0.how: The JR Shiokaze limited express takes about 2 hours 40 minutes to Matsuyama Station
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.access.1.how: The airport bus takes about 1,000 to JR Matsuyama Station and about ¥1,200 to Dogo Onsen
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.access.2.how: Take a high-speed ferry from Hiroshima Port to Matsuyama Sightseeing Port. The trip takes just over 1 hour, followed by a bus into the city
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.access.3.how: The JR Shiokaze/Ishizuchi limited express takes about 2.5 hours to Matsuyama Station
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.0.name: Tai meshi
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.0.text: Ehime has two styles of tai meshi. Around Matsuyama, a whole sea bream is simmered with rice. In the southern Uwajima style, raw sea bream slices are soaked in a sauce with raw egg and poured over hot rice. Both are worth trying.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.0.where: Dogo Onsen shopping street and the Okaido area in central Matsuyama
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.1.name: Ehime mikan
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.1.text: Ehime is Japan's leading citrus-growing region. Besides the familiar satsuma mandarins, it produces premium varieties such as Beni Madonna and Kanpei. Fresh-squeezed juice shops at stations and on shopping streets let you compare different varieties.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.1.where: Matsuyama Station, Dogo Onsen shopping street, and Matsuyama Airport
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.2.name: Jakoten
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.2.text: A fish cake from the Uwajima and Yawatahama areas, made by grinding small fish with their bones and skin, flattening the paste, and frying it. It is gray-brown, with a coarse texture from the fish bones and a rich savory flavor. Freshly fried jakoten is best with beer.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.2.where: The souvenir area at Matsuyama Station and Dogo Onsen shopping street
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.3.name: Botchan dango
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.3.text: These three-color skewered dumplings have green, yellow, and brown layers flavored with matcha, egg, and red bean paste. They are named after the hero's dumpling stop in Natsume Soseki's novel Botchan. One is just right after a soak in the hot springs.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.foods.3.where: Long-running shops on Dogo Onsen shopping street
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.intro.0: Ehime Prefecture sits in northwestern Shikoku, facing the Seto Inland Sea. Matsuyama, the prefectural capital, has streetcars. At one end is Matsuyama Castle, with one of Japan's original Edo-period keeps. At the other is Dogo Onsen, said to be 3,000 years old and considered one of the inspirations for the bathhouse in Spirited Away. Both are in the city, just over 20 minutes apart by streetcar.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.intro.1: To the north, the Shimanami Kaido crosses six islands from Imabari to Onomichi in Hiroshima. Its bridges have dedicated bike lanes, making it a bucket-list route for cyclists worldwide. To the south are quiet old towns such as Uchiko and Ozu, plus seaside Shimonada Station. Ehime is also Japan's best-known citrus-growing region, with mikan everywhere from fall through early spring.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.name: Ehime
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.seasons.note: Spring and fall are the most comfortable seasons for cycling the Shimanami Kaido. Summer is intensely sunny, and winter brings cold sea winds. The mikan season runs from November to March.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.sources.0.title: Dogo Onsen official website: Honkan
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.sources.1.title: Matsuyama Castle official website: Tickets and hours
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.sources.2.title: Matsuyama Airport: Bus transportation
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.sources.3.title: JR Shikoku: ALL SHIKOKU Rail Pass change notice (2025-10)
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.sources.4.title: Shimanami Kaido bike rental official website
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.0.name: Dogo Onsen Honkan
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.0.text: Built in 1894, this wooden public bathhouse was the first public bath in Japan to be designated an Important Cultural Property. A preservation and restoration project lasting about 6 years was completed in December 2024. The simplest option is to bathe in Kami no Yu on the first floor. Pay extra to relax and have tea on the second floor. The nearby Asuka-no-Yu and Tsubaki-no-Yu baths are also worth trying.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.0.tip: It is less crowded when the doors open at 6 a.m. and after dinner. The three-bath pass is valid for two days and costs about 20% less than buying separate tickets.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.1.name: Matsuyama Castle
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.1.text: This castle stands atop Mount Katsuyama in the city center and is one of Japan's 12 original castle keeps. Its many layers of walls are impressive. Take the ropeway or chairlift up. On the way down, you can take either one, or walk for about 20 minutes. The top floor of the keep overlooks the entire Matsuyama Plain and the Seto Inland Sea. The grounds are full of cherry blossoms in spring.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.1.tip: The chairlift has no cover and stops in the rain. The ropeway and chairlift use the same ticket, so you can choose either one.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.2.name: Shimanami Kaido & Mt. Kiro Observatory
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.2.text: The route from Imabari to Onomichi is about 70 kilometers long and crosses six islands and seven major bridges. The bridges have bike lanes, and blue lines painted on the road make the route easy to follow. Cycling the entire route in one day is exhausting, so you can ride just the section from Imabari to Oshima. The Mt. Kiro Observatory on Oshima overlooks the Kurushima Kaikyo Bridge and offers the best view along the route.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.2.tip: There are around a dozen rental-bike locations along the route, and some allow one-way returns. If you run out of energy, ride part of the way and switch to a bus or boat.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.3.name: Oyamazumi Shrine
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.3.text: This ancient shrine on Omishima is dedicated to the mountain and sea gods. Generations of warriors came here to pray for victory and later offered armor and swords, so the treasure museum holds a large collection of weapons designated as National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties. The grounds contain a camphor tree said to be about 2,600 years old. Stop here along the way when cycling the Shimanami Kaido.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.4.name: Uchiko & Ozu
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.4.text: These two quiet towns south of Matsuyama are each about 30 minutes away by JR limited express. Uchiko grew wealthy from wood wax and retains white-walled streets and the 1916 Uchiko-za kabuki theater. Ozu has a wooden reconstruction of Ozu Castle and Garyu Sanso, a villa built on a riverside cliff. The fall foliage is beautiful.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.5.name: Shimonada Station
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.5.text: This unmanned station has just one platform, with the Iyo Sea directly in front. It has appeared in many Japanese TV dramas and commercials, and the sunset is especially photogenic. From Matsuyama Station, take a local train on the JR Yosan Line for about 1 hour. The sightseeing train Iyonada Monogatari also stops here for a few minutes.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.5.tip: Trains run only once every 1–2 hours, so check the return schedule before arriving.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.6.name: Mount Ishizuchi
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.6.text: Western Japan's highest peak, Mount Ishizuchi is also a sacred mountain on the ancient Shugendo pilgrimage route. Take the Ishizuchi Tozan Ropeway to the middle of the mountain, then allow about 3 hours one way to the summit. The route includes steep sections with fixed chains, but an easier bypass is available. The fall foliage arrives earlier here than in the lowlands and is at its best from late September to mid-October. Snow in winter requires specialized gear.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.spots.6.tip: Weather changes quickly on the mountain. Bring a windproof jacket and enough water. Do not attempt the climb casually in winter.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.stay: Stay one night at a ryokan in Dogo Onsen. For the rest of your trip, stay around Okaido in central Matsuyama. If you plan to cycle the Shimanami Kaido, stay in Imabari or Onomichi the night before.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.tagline: Dogo Onsen, Shimanami Kaido cycling, and citrus everywhere
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.tips.0: Matsuyama's streetcars, operated by Iyo Railway, will no longer be covered by the ALL SHIKOKU Rail Pass from March 2026. You will need to buy a separate ticket.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.tips.1: Dogo Onsen Honkan can have long lines when busy. Its official website shows real-time wait times for each bathhouse, so visit during a less crowded period.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.tips.2: Protect yourself from the sun and stay hydrated when cycling the Shimanami Kaido. The bridges are windy, so secure your hat.
2525f2bc9d9b0b09c8e2.tips.3: Trains are infrequent to small stations such as Shimonada and Uchiko. Always check the schedule in advance.

259cae3e84947a2d904d.access.0.how: Take the Sonic limited express from Hakata to Beppu in about 2 hours. To Yufuin, take the Yufuin no Mori in about 2 hours 15 minutes, or a highway bus in about 2.5 hours
259cae3e84947a2d904d.access.1.how: The airport bus takes about 50 minutes to Beppu Station, for about ¥1,600; Oita Station is about 1 hour away
259cae3e84947a2d904d.access.2.how: The Kyushu Odan Bus takes about 4 hours 20 minutes to Yufuin via Aso, and reservations are required for some sections. You can also take a JR limited express
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.0.name: Jigoku-mushi
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.0.text: Seafood, chicken, vegetables, and eggs are cooked in hot-spring steam without seasoning, giving them a hint of salt from the spring water. The natural sweetness of the ingredients comes through clearly. It's healthy and fun.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.0.where: Jigoku Mushi Kobo and restaurants around Kannawa Onsen in Beppu
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.1.name: Toriten
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.1.text: A home-style Oita dish of marinated chicken coated in batter and fried tempura-style. It's served with vinegar-soy dipping sauce and Japanese mustard, and feels lighter than fried chicken. Nearly every diner in Oita serves it.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.1.where: Diners and izakayas in Beppu and central Oita City
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.2.name: Dangojiru
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.2.text: Hand-rolled, flat, wide noodles are simmered with vegetables and shiitake mushrooms in miso soup. It's somewhat like Chinese noodle-skin soup. This local Oita dish is especially comforting in winter.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.2.where: Local cuisine restaurants in Yufuin and Beppu
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.3.name: Beppu reimen
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.3.text: Beppu's take on Korean cold noodles uses thick noodles made partly with buckwheat flour, served with a Japanese-style broth, kimchi, and chashu pork. The texture is softer. It's just right after a soak in the hot springs.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.foods.3.where: Cold-noodle specialty shops and yakiniku restaurants around Beppu Station
259cae3e84947a2d904d.intro.0: Known as Japan's hot-spring prefecture, Oita has the country's highest number of hot-spring sources and the largest volume of water gushing from them. Beppu is a lively old hot-spring city, with steam rising everywhere. You can see the Hells, try a sand bath, and eat food steamed in hot-spring vapor. Yufuin sits in a mountain basin. It's smaller and slower-paced, making it ideal for a night at a good ryokan.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.intro.1: The two towns are about an hour apart by bus, and many travelers plan two nights between them. Farther afield, you'll find Usa Jingu, the head shrine of Japan's 40,000-plus Hachiman shrines; Yabakei Gorge, known for its beautiful fall colors; and Kokonoe Yume Otsurihashi, a suspension bridge high above the ground. Buses between sights are infrequent, so join a tour or hire a car and driver if you want to see several places.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.name: Oita
259cae3e84947a2d904d.seasons.note: Hot springs are especially enjoyable in fall and winter. Yabakei Gorge and Kokonoe are covered in fall colors in November. Yufuin often has morning mist in winter. Beppu is very hot in summer, so keep your stay short.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.sources.0.title: Official Hells of Beppu website
259cae3e84947a2d904d.sources.1.title: JR Kyushu: Yufuin no Mori train guide
259cae3e84947a2d904d.sources.2.title: Nishitetsu: Yufuin highway bus
259cae3e84947a2d904d.sources.3.title: Official Kokonoe Yume Otsurihashi website
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.0.name: Hells of Beppu
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.0.text: Seven hot-spring sources that are for viewing, not bathing: cobalt-blue Umi Jigoku, blood-red Chinoike Jigoku, the periodically erupting Tatsumaki Jigoku, and more. Five are clustered in Kannawa and within walking distance. The other two are about 3 km away in Kamegawa and require a bus. The combination ticket is the best value.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.0.tip: The combination ticket is valid for two days, including the day of purchase and the following day. The hot-spring steamed pudding and eggs sold in the park are worth trying.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.1.name: Kannawa Onsen
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.1.text: Beppu's most atmospheric hot-spring district, where steam rises from cracks in the pavement and storm drains. At Jigoku Mushi Kobo, you can steam seafood and vegetables in hot-spring vapor. Small neighborhood baths cost a few hundred yen per visit. The steam and streetlights make great photos at night.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.1.tip: At the hot-spring steam kitchen, you manage the heat with a timer. Lines can be long around mealtimes, so avoid 12 p.m.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.2.name: Takegawara Onsen
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.2.text: A wooden public bathhouse that opened during the Meiji era, with an impressive karahafu roof. It's tucked into the old streets near Beppu Station. Besides a regular hot-spring bath, it offers sand baths, where staff cover you in hot sand. You'll work up a sweat in about ten minutes. It's a memorable experience.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.2.tip: The regular bath is very hot. Bring your own towel and soap. Sand baths are popular, and there may be a wait in the afternoon.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.3.name: Yufuin Onsen
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.3.text: From the station to Kinrin Lake, Yunotsubo Street is lined with general stores, dessert shops, and small art museums, with twin-peaked Mount Yufu in the background. Daytime crowds are heavy, but the town quiets down after day-trippers leave in the evening, making it worth staying overnight.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.3.tip: Kinrin Lake's morning mist is most visible on fall and winter mornings. Go before 7 a.m. You can leave your luggage at the station.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.4.name: Usa Jingu
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.4.text: The head shrine of more than 40,000 Hachiman shrines across Japan, Usa Jingu has a vermilion main hall designated a national treasure. Its worship ritual is different from elsewhere: bow twice, clap four times, then bow once. The grounds are extensive, with an approach, ponds, and tree-lined paths. It's less crowded than Beppu and ideal for history lovers.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.4.tip: Take a JR train from Beppu to Usa Station, then transfer to a bus or taxi for about 10 minutes.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.5.name: Yabakei Gorge
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.5.text: Strange rock peaks line the Yamakuni River and are considered one of Japan's three great scenic wonders. The gorge is at its best during fall foliage season. At the Hitome Hakkei viewpoint, you can see several peaks at once. Nearby, Aonodomon is a tunnel hand-carved by a monk over 30 years during the Edo period.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.5.tip: Take a bus from Nakatsu Station. Services are infrequent. Fall colors usually peak from mid- to late November, and traffic is heavy on weekends.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.6.name: Kokonoe Yume Otsurihashi
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.6.text: Japan's highest pedestrian suspension bridge is 390 meters long and 173 meters above the valley floor. You can feel it sway as you cross. The bridge offers views of Shindonotaki Falls, and the surrounding valleys turn bright red in fall. It's a good stop on a day-trip route between Yufuin and Aso.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.spots.6.tip: By public transportation, take a bus from Bungo-Nakamura Station. Services are infrequent. People with a fear of heights should take care, and the bridge may close in strong winds.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.stay: In Beppu, stay around Beppu Station or Kannawa Onsen for easy access to the Hells. In Yufuin, stay at a hot-spring ryokan. Many have private open-air baths, and popular ones should be booked 1–2 months ahead.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.tagline: Japan's top hot-spring prefecture: see the Hells of Beppu and soak in Yufuin
259cae3e84947a2d904d.tips.0: All seats on the Yufuin no Mori are reserved. Trains often sell out in peak seasons, so book a month ahead.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.tips.1: Beppu has frequent city buses. The bus to Kannawa for the Hells takes about 20 minutes.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.tips.2: Most hot springs in Japan do not allow swimsuits. If you have tattoos, check the rules first or choose a private bath.
259cae3e84947a2d904d.tips.3: Popular ryokan in Yufuin fill up quickly on weekends and during fall foliage season. Book as soon as your dates are set.

26badb3bcd7405735a03.0: Linking Kanazawa, Shirakawa-go, and Takayama across Japan's Hokuriku and Hida regions makes for the country's most cinematic winter corridor. One day you are admiring yukitsuri rope cones cradling Edo-era pines in Kanazawa and feasting on winter yellowtail at Omicho Market; the next you emerge from a mountain tunnel into waist-deep snow among thatched-roof farmhouses before grilling melt-in-your-mouth Hida beef in Takayama's historic streets.
26badb3bcd7405735a03.1: One unforgiving transport hurdle stands in the way: Shirakawa-go has no train station. Every bus in and out is jointly operated by Nohi Bus and Hokutetsu, and core winter departures are strictly all-reserved (marked R), often selling out within minutes of release. Follow this real-world walkthrough step by step, starting with the booking alarm 30 days before departure.

26c37e587df14a6442d7.s: Original travel guides for Japan, Australia, and the United States: interactive maps, photos of sights and food, itinerary templates, one-minute guide generation, budget calculators, and offline travel tools.

26e27148cef5b575df06.s: Maps: Boundaries come from Natural Earth (public domain) and have been simplified. They are not suitable for measuring. Use the map link beside a sight for directions.

2732086537bd59f9c973.access.0.how: The Kintetsu limited express takes about 1 hour 45 minutes to Ujiyamada. The Shimakaze sightseeing train runs directly to Kashikojima in about 2 hours 20 minutes.
2732086537bd59f9c973.access.1.how: The Kintetsu limited express takes about 1 hour 20 minutes to Ujiyamada. Nagoya is also the closest major city to Chubu Airport.
2732086537bd59f9c973.access.2.how: The Kintetsu limited express takes about 2 hours to Ujiyamada. Some trains require a transfer at Yamato-Yagi.
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.0.name: Ise udon
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.0.text: The noodles are remarkably thick but cooked until very soft, so they require almost no chewing. They're tossed with a dark, sweet-and-savory sauce. The dish was originally designed to let pilgrims eat quickly and get back on the road, and the recipe has changed little in hundreds of years.
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.0.where: Traditional noodle shops along the Oharai-machi approach and around Iseshi Station.
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.1.name: Tekone sushi
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.1.text: This Shima fishermen's dish features raw bonito or tuna marinated in soy sauce, served over vinegared rice and topped with shiso and nori. It was originally mixed by hand on boats, hence the name. The flavor is light and savory.
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.1.where: Restaurants in Oharai-machi, Toba, and Shima.
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.2.name: Akafuku mochi
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.2.text: Ise's most famous sweet consists of soft mochi covered with red bean paste. Three ridges pressed into the top represent the flowing waters of the Isuzu River. The main shop is in front of Naiku. For the most local experience, enjoy it with a bowl of bancha tea by the river.
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.2.where: Akafuku's main shop in Oharai-machi in front of Naiku. It's also sold at stations and the airport.
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.3.name: Matsusaka beef
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.3.text: One of Japan's three great wagyu brands, Matsusaka beef has a low melting point and a sweet aroma. Sukiyaki and charcoal-grilled beef are the specialties in Matsusaka. On a smaller budget, try a Matsusaka beef bento or croquette.
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.3.where: Long-established restaurants around Matsusaka Station. There are also branches in central Ise.
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.4.name: Ise lobster
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.4.text: The lobster caught off the coast of Shima has firm, sweet meat and is served as sashimi, grilled over charcoal, or in miso soup. Fall and winter are the fishing season. A lobster meal at a seaside inn is one of the main reasons to stay in Shima.
2732086537bd59f9c973.foods.4.where: Seaside hot-spring inns and seafood restaurants in Toba and Shima.
2732086537bd59f9c973.intro.0: Mie lies between Osaka and Nagoya. Its main draw is Ise Jingu, Japan's highest-ranking shrine, rebuilt every twenty years for the past 2,000 years. After paying your respects, eat Ise udon and Akafuku mochi on the old street in front of the torii. For many Japanese people, it's a once-in-a-lifetime trip.
2732086537bd59f9c973.intro.1: South of Ise is the Shima Peninsula, with the winding waters of Ago Bay, pearl farms, and ama diving culture. To the west, Iga is the birthplace of ninjas. To the north, Kuwana has a major light show. Kintetsu limited express trains take about 1.5–2 hours from Osaka or Nagoya. Plan to stay at least one night.
2732086537bd59f9c973.name: Mie
2732086537bd59f9c973.seasons.note: Spring and fall are the most comfortable seasons for visiting the shrines. Ise Jingu is extremely crowded around New Year's, summer is best for the sea in Shima, and winter is the season for light shows.
2732086537bd59f9c973.sources.0.title: Ise Jingu: Visitor information
2732086537bd59f9c973.sources.1.title: Wikipedia: Kintetsu limited express
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.0.name: Ise Grand Shrine Naiku
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.0.text: Naiku, dedicated to Amaterasu, is the heart of Ise Jingu. After crossing Uji Bridge, follow the gravel approach through a forest of ancient cedars. At the main sanctuary, visitors can pray only from outside the white curtain, and photography is not allowed. The entire forest is quiet and solemn, completely unlike Kyoto's busy shrines. Admission is free. It opens at 5 a.m.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.0.tip: Go at 6–7 a.m. for the quietest visit. Photography is prohibited on the steps leading to the main sanctuary.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.1.name: Ise Grand Shrine Geku
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.1.text: Traditionally, visitors pray at Geku before Naiku. Geku is about a 5-minute walk from Iseshi Station. Its flat approach is quieter than Naiku's. The nearby Sengukan Museum introduces the Shikinen Sengu rebuilding ceremony. Afterward, take a bus to Naiku in about 15 minutes.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.1.tip: Geku and Naiku are about 5 km apart. Take a bus or taxi instead of walking.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.2.name: Oharai-machi & Okage Yokocho
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.2.text: This old shopping street stretches about 800 meters in front of Naiku. Wooden buildings line the approach, selling Ise udon, charcoal-grilled seafood, Akafuku mochi, and souvenirs. Okage Yokocho, in the middle, recreates streetscapes from the late Edo period through the Meiji period. It's the best place to have lunch after visiting the shrine.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.2.tip: Many shops close around 5 p.m., so don't wait until evening to eat.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.3.name: Meoto Iwa
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.3.text: Two rocks of different sizes rise from the sea at Futamiura, linked by a thick sacred rope to symbolize marital harmony. In good weather from May–July, the sun rises between the rocks, and Mount Fuji may be visible in the distance. Located between Ise and Toba, Meoto Iwa can be combined with a visit to Toba Aquarium.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.3.tip: Check the sunrise time for the day and arrive at the shore 20 minutes early.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.4.name: Yokoyama Observatory, Ago Bay
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.4.text: From the observatory, look down on Ago Bay, where more than sixty islands dot its winding waters and wooden rafts used for pearl farming line the sea. It's one of Ise-Shima National Park's signature views. You can also take a sightseeing cruise from Kashikojima for a closer look at the bay and pearl farms.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.4.tip: It's about a 10-minute taxi ride from Ugata Station. On clear days, the morning light is best.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.5.name: Iga-ryu Ninja Museum
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.5.text: Iga is one of Japan's birthplaces of ninjas. The museum has a ninja house packed with secret mechanisms, including revolving walls, hidden doors, and underground passages. Staff demonstrate the features, and there are also shuriken and ninja performances. Iga Ueno Castle is next door, making this a good stop for families.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.5.tip: Getting here from Osaka requires transfers between Kintetsu and the Iga Railway and takes longer than the route to Ise. Set aside half a day.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.6.name: Nabana no Sato
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.6.text: This large garden in Kuwana combines seasonal flower displays with a huge greenhouse. Its hydrangea and iris gardens in early summer are said to be among Japan's largest. The biggest draw is the light show from fall and winter through spring, when millions of bulbs form tunnels and themed displays. It's about 40 minutes by highway bus from Nagoya Station.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.6.tip: The light show is extremely crowded on weekend evenings. Go on a weekday or arrive later after dark.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.7.name: Akame 48 Waterfalls
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.7.text: Follow the valley upstream for about 4 km, passing one waterfall and deep pool after another. The water is a clear green. Most of the route consists of maintained paths and stairs, and the one-way walk takes about 1.5 hours. The area is said to have been a place where ninjas trained, and the fall foliage is beautiful. From Kintetsu Akameguchi Station, take a bus for about 10 minutes.
2732086537bd59f9c973.spots.7.tip: You can turn back halfway. The stone steps are slippery after rain, so wear shoes with good traction.
2732086537bd59f9c973.stay: If you're visiting only the shrine, stay near Iseshi Station or Ujiyamada Station. For the sea and Ise lobster, stay at a seaside hot-spring inn in Toba or Shima.
2732086537bd59f9c973.tagline: Home of Ise Jingu, ama divers, and ninjas
2732086537bd59f9c973.tips.0: Ise Jingu's hours change with the seasons. It opens as early as 5 a.m. and closes as late as around 5–7 p.m. Check the official website before you go.
2732086537bd59f9c973.tips.1: Visitor numbers are extremely high during the first three days of the New Year, with traffic controls and lines lasting for hours. First-time visitors should avoid this period.
2732086537bd59f9c973.tips.2: Kintetsu limited express trains require a separate limited express ticket. Reserve seats online in advance for weekends and holidays.
2732086537bd59f9c973.tips.3: Attractions on the Shima Peninsula are spread out and buses are infrequent. If your licence is not valid for driving in Japan, join a local one-day bus tour. Licence rules depend on your licence and destination; check the official source before driving.

2acc1f6f649197577759.access.0.how: There are currently no nonstop flights. Common connections include Tokyo, Osaka, and Seoul. Tokyo to Honolulu takes about 7–8 hours. You can also connect through Los Angeles or San Francisco.
2acc1f6f649197577759.access.1.how: Flights from Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Seattle to Honolulu take about 5.5–6.5 hours. Some flights go nonstop to Maui, Kona, and Kauaʻi.
2acc1f6f649197577759.access.2.how: Flights from Honolulu to Maui, Kona, Hilo, and Lihue take about 35–50 minutes. There are many flights, and booking early usually means lower fares.
2acc1f6f649197577759.cover.alt: Diamond Head and the Waikiki coastline
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.0.name: Poke
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.0.text: Hawaii's everyday seafood dish is made with diced tuna or salmon tossed with soy sauce, sesame oil, sea salt, seaweed, and onion, then served over white rice. Supermarket deli counters often mix it to order. It is fresher and cheaper than at restaurants and is ideal for a beach picnic.
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.0.where: Supermarket deli counters and dedicated poke shops on every island.
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.1.name: Loco Moco and plate lunch
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.1.text: A classic of Hawaii's plate-lunch culture: two scoops of white rice, a serving of macaroni salad, and a main dish. Loco moco comes with a hamburger patty and fried egg over rice, covered in gravy. It is filling, and you can also choose teriyaki chicken, barbecue, or kalua pork.
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.1.where: Plate-lunch shops and local restaurants on every island.
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.2.name: Shave ice
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.2.text: Ice is shaved into snow-fine flakes and topped with fruit-flavored syrups in several colors. You can add ice cream or azuki beans underneath and condensed milk on top. It is softer and finer than machine-crushed ice and melts in your mouth, making it especially refreshing on a hot day.
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.2.where: Shave ice shops in Haleiwa on the North Shore and near beaches across the islands.
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.3.name: Spam musubi
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.3.text: A slice of pan-fried Spam brushed with sweet-savory teriyaki sauce is pressed onto a rectangular rice ball and wrapped with a strip of nori. This local favorite spread after World War II. It is widely available at convenience stores and supermarkets and makes an easy breakfast or hiking snack.
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.3.where: Convenience stores, supermarkets, and plate-lunch shops on every island.
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.4.name: Kona coffee
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.4.text: Grown on the slopes of Kona on the west side of Hawaiʻi Island, this is one of the few coffee-growing regions in the United States. The coffee is smooth and low in acidity. Coffee farms around Kona offer tours and tastings. Check the label when buying beans: a “Kona blend” may contain only 10% Kona coffee.
2acc1f6f649197577759.foods.4.where: Coffee farms around Kona on Hawaiʻi Island and cafés across the islands.
2acc1f6f649197577759.intro.0: Hawaii lies in the middle of the Pacific and is made up of several major islands, each with its own character. Oahu has Honolulu, Waikiki, and Pearl Harbor and is the easiest base. Maui is known for sunrise at Haleakalā and the Road to Hana. Hawaiʻi Island has active volcanoes and stargazing at Maunakea. Kauaʻi is all about canyons and the Nāpali Coast. First-time visitors usually choose Oahu plus one neighbor island. 7–8 days is ideal.
2acc1f6f649197577759.intro.1: Hawaii is more than a place to lie on the beach. Many popular sights now require reservations. Diamond Head, Hanauma Bay, the USS Arizona Memorial at Pearl Harbor, and sunrise at Haleakalā all require advance online booking. Release times follow Hawaii time (UTC−10), so set an alarm in your own time zone.
2acc1f6f649197577759.intro.2: Outside Waikiki, you will generally need a rental car on every island. Interisland flights take less than 1 hour, but allow time to get to the airport and return the car. Do not pack too much into an island-hopping day. Hawaii is expensive, and hotel taxes and fees are high, so budget more than you would for the mainland United States.
2acc1f6f649197577759.name: Hawaii
2acc1f6f649197577759.seasons.note: Hawaii is a year-round destination. April–May and September–October are less crowded and cheaper. Humpback whales visit Maui's waters from December–March. Winter waves on the North Shore are too rough for swimming.
2acc1f6f649197577759.sources.13.title: FlightConnections: nonstop routes from HNL
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.0.name: Waikiki Beach
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.0.text: Honolulu's urban beach is lined with hotels, malls, and restaurants. The small waves are good for first-time surfers and stand-up paddleboarders, and you can rent boards and book lessons right on the beach. Sunset is best enjoyed from the sand. Kapiʻolani Regional Park at the eastern end is quieter and offers views of Diamond Head.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.0.tip: When sea turtles come ashore to rest, stay at least about 3 meters away. Do not leave valuables on the beach.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.1.fee: About $5 per person; about $10 per vehicle for parking
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.1.name: Diamond Head State Monument
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.1.text: This volcanic crater east of Waikiki has a trail that climbs from inside the crater to an old summit bunker. The one-way route is about 1.3 kilometers and includes stairs and a tunnel. From the top, you can look over the entire Waikiki coastline. Visitors who are not Hawaii residents must reserve an entry time in advance on the state park website. Reservations open about 30 days ahead, and the early time slots around sunrise are the most popular.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.1.tip: After 10 a.m., the trail is intensely sunny with almost no shade. Bring enough water and wear athletic shoes.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.2.fee: About $25 for visitors ages 13 and up; about $3 for parking, cash only
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.2.name: Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.2.text: This semicircular bay formed when a volcanic crater collapsed. Its waters are a coral reef preserve where you can see tropical fish while snorkeling, and you may spot sea turtles. Nonresidents must book online at 7 a.m. Hawaii time, two days before entry. The preserve is open only Wednesday–Sunday. Before entering, you must watch a short conservation video.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.2.tip: Use sunscreen that does not contain oxybenzone. Do not stand on coral at low tide.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.3.fee: Free; online reservations charge about a $1 service fee
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.3.name: Pearl Harbor National Memorial
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.3.text: This historic site commemorates Japan's 1941 attack on Pearl Harbor. The National Park Service's USS Arizona Memorial is free and includes a documentary and a boat ride to the white memorial above the sunken battleship. The visit takes about 75 minutes. Oil still seeps from the wreck below the memorial. The nearby USS Missouri battleship and aviation museums require separate tickets.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.3.tip: Bags are not allowed in the park. Paid storage is available at the entrance. Same-day free tickets are no longer distributed at the memorial.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.4.name: North Shore, Oahu
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.4.text: The North Shore is about a 1-hour drive from Waikiki and has a much slower pace. From December–February, waves several meters high make it a world-class surfing destination. In summer, the water is calmer and better for swimming and snorkeling. The town of Haleiwa has shave ice and garlic shrimp trucks. Sea turtles often come ashore to bask at Laniakea Beach.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.4.tip: Winter waves on the North Shore are large and currents are strong. Stay out of the water when you see red flags or warning signs.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.5.fee: About $30 per vehicle; sunrise reservations cost about $1 extra
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.5.name: Sunrise at Haleakalā
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.5.text: Maui's highest peak rises to about 3,055 meters and is topped by a red-brown volcanic landscape. Watching the sunrise above the clouds is Maui's signature experience. The drive from Kahului to the summit takes about 2 hours. Entry from 3–7 a.m. requires an advance reservation. The earliest reservations are released about 60 days ahead, with some additional slots released two days before. No reservation is needed for sunset or daytime entry.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.5.tip: Before sunrise, temperatures at the summit are often around 0°C, with strong winds. Bring a down jacket, hat, and gloves.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.6.fee: About $5 per person for the black-sand beach; about $10 for parking
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.6.name: Road to Hana
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.6.text: This mountain road follows Maui's northeast coast from Paia to Hana, covering about 80 kilometers with hundreds of curves and dozens of one-lane bridges. The route passes rainforests, waterfalls, and sea cliffs. It takes 2.5–3 hours without stopping, and a round trip with stops takes a full day. Waiʻānapanapa State Park along the way has a black-sand beach. Nonresidents must reserve entry and parking in advance.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.6.tip: Leave before 7 a.m. Do not park illegally or enter private land. Most rental agreements prohibit driving on the rough roads south of Hana.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.7.name: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.7.text: On the southeast side of Hawaiʻi Island, Kīlauea is one of the world's most active volcanoes. Along the Crater Rim Drive, you can see the steaming Halemaʻumaʻu crater, walk through part of Thurston Lava Tube, and follow Chain of Craters Road toward the coast to see a sea arch formed by lava flows. Whether you can see lava depends entirely on current volcanic activity. Check the U.S. Geological Survey's Hawaiian Volcano Observatory before you go.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.7.tip: Some areas may close because of volcanic gas or eruptions. People with heart or lung conditions, pregnant travelers, and those traveling with infants should pay attention to air-quality alerts.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.8.name: Stargazing at Maunakea
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.8.text: More than a dozen large astronomical telescopes stand at the summit, about 4,207 meters above sea level, making Maunakea one of the world's best stargazing sites. It is also a sacred mountain for Native Hawaiians. Most visitors drive to the Visitor Information Station at about 2,800 meters to acclimatize, watch the sunset, and stargaze. Above it, a steep gravel road requires a 4WD vehicle. You must descend 30 minutes after sunset, so many visitors join a tour to the summit.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.8.tip: Children under 13, pregnant travelers, and anyone feeling unwell should not go above the visitor station. Most rental agreements prohibit driving to the summit.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.9.fee: About $5 per nonresident; about $10 for parking
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.9.name: Waimea Canyon and the Nāpali Coast, Kauaʻi
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.9.text: On western Kauaʻi, the red layers of Waimea Canyon unfold along the mountain road, which has several viewpoints. At the end, Kalalau Lookout overlooks the Nāpali Coast, where jagged green ridges plunge into the sea. You can also see the Nāpali Coast by boat or helicopter. Hāʻena State Park in the north offers access to part of the Kalalau Trail. Nonresidents must reserve within 30 days before their visit.
2acc1f6f649197577759.spots.9.tip: Clouds and mist often roll into Kalalau Lookout in the afternoon, so go in the morning for clearer views. Summer seas are calmer and more comfortable for boat trips.
2acc1f6f649197577759.stay: On Oahu, stay in Waikiki for easy access to restaurants, beaches, and public transit. On Maui, stay in Kihei or Wailea in the south, or Kāʻanapali in the west. On Hawaiʻi Island, stay in Hilo or Volcano Village for the volcano, and in Kona for the beaches.
2acc1f6f649197577759.tagline: Beyond the beaches: volcanoes, canyons, and sunrise
2acc1f6f649197577759.tips.0: Hotel room rates are subject to about 18–19% in taxes and other fees. Many resort hotels also charge a resort fee of several dozen dollars per night. Check the total price when comparing hotels.
2acc1f6f649197577759.tips.1: Diamond Head, Hanauma Bay, Pearl Harbor, and sunrise at Haleakalā all require advance online reservations. Release times follow Hawaii time (UTC−10), so convert them to your own time zone.
2acc1f6f649197577759.tips.2: Requirements for foreign driver's licenses are stricter in Hawaii than in California. Rules depend on your license and rental company. Bring your passport, driver's license, and a certified English translation. Check with the state transportation department and your rental company before you leave.
2acc1f6f649197577759.tips.3: Swim only at beaches with lifeguards. Stay about 3 meters from sea turtles and at least about 15 meters from monk seals. Do not touch or feed them.
2acc1f6f649197577759.tips.4: Hawaii bans the sale of sunscreens containing oxybenzone and certain other ingredients. Check the ingredients before bringing sunscreen from home.

2bd6d4aca7371d01083c.0: The golden rule: on departure day, go straight to a tax-free verification KIOSK and scan your passport FIRST—only check your bags after you get a green light or finish manual customs inspection.
2bd6d4aca7371d01083c.1: Two big wins: consumables and general goods are now combined toward the ¥5,000 pre-tax minimum per store per day, and both sealed tamper-evident bags and the ¥500,000 consumables cap are gone—pack your cosmetics straight into your suitcase.
2bd6d4aca7371d01083c.2: All-or-nothing inspection rule: if the KIOSK flashes red for a manual customs check, officers verify every item on the entire receipt—miss 1 sample or open a snack early and the whole receipt's refund is voided.
2bd6d4aca7371d01083c.3: Taxes to budget for: tickets issued after July 2026 already fold in the ¥3,000 departure tax; luxury Kyoto stays can carry an accommodation tax of up to ¥10,000 per person per night, usually paid at check-in.

2be3db44c7e998f6377a.name: Fukuoka Airport
2be3db44c7e998f6377a.options.0.name: Fukuoka City Subway Airport Line
2be3db44c7e998f6377a.options.0.note: The subway station is directly connected to the domestic terminal. From the international terminal, first take the free shuttle bus from near Stop 5 to the domestic terminal, about 10 minutes, then enter the station.
2be3db44c7e998f6377a.options.0.price: Fares depend on distance, starting at ¥210; Hakata and Tenjin both cost only a few hundred yen
2be3db44c7e998f6377a.options.0.time: About 5 minutes to Hakata and 11 minutes to Tenjin
2be3db44c7e998f6377a.options.1.name: Direct international terminal bus
2be3db44c7e998f6377a.options.1.note: Departs directly from the international terminal, eliminating the shuttle transfer. Consider it if you have lots of luggage. Check the operator for schedules and fares.
2be3db44c7e998f6377a.options.1.price: Check the fare at the stop
2be3db44c7e998f6377a.options.2.name: Taxi
2be3db44c7e998f6377a.options.2.note: The airport is very close to the city center. Sharing a taxi among three or four people is reasonably priced and practical when you have lots of luggage or are short on time.

2c31399491554397c72f.author.role: U.S. West road-trip editor · 5-time Highway 1 driver
2c31399491554397c72f.cover.alt: Bixby Bridge spanning California's Big Sur coastal cliffs at golden sunset
2c31399491554397c72f.cover.caption: Golden light sweeping across Bixby Bridge's single concrete arch and the roaring Pacific cliffs is Highway 1's defining sight—just stick to marked turnouts now that shoulder parking is strictly banned.
2c31399491554397c72f.excerpt: Two headaches haunt a 2026 San Francisco-to-Los Angeles Highway 1 road trip: hitting a surprise Big Sur slide closure that wastes two hours backtracking, and eating a triple-digit ticket for pulling onto Bixby Bridge's banned shoulders. This 3-day field report maps out real-time road checks, the exact US-101 detour cutoff, and every north-and-south highlight.
