2e4b488a37623cd357d3.cost: The Met adult admission $30; Levain cookie ~$5.50 each
2e4b488a37623cd357d3.location: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (The Met) → Central Park → Levain Bakery
2e4b488a37623cd357d3.paragraphs.0: Save day five for America's greatest cultural powerhouse on the east edge of Fifth Avenue: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (The Met). With over two million works, don't try to conquer it all in one go. Our tried-and-true 3.5-hour highlight route starts on the first floor at the sunlit, glass-walled Temple of Dendur and the American Wing courtyard, moves upstairs to the European Paintings galleries (Van Gogh, Monet, Vermeer), and finishes through the tranquil Chinese Suzhou garden court and monumental Buddhist frescoes.
2e4b488a37623cd357d3.paragraphs.1: Step down The Met's grand front stairs—famous from Gossip Girl—and walk straight into Central Park. Wander beneath leafy canopies past Bethesda Terrace and romantic cast-iron Bow Bridge, then exit into the Upper West Side for an oven-warm, half-pound gooey chocolate-chip walnut cookie from Levain Bakery to cap your 5 days in New York.
2e4b488a37623cd357d3.phase: Step 05 · Day 5 Uptown art finale: The Met + Central Park
2e4b488a37623cd357d3.tip: The Met is closed every Wednesday! Both the American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) and MoMA also merit half a day each—check each museum's weekly closing day before plotting your schedule.
2e4b488a37623cd357d3.title: Give The Met at least 3.5 hours for its headline treasures, then wrap up via Central Park's Bow Bridge and Upper West Side cookies

2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.0.items.0.note: Pick up your car at Jackson Hole Airport. It takes about 20 minutes to reach town
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.0.title: Arrive in Jackson
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.1.items.2.note: Go to Oxbow Bend in the evening to see Mount Moran reflected in the water, and watch for moose
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.1.move: Jackson → Mormon Row about 25 minutes; → Jenny Lake about 30 minutes
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.1.title: A day in Grand Teton
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.2.items.0.note: Enter through the south entrance and stop at West Thumb Geyser Basin along the lake
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.2.move: Jackson → Old Faithful about 155 km, 2.5–3 hours; bison crossings can make it longer
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.2.title: Enter Yellowstone through the south entrance · geysers
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.3.items.1.note: Stop at Norris Geyser Basin along the way for 1 hour
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.3.move: Old Faithful → Grand Prismatic Spring about 20 minutes; Grand Prismatic Spring → Mammoth about 70 km, 1.5–2 hours
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.3.title: Grand Prismatic Spring to Mammoth Hot Springs
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.4.items.2.note: Go to Hayden Valley in the evening to look for bison and bears again
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.4.move: Leave Gardiner before dawn and reach Lamar Valley in about 1 hour; then go via Dunraven Pass to Canyon Village in about 1.5 hours
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.4.title: Wildlife in Lamar Valley
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.5.items.0.note: Head south along Yellowstone Lake and make one last stop by the water
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.5.items.1.note: Exit through the south entrance, drive through Grand Teton, and return the car at the airport
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.5.move: Canyon Village → Jackson Hole Airport about 170 km, 3–3.5 hours
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.days.5.title: Head south along the lake and return
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.for: Travelers who want to see geysers, snow-capped mountains, and wildlife and can drive
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.season: June–September, when all park roads are open
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.summary: Fly in and out of Jackson Hole. Spend the first day viewing the peaks in Grand Teton, then enter Yellowstone through the south entrance and follow a counterclockwise loop through the geysers, Mammoth, Lamar Valley, and the Grand Canyon. Stay in a different area each night to avoid backtracking. Look for animals in the early morning and visit geothermal areas during the day. Park lodging must be booked well in advance. If you can't find a room, stay in West Yellowstone or Gardiner instead.
2f6f1669bc5cbaa8cbb1.title: Yellowstone and Grand Teton · 6 days

2fc72c3c1fadd1174ee5.s: Thousands of hot springs across Japan, each with its own water and atmosphere. Stay overnight in an old hot-spring town and stroll in a yukata; those near cities are good for day trips.

301755ce0efa9edc6f10.0: Skipping Caltrans QuickMap before setting out—driving all the way to a Big Sur hard closure only to burn two hours of gas and daylight turning back.
301755ce0efa9edc6f10.1: Parking illegally along Bixby Bridge's narrow shoulders or yellow lines for a quick photo—highway patrol actively tickets and tows here, easily costing hundreds of dollars.
301755ce0efa9edc6f10.2: Blindly trusting a GPS detour onto unpaved mountain dirt roads during a closure—you risk scraping the undercarriage or blowing a tire, and rental insurance rarely covers off-pavement damage. Stick to US-101.
301755ce0efa9edc6f10.3: Leaving backpacks or luggage visible inside your parked car around San Francisco and Bay Area sights—smash-and-grab thefts happen fast, so keep the cabin completely empty and valuables on you.

30b13cc1e6d376b506cf.options.0.time: About 13 minutes to Kencho-mae and 27 minutes to Shuri

30b13cc1e6d376b506cf.options.1.note: Take this if you want to reach a resort hotel without driving. Board near Stop 1 at the airport. Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your licence and required documents; check the official source.
30b13cc1e6d376b506cf.options.1.price: Depends on the route; check the operator
30b13cc1e6d376b506cf.options.1.time: Depends on the route and traffic; allow plenty of time for northern destinations

3104474894c5ba46e994.location: New Chitose Airport B1 JR Station → Sapporo Station / Odori Park / Tanukikoji
3104474894c5ba46e994.paragraphs.0: Head straight down to New Chitose Airport's B1 JR station. If you're using a 5- or 7-day JR Hokkaido Rail Pass, exchange it at the Foreigner Desk and reserve all your Hokuto Limited Express seats to Noboribetsu and Toya right away—JR Hokkaido's main limited expresses are now fully reserved-seat trains.
3104474894c5ba46e994.paragraphs.1: Book your hotel near Sapporo Station South Exit or Odori with direct access to the Chi-Ka-Ho underground walkway: in heavy snow you can walk indoors all the way from Sapporo Station to Odori and Susukino without dragging bags through drifts. Pick up slip-on ice cleats underground, stroll Odori Park's winter illuminations, and kick off dinner with Sapporo's signature soup curry—charred pumpkin, lotus root, and tender chicken leg in spiced broth over turmeric rice.
3104474894c5ba46e994.phase: Step 01 · Day 1 Land at New Chitose → Sapporo
3104474894c5ba46e994.photo.alt: Steaming bowl of Hokkaido Sapporo soup curry with roasted vegetables
3104474894c5ba46e994.photo.caption: Make Sapporo soup curry your first winter meal—charred Hokkaido vegetables in fragrant spiced broth hit differently with snow drifting outside.
3104474894c5ba46e994.tip: Dress 'thick outer, light inner': Sapporo malls, subways, and trains blast heating above 24°C! A heavy turtleneck makes you sweat indoors and freeze outside. Go quick-dry thermal + light knit/fleece + waterproof long down parka, and fleece-lined windproof pants (skip moisture-trapping jeans).
3104474894c5ba46e994.title: Ride JR Rapid Airport 37 Minutes Downtown, Grab Ice Cleats & Warm Up with Soup Curry

3208dc8a1c1411d20ed5.duration: About 3 hours shopping + 20 minutes by monorail to the airport
3208dc8a1c1411d20ed5.location: Yui Rail Omoromachi Station (Shintoshin) → Naha Airport
3208dc8a1c1411d20ed5.paragraphs.0: Check out on your final morning, leave your bags with the hotel front desk, and ride the monorail 10 minutes to Omoromachi Station in Naha Shintoshin. Its wide, sunlit avenues house the Okinawa Prefectural Museum & Art Museum (styled like an ancient Ryukyu stone castle), the huge local mall Naha Main Place—whose ground-floor supermarket sells brown sugar, Yukishio chinsuko cookies, awamori, and Okinawa-only snacks for far less than airport gift shops—and T Galleria by DFS, Okinawa's sole downtown duty-free mall.
3208dc8a1c1411d20ed5.paragraphs.1: Before noon, grab a plate of taco rice, Okinawa's beloved U.S.-Japanese mashup piling spiced ground beef, shredded cheese, crisp lettuce, tomatoes, and salsa over hot white rice. Swing back to your hotel for your suitcases, hop the 11-minute monorail to Naha Airport, and leave extra time under Japan's 2026 tax-free rules to scan your passport at the airport self-service refund kiosks before checking your bags.
3208dc8a1c1411d20ed5.phase: Step 06 · Day 4 Shintoshin shopping & smooth departure
3208dc8a1c1411d20ed5.tip: Naha Airport's international terminal is compact, and security lines move slowly during the 13:00–16:00 wave of flights across East Asia—arrive 2.5–3 hours before takeoff.
3208dc8a1c1411d20ed5.title: Visit Omoromachi for the Prefectural Museum & DFS, then glide to the airport in 15 minutes

32a0381b92c3ceb948ef.0: Driving California Highway 1 (Pacific Coast Highway) from San Francisco to Los Angeles tops countless American West bucket lists. Always drive north to south (SF → LA): staying in the right-hand ocean-side lane gives you unobstructed Pacific views and lets you pull straight into seaside overlooks without cutting across oncoming traffic.
32a0381b92c3ceb948ef.1: Just don't rely on static maps from years past in 2026. Even though Big Sur's multi-year Regent's Slide repair has reopened, California's fragile coastal cliffs can still shed rock after heavy storms or post-wildfire rains, prompting Caltrans to impose sudden closures or alternating one-way traffic. Here's how to run a 3-minute live road check before you roll, pivot cleanly onto US-101 without losing half a day if a slide hits, and steer clear of Bixby Bridge's latest no-parking traps.

32e2476d675247b2ca92.name: New Chitose Airport

32e2476d675247b2ca92.options.0.note: Most seats do not require reservations, and you can tap in directly with Suica and other transit IC cards. Some services run directly to Otaru. Heavy snow can occasionally suspend service in winter, so allow extra time.

32e2476d675247b2ca92.options.1.time: Considerably slower than JR; depends on traffic

33c015b628207bb18637.access.0.how: The JR Miyazaki Airport Line takes about 15 minutes to Miyazaki Station. The bus to Aoshima takes about 25–30 minutes.
33c015b628207bb18637.access.1.how: The highway bus to Takachiho takes about 3 hours. Services are infrequent, and reservations are required.
33c015b628207bb18637.access.2.how: The highway bus from Hakata to Miyazaki takes more than 4 hours. Alternatively, take the Shinkansen to Kagoshima-Chuo, then transfer to a JR limited express.
33c015b628207bb18637.access.3.how: The local bus from Nobeoka Station to Takachiho takes about 1.5 hours.
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.0.name: Chicken nanban
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.0.text: Miyazaki's signature fried chicken: chicken coated in egg, fried, soaked in sweet vinegar, and topped with a thick layer of tartar sauce. It's tangy, sweet, and creamy, and goes perfectly with white rice.
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.0.where: Cafeterias and izakayas around Miyazaki Station and in Nobeoka
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.1.name: Charcoal-grilled jidori chicken
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.1.text: Miyazaki jidori chicken is stir-fried over hot charcoal until the surface is blackened and smoky. The meat is pleasantly chewy and full of charcoal aroma. Locals often have it with beer or shochu for dinner.
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.1.where: Izakayas in central Miyazaki; convenience stores also sell vacuum-packed versions
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.2.name: Hiyajiru
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.2.text: This Miyazaki summer staple is made by crushing grilled miso and fish, dissolving them in cold water, and adding cucumber, tofu, and shiso. Pour it over barley rice for a cool, refreshing meal.
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.2.where: Local-food restaurants and cafeterias in central Miyazaki
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.3.name: Miyazaki mangoes
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.3.text: These greenhouse-grown mangoes are picked only after ripening fully and naturally dropping into a net. They are intensely sweet and fragrant. Whole mangoes are expensive, so try mango shaved ice or another mango dessert instead.
33c015b628207bb18637.foods.3.where: Dessert shops around Miyazaki Station, the airport, and souvenir shops
33c015b628207bb18637.intro.0: Miyazaki lies in southeastern Kyushu. Its warm climate and palm-lined coast once made it a popular honeymoon destination for Japanese travelers. The Nichinan Coast in the south is home to Aoshima, Udo Jingu, and the castle town of Obi. In the northern mountains, you'll find Takachiho Gorge and Amano Iwato, where legend says Amaterasu hid.
33c015b628207bb18637.intro.1: Miyazaki sees far fewer visitors than Fukuoka and Beppu. The pace is slow, making it a good choice for a second Kyushu trip or anyone looking for something different. The challenge is getting around: Takachiho is deep in the northern mountains and is closer to Kumamoto than Miyazaki City. The Nichinan Coast is accessible by the JR Nichinan Line and buses, but services are infrequent, so plan carefully.
33c015b628207bb18637.name: Miyazaki
33c015b628207bb18637.seasons.note: Warm year-round. Summer is good for beaches and surfing, while Takachiho's fall colors peak in mid- to late November. Watch for typhoons in summer and fall. Mountain areas are colder in winter.
33c015b628207bb18637.sources.0.title: Takachiho Town Tourism Association official website
33c015b628207bb18637.sources.1.title: Takachiho Town Tourism Association access information
33c015b628207bb18637.sources.2.title: JR Kyushu Rail Pass official information
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.0.name: Takachiho Gorge
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.0.text: This gorge was carved by the Gokase River through lava formed when Mount Aso erupted and later cooled. Its walls feature neat columnar joints, and Manai Falls drops from above into the emerald-green water. Walk about 1 kilometer along the gorge trail, or rent a rowboat for a view of the falls from the water. The latter is the classic scene.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.0.tip: Rowboats accept online reservations only. Bookings open at 9 a.m. two weeks ahead and fill quickly in peak season. Each boat is rented for 30 minutes and seats up to 3 people.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.1.name: Takachiho Shrine
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.1.text: This ancient shrine is surrounded by cedar trees and has two married cedar trees joined at the roots. Each evening, a night kagura performance at the kagura hall uses dance to tell the myth of Amaterasu hiding in a cave. It lasts about one hour and is the main reason to spend a night in Takachiho.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.1.tip: Night kagura is performed every evening. Tickets are sold on-site; check the time and price before you leave.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.2.name: Amano Iwato Shrine
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.2.text: This shrine enshrines the cave where Amaterasu is said to have hidden. At the West Sanctuary, you can follow a priest to a viewpoint overlooking the cave. About a 10-minute walk along the river from the shrine is Amano Yasugawara, a large cave filled with small stone towers stacked by visitors. The atmosphere is unique.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.2.tip: The shrine is about 8 kilometers from central Takachiho. Take a bus or taxi. The path to Amano Yasugawara has steps and is slippery when wet.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.3.name: Aoshima Island and Devil's Washboard
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.3.text: This small island is connected to the mainland by a bridge. It is covered in subtropical plants and centered on the vermilion Aoshima Shrine, a popular spot for prayers for good relationships. Around the island, waves have carved the rocks into rows of ripples known as the Devil's Washboard. They are most visible at low tide.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.3.tip: From Miyazaki Station, take the JR Nichinan Line to Aoshima Station, then walk about 10 minutes. Check the tide tables and visit at low tide.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.4.name: Udo Jingu
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.4.text: The vermilion main hall sits inside a cave beneath a seaside cliff. You have to walk down a flight of stone steps to reach it. In the sea in front of the hall is a turtle-shaped rock. Toss a wishing stone through the rope circle on the rock to make a wish—men use their left hand, and women use their right.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.4.tip: The bus from Miyazaki Station takes about 1.5 hours, and services are infrequent. You can combine it with Obi in the same day.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.5.name: Obi castle town
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.5.text: Known as the Little Kyoto of Kyushu, this castle town has well-preserved stone walls and samurai residences. Obi Castle's Otemon Gate and moss-covered stone steps are especially photogenic. Buy a walk-and-eat pass to sample snacks such as fried fish cakes and thick rolled omelets as you explore.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.5.tip: Take the JR Nichinan Line to Obi Station, then walk about 15 minutes. Services on the Nichinan Line are infrequent, so check the timetable first.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.6.name: Cape Toi
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.6.text: This cape is the southernmost point of Miyazaki. Misaki horses, a protected natural monument, roam the grassy slopes, grazing along the cliffs with the Pacific behind them. A white lighthouse at the tip offers ocean views from the top. It's ideal for animal lovers and fans of wild landscapes.
33c015b628207bb18637.spots.6.tip: It's far from the city, and public transportation is limited. Whether you can drive depends on your licence; check the official requirements. A private car and driver is recommended. Do not feed the horses or approach them too closely.
33c015b628207bb18637.stay: For the Nichinan Coast, stay near Miyazaki Station or Aoshima. For Takachiho, spend one night in Takachiho town to see the evening kagura performance, then visit the gorge early the next morning to avoid the crowds.
33c015b628207bb18637.tagline: Tropical coastlines and mythical gorges in Kyushu's most laid-back corner
33c015b628207bb18637.tips.0: Takachiho is closer from Kumamoto, so you can combine it with Aso in one route.
33c015b628207bb18637.tips.1: The JR Nichinan Line may have only one train every one or two hours. Check the timetable before heading to Aoshima or Obi.
33c015b628207bb18637.tips.2: Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your licence; check the official requirements. A private car and driver or an organized tour is recommended for the Nichinan Coast and Cape Toi.
33c015b628207bb18637.tips.3: Summer and fall are typhoon season. Coastal attractions and boats may close temporarily.

3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.access.0.how: China Southern's nonstop Guangzhou–Darwin service ends after December 3, 2026. The usual route is via Singapore, with a flight of about 4.5 hours to Darwin, or via Sydney or Melbourne.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.access.1.how: Nonstop flights to Ayers Rock Airport (Uluru) and Alice Springs take about 3 hours. Flights to Darwin take about 4–4.5 hours.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.access.2.how: Fly to Alice Springs in about 2 hours, or take The Ghan train via Alice Springs to Darwin. The full train journey takes about 3 days.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.access.3.how: Fly to Alice Springs in about 2 hours. Driving takes more than two days and is generally not recommended.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.0.name: Barramundi
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.0.text: The Northern Territory's signature fish has thick flesh and few bones. It is often pan-fried skin-on until crisp and served with salad or fries. Almost every waterfront restaurant in Darwin serves it, and it pairs well with Southeast Asian sauces.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.0.where: Restaurants on Darwin's waterfront and in the city center, and resort restaurants in Kakadu.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.1.name: Darwin laksa
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.1.text: Darwin is closer to Southeast Asia than to Sydney, and laksa is a local staple. Its coconut curry broth comes with thick rice noodles, shrimp, chicken, and tofu puffs, with a choice of spice levels. Find it at morning and night markets. Many locals have a favorite stall they swear by.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.1.where: Palmerston? No—Asian food stalls at Parap Saturday Market and Mindil Beach Sunset Market.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.2.name: Kangaroo and crocodile meat
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.2.text: The Northern Territory is a good place to try distinctive Australian meats. Kangaroo is lean red meat, best served rare to medium-rare. Crocodile is white meat with a chicken-like texture, often served as skewers or burgers. Many restaurants offer tasting platters so you can try several kinds.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.2.where: Restaurants and pubs in Alice Springs, Yulara, and Darwin.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.3.name: Damper
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.3.text: This traditional outback bread is made from flour, water, and a little salt, then baked in campfire coals. It has a firm crust and dense crumb, and is now often served with butter and golden syrup. You can often try it freshly baked at dinners under the stars and bush experiences in the Red Centre.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.foods.3.where: Outdoor dinners and bush experiences in Yulara and Alice Springs.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.intro.0: The Northern Territory has two very different regions. In the south, the Red Centre has Uluru, the domes of Kata Tjuta, and Kings Canyon, surrounded by hundreds of kilometers of red desert. In the north, the Top End centers on the capital, Darwin, with tropical national parks such as Kakadu and Litchfield, home to wetlands, waterfalls, and crocodiles.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.intro.1: The two regions are about 1,500 kilometers apart. Most trips focus on one or include a flight between them. For the Red Centre, fly into Ayers Rock Airport or Alice Springs and allow 3–5 days. For the Top End, rent a car in Darwin and allow 3–5 days. This is not a place to rush between sights. Driving, hiking, and watching sunrises and sunsets are the main attractions.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.intro.2: Uluru is sacred to the Anangu people. Climbing has been permanently banned since October 2019. Today, visitors explore the trails around its base and watch its colors change in the morning and evening light. Uluru and Kakadu require national park tickets. Other parks managed by the Northern Territory government have a separate visitor pass.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.name: Northern Territory
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.seasons.note: The dry season, May–September, is best. The Top End's wet season runs roughly November–April, when many roads and waterfalls close. In the Red Centre, temperatures often exceed 40°C in November–March, while nights can drop to around 0°C in June–July.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.0.fee: About A$38 per adult / 3 days; free for those under 18
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.0.name: Uluru, Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.0.text: This single mass of red sandstone rises about 350 meters above the plains and is Australia's best-known landmark. Watch a sunrise and a sunset, then walk all or part of the roughly 10-kilometer base trail to see caves, waterholes, and rock art. Visit the Cultural Centre first to learn about Anangu stories. It will change how you see the rock.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.0.tip: Some sacred sites have signs prohibiting photography. Please respect them. The park opens between 5 and 6:30 am, depending on the month.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.1.fee: Included in the Uluru park ticket
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.1.name: Kata Tjuta, Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.1.text: About 50 kilometers by road from Uluru, these 36 red rock domes rise even higher than Uluru at their tallest point. The full Valley of the Winds walk covers about 7.4 kilometers in about 4 hours, climbing and descending between the domes. Even the roughly 2.2-kilometer return walk to the first lookout is worthwhile. The same park ticket covers both sites. Many visitors find Kata Tjuta better for hiking and photography than Uluru.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.1.tip: When temperatures are forecast to reach or actually reach 36°C or higher, the Valley of the Winds walk is open only as far as the first lookout from 11 am.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.2.fee: Northern Territory parks visitor pass required
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.2.name: Kings Canyon, Watarrka National Park
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.2.text: About 3.5 hours by car from Uluru, Kings Canyon has red sandstone cliffs over 100 meters high. The classic Rim Walk is a loop of about 6 kilometers that takes about 3 hours. The steep steps at the start are the hardest part. Once on top, the trail follows the cliff edge, with a descent into the lush Garden of Eden waterhole along the way. For a gentler option, take the short trail along the canyon floor.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.2.tip: When temperatures above 36°C are forecast, you must start the Rim Walk before 9 am. Swimming is prohibited in the Garden of Eden waterhole.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.3.name: Tjoritja / West MacDonnell National Park
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.3.text: These ranges stretch west from Alice Springs, with gorges and waterholes along the road. Rock wallabies are often seen at Simpsons Gap. At Standley Chasm, the walls glow red in the midday sun. Farther out, Ormiston Gorge has a waterhole where you can swim, though the water is very cold. A round-trip drive takes a day, making this a good first or last day on a Red Centre itinerary.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.3.tip: Standley Chasm is run by an Aboriginal community and charges a separate fee. The other sites require a Northern Territory parks pass.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.4.name: Mindil Beach Sunset Market, Darwin
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.4.text: Darwin's liveliest dry-season night market has hundreds of beachside stalls selling Southeast Asian, Greek, and local food, along with crafts and street performances. Grab something to eat and sit on the sand as the sun sets over the Timor Sea—a favorite weekend ritual for locals. About 2 kilometers from the city center, it is easy to reach by taxi or bus.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.4.tip: Open only on Thursdays and Sundays, 4–9 pm, from around late April to late October. Do not swim in the sea.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.5.fee: About A$25–40 per adult, depending on the season; valid for 7 days
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.5.name: Kakadu National Park
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.5.text: Australia's largest national park is a World Heritage site recognized for both nature and culture. The rock art at Ubirr is thousands of years old. Climb to the top in the evening for sunset over seemingly endless wetlands. Year-round cruises on Yellow Water bring you close to saltwater crocodiles and large flocks of waterbirds. The park is about 3 hours by car from Darwin. Stay at least one night.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.5.tip: Jim Jim Falls is accessible by 4WD only during the dry season. Check daily road conditions on the park's official website before setting out.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.6.fee: Northern Territory parks visitor pass required; about A$10 for 1 day
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.6.name: Litchfield National Park
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.6.text: About 1.5–2 hours south of Darwin on paved roads, Litchfield is one of the Top End's best day trips. Natural pools below Florence Falls and Wangi Falls are open for swimming in the dry season. Beside the road, magnetic termite mounds stand like gravestones, aligned north–south. It is closer than Kakadu and makes for a more relaxed outing.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.6.tip: Check signs at each site before swimming. Pools often close during the wet season because of strong currents and crocodile risks.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.7.fee: Northern Territory parks visitor pass required; boat cruises cost extra
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.7.name: Nitmiluk (Katherine Gorge) National Park
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.7.text: Near the town of Katherine, a river winds through a series of sandstone gorges between red cliffs. A boat cruise is the most popular way to explore. You can also rent a canoe or walk to a clifftop lookout. About 3–3.5 hours from Darwin, it can be combined with Litchfield or Kakadu in a loop.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.spots.7.tip: When wet-season water levels are high, cruises may follow shorter routes or switch to speedboats. Listen carefully to the crocodile safety briefing before canoeing.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.stay: To visit Uluru, the only place to stay is Yulara, home to Ayers Rock Resort. Book several months ahead in peak season. At Kings Canyon, stay at the resort beside the canyon. In Darwin, choose the city center or waterfront. For Kakadu, spend a night or two near Jabiru or Yellow Water.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.tagline: The Red Centre and the tropical Top End: two sides of Australia
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.tips.0: The Northern Territory is on UTC+9:30 and does not observe daylight saving time. From October to April of the following year, it is 1.5 hours behind Sydney and Melbourne.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.tips.1: Saltwater crocodiles may be present in the Top End's rivers, waterholes, and coastal waters. Swim only where signs permit it. Box jellyfish occur along Darwin's beaches roughly October–May.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.tips.2: Flies are common in the Red Centre, so bring a fly net. Drink about 1 liter of water per hour when hiking, and avoid midday walks in hot weather.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.tips.3: Many rental agreements prohibit driving on unsealed roads or at night. Before a long drive, check the Northern Territory road conditions website at roadreport.nt.gov.au.
3468f4ae0918bd7cac0e.tips.4: Driving requirements depend on your license. Check the Northern Territory government's official website before setting out, including whether you need a NAATI-certified English translation. Drive on the left.

35b6727a839fdbb7fbf4.for: For travelers who have visited Kansai once and want to take their time exploring Kyoto during flower season
35b6727a839fdbb7fbf4.season: late March–early April, or mid-November–early December
35b6727a839fdbb7fbf4.summary: In Kyoto during flower season, the key is not where you go but when. This route puts the busiest sights early in the day: start with an early visit to Fushimi Inari Taisha, then see Tofukuji and Uji on day 1; walk the Philosopher's Path and visit Kiyomizu-dera in the evening on day 2; enter the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove at dawn, then visit Kinkaku-ji in the afternoon on day 3. Each day includes just 3–4 stops, leaving time for tea and breaks.
35b6727a839fdbb7fbf4.title: Kyoto at a slower pace · 3 days (cherry blossom or fall foliage season)

3993335b14966cc4943e.location: Surry Hills (Bills / Single O) → Sydney Fish Market → Queen Victoria Building (QVB)
3993335b14966cc4943e.paragraphs.0: Sydney's coffee and brunch culture easily deserves a dedicated morning. Around 08:30, hop the light rail or stroll into leafy, creative Surry Hills and head to Australian brunch institution Bills for warm, pillowy Ricotta Hotcakes topped with melting honeycomb butter and a velvety Flat White—or swing by nearby Single O for specialty pour-over coffee.
3993335b14966cc4943e.paragraphs.1: Around midday, ride the L1 light rail to Fish Market Station to explore the Southern Hemisphere's largest seafood market, the Sydney Fish Market. Pick out a dozen sweet, briny Sydney Rock Oysters, freshly shucked sea urchin, garlic-cheese grilled scallops, and creamy sashimi prawns, then dig in at the waterside wooden tables. On your way back, wander through the century-old Queen Victoria Building (QVB), whose stained-glass domes and heritage hanging clocks feel like a palace.
3993335b14966cc4943e.phase: Step 05 · Day 4 brunch & creative Surry Hills
3993335b14966cc4943e.photo.alt: Australian smashed avocado toast and brunch at a Sydney cafe
3993335b14966cc4943e.photo.caption: Kick off your final day in Sydney at a sun-drenched corner cafe in Surry Hills with classic Aussie smashed avocado on sourdough and a flat white.
3993335b14966cc4943e.tip: Tour buses pack the Sydney Fish Market between 12:00–13:30 and outdoor tables disappear fast. Aim for 10:30–11:30 for a late-morning seafood brunch when the catch is freshest and seats are wide open.
3993335b14966cc4943e.title: Feast on world-class hotcakes and flat whites in Surry Hills, then pair QVB with the Sydney Fish Market

399f19dd09ab95ca641c.cost: Luggage storage ¥500–1,000; viewpoint shuttle bus ¥200 one way
399f19dd09ab95ca641c.location: Shirakawa-go Ogimachi Bus Terminal → Shiroyama Viewpoint → Wada House
399f19dd09ab95ca641c.paragraphs.0: Once the bus leaves Kanazawa and bores through the long tunnels under the Hida Mountains, the moment you exit into daylight—walls of waist-high white snow filling every window—draws an audible gasp from the whole cabin. Upon pulling into Shirakawa-go Bus Terminal, immediately stow large suitcases in the coin lockers beside the waiting hall (if full, the staffed baggage room right next door takes bags per piece).
399f19dd09ab95ca641c.paragraphs.1: Order matters here: don't burn the best morning light taking snapshots at the village entrance. Line up immediately for the Shiroyama Viewpoint shuttle minibus (every 20 minutes, ¥200 one way—skip walking up the icy steep trail in winter) to capture the fairytale panorama while crowds are thin and the sun sits low. Ride back down to stroll the quiet lanes and pay ¥400 to enter Wada House, the largest gassho-zukuri residence, climbing to the upper attics to see massive thatched beams lashed together solely with rope and timber joinery—not a single nail.
399f19dd09ab95ca641c.phase: Step 03 · Day 2 08:40 Leave Kanazawa for the snow valley
399f19dd09ab95ca641c.photo.alt: Traditional wooden lattice teahouses lining Kanazawa's Higashi Chaya District in light winter snow
399f19dd09ab95ca641c.photo.caption: Before heading out to Shirakawa-go, save a quiet afternoon for Kanazawa's Higashi Chaya District, where light snow dusts the dark timber lattices.
399f19dd09ab95ca641c.tip: Packed snow along Shirakawa-go's main street turns skating-rink slick, and heavy roof slabs periodically slide off thatched eaves. Stay clear of roof overhangs as you walk, and slip on traction cleats before wandering the narrow rice-paddy paths.
399f19dd09ab95ca641c.title: Emerge into Shirakawa-go: stash your bags first, then shuttle up to Shiroyama Viewpoint

3b035f92f59236bec2bd.1: Blindly buying the ¥800 Enoden 1-day pass—if you're only stopping at Enoshima, Kamakurakokomae, Hase, and Kamakura, single Suica taps save money.
3b035f92f59236bec2bd.2: Stepping into the road at Kamakurakokomae crossing for photos—local residents and patrolling police enforce the boundary strictly; it's dangerous and earns an instant whistle.
3b035f92f59236bec2bd.3: Expecting raw shirasu from January to March—winter is Shonan's statutory fishing ban, so restaurants across the coast serve boiled whitebait only.

3b66c0f85304a94d9644.access.0.how: Take the Nankai Koya Line to Gokurakubashi, then transfer to the cable car up to Koyasan. The limited express takes about 1.5–2 hours.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.access.1.how: The JR Limited Express Kuroshio takes about 2.5 hours to Shirahama and about 4 hours to Kii-Katsuura.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.access.2.how: Take the JR Kansai Airport Rapid to Hineno and transfer to a train for Wakayama Station, for a total journey of about 1 hour. Shirahama is also closer from here than from central Osaka.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.access.3.how: Haneda has flights to Nanki-Shirahama Airport that take about 1 hour 15 minutes, making this a good option for going straight to Shirahama and Kumano.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.0.name: Wakayama ramen
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.0.text: A rich, slightly salty pork-bone and soy-sauce broth with thin straight noodles. Local custom is to place haya-zushi, pressed mackerel sushi, and boiled eggs on the table. Take what you want and tell the cashier how many you had when you pay.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.0.where: Long-running shops around Wakayama Station and Wakayamashi Station.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.1.name: Koyasan shojin ryori
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.1.text: Vegetarian Buddhist cuisine served at temple lodgings, without meat, fish, or the five pungent roots. Specialties include sesame tofu, with a springy texture and nutty flavor, as well as koya tofu and tempura made with seasonal vegetables. The presentation is carefully arranged.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.1.where: Dinner and breakfast at Koyasan temple lodgings; vegetarian restaurants are also found around the mountain.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.2.name: Kii-Katsuura tuna
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.2.price: About ¥1,500–3,000 for a tuna rice bowl
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.2.text: Kii-Katsuura is one of Japan's major ports for fresh tuna. After auction, the fish goes straight to the table without being frozen, giving it a softer, sweeter texture than frozen tuna. Try it as sashimi, in a tuna rice bowl, or fried.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.2.where: Seafood diners around Kii-Katsuura Station and the fishing port.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.3.name: Kishu Nanko ume
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.3.text: Wakayama is Japan's largest plum-growing region. Nanko plums have thick, soft flesh and make umeboshi with a tart, salty flavor and a lingering sweetness. Honey-sweetened versions are easier for first-time tasters. Plum wine is also famous.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.foods.3.where: Specialty shops around Shirahama and Tanabe; also available at Wakayama Station and the airport.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.intro.0: At the southern tip of Kansai, Wakayama is best known for three things: Koyasan, a Buddhist sanctuary in the mountains; the Kumano Kodo deep in the forest; and Shirahama Onsen and its beaches on the Pacific coast. It lacks the bustle of a big city, making it a good choice if you have already visited Kyoto and Osaka and want a slower pace.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.intro.1: The region is large and travel is slow, so do not try to see it all in one day. Koyasan takes about 2 hours from Namba, and an overnight temple stay is well worth it. The Kumano Kodo and Nachi Falls need 2–3 days. Shirahama can be combined with Kumano. From Osaka, take the JR Limited Express Kuroshio south along the coast for ocean views all the way.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.name: Wakayama
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.seasons.note: Shirarahama is busiest in July–August. Koyasan is very cold and often snowy in winter, while the Kumano Kodo trails can be slippery during the rainy season.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.sources.0.title: Nankai Electric Railway: New limited express fares from April 1, 2026
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.sources.1.title: Wikipedia: Koyasan
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.sources.2.title: Wikipedia: Kuroshio (train)
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.0.name: Koyasan Okunoin
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.0.text: The final resting place of Kobo Daishi Kukai. The approach from Ichi-no-hashi to the mausoleum is about 2 km, lined with towering cedars and more than 200,000 gravestones and memorial stupas, from feudal lords to modern companies. It is remarkably cool and quiet. Most temple lodgings offer evening tours, and the atmosphere is even more intense at night.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.0.tip: Photography, food, and drinks are prohibited beyond Gobyo Bridge. Put your phone away before entering.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.1.name: Kongobu-ji & Danjo Garan
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.1.text: The head temple of Koyasan Shingon Buddhism, Kongobu-ji has Japan's largest rock garden, Banryu-tei, and grand halls decorated with painted sliding screens. Danjo Garan is a few minutes' walk west. Its red Konpon Daito is one of Koyasan's symbols. Together with Okunoin, these are Koyasan's highlights, and buses connect them around the mountain.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.1.tip: It is about 5 degrees colder on the mountain than on the plains, so bring an extra layer in fall and winter.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.2.name: Kumano Kodo Nakahechi
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.2.text: A thousand-year-old pilgrimage route and a World Heritage site. Beginners should walk from Hosshinmon-oji to Kumano Hongu Taisha, a route of about 7 km that takes 2–3 hours. It is mostly downhill, with forest paths and stone steps, small shrines, and villages along the way. Afterward, soak your feet in Yunomine or Kawayu Onsen to relax.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.2.tip: Bring rain gear and shoes with good traction. Bus services are infrequent, so check the last departure before setting out.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.3.name: Kumano Hongu Taisha
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.3.text: The center of the Kumano Sanzan, this shrine has simple, dignified buildings with cypress-bark roofs. A few minutes away is the former site, Oyunohara, marked by one of Japan's largest torii gates, about 34 meters high. It makes a striking sight standing in the middle of the fields. The ancient trail ends here, making it a good first stop on a Kumano trip.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.3.tip: After visiting the shrine, head to Tsuboyu at nearby Yunomine Onsen. It is the only World Heritage hot spring you can bathe in.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.4.name: Nachi Falls
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.4.text: With a drop of 133 meters, Nachi Falls is Japan's tallest single-drop waterfall. From Seiganto-ji beside Kumano Nachi Taisha, the red three-story pagoda frames the falls in Wakayama's most iconic view. You can also climb the stone steps from Daimon-zaka, a walk of about 30 minutes through towering old-growth trees that evokes the area's pilgrimage history.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.4.tip: The stone steps at Daimon-zaka are slippery when wet. Wear shoes with good traction on rainy days and take the bus downhill on the return.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.5.name: Shirahama Beach & Shirahama Onsen
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.5.text: This beach has soft white sand and clear blue water, and is a favorite Kansai swimming destination in summer. There is a free open-air footbath by the beach, while nearby Saki-no-Yu is a seaside open-air hot spring facing the Pacific. Other attractions include the sea cliffs at Sandanbeki, sunset views at Engetsu Island, and Adventure World, home to giant pandas.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.5.tip: Hotels are expensive and hard to book on weekends in July–August. Visit Engetsu Island around sunset.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.6.name: Wakayama Castle
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.6.text: The former stronghold of the Kishu Tokugawa family, one of the three major branches of the Tokugawa clan. Its white keep stands on a hill in the city center, surrounded by well-preserved stone walls and gardens. About 600 cherry trees bloom in the park in spring, making it Wakayama City's top cherry-blossom spot. It is about a 10-minute walk from Wakayamashi Station and easy to visit on the way to the airport or Koyasan.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.spots.6.tip: The keep is a postwar reconstruction. Focus instead on the stone walls and Momijidani Garden.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.stay: Stay at a temple lodging in Koyasan, eat Buddhist vegetarian meals, and join the morning service. In Kumano, stay at one of the hot-spring towns around Hongu. In Shirahama, choose a seaside hot-spring hotel with sunset views.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.tagline: Temple stays, ancient trails, and seaside hot springs
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.tips.0: Book Koyasan temple lodgings in advance. Rooms are usually tatami-style with shared bathrooms, and you should note the curfew and dinner time.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.tips.1: Buses around Kumano are infrequent. Plan each day's schedule backward from the bus timetable so you do not miss the last bus.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.tips.2: Phone service can be unreliable along the ancient trail. Download offline maps and bring water and simple snacks.
3b66c0f85304a94d9644.tips.3: Renting a car is convenient here, but whether you can drive in Japan depends on your licence and the required documents. Check the official rules before driving; without a licence, use trains and buses.

3b6b48af54f3bc8ea423.location: Shinjuku West Odakyu Line → Hakone-Yumoto Station
3b6b48af54f3bc8ea423.paragraphs.0: Leave your large suitcases with your Tokyo hotel front desk (returning to the same hotel two days later is effortless) and carry just an overnight backpack. If you're checking out permanently, ask your hotel the day before to send trunks via Yamato Takkyubin directly to your Kawaguchiko ryokan.
3b6b48af54f3bc8ea423.paragraphs.1: Board a 07:00 Odakyu Romancecar from Shinjuku directly to Hakone-Yumoto (reserve front observation-deck seats online a month ahead if you want panoramic views). Arrive at 08:30, stash any daypack if needed, and hop straight onto the red Hakone Tozan Mountain Railway climbing into the cedars.
3b6b48af54f3bc8ea423.tip: Hakone-Yumoto's same-day Hakone Carry Service only delivers to partner inns inside Hakone (cutoff 12:30)—if you're sleeping in Kawaguchiko (Yamanashi), use station lockers or Tokyo Takkyubin instead.
3b6b48af54f3bc8ea423.title: Board the Odakyu Romancecar to Hakone-Yumoto & Travel Hands-Free

3d34a526265a6303ae6b.duration: About 3 hours direct (saves 2 hours over backtracking the coast)
3d34a526265a6303ae6b.location: Port Campbell → Camperdown → Colac → M1 → Melbourne CBD
3d34a526265a6303ae6b.paragraphs.0: The classic rookie mistake is turning around and driving the twisty Great Ocean Road in reverse—repeating the same scenery while grinding out another three hundred kilometers of hairpin bends that leave shoulders knotted. Top up at midday in Port Campbell (small-town fuel runs pricier, so put in half a tank and fill up properly at the larger inland hub of Colac), then cut north across rolling pastures onto the wide, straight A1 Princes Highway.
3d34a526265a6303ae6b.paragraphs.1: Past grazing herds, rolled hay bales, and volcanic crater lakes, cruising at 100 km/h feels effortless, putting you back in central Melbourne in under three hours to drop the car. Celebrate with a closing flat white in the street-art laneways and a hearty chicken parma or chargrilled steak near Queen Victoria Market or Southbank.
3d34a526265a6303ae6b.phase: Step 06 · Day 3 12:30 Cruise back to Melbourne on inland A1
3d34a526265a6303ae6b.tip: Approaching Melbourne, motorways like West Gate and CityLink use cashless electronic tolls (Linkt); rental cars usually bill tolls automatically plus a small daily admin fee, or simply toggle "Avoid Tolls" in Google Maps for only 10 extra minutes.
3d34a526265a6303ae6b.title: Skip backtracking along coastal bends—take the inland Princes Highway (A1) back in 3 smooth hours

3d815f072f9262fd9710.s: The cherry blossom front starts in late March from Kyushu and around Tokyo, reaches Tohoku in mid-to-late April, and arrives in Hokkaido in early May. A tree stays in full bloom for only about one week. If you miss the blossoms in the lowlands, head north or up into the mountains.

3e0e050c6aaa941ec364.0: [Kizu Market cutoff] This is a real wholesale market—doors open at 06:00 and stalls pack up after 11:00! Closed most Wednesdays, Sundays, and Japanese public holidays; always check the calendar first.
3e0e050c6aaa941ec364.1: [Kuromon trap check] Skip the first three entrance stalls, double-check whether crab legs and sashimi are priced per serving or per 100g, and stick to Takahashi Soy Milk and Ishibashi Oden for honest local snacks.
3e0e050c6aaa941ec364.2: [How to do Ura-Namba] Head to the maze of alleys east of Nankai Namba Station near Doguyasuji—standing bars (tachinomi) serving oden and yakitori deliver unbeatable value at ¥2,000–3,000 a round.
3e0e050c6aaa941ec364.3: [Kushikatsu house rule] Many Shinsekai shops switched to squeeze bottles, but wherever a shared metal sauce tray sits on the counter, strictly no double-dipping—use free raw cabbage leaves to scoop extra sauce.

3ecbbafc652114dde798.summary: Fly into Ayers Rock Airport and out of Alice Springs, driving about 800 km in a rental car along the way. Spend the first two nights in Yulara, catch Uluru at sunrise and sunset twice, walk part of the Uluru Base Walk, and hike the Valley of the Winds at Kata Tjuta. Drive to Kings Canyon on day three. Start the Kings Canyon Rim Walk early on day four, then head to Alice Springs. Spend the final half a day exploring the West MacDonnell Ranges.

3f401a8097e79dac445c.location: Namba · Hozenji Yokocho / Dotonbori side lanes
3f401a8097e79dac445c.paragraphs.0: Mid-afternoon around 14:30 is peak off-peak for Osaka's beloved konamon (flour-based comfort food). Sidestep Dotonbori's selfie bottleneck and slip two turns south into Hozenji Yokocho—a damp 50-meter flagstone lane leading to the lush emerald-moss statue of Mizukake Fudo.
3f401a8097e79dac445c.paragraphs.1: Heritage okonomiyaki griddles around the lane (like Mizuno and neighboring teppan veterans) have their shortest waits near 15:00. Watch mountain-yam batter, cabbage, and pork belly sizzle crisp before sharing a glazed pancake to save room for dinner. On your way out, grab two piping-hot 551 Horai pork buns at the Namba main store—slightly sweet dough packed with juicy pork and onion.
3f401a8097e79dac445c.tip: Eat 551 Horai buns right outside—never carry hot buns onto a sealed Shinkansen train, where their legendary onion-pork aroma earns stares from the entire carriage.
3f401a8097e79dac445c.title: Skip Hour-Long Dotonbori Queues—Duck into Mossy Hozenji Alley for Okonomiyaki & 551 Pork Buns

417ea5c4edfe0682fdca.paragraphs.0: After breakfast and check-out, stash your daypack in a Kawaguchiko Station locker and take the Red Line bus to Oishi Park—vivid crimson kochia bushes in autumn or crisp snowy lakeside framing in winter, paired with blueberry-vanilla soft-serve at the Natural Living Center.
417ea5c4edfe0682fdca.paragraphs.1: Before noon, ride the Fujikyu Railway a few stops to Shimoyoshida and walk 10 minutes to Arakurayama Sengen Park. Climb the 398 stone steps (or the gentler paved winding path alongside) to the hilltop deck for Japan's most famous postcard: vermilion five-story Chureito Pagoda, seasonal foliage, and snow-crowned Mt. Fuji dead center. Stroll Honcho Street below afterward, staying strictly on sidewalks and pedestrian crossings.

43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.calculator.note: minPurchase is based on the pre-tax total at the same store on the same day. Food and other goods can be combined to reach the threshold. Maximum refund = pre-tax price × tax rate. If you only know the tax-inclusive price, use tax-inclusive price × 10/110 for items taxed at 10%, or tax-inclusive price × 8/108 for items taxed at 8%. This is the full consumption tax amount. The actual refund will be lower if the refund company deducts a processing fee; fees vary by company and are not included in the calculator.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.0.a: Under the new system, the store must wait for customs to confirm that you are taking the items out of Japan before processing the sale as tax-free. It therefore collects the tax-inclusive price first and issues the refund afterward. The extra amount you pay at checkout is the consumption tax that will later be refunded.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.0.q: Why do I have to pay in full now when I used to pay the tax-free price directly?
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.1.a: In principle, the refund is processed only after customs confirms the items. The store or refund company decides the timing and method. The government does not charge a fee, but the refund company may charge one. Rates vary, so ask at the time of purchase.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.1.q: When will the refund arrive? Will there be a fee?
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.2.a: Some stores or refund companies support cash refunds at the departure airport after customs confirmation. Others refund only to a card or app. Follow the store's instructions at the time of purchase.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.2.q: Can I collect the refund in cash at the airport?
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.3.a: The entire receipt containing that snack becomes ineligible for a refund. Other receipts are not affected. It is best to pay separately for snacks and cosmetics, and leave anything you plan to eat or use out of your tax-free purchase.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.3.q: I ate one of the snacks I bought in Japan. Can I still get a refund?
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.4.a: Complete it at the airport where you will finally leave Japan, and do so before checking in your luggage. If you check your luggage through to the final destination on the domestic flight, customs cannot inspect it at the last airport. Plan accordingly before departure.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.4.q: I am taking a domestic flight before my international flight out of Japan. Where do I complete the process?
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.5.a: If customs has not confirmed the items within 90 days counted from the day after purchase, the sale is treated as a regular tax-inclusive sale and no refund will be issued.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.5.q: What happens if I leave more than 90 days after buying the items?
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.6.a: Tax-free items that have been confirmed must be taken out of Japan. If you do not take them, customs will collect the equivalent of the exempted consumption tax, and you may also be penalized.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.6.q: What if I decide not to take the items after customs has confirmed them?
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.7.a: The Japanese government plans to lower the consumption tax on food to 1% for two years starting April 1, 2027, but the plan still requires approval by the Diet. If implemented, food bought at supermarkets and convenience stores will already cost less, so there will be less tax to refund.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.faq.7.q: Will this system still be used in the future?
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.0.text: At checkout, pay the tax-inclusive price just like any other customer. The staff will check your passport and record the purchase. When you leave Japan, customs must confirm that you are taking the items out of the country before the consumption tax can be refunded. The purchase date determines which system applies: items bought on or after November 1 use the new system.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.0.title: Pay in full first, then get a refund after departure
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.1.text: Foreign visitors entering Japan under statuses such as “Temporary Visitor” can use the system. You must show your original passport at the time of purchase. Participating stores may also accept the tax-free QR code in Visit Japan Web (screenshots are not accepted).
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.1.title: Who is eligible
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.2.text: You must spend at least ¥5,000 before tax at the same tax-free store on the same day. Consumables such as food and cosmetics and general goods such as clothing and electronics are no longer calculated separately, so you can combine them to reach the threshold.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.2.title: Threshold: ¥5,000 before tax at the same store on the same day
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.3.text: The former limit of ¥500,000 per store per day for consumables has been removed, and items no longer need to be sealed in a special bag. However, you may only buy as much as you can personally take out of Japan when you leave. Gold and platinum bars and coins are not eligible for tax-free shopping.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.3.title: No upper limit, but only buy what you can take with you
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.4.text: You must leave Japan within 90 days, counted from the day after purchase. Before checking in your luggage, scan your passport at a tax-free procedure terminal in the departure hall. Once your luggage has been checked in, the items cannot be inspected later and you cannot retrieve the luggage.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.4.title: Complete the process within 90 days, before checking in luggage
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.5.text: Customs checks each receipt, or purchase record, as one unit. If even one item on a receipt has been eaten, used, given away, or shipped separately, nothing on that receipt will be refunded.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.5.title: Customs checks each receipt as a whole
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.6.text: Since April 2025, the option of buying tax-free items and mailing them yourself by EMS has been canceled. If you want to ship items overseas, you must arrange it directly at the store, which will handle the shipment. In that case, you do not need to have customs confirm the items when you leave Japan.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.6.title: You can no longer mail items home yourself
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.7.text: The refund may go to a bank card, credit card, or app, or you may be able to collect cash at the airport when you leave Japan. Each store or its refund company decides the details. The government does not charge a fee, but the refund company may deduct one. Ask before you buy.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.7.title: The refund method and fees depend on the store
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.8.text: For a single item priced at ¥1,000,000 or more before tax, customs may require you to show an appraisal certificate or warranty card. Preparing these documents before departure will make the process smoother.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.rules.8.title: Prepare documentation for items priced at ¥1,000,000 or more

43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.0.text: Look for the tax-free store sign at the entrance, or ask the staff whether the store offers tax-free shopping. Once your purchases at the same store total at least ¥5,000 before tax that day, go to the tax-free counter.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.0.title: Before buying: confirm that the store is tax-free
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.1.text: Give the staff your original passport or the tax-free QR code from Visit Japan Web, then pay the tax-inclusive price. Ask how the refund will be paid, whether a fee will be deducted, and where the refund will go. Enter any required refund details at the time of purchase, and keep the receipt.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.1.title: At checkout: show your passport and pay in full
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.2.text: Do not open or use consumables such as cosmetics, snacks, or alcohol before leaving Japan. If even one item is missing from a receipt, the entire receipt becomes ineligible for a refund. Keep all tax-free items together in the luggage you plan to take to the airport.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.2.title: During your trip: do not open or use the items
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.3.text: Arrive at the airport earlier than usual. Scan your passport at a tax-free procedure terminal in the international departure hall; the result appears within seconds. At Narita, Haneda, Kansai, Chubu, New Chitose, Fukuoka, and Naha airports, you can also connect to the airport's designated Wi-Fi and complete the process online in Visit Japan Web. The interface is available only in English.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.3.title: On departure day: scan your passport before checking in luggage
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.4.text: If the display says no inspection is required, you are done. If it says an inspection is required, take the tax-free items to the customs inspection area and show them to the staff. If you have already used any items, do not use the terminal. Go directly to the counter and explain the situation to customs.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.4.title: Check the result: proceed on green, go for inspection on red
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.5.text: After customs confirms the items, the store will issue the refund using the method you selected at purchase. Processing times vary. If the refund does not arrive, contact the store or refund company, and keep the receipt.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.steps.5.title: After leaving Japan: wait for the refund
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.summary: Starting November 1, 2026, Japan's tax-free shopping system will switch to a refund system: pay the tax-inclusive price at a tax-free store, then have customs confirm at the airport within 90 days of purchase, before checking in your luggage. The store or refund company will then refund the consumption tax. You must spend at least ¥5,000 before tax at the same store on the same day. Items used in Japan are no longer eligible for a refund.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.taxRates.0.items: Food and beverages, excluding alcohol—for example, snacks, pastries, tea, coffee, seasonings, fruit, and takeout bento and onigiri.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.taxRates.0.label: 8% (reduced tax rate)
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.taxRates.0.note: Dine-in purchases are taxed at 10%. The same bento is taxed at 8% when taken out and 10% when eaten in the store.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.taxRates.1.items: Cosmetics, skin-care products, medicine, electronics, clothing, shoes and bags, watches and jewelry, daily necessities, and all alcoholic beverages, including sake, whisky, and beer.
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.taxRates.1.label: 10% (standard tax rate)
43e159eb5a9d2d2311e5.taxRates.1.note: Most items at drugstores are taxed at 10%. Follow the tax rate shown on the receipt.

445581fd131ff52da8e7.location: Loch Ard Gorge → London Bridge → The Grotto
445581fd131ff52da8e7.paragraphs.0: The second huge payoff of sleeping in Port Campbell is having the neighboring sea gorges practically to yourself at dawn. At 08:30, start 3 minutes from the Twelve Apostles at Loch Ard Gorge, where soft morning light illuminates twin razor-cut ochre cliffs cradling a luminous turquoise cove. Walk down the stairs to the quiet beach where only waves echo—the legendary shelter reached by the two survivors of an 1878 shipwreck.
445581fd131ff52da8e7.paragraphs.1: Continue 15 minutes west to see London Bridge—whose inner span abruptly collapsed into the ocean in 1990, leaving an isolated natural sea arch—followed by The Grotto, where steps lead down to a natural limestone window framing a tranquil tidal pool against pounding surf. Before half past ten, crowds are thin and every vantage point is queue-free.
445581fd131ff52da8e7.phase: Step 05 · Day 3 08:30 Morning finale: Loch Ard Gorge & London Bridge
445581fd131ff52da8e7.photo.alt: Velvety flat white coffee served in a coastal town cafe along Victoria's Great Ocean Road
445581fd131ff52da8e7.photo.caption: Before swinging inland off the Great Ocean Road's cliffs and gorges, pause in a small town for an Australian flat white and brunch to melt away highway fatigue.
445581fd131ff52da8e7.tip: Clifftop soil west of London Bridge and The Grotto is fragile and prone to sudden collapse—stay strictly behind wooden guardrails and never cross barriers for a photo angle.
445581fd131ff52da8e7.title: Beat the tour coaches for crystal-clear morning light at Loch Ard Gorge, London Bridge & The Grotto

45a8c47c682c9746c91a.gateways.0.how: The monorail takes about 13 minutes to Kencho-mae Station (Kokusai-dori) and costs about ¥290. To reach the north, take a highway bus to Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium; the ride takes about 2.5 hours.
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.gateways.0.name: Naha Airport (OKA)
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.gateways.1.how: Take an airport bus or taxi to Ishigaki Port’s remote-island ferry terminal, then take a ferry to Taketomi or Iriomote. Buy tickets at the terminal window.
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.gateways.1.name: New Ishigaki Airport (ISG)
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.gateways.2.how: It is not far from Hirara’s city center, but buses are limited on the island. Consider renting a car with a driver, taking taxis, or booking a day tour.
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.gateways.2.name: Miyako Airport (MMY)
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.intro.0: Okinawa lies at Japan’s southernmost point, much closer to Taiwan than Tokyo. Winter temperatures stay in the teens, making it a popular getaway for Japanese travelers. Once the independent Ryukyu Kingdom, Okinawa still feels very different from mainland Japan, with historic sites such as Shurijo Castle and Sefa-Utaki, plus Okinawa soba, awamori, and the sanshin. Direct flights to Naha are available from Shanghai, Hong Kong, and Taipei, so you can visit for a weekend.
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.intro.1: Okinawa Island stretches from north to south. Naha and the southern historic sites are easy to explore by monorail and bus. For the northern attractions, including Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium and Kouri Island, consider booking a day tour. Driving rules in Japan depend on your licence and documentation, so check the official requirements before driving. For even bluer water, fly about one hour from Naha to Ishigaki or Miyako. From Ishigaki, you can also take ferries to Taketomi and Iriomote.
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.name: Okinawa
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.passes.0.name: Yui Rail 1-day / 2-day pass
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.passes.0.text: The 1-day pass costs about ¥1,000 and the 2-day pass about ¥1,800. They are valid for 24/48 hours from purchase. In Naha, the pass pays for itself after a few stops.
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.passes.1.name: Northern Okinawa day tour
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.passes.1.text: Most tours leave from Naha and visit Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium, Kouri Island, Cape Manzamo, and other sights. It is the easiest way to explore the north without driving.
45a8c47c682c9746c91a.season: April and October–November are the most comfortable. Summer is good for swimming, but typhoons are common from July–October.
