45a8c47c682c9746c91a.tagline: Japan’s southern islands, easy to explore without driving

4660adec9c1d71b54f38.access.0.how: Take the Tohoku Shinkansen Hayabusa to Shin-Aomori in about 3 hours, then transfer to a JR train for the few-minute ride to Aomori Station
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.access.1.how: Take the Hayabusa shinkansen to Shin-Aomori in about 1.5 hours
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.access.2.how: Take the Hokkaido Shinkansen from Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto Station to Shin-Aomori in about 1 hour
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.0.name: Nokkedon seafood bowl
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.0.text: First, buy a stack of meal tickets and exchange one for a bowl of white rice. Then walk through the market and use the tickets to add portions of whatever catches your eye, such as tuna, scallops, or roe. You choose the combination and control the amount.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.0.where: Aomori Furukawa Fish Market near Aomori Station
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.1.name: Aomori apples
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.1.text: Aomori grows more apples than any other prefecture in Japan, with the most orchards around Hirosaki. The fresh-fruit season runs from fall into early winter, when you can try many varieties that are uncommon elsewhere. Apple pie, juice, and cider are also worth trying.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.1.where: Dessert shops in central Hirosaki and A-FACTORY at Aomori Station
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.2.name: Scallops
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.2.text: Mutsu Bay is one of Japan's major scallop-producing regions. A local specialty, kaiyaki miso, cooks scallops with egg and miso in a large scallop shell. It's savory and goes well with rice. Sashimi and grilled scallops are also common.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.2.where: Izakaya and seafood markets in Aomori City
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.3.name: Senbei-jiru
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.3.text: A local hot pot from Hachinohe. Break up special Nanbu senbei rice crackers and simmer them in soy-based broth. Once they absorb the soup, their texture is a little like dumplings. A bowl is especially comforting in winter.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.foods.3.where: Restaurants in central Hachinohe; meal kits are also sold at souvenir shops around Aomori Prefecture
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.intro.0: Aomori sits at the northern tip of Honshu. The shinkansen from Tokyo to Shin-Aomori takes about 3 hours. Three things stand out: the Nebuta Festival in early August, cherry blossoms at Hirosaki Castle, and the Oirase Stream flowing from Lake Towada. In winter, Mount Hakkoda is known for heavy snow. Rime-covered trees and a soak in Sukayu Onsen are unforgettable.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.intro.1: The sights are spread out across the prefecture. Plan one relaxed day each for Aomori City, Hirosaki, and Towada-Oirase. Without a driver's license, you'll mainly rely on JR trains and seasonal buses, so check the schedules before you go. The shinkansen from Hakodate in Hokkaido takes about 1 hour, making Aomori easy to combine with Hakodate.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.name: Aomori
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.seasons.note: Hirosaki's cherry blossoms: late April; Nebuta Festival: August 2–7; Oirase fall colors: mid- to late October; Hakkoda's rime-covered trees: January–February.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.sources.0.title: Hirosaki Park · Paid areas and admission
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.sources.1.title: Hakkoda Ropeway · Operating hours and fares
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.sources.2.title: Sannai-Maruyama Site Center
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.sources.3.title: JR Group · Hayabusa stops and travel times
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.0.fee: About ¥320 for the main keep area
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.0.name: Hirosaki Castle and Hirosaki Park
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.0.text: One of Japan's twelve remaining original castle keeps. The park has about 2,600 cherry trees, which bloom in late April. The most photogenic sight is the moat covered with fallen petals, known as a 'flower raft.' The fall colors and February Snow Lantern Festival are also worth seeing. From Aomori, Hirosaki Station is about 40 minutes by JR Ou Main Line.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.0.tip: The paid area around the main keep is free from November 24 through the end of March. Visit early in the morning during cherry blossom season for the fewest crowds.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.1.name: Oirase Stream
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.1.text: This stream runs about 14 kilometers downstream from Nenokuchi on Lake Towada. Waterfalls appear one after another along the mostly gentle trail. Walking the entire route takes most of a day. Most visitors choose the section from Ishigedo to Nenokuchi, walking partway and taking the bus for the rest. Fresh greenery in May–June and fall colors in mid- to late October are the best times to visit.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.1.tip: Traffic is heavy on weekends during fall color season, so leave in the morning. Wear shoes with good traction; the rocks are very slippery after rain.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.2.name: Hakkoda Ropeway
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.2.text: The ride to Sancho Park Station takes about 10 minutes. On clear days, you can see Mutsu Bay. In January–February, wind and snow turn the fir trees at the summit into 'snow monsters,' making this one of Tohoku's best places to see rime-covered trees. In fall, the mountain slopes change color earlier than the lowlands, with peak color around early October.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.2.tip: Service may stop in strong winds, so check the official operating status before you leave. Temperatures at the summit can fall below -10°C in winter.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.3.name: Sukayu Onsen
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.3.text: This historic hot-spring ryokan sits in the Hakkoda Mountains. Its signature bath is Sen-nin Buro, a huge wooden bathhouse with milky, acidic water. Traditionally, the bath is mixed-gender, with designated hours for women. Snowfall often reaches two or three meters in winter. The ryokan is on the same bus line as the Hakkoda Ropeway, so the two make a good combination.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.3.tip: Women who prefer not to use the mixed-gender bath can visit during the women-only hours. Rinse off after bathing in the acidic water.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.4.name: Sannai-Maruyama Site
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.4.text: The remains of a large Jomon-period settlement dating back about 5,000 years, now a World Cultural Heritage site. The most striking feature is a reconstructed raised structure made with six huge chestnut posts. The museum has many pieces of pottery and clay figurines. Next door, the Aomori Museum of Art makes an easy half-day combination.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.4.tip: Closed on the 4th Monday of each month. From June–September, it stays open until 6 p.m.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.5.name: Aomori Museum of Art
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.5.text: The white, boxlike building is set into an excavated pit and is worth seeing in its own right. The museum has many works by Aomori-born artist Yoshitomo Nara, including the must-see outdoor Aomori Dog, which stands more than eight meters tall. A huge backdrop painted by Marc Chagall for a ballet fills an entire lofty gallery.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.5.tip: Aomori Dog is outdoors, and the path may be closed when there is snow in winter.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.6.name: Nebuta Museum WA-RASSE
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.6.text: Just a short walk from Aomori Station, this museum displays several enormous lantern floats that took part in the Nebuta Festival. You can get close to their frames and painted details. If you miss the festival on August 2–7, this is the next best way to experience it. Drumming and dancing demonstrations are sometimes available.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.6.tip: It's by the waterfront, so stop by nearby A-FACTORY to buy cider.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.7.name: Juniko Lakes
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.7.text: A group of small lakes scattered along the edge of the Shirakami Sanchi mountains. The most famous, Aoike, is an intense blue, like blue ink poured into the water. A loop through the beech forest takes about 1 hour. Juniko is often combined with the Resort Shirakami sightseeing train on the JR Gono Line. The slow ride along the Sea of Japan coast is an attraction in itself.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.spots.7.tip: The Gono Line has infrequent service, and all seats on the sightseeing train are reserved. Book ahead.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.stay: For a first visit, stay near Aomori Station for easy trips to Hirosaki and Hakkoda. To see Oirase's fall colors, spend a night at a hot-spring ryokan by Lake Towada or the stream.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.tagline: Honshu's northern tip: Nebuta Festival, Hirosaki's cherry blossoms, and Oirase's fall colors
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.tips.0: Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your license and the required documents. Check the official rules before driving. For Oirase and Lake Towada, you can take a JR bus or join a local tour.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.tips.1: Hotels in central Aomori fill up far in advance during the Nebuta Festival. If you can't find a room, stay in Hirosaki or Hachinohe and travel by JR.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.tips.2: Snow is deep around Hakkoda and Sukayu in winter, and route buses are often delayed by weather. Leave plenty of time for your return trip.
4660adec9c1d71b54f38.tips.3: Shin-Aomori Station is some distance from the city center. Transfer to the JR Ou Main Line to reach Aomori Station.

4741f86b843a9285ebe6.access.0.how: There are no nonstop flights to Florida. Most routes connect in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Dallas, or Detroit before continuing to Orlando (MCO) or Miami (MIA), taking about 18–24 hours in total.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.access.1.how: Flights to Orlando or Miami take about 2.5–3 hours, with frequent service from low-cost airlines.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.access.2.how: The Brightline high-speed train takes about 3.5 hours, with a station at Orlando International Airport. Driving takes about 3.5–4 hours, and there are many toll roads along the way.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.access.3.how: Driving along US 1 and the Overseas Highway takes about 3.5–4.5 hours. You can also fly; the flight takes about 1 hour.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.cover.alt: South Beach and lifeguard stands in Miami at dawn
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.0.name: Cuban sandwich
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.0.text: Roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickles, and yellow mustard are layered in Cuban bread, pressed flat, and toasted until crisp. Cuban immigrants made it a Florida staple. Pair it with a cup of Cuban coffee for a classic local lunch.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.0.where: Eighth Street in Little Havana, Miami, and Ybor City, Tampa's historic Cuban district
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.1.name: Cafecito
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.1.text: This small, intensely sweet coffee is made by whipping cane sugar into espresso to create a light layer of foam. In Miami, locals drink it standing at walk-up windows. A larger serving is split among several small cups, while the version with milk is called a cortadito.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.1.where: Little Havana and walk-up windows outside Cuban restaurants throughout the city
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.2.name: Key lime pie
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.2.text: Made with small Key limes, condensed milk, and egg yolks on a graham cracker crust, this pie is tangy, sweet, and creamy. The filling is pale yellow, not green. Some shops top it with whipped cream, while others use meringue. Don't leave Key West without trying a slice.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.2.where: Dessert shops in Old Town Key West and seafood restaurants throughout the Keys
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.3.name: Stone crab claws
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.3.price: Priced by size; a serving often costs more than $50
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.3.text: A Florida specialty, stone crab is harvested by taking only the claws so the crab can return to the sea and regrow them. The claws are served chilled after cooking, with firm, sweet meat and mustard sauce. The season runs from about mid-October to early May; outside the season, most claws are frozen. Prices vary by size, and they aren't cheap.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.3.where: Long-established seafood restaurants at the southern end of Miami Beach and seafood restaurants throughout the Keys
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.4.name: Conch fritters
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.4.text: A Florida Keys street food made by mixing chopped conch meat into batter and frying it into balls. They're crisp outside and soft inside, usually served with sweet-and-spicy sauce. Florida bans conch fishing, so the meat is mostly imported from the Caribbean, but the dish is a long-standing Keys tradition.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.foods.4.where: Seafood shops and bars in Key West and throughout the Keys
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.intro.0: Florida is a top choice for family vacations in the United States. Central Florida's Orlando is home to the two major theme park resorts, Walt Disney World and Universal Orlando; Universal's new Epic Universe opened in 2025. Drive an hour east to Kennedy Space Center, where you might get lucky and see a rocket launch. With the theme parks and space center, a family can easily fill four or five days.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.intro.1: South of Orlando, you'll find a different side of Florida: Art Deco buildings on Miami Beach, coffee and sandwiches in Little Havana's Cuban neighborhood, and alligators and wading birds in Everglades National Park farther south. Driving across the Florida Keys from bridge to bridge to Key West is one of the most famous road trips in the United States.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.intro.2: Sights are spread out. Other than the high-speed train from Orlando to Miami, you'll generally need a car. June–November is hurricane season, and summer brings thunderstorms almost every afternoon. November–April is dry and comfortable, but also the most expensive time for hotels.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.name: Florida
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.seasons.note: November–April is dry and comfortable but most expensive; theme parks are busiest during spring break in March. June–November is hurricane season, with the highest risk in August–October. Summer is hot, humid, and stormy.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.0.fee: About $140–210 for a one-day ticket, before tax
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.0.name: Walt Disney World Resort
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.0.text: The world's largest Disney resort has four theme parks—Magic Kingdom, EPCOT, Disney's Hollywood Studios, and Disney's Animal Kingdom—plus two water parks. Plan at least three days for your first visit: see the castle and fireworks at Magic Kingdom, take a safari through the African savanna at Animal Kingdom, and visit the Star Wars and Toy Story areas at Hollywood Studios.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.0.tip: Ticket prices vary by date, and multi-day tickets are cheaper per day. You can pay extra for Lightning Lane access to popular rides. Arrive at opening time.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.1.fee: Varies by date; buy tickets on the official website
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.1.name: Universal Orlando Resort and Epic Universe
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.1.text: Universal Orlando now has three parks. Ride the Hogwarts Express between Universal Studios Florida and Islands of Adventure, each of which has a Harry Potter area. Epic Universe, which opened in 2025, has Super Nintendo World, How to Train Your Dragon, and the Ministry of Magic areas, making it the newest attraction. It has more thrill rides than Disney and is better suited to older children and adults.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.1.tip: Epic Universe is not included with tickets to the original two parks; buy a separate date-based ticket. You need a park-to-park ticket to ride the Hogwarts Express.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.2.fee: About $77 for a one-day ticket; about $67 for ages 3–11
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.2.name: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.2.text: This is the launch site for U.S. human spaceflight. At the visitor complex, you can see the actual Space Shuttle Atlantis. Admission includes a bus tour into the base and the Apollo/Saturn V Center, where the massive Saturn V rocket on display is 110 meters long. Check the launch schedule before you go. If you time it right, you can watch a launch from a nearby beach. It's about a 1-hour drive from Orlando.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.2.tip: Arrive early and take the bus tour to see the Saturn V first. Lines are much longer in the afternoon. Parking costs extra.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.3.name: Miami Beach Art Deco Historic District
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.3.text: On South Beach, Ocean Drive faces white sand and colorful lifeguard stands on one side and 1930s–40s Art Deco buildings on the other. Pink, mint-green, and pale-yellow facades glow with neon lights, especially at night. Swim and sunbathe during the day, then stroll along Collins Avenue and Ocean Drive at sunset to see the historic buildings.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.3.tip: Restaurants on Ocean Drive often add a service charge directly to the bill. Check before paying and adding a tip.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.4.name: Wynwood Walls
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.4.text: Once a warehouse district, Wynwood now has large murals covering the exterior of nearly every building. It's one of the best places in Miami for photos. The central Wynwood Walls attraction charges admission, while murals on the surrounding streets are free to see. You'll also find galleries, cafés, and craft beer bars. It pairs well with Little Havana on the same day.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.4.tip: Go during the day; some streets are quiet at night. The midday sun is intense in summer, so morning or evening is best.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.5.fee: $35 per vehicle; non-U.S. residents ages 16 and up pay an additional $100 per person
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.5.name: Everglades National Park
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.5.text: The largest subtropical wetland in the continental United States is a seemingly endless “river of grass” filled with alligators, herons, and egrets. The Anhinga Trail in the Royal Palm area is the easiest place to explore, with alligators often sunning themselves beside the boardwalk. Shark Valley in the north has a sightseeing tram and observation tower. Animals are easiest to spot from December–April, the dry season, when there are also fewer mosquitoes.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.5.tip: Stay at least about 4.5 meters from alligators. The park does not accept cash; cards are the only payment method.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.6.name: Overseas Highway
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.6.text: US 1 links the Florida Keys from Key Largo to Key West, crossing the sea on more than forty bridges. The water on both sides is blue-green and shallow. The most famous section is the approximately 11-kilometer Seven Mile Bridge; the abandoned old bridge beside it was once a railway bridge. Stop at Bahia Honda State Park to swim, see the beach, and view the old bridge.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.6.tip: Most of the route is a two-lane road with low speed limits. Weekend round trips are often congested, so leave early. Fill up at a gas station before the tank gets low.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.7.name: Key West
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.7.text: This small island is the southernmost point in the continental United States, about 145 kilometers from Cuba. Old Town has wooden white houses and chickens wandering the streets. Duval Street is lined with bars, and the Ernest Hemingway Home and Museum is home to dozens of six-toed cats. Go to Mallory Square at sunset for views and street performances. If you have more time, take a ferry to Dry Tortugas National Park to see the offshore fort and go snorkeling.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.spots.7.tip: Ferry seats to Dry Tortugas are limited, so book several months ahead. Parking is difficult on the island; renting a bicycle is more convenient.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.stay: For theme park trips, stay near the Disney or Universal resort areas in Orlando to use the shuttles and avoid parking fees. In Miami, stay in South Beach or downtown Brickell. Hotels in Key West are expensive, so book at least one month ahead.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.tagline: Theme parks, rockets, beaches, and swamps—even winter feels like summer
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.tips.0: If traveling during hurricane season from June–November, buy insurance that covers weather-related cancellations. When a hurricane warning is issued, follow local evacuation orders and stay away from the beach to watch the waves.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.tips.1: Toll roads and the Overseas Highway mostly use electronic tolling. Ask the rental company about its toll plan, or your bill may include an additional fee.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.tips.2: Whether you can drive in Florida with a valid license from your home country depends on your license and the applicable rules. Check with the rental company and the official source; you may also need a translation or international driving permit.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.tips.3: Lakes and canals may contain alligators. Do not enter the water outside designated areas, and keep children and pets away from the shore.
4741f86b843a9285ebe6.tips.4: Florida's sales tax is 6%, with most counties adding another 0.5–1.5%. Hotels also charge a tourist tax, and listed prices do not include these taxes.

47ad395239744a2910d8.access.0.how: Take the Limited Express Yakumo from Okayama Station to Matsue Station in about 2.5 hours
47ad395239744a2910d8.access.1.how: Airport buses reach Izumoshi Station and Matsue Station in about 30 minutes each; flights to Tokyo are available
47ad395239744a2910d8.access.2.how: Take a JR limited express from Tottori Station to Matsue Station in about 1.5 hours
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.0.name: Izumo soba
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.0.text: Made from buckwheat ground with the hulls, this soba is dark in color and rich in flavor. The most common style, warigo soba, is served in three stacked round lacquer boxes. Pour the sauce directly over the noodles, then pour any remaining sauce into the next layer after finishing one.
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.0.where: Many restaurants are around Shinmon-dori, the approach to Izumo Taisha
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.1.name: Lake Shinji shijimi clam soup
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.1.text: Lake Shinji is a brackish lake known for its large, flavorful shijimi clams. Many clams sold in Japanese supermarkets come from here. The simplest way to try them is in a bowl of miso soup, which is a standard part of ryokan breakfasts.
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.1.where: Restaurants in Matsue and ryokan breakfasts
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.2.name: Matsue wagashi with matcha
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.2.text: A tea-loving feudal lord helped establish Matsue’s tea culture during the Edo period, and the tradition continues today. Along with Kyoto and Kanazawa, Matsue is known as one of Japan’s great wagashi cities. After visiting Matsue Castle, stop at a tea shop for a bowl of matcha and a seasonal wagashi.
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.2.where: Tea shops around Matsue Castle and in the Shiomicho area
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.3.name: Izumo zenzai
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.3.text: The Japanese dessert zenzai is said to have originated in Izumo, where red beans and mochi were offered during Kamiarizuki. Today, specialty shops line the approach to Izumo Taisha. A bowl is warm and comforting without being too heavy in winter.
47ad395239744a2910d8.foods.3.where: Shinmon-dori, the approach to Izumo Taisha
47ad395239744a2910d8.intro.0: Shimane Prefecture lies along the Sea of Japan in western Honshu. It is sparsely populated and moves at a slower pace, making it the heartland of Japanese mythology. The region centers on two cities: Izumo is home to Izumo Taisha, dedicated to the deity of matchmaking and a must-visit for anyone seeking love; Matsue has Matsue Castle, one of Japan’s original castle towers still standing. Lake Shinji is right beside the castle, and watching the sunset there is a local tradition.
47ad395239744a2910d8.intro.1: Farther afield, you’ll find the Adachi Museum of Art, whose garden has been rated Japan’s best for many consecutive years; Iwami Ginzan Silver Mine, a World Heritage Site; and Tsuwano, known as the “Little Kyoto of San’in.” Transportation is slower than on the Sanyo side. Staying two nights in Matsue or Izumo and exploring one area per day is more comfortable than rushing between sights.
47ad395239744a2910d8.name: Shimane
47ad395239744a2910d8.seasons.note: Spring and fall are best. Matsue Castle’s cherry blossoms are beautiful in early April. Izumo Taisha is crowded during Kamiarizuki in November, so book your hotel early.
47ad395239744a2910d8.sources.0.title: Matsue Castle official website: admission and hours
47ad395239744a2910d8.sources.1.title: Adachi Museum of Art official website
47ad395239744a2910d8.sources.2.title: JR West: Tottori–Matsue Pass
47ad395239744a2910d8.sources.3.title: Shimane tourism official website
47ad395239744a2910d8.sources.4.title: Wikipedia: Iwami Ginzan Silver Mine
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.0.name: Izumo Taisha
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.0.text: One of Japan’s oldest shrines, dedicated to Okuninushi Okami, the deity of matchmaking. A huge shimenawa rope hangs in front of the Kaguraden, creating an impressive sight. Worship here follows a different custom from most shrines: two bows, four claps, and one bow. From Izumoshi Station, take a bus for about 25 minutes, or take the Ichibata Railway to Izumotaisha-mae Station.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.0.tip: In the evening, walk west to Inasa Beach for sunset. It takes about 15 minutes on foot, and legend says this is where the gods came ashore.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.1.name: Izumo Hinomisaki Lighthouse
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.1.text: This white stone lighthouse stands on a Sea of Japan cliff and is one of the tallest stone lighthouses in Japan. You can climb to the top for sea views. Nearby, vermilion Hinomisaki Shrine and a coastal walking trail take about 40 minutes to visit. From Izumo Taisha, it is about 20 minutes by bus. Services are infrequent, so plan it for the same day as Izumo Taisha.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.2.name: Matsue Castle
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.2.text: One of Japan’s 12 original castle towers and one of its 5 national treasure castle towers. Its black wooden exterior feels imposing, and the stairs are steep and narrow. From the top, you can see Lake Shinji and the entire castle town. Outside the castle, take a Horikawa sightseeing boat around the moat. The ride takes about 50 minutes, and the roof lowers when the boat passes under low bridges, which is great fun.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.2.tip: The Shiomicho area north of the castle preserves samurai residences and Lafcadio Hearn’s former home. Take a walk there if you have time.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.3.name: Lake Shinji Sunset
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.3.text: Japan’s seventh-largest lake sits beside central Matsue. At sunset, the water turns golden red and Yomegashima Island becomes a silhouette, making this one of Japan’s best-known sunset spots. From Matsue Station, walk about 15 minutes to the Lake Shinji Sunset Spot. On clear evenings, arrive 20 minutes early to claim a place.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.3.tip: Sunset time changes every day. Check it on your phone before heading out. Days with fewer clouds offer the best views.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.4.name: Adachi Museum of Art
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.4.text: This museum is known for its garden, which a U.S. magazine dedicated to Japanese gardens has rated Japan’s best for many consecutive years. You cannot walk through the garden; instead, view it through large windows, like a series of paintings hanging on the wall. The museum also holds a collection of modern Japanese paintings, including works by Yokoyama Taikan. Take the museum’s free shuttle from JR Yasugi Station.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.4.tip: The garden is especially beautiful in fall foliage and winter snow. Arrive early after opening, before the tour groups.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.5.name: Tamatsukuri Onsen
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.5.text: This historic hot-spring town has more than 1,000 years of history and is known for its “beauty-enhancing waters,” which feel silky on the skin. The hot-spring district follows the Tamayu River, with a spot where you can fill a bottle with hot-spring water to use as toner. It is about 20 minutes by car from Matsue Station and makes a good overnight ryokan stay after exploring Matsue.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.6.name: Iwami Ginzan Silver Mine
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.6.text: This former mine produced a large share of the world’s silver and became a World Heritage Site in 2007. Omori’s old town in the valley is so quiet it feels frozen in time. The walk along the stream to the open Ryugenji Mabu mine shaft takes about 40–50 minutes. You can also rent an electric bicycle. From Ota-shi Station, take a bus for about 30 minutes to Omori.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.6.tip: The mine shaft is low and damp, so wear shoes with good traction. Many shops in the old town close before evening.
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.7.name: Tsuwano
47ad395239744a2910d8.spots.7.text: This small castle town is surrounded by mountains. Tonomachi Street is lined with white walls and lattice windows, and schools of koi swim in the drainage channels. On the mountainside, Taikodani Inari Shrine has a path lined with more than 1,000 red torii gates. From Shin-Yamaguchi Station in Yamaguchi Prefecture, take a JR limited express for about 1 hour. Tsuwano is often combined with Hagi in Yamaguchi Prefecture.
47ad395239744a2910d8.stay: Matsue is the most convenient base. The castle, lake, and hot springs are all nearby, and both Izumo and the Adachi Museum of Art are a single train ride away. For a hot-spring stay, choose Tamatsukuri Onsen.
47ad395239744a2910d8.tagline: Izumo Taisha, original castle towers, and Lake Shinji sunsets
47ad395239744a2910d8.tips.0: At Izumo Taisha, worship follows the two-bows, four-claps, one-bow custom, unlike the two claps used at most shrines.
47ad395239744a2910d8.tips.1: Visitors can buy the JR Tottori–Matsue Pass. It costs about ¥4,000 for 3 days and covers unreserved seats on limited express trains.
47ad395239744a2910d8.tips.2: The Ichibata Railway from Matsue to Izumo Taisha follows the north shore of Lake Shinji and is more interesting than taking the bus.
47ad395239744a2910d8.tips.3: Iwami Ginzan Silver Mine and Tsuwano are both far from Matsue. Plan only one of them per day.

494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.access.0.how: Take the Keisei Line or JR to Narita Station, about 10 minutes, then walk for just over 10 minutes to Naritasan Shinshō-ji. It works well for a layover or a half-day visit before a late flight.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.access.1.how: The JR Keiyō Line takes about 15 minutes from Tokyo Station to Maihama Station. From there, take the Disney Resort Line or walk directly to the parks.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.access.2.how: Take the JR Uchibō Line to Hamakanaya Station for Mount Nokogiri. You can also take the Tokyo Bay Ferry from Kurihama in Kanagawa to Kanaya Port in about 40 minutes.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.foods.0.name: Narita eel rice
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.foods.0.text: Omotesandō at Naritasan Shinshō-ji is lined with eel restaurants. At many of them, staff prepare and grill the eel over charcoal in front of the entrance, filling the street with its aroma. The Kantō style steams the eel before grilling it, giving it a soft, tender texture. It makes a good final meal before your flight home, and a convenient way to use up yen. Lunch lines can be long, so avoid peak meal times.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.foods.1.name: Chōshi nure senbei
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.foods.1.text: A grilled rice cracker is dipped in soy sauce while still hot, giving it a soft, chewy texture and a rich sweet-salty flavor. Chōshi is a soy sauce-producing area, and this style originated here. The Chōshi Electric Railway survived a financial crisis in part by selling nure senbei, so buying a bag at one of its stations is also a way to support the local railway.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.foods.1.where: Chōshi Electric Railway stations and around Inubōsaki
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.foods.2.name: Katsuura tantanmen
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.foods.2.text: This local noodle dish comes from the fishing port of Katsuura on the Bōsō Peninsula. It is completely different from Chinese sesame dan dan noodles: a soy sauce broth is topped with red chili oil, stir-fried onions and ground meat. It is spicy and warming, and is said to have been eaten by fishermen after going out to sea in cold weather.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.foods.2.where: Katsuura city on the east coast of the Bōsō Peninsula
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.intro.0: For many visitors, Chiba is their first stop in Japan—Narita Airport is here, and so is Tokyo Disney Resort. Beyond those two attractions, Chiba has plenty of places suited to a half-day or full-day visit: Naritasan Shinshō-ji is only a short drive from the airport, Sawara Historic District feels like a little Edo, Mount Nokogiri offers views over Tokyo Bay from its cliffs, and Inubōsaki is the easternmost point of the Kantō Plain.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.intro.1: The most practical way to visit is to use Chiba as an airport buffer: if your flight arrives early, spend half a day in Narita before heading into the city; before a late flight home, visit Naritasan Shinshō-ji. Tokyo Disney Resort deserves a full day on its own. Buses are infrequent on the Bōsō Peninsula, so taking the JR Uchibō Line or an express bus from Tokyo is more realistic. Focus on one direction per day.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.name: Chiba
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.seasons.note: Canola flowers bloom in late winter and early spring on the Bōsō Peninsula, where it is warmer than Tokyo. Yōrō Valley's autumn colors peak from late November to early December. The coast is crowded in summer.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.sources.0.title: Nihon-ji official website: Visiting hours and fees
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.sources.1.title: Wikipedia: Naritasan Shinshō-ji
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.sources.2.title: Wikipedia: Sawara Historic District
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.sources.3.title: Wikipedia: Inubōsaki
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.sources.4.title: japan-guide: Transportation from Narita Airport to Tokyo
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.0.name: Naritasan Shinshō-ji
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.0.text: This thousand-year-old temple is Japan's most popular destination for hatsumōde, the first temple visit of the year. From JR or Keisei Narita Station, walk along Omotesandō for about 13 minutes. The street is lined with old inns, eel restaurants and souvenir shops. The temple grounds include the Main Hall and a three-story pagoda. Behind them, Naritasan Park has ponds and maple trees, with beautiful autumn colors in mid-to-late November.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.0.tip: It is convenient to visit before your flight home. Store large luggage in a locker at the airport or Narita Station.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.1.name: Tokyo Disney Resort
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.1.text: Tokyo Disneyland and Tokyo DisneySea are next to each other. DisneySea is unique in the world, with harbor and volcano themes, and appeals to adults. Disneyland is better suited to families with children. Ticket prices vary by date, and tickets are only sold for specified dates and must be bought online in advance. Paid priority access can shorten waits for popular attractions. Check show and parade times in the official app ahead of time.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.1.tip: Weekends and Japanese school holidays are the busiest. Choose a weekday if possible, and queue at the entrance 30 minutes before opening.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.2.name: Sawara Historic District
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.2.text: This merchant town prospered during the Edo period through shipping on the Tone River. Wooden shops and warehouses line both sides of the Ono River. It was the first area in the Kantō region to be designated a Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings. You can take a slow boat along the river, and the nearby former home of Inō Tadataka, who created one of Japan's first complete maps, is also worth seeing. It is about a 10-minute walk from JR Sawara Station.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.2.tip: The Sawara Grand Festival features large float processions in July and October. Weekdays are quiet and ideal for taking photos at a leisurely pace.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.3.name: Mount Nokogiri and Nihon-ji
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.3.text: This former quarry has cliffs cut into a jagged, sawtooth shape. The entire mountain belongs to Nihon-ji, home to a 31-meter stone Buddha, the Hyaku-shaku Kannon carved into the rock face, and more than 1,000 statues of arhats. The best-known spot is Jigoku Nozoki, a rock that juts out over a cliff. From it, you can look down over Tokyo Bay and see Mount Fuji on clear days. Take the ropeway up from near Hamakanaya Station.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.3.tip: The mountain is all stairs, so wear walking shoes. The temple stops admitting visitors after 3 p.m.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.4.name: Inubōsaki Lighthouse
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.4.text: This cape marks the easternmost point of the Kantō Plain. Apart from outlying islands and high mountains, it is the first place in Japan to see the New Year's sunrise. The white brick lighthouse, designed by a British engineer in 1874, is open for views over the Pacific. A coastal path offers wide-open scenery. From Chōshi, take the Chōshi Electric Railway to Inubō Station, then walk about 10 minutes.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.4.tip: The Chōshi Electric Railway is a popular local line. Its stations sell nure senbei, a local specialty.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.5.name: Yōrō Valley
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.5.text: The Yōrō River cuts through the Bōsō Hills, creating a valley with several easy riverside trails and waterfalls. The largest, Awamata Falls, is about 30 meters high. The valley's autumn colors arrive late by Kantō standards, peaking from late November to early December. It is a good choice if you miss the colors in Kyoto or Nikko. Take the nostalgic Kominato Railway; canola flowers and cherry blossoms bloom along the line in spring.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.5.tip: The Kominato Railway runs infrequently, so check the timetable first. Some trails are slippery after rain.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.6.name: Mother Farm
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.6.text: This large tourist farm sits in the hills of the Bōsō Peninsula. You can see and feed sheep, alpacas and cows, and try milking a cow. In spring, the canola fields on the hillsides are spectacular. Depending on the season, you may also see nemophila, hydrangeas and cosmos. The farm's soft-serve ice cream made with freshly milked milk is popular. It is a good place to spend a full day with children.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.spots.6.tip: The bus from JR Sanukimachi Station takes about 25 minutes. Services are infrequent, so check the timetable in advance.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.stay: For an early flight, stay in Narita or at a hotel near the airport. For Tokyo Disney Resort, stay around Maihama at an official or partner hotel. Visits to the Bōsō Peninsula are usually day trips from Tokyo.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.tagline: Home to Narita Airport, Disney, ancient temples and the coast
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.tips.0: Several options connect Narita Airport and Tokyo, including the TYO-NRT low-cost bus, Skyliner and N'EX. Choose based on the area where you are staying.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.tips.1: Tokyo Disney Resort tickets are date-based and limited in number. Buy them through official channels one or two months ahead during peak seasons.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.tips.2: Driving is the easiest way to explore the Bōsō Peninsula, but the rules depend on your licence. Check whether you need a Japanese licence or an approved translation before driving.
494ce7a612edb0a4dc9a.tips.3: The Tokyo Bay Ferry from Kanagawa to Kanaya Port lets you combine Kamakura, Yokosuka and Mount Nokogiri in a loop.

49777e2633df98ce91f0.cost: ¥200–¥10,000 per person per night (varies by city and room rate)
49777e2633df98ce91f0.location: Hotel front desks in Kyoto, Tokyo, Osaka, Fukuoka, Kanazawa, Hokkaido, and beyond
49777e2633df98ce91f0.paragraphs.0: Plenty of travelers prepay their room in full on Agoda, Booking.com, or Trip.com, only to be asked for a few thousand yen more at a Kyoto front desk and assume it's a hidden fee. In fact, it's Japan's local accommodation tax (shukuhakuzei), which third-party booking sites rarely collect upfront and hotels charge per person, per night upon arrival.
49777e2633df98ce91f0.paragraphs.1: Kyoto saw the biggest 2026 overhaul with steep tiered brackets: standard business hotels start around ¥200–¥400 per person per night, mid-to-upscale properties jump to ¥1,000–¥4,000, and top luxury hotels or high-end ryokans can reach ¥10,000 per person per night! Tokyo still charges ¥100 per night for rooms from ¥10,000 and ¥200 from ¥15,000 (though it has announced plans to shift to a 3% rate covering short-term rentals in April 2027). Osaka, Fukuoka, Kanazawa, and parts of Hokkaido also levy tiered taxes.
49777e2633df98ce91f0.phase: Step 04 · Budget for pay-at-hotel accommodation tax
49777e2633df98ce91f0.photo.alt: Warm lantern-lit cedar check-in lobby of a Kyoto boutique ryokan overlooking a moss garden at dusk
49777e2633df98ce91f0.photo.caption: Upscale Kyoto inns and hot-spring ryokans commonly settle accommodation and bathing taxes separately at check-in—give them their own line in your budget so there are no surprises.
49777e2633df98ce91f0.tip: When booking a splurge ryokan or high-rate double room in Kyoto, check the fine print for 'taxes payable at property,' and carry a little yen cash or a tap-to-pay card for traditional inns that still only take cash for local taxes.
49777e2633df98ce91f0.title: Look past the booking-site total: Kyoto's tiered lodging tax now climbs to ¥10,000 a night

4b0507e71a149f7c9d31.cost: Hida beef yakiniku or hoba miso dinner about ¥4,500–7,000 per person
4b0507e71a149f7c9d31.duration: 50-minute bus ride + evening stroll and dinner
4b0507e71a149f7c9d31.location: JR Takayama Station / Nohi Bus Center → Sanmachi Suji old town
4b0507e71a149f7c9d31.paragraphs.0: By mid-afternoon your bus rolls into Takayama Nohi Bus Center right beside JR Takayama Station, a 5-minute luggage roll from downtown business hotels complete with rooftop natural hot-spring baths. Most shops along Kami-Sannomachi close around 17:00, so drop your bags and head straight out as the dusk crowds thin to sample crisp local Hida sake for a few hundred yen at historic breweries.
4b0507e71a149f7c9d31.paragraphs.1: Dinner has one undisputed star: Hida beef. Aim for a butcher-run charcoal yakiniku house like Maruaki or Ajikura Tengoku (both wildly popular—grab a waitlist number right when doors open at 17:00 or book ahead), or slip into a timber-framed restaurant for Hida beef hoba miso, where sweet-savory miso caramelizes on a dried magnolia leaf over a tabletop clay brazier and rich beef juices melt right in—guaranteed to make two bowls of Koshihikari rice disappear.
4b0507e71a149f7c9d31.phase: Step 04 · Day 2 14:30 Arrive in Takayama, "Little Kyoto of Hida"
4b0507e71a149f7c9d31.photo.alt: Charcoal-grilled Hida beef and sizzling hoba miso cooked over a tabletop ceramic grill in Takayama
4b0507e71a149f7c9d31.photo.caption: Nothing warms a freezing Takayama night like sizzling Hida beef hoba miso, where caramelized miso and marbled beef fat coat every spoonful of steaming rice.
4b0507e71a149f7c9d31.tip: If heavy snow in Shirakawa-go delays your arrival in Takayama by 1 hour, don't stress: pivot dinner to a cozy izakaya or classic Takayama soy-broth ramen shop near the station open until 21:00, and explore the old town fresh the next morning.
4b0507e71a149f7c9d31.title: Check into a hot-spring hotel and dive into Sanmachi old town for charcoal-grilled A5 Hida beef

4cd86a017808c53623ec.cost: Included in your daily Opal cap
4cd86a017808c53623ec.duration: 30 minutes each way + 2 hours strolling Manly
4cd86a017808c53623ec.paragraphs.0: Visitors routinely drop fifty or sixty Australian dollars on harbor sightseeing cruises, yet savvy locals just tap onto the public F1 Manly Ferry leaving from Circular Quay Wharf 3. Snag an open-air seat on the aft deck: within three minutes the Opera House and Harbour Bridge fan out behind you as you cut through salty sea air across the wide harbor heads—identical views to the tour boats at commuter bus prices.
4cd86a017808c53623ec.paragraphs.1: Step off the wharf and stroll 5 minutes along pine-lined The Corso straight across the peninsula to sweeping Manly Surf Beach. Grab fish and chips, settle onto the beachfront steps for sunset, and ride the return ferry back to Circular Quay after dark—gliding head-on toward the lit-up Opera House and glowing CBD skyline for the most romantic 30 minutes of a Sydney night.
4cd86a017808c53623ec.phase: Step 04 · Day 3 evening: harbor ferry to Manly for sunset
4cd86a017808c53623ec.tip: Whenever you eat fish and chips or oysters near the wharf or beach, stay on guard against bold, circling seagulls! They'll swoop right past your hand for a fry, so sit with your back to a wall or under a table umbrella.
4cd86a017808c53623ec.title: Skip pricey sightseeing cruises—tap onto the public F1 Manly Ferry for 30 minutes of sweeping harbor views

4dc573bfb367c3d09812.cover.caption: From November 2026 onward, the real action of Japan's tax-free shopping shifts from department store counters to the self-service verification kiosks in airport departure halls.
4dc573bfb367c3d09812.excerpt: Under Japan's November overhaul, drugstore hauls no longer get locked in sealed plastic bags—but whatever you do, don't check your luggage before verifying! 4e00715bac197dc6e391.gateways.0.how: The airport bus takes about 45 minutes to Takamatsu Station and costs about ¥1,300. Flights are available from Shanghai, Seoul, Taipei, and other cities.
4e00715bac197dc6e391.gateways.0.name: Takamatsu Airport (TAK)
4e00715bac197dc6e391.gateways.1.how: The airport bus takes about 1,000 yen to JR Matsuyama Station and about 1,200 yen to Dogo Onsen.
4e00715bac197dc6e391.gateways.1.name: Matsuyama Airport (MYJ)
4e00715bac197dc6e391.gateways.2.how: Okayama is Shikoku's rail gateway. The rapid Marine Liner takes about 55 minutes to Takamatsu. Limited express trains take about 2.5 hours to Matsuyama or Kochi.
4e00715bac197dc6e391.gateways.2.name: Take JR from Okayama
4e00715bac197dc6e391.gateways.3.how: Buses from Osaka and Kobe pass through Awaji Island and take about 2–2.5 hours to Tokushima and about 3.5 hours to Takamatsu.
4e00715bac197dc6e391.gateways.3.name: Take an express bus from Kansai
4e00715bac197dc6e391.intro.0: Shikoku is the smallest of Japan's four main islands. It consists of Kagawa, Tokushima, Ehime, and Kochi prefectures and is linked to Honshu by three bridges. The north faces the Seto Inland Sea, with art islands such as Naoshima, Dogo Onsen, and the Shimanami Kaido. The south faces the Pacific, with Kochi's seared bonito and the Shimanto River. In the center are mountain gorges such as Oboke and Iya.
4e00715bac197dc6e391.intro.1: Shikoku gets far fewer visitors than Kansai and moves at a slower pace. But JR limited express trains between prefectures still take 2–3 hours, so it's best to choose two or three prefectures and stay one or two nights in each. For a first visit, take the Seto Ohashi Line from Okayama to Takamatsu, visit the art islands, then head to Matsuyama for a soak at Dogo Onsen. For nature, explore the mountains of Kochi and Tokushima.
4e00715bac197dc6e391.name: Shikoku
4e00715bac197dc6e391.passes.0.text: Covers all JR Shikoku lines, as well as Kotoden, Tosaden, and other services. From December 2026, reserved seats are included. The pass costs about ¥15,000 for 3 days or ¥23,000 for 7 days. Matsuyama city trams are not included.
4e00715bac197dc6e391.passes.1.name: What the Shikoku Pass does not cover
4e00715bac197dc6e391.passes.1.text: The section from Okayama to Kojima belongs to JR West. Matsuyama city trams, ferries to the islands, and express buses are also not included and require separate payment.
4e00715bac197dc6e391.season: Spring and fall are best. The islands are hot and sunny in summer, especially for cycling. During typhoon season, check for ferry and train cancellations.

4e2396e20cff36970a4e.location: Midtown Manhattan / Long Island City (LIC) hotels & citywide dining
4e2396e20cff36970a4e.paragraphs.0: Manhattan hotel rates stay sky-high year-round. For safety, modern rooms, and genuine value, look one subway stop across the East River in Queens' Long Island City (LIC). Served by the 7, E, M, N, and W lines, it rockets you into Times Square or Grand Central in 8–12 minutes—with quieter modern streets, noticeably larger rooms than aging Manhattan hotels, and rates often 30%–40% lower.
4e2396e20cff36970a4e.paragraphs.1: Budget for meals realistically: menu prices exclude 8.875% New York sales tax and an 18%–20% sit-down tip. Balance the math with a $6 street-cart Bagel & Lox or bakery croissant for breakfast, casual counter lunches like Chelsea tacos, Joe's Pizza, or halal chicken over rice (no 20% table-service tip required), and save your sit-down splurge for one or two memorable dinners plus Katz's.
4e2396e20cff36970a4e.phase: Step 06 · Eating, staying & tipping survival guide
4e2396e20cff36970a4e.tip: Many counter-service coffee shops and fast-casual spots flash default 18%/20%/25% tip prompts on their card screens. When you're grabbing takeout with no table service, tapping 'No Tip' or leaving a token $1 is completely fine—no guilt needed.
4e2396e20cff36970a4e.title: Where to stay safely for less and how to tip without awkwardness: three honest rules that save real money

4eba1747c3cbe036826b.0: Staying on the Great Ocean Road or rural highways after dark—kangaroos freeze into headlights in the middle of the lane and nighttime collisions are frequent; pull into your overnight town before 17:00.
4eba1747c3cbe036826b.1: Forgetting to download offline maps before departure—cell signal vanishes across Great Otway National Park and pockets of the coast, leaving you blind to fuel stops and turnoffs.
4eba1747c3cbe036826b.2: Underestimating how early beach towns close—many Apollo Bay and Port Campbell kitchens call last orders by 19:30, so don't wait for big-city dinner hours.
4eba1747c3cbe036826b.3: Cramming a 3-day route into a 1-day round trip—driving and stops alone take over 6 hours one way, turning a day trip into nonstop rushing.

4efcb15233f086710656.budget.note: Estimated using 2026 prices in major East Coast cities, including tax and tips for food. Prices are noticeably higher during peak season and holidays, and for hotels in New York City. Theme park and national park admission are not included.
4efcb15233f086710656.numbers.0.label: Police / ambulance / fire
4efcb15233f086710656.numbers.0.note: Available nationwide and free. Give your location first, then explain what happened. State your language to request an interpreter.
4efcb15233f086710656.numbers.1.label: City nonemergency lines
4efcb15233f086710656.numbers.1.note: Available in cities such as New York, Chicago, and Washington for questions or nonemergency reports.
4efcb15233f086710656.numbers.2.label: Poison control
4efcb15233f086710656.numbers.2.note: Call after swallowing medication or chemicals or being bitten by a poisonous insect. Available 24 hours.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.0.items.0.text: For tourism or visiting family, apply for a B1/B2 visitor visa: complete the DS-160 online, pay the approximately $185 application fee, then schedule an interview at a U.S. embassy or consulate in your country. Processing times vary and may be long, so start at least two or three months ahead. Don't buy a nonrefundable ticket first.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.0.items.0.title: Most travelers need a B1/B2 visa
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.0.items.1.text: Since 2025, interview waivers have been greatly restricted. They generally apply only to renewals of the same type of B1/B2 visa, when the previous visa expired no more than 12 months ago, the applicant was at least 18 when it was issued, the application is made in the applicant's country, and the applicant has never been refused a visa. Children under 14 must also attend an interview with a parent. Check the latest rules on the ustraveldocs appointment website.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.0.items.1.title: Interview waivers are now limited
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.0.items.2.text: A U.S. law passed in 2025 requires an additional visa integrity fee of at least $250 when a nonimmigrant visa is issued. It is not charged if the visa is refused. As of November 2026, collection policies vary by embassy and consulate. Check the latest fee information on the appointment website before your interview and set aside this amount in your budget.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.0.items.2.title: Visa integrity fee
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.0.items.3.text: Travelers with a 10-year B1/B2 visa must register at evus.gov before each trip to the United States. Registration is valid for two years, and you must register again after changing your passport or visa. Starting September 30, 2025, each new registration costs $30. Airlines may refuse boarding without a valid registration. Use only the official website and avoid expensive third-party services.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.0.items.3.title: Register EVUS for a 10-year visa
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.0.items.4.text: A visa only allows you to seek entry. A border officer decides whether you may enter and how long you may stay, as recorded on your electronic I-94. Have your return ticket, hotel booking, and itinerary ready. Answer the questions directly and don't exaggerate or hide anything. Border officers may inspect phones and computers, so think carefully about what is on your devices before you leave.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.0.items.4.title: Answer truthfully at the border
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.0.title: Visas and entry
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.1.items.0.text: Declare all food and agricultural products for inspection. Meat and meat snacks, seasoning packets, fresh fruit and vegetables, seeds, plants, and soil are often prohibited or restricted. Egg-yolk mooncakes are also frequently confiscated. If you declare an item that is not allowed, you can surrender it on the spot. If you fail to declare it and it is found, it may be confiscated and you may be fined.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.1.items.0.title: Declare all agricultural products
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.1.items.1.text: You must declare cash and negotiable instruments totaling more than $10,000 when entering or leaving the United States. You can complete FinCEN 105 online in advance. Declaring the money does not mean you cannot carry it, but failing to declare it may result in the entire amount being confiscated.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.1.items.1.title: Cash over $10,000
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.1.items.2.text: Foreign visitors may bring in gifts worth up to $100 duty-free. Travelers age 21 or older may bring 1 liter of alcohol and 200 cigarettes. You must pay duty on anything over the limit. Commercial quantities and counterfeit goods are not allowed.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.1.items.2.title: Duty-free allowance for nonresidents
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.1.items.3.text: Keep medication for personal use in its original packaging. For prescription drugs, bring an English prescription or instructions from your doctor, and carry only enough for your trip. Check in advance whether medicines containing narcotic or psychotropic ingredients are allowed.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.1.items.3.title: Keep medication in its original packaging
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.1.title: Declarations and quarantine
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.2.items.0.text: Visa and Mastercard credit cards work almost everywhere, and contactless mobile payments such as Apple Pay are widely accepted. UnionPay cards work in fewer places. Bring one or two credit cards that support international transactions, plus a small amount of U.S. cash for tips and small vendors. Turn on overseas transaction alerts to help prevent fraud.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.2.items.0.title: Cards are widely accepted, but UnionPay is limited
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.2.items.1.text: The United States has no nationwide sales tax. States and cities set their own rates, which are added at checkout. New York City is about 8.875% and Chicago about 10.25%. Oregon and Delaware are among the states with no sales tax. Hotels also charge lodging taxes and various fees, so check the final price when booking.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.2.items.1.title: Sales tax is not included in the price
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.2.items.2.text: The United States does not offer tourist tax refunds like Japan and Europe. Sales tax generally cannot be refunded, although a very small number of places, including Texas, offer refund programs for international visitors. Include tax in your budget before buying expensive items.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.2.items.2.title: There is generally no tax refund when you leave
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.2.items.3.text: At sit-down restaurants, tip about 18–22% of the pretax amount. If the bill already includes a service charge or gratuity, you don't need to tip again. Tip about $1–2 per drink at a bar, 15–20% for taxis and rideshares, and $2–5 per night for hotel housekeeping. At counter-service restaurants, you can choose no tip on the payment screen.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.2.items.3.title: Tips are usually expected
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.2.title: Payments, tips, and tax refunds
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.3.items.0.text: Amtrak is the most convenient option between Boston, New York, Philadelphia, and Washington. Buying tickets early can save a lot. Most other long-distance trips require domestic flights. Budget airlines often charge separately for checked bags, seat selection, and carry-on bags, so include these fees when comparing prices.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.3.items.0.title: Take the train or fly between cities
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.3.items.1.text: The rules for using a foreign driver's license vary by state, and the requirements depend on your license and the state where you drive. Some states, such as Florida, allow visitors to drive temporarily with a valid license from their home country. In many cases, you need the original license plus an English translation. Check the destination state's transportation department and your rental company's rules before leaving.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.3.items.1.title: Driver's license rules vary by state
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.3.items.2.text: Most rental companies require drivers to be at least 20 or 21. Drivers under 25 usually pay a young-driver fee. The base rate often excludes collision coverage and sufficient third-party liability insurance. Consider booking a package with comprehensive coverage, and photograph the vehicle when you pick it up. Highway tolls are often collected electronically, so ask how the toll plan works.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.3.items.2.title: Rental age and insurance
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.3.items.3.text: Drive on the right. When a school bus stops with its stop sign extended, vehicles in both directions generally must stop. In most places, you may turn right after coming to a complete stop at a red light, except in New York City. If police pull you over, stop at the roadside, stay in the vehicle, keep your hands on the steering wheel, and don't get out or search through your belongings. Follow instructions.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.3.items.3.title: A few driving rules
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.3.items.4.text: Gas pumps often require a U.S. ZIP code for card payments, and foreign cards often do not work. Go inside and tell the attendant the pump number and how much you want to prepay. After fueling, collect your change or refund for the difference.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.3.items.4.title: Pay inside before fueling
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.3.title: Transportation and driving
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.4.items.0.text: The easiest option is to buy a U.S. eSIM data plan before departure. It will work as soon as you turn on your phone after landing. The three major carriers are AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile. Bring your passport when buying a prepaid SIM in a store. If you need to keep your home number for verification codes, you can also buy a roaming package from your home carrier.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.4.items.0.title: Buy an eSIM before you leave
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.4.items.1.text: Service is good in cities, but national parks, mountains, deserts, and islands may have no signal for dozens of kilometers. Download offline maps and ticket QR codes in advance, and tell your companions your route.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.4.items.1.title: National parks often have no signal
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.4.items.2.text: U.S. numbers use +1 followed by 10 digits. To call another country from the United States, dial that country's country code followed by the area code or mobile number. You can call 911 free from any phone, even without a SIM card.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.4.items.2.title: Phone number format
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.4.title: Internet and phone service
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.5.items.0.text: If you are robbed, hand over your belongings. Don't fight or chase the person. Many people legally own guns in the United States, so avoid arguments, insults, and aggressive gestures. At night, avoid unfamiliar neighborhoods and isolated stations; take a taxi or rideshare back to your hotel. In a shooting or other dangerous situation, get away and find cover first, then call 911.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.5.items.0.title: Protect yourself first
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.5.items.1.text: The Atlantic hurricane season runs about June–November, with Florida and the southeastern coast most affected. Check forecasts from the National Hurricane Center. Heat waves are common in summer, and wildfire smoke can affect the West in summer and fall; check air quality on AirNow. Winter blizzards in the Northeast can cause widespread flight cancellations.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.5.items.1.title: Check the weather before you go
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.5.items.2.text: Deserts and canyons can be extremely hot in summer. Carry plenty of water and avoid hiking in the afternoon. Watch for altitude sickness at high elevations. Stay at least about 90 meters from bears and wolves and about 23 meters from other wildlife. Never feed animals. Swim only where lifeguards are present.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.5.items.2.title: Take national parks seriously
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.5.items.3.text: Medical care in the United States is very expensive. An emergency-room visit can easily cost several thousand dollars. Buy travel insurance with substantial medical and emergency evacuation coverage. For a non-life-threatening illness, an urgent care clinic is usually cheaper and has a shorter wait than an emergency room.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.5.items.3.title: Medical care is expensive
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.5.items.4.text: Cannabis is legal in some states, but it remains illegal under federal law. You can run into problems when entering or leaving national parks and airports. Drug laws in your home country may also apply to your conduct abroad. You must be 21 or older to drink alcohol, and drinking on the street is prohibited in many places.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.5.items.4.title: Legal cannabis still comes with risks
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.5.title: Safety and weather
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.6.items.0.text: The voltage is 120V at 60Hz. Outlets take two flat pins or two flat pins and one round pin. Plugs with two flat pins generally work without an adapter; three-prong plugs require one. Most phone and laptop chargers support 100–240V. Do not use hair dryers or electric cookers marked only 220V.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.6.items.0.title: 120V, type A/B outlets
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.6.items.1.text: Eastern Time (New York, Washington and most of Florida) is UTC−5, or UTC−4 during daylight saving time. Chicago is one hour behind Eastern Time, and the West Coast is UTC−8, or UTC−7 during daylight saving time. Daylight saving time runs from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.6.items.1.title: Time zones and daylight saving time
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.6.items.2.text: Distance is measured in miles (about 1.6 kilometers), temperature in Fahrenheit (subtract 30 and divide by 2 for a rough Celsius conversion), fuel in gallons (about 3.8 liters), and weight in pounds (about 0.45 kilograms). Dates are written month/day/year.
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.6.items.2.title: Imperial units
4efcb15233f086710656.sections.6.title: Plugs, voltage, and time zones
4efcb15233f086710656.sources.2.title: A U.S. embassy or consulate in your country · Nonimmigrant Visas (EVUS, interviews for children under 14)
4efcb15233f086710656.sources.3.title: Official EVUS registration website

4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.access.0.how: The Hayabusa on the Tohoku Shinkansen takes as little as about 1.5 hours to Sendai
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.access.1.how: The Sendai Airport Line takes about 25 minutes to Sendai Station and costs about ¥680
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.access.2.how: The JR Senseki Line takes about 40 minutes to Matsushima-Kaigan
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.foods.0.name: Grilled beef tongue
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.foods.0.text: Sendai's signature dish: thick-cut beef tongue grilled over charcoal, with a pleasantly chewy texture. A standard set comes with barley rice, oxtail soup, and pickles. Sendai Station's third floor has a whole street of beef tongue restaurants, making it easy to eat before catching a train.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.foods.0.where: Inside Sendai Station and around Ichibancho in front of the station
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.foods.1.name: Zunda mochi
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.foods.1.text: Mochi covered in chunky green edamame paste. It is mildly sweet, with a distinct bean flavor. Zunda shakes are also popular, and many people line up for them inside Sendai Station.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.foods.1.where: Dessert shops and souvenir stores inside Sendai Station
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.foods.2.name: Matsushima oysters
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.foods.2.text: Oysters farmed in Matsushima Bay are small but richly flavored and at their plumpest in winter. Waterfront shops sell grilled, fried, and rice-topped oysters. In winter, some also offer all-you-can-eat grilled oysters for a limited time.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.foods.3.name: Sasa-kamaboko
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.foods.3.text: These bamboo-leaf-shaped grilled fish cakes are soft and springy. They taste best freshly grilled. Some shops let you grill your own, making them good as a snack or souvenir.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.foods.3.where: Long-established shops in Sendai Station and Matsushima
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.intro.0: Sendai, Miyagi's capital, is the largest city in Tohoku. The Shinkansen takes about 1.5 hours from Tokyo, and Sendai Airport has international flights, making the city a popular starting point for exploring Tohoku. The city is full of Date Masamune-related historic sites, and it's easy to find beef tongue and drinks at night.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.intro.1: From Sendai, Matsushima, Akiu Onsen, and Naruko Gorge are all about an hour away, making Sendai a good base for day trips. The Hitome Senbonzakura cherry blossoms along the Shiroishi River and Zao Okama Crater Lake are highly seasonal, so plan carefully. Yamadera in Yamagata and Aizu in Fukushima are also within easy reach.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.name: Miyagi
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.seasons.note: Hitome Senbonzakura: early to mid-April; Zao Okama is accessible only from late spring through fall; Naruko Gorge's fall colors: late October to early November.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.sources.0.title: Zuihoden · Visitor guide
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.sources.1.title: Zuigan-ji · Visitor guide
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.sources.2.title: Matsushima Tourism Association · Transportation
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.sources.3.title: Sendai Airport Transit
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.0.name: Matsushima
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.0.text: More than 200 pine-covered islands dot the bay, which is considered one of the Three Views of Japan. The easiest option is a sightseeing cruise around the bay. Afterward, cross the red bridge to Fukuura Island or see Godaido Temple by the water. Stop for grilled oysters at lunch.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.0.tip: Matsushima-Kaigan Station on the Senseki Line is much closer to the sights than Matsushima Station on the Tohoku Main Line.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.1.name: Zuigan-ji
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.1.text: This Zen temple, built by Date Masamune, is about a 10-minute walk from Matsushima-Kaigan Station. Highlights include the richly decorated sliding-door paintings in the main hall, the cedar trees along the approach, and the rock caves in the hillside. Combined with Matsushima Bay, it makes a good half-day outing.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.1.tip: In winter, it closes around 3:30 p.m. Go here first if you plan to take a cruise in the afternoon.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.2.name: Zuihoden
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.2.text: The mausoleum of Date Masamune stands out among the cedar trees with its black-lacquered buildings covered in colorful carvings and gold details. The original was destroyed in World War II, so today's structure is a vivid reconstruction. Take Sendai's Loople sightseeing bus to get there.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.2.tip: The stone steps at the entrance are fairly long. Last admission is at 4 p.m. in winter.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.3.name: Sendai Castle Ruins
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.3.text: The castle is long gone, leaving only stone walls and an equestrian statue of Date Masamune. But the hill offers sweeping views of Sendai, and it's also a good spot for night views. Stop here on a Loople sightseeing bus route and visit it and Zuihoden in the same morning.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.4.name: Akiu Onsen
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.4.text: This historic hot-spring town in Sendai is about 50 minutes by bus from Sendai Station. Many inns are mid- to large-size hotels with open-air baths, and some offer shuttles from Sendai Station. In fall, continue farther into the area to see the more than 50-meter-high Akiu Great Falls.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.4.tip: Many inns offer free shuttle buses. Ask when booking whether reservations are required.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.5.name: Naruko Gorge
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.5.text: This V-shaped gorge is about 100 meters deep. From late October to early November, the hills turn red and gold. A train on the JR Rikuu East Line occasionally crosses the railway bridge above the gorge, creating one of Tohoku's most classic fall scenes. Afterward, soak in a bath at nearby Naruko Onsen.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.5.tip: The parking lots and viewpoints are crowded on weekends during the fall-color season. Go on a weekday or in the morning.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.6.name: Hitome Senbonzakura
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.6.text: A cherry-lined path runs for about 8 kilometers along the Shiroishi River, with the snow-capped Zao mountain range in the background. From Sendai, take the JR Tohoku Main Line to Ogawara Station, about 40 minutes away. The river is right outside the station. Nearby Funaoka Castle Ruins Park has a slope train up the hill, offering elevated views of the riverside blossoms.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.6.tip: The blossoms usually peak in early to mid-April, but timing varies widely each year. Check the bloom forecast before setting out.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.7.name: Zao Okama Crater Lake
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.7.text: This crater lake sits at the summit of Mount Zao. Its water is emerald green, though the color changes with the weather and light. The parking lot is a few minutes' walk from the viewpoint. Take a bus from Sendai or join a day tour. Mountain weather changes quickly, and a sudden bank of fog can hide the lake completely.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.spots.7.tip: The mountain road closes in winter. It is generally accessible from late April to early November, depending on the opening date.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.stay: Stay around Sendai Station or Ichibancho, where transportation and dining are concentrated. For a hot-spring stay, spend a night in Akiu or Naruko.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.tagline: Gateway to Tohoku: beef tongue in Sendai and bay islands in Matsushima
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.tips.0: Your licence must meet Japan's requirements for driving. For Zao Okama, consider a day-tour bus departing from Sendai.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.tips.1: For sightseeing in Sendai, you can buy a one-day Loople sightseeing bus pass to connect Zuihoden and Sendai Castle Ruins.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.tips.2: Hotels in the city fill up during the Sendai Tanabata Festival on August 6–8, so book early.
4fc1caaf76805a25fb9e.tips.3: Popular beef tongue restaurants have long lines at mealtimes. Go between 2–5 p.m. for a shorter wait.

52f36bf24488e0def54f.cost: Highway bus covered by pass (seat booking required); JR Fuji Excursion ~¥4,130
52f36bf24488e0def54f.location: Kawaguchiko Bus Terminal / JR Fujikyu Platform → Shinjuku
52f36bf24488e0def54f.paragraphs.0: Two main routes take you back to Shinjuku: first, the Fujikyu Highway Bus from right outside Kawaguchiko Station (~2 hours to Busta Shinjuku; included one-way with the Fuji-Hakone Pass, though advance seat reservation is mandatory). Bags slide under the coach effortlessly, though Sunday afternoon Chuo Expressway traffic can add 30–60 minutes.
52f36bf24488e0def54f.paragraphs.1: Second, the traffic-proof JR Fuji Excursion Limited Express—all reserved seats, direct to Shinjuku in 1 hour 55 minutes. With few daily departures it sells out fast; for weekend afternoons, book 2–4 weeks ahead on JR East's website rather than hoping for same-day seats.
52f36bf24488e0def54f.tip: Heading to Kyoto or Osaka next? Never backtrack to Shinjuku! Catch the direct Fujikyu bus from Kawaguchiko to Mishima Station (~1.5 hours) and transfer right onto the Tokaido Shinkansen—saving 2 full hours.
52f36bf24488e0def54f.title: Highway Bus vs. JR Fuji Excursion: Reserve Seats Early to Beat Weekend Jams & Sellouts

53336b918321dc5e0e97.s: Answer a few questions: where, when, how long, how many people, your budget, and your preferences. Get a day-by-day itinerary right away.

53cbca6cb47bc9849a71.duration: ~2.5 hours if open; ~2 extra hours via US-101 detour
53cbca6cb47bc9849a71.location: Option A: Straight through Big Sur → Ragged Point; Option B: CA-68 → US-101 → CA-41 → Morro Bay
53cbca6cb47bc9849a71.paragraphs.0: [If QuickMap shows the whole corridor open]: You hit the jackpot. Continue south on Highway 1 to Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park for a 10-minute stroll overlooking 24-meter McWay Falls plunging directly onto an untouched turquoise cove (beach access is strictly prohibited; admire from the overlook). Keep rolling past Ragged Point to San Simeon, where hundreds of elephant seals sprawl across the sand tossing dry grains over their backs.
53cbca6cb47bc9849a71.paragraphs.1: [If storms or rockslides close the middle section]: Never follow a navigation shortcut onto unpaved mountain tracks like Nacimiento-Fergusson or Old Coast Road—rental insurance typically voids off-pavement undercarriage damage, and those narrow ledges are genuinely hazardous. After photographing Bixby Bridge, cleanly double back to Carmel, take CA-68 east onto smooth, fast US-101 south past golden oak hills and Paso Robles wine country (a fantastic coffee stop), then cut west on CA-41 right back to the coast at Morro Bay.
53cbca6cb47bc9849a71.phase: Step 03 · Handling a road closure: the smart US-101 detour
53cbca6cb47bc9849a71.photo.alt: Golden rolling hills and vineyard valleys along California's inland US-101 at sunset
53cbca6cb47bc9849a71.photo.caption: Don't feel deflated if a Big Sur closure sends you inland on US-101—the rolling golden ranches and vineyard valleys around Paso Robles showcase a whole other wild side of California.
53cbca6cb47bc9849a71.tip: Whether you stay on the coast or detour via 101, book night two in Cambria, Morro Bay, or San Luis Obispo (SLO). All three give you complete flexibility if closures pop up and leave just 3.5 hours to Los Angeles the next day.
53cbca6cb47bc9849a71.title: Cruise straight to McWay Falls if open—or pivot onto CA-68 → US-101 instead of risking dirt backroads
