574eb76436e8ea4acde4.access.0.how: JR Special Rapid trains take about 25 minutes from Osaka Station to Sannomiya and about 60 minutes to Himeji. Hankyu and Hanshin trains also serve Kobe-Sannomiya.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.access.1.how: The Sanyo Shinkansen takes about 15 minutes to Shin-Kobe and about 30 minutes to Himeji.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.access.2.how: Take the high-speed ferry to Kobe Airport in about 30 minutes, or an airport bus to Sannomiya in about 65 minutes.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.access.3.how: JR Special Rapid trains reach Sannomiya in about 50 minutes. The Kinosaki limited express takes about 2.5 hours to Kinosaki Onsen.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.0.name: Kobe beef
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.0.text: Only Tajima beef that meets strict standards can be called Kobe beef. Fine marbling gives it a melt-in-your-mouth texture. Teppanyaki is the most common way to try it, with a chef cooking in front of you. Lunch sets cost much less than dinner, making midday a good time for a first taste.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.0.where: Teppanyaki restaurants around Sannomiya and Kitano. Look for the official bronze statue or certificate inside.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.1.name: Akashiyaki
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.1.text: These look like takoyaki, but their egg-rich batter gives them a soft, omelet-like texture. Dip them in a light bonito broth. They taste quite different from Osaka's takoyaki.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.1.where: Most shops are around the Uonotana shopping street near Akashi Station. You can also find them in central Kobe.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.2.name: Matsuba crab
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.2.price: From about ¥30,000 per person for an overnight stay with a crab dinner
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.2.text: This winter snow crab from the Sea of Japan has sweet, tender leg meat. Ryokan around Kinosaki and Kasumi serve full crab feasts with hot pot, charcoal-grilled crab, and sashimi. Look for origin tags to confirm the crab was caught locally.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.2.where: Crab dinner packages at Kinosaki Onsen ryokan, or seafood restaurants in town.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.3.name: Nankinmachi street food
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.3.text: Kobe's Chinatown packs food stalls along a short street, selling butaman pork buns, xiaolongbao, and Peking duck wraps. It is an interesting place to sample Japan's take on Chinese food.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.foods.3.where: About 5 minutes on foot south of Motomachi Station.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.intro.0: Hyogo stretches from the Sea of Japan to the Seto Inland Sea. It includes the port city of Kobe, Japan's best-preserved original castle at Himeji, Kinosaki Onsen in the north, and Arima Onsen in the mountains. From Osaka, Kobe is about 25 minutes away and Himeji about 30 minutes by Shinkansen. Both make easy day trips.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.intro.1: Allow half a day to a full day for Kobe: visit Kitano Ijinkan, see the waterfront lights, and enjoy a Kobe beef meal. Himeji Castle deserves half a day on its own. Kinosaki Onsen is about 2.5 hours from Osaka and is best with an overnight stay. Put on a yukata and visit all seven public baths. In winter, you can also feast on crab.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.name: Hyogo
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.seasons.note: Cherry blossoms at Himeji Castle are best in early April. Winter is best for Kinosaki Onsen and crab, while summer suits seaside trips to Awaji Island.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.sources.0.title: Himeji Castle management office: Admission fees and opening hours
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.sources.1.title: Kinosaki Onsen: Visit Kinosaki
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.sources.2.title: Wikipedia: Kinosaki Onsen
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.0.name: Himeji Castle
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.0.text: Japan's best-preserved original castle keep is a World Heritage Site. Its white walls and roof resemble a white heron spreading its wings, earning it the name White Heron Castle. Inside, you remove your shoes and climb six floors on steep wooden stairs. Walk straight from Himeji Station for about 20 minutes to reach the castle. The neighboring Kokoen garden has lovely fall colors.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.0.tip: From March 2026, admission for adults living outside Himeji is about ¥2,500. During cherry blossom season, lines form before opening.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.1.name: Kitano Ijinkan
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.1.text: These Western-style houses on the slopes north of Sannomiya were home to foreign merchants after the port opened. Red brick, pointed roofs, and wooden balconies give the area a distinctive feel. Many houses charge separate admission, so choose one or two to enter and admire the rest from outside. The hillside cafes and bakeries are good breakfast stops.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.1.tip: Expect plenty of uphill walking. It is about 15 minutes on foot from Sannomiya Station, so wear comfortable shoes.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.2.name: Kobe Port & Meriken Park
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.2.text: This is Kobe's signature waterfront view: the red Kobe Port Tower, the white lattice roof of the Kobe Maritime Museum, and Harborland's Ferris wheel across the water. Come at dusk for a seaside walk as the lights come on. The park also preserves a collapsed section of wharf as a memorial to the Great Hanshin Earthquake.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.2.tip: Arrive before dusk, then head to nearby Nankinmachi Chinatown for dinner after your walk.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.3.name: Mt. Maya Kikuseidai
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.3.text: This is the place for Kobe's “$10 million night view.” From the summit lookout, lights stretch along the coast from Kobe across Osaka Bay to Osaka. The cable car and ropeway take about half an hour in total. The summit is windy; arrive in the late afternoon to catch both sunset and the city lights.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.3.tip: In winter, the summit is several degrees colder than the city. Bring a heavy jacket and check the last cable car time before heading up.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.4.name: Arima Onsen
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.4.text: One of Japan's oldest hot spring towns is only about 30–40 minutes by car from Sannomiya. Its signature waters are the reddish-brown, iron-rich kinsen and the clear ginsen. Public bathhouses Kin no Yu and Gin no Yu welcome day visitors. The narrow, sloping old streets have shops selling tansan senbei crackers and Arima soda.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.4.tip: The kinsen water stains white towels brown, so do not use your hotel's white towels.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.5.name: Kinosaki Onsen
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.5.text: Willows, a stream, and stone bridges surround seven public bathhouses. Guests stroll between them in yukata and wooden geta sandals, making this one of Japan's most atmospheric hot spring towns. Limited express trains take about 2.5 hours from Kyoto or Osaka. November to March is Matsuba crab season, when ryokan crab dinners are a major draw.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.5.tip: Ryokan fill up early on weekends during crab season. Book at least a month or two ahead.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.6.name: Takeda Castle Ruins
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.6.text: Only stone walls remain of this mountaintop castle. On misty autumn mornings, it seems to float above a sea of clouds, earning it the name “castle in the sky.” The most dramatic views are from Ritsuunkyo across the valley. Access takes some effort: hike from JR Takeda Station or take a seasonal bus. It suits photographers willing to get up early.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.6.tip: The sea of clouds is most common on clear, calm mornings from September–November. Your best chance is around sunrise.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.7.name: Awaji Island
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.7.text: Cross the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge to this large island for sea views, flowers, and local onions. Tadao Ando's Awaji Yumebutai is near the island end of the bridge, and Akashi Kaikyo National Government Park has broad sweeps of flowers in spring. Local buses are limited. The easiest way to reach the island is by highway bus from Sannomiya.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.spots.7.tip: Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your license. Check official requirements before traveling. If your license is not valid for use in Japan, join a day tour or take the bus.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.stay: If you are only visiting Kobe and Himeji, stay in Osaka or Kobe's Sannomiya district and take day trips. At Kinosaki Onsen, stay in a hot spring ryokan: guests get free access to all the public baths.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.tagline: Kobe's waterfront, Himeji Castle, and hot springs in one prefecture
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.tips.0: From March 2026, Himeji Castle charges visitors aged 18 and over who live outside Himeji about ¥2,500. Visitors under 18 enter free.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.tips.1: Kinosaki's public bathhouses close on different days. Ask your ryokan which ones are open when you check in.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.tips.2: Kobe's Sannomiya area has separate JR, Hankyu, Hanshin, and subway stations with similar names. Check carefully when transferring.
574eb76436e8ea4acde4.tips.3: If you plan to drive to Awaji Island or Takeda Castle, check official requirements for your license in advance and arrange the required documents, or take the bus.

582c2961035769bdec7b.access.0.how: Nonstop options include Hainan Airlines' Beijing–Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) service several times a week, taking about 13–14 hours. Other options generally connect through New York, Hong Kong, or Tokyo.
582c2961035769bdec7b.access.1.how: Free airport shuttle buses connect to Airport station on the Blue Line for trains into the city. You can also take the Silver Line SL1 bus to South Station, about 20–30 minutes.
582c2961035769bdec7b.access.2.how: Amtrak takes about 3.5–4.5 hours to Boston South Station; flying takes about 1 hour 15 minutes.
582c2961035769bdec7b.cover.alt: Boston in fall, seen from across the Charles River
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.0.name: Lobster roll
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.0.text: A New England summer classic: a toasted hot dog bun packed with chunks of lobster meat. Try it cold with a little mayonnaise and celery, or warm with melted butter. Lobster prices vary with the market each year, and seaside shacks are not necessarily cheaper than city restaurants.
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.0.where: Boston's North End and Seaport District, plus seafood shacks on Cape Cod and the islands.
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.1.name: New England clam chowder
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.1.text: A creamy soup with clams, potatoes, and diced salt pork, served with oyster crackers. It is everywhere in Boston, and a bowl is especially comforting in a cold sea breeze. Some places serve it in a hollowed-out sourdough bread bowl.
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.1.where: Seafood restaurants around Faneuil Hall and in the Seaport District.
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.2.name: Cannoli in the North End
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.2.text: The North End is Boston's Italian neighborhood, where lines often form outside longstanding pastry shops. Cannoli are crisp, fried pastry shells filled to order with ricotta, with chocolate chips or chopped pistachios at each end. Sweet without being cloying, they make an easy snack as you continue along the Freedom Trail.
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.2.where: Italian pastry shops around Hanover Street in the North End.
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.3.name: Fried whole-belly clams
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.3.text: A summer favorite on the Massachusetts North Shore. Whole clams, bellies included, are coated in flour and fried until crisp outside and tender inside, with a briny flavor. They come with tartar sauce and fries. Order at a seaside takeout shack and eat at a picnic table for the classic experience.
582c2961035769bdec7b.foods.3.where: Seafood shacks around Ipswich and Essex on the North Shore, and on Cape Cod.
582c2961035769bdec7b.intro.0: Boston, one of America's oldest cities, is the heart of Massachusetts. Its compact downtown is easy to explore on foot, with the red-brick Freedom Trail linking historic buildings from the American Revolution. Across the Charles River in Cambridge, you can stroll through the Harvard and MIT campuses. Allow 2–3 days for the city.
582c2961035769bdec7b.intro.1: In summer, head east to Cape Cod and Martha's Vineyard for dunes, lighthouses, seaside towns, and lobster rolls. In fall, head west to the Berkshires or north to Salem, where October brings fall colors and Halloween festivities. For the islands and mountains, rent a car or plan around ferry and bus schedules.
582c2961035769bdec7b.intro.2: Massachusetts winters are long, cold, and snowy. Many shops in seaside towns close for the season from November through March of the following year. June–October is the best time to visit, but lodging prices rise sharply in peak season, especially on the islands and on fall foliage weekends.
582c2961035769bdec7b.name: Massachusetts
582c2961035769bdec7b.seasons.note: June–August for the islands and coast; late September–mid-October for fall colors. December–March is cold and snowy, with many businesses in seaside towns closed for the season.
582c2961035769bdec7b.sources.5.title: China–U.S. nonstop flight roundup (US Credit Card Guide)
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.0.name: Freedom Trail
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.0.text: A red-brick line runs about 4 kilometers from Boston Common to Charlestown, linking 16 historic sites from before and during the American Revolution. Stops include the Massachusetts State House, Old South Meeting House, Faneuil Hall, Paul Revere House, and Old North Church. Follow the line on your own and stop for lunch in the Italian North End.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.0.tip: Some buildings charge separate admission. Pick 1 or 2 to visit inside, and wear comfortable walking shoes.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.1.name: Harvard University & MIT
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.1.text: Both universities are in Cambridge, a few stops away on the Red Line. Harvard Yard has historic red-brick buildings and the John Harvard statue, with bookstores and cafes nearby adding to the college atmosphere. MIT sits along the Charles River; look for the Great Dome and Frank Gehry's twisting Stata Center. You can walk around the campuses, but do not enter academic buildings or dorms without permission. Book student-led tours ahead on the official websites.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.1.tip: Walk from MIT across the Harvard Bridge to Back Bay for the best river and skyline views.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.2.name: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.2.text: One of America's leading art museums, with notable collections of classical Chinese paintings and Japanese Buddhist sculpture. The Impressionist and American painting galleries are also excellent. Choose 2 or 3 sections to fill half a day. Fenway Park and the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum are nearby, making it easy to plan a full day of sightseeing.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.2.tip: Closed Tuesdays. Weekday mornings are the quietest.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.3.name: Salem
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.3.text: This port town is known for the 1692 witch trials. Its old streets are lined with colonial wooden houses and witch-themed shops. The Peabody Essex Museum is worth a trip in its own right. Its Yin Yu Tang house is an entire Qing-dynasty home brought over from China's Huizhou region. Seeing its traditional stepped gables and open courtyard in the United States is a remarkable experience.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.3.tip: Halloween events run throughout October. Weekends are packed, so book lodging early.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.4.name: Cape Cod National Seashore
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.4.text: Cape Cod curves into the Atlantic like a bent arm, with beaches, dunes, and lighthouses stretching for tens of kilometers along its outer shore. In summer, relax on the beach or cycle trails built along former rail lines. Provincetown, at the northern tip, is a lively arts town. The drive from Boston takes about 2 hours, but the bridges onto and off the Cape get congested on summer weekends.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.4.tip: The Atlantic-facing beaches have chilly water and rip currents. Swim only at beaches with lifeguards.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.5.name: Martha's Vineyard
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.5.text: A vacation island south of Cape Cod. Oak Bluffs has clusters of colorful wooden gingerbread cottages, while Edgartown has white-painted former whaling captains' homes. At the southwestern tip, the Gay Head Cliffs reveal bands of colored clay. Buses and bike rentals make it possible to explore the island, which is liveliest in summer.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.5.tip: The ferry from Woods Hole takes about 45 minutes. Vehicle reservations are required in advance and are hard to get in peak season.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.6.name: The Berkshires
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.6.text: These low mountains and rolling hills in westernmost Massachusetts turn red and gold from late September to mid-October, making them a classic New England fall destination. Stockbridge's Main Street looks like an old painting, and the Norman Rockwell Museum is nearby. Farther north, Mount Greylock is the state's highest point. Drive up in fall for views across layers of forested hills.
582c2961035769bdec7b.spots.6.tip: Weekend room rates double during foliage season, so visit on weekdays. Cell service is patchy in the mountains; download offline maps ahead of time.
582c2961035769bdec7b.stay: For a first visit, stay in downtown Boston, Back Bay, or the Seaport District. You can reach the Freedom Trail and Cambridge on foot and by subway. Stay overnight on Cape Cod or the islands; a day trip feels rushed.
582c2961035769bdec7b.tagline: Where the American Revolution began, with renowned universities, islands, and fall colors
582c2961035769bdec7b.tips.0: On Boston's subway, the T, you can tap a bank card or phone at the fare gate, which is easier than buying a paper ticket.
582c2961035769bdec7b.tips.1: Massachusetts sales tax is about 6.25%, and Boston's meals tax is about 7%. Neither is included in listed prices; tips are extra.
582c2961035769bdec7b.tips.2: The Museum of Fine Arts, Boston is closed Tuesdays, and many businesses in seaside towns close for winter. Check opening hours before you go.
582c2961035769bdec7b.tips.3: Book lodging 1–2 months ahead for October foliage season and July–August island stays. Prices rise as the dates approach.
582c2961035769bdec7b.tips.4: Before driving, check the Massachusetts RMV's requirements for foreign licenses and confirm with your rental company whether it accepts your license and requires a translation.

5874c59d4ee7f696b7b0.cost: All walks free; drinks at Opera Bar ~A$16
5874c59d4ee7f696b7b0.location: Circular Quay → The Rocks → Sydney Opera House → Royal Botanic Garden
5874c59d4ee7f696b7b0.paragraphs.0: Drop your bags first (staying around Wynyard, Town Hall, or Circular Quay makes getting anywhere effortless), then slip west from Circular Quay into Sydney's birthplace, The Rocks. Old sandstone warehouses, ivy-draped cobblestone alleys, and weekend artisan markets radiate historic port charm—grab a quick bite at the longtime staple Pancakes on the Rocks or a neighborhood coffee shop.
5874c59d4ee7f696b7b0.paragraphs.1: Around four in the afternoon, follow the waterfront promenade to the Sydney Opera House to see its one million pale-cream Swedish tiles catch the sun up close. Next, duck straight into the neighboring Royal Botanic Garden and wander 25 minutes along harbor-facing flower beds to Mrs Macquaries Point—the one vantage point in Sydney that frames the Opera House sails and the Harbour Bridge's steel arch together in a single unobstructed sunset postcard. Walk back down to Opera Bar beneath the Opera House after dark for a craft beer in the sea breeze.
5874c59d4ee7f696b7b0.phase: Step 01 · Day 1 arrival & classic harbor golden loop
5874c59d4ee7f696b7b0.photo.alt: Panoramic twilight view of the Sydney Opera House and Sydney Harbour Bridge
5874c59d4ee7f696b7b0.photo.caption: Looking across the harbor from Mrs Macquaries Point at dusk, twilight paints the Opera House shells and Harbour Bridge in molten gold.
5874c59d4ee7f696b7b0.tip: Whether you board a train, ferry, bus, or light rail, always tap on and tap off! Forget to tap off on a Sydney bus or light rail and the system automatically charges the maximum fare for that route.
5874c59d4ee7f696b7b0.title: Start in The Rocks' cobbled lanes, then stroll Opera House → Royal Botanic Garden → Mrs Macquaries Point for sunset

59ac18d53e0d5c0bf604.s: Images: Covers of places across Japan use woodblock-print-style illustrations. Images of sights, food, and Australian and U.S. states are AI-generated from real-world descriptions to help you recognize each place. They are not photos.

5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.access.0.how: The bus from Shinjuku to Kawaguchiko Station takes about 1 hour 45 minutes and costs about ¥2,000–2,200. Reservations required.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.access.1.how: The JR Fuji Excursion limited express runs directly to Lake Kawaguchi in about 2 hours. All seats are reserved.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.access.2.how: The JR Chuo Line limited express Azusa or Kaiji takes about 1 hour 30 minutes to Kofu.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.foods.0.name: Hoto noodles
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.foods.0.text: Yamanashi's regional hot pot: wide, flat noodles simmered with pumpkin and vegetables in a thick miso broth. The noodles go in uncooked, which makes the broth especially thick. A bowl is warming in winter and filling enough to serve as a full meal.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.foods.0.where: Hoto specialty restaurants around Kawaguchiko Station and in central Kofu
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.foods.1.name: Yoshida udon
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.foods.1.text: Fujiyoshida's udon is thick, firm, and very chewy. The broth combines soy sauce and miso, with cabbage and horse meat, plus a spoonful of spicy suridane seasoning. Many shops open only for lunch.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.foods.2.name: Shingen mochi
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.foods.2.text: Small pieces of sticky rice cake coated in soybean flour and drizzled with brown sugar syrup before eating. Wrapped in a small cloth bundle, it is one of Yamanashi's most common souvenirs. The soybean flour spills easily, so unwrap it and eat it over the cloth.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.foods.2.where: Souvenir shops at Kawaguchiko Station, Kofu Station, and highway service areas
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.foods.3.name: Koshu wine and fruit
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.foods.3.text: The Kofu Basin is Japan's largest producer of peaches and grapes, which are sold along the roads from July–September. White wine made from local Koshu grapes is crisp and on the dry side. Wineries around Katsunuma offer tastings.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.foods.3.where: Wineries and farm stands around Katsunuma and Isawa Onsen
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.intro.0: When people say they're going to see Mt. Fuji, they usually mean the Fuji Five Lakes in Yamanashi. The highway bus from Shinjuku to Lake Kawaguchi takes less than 2 hours. From the lakeshore, Chureito Pagoda, and old villages, you can photograph Fuji head-on. In summer, you can also start the climb from the Yoshida Trail's 5th Station. A day trip feels rushed. Stay one night around Lake Kawaguchi for a much better chance of seeing the mountain the next morning.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.intro.1: The Kofu Basin in northern Yamanashi is known for fruit and wine. Peaches and grapes are sweet and inexpensive in summer, and the fall colors at Shosenkyo Gorge are worth a detour. Popular Fuji viewpoints around the Fuji Five Lakes can get very crowded, and places such as Fujiyoshida have begun restricting access. Follow local rules when taking photos: don't block roads or enter private property.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.name: Yamanashi
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.seasons.note: The air is clearest from November–February, making it the best time to see the mountain. April brings cherry blossoms and moss phlox. Clouds often cover Fuji in summer, but July–September is climbing season.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.sources.0.title: 富士登山オフィシャルサイト: climbing season dates
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.sources.1.title: トラベル Watch: Yoshida Trail reservations and trail fee
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.sources.2.title: 富士急バス: Fuji Five Lakes–Shinjuku route
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.sources.3.title: 富士吉田市観光ガイド: transportation during the Arakurayama Sengen Park cherry blossom season
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.sources.4.title: 富士の国やまなし: 富士芝桜まつり2026
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.0.name: Arakurayama Sengen Park (Chureito Pagoda)
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.0.text: The classic view of a red five-story pagoda, cherry blossoms, and Mt. Fuji is here. From Shimoyoshida Station on the Fujikyu Line, walk about 10 minutes to the foot of the hill, then climb nearly 400 steps to the viewpoint. It looks best during the cherry blossom season in early to mid-April and the fall foliage season in November. On ordinary days, early morning is quieter and the light is softer.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.0.tip: During cherry blossom season, vehicles are banned from nearby roads, and access to the viewpoint is rotated in timed sessions. You may wait 1–3 hours. Do not enter residential alleys nearby to take photos.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.1.name: Lake Kawaguchi (Oishi Park)
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.1.text: The easiest of the Fuji Five Lakes for transportation and accommodation, Lake Kawaguchi offers views of Mt. Fuji across the lake from Oishi Park on the north shore. Lavender blooms from late June through July, while kochia turns red in fall, giving each season a different foreground. Sightseeing buses circle the lake, and you can also rent a bicycle and ride along the shore.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.1.tip: Go early for the best chance of seeing the mountain. Clouds often gather after 10 a.m. Buses around the lake are very crowded on weekends, so leave extra time for the return trip.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.2.name: Oshino Hakkai
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.2.text: Eight spring-fed ponds, formed by Mt. Fuji's snowmelt after years of underground travel. The water is so clear that you can see plants and fish on the bottom. The village has thatched houses and waterwheels, with Mt. Fuji as a backdrop. The site is free and not large; you can see the main ponds in half an hour. Buses run from Kawaguchiko Station and Mt. Fuji Station.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.2.tip: Tour groups crowd the site during the day. Go before 9 a.m. for a quieter visit. The ponds are protected, so don't throw in coins or reach into the water.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.3.name: Mt. Fuji Yoshida Trail
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.3.text: Starting at the Fuji Subaru Line 5th Station, at an elevation of about 2,305 meters, this is the best route for first-time climbers, with the most mountain huts and supply points. The ascent takes about 6 hours. A common plan is to set out in the afternoon, stay at a hut at the 8th Station, then continue before dawn to see the sunrise. The 2026 climbing season runs from July 1 to September 10.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.3.tip: Online reservations and a fee are required. Daily visitor numbers are capped, and a mountain-hut reservation is required for entry from the afternoon through early morning.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.4.name: Saiko Iyashi-no-Sato Nenba
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.4.text: A restored thatched-roof village on the shore of Lake Saiko, with about twenty traditional houses arranged along the slope. Inside are craft workshops, small museums, and teahouses. On clear days, you can see Mt. Fuji from the village entrance. Quieter than Oshino Hakkai, it is a good place to slow down and take photos. After a snowfall, it has the feel of a Japanese folktale. Take the Saiko sightseeing bus from Kawaguchiko Station.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.4.tip: The village has many slopes and stone steps, which become slippery after snow. Wear shoes with good traction.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.5.name: Fuji Shibazakura Festival
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.5.text: The festival venue near Lake Motosu is planted with about 500,000 moss phlox plants. Pink, white, and purple flowers form a vast carpet with Mt. Fuji behind them. The festival runs from mid-April to late May each year, with peak bloom generally around early May. A seasonal shuttle bus runs from Kawaguchiko Station and takes about 40 minutes.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.5.tip: Traffic is very heavy during Golden Week (late April to early May), so avoid it if possible. Flower conditions are updated daily on the official website.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.6.name: Shosenkyo Gorge
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.6.text: This granite gorge north of Kofu has a riverside trail that takes about 1 hour. Strange rock formations and pine trees line the gorge, ending at the 30-meter-high Sengataki Waterfall. You can also take a cable car to the summit for views of Mt. Fuji and the Southern Alps. The gorge is most beautiful in November, when the leaves change. Combine it with fruit and winery visits in Kofu for a full day. Buses run from Kofu Station.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.6.tip: Walking from downstream to upstream is easier. Take a bus back to Kofu near the waterfall.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.7.name: Fuji-Q Highland
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.7.text: This amusement park is famous for its extreme roller coasters. Several major rides have held world records, and the park also has a haunted house billed as one of the world's most difficult. The park sits beside Mt. Fuji, which you can see from the top of a roller coaster. The Fujikyu Line has a station with the same name, just one stop from Kawaguchiko Station.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.spots.7.tip: Popular rides can have very long lines, so enter early on weekends. Some roller coasters stop operating in high winds.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.stay: Stay near Kawaguchiko Station or at a hot-spring ryokan on the lake's north shore. Buses and sightseeing buses leave from Kawaguchiko Station, and north-shore rooms often offer views of Mt. Fuji across the lake. For a lower budget, stay around Mt. Fuji Station.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.tagline: Mt. Fuji's closest side trip from Tokyo: the Fuji Five Lakes, Chureito Pagoda, and trailheads
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.tips.0: Mt. Fuji is often hidden by clouds. Set aside at least one morning specifically for mountain views instead of relying on a single afternoon.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.tips.1: Buses around Lake Kawaguchi and the Fuji Excursion limited express fill up during peak season. Reserve seats in advance for both directions.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.tips.2: Driving rules in Japan depend on your licence and required documents. Check the official requirements before driving; between the Fuji Five Lakes, use sightseeing buses or a one-day tour.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.tips.3: Popular viewpoints are also residential areas. Don't take photos in the middle of the road, linger where you block people, or litter.
5a0276ab0881c3a4fc09.tips.4: Bring a headlamp, warm clothing, and rain gear for the climb. Even in summer, temperatures near the summit can approach 0℃.

5b40c7b8810ee99ce550.cost: JR Limited Express ~¥2,600; Usuzan Ropeway round-trip ~¥2,000
5b40c7b8810ee99ce550.location: JR Toya → 20 min Donan Bus → Toyako Onsen & Mt. Usu
5b40c7b8810ee99ce550.paragraphs.0: A quick 40-minute Hokuto ride south brings you to JR Toya, where another timed Donan Bus drops you right along Toyako Onsen. As Japan's northernmost ice-free volcanic caldera lake, Lake Toya feels calmer and more serene than Noboribetsu—deep indigo water framing Nakajima Island and snowy Mount Yotei rising like a northern Mount Fuji.
5b40c7b8810ee99ce550.paragraphs.1: On clear mornings, take a bus or 15-minute taxi to Showa Shinzan for the Mt. Usu Ropeway: in minutes you're overlooking smoking rust-red Showa Shinzan on one side and mirror-calm Lake Toya on the other. Pick a lakefront onsen hotel (like Nonokaze or Kohantei) for a rooftop infinity bath facing the water—and in early February (2), Lake Toya's winter fireworks explode right above the steam.
5b40c7b8810ee99ce550.phase: Step 04 · Day 4 Noboribetsu → Quiet Lake Toya
5b40c7b8810ee99ce550.photo.alt: Snow-blanketed Hokkaido winter outdoor hot-spring valley
5b40c7b8810ee99ce550.photo.caption: Central Hokkaido winter retreats always come down to deep snow and rising hot-spring steam—whether by Lake Toya or Jozankei valley, soaking in the snow heals everything.
5b40c7b8810ee99ce550.tip: Donan Buses serving Noboribetsu and Toya run every 30–60 minutes synced to JR Hokuto arrivals—walk straight out to the bus stop after getting off the train rather than lingering on the platform.
5b40c7b8810ee99ce550.title: Head South to Ice-Free Lake Toya: Ride the Mt. Usu Ropeway & Soak Facing Snowy Caldera Peaks

5df8ed3df540eb34e929.cover.caption: Be first through Eikando's gates at 08:30 for the golden 20 minutes when morning sun ignites crimson maples over a glass-still Hojo Pond—well worth losing 1 hour of sleep.
5df8ed3df540eb34e929.excerpt: In late November, Eikando, Nanzen-ji, and Tofuku-ji are Kyoto's three most mobbed autumn icons. Setting my alarm 1 hour earlier and taking the Tozai Subway Line to Keage got me mirror-still reflections at Hojo Pond—and a relaxed yudofu lunch before the rush.

5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.access.0.how: Nankai rapi:t takes about 35–40 minutes to Namba, with a separate limited express surcharge. The Airport Express takes about 45 minutes with no extra charge. JR HARUKA takes about 50 minutes to Shin-Osaka.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.access.1.how: The JR Special Rapid takes about 30 minutes to Osaka Station. The Hankyu train from Kyoto-Kawaramachi to Osaka-Umeda takes about 45 minutes.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.access.2.how: The Tokaido Shinkansen Nozomi takes about 2 hours 30 minutes to Shin-Osaka. Transfer to the subway or JR to reach central Osaka.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.access.3.how: This is a domestic airport. The airport bus takes about 25–30 minutes to Umeda.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.0.name: Takoyaki
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.0.text: Chunks of octopus are cooked in batter and turned into balls on a griddle. The outside is lightly crisp, while the inside is soft and piping hot. Osaka locals eat them as a snack, usually topped with sauce, mayonnaise, and aonori. Some shops serve them with only dashi.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.0.where: Street stalls around Dotonbori and Namba. You'll also find them throughout Shinsekai and Umeda.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.1.name: Okonomiyaki
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.1.text: Cabbage and batter are cooked into a thick pancake on a griddle, then topped with sweet sauce and mayonnaise. Many restaurants cook it on the griddle in front of you, and you cut it into pieces with a small spatula. It's hot, filling, and perfect with beer.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.1.where: Long-running restaurants and chains around Namba, Shinsaibashi, and Umeda's underground malls.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.2.name: Kushikatsu
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.2.text: Meat, seafood, and vegetables are coated in fine breadcrumbs, deep-fried, and served on skewers with dipping sauce. Shinsekai is where the dish originated, and the restaurants are lively. Cabbage helps cut the richness. Skewers start at a little over ¥100 each.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.2.where: Most concentrated around Shinsekai, with branches in Namba and Umeda.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.3.name: Kitsune udon
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.3.text: Osaka is the birthplace of kitsune udon. Sweet fried tofu sits on soft, smooth udon noodles in a kombu-and-bonito broth. The broth is light in color but full of flavor, completely different from the darker soy-based broth of the Kanto region.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.3.where: Long-running udon shops in Shinsaibashi and Namba. You can also find it at standing noodle shops in stations.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.4.name: 551 Horai pork buns
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.4.text: These pork buns are a childhood staple for many Osaka locals, with thick, fluffy dough and juicy pork filling with a hint of onion sweetness. The chain only operates in Kansai. At the Nankai-Shin-Osaka and Osaka stations, most people waiting in line are locals buying them as gifts to take home.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.foods.4.where: The Namba main store, Shin-Osaka Station, Osaka Station, and the basements of major department stores.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.intro.0: Osaka is Kansai's liveliest city. The main draw isn't historic sites but eating and exploring: Dotonbori's neon, Kuromon Market's seafood, and Shinsekai's kushikatsu. There's something to eat from morning to night. People speak their minds, prices are more reasonable than in Kyoto, and it's an easy place to stay on your first trip to Japan.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.intro.1: The city has two main areas: Umeda in the north has major stations, department stores, and skyscrapers, while Namba and Shinsaibashi in the south are best for food and shopping. Osaka Castle sits between them, and Universal Studios Japan is on the western waterfront. Stay in the middle and Kyoto, Nara, and Kobe are all within an hour, making Osaka an ideal Kansai base.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.name: Osaka
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.seasons.note: Spring and fall are the most comfortable. July–August is hot and humid, making outdoor lines tough. Winters are mild, and there are plenty of holiday light displays at the end of the year.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.sources.0.title: Osaka Prefecture: Osaka Prefecture accommodation tax
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.sources.1.title: Nankai Electric Railway: New limited express fares from April 1, 2026
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.sources.2.title: JR West: WEST QR HARUKA One-way Ticket
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.sources.3.title: Wikipedia: Osaka Castle keep
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.0.name: Dotonbori & Shinsaibashi
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.0.text: Osaka's most iconic streetscape has giant signs along the river, including the Glico Running Man. You can eat everything from takoyaki to ramen along one street. Shinsaibashi's covered shopping arcade continues north, so you can browse even in the rain. The neon is best after dark, and you can see it from the water on a Dotonbori river cruise.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.0.tip: Ebisu Bridge in front of the Glico sign gets very crowded at night. Keep an eye on your belongings.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.1.name: Kuromon Market
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.1.text: This old market next to Namba now caters mainly to tourists. You can eat grilled seafood, wagyu skewers, oysters, and fruit as you walk. Prices are considerably higher than at supermarkets, so treat it as a food-and-browsing experience. It's about a 10-minute walk from Dotonbori, making it easy to visit both together.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.1.tip: By 10–11 a.m., most shops are open and the market isn't too crowded. Many vendors close in the early evening.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.2.name: Osaka Castle
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.2.text: This famous castle was built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The current keep is a reinforced-concrete reconstruction from 1931, with a history museum inside and city views from the top floor. The huge stone walls, moat, and park outside are more impressive. Nishinomaru Garden is a popular cherry blossom spot, and a yakatabune boat ride around the moat is another good option.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.2.tip: The castle keep has an elevator, but lines are often long. If you only want a photo of the keep, the park is free and you can simply walk around it.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.3.name: Shinsekai & Tsutenkaku
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.3.text: This downtown neighborhood retains a Showa-era feel, with colorful signs, kushikatsu restaurants, and Tsutenkaku Tower in the middle. Come during the day for kushikatsu and old-fashioned streets. Tennoji Park and Abeno Harukas, one of Japan's tallest buildings, are nearby. Go up toward evening for city views after dark.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.3.tip: Some nearby areas can feel rough at night. Stick to main streets when walking back to the station.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.4.name: Umeda Sky Building
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.4.text: The two towers are linked at the top by the open-air Kuchu Teien Observatory, which offers 360-degree views of Osaka at night. It's a roughly 10-minute walk from Osaka Station. A retro-style restaurant street is underground. Come up after dark after browsing Umeda's department stores and station complex.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.4.tip: Go up about 30 minutes before sunset to see both the evening sky and the city lights.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.5.fee: Varies by date; buy in advance on the official website
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.5.name: Universal Studios Japan
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.5.text: Super Nintendo World and The Wizarding World of Harry Potter are both here, and you'll need at least a full day. From Osaka Station, take JR about 15 minutes to Universal City Station. Ticket prices vary by date, with weekends and holidays being both more expensive and more crowded. If you want to ride many popular attractions, consider buying an Express Pass.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.5.tip: Entering Super Nintendo World often requires a timed-entry ticket. Get one through the official app as soon as you enter the park.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.6.name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.6.text: This world-class aquarium has whale sharks in its main tank. The route spirals down from the top, making you feel as if you're diving into the Pacific. It's highly recommended for families with children. The Tempozan Ferris Wheel is right outside. From Osakako Station on the Chuo Line, it's a 5–10-minute walk.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.6.tip: It is less crowded in the evening. Booking an entry time online can save you from waiting in line.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.7.name: Sumiyoshi Taisha
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.7.text: One of Osaka's oldest shrines, Sumiyoshi Taisha has several main halls designated as National Treasures and preserves an ancient shrine style from before the arrival of Buddhism. The steep vermilion Sorihashi Bridge at the entrance is the main photo spot. It gets far fewer visitors than Kyoto's shrines and is about 10 minutes from Namba by Nankai train.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.7.tip: This is one of Osaka's busiest places for hatsumode around New Year's. It's best to avoid that period.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.8.name: Expo '70 Commemorative Park
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.8.text: This is the former site of the 1970 Osaka Expo. Taro Okamoto's Tower of the Sun stands dramatically in the middle of the lawn. The large park offers seasonal flowers, including cherry blossoms in spring, poppies in early summer, and cosmos and fall foliage in autumn. From Umeda, take the subway and transfer to the monorail; the trip takes about 40 minutes.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.8.tip: You need to book online in advance to visit the inside of the Tower of the Sun.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.9.name: Minoh Falls
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.9.text: This easy hike is in the northern Osaka suburbs. From Hankyu Minoh Station, follow the valley about 3 km to the 33-meter waterfall, passing woods and small temples along the way. The scenery is best during the November foliage season. Shops along the route sell deep-fried maple leaves, which are crisp and sweet like cookies. The trip from Umeda by Hankyu takes about 30 minutes.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.spots.9.tip: There are wild monkeys in the mountains. Don't wave food around or feed them.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.stay: Namba and Shinsaibashi are best if you want to eat and shop every day, and they're convenient for Kansai International Airport. Umeda and Osaka Station are better for frequent trips to Kyoto and Kobe. The two areas are 10 minutes apart on the Midosuji Line.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.tagline: Kansai's home base for food, fun, and shopping
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.tips.0: At kushikatsu restaurants, dip each skewer in the communal sauce only once. Don't put a bitten skewer back in. Use a cabbage leaf to add more sauce.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.tips.1: On Osaka escalators, stand on the right and let people pass on the left—the opposite of Tokyo.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.tips.2: Osaka Prefecture accommodation tax: about ¥200–500 per person per night for rooms costing ¥5,000 or more. Pay it separately at check-in.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.tips.3: Osaka Station in Umeda and the connected subway and private railway stations form a maze. Allow an extra 10–15 minutes for transfers.
5e6f2a62f0ecac46f80e.tips.4: If you want to visit several paid attractions in one day, look into the Osaka Amazing Pass. For simply eating, shopping, and getting around, use an ICOCA card.

5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.access.0.how: The JR Biwako Line reaches Otsu in about 10 minutes. Special Rapid trains take about 35 minutes to Omi-Hachiman and about 50 minutes to Hikone.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.access.1.how: Direct JR Special Rapid trains run from Osaka Station to Hikone in about 1 hour 20 minutes, passing through Kyoto.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.access.2.how: Take the Tokaido Shinkansen to Maibara in about 30 minutes, then transfer to a JR train for 1 stop to Hikone.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.foods.0.name: Omi beef
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.foods.0.text: One of Japan’s three great wagyu varieties, Omi beef has the longest history of cattle raising. Its fat tastes sweet without feeling greasy. Try it as sukiyaki or teppanyaki, or pick up Omi beef croquettes and beef nigiri in Omi-Hachiman or Hikone.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.foods.0.where: Specialty restaurants in Omi-Hachiman, Hikone’s castle town, and the Otsu area.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.foods.1.name: Funazushi
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.foods.1.text: Made by fermenting Lake Biwa crucian carp with salt and rice for more than a year, funazushi is sushi’s oldest form. It has a pungent smell and a sour, salty, cheese-like taste. Eat small bites with sake, and order it if you feel adventurous.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.foods.1.where: Long-established shops in Otsu and Takashima and lakeside restaurants, usually served in small portions of sliced fish.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.foods.2.name: Baumkuchen
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.foods.2.text: An Omi-Hachiman confectionery brand has made freshly baked baumkuchen its signature: crisp on the outside and moist within. Its La Collina Omihachiman shop on the outskirts has a grass-covered roof, and many people come just to photograph it.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.foods.2.where: La Collina Omihachiman (about 10 minutes by bus from Omi-Hachiman Station).
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.intro.0: Lake Biwa, Japan’s largest lake, covers almost half of Shiga. Just over the mountains from Kyoto, Otsu is only 10 minutes away by JR train. Highlights include Hikone Castle, a National Treasure, Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei, the waterways of Omi-Hachiman, and a torii gate standing in the lake, all with far fewer crowds than Kyoto.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.intro.1: Shiga makes an easy day trip from Kyoto or a change of pace during a longer stay there. Spend a day in Hikone and Omi-Hachiman on the east shore, and another at Shirahige Shrine and Mount Hiei on the west shore. The north gets snow in winter, while lakeside cherry blossoms in spring and fall foliage are both lovely.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.name: Shiga
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.seasons.note: Early April brings cherry blossoms at Hikone Castle, and November brings fall colors to Mount Hiei. Snow blankets the northern lakeshore in winter, when you can see the metasequoia avenue covered in white.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.sources.0.title: Hikone Castle official website
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.sources.1.title: Wikipedia: Hikone Castle
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.0.name: Hikone Castle
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.0.text: One of only five castle keeps in Japan designated as National Treasures, this compact, elegant wooden keep survives from more than four hundred years ago. The top floor overlooks Lake Biwa. About a thousand cherry trees line the moat, making spring especially beautiful. Nearby Genkyuen Garden offers views of the keep reflected in its pond, and the mascot Hikonyan appears at scheduled times each day in the castle grounds.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.0.tip: The stairs inside the keep are nearly 60 degrees steep. You must remove your shoes, so wear socks that are comfortable to walk in.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.1.name: Omi-Hachiman
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.1.text: The hometown of Edo-period Omi merchants, Omi-Hachiman has white-walled storehouses and stone steps lining the Hachiman-bori canal. A ride through the reeds in a hand-rowed boat feels like stepping into a period drama. You can visit merchant houses in the old town and enjoy the greenery at nearby Himure Hachimangu Shrine. The popular dessert destination La Collina Omihachiman is on the outskirts.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.1.tip: The old town is about 7 minutes by bus or about 30 minutes on foot from JR Omi-Hachiman Station.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.2.name: Shirahige Shrine’s lakeside torii
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.2.text: A vermilion torii stands in the water off Lake Biwa’s west shore, backed by open water and distant mountains. Most beautiful at sunrise, it is known as the “Itsukushima of Omi.” The shrine itself is small; allow about half an hour to see the torii. Walk about 40 minutes from JR Omi-Takashima Station or take a taxi.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.2.tip: A national highway with fast-moving traffic separates the shrine from the lake. Do not cross it to take photos.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.3.name: Enryaku-ji
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.3.text: The head temple of Japan’s Tendai Buddhist school and a World Heritage Site, Enryaku-ji spans Mount Hiei. Its three areas—Todo, Saito, and Yokawa—sit among deep, quiet woods. The “eternal flame” in the Konpon Chudo hall is said to have burned for more than twelve hundred years. The mountain overlooks Lake Biwa and has beautiful fall foliage. You can take a cable car up from Sakamoto.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.3.tip: Use the mountain buses to travel between the three areas. Service is reduced in winter, so check before setting out.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.4.name: Makino Metasequoia Avenue
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.4.text: About 500 metasequoia trees line this roughly 2.4-kilometer road. Their colors change with the seasons: fresh green in spring, deep green in summer, orange-brown in fall, and a white tunnel after winter snow. About 10 minutes by bus or taxi from JR Makino Station, it suits anyone willing to go a little farther for photos.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.4.tip: This is a road open to traffic. Take photos from the sidewalk and stay out of the road.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.5.name: Miho Museum
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.5.text: Designed by I. M. Pei, this mountain museum draws on the idea of the “Peach Blossom Spring,” a hidden paradise. You pass along a cherry-lined path, through a stainless-steel tunnel, and across a suspension bridge before reaching the galleries. The architecture is the main attraction, with a collection of ancient artifacts from East and West. Buses from JR Ishiyama Station take about 50 minutes and run infrequently.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.spots.5.tip: The museum closes for an extended period in winter and between exhibitions. Check exhibition dates on the official website and the bus schedule before setting out.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.stay: Most visitors stay in Kyoto and come for the day. For a lakeside stay, choose a hotel with lake views in Otsu or stay at Ogoto Onsen. You can enjoy Lake Biwa after dark, and Kyoto is only about half an hour away.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.tagline: Old castle towns and mountain temples by Lake Biwa
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.tips.0: JR Special Rapid trains are the easiest way to reach Shiga. You do not need a limited express ticket when traveling from Kyoto.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.tips.1: Lake Biwa is huge. Choose either the east or west shore for a day trip; do not try to circle the whole lake in a day.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.tips.2: The northern lakeshore gets heavy snow in winter. Check the weather and train service before heading to Makino or Nagahama.
5e924c7dd1c3ba27f353.tips.3: Driving along the lake is enjoyable, but whether you can drive in Japan depends on your license. Check the official requirements. You can also explore by train and bus.

5edd522035ae5eea61d0.location: New Chitose Domestic Terminal 2F & 3F (8 min indoor walk from International)
5edd522035ae5eea61d0.paragraphs.0: New Chitose is the one airport in Japan people happily arrive half a day early for. Before checking bags at International (remember 2026's airport tax-free KIOSK check first!), walk 8 minutes through the indoor link to Domestic Terminal 2F–3F: freshly baked Kinotoya cheese tarts, Kitakaro puffs, Rokkatei butter sandwiches, LeTAO, and over 20 dairy-direct milk soft-serve counters all live under one roof.
5edd522035ae5eea61d0.paragraphs.1: Grab lunch on 3F at Hokkaido Ramen Dojo—Ebisoba Ichigen shrimp ramen, Baikohken soy ramen, and Shirakaba Sanso miso ramen sit side by side—then peek into Doraemon Wakuwaku Sky Park or Royce Chocolate World. Leave 50 minutes to walk back for International security and end your snow trip on a sweet high.
5edd522035ae5eea61d0.phase: Step 06 · Day 5 The Ultimate 3 Hours at New Chitose Airport
5edd522035ae5eea61d0.tip: Fresh puddings, nama chocolate with ice packs, and soft custards from Domestic 2F can count as liquids/gels at International security—ask clerks whether your items must go inside checked luggage.
5edd522035ae5eea61d0.title: Treat New Chitose as Your Final Stop: Domestic Ramen Dojo, Farm Soft-Serve & All Hokkaido Sweets

5fd63cc175b0b410b52a.cost: Coastal walk free; Icebergs Pool swim/entry ~A$9
5fd63cc175b0b410b52a.duration: ~2.5–3 hours at a photo-friendly pace (6 km)
5fd63cc175b0b410b52a.paragraphs.0: Hop on bus 333 straight from Circular Quay in the morning (or ride the T4 train to Bondi Junction and transfer seamlessly to the 333, about 35 minutes total), and step off into South Pacific sunshine, surfboards, and rolling whitewater. Walk to the southern end of the sand to the famed Bondi Icebergs Pool: the upper terrace gives you a free bird's-eye shot of ocean surf crashing into the bright blue lap lanes, and if you packed swimwear, paying under 10 Australian dollars for a few laps is pure magic.
5fd63cc175b0b410b52a.paragraphs.1: From there, hit the 6 km Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk. Hugging dramatic golden sandstone cliffs almost the entire way, the path curves into a fresh secret cove every ten or fifteen minutes—surfer-packed Tamarama, picnic- and snorkel-friendly Bronte with its free natural rock pool, scenic cliffside Waverley Cemetery—before finishing at wide-open Coogee Beach, where you can kick off your shoes in the surf, grab an iced latte, and bus easily back to the city.
5fd63cc175b0b410b52a.phase: Step 03 · Day 3 morning: Bondi Beach & the 6 km cliff walk
5fd63cc175b0b410b52a.photo.alt: Golden sandstone cliffside boardwalk on Sydney's Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk
5fd63cc175b0b410b52a.photo.caption: The 6 km cliff trail from Bondi to Coogee strings together Sydney's best shoreline—every bend shifts the ocean into a new shade of blue.
5fd63cc175b0b410b52a.tip: There is almost no tall shade along the trail. Beyond SPF50+ sunscreen, sunglasses, and a cap, bring a 500ml refillable bottle—free chilled drinking-water fountains appear roughly every 1 km so you can top up anytime.
5fd63cc175b0b410b52a.title: Take the 333 beach express straight to Bondi Icebergs, then walk south along one of the world's finest urban coastlines

60fd04456d3dce311d26.access.0.how: The Sanyo Shinkansen takes about 1 hour 20–40 minutes from Shin-Osaka to Hiroshima Station, depending on the train
60fd04456d3dce311d26.access.1.how: The airport bus takes about 50 minutes to Hiroshima Station Shinkansen Exit and costs about ¥1,500
60fd04456d3dce311d26.access.2.how: The Shinkansen takes about 1 hour from Hakata to Hiroshima Station
60fd04456d3dce311d26.access.3.how: Take the JR Sanyo Line about 30 minutes to Miyajimaguchi, then take a ferry for about 10 minutes. The ferry costs about ¥200, plus an admission tax of about ¥100
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.0.name: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.0.text: The biggest difference from Osaka-style okonomiyaki is the layering. A thin crepe-like batter is topped with plenty of cabbage, bean sprouts, and pork, followed by yakisoba and an egg. Watch the cook work at the griddle and eat it straight from the hot plate with a small spatula for the classic experience.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.0.where: Restaurants are concentrated in the food floors in and around Hiroshima Station and around Okonomimura downtown
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.1.name: Hiroshima oysters
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.1.text: Hiroshima is Japan's top oyster-producing prefecture, and the oysters are plumpest from November to February of the following year. Miyajima's Omotesando Shopping Street has freshly grilled oysters, as well as fried oysters and oyster rice. If you have a sensitive stomach, go easy on raw oysters and choose grilled or fried instead.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.1.where: Omotesando Shopping Street on Miyajima and izakayas in Hiroshima
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.2.name: Anago meshi
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.2.text: A Miyajima specialty: grilled conger eel with a lightly charred aroma over rice seasoned with sauce. It is milder than eel rice and still tastes good cold. Many people buy a bento near Miyajimaguchi and eat it on the ferry.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.2.where: Near the Miyajimaguchi ferry terminal and on Miyajima
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.3.name: Momiji manju
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.3.text: These small maple-leaf-shaped cakes traditionally contain red bean paste, but you can also find flavors such as custard, matcha, and cheese. Miyajima sells freshly baked versions, as well as battered and deep-fried agemomiji. Eat them hot.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.3.where: Omotesando Shopping Street on Miyajima and the souvenir area at Hiroshima Station
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.4.name: Onomichi ramen
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.4.text: This ramen has a clear soy sauce broth dotted with pork back fat and flat noodles. It tastes lighter than it looks. A bowl is just the thing after walking Onomichi's slopes.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.foods.4.where: Around the area between Onomichi Station and Onomichi Hondori Shopping Street
60fd04456d3dce311d26.intro.0: Hiroshima Prefecture lies on the Seto Inland Sea in western Honshu. Its two best-known sights are the Atomic Bomb Dome and Peace Memorial Park, and the great torii gate on the sea at Miyajima. Both are World Heritage sites, and each is less than 1 hour from Hiroshima Station. If this is your first trip to western Japan, Hiroshima is an easy place to start.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.intro.1: With two extra days, head east to the seaside historic districts of Onomichi and Tomonoura, or cycle from Onomichi across the islands to Shikoku on the Shimanami Kaido. The pace is slower than in Tokyo or Osaka, and the food is hearty: layered Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki cooked on a griddle, and oysters in winter, are worth a special trip.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.name: Hiroshima
60fd04456d3dce311d26.seasons.note: Cherry blossoms are best in early April, and fall colors peak in mid- to late November. Winter is oyster season. Hotels fill up around August 6 because of the many memorial events.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.sources.0.title: Hatsukaichi City: Miyajima admission tax information
60fd04456d3dce311d26.sources.1.title: Itsukushima Shrine official site: Visiting hours and entrance fees
60fd04456d3dce311d26.sources.2.title: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum official site
60fd04456d3dce311d26.sources.3.title: Miyajima Ropeway official site: Fares
60fd04456d3dce311d26.sources.4.title: Hiroshima Airport: Bus schedules to Hiroshima Station
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.0.fee: About ¥300 to enter the shrine buildings
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.0.name: Itsukushima Shrine
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.0.text: The great torii gate on the sea and vermilion corridors are Miyajima's signature sights. At high tide, the gate appears to float on the water; at low tide, you can walk to its base. Both views are worth seeing, so check the tide chart before you go. Walking around the shrine buildings takes about 30 minutes. Do not feed the deer on the island. They may snatch paper bags and maps.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.0.tip: The shrine is quietest after the day-trippers leave in the evening. The torii gate is lit up after dark, so staying overnight is well worth it.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.1.fee: About ¥2,000 round trip on the ropeway
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.1.name: Mount Misen
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.1.text: Miyajima's highest peak offers views of the many islands of the Seto Inland Sea. The easiest route is to take the Miyajima Ropeway to Shishiiwa Station, then walk about 30 minutes to the summit. If you are fit, you can hike up from Momijidani Park in about 1.5 hours. In fall, Momijidani turns bright red and is at its most beautiful.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.1.tip: The ropeway's last downhill departure is around 16:30, so do not linger too long at the summit. The trail has many steps; wear athletic shoes.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.2.name: Peace Memorial Park
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.2.text: The Atomic Bomb Dome stands across the river much as it did after the 1945 bombing. The Peace Memorial Museum is at the south end of the park. Its exhibits are frank and difficult, so allow plenty of time to take them in. From Hiroshima Station, take the streetcar to Atomic Bomb Dome-mae Station; the ride takes about 15 minutes. The park and dome are free.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.2.tip: From 7:30–8:30 in the morning, the museum admits only visitors with online reservation tickets, so it is much less crowded.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.3.name: Shukkeien Garden
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.3.text: This strolling garden was built for the lords of Hiroshima. It is about a 15-minute walk from Hiroshima Station. Though compact, it is finely designed, and a walk around the pond takes about 40 minutes. Cherry blossoms in spring and fall colors in late November are the highlights. The garden was destroyed in the bombing and has been gradually restored since the war.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.4.name: Onomichi slopes and Senko-ji
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.4.text: This port town is packed with temples and old houses on the hillsides. Take the ropeway up to Senko-ji Park for views of the Onomichi Channel, then walk downhill along stone steps and lanes where cats roam. Onomichi is also the starting point for the Shimanami Kaido. Stay the night before and set out early the next morning for an easy start.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.4.tip: The slopes are all steps, so do not take your luggage uphill. Leave your bags at Onomichi Station first.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.5.name: Kosan-ji Temple and Miraishin no Oka
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.5.text: This unusual temple on Ikuchijima was built by an industrialist in memory of his mother. Its vivid buildings imitate famous structures from Nikko, Kyoto, and elsewhere. Behind the temple, Miraishin no Oka is a large collection of white marble sculptures that look striking under a blue sky. Come by boat from Onomichi or cycle over on the Shimanami Kaido. On the way, explore Setoda's old shopping street and try a lemon dessert.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.6.name: Okunoshima (Rabbit Island)
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.6.text: Hundreds of wild rabbits roam this island. The ferry from the pier beside JR Tadanoumi Station takes about 15 minutes. During World War II, the island secretly produced poison gas; ruins and a poison gas museum remain. The rabbit population has fallen noticeably in recent years. Do not hold or chase the rabbits. Put food on the ground and take away anything they do not finish.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.6.tip: The island has only one resort hotel and limited supplies. Bring water and rabbit food before you leave.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.7.name: Tomonoura
60fd04456d3dce311d26.spots.7.text: This old port town on the Seto Inland Sea still has stone night lanterns and a stepped pier much as they appeared in the Edo period. It also helped inspire Hayao Miyazaki's Ponyo. The bus from Fukuyama Station takes about 30 minutes. Half a day is ideal, and you can take a ferry for a few minutes to nearby Sensui Island.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.stay: For a first visit, stay around Hiroshima Station, where you can catch the Shinkansen, airport buses, and JR trains to Miyajima. To see the great torii gate without the crowds, spend a night on Miyajima. Onomichi is a good starting point for a Shimanami Kaido cycling trip.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.tagline: See two World Heritage sites—the Atomic Bomb Dome and the great torii gate on the sea—in one day
60fd04456d3dce311d26.tips.0: The ferry to Miyajima charges an additional admission tax of about ¥100. It is collected with the ferry fare, or deducted automatically when you tap a transit card at the gate.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.tips.1: The keep at Hiroshima Castle closed on March 22, 2026. You can no longer go inside, but you can view it from outside and explore Ninomaru.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.tips.2: Streetcars operated by Hiroden are the easiest way to get between sights in the city. Transit cards can be used directly.
60fd04456d3dce311d26.tips.3: Staying overnight on Miyajima lets you see the great torii gate in the quiet of evening and early morning. It is a much better experience than a day trip.
