623dbc557c37cfb4fde1.cost: Full eligible tax refunded (some third-party processors deduct a small fee)
623dbc557c37cfb4fde1.duration: Refunds typically post in 3–14 business days after departure
623dbc557c37cfb4fde1.location: Narita Express (N'EX) / Keisei Skyliner / Nankai Rapi:t
623dbc557c37cfb4fde1.paragraphs.0: Once you clear the customs KIOSK and fly out, refunds to credit cards or e-wallets (such as WeChat Pay or Alipay) generally arrive within 3 to 14 business days. Hold onto your paper receipts, J-TaxRefund screenshots, and boarding pass until the deposit clears—if a bank delay requires a follow-up claim, those transaction IDs are your only proof.
623dbc557c37cfb4fde1.paragraphs.1: One last transit tip for departure day: afternoon reserved seats on the Keisei Skyliner and N'EX from Tokyo—or the Nankai Rapi:t from Osaka Namba—routinely sell out an hour ahead during foliage, sakura, and ski peaks. Reserve your seat on your phone or at a ticket machine before hotel checkout so you don't burn precious customs-kiosk buffer waiting for the next train.
623dbc557c37cfb4fde1.phase: Step 06 · Track your payout & book express seats early
623dbc557c37cfb4fde1.photo.alt: Golden sunset sky over a river bridge seen from an airport express train leaving Tokyo
623dbc557c37cfb4fde1.photo.caption: Catching the airport express 1 hour earlier leaves breathing room for tax verification and last-minute terminal snacks—turning a frantic dash into an easy send-off.
623dbc557c37cfb4fde1.tip: When department stores route card refunds through third-party operators like Global Blue or Pie VAT, expect a service fee of roughly 1.1%–1.55% deducted from the payout—it's standard policy, not a billing error.
623dbc557c37cfb4fde1.title: Keep verification records until the refund lands, and lock in airport express seats before rush hour

63b6e32895bb9677383a.access.0.how: The Meitetsu μSky takes about 29 minutes to Meitetsu Nagoya and costs about ¥1,430; the limited express takes about 38 minutes and costs about ¥980
63b6e32895bb9677383a.access.1.how: The Tokaido Shinkansen Nozomi takes about 1 hour 40 minutes
63b6e32895bb9677383a.access.2.how: The shinkansen takes about 35 minutes from Kyoto to Nagoya and about 50 minutes from Shin-Osaka
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.0.name: Hitsumabushi
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.0.text: Grilled eel is cut into small pieces and served over rice, then eaten in four ways: plain, with green onions and nori, as ochazuke with dashi poured over it, and finally in whichever style you prefer. The eel is grilled without steaming, giving it crisp skin.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.0.where: Long-established eel restaurants around Atsuta Jingu, Nagoya Station, and Sakae
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.1.name: Miso katsu
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.1.text: A fried pork cutlet topped with a dark sauce made from Hatcho miso. The sauce is rich, sweet, and salty, and the dish comes with rice and shredded cabbage. Nagoya locals use this soybean miso in many dishes.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.1.where: Tonkatsu restaurants around Nagoya Station, Yabacho, and Osu
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.2.name: Nagoya-style chicken wings
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.2.text: Chicken wings are fried until crisp, brushed with a sweet-and-spicy sauce, and covered with pepper and sesame seeds. They're a classic beer snack. To eat them, pull the joint apart and strip the meat off in one bite.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.2.where: Izakaya around Sakae and Nagoya Station
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.3.name: Kishimen
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.3.text: These broad, flat noodles are smooth and easy to eat, served in bonito broth with fried tofu and fish cake. There are standing noodle shops on the shinkansen platforms at Nagoya Station, making them convenient for a quick bowl before your train.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.3.where: The shinkansen platforms at Nagoya Station and noodle shops around the city
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.4.name: Nagoya morning set
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.4.price: About ¥500–700, the price of a coffee
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.4.text: At Nagoya cafés, ordering a coffee in the morning often comes with thick toast and a boiled egg. Some also include Ogura toast with sweet red bean paste. Locals sometimes make a special weekend trip for morning coffee.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.foods.4.where: Kissaten cafés around the city, generally served before 11 a.m.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.intro.0: Aichi's center is Nagoya, Japan's fourth-largest city. It's often said to have little to offer, but it's a practical base for travelers: Chubu Centrair International Airport has many flights to China, and it's convenient for reaching Takayama, Shirakawa-go, Kanazawa, and Ise. One or two days is enough for the city. Highlights include Nagoya Castle, Atsuta Jingu, Osu Shopping District, and Nagoya specialties such as hitsumabushi and miso katsu.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.intro.1: Outside the city are several places worth a separate trip: Inuyama Castle and its old castle town, Ghibli Park with scenes recreated from the films, Korankei Gorge covered in fall foliage, and the pottery town of Tokoname. Aichi is the birthplace of Toyota, so fans of machines and cars can add the Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.name: Aichi
63b6e32895bb9677383a.seasons.note: Early April: cherry blossoms at Nagoya Castle and Inuyama Castle. Mid- to late November: fall foliage at Korankei Gorge. Summers are hot and humid, so plan some indoor sights.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.sources.0.title: Nagoya Castle official site
63b6e32895bb9677383a.sources.1.title: National Treasure Inuyama Castle official site
63b6e32895bb9677383a.sources.2.title: Ghibli Park tickets
63b6e32895bb9677383a.sources.3.title: Meitetsu transfer search (Chubu Centrair International Airport → Meitetsu Nagoya)
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.0.name: Nagoya Castle
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.0.text: This massive castle was built by Tokugawa Ieyasu for his son. Its roof is topped with golden shachihoko, mythical creatures with tiger heads and carp bodies. The reinforced-concrete keep is currently closed for a planned wooden reconstruction, so you can't go inside, but you can still photograph the exterior. The real highlight is the Honmaru Palace, restored in 2018 and filled with dazzling wall paintings. Admission is included.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.0.tip: The last entry to Honmaru Palace is at 4 p.m. It takes about 10 minutes to walk there from the main gate, so don't arrive too late.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.1.name: Atsuta Jingu
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.1.text: This ancient shrine enshrines the Kusanagi sword, one of Japan's Three Sacred Treasures, and ranks just below Ise Jingu in importance. Its grounds are shaded by a large old-growth forest and a thousand-year-old camphor tree. The treasure hall displays many swords. It's a few minutes' walk from Meitetsu Jingu-mae Station or the subway's Jingu-nishi Station. You can also stop nearby for hitsumabushi.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.1.tip: Admission is free. The first few days of the New Year are extremely crowded, so avoid them if you can.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.2.name: Osu Shopping District and Osu Kannon
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.2.text: This old shopping district starts at Osu Kannon and extends through more than a dozen covered streets lined with vintage clothing stores, electronics shops, anime figure stores, and food from around the world. It's Nagoya's most lively area. Osu Kannon's bright-red main hall is highly photogenic, and an antiques market is held on the 18th and 28th of each month. Get off at Osu Kannon or Kamimaezu subway station.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.2.tip: Many snack shops close around 6 p.m., so afternoon is the best time to visit. The covered streets are still easy to explore in the rain.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.3.name: Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.3.text: Housed in the red-brick buildings of Toyota's first textile factory, this museum traces the company from automatic looms to automobile manufacturing. Many old machines are demonstrated in operation, and the automotive pavilion shows the full process of stamping, welding, and assembly. You don't need to know Japanese to enjoy it. Families and machine enthusiasts can easily spend half a day here. It's one Meitetsu stop from Nagoya Station, followed by a walk of about 3 minutes.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.3.tip: The museum is often closed on Mondays. Demonstrations run at set times, so check the schedule when you enter.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.4.fee: The Grand Park Pass costs about ¥3,300–7,800
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.4.name: Ghibli Park
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.4.text: Set inside Expo 2005 Aichi Commemorative Park, Ghibli Park recreates scenes from films such as My Neighbor Totoro, Kiki's Delivery Service, and Princess Mononoke. There are no rides; it's more like walking through a forest park and seeing the scenes in person. Ghibli's Grand Warehouse is an indoor exhibition area, so you can enjoy it in the rain. From Nagoya, take the subway and transfer to the Linimo maglev line. The trip to Ai-Chikyu-Haku-Kinen-Koen Station takes about 50 minutes.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.4.tip: All tickets must be reserved in advance; no tickets are sold on-site. Tickets for dates two months ahead go on sale at 2 p.m. on the 10th of each month, and popular dates sell out quickly.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.5.name: Inuyama Castle
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.5.text: One of Japan's 5 national treasure keeps, this castle sits on a small hill beside the Kiso River. Its keep is one of the oldest surviving examples of its kind. At the top, you can walk along the open-air gallery and look over the Kiso River and Nobi Plain. The wind is strong. The old castle-town streets below are lined with skewers, dango, and other snacks. From Meitetsu Nagoya, the train to Inuyama Station takes about 30 minutes.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.5.tip: The stairs inside the keep are very steep, and you'll need to remove your shoes. Queues and visitor limits are possible during cherry blossom season and on weekends, so arrive when it opens.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.6.name: Korankei Gorge
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.6.text: This mountain valley in Asuke, Toyota, is lined with about 4,000 maple trees along both banks of the river. The entire valley turns red in mid- to late November, with red Taigetsukyo Bridge providing a classic photo spot. The foliage season brings nighttime illumination and beautiful reflections. Other seasons are quieter, and dogtooth violets bloom on the slopes in spring. There is no direct train. Take a bus from Meitetsu Higashi-Okazaki Station or Toyota-shi Station.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.6.tip: Traffic can cause delays of several hours on weekends during the foliage season. Go early on a weekday if possible, and avoid returning after 4 p.m.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.7.name: Tokoname Pottery Footpath
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.7.text: This old kiln district in Tokoname, one of Japan's Six Ancient Kilns, has sloping lanes lined with walls embedded with clay pipes and shochu bottles. Brick chimneys rise above the rooftops, and former workshops are now pottery studios and cafés. The best-known spot is Toko-zaka. Tokoname Station is only two stops and about 5 minutes from the airport, making this a good stop for 1–2 hours on the day you arrive or depart.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.spots.7.tip: Tokoname is a major producer of maneki-neko lucky cats. A giant one near the entrance makes a fun photo stop.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.stay: Stay near Nagoya Station. The shinkansen, Meitetsu, Kintetsu, and airport lines all meet here, with direct trains to Takayama, Ise, and Inuyama. For evening dining, drinks, and shopping, stay around Sakae or Fushimi.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.tagline: Nagoya food and drink, Inuyama Castle, and Ghibli Park
63b6e32895bb9677383a.tips.0: The Nagoya Castle keep is closed, so you can only see it from outside. Honmaru Palace is the main attraction, so don't just take a photo outside and leave.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.tips.1: Meitetsu, Kintetsu, JR, and subway services use different entrances at Nagoya Station. Check the signs before transferring.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.tips.2: Ghibli Park tickets can only be bought online in advance. Reserve as soon as your dates are set; tickets are not sold on-site.
63b6e32895bb9677383a.tips.3: International visitors traveling to Takayama and Shirakawa-go can buy the JR Takayama-Hokuriku Area Tourist Pass at Nagoya Station or Chubu Centrair International Airport.

63fc705d8935fe192d12.access.0.how: The JR Nanpu Limited Express reaches Kochi Station in about 2.5 hours, passing through Oboke Gorge.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.access.1.how: Take the airport limousine bus to Kochi Station. There are international routes from Taipei and other cities.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.access.2.how: JR Limited Express trains take a little over 2 hours to Kochi Station. Some services require a transfer at Utazu or another station.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.foods.0.name: Katsuo no tataki
63fc705d8935fe192d12.foods.0.text: A block of bonito is seared over a large straw fire for a few seconds, leaving the outside charred. It is cut into thick slices and served with garlic, onion, and ponzu, or simply salted in the shio tataki style. The outside is smoky and crisp while the inside remains raw. People in Kochi eat it as an everyday dish.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.foods.0.where: Hirome Market and izakayas in Kochi City
63fc705d8935fe192d12.foods.1.name: Sawachi ryori
63fc705d8935fe192d12.foods.1.text: A Kochi banquet platter: one large round plate piled with sashimi, sushi, fried food, and desserts for everyone to share. It is best ordered for a group of three to five and offers a taste of Kochi's lively dining culture.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.foods.1.where: Long-established restaurants and large izakayas in central Kochi City
63fc705d8935fe192d12.foods.2.name: Yuzu
63fc705d8935fe192d12.foods.2.text: Kochi is Japan's top yuzu-producing region. Yuzu ponzu, yuzu juice, and yuzu kosho are local specialties. Yuzu drinks and seasonings from Umaji Village are famous throughout Japan and make good souvenirs.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.foods.2.where: The souvenir area at Kochi Station and Hirome Market
63fc705d8935fe192d12.intro.0: Kochi Prefecture covers much of southern Shikoku and faces the Pacific. It is the hometown of Sakamoto Ryoma, a hero of the late Edo period. Kochi City is easy to explore: Kochi Castle, with its original keep; the lively food hall Hirome Market; and the Sakamoto Ryoma statue at Katsurahama Beach are all within the city or a 30-minute drive. Locals love to drink and are known for their outgoing nature, so meals are often lively.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.intro.1: Beyond the city are some of Japan's clearest rivers: the low, railing-free Chinka bridges over the Shimanto River and the crystal-clear 'Niyodo blue' of the Niyodo River. Distances between sights are long and public transportation is slow. Use Kochi City as your base, then set aside a full day for one river.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.name: Kochi
63fc705d8935fe192d12.seasons.note: Spring and fall are the most comfortable. The Yosakoi Festival takes place August 9–12, and hotels fill up quickly. Typhoons are common in summer and fall, so check the weather before you go.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.sources.0.title: Kochi Castle official website: Visitor guide
63fc705d8935fe192d12.sources.1.title: Hirome Market official website
63fc705d8935fe192d12.sources.2.title: Wikipedia: Niyodo River
63fc705d8935fe192d12.sources.3.title: Kochi Ryoma Airport official website
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.0.name: Kochi Castle
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.0.text: One of Japan's 12 original castle keeps and the only castle whose buildings inside the honmaru have all survived. Its keep is connected to the honmaru palace, where you can see the former domain lord's office. The castle is about 10 minutes from Kochi Station by streetcar. A 1-kilometer open-air Sunday market stretches below the castle.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.0.tip: Visit the Sunday Market below the castle first on Sunday morning, then head up to the castle and grab breakfast along the way.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.1.name: Hirome Market
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.1.text: A large food hall at the foot of Kochi Castle, with dozens of small vendors around communal tables. Buy what you like and find a seat. The specialty is bonito seared over rice straw in front of you, best paired with a beer or Tosa sake. People start drinking around noon. Seats are hard to find on weekend evenings, and sharing a table with strangers is normal.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.1.tip: Claim a table first, then take turns buying food. Leave someone at the table to watch your things.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.2.name: Katsurahama Beach
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.2.text: This curved beach south of Kochi City has dramatic pine woods, rocks, and Pacific waves. A Sakamoto Ryoma statue faces the sea from a hilltop. The waves and currents are strong, so swimming is prohibited; come for a walk and the views instead. The Sakamoto Ryoma Memorial Museum is nearby. Buses from Kochi Station take about 35 minutes.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.3.name: Shimanto River Chinka Bridges
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.3.text: Known as 'Japan's last pristine river,' the Shimanto is crossed by dozens of low, railing-free Chinka bridges. They are designed to go underwater during floods rather than be swept away. The best-known is Sada Chinka Bridge downstream. The best way to explore is to rent a bicycle around Nakamura and ride along the river, or take a houseboat downstream.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.3.tip: The bridges have no railings, so take care when cycling or traveling with children. The drive from Kochi City takes about 2 hours.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.4.name: Niyodo River
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.4.text: The Niyodo has repeatedly been named one of Japan's best-quality major rivers. On sunny days, its deep pools and waterfalls glow transparent blue-green, a color known as 'Niyodo blue.' Highlights include the mountain waterfall pool Nikobuchi and Yasui Gorge. The area is about a 1–1.5-hour drive from Kochi City. Buses are inconvenient, so consider joining a local day tour.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.4.tip: The blue is most vivid from morning to noon on sunny days. Nikobuchi is a sacred place, and entering the water is prohibited.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.5.name: Makino Botanical Garden
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.5.text: Built to honor Tomitaro Makino, known as the 'father of Japanese botany,' this hillside garden has a greenhouse, native plant areas, and beautifully designed exhibition buildings. Flowers bloom year-round, with the busiest displays in spring and early summer. It is on Mount Godai, in the same direction as Katsurahama Beach, so the two can be visited on the same day.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.6.name: Monet's Garden Marmottan
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.6.text: Modeled after Monet's garden in Giverny, this is the only garden outside Giverny officially authorized by a Monet-related foundation to use the name 'Monet's Garden.' It has a water-lily pond, Japanese bridge, and garden cottage. The water lilies are at their best in spring and summer. In eastern Kochi, it takes about 2 hours from Kochi City by train and bus, so plan a full day for it.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.spots.6.tip: The garden closes for part of the winter. Check the official website for opening dates before you go.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.stay: Stay around Kochi Station, Harimayabashi, or Hirome Market for easy access to food, drinks, and streetcars. For the Shimanto River, consider spending one night in Nakamura (Shimanto City).
63fc705d8935fe192d12.tagline: Sakamoto Ryoma's hometown, charcoal-seared bonito, and pristine rivers
63fc705d8935fe192d12.tips.0: Streetcars operated by Tosaden Traffic can take you to Kochi City's main sights. Transit cards are accepted.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.tips.1: The Shimanto and Niyodo rivers are far from the city, and buses are infrequent. Check schedules in advance or join a day tour.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.tips.2: People in Kochi are enthusiastic drinkers and may encourage you to drink at banquets. If you do not drink, say so early.
63fc705d8935fe192d12.tips.3: The city is especially lively during the Yosakoi Festival in August, but book your hotel one or two months ahead.

6444f1c53bbbd2251a8b.author.name: Lu Chen
6444f1c53bbbd2251a8b.author.role: Southern Hemisphere & U.S. West road-trip editor · 80,000+ km driven
6444f1c53bbbd2251a8b.cover.alt: Twelve Apostles limestone sea stacks glowing in golden sunset along Australia's Great Ocean Road
6444f1c53bbbd2251a8b.cover.caption: Only by spending night two in Port Campbell, just 10 minutes down the road, can you savor the golden twenty minutes when Southern Ocean sunset sets the Twelve Apostles ablaze.
6444f1c53bbbd2251a8b.excerpt: Squeezing the Great Ocean Road into a single day turns it into an exhausting blur. The golden rhythm is 3 days and 2 nights: sleep first in Apollo Bay, then Port Campbell for a relaxed Twelve Apostles sunset, while sidestepping left-side driving traps, post-17:00 kangaroo hazards, and early-closing beach towns.

6715bf7d3099e58efba5.paragraphs.0: Locals call it 'Autumn's Eikando' for a reason: more than 3,000 Japanese maples cascade down the hillside in layers of scarlet and amber. When the gates open at 08:30, roughly 70% of visitors stop immediately at the Middle Gate and entry grove—keep walking right past them and head briskly toward Hojo Pond and Gokuraku Bridge on the right.
6715bf7d3099e58efba5.paragraphs.1: Right then, the morning sun clears the Higashiyama ridge at a low angle, backlighting the oldest crimson maples while the pond stays dead calm. After shooting the reflections, climb the steps to Tahoto Pagoda for sweeping views over the red canopy and Kyoto skyline, then slip off your shoes to wander the winding Garyuro corridor and Amida Hall. As the 10:00 tour-bus wave rolls in, you'll be strolling calmly out the gate.
6715bf7d3099e58efba5.photo.alt: Sunlit timber veranda and mossy stone path framed by fallen autumn leaves at a quiet Kyoto temple
6715bf7d3099e58efba5.photo.caption: Around 08:40, morning dew still clings to the wooden corridors as low sunlight filters through timber pillars and scarlet leaves—easily Kyoto's quietest moment.
6715bf7d3099e58efba5.tip: Eikando clears the grounds and sells separate tickets for its evening illumination. If you want to see the glowing pond by night, return around 16:45 to queue for the 17:30 night session—it feels like an entirely different temple after dark.
6715bf7d3099e58efba5.title: Head straight for Hojo Pond and Tahoto Pagoda to catch the cleanest 20 minutes of reflections

676a24d4daacf5fcabe9.s: {name} travel guide: {tagline}. {spots} attractions, {foods} local foods, plus tips on transport and lodging.

67b96893695a77ee8767.cost: OMNY subway $3/ride; Top of the Rock ~$45–60 (sunset slots cost extra)
67b96893695a77ee8767.location: Grand Central Terminal → New York Public Library → Fifth Avenue → Rockefeller Center → Times Square
67b96893695a77ee8767.paragraphs.0: Getting from JFK Airport into Manhattan is smoothest via the AirTrain to Jamaica Station ($8.50, also OMNY tap-friendly), followed by a 20-minute LIRR commuter train straight to Grand Central or Penn Station—faster and far cheaper than sitting in taxi traffic. Step into Grand Central Terminal's vaulted main concourse as shafts of light slice across the four-faced brass clock, and you're immediately inside a movie set.
67b96893695a77ee8767.paragraphs.1: Stroll 8 minutes down 42nd Street to the lion-guarded New York Public Library and leafy Bryant Park, then turn north up Fifth Avenue past St. Patrick's Cathedral. Book a timed ticket for Top of the Rock roughly 1 hour before sunset so a single visit captures daylight, golden hour, and Manhattan's glittering night grid. Afterward, walk 10 minutes into electric, bright-as-day Times Square—or catch a Broadway musical booked online or at the TKTS booth.
67b96893695a77ee8767.photo.alt: Neon-lit Times Square in Midtown Manhattan at dusk
67b96893695a77ee8767.photo.caption: Ten minutes on foot from Rockefeller Center or Midtown's observation decks drops you straight into neon-drenched Times Square—pure first-night New York energy.
67b96893695a77ee8767.tip: Every major New York observation deck runs strict Timed Entry slots. Prime sunset windows routinely sell out 1–2 weeks in advance and carry a $10–15 sunset surcharge, so lock in your ticket the moment your dates are set.
67b96893695a77ee8767.title: Tap OMNY into Manhattan for Grand Central, Fifth Avenue, and sunset from Top of the Rock

67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.access.0.how: There are usually no nonstop flights. Most routes connect through Los Angeles or San Francisco, where you clear U.S. immigration. The transpacific flight takes about 11–13 hours, followed by a flight of about 1–1.5 hours to Las Vegas.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.access.1.how: The drive along I-15 is about 430 kilometers (270 miles) and takes 4–5 hours, with frequent traffic on Friday evenings and Sunday afternoons. Flying takes about 1 hour.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.access.2.how: The drive is about 450 kilometers (280 miles) and takes about 4.5 hours, passing Hoover Dam as you approach Las Vegas.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.access.3.how: Drive about 3.5–4 hours to Lake Tahoe, or fly to Reno (about 1 hour) and drive about 1 hour to the eastern shore.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.cover.alt: A road winding through the red rocks of Valley of Fire
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.0.name: Las Vegas buffet
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.0.price: Dinner about $60–100 per person, excluding tips
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.0.text: A classic Las Vegas meal. Buffets at several upscale Strip hotels offer long spreads of seafood, steak, international dishes, and desserts. Prices have risen considerably over the past decade or so, but you can still try a wide range in one meal. Lines are long on weekends and holidays, so reserve online when possible. Lunch costs less than dinner.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.0.where: Strip hotels including Caesars Palace, Wynn, and The Cosmopolitan
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.1.name: Spring Mountain Road Chinatown
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.1.text: West of the Strip, the Spring Mountain Road area is Las Vegas’s hub for Asian food. Sichuan cooking, Cantonese dim sum, hot pot, pho, ramen, and Korean barbecue stretch for several kilometers, with many restaurants open late. If you want a break from large American meals or get hungry after a show, it is about a ten-minute taxi ride away.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.1.where: Along Spring Mountain Road, west of the Strip
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.2.name: Shrimp cocktail
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.2.text: An old Las Vegas classic: a stemmed glass packed with chilled shrimp, topped with tangy, slightly sweet tomato sauce with horseradish, and served with lemon and saltine crackers. Downtown casinos once used it as a cheap draw. You can still order it at downtown restaurants and at steakhouses and bars on the Strip.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.2.where: Older casinos near Fremont Street downtown and steakhouses on the Strip
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.3.name: Basque family-style dinner
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.3.text: More than a century ago, many Basques from Spain came to Nevada to herd sheep. Their legacy lives on in northern towns, where Basque restaurants serve communal meals at long tables. Soup, salad, beans, and bread arrive in turn, followed by lamb chops or steak, with a bittersweet Picon Punch before dinner. Portions are generous and suit a group.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.foods.3.where: Northern towns including Reno, Elko, and Gardnerville
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.intro.0: Much of Nevada is dry basin-and-range country, and most visitors arrive and leave through Las Vegas. The Strip’s hotels, shows, and buffets can fill two or three days, but the real rewards lie within an hour’s drive: Red Rock Canyon, Valley of Fire, and Hoover Dam. Las Vegas is also a common starting point for a loop through Zion and the Grand Canyon.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.intro.1: Las Vegas is hot by day and lively by night. From June–August, midday temperatures often top 40°C. Plan outdoor activities for the morning, rest at your hotel in the afternoon, and head out after dark to explore the Strip and downtown Fremont Street. Book shows and restaurants ahead through their official websites, and remember to add resort fees and parking to hotel rates.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.intro.2: At the other end of the state are Reno and Lake Tahoe’s eastern shore, with clear water in summer and skiing in winter. They are much closer to San Francisco than to Las Vegas and pair well with a trip through Northern California. Great Basin National Park, in eastern Nevada, is remote, but its night skies and bristlecone pines thousands of years old are hard to match.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.name: Nevada
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.seasons.note: March–May and October–November are the most comfortable months; Las Vegas often tops 40°C in June–August. Lake Tahoe is best in June–September, with ski season in December–March.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.sources.0.title: NPS: Non-U.S. resident surcharge
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.sources.1.title: NPS: America the Beautiful annual pass
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.sources.2.title: Bureau of Reclamation: Hoover Dam visitor information
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.sources.3.title: Nevada State Parks: Valley of Fire
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.sources.4.title: Nevada State Parks: Sand Harbor
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.sources.5.title: BLM: Visiting Red Rock Canyon

67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.sources.7.title: Nevada DMV FAQs: Foreign driver’s licenses
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.0.name: Las Vegas Strip
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.0.text: The Strip stretches about 6.8 kilometers, lined with one themed hotel after another. Bellagio’s dancing fountains, the Venetian’s indoor canals, and Sphere’s illuminated exterior are all free to see. Hotels look close together, but walking between them often takes more than ten minutes via pedestrian bridges and indoor passages. Book any shows you want to see through their official websites.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.0.tip: Bellagio’s fountains run about every 15 minutes after dark. Most Strip hotels charge for parking; check before your stay.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.1.name: Fremont Street Experience
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.1.text: In downtown Las Vegas, a giant LED canopy covers a five-block pedestrian mall, with light shows on the hour after dark and a zip line overhead. Low table minimums and plenty of street performers give it a wilder feel than the Strip. Head east to the Fremont East area for bars and small restaurants.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.1.tip: From the Strip, take the 24-hour Deuce double-decker bus or a taxi, which takes about 15–20 minutes. Walk with others late at night.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.2.name: Hoover Dam
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.2.text: Built in the 1930s, this concrete arch dam stands about 221 meters high and holds back the Colorado River to form Lake Mead. The Nevada–Arizona state line runs through the center of the dam. Walking across the top is free; the best panoramic view is from the pedestrian walkway on the memorial bridge downstream. To go inside and see the generator room, buy a visitor center ticket or a dam tour ticket.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.2.tip: Tour tickets are sold only on-site, after security screening. From November–March, the two sides of the dam have a 1-hour time difference.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.3.name: Valley of Fire State Park
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.3.text: Nevada’s oldest state park has red sandstone weathered into waves, honeycombs, and elephant shapes, along with ancient petroglyphs on the rock walls. Driving White Domes Road takes you past most of the highlights. Fire Wave and the White Domes Loop are both short hikes. About 1 hour from Las Vegas, the park makes an easy half-day trip.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.3.tip: Several popular trails close for extreme heat from about May 15–September 30. In summer, stick to roadside sights.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.4.fee: About $20 per vehicle; annual passes accepted
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.4.name: Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.4.text: About a 30-minute drive from the Strip, this area has a one-way scenic loop of about 21 kilometers (13 miles), winding past the red-and-white Calico Hills and towering gray cliffs. Driving it without stops takes about 45 minutes. Short trails and climbing spots line the route. Early mornings in spring and fall are the most comfortable, and it is a good first-day outing while adjusting to the time difference.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.4.tip: From October 1–May 31, entry to the scenic drive during the hours of 8–17 requires a timed reservation through recreation.gov.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.5.name: Sand Harbor, Lake Tahoe
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.5.text: Lake Tahoe’s eastern shore lies in Nevada, and Sand Harbor has some of its clearest water. Rounded granite boulders dot the shallows, where green water fades into deep blue. In summer, paddleboard or sunbathe on the small beaches; July–August also brings an outdoor Shakespeare festival. The lake sits at about 1,900 meters, so the water stays chilly even in summer.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.5.tip: The parking lot fills early on summer weekends. Roadside parking is prohibited along Highway 28, so aim to arrive before 8.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.6.fee: Free park entry; cave tours about $8–15
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.6.name: Great Basin National Park
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.6.text: This remote national park in eastern Nevada has no entrance fee. Its three main draws are stalactite-filled Lehman Caves, accessible only on a guided tour; Wheeler Peak, which rises to nearly 4,000 meters; and bristlecone pines that can live for thousands of years. It is an International Dark Sky Park, with clear views of the Milky Way on cloudless nights. The drive from Las Vegas takes about 5 hours, so plan to stay overnight.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.spots.6.tip: Lehman Caves tours have limited spaces; book ahead through recreation.gov. The upper section of Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive closes in winter.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.stay: For a first visit, stay near the middle of the Strip, around Caesars Palace and Bellagio, for easy walks between hotels and shows. For lower prices and a lively setting, stay near Fremont Street downtown. Compare room totals including resort fees.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.tagline: Beyond the neon: red rocks, a mighty dam, and an alpine lake
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.tips.0: Daytime temperatures often top 40°C in June–August. Plan outdoor activities for the first two or three hours after sunrise, keep plenty of water in the car, and never leave phones or children inside.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.tips.1: Strip hotels often add resort fees of several dozen dollars per night to room rates, plus parking charges if you drive. Compare the total cost when booking.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.tips.2: Nevada recognizes valid foreign driver’s licenses; an International Driving Permit serves only as a translation. Requirements depend on your license. Check official Nevada DMV guidance and your rental company’s requirements.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.tips.3: Nevada uses Pacific Time; set your clock forward 1 hour when entering Utah. You must be at least 21 to drink alcohol or enter casinos. Carry your passport.
67bb0fd1163f80a6d14b.tips.4: The Grand Canyon West Skywalk, a common day trip from Las Vegas, is on Hualapai tribal land and is separate from the national park’s South Rim. Choose based on what you want to see.

68a8fc4671d5fe30f181.s: The waters around Okinawa and southern Kyushu are tropical blue, the Seto Inland Sea is dotted with calm islands, and the Pacific side has big waves and rugged coastlines. Watch for typhoons in summer and fall.

68ed4810bdb0aa2b965d.s: Offline & Feeds: Pages you open are cached for offline reading, and an RSS feed tracks daily updates. Found outdated info or have suggestions? Email contact@cloudborne.cn.

692bc75b3d0a288f454b.access.0.how: Most travelers connect in Los Angeles or San Francisco after entering the United States, then fly to Phoenix, a flight of about 1.5 hours. Another option is to fly to Las Vegas and drive into Arizona. The transpacific flight takes about 11–13 hours.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.access.1.how: The Grand Canyon South Rim is about 450 kilometers (280 miles) away, or about 4.5 hours by car. Page is about 440 kilometers away, or about 4.5 hours.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.access.2.how: Sedona is about 190 kilometers away, or about 2 hours by car. The Grand Canyon South Rim takes about 4 hours, and Tucson takes about 1.5–2 hours.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.access.3.how: Page is about 190 kilometers (120 miles) away, or about 2 hours by car. Watch for the time-zone change after entering Arizona.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.cover.alt: Layered cliffs at dusk on the Grand Canyon South Rim
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.0.name: Navajo Taco
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.0.text: A Navajo fry bread base topped with pinto beans, ground beef, lettuce, tomatoes, and cheese. One serving is about the size of a full plate. The fry bread is crisp outside and soft inside. It can also be served with honey or sugar as a snack. Roadside stands and restaurants around Monument Valley and Antelope Canyon often serve it.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.0.where: The Navajo Nation, Monument Valley, and Page
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.1.name: Sonoran Hot Dog
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.1.text: A Tucson street-food favorite from across the Mexican border. A hot dog is wrapped in bacon and grilled, placed in a soft bun, and piled with beans, onions, tomatoes, mustard, mayonnaise, and green chile sauce. It's rich and filling, and food trucks are most common in the evening.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.1.where: Food trucks and Mexican restaurants in southern Tucson
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.2.name: Chimichanga
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.2.text: A large burrito filled with beef or chicken and beans, deep-fried until the tortilla is golden and blistered, then topped with sauce and cheese and served with sour cream and guacamole. Tucson and Phoenix both claim to have invented it. Nearly every Mexican-style restaurant serves one.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.2.where: Mexican-style restaurants in Tucson and Phoenix
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.3.name: Prickly Pear Lemonade
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.3.text: Prickly pear syrup is a vivid magenta color, with a flavor somewhere between watermelon and berries. It's mixed into lemonade, smoothies, or margaritas and is especially refreshing after a walk through the desert. Gift shops also sell prickly pear jam and gummies.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.foods.3.where: Cafes and restaurants in Sedona, Tucson, and Phoenix
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.intro.0: Northern Arizona is part of the Colorado Plateau. The Grand Canyon, Horseshoe Bend, Antelope Canyon, and Monument Valley are all here, about 2–3 hours apart by car. The easiest way to see them is on a road trip from Las Vegas or Phoenix. Southern Arizona is Sonoran Desert country, with towering cacti everywhere. Tucson and Phoenix are warm in winter and extremely hot in summer.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.intro.1: Distances are long here: the Grand Canyon South Rim to Page takes about 2.5 hours, and Page to Monument Valley takes about 2 hours. Don't plan more than two major sights in one day. Antelope Canyon can only be visited with a Navajo guide company. Reserve a time slot in advance during peak season, then work backward to decide where to stay the night before.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.intro.2: Time zones are the easiest thing to get wrong. Arizona does not observe daylight saving time, but the northeastern Navajo Nation does. From March–November, Navajo time at Antelope Canyon and Monument Valley is 1 hour ahead of Page. Confirm the time zone when booking tours and checking sunset times.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.name: Arizona
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.seasons.note: Northern Arizona is best from March–May and September–November. July–September is monsoon season, with frequent afternoon thunderstorms and flash floods. Southern Arizona's desert is comfortable from November–March, while June–August often exceeds 43°C.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.sources.0.title: NPS: Grand Canyon entrance fees
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.sources.1.title: NPS: non-U.S. resident surcharge
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.sources.10.title: ADOT: driving in Arizona for foreign visitors
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.sources.2.title: NPS: Grand Canyon transportation and routes
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.sources.3.title: NPS: Grand Canyon North Rim status
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.sources.4.title: NPS Glen Canyon: Horseshoe Bend
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.sources.5.title: Navajo Tribal Parks: Lake Powell and Antelope Canyon
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.sources.6.title: Navajo Tribal Parks: authorized Antelope Canyon tour companies
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.sources.7.title: Navajo Tribal Parks: Monument Valley
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.sources.8.title: NPS: Saguaro National Park entrance fees
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.sources.9.title: U.S. Forest Service: Red Rock Pass
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.0.fee: About $35 per vehicle, plus an additional $100 per foreign visitor
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.0.name: Grand Canyon South Rim
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.0.text: Open year-round and the most developed side of the canyon, at an elevation of about 2,100 meters. Mather Point is closest to the visitor center. Walk west along the rim trail for changing views. From March–November, Hermit Road is served only by a free shuttle, and Hopi Point is a popular sunset spot. The trail into the canyon is easy on the way down, but the return climbs more than 1,000 meters. Don't try to hike to the bottom and back in one day.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.0.tip: Don't hike below the rim from 10–16 in June–August. Hotels inside the park often sell out a year in advance during peak season.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.1.name: Desert View Watchtower
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.1.text: The eastern end of the South Rim, marked by a stone watchtower modeled on ancient Pueblo architecture from the 1930s. The walls inside feature murals by Hopi artists. You can see a bend in the Colorado River and the colorful desert beyond. It's about 40 kilometers from Grand Canyon Village along Desert View Drive, with several quieter viewpoints along the way.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.1.tip: If you're coming from Page, enter through the East Entrance and stop here first. Check on-site for the tower's opening hours.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.2.fee: About $10 per vehicle for parking; national park annual passes are not accepted
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.2.name: Horseshoe Bend
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.2.text: The Colorado River makes an almost 270-degree bend south of Page. The rim is about 300 meters above the water. The round trip from the parking lot to the overlook is about 2.4 kilometers on a paved trail with almost no shade. Only part of the rim has a railing; stay back from the edge when taking photos. Arrive after sunrise for the fewest people. Sunset is backlit but busiest.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.2.tip: The ground is scorching at midday in summer. Bring water and wear a hat. Drones are prohibited.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.3.fee: About $60–150 per person for a tour, depending on the booking
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.3.name: Antelope Canyon
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.3.text: A slot canyon in the Navajo Nation, shaped by water into curving sandstone waves. Upper Antelope Canyon is flat and easy to walk, with light beams at midday in summer. Lower Antelope Canyon involves several metal ladders, with more curves and slightly fewer people. All areas can only be visited with a Navajo-authorized company. Book several weeks ahead during peak season. Tours usually run on Navajo time, 1 hour ahead of Page from March–November.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.3.tip: Tours are canceled when it rains during monsoon season. Flash floods killed 11 people in Lower Antelope Canyon in 1997, so follow your guide's instructions.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.4.name: Monument Valley Navajo Tribal Park
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.4.text: The isolated red buttes seen in Western movies are here. The park belongs to the Navajo Nation, and the visitor center is on the Arizona side. You can drive the roughly 27-kilometer dirt loop, but the road is bumpy and has sandy patches; an SUV is more stable. To visit areas that require a guide, book a Navajo-guided jeep tour at the visitor center. Staying near the valley entrance lets you see the buttes silhouetted at sunrise.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.4.tip: The park operates on Navajo time. In winter, entry to the loop road ends at about 14:30. National park annual passes are not accepted.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.5.fee: About $5 per day for trailhead parking; annual passes accepted
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.5.name: Sedona Red Rock Country
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.5.text: This town is surrounded by orange and red rock formations. Cathedral Rock and Bell Rock both have short trails near town. The round trip to the Cathedral Rock saddle takes about 1–1.5 hours, with some scrambling on the upper section. Oak Creek Canyon north of town is beautiful in fall, when the leaves turn red. There are many trails but few parking spaces, and popular trailheads fill early on weekends.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.5.tip: Take the free Sedona Shuttle to popular trailheads instead of competing for parking. Check the official website for the schedule.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.6.name: Saguaro National Park
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.6.text: There are two districts on opposite sides of Tucson, protecting the giant saguaros of the Sonoran Desert. Some grow more than 10 meters tall and live for over 100 years. The west district has denser cactus forests, short trails, and a dirt loop road, with the best views at sunset. The east district has an approximately 13-kilometer paved loop. Saguaros bloom with white flowers in May–June. Avoid hiking at midday in summer.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.6.tip: The same admission ticket is valid in both districts for 7 days. Watch for rattlesnakes in the desert, and don't reach into cracks between rocks.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.7.name: Historic Route 66, Seligman
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.7.text: This town was bypassed when the interstate opened but survived on nostalgia for old Route 66. Former gas stations, neon signs, classic cars, and souvenir shops line one street. West of here, the road runs through Kingman to Topock and is the longest remaining continuous stretch of old Route 66. Kingman is about 140 kilometers away. The road is quiet and the grasslands are wide open, making it a scenic detour on the drive from the Grand Canyon to Las Vegas.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.spots.7.tip: There aren't many places to refuel or eat in town. The old road west has no streetlights at night.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.stay: For the Grand Canyon, stay at a hotel inside the park on the South Rim or in Tusayan just outside the South Entrance. For Horseshoe Bend and Antelope Canyon, stay in Page. For Monument Valley, stay at a hotel near the valley entrance or around Goulding's. Sedona is expensive, so consider staying in Flagstaff.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.tagline: Home to the Grand Canyon, Antelope Canyon, and red-rock deserts
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.tips.0: Arizona does not observe daylight saving time, but the Navajo Nation does. From March–November, Antelope Canyon and Monument Valley are 1 hour ahead of Page. Check the time zone when booking tours.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.tips.1: The Grand Canyon charges an additional $100 per foreign visitor age 16 and older. The $250 non-U.S. resident annual pass covers everyone in one vehicle, so it pays for itself if you visit one more park.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.tips.2: Afternoon thunderstorms are common during the July–September monsoon season. Rain can trigger flash floods in slot canyons and dry riverbeds, so follow your guide's evacuation instructions even when rain is falling far away.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.tips.3: Arizona accepts valid foreign driver's licenses, and an international driving permit is recommended. Requirements depend on your license and rental company, so check with the rental company in advance.
692bc75b3d0a288f454b.tips.4: The Grand Canyon North Rim was affected by a wildfire in 2025. Some lodging and visitor centers were damaged, so check the NPS for the latest opening information before visiting the North Rim.

6a44bc53a08920f601b1.access.0.how: There are direct flights to Brisbane from Guangzhou and Shanghai, taking about 9–10 hours. Cairns has no direct flights, so connect through Brisbane or Sydney.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.access.1.how: Fly to Cairns in about 2.5 hours, or drive to the Gold Coast in about 1 hour.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.access.2.how: Fly to Brisbane in about 1.5 hours, Cairns in about 3 hours, or Proserpine for the Whitsundays in about 2.5 hours.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.access.3.how: Fly to the Gold Coast or Brisbane in about 2 hours, or Cairns in about 3.5 hours.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.cover.alt: White sand swirls at Hill Inlet in the Whitsundays
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.0.name: Moreton Bay Bugs
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.0.text: Flat slipper lobsters from the waters around Brisbane. Their meat is sweet and firm, and they're less expensive than lobster. They're often split in half, brushed with garlic butter, and grilled, or served in pasta and burgers.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.0.where: Seafood restaurants and harbor fish shops in Brisbane and the Gold Coast
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.1.name: Mud Crab
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.1.text: Large green crabs from Queensland's mangroves, with especially big claws and thick, sweet meat. They're commonly steamed or prepared as chili crab. Many Asian restaurants sell them by weight and cook them to order. Seafood restaurants in Cairns and Port Douglas serve them, and some boat tours take you out to check crab pots in the river.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.1.where: Seafood restaurants around the Cairns Esplanade and in Port Douglas
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.2.name: Barramundi
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.2.text: Known locally as barra, this native fish comes from northern rivers and coastal waters. Its name comes from an Aboriginal language. The flesh is white, with few bones and a mild flavor; it's best pan-fried with the skin crisp. It's on menus throughout northern Queensland, and with fries it makes a simple meal. Wild barramundi has more flavor than farmed fish.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.2.where: Restaurants and seafood takeaway shops in Cairns and Port Douglas
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.3.name: Queensland Mangoes
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.3.price: About A$20–30 per box in season
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.3.text: Queensland is Australia's largest mango-growing region. Mangoes are in season from November to February and are sold by the box at roadside farm stands and supermarkets. Kensington Pride is the most common variety, with a strong aroma and little fiber. Tropical fruit farms around Cairns also offer unusual fruits such as mangosteen, rambutan, and langsat.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.foods.3.where: Supermarkets, roadside fruit stands, and Rusty's Markets in Cairns from November–February
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.intro.0: Queensland covers a huge part of northeastern Australia, from Brisbane and the Gold Coast in the south to tropical Cairns in the north—a 2-day drive. Most visitors come for two things: taking a boat out to the Great Barrier Reef from Cairns or the Whitsundays, and enjoying the sun and theme parks on the Gold Coast.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.intro.1: The climate varies widely from south to north. Brisbane and the Gold Coast are subtropical, with weather warm enough for swimming most of the year. North of Cairns is tropical. May–October is the most comfortable dry season, while the wet season begins in November, when dangerous jellyfish are also more active. When planning your trip, decide whether to focus on the south or north, then connect the two by domestic flight.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.intro.2: For a first visit, spend 3–4 nights in Cairns: one day on the Outer Great Barrier Reef, one day in Kuranda Rainforest, and one day in Daintree Rainforest and Mossman Gorge. Then fly to the Gold Coast or Brisbane for 2–3 nights. If you like sand islands and 4WD adventures, add K'gari or Whitehaven Beach as separate stops.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.name: Queensland
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.seasons.note: May–October is the best time for the north's dry season; November–May is tropical jellyfish season, and cyclones are possible from December–March.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.0.name: South Bank Parklands, Brisbane
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.0.text: A long park on the south bank of the Brisbane River, with a free man-made beach and swimming pool monitored by lifeguards. You can swim right in the city. Next door are the Queensland Art Gallery and Gallery of Modern Art, both with free permanent exhibitions. In the evening, take a free CityHopper ferry or CityCat along the river, then head to Kangaroo Point Cliffs for city views after dark.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.0.tip: Weekends are busy in the morning, so weekdays are more relaxing for swimming. UV levels are strong during the day, so use sun protection.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.1.name: Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.1.text: This koala sanctuary, founded in 1927, is home to dozens of koalas and a large lawn where you can feed kangaroos. Scheduled activities include koala talks, sheepdog shows, and bird-of-prey flight demonstrations. Note: Since July 2024, the sanctuary has stopped offering koala-holding photos. Instead, it offers paid close-up encounters where you can gently touch a koala and take a photo beside it.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.1.tip: Check the official website's daily schedule before you go. Kangaroo food is sold inside the sanctuary.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.2.name: Surfers Paradise, Gold Coast
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.2.text: The center of the Gold Coast, with a beach stretching for dozens of kilometers in front of a row of high-rises. Lifeguards patrol daily; swim only between the red and yellow flags. Go up to the observation deck near the top of Q1 for views of the entire coastline. At sunset, head south to Burleigh Heads, where locals prefer watching the sun light up the skyline from the headland.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.2.tip: The G:link light rail runs along the coast, so you generally won't need a car if you stay in Surfers Paradise.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.3.name: Gold Coast Theme Parks
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.3.text: Dreamworld, Warner Bros. Movie World, and Wet'n'Wild are around Coomera and Oxenford north of the Gold Coast. Sea World is on Main Beach. If you're traveling with children, allow at least a full day for each park. Movie World has some of Australia's best roller coasters, while Sea World is good for seeing dolphins and penguins. Wet'n'Wild is most popular in summer.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.3.tip: Buy tickets online in advance. Multi-park passes offer better value. Queues are longest during the December–January school holidays.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.4.name: K'gari (Fraser Island)
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.4.text: The world's largest sand island and a World Heritage site. There are no paved roads, so you'll need a 4WD to drive across the sand and along the beaches. The island's best-known sight is Lake McKenzie, with white sand on the lakebed and clear blue water. Other highlights include Eli Creek, where you can float downstream, and the wreck of the Maheno on Seventy-Five Mile Beach. If you're not experienced with 4WDs, a 1–2-day tour is the easiest option.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.4.tip: Buy a vehicle permit in advance (about A$62 for one month). Don't feed dingoes or swim in the open ocean.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.5.fee: Half-day boat trips from about A$139
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.5.name: Whitehaven Beach & Hill Inlet
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.5.text: The Whitsundays' signature beach is about 7 kilometers long, with extremely fine silica sand that squeaks underfoot. From the Hill Inlet lookout, the white sand and blue-green water form swirling patterns at low tide—one of Queensland's most famous images. You can reach it only by boat or seaplane, departing from Airlie Beach or Hamilton Island.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.5.tip: The lookout is most beautiful at low tide. From November–May, wear a stinger suit in the water.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.6.name: Outer Great Barrier Reef
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.6.text: Take a large boat from Cairns or Port Douglas for about 1.5 hours to a pontoon or the edge of a reef, then snorkel. The outer reef has clearer water and more coral and fish. Trips usually include lunch, snorkeling gear, and a semi-submersible or glass-bottom boat. Introductory scuba dives are available for an extra fee. Non-swimmers can wear a life jacket and follow a guide while snorkeling, or simply view the reef from a semi-submersible.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.6.tip: If you get seasick, take medication in advance and sit toward the middle or rear of the boat. Choose a day with light winds and book a few days ahead.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.7.name: Green Island
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.7.text: A coral cay about 45 minutes from Cairns by fast ferry. The island is covered in rainforest, and a walk around it takes less than an hour. Step straight into the water from the beach to snorkel with fish and sea turtles, or take a glass-bottom boat. It's easier and cheaper than an Outer Great Barrier Reef day trip, making it suitable for older travelers and children, as well as anyone prone to seasickness or just looking for a quick introduction.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.7.tip: Early ferries are less crowded. From November–May, wear a stinger suit while snorkeling and enter the water only in marked areas.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.8.name: Kuranda Skyrail & Scenic Railway
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.8.text: A rainforest village in the mountains northwest of Cairns. The classic itinerary is to take Skyrail one way, gliding over the canopy of the World Heritage rainforest and stopping to see Barron Falls. Return on the Kuranda Scenic Railway, which has wound through gorges and past waterfalls since 1891. The village has butterfly and bird sanctuaries, plus markets. Allow 2–3 hours there.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.8.tip: Take Skyrail up and the train down for the smoothest schedule. Waterfalls are at their fullest during the wet season.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.9.name: Daintree Rainforest & Cape Tribulation
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.9.text: One of the world's oldest tropical rainforests, where the forest reaches the coast and sits alongside the Great Barrier Reef—two World Heritage sites in one area. Heading north from Port Douglas, first walk the rainforest trails at Mossman Gorge, then take the car ferry across the Daintree River. You can join a river cruise to look for crocodiles before driving to the beaches of Cape Tribulation. It's a full day by car or on a tour.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.spots.9.tip: The ferry runs 5:00–24:00. A small car costs about A$57 round trip. If you see a crocodile warning sign by the river or beach, stay out of the water and away from the edge.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.stay: In Cairns, stay around the Esplanade for easy walks to the marinas, or choose Port Douglas for a quieter base. On the Gold Coast, stay in Surfers Paradise or Broadbeach for easy access to the light rail. In Brisbane, stay in the city center or South Bank.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.tagline: The Great Barrier Reef, tropical rainforests, and one long stretch of beaches
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.tips.0: November–May is tropical jellyfish season. Wear a stinger suit in northern waters and swim inside stinger nets, between the red and yellow flags.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.tips.1: Saltwater crocodiles may be present in estuaries, mangroves, and coastal areas north of Cairns. If you see a warning sign, stay out of the water and away from the edge.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.tips.2: Queensland does not observe daylight saving time. It is on UTC+10 year-round, and 1 hour behind Sydney and Melbourne from October–April.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.tips.3: Boat fares for day trips generally include the Great Barrier Reef environmental management charge. Trips may be canceled or rescheduled on windy days.
6a44bc53a08920f601b1.tips.4: Australians drive on the left. If you drive with an overseas licence, check Queensland's current requirements for an English translation; the Department of Transport and Main Roads recommends a NAATI-certified translator.

6a8541eec02c4523bd27.s: IC cards, Shinkansen luggage, rail passes: worth it?

6a8ebce8fd9b7747d209.0: Fare math check: staying in Shinjuku or Shibuya? Grab Odakyu's Enoshima-Kamakura Freepass (~¥1,640). Staying near Tokyo Station, Shinagawa, or Ginza? Just tap Suica on JR + Shonan Monorail—and skip the ¥800 Enoden 1-day pass if you board fewer than 3 times (single fares cost less!).
6a8ebce8fd9b7747d209.1: Top timing rule: go Monday through Friday if you possibly can—on weekends, you can easily wait through 2–3 packed Enoden trains before squeezing aboard.
6a8ebce8fd9b7747d209.2: Raw shirasu heads-up: January through mid-to-late March is Shonan's legal off-season, so translucent raw whitebait (nama shirasu) isn't served—only fluffy boiled whitebait.
6a8ebce8fd9b7747d209.3: Save your knees on the island: traveling with older relatives or saving legs for Kamakura? Buy the Escar escalator ticket right at Enoshima's entrance to skip most of the steep sun-baked stairs.

6b53d7dc20ccdf158c94.s: Privacy: No registration required. Your itineraries, lists, and saved items stay in your browser, where we can't see them. Shared links encode the itinerary in the URL, so only people with the link can view it.

6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.access.0.how: There are no direct flights. Fly first to Melbourne or Sydney (about 9–12 hours), then take a domestic flight to Hobart or Launceston.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.access.1.how: The flight to Hobart takes about 1 hour 15 minutes, and the flight to Launceston about 1 hour. You can also take a car ferry from Geelong to Devonport, which takes about 10–11 hours.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.access.2.how: The flight to Hobart takes about 1 hour 45 minutes, and the flight to Launceston about 1.5 hours.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.access.3.how: The flight to Hobart takes about 2.5 hours. There are fewer flights than from Sydney or Melbourne.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.cover.alt: Cradle Mountain and the old boat shed beside Dove Lake
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.0.name: Tasmanian oysters
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.0.text: The estuarine waters of southeastern Tasmania are cold and clean, producing plump Pacific oysters with a fresh, briny flavor. Farms on Bruny Island and the east coast have direct-sale shops where oysters are shucked to order. Add a squeeze of lemon and eat them fresh. Prices are much lower than at restaurants in big cities.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.0.where: Farm shops on Bruny Island and around Coles Bay on the east coast
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.1.name: Tasmanian scallop pie
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.1.text: This Tasmanian specialty is a pastry filled not with ground beef but with whole scallops, usually cooked in a mild curry cream sauce. Many bakeries around the island sell them. Picking up a hot one for lunch on a self-drive trip is one of the most recommended local snacks.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.1.where: Bakeries in Hobart and towns along the route
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.2.name: Leatherwood honey
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.2.text: Leatherwood trees grow only in Tasmania's western rainforests. Honey made from their flowers has a rich aroma, slightly spicy floral notes, and a thick texture. Markets and farm shops often let you taste it before buying. It is also used in ice cream and mead. Before taking it home, check the entry rules for food in your country.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.2.where: Salamanca Market and honey farm shops in the northwest
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.3.name: Tasmanian whisky
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.3.text: Tasmania's cool climate, clean water, and local barley have made it a center of Australian whisky production. The island has dozens of small distilleries. Hobart's waterfront has tasting bars where you can compare single malts from several producers. If you're driving, save tastings for the evening.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.foods.3.where: Tasting bars on Hobart's waterfront and nearby distilleries
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.intro.0: Tasmania is a large island south of mainland Australia. About two-fifths of its land is national park or protected area. The draw here is the air, mountains, and sea: Cradle Mountain's glacial lakes, Wineglass Bay's sweeping curve, and the orange-lichen-covered granite at the Bay of Fires. Wombats, wallabies, and echidnas can appear at any moment along the road.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.intro.1: A self-drive trip is the best way to go. The most common route starts in Hobart and ends in Launceston, or the other way around, over about a week: spend 2–3 days in Hobart and nearby, then head north along the east coast to Freycinet and the Bay of Fires, and finally go west to Cradle Mountain. The island is not huge, but the mountain roads are winding. Keep each day's driving to no more than 3–4 hours.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.intro.2: Hobart itself is worth a longer stay: visit Salamanca Market on Saturday, take a boat to MONA for contemporary art, and drive up Mount Wellington for views over the city. Oysters, scallops, cheese, whisky, and cool-climate wines are all excellent. Small farms around the island sell directly to visitors.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.name: Tasmania
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.seasons.note: December–March is the warmest period, with long days. The deciduous beech at Cradle Mountain turns golden in late April–early May. June–August is cold, and mountain areas often get snow.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.0.name: kunanyi / Mount Wellington
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.0.text: This mountain rises about 1,270 meters behind Hobart. It takes about 30 minutes to drive from the city center to the summit. From the lookout, you can see the entire city, the Derwent River, and distant peninsulas. The summit is covered with huge dolerite columns and boulders. If you're fit, you can hike part of a trail from The Springs halfway up the mountain.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.0.tip: The summit can be more than 10 degrees colder than the city. Snow is possible in any month, so bring a warm jacket. The road may close during high winds or heavy snow.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.1.name: Salamanca Market & Battery Point
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.1.text: Every Saturday, several hundred stalls fill Salamanca Square in front of its sandstone warehouses. You'll find local produce, cheese, honey, woodwork, crafts, and plenty of snacks. The warehouses date from the 19th-century whaling era and now house galleries and restaurants. After the market, walk uphill to Battery Point, where colonial cottages and narrow lanes are ideal for a stroll.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.1.tip: The market is open only on Saturdays, 8:30–15:00. Go in the morning for the widest selection. On weekdays, explore the warehouses and Battery Point instead.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.2.name: Mona (Museum of Old and New Art)
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.2.text: This underground museum was built by a private collector into the sandstone cliffs beside the river. Its collection ranges from ancient Egyptian artifacts to highly provocative contemporary installations, and some works are not suitable for children. The best way to get there is by the museum's fast ferry from Brooke Street Pier in Hobart. The trip takes about 30 minutes, followed by a climb up the steps from the dock. The museum has a winery and restaurants, so you can spend most of a day here.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.2.tip: Open Thursday–Monday and closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Nonlocal adults pay about A$45. Booking museum and ferry tickets ahead is recommended.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.3.name: Port Arthur Historic Site
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.3.text: This 19th-century convict prison site is a World Heritage site. The most striking building is the roofless four-story sandstone prison. The grounds also include a church, officers' residences, a psychiatric hospital, and the Separate Prison, where inmates were held in isolation. Lawns stretch down to the bay. The site is about a 1.5-hour drive from Hobart. On the way, you can stop at sea arches and Tasman Peninsula blowholes.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.3.tip: Open daily, 9:00–17:00. Lantern-lit ghost-story tours cost about A$35 and run Wednesday–Sunday.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.4.name: Bruny Island
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.4.text: Drive about 40 minutes south of Hobart to Kettering, then take the 20-minute car ferry to the island. The island's north and south sections are joined by a narrow sandy isthmus. Climb to the nearby lookout for spectacular views of both bays. Food is the main attraction: freshly shucked oysters, cheese, honey, and berries. You can also take a speedboat along the southern cliffs to see seals. On clear nights, people often watch for the aurora australis in the island's south.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.4.tip: Ferries run about every 20 minutes. A small car costs about A$59 return or more. Boarding is first come, first served. Many roads on the island are gravel, so drive slowly.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.5.name: Freycinet National Park & Wineglass Bay
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.5.text: This is Tasmania's most famous landscape: a perfect arc of white sand between pink granite mountains. The walk from the car park to the Wineglass Bay lookout and back is about 2.6 kilometers and takes 1–1.5 hours, with plenty of uphill sections. To reach the beach, continue onto the Hazards Beach Circuit for a total of about 11 kilometers and 4–5 hours. The drive from either Hobart or Launceston takes 2.5–3 hours.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.5.tip: A national park pass is required. The car park fills quickly around midday in summer, so arrive before 9:00.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.6.name: Bay of Fires
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.6.text: This long stretch of northeastern coast runs north from Binalong Bay. It has white sand, clear water, and granite boulders covered in orange-red lichen that seem to catch fire in the sun. The town of Binalong Bay is at the southern end. Drive slowly along the coast and look for quiet coves. The drive from St Helens takes about 15 minutes, and the entire route is free.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.6.tip: The water is cool year-round. Beaches without lifeguards can have strong currents, so take care if you go in. The area is best for wading and playing in the water.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.7.fee: About A$30.7 for adults for a single day
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.7.name: Cradle Mountain & Dove Lake
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.7.text: This is the gateway to a World Heritage wilderness area. Jagged dolerite peaks are reflected in Dove Lake, beside an old wooden boat shed. The circuit around the lake is about 6 kilometers and takes 2–3 hours, passing through cool-temperate rainforest thick with moss. In peak season, private cars cannot drive to the lake. Take the shuttle bus from the visitor center instead; the ride takes about 20 minutes each way. Wombats are easy to spot in the Ronny Creek meadows in the evening.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.spots.7.tip: Snow is possible in every season, so bring a windproof, waterproof jacket. The adult single-day Cradle Mountain ticket includes the shuttle bus; holiday passes do not.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.stay: In Hobart, stay around the waterfront, Salamanca, or Battery Point for easy access to restaurants and markets on foot. On the east coast, stay in Coles Bay or Bicheno. At Cradle Mountain, stay at a resort near the park entrance, where wombats are easier to spot in the early morning and evening.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.tagline: Drive around the island for mountains, sea, wombats, and oysters
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.tips.0: All national parks require a pass. A holiday vehicle pass costs about A$98 and covers one vehicle with up to 8 people for two months.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.tips.1: Tasmania has strict quarantine rules. Fresh fruit and vegetables brought from mainland Australia will be confiscated. Eat them or put them in a quarantine bin before your flight lands.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.tips.2: Wildlife is abundant on the roads at dusk and at night. Try to reach your accommodation before dark. Drive on the left and slow down on curves.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.tips.3: Whether your licence is valid for driving in Tasmania depends on your licence and the applicable rules. Check the Tasmanian transport department's official website for current requirements.
6b7ae36ea882410d3f67.tips.4: Weather changes quickly. Bring a fleece and rain jacket even in summer. On clear, moonless nights, check the aurora australis forecast.

6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.gateways.0.how: Very close to the city center. The domestic terminal is about 5 minutes from Hakata Station by subway; the international terminal is about 20 minutes by bus, costing about ¥400
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.gateways.0.name: Fukuoka Airport (FUK)
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.gateways.1.how: The airport bus takes about 40 minutes to Kagoshima-Chuo Station. It's convenient for traveling north from the south or visiting Yakushima
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.gateways.1.name: Kagoshima Airport (KOJ)
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.gateways.2.how: Some have international flights. Airport buses take about 45–65 minutes to the city centers, making them convenient for open-jaw trips
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.gateways.2.name: Kumamoto, Nagasaki, and Oita airports
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.gateways.3.how: Ferries run to and from Busan, South Korea. From Honshu, take the Sanyo Shinkansen to Hakata
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.gateways.3.name: Hakata Port
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.intro.0: Kyushu is Japan's southwesternmost main island, close to China. Flights from Shanghai to Fukuoka take less than two hours. It has Japan's highest concentration of hot springs, with Beppu, Yufuin, and Kurokawa Onsen each offering a different experience. Aso and Sakurajima are active volcanoes, while Nagasaki and Kagoshima show traces of historic exchange with China and the West. Local specialties include Hakata ramen, Nagasaki champon, and Kagoshima kurobuta pork.
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.intro.1: Most first-time trips start in Fukuoka. From there, head east to Oita for hot springs, south on the Kyushu Shinkansen to Kumamoto and Kagoshima, or west to Nagasaki. Shinkansen and limited express trains connect the cities in one to two hours. Public transit is less frequent in mountain and island destinations such as Aso, Takachiho, and Yakushima, so consider a day tour or private car. Driving rules depend on your licence; check the official requirements before driving in Japan.
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.name: Kyushu
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.passes.0.name: JR Kyushu Rail Pass (All Kyushu)
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.passes.0.text: About ¥22,000/24,000/26,000 for 3/5/7 days, including the Kyushu Shinkansen and unlimited reserved-seat rides. Worth it only for long-distance travel across the island
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.passes.1.name: JR Kyushu Rail Pass (Northern Kyushu)
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.passes.1.text: About ¥15,000 for 3 days and ¥17,000 for 5 days. Covers Fukuoka, Saga, Nagasaki, Oita, and Kumamoto. Choose this pass if you're only visiting northern Kyushu
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.passes.2.name: SUNQ Pass
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.passes.2.text: Unlimited rides on Kyushu highway buses and some local bus routes. Available for Northern Kyushu, Southern Kyushu, and all Kyushu. A better choice for places without rail service, such as Kurokawa Onsen and Takachiho
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.season: Spring and fall are the most comfortable. Winter is ideal for hot springs. The rainy season falls in June, and typhoons are possible in summer and fall.
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.sources.0.title: JR Kyushu Rail Pass official information
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.sources.1.title: Nishitetsu: Fukuoka Airport to Hakata transportation
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.sources.2.title: Kyushu Sanko Bus: Kyushu Crossing Bus
6bcf99d943f6fe0d6ba4.tagline: Hot springs, volcanoes, and great food, from Fukuoka to the far south

6c867cdfe3ddbafe71f6.location: Kawaguchiko North Shore (Ubuyagasaki / Nagasaki Park / lakeside ryokans)
6c867cdfe3ddbafe71f6.paragraphs.0: Check into your Kawaguchiko ryokan (if budget permits, choose a north-shore Fuji-facing room such as Fuji Lake Hotel or La Vista Kawaguchiko). For dinner, order Yamanashi's hearty iron-pot hoto—thick hand-cut flat noodles simmered with sweet pumpkin and daikon in rich miso broth—before soaking in the open-air bath beneath Fuji's starlit silhouette.
6c867cdfe3ddbafe71f6.paragraphs.1: Set your alarm for 06:15 the next morning! Reverse Fuji demands clear skies and zero breeze—by 9 AM winds almost always ripple the lake. Bundle up and walk out to Ubuyagasaki Peninsula or Nagasaki Park as pink dawn light creeps down the snow cone and paints an identical twin across the water.
6c867cdfe3ddbafe71f6.phase: Step 04 · Day 1 Night & Day 2 06:30 Dawn Patrol
6c867cdfe3ddbafe71f6.photo.alt: Steaming Yamanashi pumpkin miso hoto noodles in an iron pot
6c867cdfe3ddbafe71f6.photo.caption: After a chilly evening soak at Lake Kawaguchiko, a bubbling iron pot of Yamanashi pumpkin-miso hoto noodles warms you straight down to your toes.
6c867cdfe3ddbafe71f6.tip: Check the Fuji-san Visibility Index the day before departure: if Day 1 is crystal clear and Day 2 looks cloudy, flip the loop—rush straight to Kawaguchiko on Day 1 and unwind in Hakone's museums and onsen on Day 2!
6c867cdfe3ddbafe71f6.title: Warm Up with Hoto Noodles & Onsen, Then Hit Ubuyagasaki at 06:30 for Mirror-Still Reverse Fuji
