6df06299ccd4b4e61826.access.0.how: There are currently no nonstop flights to Chicago. Common routes connect through Hong Kong, Taipei, the U.S. West Coast, or New York before continuing to O'Hare International Airport (ORD). The total journey takes about 17–20 hours.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.access.1.how: The elevated Blue Line runs directly downtown in about 45 minutes. Entering the airport station costs about $5. A taxi takes about 40–60 minutes, depending on traffic.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.access.2.how: Flights take about 2 hours. Amtrak has overnight trains, but the trip takes nearly 20 hours.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.cover.alt: The Chicago River and skyscrapers at dusk
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.0.name: Chicago Deep-Dish Pizza
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.0.text: The opposite of New York thin crust: it is baked in a deep pan with a pastry-like crust, a thick layer of cheese and sausage, and tomato sauce on top. Baking takes more than 40 minutes. Most restaurants let you order first and take a seat afterward. One medium pizza serves two or three people.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.0.where: Old-school deep-dish restaurants downtown and in River North.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.1.name: Chicago-style Hot Dog
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.1.text: An all-beef hot dog on a poppy-seed bun, piled with yellow mustard, bright green relish, diced onions, tomato slices, pickled peppers, and a whole pickle, then sprinkled with celery salt. The rule is no ketchup.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.1.where: Hot dog stands and sports venues throughout the city.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.2.name: Italian Beef Sandwich
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.2.text: Thin-sliced roast beef is soaked in seasoned jus and tucked into a long roll, with sweet peppers or spicy giardiniera. You can ask for the whole sandwich to be dipped in the jus again. It gets messy, so locals eat it standing up and leaning forward.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.2.where: Old-school Italian beef shops throughout the city, especially in the West Side and Little Italy.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.3.name: Chicago Mix Popcorn
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.3.text: Caramel popcorn and cheddar cheese popcorn mixed together for a sweet-and-salty combination that is hard to stop eating. Several old-school popcorn shops downtown often have lines out front. The tins make good souvenirs.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.foods.3.where: Old-school popcorn shops on Michigan Avenue and in the Loop.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.intro.0: Almost everyone visiting Illinois heads to Chicago. This lakeside city is the birthplace of the modern skyscraper. The Chicago River runs through downtown, lined with landmark buildings from different eras. A river architecture cruise feels like a lesson in architectural history. Millennium Park's Cloud Gate, the Art Institute of Chicago, and the lakefront trail are all within walking distance.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.intro.1: Chicago is a little cheaper than New York and easier to get around. Downtown's Loop is laid out in a neat grid, with elevated trains circling it. Three days is enough for downtown, the lakefront, and one or two museums. Leave another half day for Oak Park, where you can see Frank Lloyd Wright's early homes.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.intro.2: Winters here are famously cold. With the wind off the lake, it often feels like the temperature is in the teens below zero. River cruises and many outdoor activities stop from November through March. The best time to visit is May–October, when the lakefront has beaches, outdoor concerts, and fireworks.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.name: Illinois
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.seasons.note: May–October is best. Architecture cruises usually run from around mid-March to late November. December–February brings bitter cold and strong winds, but there are Christmas markets and ice rinks.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.0.name: Millennium Park & Cloud Gate
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.0.text: This free lakefront park in downtown Chicago is known for Cloud Gate, a stainless-steel sculpture shaped like a giant bean. It reflects the skyline and the crowds, which is why everyone calls it “the Bean.” Nearby, two screens at Crown Fountain display the faces of Chicago residents, while children play in the water below in summer. The outdoor pavilion designed by Frank Gehry hosts free concerts in summer.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.0.tip: Go early in the morning for the smallest crowds at the Bean. There is an outdoor ice rink nearby in winter.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.1.name: Art Institute of Chicago
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.1.text: One of the best art museums in the United States, it sits beside Millennium Park and is marked by two bronze lions at the entrance. Its Impressionist collection is especially strong, with Seurat's A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, Monet's haystacks and water lilies, and American masterpieces including American Gothic and Nighthawks. Even a highlights visit takes half a day.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.1.tip: Closed Tuesdays. Open until 8 p.m. on Thursdays.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.2.name: Chicago Architecture River Cruise
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.2.text: Chicago's best paid attraction. The cruise spends about 75 minutes on the main branch of the Chicago River and its north and south branches. From art deco buildings to new glass towers, the guide explains the history of each one. Chicago Architecture Center cruises have the most knowledgeable commentary and depart from the dock by the Michigan Avenue Bridge.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.2.tip: Choose an open-air seat on the upper deck. The evening light is best, and summer departures should be booked in advance.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.3.name: Skydeck Chicago, Willis Tower
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.3.text: This black tower was once the world's tallest building. From the 103rd-floor observation deck, the view stretches across several states. Its signature attraction is The Ledge, a glass box extending from the exterior. Step inside and there are more than 400 meters of air beneath your feet. Go on a clear day; the line can be longer than the visit itself.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.3.tip: Check the weather before buying a ticket. Fog can turn the view completely white. Going up before sunset offers the best value.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.4.fee: Free to enter the pier; Ferris wheel costs extra
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.4.name: Navy Pier & Lakefront Trail
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.4.text: This long pier extends into Lake Michigan and has a Ferris wheel, cruise docks, restaurants, and a children's museum. Free fireworks are common on summer evenings. The pier itself is touristy. A better option is to walk or rent a shared bike south along the Lakefront Trail. You get beaches and the lake on one side and the skyline on the other, and can ride all the way to Museum Campus.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.4.tip: The lakefront is windy and cold in winter. Indoor areas of the pier remain open, but skip the outdoor trail.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.5.name: Museum Campus
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.5.text: Three major museums occupy a lakeside peninsula. The Field Museum of Natural History has an exceptionally complete T. rex skeleton, the Shedd Aquarium has beluga whales and dolphins, and Adler Planetarium offers the classic Chicago skyline view from its entrance. Families with children can easily spend a full day here.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.5.tip: All three museums charge admission, so choose carefully if you only plan to visit one or two. The skyline view from the lakefront behind the planetarium is free.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.6.name: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio, Oak Park
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.6.text: This suburban town west of Chicago is where architect Frank Lloyd Wright lived for twenty years. His home and studio are open for guided tours. More than twenty Prairie-style homes he designed stand in the surrounding neighborhoods, with low rooflines and long horizontal lines. Follow an audio tour as you walk. The elevated Green Line reaches Oak Park station in about 30 minutes.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.spots.6.tip: Indoor tour spaces are limited, so book ahead on the official website. Hours are shorter in January–February.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.stay: Stay in the Loop or around the Magnificent Mile on Michigan Avenue. Millennium Park, the river, and the museums are within walking distance. Elevated trains reach almost everywhere, so staying farther out is also an option, but avoid isolated stations at night.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.tagline: A place that grew up with skyscrapers—take a boat tour for a lesson in Chicago architecture
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.tips.0: You can tap a bank card or phone on elevated trains and buses. A single ride costs about $2.5, and entering at O'Hare station costs about $5.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.tips.1: Chicago's sales tax is about 10.25% downtown and higher for dining. Listed prices do not include tax. Tipping is extra.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.tips.2: The Art Institute of Chicago is closed Tuesdays, and architecture cruises stop in winter. Check schedules before planning your itinerary.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.tips.3: Late at night, avoid walking around isolated elevated stations and unfamiliar streets in the South and West sides. Take a taxi back to your hotel.
6df06299ccd4b4e61826.tips.4: In winter, bring a hat, gloves, and a windproof jacket. The lakefront is very windy.

7004921fb402678f4d48.0: Checking luggage before scanning at the airport KIOSK—if you trigger a red-light inspection and your liquids or suitcase are already down the belt, the entire refund is forfeited.
7004921fb402678f4d48.1: Mixing immediate-use snacks or skincare onto a tax-free receipt—missing even 1 item voids the entire receipt on inspection, so pay for trip essentials separately.
7004921fb402678f4d48.2: Underestimating airport verification lines—arriving only 1.5 hours early leaves no margin if a red-light manual check stalls your schedule.
7004921fb402678f4d48.3: Assuming prepaid booking-site totals cover every tax—most Kyoto and Osaka hotels still collect local accommodation tax at the front desk.

70088aaa20490e206187.0: New York cranks your adrenaline to the max, yet it can also disorient first-timers within the first two hours: express and local trains share corridors, tickets for all five observation decks add up to nearly two hundred dollars, costumed characters in Times Square ambush you for tips, and restaurant bills swell nearly 30% once tax and tip land.
70088aaa20490e206187.1: The upside? After more than three decades, New York's finicky yellow magnetic MetroCard has officially retired, leaving seamless OMNY tap-to-pay across the network. This 5-day walkthrough slices the city cleanly into five vertical zones—Midtown, Hudson West Side, Lower Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Uptown museums—so you never waste hours zig-zagging up and down Manhattan.

7177be201a2b1cb438a9.s: Autumn colors begin at Daisetsuzan in Hokkaido in late September, reach Tohoku and Nikko in mid-October, peak in Kyoto and Kansai in mid-to-late November, and arrive on the plains of Kyushu and Kanto in early December.

7192fbf293cbfd7b5ae6.0: Forgetting to tap off on Sydney transit—or switching back and forth between a physical card and Apple Pay. The former bills the maximum route fare, while the latter breaks your daily and weekly cap tracking.
7192fbf293cbfd7b5ae6.1: Underestimating Australia's sun and skipping sunscreen. With a thinner ozone layer and sky-high UV levels year-round, walking the 2.5-hour Bondi coast trail without reapplying practically guarantees a sunburn.
7192fbf293cbfd7b5ae6.2: Walking around the Fish Market or Circular Quay holding food up for photos. Sydney seagulls dive-bomb like hawks—keep a close eye on your plate.
7192fbf293cbfd7b5ae6.3: Ignoring the temperature drop between the Blue Mountains and the city. Even when Sydney's beaches hit 28°C, gusty canyon winds can feel like 17°C—always pack a light windbreaker.

720963b596f46ee853ab.access.0.how: Take the Shinkansen to Shin-Iwakuni Station in about 15 minutes, then a bus to Kintai Bridge in about 15 minutes
720963b596f46ee853ab.access.1.how: Take the Shinkansen from Hakata to Shin-Shimonoseki Station in about 15–20 minutes, then a bus to the Karato area
720963b596f46ee853ab.access.2.how: Served by the Shinkansen, with buses to Akiyoshidai in about 45 minutes and Hagi in a little over 1 hour
720963b596f46ee853ab.foods.0.name: Fugu dishes
720963b596f46ee853ab.foods.0.text: Shimonoseki is a major hub for Japan's fugu trade. Locally, the fish is called fuku, which also sounds like the word for good fortune. A standard set meal includes translucent slices of fugu sashimi, hot pot, and rice porridge to finish. Winter is peak season. Eat only at reputable, licensed restaurants.
720963b596f46ee853ab.foods.0.where: Restaurants around Karato Market and Shimonoseki Station
720963b596f46ee853ab.foods.1.name: Kawara soba
720963b596f46ee853ab.foods.1.text: Matcha soba noodles are served on a hot roof tile, topped with shredded beef, thin strips of egg, and nori. Dip them into warm sauce as you eat. The noodles touching the tile turn crisp. The dish is said to have been inspired by soldiers cooking on roof tiles during the Satsuma Rebellion.
720963b596f46ee853ab.foods.1.where: Originated around Kawatana Onsen in Shimonoseki; also served elsewhere in the city
720963b596f46ee853ab.foods.2.name: Iwakuni sushi
720963b596f46ee853ab.foods.2.text: This pressed sushi is built in layers inside a large wooden mold, with lotus root, fish flakes, and thin strips of egg. Sliced open, it resembles a colorful layer cake. Once a preserved food in the Iwakuni domain, it is now sold at shops around Kintai Bridge.
720963b596f46ee853ab.foods.2.where: Casual restaurants and souvenir shops around Kintai Bridge
720963b596f46ee853ab.intro.0: Yamaguchi Prefecture lies at the western tip of Honshu, with sea on three sides and Fukuoka across the Kanmon Strait. Its sights are spread far apart. In the east, Iwakuni's Kintai Bridge is close to Hiroshima. In the west, Shimonoseki draws visitors for fugu and Karato Market. Along the Sea of Japan coast to the north are Tsunoshima Bridge and the red torii gates of Motonosumi Shrine. Inland lie the Akiyoshidai karst plateau and Hagi Castle Town.
720963b596f46ee853ab.intro.1: Public transportation connects only some of these sights. Kintai Bridge is an easy side trip from Hiroshima, as is Shimonoseki from Fukuoka. Along the northern coast, services are sparse and stops are far from the sights. To see Tsunoshima Bridge and Motonosumi Shrine in one day, join a local day tour or travel with someone licensed to drive in Japan. Driving eligibility depends on your license; check the official requirements.
720963b596f46ee853ab.name: Yamaguchi
720963b596f46ee853ab.seasons.note: See cherry blossoms at Kintai Bridge in early April and Tsunoshima's bluest seas in summer. Winter is fugu season. Akiyoshidai's grasslands are burned each February.
720963b596f46ee853ab.sources.0.title: Official Akiyoshidai tourism website: Akiyoshido Cave
720963b596f46ee853ab.sources.1.title: Official Karato Market website
720963b596f46ee853ab.sources.2.title: Wikipedia: Tsunoshima Bridge
720963b596f46ee853ab.sources.3.title: Wikipedia: Motonosumi Shrine
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.0.name: Kintai Bridge
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.0.text: This wooden bridge spans the Nishiki River in five graceful arches and is considered one of Japan's three great bridges. There is a fee to cross. Kikko Park is on the far bank, with a ropeway up to Iwakuni Castle. Early April is the busiest time, when cherry blossoms line both banks. Fall brings colorful foliage. Allow half a day for a trip from Hiroshima.
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.0.tip: A combination ticket covers Kintai Bridge, the ropeway, and Iwakuni Castle. Buy it at the bridge ticket office for better value.
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.1.name: Motonosumi Shrine
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.1.text: A line of 123 red torii gates follows the cliff down toward the Sea of Japan. The blue sea, green grass, and red gates make a striking photo. An offering box sits about 5 meters up on the large torii gate; landing a coin inside is said to grant your wish. Public transportation nearby is almost nonexistent, so most visitors combine it with Tsunoshima Bridge on a day tour or by car.
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.1.tip: The coast is windy. High winter waves make it even more dramatic, and colder. Confirm your return transportation before going.
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.2.name: Tsunoshima Bridge
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.2.text: This toll-free bridge stretches about 1.8 kilometers over unusually clear, emerald-green water. It has appeared in many car commercials. The classic view is from Amagase Park at the mainland end. Across the bridge, Tsunoshima has a lighthouse and sandy beaches where you can swim in summer.
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.2.tip: The water looks its best around midday in clear weather. The bridge closes in strong winds.
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.3.name: Akiyoshidai & Akiyoshido Cave
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.3.text: Above ground, white limestone outcrops dot the grasslands of Japan's largest karst plateau. Below lies Akiyoshido Cave, one of Japan's largest limestone caves. It stays around 17°C year-round, making it a cool retreat in summer. The path through the cave is about 1 kilometer long. Walk through to the exit, then take an elevator up to the plateau's observation deck.
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.3.tip: The cave floor is wet and slippery, so avoid flip-flops. Admission is slightly higher in summer and during Golden Week.
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.4.name: Hagi Castle Town
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.4.text: Once the castle town of the Choshu domain during the Edo period, Hagi preserves streets of samurai residences enclosed by white plaster walls, earthen walls, and summer orange trees. Rent a bicycle to explore at an easy pace. Several key figures in the Meiji Restoration came from here, and related sites, including Shokasonjuku Academy, have World Heritage status. Hagi ware pottery is also well known; look for a teacup to take home.
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.5.name: Karato Market
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.5.text: This seafood wholesale market in Shimonoseki hosts the Iki Iki Bakan-gai food market on Friday through Sunday mornings and holiday mornings. Stalls sell freshly made sushi and fugu dishes. Take your food to the waterfront and eat with a view of Mojiko in Kyushu across the strait. A ferry takes just a few minutes to cross to Mojiko for a stroll.
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.5.tip: Most sushi stalls close before 3 p.m., and the best items sell out in the morning. Arrive early.
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.6.name: Nagato Yumoto Onsen
720963b596f46ee853ab.spots.6.text: One of Yamaguchi's oldest hot spring resorts, Nagato Yumoto Onsen stretches along the Otozure River. The hot spring district has been renovated in recent years, with riverside paths, foot baths, cafes, and soft lighting at night. At Onto public bathhouse, mild spring water flows directly from the source. Stay here for easy access to Motonosumi Shrine and Tsunoshima the next day.
720963b596f46ee853ab.stay: For Kintai Bridge alone, take a day trip from Hiroshima. For Shimonoseki, stay near Shimonoseki Station. To combine the northern coast with Akiyoshidai, stay at Nagato Yumoto Onsen or Yuda Onsen in Yamaguchi City.
720963b596f46ee853ab.tagline: Honshu's western tip: sea bridges, coastal torii gates, and fugu
720963b596f46ee853ab.tips.0: Buses along the northern coast are infrequent, so join a day tour if you are not driving. Driving eligibility in Japan depends on your license; check the official requirements.
720963b596f46ee853ab.tips.1: Karato Market's sushi stalls operate only on Friday through Sunday mornings and holiday mornings. They will not be open on other weekdays.
720963b596f46ee853ab.tips.2: Eat fugu only at reputable restaurants. Do not buy fish from unknown sources to prepare yourself.
720963b596f46ee853ab.tips.3: The ferry from Shimonoseki to Mojiko takes about 5 minutes, so you can visit two prefectures in one day.

7297b6190180fbe45bde.bases.3: Cambria or San Luis Obispo · 1 night
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.0.items.2.note: Take a cable car back to Union Square in the evening and go to bed early to adjust to the time difference
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.0.move: Use buses and cable cars around the city; don't rent a car yet
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.0.title: San Francisco: Golden Gate Bridge
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.1.move: Ferries to Alcatraz Island leave from Pier 33; the round trip takes about 3 hours
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.1.title: San Francisco: Alcatraz Island
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.2.items.0.note: Pick up the car in the morning and leave the Bay Area before the morning rush
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.2.items.2.note: Watch the sunset over the valley from Tunnel View
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.2.move: San Francisco to Yosemite Valley is about 300 kilometers, or about 4–5 hours by car
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.2.title: Drive to Yosemite
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.3.items.1.note: Walk the lower Yosemite Falls Trail in the morning, then visit Mariposa Grove in the afternoon
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.3.items.2.note: When the road to Glacier Point is open in summer and fall, go there at sunset for a view over Half Dome
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.3.move: Free shuttle buses run through the valley. Parking is easiest to find before 8 a.m.
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.3.title: A full day in Yosemite
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.4.items.0.note: Leave Yosemite in the morning and drive west toward the coast
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.4.items.1.note: Spend the afternoon exploring Fisherman's Wharf in Monterey and Carmel-by-the-Sea
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.4.move: Yosemite to Monterey is about 330 kilometers, or about 4–4.5 hours by car
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.4.title: Down to Monterey
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.5.items.1.note: After San Simeon, watch for the roadside elephant seal viewing areas
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.5.move: Monterey to Cambria is about 160 kilometers and takes about 3 hours without stops; allow a full day with sightseeing stops
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.5.title: Big Sur on Highway 1
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.6.items.0.note: Stop in Santa Barbara around noon for lunch and a walk along the waterfront
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.6.move: Cambria to Santa Monica is about 340 kilometers, or about 4.5–5 hours by car. Traffic is often heavy entering Los Angeles
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.6.title: Head south to Los Angeles for the coast
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.7.items.0.note: Plan the day as you like. With an extra day, visit Disneyland or Universal Studios Hollywood
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.7.items.3.note: For a late-night flight home, allow 2 hours to return the car
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.7.move: Drive around the city; the observatory to Los Angeles International Airport takes about 40–60 minutes
7297b6190180fbe45bde.days.7.title: Los Angeles city lights before heading home
7297b6190180fbe45bde.for: First-time visitors to the U.S. West Coast who can drive and want a mix of cities and nature
7297b6190180fbe45bde.summary: Arrive in San Francisco and leave from Los Angeles, with a detour to Yosemite in between before heading south along the Big Sur section of Highway 1. You won't need a car in San Francisco for the first 2 days, so pick it up on day 3. Parking is difficult in Yosemite, so start early both days. Don't rush Big Sur—set aside a full day to stop along the way. On the last day, see the ocean and city lights in Los Angeles, then take a flight home from Los Angeles International Airport that night.
7297b6190180fbe45bde.title: California coast and Yosemite · 8 days

730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.access.0.how: The Tobu Limited Express, including SPACIA X, takes about 1 hour 50 minutes to Tobu-Nikko. Some trains require a transfer at Shimo-Imaichi.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.access.1.how: The Tohoku Shinkansen takes about 50 minutes. Transfer to the JR Nikko Line, which takes a little over 40 minutes to Nikko. JR Passes are valid.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.access.2.how: The Tohoku Shinkansen takes about 75 minutes to Nasushiobara. From there, take a bus for about 50 minutes to Nasu-Yumoto Onsen.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.foods.0.name: Utsunomiya gyoza
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.foods.0.text: Utsunomiya calls itself Japan's gyoza capital. The filling is mainly cabbage, napa cabbage, and chives. The wrappers are thin and the filling is generous, with pan-fried, boiled, and deep-fried versions available. Gyoza shops cluster around the station, and plates are inexpensive, so order from several places and compare them. There is also a gyoza statue in front of the station for a quick photo.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.foods.1.name: Nikko yuba
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.foods.1.text: Yuba is the thin skin that forms on the surface of heated soy milk. In Nikko, it is lifted from the center, folded, and rolled into a thick coil, giving it a firmer texture than Kyoto-style yuba. The Nikko area has many restaurants specializing in yuba dishes. Order a set yuba meal, and vegetarians will have plenty of options.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.foods.1.where: The main street between Tōshō-gū and Shinkyō Bridge
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.foods.2.name: Tochigi strawberries
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.foods.2.text: Tochigi is Japan's top strawberry-producing prefecture. Tochiotome and Skyberry are local varieties known for their sweetness and rich aroma. From January to May, many farms let visitors pick and eat strawberries as much as they like. Station shops and highway rest stops also sell seasonal strawberry desserts.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.foods.2.where: Farms around Utsunomiya and Mooka, plus station dessert shops
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.intro.0: The highlight of Tochigi is Nikko. At the foot of the mountains are the lavishly decorated Nikkō Tōshō-gū and Futarasan-jinja, both part of a World Heritage site. Farther into the mountains are Lake Chūzenji, Kegon Falls, and the Senjōgahara Wetland. In fall, the colors spread downhill from the highlands. Add Kinugawa Onsen, the Nasu Highlands, and the wisteria at Ashikaga Flower Park in spring, and you have a reason to visit in every season.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.intro.1: The Tobu Limited Express from Asakusa to Nikko takes about 2 hours. You can see the Tōshō-gū area on a day trip, but stay 1 night if you want to visit Lake Chūzenji. Traffic on the mountain roads is heavy during fall color season, so leave plenty of extra time. Utsunomiya is a Shinkansen stop, making it easy to grab a plate of gyoza while changing trains.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.name: Tochigi
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.seasons.note: Ashikaga's wisteria blooms from late April to mid-May. Fall colors peak around Lake Chūzenji in mid-to-late October and in central Nikko from early November. Weekends bring heavy traffic.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.sources.0.title: Tobu Railway: NIKKO PASS
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.sources.1.title: Nikko City Tourism Association: Getting to Nikko and getting around
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.sources.2.title: japan-guide: Tōshō-gū
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.sources.3.title: japan-guide: Kegon Falls
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.sources.4.title: Ashikaga Flower Park: Wisteria Festival 2026
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.0.name: Nikkō Tōshō-gū
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.0.text: This shrine is dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu. Unlike Kyoto's understated style, it is covered in gold leaf, bright lacquer, and elaborate carvings. You could look at Yōmeimon Gate all day and still find new details. Look for the Three Wise Monkeys—"see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil"—and the sleeping cat carving. Pass through the Sleeping Cat Gate and climb more than 200 stone steps to Ieyasu's mausoleum. It is about 10 minutes by bus from the station.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.0.tip: Arrive when it opens at 9 a.m. Tour groups arrive in large numbers after 10 a.m. From November to March, it closes at 4 p.m.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.1.name: Shinkyō Bridge
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.1.text: This vermilion arch bridge crosses the Daiya River. It is the first major sight on the way to Tōshō-gū and Nikko's signature gateway. The bridge belongs to Futarasan-jinja. You can pay to walk across it, but most visitors are happy taking photos from the road bridge beside it. In fall, the gorge and colorful trees below set off the vermilion bridge—a classic Nikko postcard view.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.1.tip: It is about a 20-minute walk from Tobu-Nikko Station along the main street, with plenty of old shops to browse along the way.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.2.name: Kegon Falls
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.2.text: Water from Lake Chūzenji plunges nearly 100 meters over a cliff. It is one of Japan's three most famous waterfalls. The upper observation deck is free. Take the elevator down to the observation deck about 100 meters below for a dramatic head-on view. The surrounding colors are at their best in mid-to-late October, and the falls freeze into icicles in winter.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.2.tip: The bus from Nikko Station takes about 50 minutes via the Irohazaka winding road. On fall-color weekends, traffic can add several hours, so leave early.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.3.name: Lake Chūzenji
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.3.text: This high-altitude lake sits at about 1,270 meters. It is cool in summer and became a summer retreat for foreign embassies after the Meiji period. Former embassy villas remain along the shore and are open to visitors. The fall colors arrive two or three weeks earlier than in central Nikko. Walk north along the lake to Ryūzu Falls and the Senjōgahara Wetland on an easy half-day trail. Early summer and fall are the most comfortable seasons.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.3.tip: Sightseeing boats operate from mid-April to November. The lakeshore is very cold in winter, and many shops close early.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.4.name: Kinugawa Onsen
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.4.text: Large hot-spring hotels line both sides of the Kinugawa Gorge. The Tobu Limited Express runs directly from Asakusa, making access easy. The mild waters are a good choice if you are new to hot springs. Nearby attractions include Edo-themed parks, Tobu World Square with its miniature buildings from around the world, and cruises through the gorge. It is a good place for a 1-night family stay.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.4.tip: Use a Tobu rail pass for both Nikko and Kinugawa, and combine 1 night in Nikko with 1 night in Kinugawa.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.5.name: Ashikaga Flower Park
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.5.text: The park is famous for its wisteria. A 160-year-old wisteria spreads across its trellis like a purple ceiling, while a white wisteria tunnel stretches about 80 meters. The Wisteria Festival runs from mid-April to mid-May, and the park feels even more dreamlike after the evening lights come on. Admission varies with the day's bloom conditions. JR's Ryōmō Line has a dedicated Ashikaga Flower Park Station, a 3-minute walk from the entrance.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.5.tip: Enter in the late afternoon to see the sunset and stay for the lights. There is also a large winter illumination show.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.6.name: Ōya History Museum
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.6.text: This former underground Ōya stone quarry was excavated by hand over several decades, leaving a vast space lined with layers of pillars and stone walls. It feels like an underground cathedral and is often used for films and music videos. It stays cool year-round, so bring a jacket even in summer. Buses run directly from Utsunomiya Station, making it an easy stop after gyoza.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.6.tip: The floor is slippery, so wear shoes with good traction. Ōya-ji Temple and the Great Ōya Kannon can be visited nearby.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.7.name: Nasu Highlands
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.7.text: This highland resort area lies at the foot of Mount Nasu. It has farms, zoos, museums, and many hot-spring inns. Summers are much cooler than in Tokyo, and the area is a summer retreat for the Japanese imperial family. A ropeway climbs the mountain, and the fall colors are beautiful. Sights are spread out and buses are infrequent, so plan to stay 1–2 days and explore at a relaxed pace.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.spots.7.tip: Buses between attractions are infrequent. Driving requires a licence or permit that Japan recognises; the rules depend on where your licence was issued.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.stay: In Nikko, stay near Tobu-Nikko Station or Lake Chūzenji. Head into the mountains early the next morning to avoid traffic. For hot springs, stay in Kinugawa. For Nasu, stay around the Nasu Highlands.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.tagline: Nikko's World Heritage sites, mountain lakes, fall colors, and a plate of Utsunomiya gyoza
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.tips.0: The Tobu NIKKO PASS for the World Heritage area costs about ¥3,000 for 2 days. It includes round-trip travel from Asakusa and buses in the area. The limited express costs extra.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.tips.1: If you plan to spend several days around Lake Chūzenji and Oku-Nikko, buy the 4-day all-area pass for about ¥8,000. It includes a lake cruise, which operates seasonally.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.tips.2: Nikko's mountain areas are much colder than Tokyo. Bring a jacket for cool spring and fall mornings and evenings. Mountain roads may be icy in winter.
730c4e8e3aa6d6864b06.tips.3: There are many stairs around Tōshō-gū, making a stroller inconvenient. A baby carrier works better.

74958881fc0d1dc50e2d.0: Waking up early for Kizu Market on a Wednesday or Sunday—it's normally closed! Always double-check the official market calendar.
74958881fc0d1dc50e2d.1: Ordering crab or wagyu at Kuromon without checking '/100g' fine print—final weigh-in prices easily double expectations.
74958881fc0d1dc50e2d.2: Bringing steaming 551 Horai pork buns onto a Shinkansen—the glorious onion-pork smell fills the entire car.
74958881fc0d1dc50e2d.3: Straying deep south past the JR overpass into inner Nishinari after dark—stick to Shinsekai's main avenues and north stations.

75d50986fe788cf877fb.access.0.how: There are usually no direct flights. Enter the United States in Los Angeles, San Francisco, or Seattle, then connect to Salt Lake City, a flight of about 1.5–2 hours; or fly to Las Vegas and drive to Zion.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.access.1.how: Zion's south entrance is about 260 kilometers (160 miles) away, or a 2.5–3-hour drive. Turn the clock forward 1 hour after entering Utah.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.access.2.how: Moab is about 370 kilometers (230 miles) away, or about 4 hours by car; Zion is about 500 kilometers (310 miles) away, or about 4.5–5 hours.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.access.3.how: Zion is about 400 kilometers (250 miles) away via Page, or about a 4.5-hour drive.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.0.name: Fry Sauce
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.0.text: This pink-orange dipping sauce is loved by nearly everyone in Utah. It is basically ketchup mixed with mayonnaise, sometimes with chopped pickles. Local burger restaurants serve it with fries; it also goes well with onion rings and burgers.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.0.where: Local burger and fast-food restaurants across the state
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.1.name: Funeral Potatoes
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.1.text: The name sounds grim, but this is a cheesy potato casserole made with shredded potatoes, cream, and cheese, topped with crunchy cornflakes. It is a staple at church gatherings and holiday meals in Utah. The name comes from its frequent appearance at meals after funerals. Some home-style restaurants and buffets in Salt Lake City serve it.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.1.where: Home-style restaurants and Sunday brunch spots in Salt Lake City
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.2.name: Utah Scone
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.2.text: Completely different from an English scone, a Utah “scone” is a large piece of fried dough, fluffy and hollow inside. It is served hot with honey butter and is somewhat like a fried dough fritter with sweet sauce. Breakfast spots and some local chains serve them.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.2.where: Breakfast spots and local restaurants around Salt Lake City
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.3.name: Capitol Reef Fruit Pie
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.3.text: The Gifford Homestead in Capitol Reef sells small fruit pies during the open season, with fillings such as apple, cherry, and peach. They are served with ice cream. The old pioneer orchards are next door, making it pleasant to eat a pie on the lawn. Pies often sell out in the afternoon; check the park website for opening months.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.3.where: Gifford Homestead in Capitol Reef's Fruita area
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.4.name: Dirty Soda
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.4.text: Utah's signature drink culture means adding coconut syrup, cream, and lime to cola or soda, then filling the cup with crushed ice. Many locals avoid coffee and alcohol and rely on it for a pick-me-up. Dedicated soda shops often have long lines of cars at the drive-through.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.foods.4.where: Soda shops across the state, mostly drive-throughs
75d50986fe788cf877fb.intro.0: Southern Utah is home to five national parks: Zion and Bryce are close to Las Vegas in the west, Arches and Canyonlands sit beside the town of Moab in the east, and Capitol Reef lies between them. Red sandstone has been carved into canyons, arches, hoodoos, and spires. You can see completely different landscapes within a few days, making this one of the most concentrated road-trip regions in the American West.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.intro.1: Seeing all five parks takes at least a week, and driving between parks takes 2–3 hours each way. If you have less time, choose one side: spend 2–3 days at Zion and Bryce, then head south to Page and the Grand Canyon; or drive south from Salt Lake City to Moab for Arches and Canyonlands. Scenic Byway 12 from Bryce to Capitol Reef is a beautiful drive in its own right.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.intro.2: Salt Lake City in the north is Utah's capital and a common arrival point. The city is small; Temple Square and a walk around Antelope Island on the Great Salt Lake are enough for most visits. There are many ski resorts nearby in winter, known for their powder snow.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.name: Utah
75d50986fe788cf877fb.seasons.note: April–May and September–October are best. Zion and Moab can approach 40°C in June–August, and flash floods are possible from July–September. Bryce is at high elevation and often gets snow from November–March.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.sources.0.title: NPS: Zion entrance fees

75d50986fe788cf877fb.sources.10.title: Utah Driver License Division: foreign driver's license recognition

75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.0.fee: About $35 per vehicle, plus $100 per non-U.S. visitor
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.0.name: Zion Canyon & The Narrows
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.0.text: The Virgin River carved a deep canyon between towering cliffs in Zion. From March–November, private cars cannot enter the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive. Take the free shuttle from the visitor center and get off to hike to Emerald Pools and along the Riverside Walk. The Riverside Walk ends at The Narrows, where you wade upstream through the river. The farther you go, the higher the cliffs and narrower the river become. Without a permit, you can turn around whenever you like, and a half-day round trip is well worth it.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.0.tip: Wear grippy canyoning shoes and bring a walking stick for The Narrows. The route closes when water levels are high or flash-flood warnings are in effect. Check the forecast at the visitor center before setting out.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.1.fee: About $6 to enter the lottery, plus about $3 per person if selected
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.1.name: Angels Landing
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.1.text: Zion's most famous and riskiest trail is about 8.7 kilometers round trip, with about 450 meters of elevation gain. The first half climbs switchbacks to Scout Lookout. The final section follows a rock ridge only a few meters wide, with chains to hold and drops of several hundred meters on both sides. There have been multiple fatal falls. Even without the chain section, the canyon views from Scout Lookout are worth the hike.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.1.tip: The chain section requires a permit. Enter the seasonal lottery, or apply the day before from 0:01–15:00 Mountain Time. Results are released at about 16:00.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.2.fee: About $35 per vehicle, plus $100 per non-U.S. visitor
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.2.name: Bryce Canyon National Park
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.2.text: Despite its name, Bryce is a huge natural amphitheater filled with dense ranks of orange and red hoodoos. The views from Sunrise Point and Sunset Point are most dramatic, but it is better to hike down among the formations. The Navajo Loop Trail combined with the Queen's Garden Trail is about 4.6 kilometers, winding between the hoodoos. At about 2,400–2,700 meters, Bryce is much cooler than Zion.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.2.tip: The hoodoos are reddest at sunrise. Bryce is an International Dark Sky Park and excellent for stargazing on clear nights. It gets cold after dark, so bring a warm jacket.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.3.fee: About $30 per vehicle, with no non-U.S. visitor surcharge
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.3.name: Arches National Park
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.3.text: The park has more than two thousand natural arches. The most famous is Delicate Arch, standing alone on a rocky slope. The round trip is about 4.8 kilometers, all uphill with almost no shade. Go in the evening to see the arch glow red in the setting sun. With less time, drive to Balanced Rock and the Windows section, where short paths lead to the arches. Timed entry reservations are not required in 2026.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.3.tip: The park is crowded from March–October. Enter before 8:00 or after 15:00. The Fiery Furnace area requires a permit booked in advance at recreation.gov.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.4.name: Canyonlands Island in the Sky
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.4.text: Canyonlands is divided into several districts. Island in the Sky is the closest to Moab, about a 50-minute drive away. This mesa rises several hundred meters above the surrounding land. From its rim, you can see layers of canyons below and the Colorado River in the distance. Mesa Arch is a popular sunrise spot, just a few minutes' walk away. Grand View Point offers the widest panorama.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.4.tip: Arrive early to claim a spot for sunrise at Mesa Arch. There is almost no food or water in the park, so stock up in Moab.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.5.fee: About $20 per vehicle for the Scenic Drive
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.5.name: Capitol Reef National Park
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.5.text: A more than 100-kilometer-long fold in the Earth's crust, Capitol Reef has layers of rock lifted into colorful cliffs and white domes. It is much less crowded than the other four parks. Fruita Historic District still has orchards planted by Mormon settlers, where you can pick fruit in summer and fall. Along Highway 24, you can see ancient rock art carved into the cliffs. The Hickman Bridge Trail is about 3 kilometers round trip.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.5.tip: Driving through the park on Highway 24 is free; the Scenic Drive charges an entry fee. There is no gas station in the park, so fill up in Torrey.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.6.name: Scenic Byway 12
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.6.text: The drive from Bryce east to Torrey near Capitol Reef is about 200 kilometers and takes around 3 hours without stops. The most spectacular stretch runs between Escalante and Boulder, where the road follows a narrow rock ridge with cliffs on both sides. The Lower Calf Creek Falls Trail is about 10 kilometers round trip and suits travelers who want a longer hike.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.6.tip: The ridge section has no guardrails, with many curves and steep grades. Drive slowly. The Boulder Mountain section can have occasional snow in winter.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.7.name: Salt Lake City & Antelope Island
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.7.text: Salt Lake City is the headquarters of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Temple Square downtown has gardens and a visitor center and is free to visit. The city is clean, with broad streets. Drive about 1 hour north to Antelope Island State Park in the Great Salt Lake, where bison and pronghorn roam freely. The lake stretches wide, and sunset is beautiful.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.spots.7.tip: There are many biting gnats along the lake on Antelope Island in May–June. Bison may charge if approached, so keep your distance.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.stay: Stay in Springdale outside Zion's south entrance and take the free shuttle into the park; stay in Bryce Canyon City outside Bryce; stay in Moab for Arches and Canyonlands; and stay in Torrey for Capitol Reef. Rooms are limited and expensive in the busy season, so book early.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.tagline: Five national parks linked by a red-rock road trip
75d50986fe788cf877fb.tips.0: Utah uses Mountain Time, 1 hour ahead of Nevada. From March–November, it is also 1 hour ahead of Arizona, except on the Navajo Nation.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.tips.1: Zion and Bryce charge an additional $100 per non-U.S. visitor age 16 and over. Arches, Canyonlands, and Capitol Reef do not. An annual pass is a better deal if you visit three or more parks.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.tips.2: Afternoon thunderstorms are common from July–September. Flash floods can happen suddenly in The Narrows and slot canyons after rain. Check the flash-flood forecast at the visitor center before entering a canyon.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.tips.3: There are few services between the parks, with gas stations sometimes 100–200 kilometers apart. Refuel when the tank is half full, and carry plenty of water and snacks.
75d50986fe788cf877fb.tips.4: Utah allows visitors with a valid foreign driver's license to drive for short periods. License rules and translation requirements depend on your license and nationality, so check the Utah Driver License Division website before setting out.

762b73e351e6a7731824.paragraphs.0: By late November, dusk drops fast over Kyoto around 16:30. If your legs still have juice, take the Keihan Line back north to Sanjo or Gion-Shijo—either line up for the 17:30 night illuminations at Eikando or Kodai-ji, where spotlights turn maples and reflections into layered ukiyo-e scenes, or slip down the lantern-lit alleys of Pontocho and Kiyamachi along the Kamo River for a counter-style obanzai tavern.
762b73e351e6a7731824.paragraphs.1: Seven or eight big ceramic bowls line the bar: order seasonal simmered daikon, blistered Kyo-nasu eggplant, and pressed saba-zushi mackerel sushi with warm sake, letting the fatigue of a 06:30 wake-up melt away under warm alley lanterns.
762b73e351e6a7731824.phase: Step 06 · 17:30 Night maples or Pontocho dinner
762b73e351e6a7731824.tip: On peak-season weekends, popular Pontocho counters fill up fast after 18:30. Walk in right at 17:30 opening to avoid waiting, or ask your hotel desk a day ahead to phone in a counter reservation.
762b73e351e6a7731824.title: Don't call it a night at dusk: glowing evening foliage and Kyoto home cooking by the Kamo River

77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.access.0.how: The Hokuriku Shinkansen Kagayaki reaches Kanazawa in as little as about 2 hours 30 minutes. All seats are reserved.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.access.1.how: Take the Limited Express Shirasagi to Tsuruga, then transfer to the Hokuriku Shinkansen. The total trip takes about 2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.access.2.how: The airport bus takes about 40–55 minutes to Kanazawa Station. Pay when you get off.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.access.3.how: Highway buses operated by Nohi Bus and other companies take about 1 hour 30 minutes from Shirakawa-go to Kanazawa. Reservations are required.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.0.name: Seafood rice bowl
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.0.text: Kanazawa sits near fishing ports on the Sea of Japan, so amaebi sweet shrimp, nodoguro blackthroat seaperch, and buri yellowtail are especially fresh. Rice bowls at Omicho Market are topped with more than a dozen kinds of sashimi. Check the price board carefully before ordering.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.0.where: Restaurants in and around Omicho Market
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.1.name: Jibuni
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.1.text: A traditional Kanazawa stew: duck coated in starch is simmered with local wheat gluten and vegetables in a thick, sweet broth, then finished with a touch of mustard. It is often included in kaiseki meal sets.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.1.where: Japanese restaurants around the Higashi Chaya District and Korinbo
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.2.name: Kanazawa oden
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.2.text: Kanazawa residents eat oden year-round. The broth is light, with local specialties such as kuruma-fu wheat gluten, bai-gai welk, and winter-only kobako crab shells packed with crab meat and roe.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.2.where: Oden restaurants around Kanazawa Station and Katamachi
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.3.name: Gold-leaf soft serve
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.3.text: Kanazawa produces more than 90% of Japan's gold leaf. Shops around the teahouse districts place a whole sheet of gold leaf on soft serve ice cream. It tastes like ordinary vanilla; the appeal is mainly the photo.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.foods.3.where: Gold-leaf shops in the Higashi Chaya District
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.intro.0: Ishikawa's main attraction is Kanazawa, the prefectural capital. During the Edo period, it was the castle town of the Maeda family, lords of the Kaga Domain. Because it escaped bombing during World War II, its old streets, samurai residences, and teahouse districts remain remarkably well preserved. Kenrokuen Garden, Kanazawa Castle, the 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa, and Omicho Market are all within walking distance or a few bus stops of one another. The pace is more relaxed than Kyoto, making it ideal for exploring slowly.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.intro.1: Kanazawa is also a hub for traveling around Hokuriku: the Hokuriku Shinkansen takes as little as about 2 and a half hours from Tokyo, while Shirakawa-go, Toyama, and Fukui are all within 1 and a half hours. For a hot-spring stay, head south to Yamanaka Onsen in Kaga. The Noto Peninsula is still recovering from the 2024 earthquake, so check the latest local transportation and business information before you go.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.name: Ishikawa
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.seasons.note: November is especially atmospheric, with fall colors and Kenrokuen's yukitsuri snow supports. Winter is crab season, cherry blossoms arrive in early April, and summer is hot, humid, and rainy.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.sources.0.title: Kenrokuen Garden: opening hours and admission
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.sources.1.title: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa: visitor information
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.sources.2.title: Hokuriku Railroad: Komatsu Airport limousine bus
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.sources.3.title: Nohi Bus: Takayama–Shirakawa-go–Kanazawa route
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.0.name: Kenrokuen Garden
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.0.text: One of Japan's three great gardens, Kenrokuen was developed over generations by the lords of the Kaga Domain as a strolling garden. Its signature feature is the Kotoji Toro lantern, with two legs of different lengths, beside Kasumigaike Pond. Starting in November, pine trees are fitted with umbrella-shaped yukitsuri ropes to protect them from heavy snow. The combination of fall colors and snow is one of Kanazawa's most photogenic scenes. The garden is across the street from Kanazawa Castle, so the two are easy to visit together.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.0.tip: There is a free admission period before opening each day, when the garden is least crowded. Check the official website for the exact times.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.1.name: Kanazawa Castle Park
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.1.text: The former castle of the Maeda family no longer has its keep, but the reconstructed Hishi Yagura turret, Gojukken Nagaya warehouse, and white lead-tile roofs are impressive. The castle grounds are free to enter and have broad lawns and plenty of cherry trees in spring. The easiest route is to enter through Ishikawa-mon Gate from Kenrokuen, then exit on the other side toward Omicho Market or Oyama Shrine.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.1.tip: The grounds are free, but the interiors of reconstructed buildings such as Hishi Yagura require a separate fee. The cherry blossoms are illuminated at night in early April.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.2.name: Higashi Chaya District
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.2.text: This Edo-period geisha district is lined with two-story wooden buildings with lattice facades. Today, many house cafés, gold-leaf craft shops, and dessert shops. Step inside one of the historic teahouses open to visitors to see the second-floor banquet room, then sit down for a cup of matcha. Across the Asano River is the quieter Kazuemachi Chaya District.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.2.tip: The area is crowded during the day. Come before 9 a.m. or after the evening lights come on for the best photos. Do not stop geisha for photos.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.3.name: Omicho Market
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.3.text: Known as Kanazawa's kitchen, this market has more than 100 seafood shops, produce vendors, and eateries. You can snack on oysters, amaebi sweet shrimp, and seafood rice bowls as you walk. In winter, you'll see piles of crab. Just a few bus stops from Kanazawa Station, it is a good place for brunch.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.3.tip: Popular rice-bowl restaurants often have long lines before noon, so arrive before 10 a.m. Closing days vary by shop, and many vendors close early in the afternoon.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.4.name: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.4.text: Designed by SANAA, this circular glass museum has entrances on all sides, and its public areas are free. Its best-known work is Leandro Erlich's The Swimming Pool: from above, it looks as if people are underwater, while an exhibition ticket lets you enter the pool itself. About a 5-minute walk from Kenrokuen Garden, it is a top choice on rainy days.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.4.tip: The museum will close for major renovations from May 6, 2027, through March 2028. The exhibition galleries are generally closed on Mondays. Buying tickets online in advance is recommended.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.5.name: Nagamachi Samurai District
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.5.text: A few narrow lanes behind Korinbo make up this former residential area for middle- and lower-ranking samurai. Earthen walls, stone paths, and open drainage channels line the streets. You can enter the Nomura House to see its garden. In winter, the earthen walls are covered with straw mats called komokake to protect them from frost, creating a striking scene. The district is about a 5-minute walk from the Korinbo shopping area.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.5.tip: People live here, and the lanes are narrow. Do not block the way when taking photos.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.6.name: Yamanaka Onsen and Kakusenkei Gorge
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.6.text: One of the most atmospheric spots in the Kaga Onsen area, Yamanaka Onsen sits beside Kakusenkei Gorge. A walk along the river takes about 30 minutes and passes the wooden Korogi Bridge and the striking Ayatori Bridge. The fall colors are beautiful. The bus from Kagaonsen Station takes about 30 minutes, and staying overnight lets you enjoy the hot springs.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.spots.6.tip: The public bath Kiku-no-yu is in the center of the hot-spring town. You can bathe there without staying overnight.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.stay: Staying near Kanazawa Station is most convenient. The Shinkansen, buses to Shirakawa-go, and airport buses all depart from here. If you want to explore the old streets at night, stay around Korinbo or the Higashi Chaya District. A taxi ride back to the station takes about 10 minutes.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.tagline: Two days is enough for Kanazawa: gardens, teahouse districts, seafood, and contemporary art
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.tips.0: Buses are the easiest way to get around central Kanazawa. If you plan to take several rides in one day, buy the Hokutetsu one-day city pass. IC cards are also accepted.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.tips.1: For direct flights, first check routes to Komatsu Airport, then compare them with flying to Nagoya or Tokyo and taking the Shinkansen.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.tips.2: Hokuriku often gets rain and snow in winter. As the saying goes, “Even if you forget your lunch, don't forget your umbrella.” Bring one.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.tips.3: Highway buses to Shirakawa-go have reserved seating for every passenger. Book a month ahead during peak season, or buses are often full on the day.
77212dd8a924b98ff2cb.tips.4: Crab season opens in early November. The season for female kobako crab is short and usually ends in late December.

7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.access.0.how: About 2 hours 10 minutes to Toyama Station on the Hokuriku Shinkansen Kagayaki service
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.access.1.how: About 20 minutes by Hokuriku Shinkansen, making a day trip easy
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.access.2.how: Take a bus from Shinano-Omachi to Ogizawa, then cross the Alpine Route to the Toyama side. Allow a full day.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.access.3.how: About 4 hours to Toyama via Takayama on the Hida limited express, with the option to stop in Takayama
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.0.name: Shiroebi (white shrimp)
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.0.text: These tiny, translucent shrimp have a pink tint and are commercially harvested on a large scale only in Toyama Bay. Known as the “jewels of Toyama Bay,” they taste sweet when raw and are also served as tempura or over rice.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.0.where: Seafood restaurants and white shrimp rice bowl shops in and around Toyama Station
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.1.name: Masu no sushi
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.1.text: Cured trout slices are laid over vinegared rice, wrapped in bamboo leaves, and pressed into a round wooden box. Toyama’s best-known station bento is tangy, lightly sweet, and refreshing—ideal for eating on the Shinkansen.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.1.where: Bento shops and souvenir shops at Toyama Station
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.2.name: Toyama black ramen
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.2.text: The broth is almost black with concentrated soy sauce, very salty, and topped with plenty of coarsely ground black pepper. Originally made for manual laborers to eat with rice, it is still commonly paired with a bowl of plain rice.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.2.where: Ramen shops in central Toyama and around Toyama Station
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.3.name: Hotaruika (firefly squid)
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.3.text: A Toyama Bay specialty in March–May, these tiny squid glow blue. They are most often boiled and served with vinegared miso, but also come raw in a soy-based marinade called okizuke or grilled on skewers.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.foods.3.where: Casual restaurants around Namerikawa and Uozu, and izakaya in Toyama city
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.intro.0: Toyama is best known for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route. From Tateyama Station on the Toyama side, cable cars, highland buses, electric buses, and a ropeway take you across the Northern Alps to Ogizawa in Nagano. Spring brings the towering snow walls of Yuki-no-Otani, while fall brings alpine foliage. Allow a full day for a one-way crossing, including waits and sightseeing.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.intro.1: Toyama city is compact. Half a day is enough for its glass art museum, designed by Kengo Kuma, and canal park. Two other sights deserve a separate trip: the much quieter Gokayama villages, which share World Heritage status with Shirakawa-go, and the Kurobe Gorge Railway, scheduled to reopen its full route in October 2026. Kanazawa is only about 20 minutes away by Shinkansen, so you can also visit from a base there.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.name: Toyama
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.seasons.note: The snow walls are open from mid-April to late June. Fall colors start at higher elevations in late September and spread downhill through November. The entire Alpine Route closes in winter, a good season for seafood and snowy mountain views across the bay.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.sources.0.title: Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route fares
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.sources.1.title: Official Toyama tourism website: Alpine Route guide
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.sources.2.title: Travel Voice: Kurobe Gorge Railway full reopening
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.sources.3.title: Toyama Airport: Shanghai route
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.0.fee: About ¥12,300 round-trip between Tateyama Station and Murodo
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.0.name: Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route (Murodo)
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.0.text: Murodo, the route’s highest point, sits at about 2,450 meters. In spring, buses pass between snow walls more than ten meters high. The Yuki-no-Otani walking area usually stays open until late June. In summer, a walk around the volcanic Mikurigaike Pond takes about 1 hour. Fall colors arrive early up here. In 2026, the full route operates from April 15 to November 30.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.0.tip: In peak season, buy a WEB ticket on the official website to reserve your departure time. The mountains are about 15℃ colder than the lowlands, so bring a warm jacket and sunglasses.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.1.name: Kurobe Dam
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.1.text: Japan’s tallest arch dam stands about 186 meters high and is a highlight midway along the Alpine Route. Climb about 220 steps to the observation deck for a view of the entire dam. Sightseeing water releases in summer and fall often create rainbows in the spray. Ogizawa on the Nagano side offers the quickest access; from Toyama, you must first cover much of the route.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.1.tip: A one-way trip along the full route costs about ¥10,940. If you have too much luggage, use the route’s baggage forwarding service.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.2.name: Kurobe Gorge Railway
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.2.text: This narrow-gauge train leaves Unazuki Onsen and climbs through a V-shaped gorge to Keyakidaira in about 80 minutes one way. The open cars can be very windy. After the 2024 earthquake, trains have operated only partway along the line. Full service resumes on October 1, 2026. Late October through November is best for fall colors. Stay in Unazuki Onsen after the ride.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.2.tip: The railway closes in winter. Some areas around Keyakidaira Station remain closed for repairs, and booking methods vary by section. Check the official website before you go.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.3.name: Gokayama Ainokura
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.3.text: This village of gassho-style houses shares World Heritage status with Shirakawa-go in Gifu. More than 20 thatched houses dot the hillside. With far fewer crowds than Shirakawa-go, it feels more like an everyday mountain village. Stay overnight in a traditional house; snowy winter nights are especially peaceful. The World Heritage Bus runs from Shin-Takaoka Station, and access from Shirakawa-go is also easy.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.3.tip: People live here, so stay out of private yards. Roads can be slippery in winter; wear shoes with good traction.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.4.name: Toyama Glass Art Museum
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.4.text: The museum occupies TOYAMA Kirari, designed by Kengo Kuma, where layers of wooden slats rise around the atrium. It shares the building with the city library. The permanent Glass Art Garden on the 6th floor features vividly colored works by American glass artist Dale Chihuly. About 10 minutes by tram from Toyama Station, it makes a good rainy-day stop.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.4.tip: The building’s public areas and library are free; exhibition galleries require a ticket. Check the calendar for regular monthly closing days.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.5.name: Fugan Canal Kansui Park
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.5.text: This canal park is about a 10-minute walk from Toyama Station’s north exit. At night, lights between the twin towers of Tenmon Bridge reflect on the water. A waterfront Starbucks is often called the “most beautiful Starbucks” for its setting. Come for an evening stroll and sunset; there is no need to set aside a separate trip.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.5.tip: On clear days, the observation rooms in the Tenmon Bridge towers offer views of the distant Tateyama mountain range.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.6.name: Amaharashi Coast
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.6.text: Off the coast of Takaoka, the small rocky islet of Meiwa stands against the 3,000-meter peaks of the Tateyama mountain range across Toyama Bay. Snowy mountains rising straight beyond the sea are a rare sight worldwide. Clear, cold winter mornings offer the best chance of seeing them; summer is often hazy. It is about a 10-minute walk from Amaharashi Station on the JR Himi Line.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.6.tip: Himi Line trains are infrequent, so check your return departure in advance. For snowy mountain views, choose a clear morning in November–February.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.7.name: Zuiryuji Temple
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.7.text: This is the family temple of Maeda Toshinaga, the second lord of the Kaga Domain. Its main gate, Buddha hall, and Dharma hall are all National Treasures. Covered corridors enclose the buildings in a neat square, giving the grounds a strong sense of Zen order. About a 10-minute walk from Takaoka Station’s south exit, it can be combined with the Great Buddha of Takaoka in half a day.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.spots.7.tip: The Buddha hall has lead roof tiles, giving it a different color from most temples. Look up as you enter.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.stay: The area around Toyama Station is the most convenient base, with trains to Tateyama Station, buses to Gokayama, and the Hokuriku Shinkansen all departing here. For mountain sunrises and starry skies, book a mountain hotel in Murodo.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.tagline: Tateyama’s snow walls, Kurobe Gorge, and 3,000-meter snowy peaks across the bay
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.tips.0: The entire Alpine Route closes from December to mid-April of the following year. Winter visits to Toyama center on seafood and snowy mountain views across the bay.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.tips.1: The Alpine Route uses 6 types of transportation, and each transfer can involve a wait in peak season. Start with the first departure of the morning for a more relaxed trip.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.tips.2: Toyama Airport’s Shanghai and Dalian routes are currently suspended. Travelers can fly to Komatsu, Nagoya, or Tokyo instead.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.tips.3: Hokuriku gets plenty of winter rain and snow. Carry a folding umbrella year-round.
7a3910a0bbb2a1b6245f.tips.4: Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your license and accompanying documents; check the official requirements. Buses and local JR trains are options for reaching Gokayama and Amaharashi.

7af25d5c510578a0d34b.0: [Rule #1: Traction] Never wear canvas sneakers or flat trainers! Pack deep-lug waterproof snow boots or pick up ¥1,000 clip-on rubber cleats (suberidome) at Sapporo's underground ABC-MART or convenience stores on arrival.
7af25d5c510578a0d34b.1: [JR seat secret] On the Hakodate Main Line from Sapporo to Otaru, grab a right-hand window seat—past Zenibako, the tracks hug the wintry Sea of Japan snow beaches.
7af25d5c510578a0d34b.2: [16:00 sunset clock] Light fades sharply by 15:30 and hits full night by 16:15 in winter Hokkaido; schedule all outdoor snow scenery and Otaru canal walks before 15:00.
7af25d5c510578a0d34b.3: [Airport as an attraction] Arrive 3.5 hours early at New Chitose Airport! The Domestic Terminal's Ramen Dojo, Royce Chocolate World, and Rokkatei/Kitakaro sweet hall rival downtown.

7afc12ccc1b2bae256ee.0: Board a Kyoto city bus toward Eikando or Tofuku-ji at 10:30 AM in late November and you'll mostly see two things: frozen red brake lights outside the window and a wall of heads on Tsutenkyo Bridge. Peak-season Kyoto isn't ruined—it's just that 90% of visitors pile into the exact same flagship temples during the five-hour window from 10:00 to 15:00.
7afc12ccc1b2bae256ee.1: This eastern-to-southern Kyoto route is the sharpest version I've honed across three autumn seasons, built on two iron rules: skip cross-town buses completely in favor of the Tozai Subway Line, walking, and the JR Nara Line; hit crowd-sensitive Eikando right at its 08:30 opening, retreat to spacious Nanzen-ji for midday yudofu, and handle Tofuku-ji or evening illuminations with smart timing.

7be98fe0f25fa6857d0e.0: Booking a central-coast beach resort without a rental car—you end up stranded outside the hotel facing ten-to-twenty-thousand-yen taxi bills; anchoring at Naha's Asahibashi Station beats it every time.
7be98fe0f25fa6857d0e.1: Heading out on a winter whale boat without seasickness medication or in a thin T-shirt—open-ocean swells and sharp wind will leave you shivering and queasy within an hour.
7be98fe0f25fa6857d0e.2: Riding northern public buses without checking the final departure—Okinawa's highway buses wrap up early, and losing track of time at the aquarium leaves you stuck.
7be98fe0f25fa6857d0e.3: Eating every meal directly on Kokusai-dori—step into side alleys, Makishi Market's second floor, or local Shintoshin spots for better flavor at lower prices.

7d22a99673f489c77359.access.0.how: Most routes connect through San Francisco, Los Angeles, or Seattle. The transpacific leg takes about 11–13 hours, followed by about 2.5 hours to Denver.
7d22a99673f489c77359.access.1.how: The A Line commuter train reaches downtown in about 37 minutes. Rocky Mountain National Park’s east entrance is about 1.5–2 hours by car.
7d22a99673f489c77359.access.2.how: Driving to Denver via I-70 takes about 8 hours for 840 kilometers (520 miles). From Moab, it’s another 6 hours east.
7d22a99673f489c77359.access.3.how: Colorado Springs is about 110 kilometers and 1–1.5 hours away. Aspen takes about 3.5 hours, and Great Sand Dunes takes about 4 hours.
7d22a99673f489c77359.cover.alt: Maroon Bells surrounded by golden aspens
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.0.name: Colorado green chile
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.0.text: A thick stew made with roasted green chiles and chunks of pork. It’s spicy and fragrant. Locals like to “smother” almost anything with it, including burritos, burgers, hash browns, and even breakfast eggs. Chiles from Pueblo in southern Colorado are especially prized.
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.0.where: Mexican restaurants and breakfast spots in Denver
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.1.name: Denver omelette
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.1.text: A classic American diner breakfast: eggs filled with diced ham, green peppers, and onions, often topped with cheese and served with hash browns and toast. Have a filling breakfast in Denver before heading into the mountains, and you won’t go hungry on the drive.
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.2.name: Palisade peaches
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.2.text: The town of Palisade, near Grand Junction in western Colorado, is a major peach and grape-growing region. Abundant sunshine and large day-to-night temperature swings produce exceptionally juicy, sweet peaches. Roadside stands sell them by the box from late July–September, and Denver farmers markets also carry them.
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.2.where: Palisade orchards and Denver farmers markets (July–September)
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.3.name: Craft beer
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.3.text: Denver and Boulder have more craft breweries than you can count. Many have tasting rooms where you can order a flight of small pours. Alcohol affects you more quickly at high elevation, so drink less during your first 1–2 days. If you’re renting a car, make sure someone in your group stays sober.
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.3.where: Denver’s RiNo Art District and Lower Downtown
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.4.name: Rocky Mountain oysters
7d22a99673f489c77359.foods.4.text: Despite the name, these are battered and fried bull testicles, a dish left over from ranching days. The texture is somewhat like fried chicken. They’re a novelty dish available at some old-school Western steakhouses and sports venues in Denver, usually served with cocktail sauce.
7d22a99673f489c77359.intro.0: Colorado is the highest state in the United States by average elevation. The Rocky Mountains run through its center, with more than 50 peaks rising above 4,200 meters. Denver is the gateway in the east, and you can reach the mountains in 1–2 hours by car. Rocky Mountain National Park’s high mountain roads, Aspen’s aspen groves, the cliff dwellings and Great Sand Dunes in the southwest all offer something different.
7d22a99673f489c77359.intro.1: The best seasons are July–August for alpine wildflowers and mid-September–early October for golden aspens. Mountain weather changes quickly. Summer brings afternoon thunderstorms almost every day, so try to finish hikes and high-elevation drives in the morning. Winter is ski season, and mountain roads require snow tires.
7d22a99673f489c77359.intro.2: Elevation is the first thing to take seriously. Denver sits at about 1,600 meters, while mountain roads rise above 3,700 meters. It’s common to have headaches, shortness of breath, or trouble sleeping during your first 1–2 days. Spend your first night in Denver to acclimate, drink plenty of water, limit alcohol, and don’t head straight up into the mountains after landing.
7d22a99673f489c77359.name: Colorado
7d22a99673f489c77359.seasons.note: High mountain roads are open June–September. Wildflowers peak in July–August, and golden aspens appear from mid-September–early October. December–March is snow season, and mountain roads require traction equipment.
