7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.0.name: Denver and Red Rocks
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.0.text: Denver is known as the “Mile High City,” at about 1,600 meters above sea level. The restored Union Station area anchors Lower Downtown, with restaurants and craft breweries clustered nearby. One step at the State Capitol is marked “one mile high.” Red Rocks, a 30-minute drive west, is built between two enormous red rock formations. Entry is free when no event is taking place, and an outdoor concert on a summer night is hard to beat.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.0.tip: Spend your first night in Denver to adjust to the elevation. Red Rocks tickets sell out early, so check the event calendar ahead of time.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.1.fee: About $35 per vehicle (7 days), plus $100 per foreign visitor
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.1.name: Rocky Mountain National Park
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.1.text: About 2 hours from Denver, with the entrance in Estes Park. The Bear Lake corridor is best for most visitors: the loop around Bear Lake is about 1 kilometer, while the round-trip hike to Dream Lake and Emerald Lake is about 6 kilometers. The trail passes alpine lakes and cirques. In fall, large herds of elk are common in the meadows, and bulls bugle during the September rut.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.1.tip: Timed-entry reservations are required from May 22, 2026–mid-October. The Bear Lake corridor requires a 5–18 entry time, while other areas require 9–14.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.2.fee: Included with the national park entry fee
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.2.name: Trail Ridge Road
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.2.text: This high mountain road crosses Rocky Mountain National Park. Its highest point is about 3,713 meters, making it the highest continuous paved road in the United States. For more than a dozen kilometers in the middle, the road stays above the tree line, with tundra and distant snowcapped peaks on both sides. Marmots and elk are often visible along the road. Driving from Estes Park to Grand Lake on the west side takes about 2 hours for 77 kilometers, even without stops.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.2.tip: The road is generally open from late May–mid-October. Afternoon thunderstorms are common, so don’t linger at the summit and bring a jacket.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.3.name: Garden of the Gods
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.3.text: This free city park on the edge of Colorado Springs features rows of upright red sandstone formations, with Pikes Peak behind them. A flat, paved trail loops around the central formations for about 2 kilometers and is manageable for older adults and children. Climbing routes and horseback riding are also available. Just over 1 hour from Denver, it’s a good stop on the way to Great Sand Dunes or farther south.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.3.tip: The rocks glow brightest at sunrise, when parking is also easier. The visitor center terrace offers views of the formations and Pikes Peak in the same frame.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.4.fee: About $16 per person round trip by shuttle
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.4.name: Maroon Bells
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.4.text: About 16 kilometers southwest of Aspen, the two striped, maroon-colored peaks are reflected in Maroon Lake. They are among Colorado’s most photographed mountain scenes. The aspen-covered slopes turn bright gold in late September, making this the busiest time. A level path runs along the lake, and those who want a longer walk can hike to Crater Lake, about 5.8 kilometers round trip.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.4.tip: From May–October, reserve a shuttle or parking permit on the official website. Permits go quickly during aspen season.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.5.fee: About $30 per vehicle in peak season
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.5.name: Mesa Verde National Park
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.5.text: Seven or eight hundred years ago, Pueblo people built stone villages in cliff alcoves on the mesa. Cliff Palace has more than 100 rooms and is the largest cliff dwelling in North America. You can see it from roadside overlooks, but a ranger-led tour is more rewarding: you’ll descend stone steps and climb several ladders. The drive from Durango to the entrance takes about 1 hour, followed by another 45 minutes on mountain roads to the cliff dwellings.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.5.tip: Cliff dwelling tours generally run from May–October. Tickets are released on recreation.gov 14 days in advance and cost about $8 per person. The park does not accept cash.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.6.fee: About $25 per vehicle, no reservation required
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.6.name: Great Sand Dunes National Park
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.6.text: The tallest sand dunes in North America rise suddenly at the foot of the Rockies, reaching about 230 meters, with snowcapped ridges behind them. You can climb the dunes or go sandboarding. From late May–June, snowmelt feeds Medano Creek into a shallow stream in front of the dunes, where children play in the water. The park is relatively quiet, and the night skies are excellent.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.6.tip: In summer, the sand is extremely hot in the afternoon and thunderstorms are common, so go in the morning. Rent a sandboard outside the park before entering.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.7.name: Million Dollar Highway
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.7.text: The 40-kilometer section of US 550 between Silverton and Ouray crosses Red Mountain Pass at about 3,350 meters. The road hugs steep cliffs, and many curves have no guardrails. Along the way are abandoned mines, red slopes, and waterfalls. The scenery is best when the aspens turn gold in late September. Ouray sits at the bottom of a canyon and is known as “the Switzerland of America,” with hot springs for soaking.
7d22a99673f489c77359.spots.7.tip: If you’re afraid of heights, drive slowly in daylight on a clear day. Avoid the road after dark or during snow. It is often closed temporarily in winter because of snow.
7d22a99673f489c77359.stay: Stay near Denver Union Station when arriving or departing. Base yourself in Estes Park for Rocky Mountain National Park, Aspen or nearby Snowmass for fall colors, and Durango or Ouray for Mesa Verde and the Million Dollar Highway in the southwest.
7d22a99673f489c77359.tagline: High mountain roads, golden aspens, and sand dunes in the Rockies
7d22a99673f489c77359.tips.0: High elevation: Denver is about 1,600 meters above sea level, and high mountain roads exceed 3,700 meters. Slow down, drink plenty of water during your first 1–2 days, and descend if a headache gets worse.
7d22a99673f489c77359.tips.1: Rocky Mountain National Park charges an additional $100 per foreign visitor age 16 and over. Mesa Verde and Great Sand Dunes do not charge this fee. The annual pass costs $250 and covers one entire vehicle.
7d22a99673f489c77359.tips.2: Mountain areas see afternoon thunderstorms almost every day in summer. Get below the tree line before noon, and turn back as soon as you hear thunder.
7d22a99673f489c77359.tips.3: From September–May, traction laws may be activated on the mountain section of I-70. Confirm tire requirements with your rental company. Licence rules depend on where your licence was issued; check with the rental company about carrying your passport and an English translation.

7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.0.items.0.note: Arrive before opening and line up first for the most popular rides
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.0.items.2.note: Stay in the park for the castle fireworks at night
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.0.move: Hotels near Disney offer shuttle service, saving you the parking fee
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.0.title: Magic Kingdom
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.1.items.1.note: One day is enough for only one park, so choose based on your children's ages and interests
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.1.move: It takes about 20–30 minutes to drive from Disney to Universal
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.1.title: Universal Studios or Epic Universe
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.2.items.1.note: Leave for the south by 3 p.m. to reach Miami around evening
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.2.move: Orlando to Kennedy Space Center takes about 1 hour; then drive south on I-95 for about 3.5 hours
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.2.title: See rockets, then drive south
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.3.move: Miami to the Royal Palm Visitor Center takes about 1–1.5 hours; return to South Beach in the afternoon
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.3.title: The Everglades and South Beach
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.4.move: Key West is about 260 kilometers from Miami, or about a 4-hour drive. Stop at a beach by one of the bridges along the way
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.4.title: Take the Overseas Highway to Key West
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.5.items.0.note: Bike around Old Town and visit the Ernest Hemingway Home and Museum in the morning
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.5.items.2.note: Leave at noon to drive back, return the car at Miami International Airport, and take an evening flight
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.5.move: Key West to Miami International Airport takes about 4 hours. Sunday afternoons are often congested
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.days.5.title: Breakfast in Old Town, then drive back
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.for: Families traveling with children who can drive and want both theme parks and beaches
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.season: November–April, avoiding March spring break and Christmas
7e41200cb3ecf7fa896e.summary: Fly into Orlando and out of Miami. Pick up a rental car at Orlando International Airport and return it in Miami. Spend one day at each of two theme parks, then visit the space center on day 3 before driving south to Miami. On the morning of day 4, see alligators in the Everglades, then return to the beach in the afternoon. On day 5, follow the Overseas Highway to Key West for one night. On day 6, drive back to Miami for an evening flight. Theme park tickets use date-based pricing, so buy ahead.

808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.access.0.how: There are currently no nonstop flights to Philadelphia from mainland China. Most travelers fly to New York or Washington and continue by train, or connect through another U.S. city to Philadelphia International Airport (PHL).
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.access.1.how: Amtrak takes about 1–1.5 hours to Philadelphia's 30th Street Station. Connecting commuter trains through New Jersey are cheaper but slower.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.access.2.how: Amtrak takes about 1.5–2 hours to Philadelphia.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.access.3.how: About 1 hour by plane, 5 hours by car, or 7 hours by Amtrak.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.cover.alt: Independence Hall and Independence Square in Philadelphia in spring
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.0.name: Philly cheesesteak
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.0.text: A long roll filled with thinly sliced beef cooked on a griddle, onions, and melted cheese is Philadelphia's signature sandwich. Two longtime rivals face each other across a South Philadelphia street, though locals each have their own neighborhood favorite. When ordering, specify your cheese and whether you want onions.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.0.where: Around the Italian Market in South Philadelphia and at Reading Terminal Market.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.1.name: Roast pork sandwich
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.1.text: Many Philadelphians consider this the city's true local sandwich: thin slices of slow-roasted pork soaked in their juices, with sautéed broccoli rabe and sharp aged provolone. It is savory, rich, and slightly bitter. A longtime stall at Reading Terminal Market draws long lines.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.1.where: Reading Terminal Market and South Philadelphia delis.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.2.name: Philly soft pretzel
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.2.text: Philadelphia's chewy pretzels are shaped like elongated 8s, baked together in rows, and sprinkled with coarse salt. Sold at street stalls and convenience stores in the morning, they are eaten with yellow mustard and are the city's cheapest snack.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.2.where: Street stalls and convenience stores; Amish stalls at Reading Terminal Market make them fresh.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.3.name: Shoofly pie
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.3.text: This traditional Pennsylvania Dutch and Amish dessert has a molasses filling and crumb topping. Very sweet, with a texture like moist cake, it pairs well with unsweetened black coffee. Farm markets and bakeries around Lancaster are the easiest places to find it.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.3.where: Amish markets and bakeries around Lancaster.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.4.name: Pittsburgh-style sandwich with fries
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.4.text: This Pittsburgh dockworker tradition puts the fries and sweet-tart coleslaw right inside the sandwich, along with meat and cheese—a whole meal in one hand. Portions are large enough for two to share.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.foods.4.where: Long-established sandwich shops in Pittsburgh's Strip District and downtown.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.intro.0: Most visitors to Pennsylvania go only to Philadelphia. The Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution were signed at Independence Hall, and the Liberty Bell is across the street. A few blocks of Old City cover the story of America's founding. Philadelphia is only an hour or two by train from New York and Washington, making it an easy overnight stop on an East Coast trip.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.intro.1: Head west for another side of Pennsylvania. Around Lancaster, Amish communities still use horse-drawn buggies and live without electricity, amid broad stretches of farmland and wooden barns. Gettysburg preserves the battlefield of a decisive Civil War battle. Farther west, Frank Lloyd Wright's Fallingwater sits in a wooded valley near the steel city of Pittsburgh.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.intro.2: These places are far apart, and public transportation does not reach the countryside. To visit Lancaster, Gettysburg, and Fallingwater, you will generally need to drive or join a local day tour.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.name: Pennsylvania
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.seasons.note: April–June and September–October are the most comfortable months. Fall colors in the western mountains are best around mid-October. July–August is hot and humid, January–February is cold, and Fallingwater closes in winter.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.0.fee: Free; online reservations cost about $1 per ticket
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.0.name: Independence Hall
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.0.text: The Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776 and the U.S. Constitution in 1787 in this redbrick building. National Park Service guides lead tours into the Assembly Room to see the tables and chairs used for those meetings. Visit neighboring Congress Hall, where the early U.S. Congress met, while you are here.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.0.tip: When reservations are required, book timed-entry tickets at recreation.gov up to 30 days ahead. Next-day tickets are released at 5 p.m. the day before.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.1.name: Liberty Bell Center
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.1.text: The famous bronze bell with its large crack sits in a glass pavilion across from Independence Hall. Through the window behind it, you can frame both landmarks in one photo. Exhibits explain how the bell became a symbol of the abolitionist and civil rights movements. No reservation is needed; just pass through security.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.1.tip: Arrive when it opens at 9 a.m. Security lines grow once tour groups arrive.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.2.name: Reading Terminal Market
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.2.text: Opened in 1893 beneath a train station, this indoor market now packs in dozens of stalls selling cheesesteaks, roast pork sandwiches, Amish desserts and pretzels, and ice cream. Lunch is the busiest time, and finding a seat takes luck. You can buy your food first, then look for a table.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.2.tip: Amish stalls generally do not open every day, and some stalls close on Sundays. Check ahead if you have a particular one in mind.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.3.name: Philadelphia Museum of Art
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.3.text: This Greek temple-style building stands on a hill above the steps made famous by Rocky. Many visitors come just to run up them. The collection is equally impressive, with European paintings, works by Duchamp, and an entire relocated temple cloister. From the top of the steps, a tree-lined boulevard stretches toward City Hall.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.3.tip: You do not need a ticket to climb the steps and enjoy the view. Sunset is especially beautiful.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.4.name: Lancaster County Amish Country
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.4.text: About 1.5 hours west of Philadelphia by car, fields, red barns, and windmills stretch across the countryside. On the roads, you will often slow down behind black horse-drawn buggies. Visit Amish farms and markets for homemade jam, handmade quilts, and pies. Amish people prefer not to be photographed, so keep your camera on the scenery.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.4.tip: Amish communities worship on Sundays, when many shops and farms are closed.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.5.fee: Battlefield access is free; the museum package costs about $21
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.5.name: Gettysburg National Military Park
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.5.text: The Civil War's bloodiest battle raged here for three days in 1863. Lincoln later delivered his famous Gettysburg Address here. Drive through the battlefield past more than a thousand monuments and artillery positions. Start with the film and cyclorama at the visitor center, then follow the driving-tour map.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.5.tip: You can book a licensed guide to ride in your car and explain the battlefield. Reserve ahead.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.6.name: Fallingwater
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.6.text: One of Frank Lloyd Wright's signature works from the 1930s, this house sits directly over a small waterfall. Its concrete terraces project outward in layers, blending with the rocks and stream. Interior visits are by guided tour only. The classic view is from the overlook downstream. The drive from Pittsburgh takes about 1.5 hours.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.6.tip: Book a tour ahead on the official website. Closed Wednesdays and from January to mid-March. Children under 6 cannot enter the house.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.7.name: Mount Washington, Pittsburgh
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.7.text: Pittsburgh sits where two rivers meet to form the Ohio River. Downtown occupies a triangular peninsula surrounded by seemingly countless bridges. Ride the 19th-century Duquesne Incline up Mount Washington for views of the three rivers, rows of yellow steel bridges, and the city skyline. Both dusk and nighttime are beautiful.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.spots.7.tip: Go up half an hour before sunset to see the rivers in daylight and the city after dark.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.stay: In Philadelphia, stay in Old City or Center City near City Hall for walks to Independence Hall and Reading Terminal Market. For Fallingwater or Pittsburgh, spend a night in downtown Pittsburgh.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.tagline: America's birthplace, with history in the cities and Amish life in the countryside
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.tips.0: Independence Hall tickets carry a fee of about $1 each and cannot be refunded or changed. If you miss out, check again at 5 p.m. the following day for the next day's tickets.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.tips.1: Sales tax is about 6% in Pennsylvania and about 8% in Philadelphia. Many basic clothing items are exempt from sales tax in Pennsylvania.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.tips.2: You will need to drive to Lancaster, Gettysburg, and Fallingwater. Requirements depend on your driver's license; check the Pennsylvania transportation department's official rules for foreign licenses before setting out.
808fa73a7e49d095b7b2.tips.3: Fallingwater closes in winter and on Wednesdays. Check opening dates and children's age restrictions when booking.

80d0fdbe0582550d9fc2.options.0.note: Reserved seating throughout and the fastest option. Meitetsu Nagoya Station is next to JR Nagoya Station, making transfers to the Shinkansen easy.
80d0fdbe0582550d9fc2.options.0.price: about ¥1,430 (about ¥980 for the fare + about ¥450 for the μ ticket)

80d0fdbe0582550d9fc2.options.1.note: Regular cars require only the fare and are just a few minutes slower. If you are staying around Kanayama, get off there.

81dc22abf7130ef0bb2a.cost: All transit included in pass; 5 black eggs ~¥500
81dc22abf7130ef0bb2a.paragraphs.0: This is Japan's finest zero-hiking mountain loop: zig-zag up by Tozan train to Gora (stop one station early at Chokoku-no-Mori if you want an hour at the Open-Air Museum), transfer to the 10-minute steep cable car up to Sounzan, and step into the glass Hakone Ropeway.
81dc22abf7130ef0bb2a.paragraphs.1: Cresting the ridge above Owakudani is pure theater—hundreds of feet below, a barren crater belches white sulfur plumes while snow-capped Mt. Fuji looms straight ahead on crisp mornings. Hop off at Owakudani for a warm bag of sulfur-boiled black eggs (kuro-tamago) with salt, then continue descending by ropeway to Togendai Port on Lake Ashi.
81dc22abf7130ef0bb2a.photo.alt: Hakone Ropeway gliding above steaming Owakudani valley with Mount Fuji
81dc22abf7130ef0bb2a.photo.caption: The moment the Hakone Ropeway clears Sounzan ridge, steaming Owakudani opens underneath with Mt. Fuji rising cleanly across the clouds.
81dc22abf7130ef0bb2a.tip: High volcanic gases or strong gusts can temporarily pause the Hakone Ropeway in favor of substitute buses—check the Hakone Navi live status page before leaving Shinjuku.
81dc22abf7130ef0bb2a.title: Switchback Train → Gora → Owakudani Ropeway for Black Eggs & Smoking Vents

82158c40f8654b801dd9.days.3.items.1.note: See the Three Sisters from Echo Point, then ride Scenic World's railway and cable cars

82158c40f8654b801dd9.days.5.move: Rent a car or join a tour to Phillip Island in the afternoon, about 2 hours each way; drive back at night

82158c40f8654b801dd9.days.6.items.1.note: Look for wild koalas at Kennett River, then have lunch in Apollo Bay
82158c40f8654b801dd9.days.6.move: Melbourne→Port Campbell takes about 4.5–5 hours along the coast, not including stops
82158c40f8654b801dd9.days.6.title: Drive west along the Great Ocean Road
82158c40f8654b801dd9.days.7.items.0.note: Visit the Twelve Apostles and Loch Ard Gorge again around sunrise

82158c40f8654b801dd9.for: First-time visitors to Australia who want to see its two major cities and a coastal road
82158c40f8654b801dd9.season: September–November and March–April are most comfortable
82158c40f8654b801dd9.summary: Spend 4 nights in Sydney: one day each for the harbor, coastal walks, and the Blue Mountains. On Day 5, fly to Melbourne, explore its laneways and markets, then head to Phillip Island in the evening to see the penguins come ashore. Spend the last 2 days driving the Great Ocean Road. Stay 1 night in Port Campbell, then see the Twelve Apostles early the next morning before driving back to Melbourne.
82158c40f8654b801dd9.title: Sydney, Melbourne and the Great Ocean Road · 8 days

833c1fef3665812e2fe4.days.0.move: Kansai International Airport → Kyoto Station by HARUKA: about 75–80 minutes; Kyoto Station → Inari Station by JR: about 5 minutes
833c1fef3665812e2fe4.days.0.title: Arrive in Kyoto · Senbon Torii
833c1fef3665812e2fe4.days.1.move: Arrive at Kiyomizu-dera when it opens, then walk downhill to Gion; take a bus or taxi to Ginkaku-ji in the afternoon
833c1fef3665812e2fe4.days.1.title: A day in Higashiyama
833c1fef3665812e2fe4.days.2.move: The JR Sagano Line takes about 15 minutes to Saga-Arashiyama Station; a taxi from Arashiyama to Kinkaku-ji takes about 20 minutes
833c1fef3665812e2fe4.days.2.title: Arashiyama and Kinkaku-ji

833c1fef3665812e2fe4.days.4.title: Osaka Castle, then departure
833c1fef3665812e2fe4.for: First-time visitors to Japan who want to see Kyoto, Nara, and Osaka

833c1fef3665812e2fe4.summary: Stay 3 nights in Kyoto and 1 night in Osaka, changing hotels just once. Explore Kyoto by area: visit Fushimi Inari Taisha in the early evening on day 1, Higashiyama on day 2, and Arashiyama and Kinkaku-ji on day 3. On day 4, take your luggage through Nara to Osaka, feed the deer, see the Great Buddha, and explore Dotonbori at night. Spend the final half day at Osaka Castle, then head to the airport from Namba.
833c1fef3665812e2fe4.title: Kansai for your first visit · 5 days

849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.access.0.how: Kyushu Shinkansen from Hakata to Kagoshima-Chuo; Mizuho trains take about 1 hour 20 minutes
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.access.1.how: Airport bus to Kagoshima-Chuo Station takes about 40 minutes. Services are frequent, and reservations are not required.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.access.2.how: Kyushu Shinkansen from Kumamoto to Kagoshima-Chuo takes about 45 minutes at the fastest
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.access.3.how: High-speed ferries from Kagoshima Port take about 1 hour 50 minutes. Flights are also available. Services are easily suspended in strong winds.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.0.name: Kurobuta pork shabu-shabu
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.0.text: Kagoshima's Kurobuta pork has fine-grained meat and sweet fat. Swish it in the hot pot for a few seconds, then dip it in soba dipping sauce or ponzu. Tonkatsu is another classic way to enjoy the pork.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.0.where: Specialty restaurants around Tenmonkan and Kagoshima-Chuo Station
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.1.name: Shirokuma shaved ice
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.1.text: This shaved ice is topped with condensed milk, fruit, and red beans. From above, it looks like a polar bear's face. The portions are large, so one bowl is just right for two people. It is a Kagoshima summer staple.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.1.where: Dessert shops and cafes around Tenmonkan
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.2.name: Kagoshima ramen
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.2.text: The broth is made with pork and chicken bones. It is lighter than Hakata ramen, with thicker noodles. Many shops first serve a dish of pickled radish to eat alongside the ramen. That is the local custom.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.3.name: Satsuma-age
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.3.text: Fish paste is seasoned with a little sweet rice wine and sugar, then deep-fried. The texture is soft and springy, with a mild sweetness. Varieties include vegetables and cheese. Freshly fried pieces are best eaten hot as you walk.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.3.where: Long-running shops and souvenir stores around Kagoshima-Chuo Station and Tenmonkan
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.4.name: Imo shochu
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.4.text: This distilled spirit is made from sweet potatoes and has a roasted sweet-potato aroma. Locals often mix it with hot water, which softens the alcohol and brings out the fragrance. It pairs well with Kurobuta pork and Satsuma-age.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.foods.4.where: Izakaya and liquor shops in Tenmonkan
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.intro.0: Sakurajima, which occasionally sends up plumes of smoke, sits just across from Kagoshima City. A 15-minute ferry takes you to the volcanic island, and on ashfall days, residents go out with umbrellas. The city is home to Sengan-en, the garden of the Shimazu family, lords of the Satsuma domain. Many figures from the Meiji Restoration also came from here, making it an interesting stop for history buffs.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.intro.1: An hour south is Ibusuki, where you can be buried in hot sand for a sand bath. Chiran preserves samurai residences and the Chiran Peace Museum for Kamikaze Pilots. Northeast, Kirishima has hot springs and a shrine. Yakushima lies offshore and requires a high-speed ferry or flight, so allow at least 2 days on its own. The southern end of the Kyushu Shinkansen is at Kagoshima-Chuo Station, making the city easy to reach from Fukuoka.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.name: Kagoshima
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.seasons.note: Spring and fall are the most comfortable. Winter is mild and good for sand baths. In summer, volcanic ash from Sakurajima often blows toward the city. Yakushima is rainy year-round, especially during the rainy season.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.sources.0.title: Sakurajima Ferry fares (Kagoshima City)
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.sources.1.title: JR Kyushu Ibusuki no Tamatebako train guide
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.sources.2.title: Kagoshima Prefecture tourism site: Toppy & Rocket high-speed ferries
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.sources.3.title: Sengan-en official site
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.0.name: Sakurajima
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.0.text: This active volcano is still erupting. It takes about 15 minutes to reach it by ferry from the city port, and the fare is very cheap. On the island, take the sightseeing bus to Yunohira Observatory for close-up views of the mountain and lava fields. Soak your feet at the foot bath near the port, then take the ferry back. Half a day is enough.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.0.tip: Ferry tickets can be paid for with credit cards and transit cards. Access near the summit may be restricted when volcanic activity is high. Wear a mask during ashfall.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.1.name: Sengan-en
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.1.text: This villa garden of the Shimazu family, lords of the Satsuma domain, uses Sakurajima across the bay as a borrowed landscape, like a miniature mountain, and Kinko Bay as a pond. Its wide-open views are rare among Japanese gardens. The nearby Shoko Shuseikan Museum displays the remains of a modern factory from that era and is part of the World Heritage site commemorating Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.1.tip: Take the sightseeing bus and get off at Sengan-en-mae. While there, look for the garden's two-stick dango and the Satsuma kiriko glass workshop.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.2.name: Shiroyama Observatory
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.2.text: This small hill in the city center was the final battlefield of the Satsuma Rebellion. The observatory faces Kinko Bay and Sakurajima and offers the classic view of the volcano. You can also see the city lights at night. Along the path up the hill is the cave where Saigo Takamori hid during his final days.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.2.tip: Take the sightseeing bus and get off at Shiroyama. Sakurajima's silhouette is best at sunrise, so go in the morning if you can get up early.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.3.fee: Sand bath from about ¥1,500, including a yukata
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.3.name: Ibusuki Sand Bath
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.3.text: Change into a yukata and lie in hot sand by the sea. Staff use shovels to bury you up to your neck, leaving only your head exposed. After about ten minutes, you'll be sweating heavily. Rinse off, then soak in a regular hot spring. Saraku Sand Bath Hall is the best-known facility. It sits by the beach, with views of the sea.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.3.tip: The Ibusuki no Tamatebako sightseeing train takes about 50 minutes from Kagoshima-Chuo. All seats are reserved, so book ahead.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.4.name: Chiran Samurai Residences & Peace Museum
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.4.text: Chiran's samurai-residence district preserves seven gardens open to the public. The neatly trimmed hedges and stone walls have a distinctive charm. Nearby, the Chiran Peace Museum for Kamikaze Pilots tells the story of the young pilots who departed from here near the end of World War II and displays their farewell letters. The exhibits are sobering.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.4.tip: The bus from Kagoshima-Chuo Station takes more than 1 hour, and services are infrequent. You can combine it with Ibusuki in the same day.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.5.name: Kirishima Jingu
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.5.text: Surrounded by towering cedar trees, this vermilion shrine has finely carved, brightly colored buildings and is known as the Nikko of western Japan. The maple leaves along the approach are beautiful in fall. Nearby Kirishima Onsen lets you pair a day of bathing with a shrine visit.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.5.tip: Take the JR train to Kirishima-Jingu Station, then transfer to a bus for about 10 minutes. Kirishima Onsen is in the mountains and is colder in winter.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.6.name: Shiratani Unsuikyo, Yakushima
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.6.text: This primeval forest is thick with moss, streams, giant cedars, and moss-covered ground. It was one of the inspirations for Hayao Miyazaki's Princess Mononoke. The round trip to the mossy forest takes about 4 hours and is moderately difficult. It is much more manageable than the 10-hour route to Jomon Sugi and suits most visitors.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.6.tip: A forest conservation contribution is required. Yakushima gets frequent rain, so bring rain gear and slip-resistant hiking shoes.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.7.name: Jomon Sugi
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.7.text: Yakushima's most famous ancient cedar is said to be several thousand years old, with a trunk so broad that you have to walk around it. But the round trip from Arakawa Trailhead is about 22 kilometers and takes around 10 hours. Most of the route follows old railway tracks, with a climb near the end. If your fitness is average, consider joining a guided group.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.spots.7.tip: Take the mountain bus to Arakawa Trailhead around 5 a.m. or earlier. Order a boxed lunch and bus ticket the night before, and return before dark.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.stay: Stay around Kagoshima-Chuo Station or Tenmonkan. The former is convenient for the Shinkansen and airport buses, while the latter has the greatest concentration of restaurants and shops. Stay in Ibusuki for sand baths, Kirishima for hot springs, and Miyanoura or Anbo on Yakushima.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.tagline: A city that lives with an active volcano, with Yakushima farther south
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.tips.0: The city sightseeing bus is the easiest way to reach urban attractions. Some day passes also include the Sakurajima ferry, so check the coverage before buying.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.tips.1: Sakurajima often sends volcanic ash into the air. Bring a mask and glasses. Ash can easily get under contact lenses.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.tips.2: Ferries and flights to Yakushima are easily canceled because of weather. Leave at least 1 buffer day after your return trip.
849304aefe3e9e0c5cb9.tips.3: Driving in Japan depends on your licence and the required documents. To visit Yakushima and Chiran, you can use buses, private cars with drivers, or guided tours.

84d0a899f70af57af07a.author.name: Suhe
84d0a899f70af57af07a.author.role: Value island & family travel · car-free Okinawa field-tester
84d0a899f70af57af07a.cover.alt: Wild humpback whale tail fluke breaching out of deep blue Kerama Islands waters off Okinawa
84d0a899f70af57af07a.cover.caption: Every year from late December to early April, humpback whales migrate from Alaska to calve in the warm Kerama waters—watching a massive fluke slice through jewel-blue ocean leaves the whole boat speechless.
84d0a899f70af57af07a.excerpt: Think you cannot enjoy Okinawa without driving? From December to April, humpback whales migrate to Okinawa while flights and hotels cost half of summer peak rates. Tested over 4 days anchored beside Naha's Asahibashi Monorail Station, pairing Yanbaru Express buses to Churaumi Aquarium with free-pickup whale tours—every yen accounted for.

84d0a899f70af57af07a.sources.2.title: Yui Rail (Okinawa Urban Monorail) Official: Fares, 24-hour passes & IC card guide
84d0a899f70af57af07a.subtitle: Balmy 20°C winter warmth with zero car rental or IDP hassle—anchor your hotel at Naha's Asahibashi Station and ride free hotel shuttles straight to the whale boats.
84d0a899f70af57af07a.title: Car-free winter Okinawa in 4 days for CNY 4,200: stay at Asahibashi, bus to Churaumi & watch Kerama humpbacks

85c1c4545a370b6ed66f.cost: Santa Barbara County Courthouse tower free; parking ~$3–6
85c1c4545a370b6ed66f.paragraphs.0: Heading south from Morro Bay toward Los Angeles on day three, the rugged Northern California headlands mellow into sun-soaked, palm-fringed Southern California. Detour briefly into Solvang, a fairy-tale village founded by Danish immigrants, for warm flaky Danish pastries, æbleskiver pancake puffs, and coffee at a traditional bakery.
85c1c4545a370b6ed66f.paragraphs.1: Another 45 minutes brings you to Santa Barbara, often dubbed the American Riviera. Step inside the free Spanish Colonial Revival Santa Barbara County Courthouse and ride the elevator to the fourth-floor clock tower deck for a 360° panorama of terracotta roofs, whitewashed walls, coastal mountains, and the Pacific beyond. Grab an avocado-packed burrito at a Mexican spot along pedestrian-friendly State Street before getting back on the road.
85c1c4545a370b6ed66f.phase: Step 05 · Day 3 morning: Danish village & Santa Barbara's red-tile coast
85c1c4545a370b6ed66f.tip: Continuing south from Santa Barbara takes you along the famed Malibu coast, but I-10 and I-405 into Santa Monica and West LA gridlock badly after 15:30—try to leave Santa Barbara before 14:00.
85c1c4545a370b6ed66f.title: Browse Solvang's windmill bakeries and take in Santa Barbara's red-tile roofs and palm beaches from the Courthouse clock tower

85f44c71dc894f3254db.access.0.how: About 2.5 hours to Tottori Station on the JR Super Hakuto Limited Express
85f44c71dc894f3254db.access.1.how: About 1 hour 50 minutes to Tottori Station on the JR Super Inaba Limited Express
85f44c71dc894f3254db.access.2.how: About 1.5 hours by JR Limited Express; about 30 minutes to Yonago
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.0.name: Matsuba crab
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.0.price: Crab meal sets from about ¥8,000 per person
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.0.text: The San'in region's name for male snow crab. It has long legs and sweet meat. The season runs from the opening of the fishing season in November through March. You can eat it as sashimi, charcoal-grilled, or in a crab hot pot. A crab kaiseki dinner at a hot-spring ryokan is the easiest option, but also the most expensive.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.0.where: Ryokan around Tottori Station, Sakaiminato, Misasa Onsen, and Kaike Onsen
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.1.name: Beef-bone ramen
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.1.text: A ramen style unique to central and western Tottori. The broth is made from beef bones and has a hint of sweetness. It is lighter than pork-bone ramen, and locals eat it as an everyday meal. Many shops have been open for decades.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.1.where: Long-running ramen shops around Yonago and Kurayoshi
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.2.name: 20th Century pear
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.2.text: Tottori's signature fruit has green skin, a crisp texture, plenty of juice, and a slight tartness. It is in season from late August to September. At other times, look for pear juice, pear jelly, or pear-flavored ice cream.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.2.where: The gift shops at Tottori Station and the 20th Century Pear Museum in Kurayoshi
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.3.name: Sakaiminato seafood rice bowl
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.3.text: Sakaiminato is one of Japan's largest fishing ports by landing volume, with exceptionally fresh tuna, salmon, and crab. After visiting Mizuki Shigeru Road, head to a fish-market restaurant by the harbor for a seafood rice bowl.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.foods.3.where: Market restaurants between Sakaiminato Station and the fishing port
85f44c71dc894f3254db.intro.0: Tottori is Japan's least populous prefecture. It faces the Sea of Japan and stretches long from east to west but is narrow from north to south. In the east, Tottori Sand Dunes roll down to the sea. Central Tottori has Kurayoshi's white-walled historic streets and Misasa Onsen. In the west, you'll find Sakaiminato, the hometown of GeGeGe no Kitaro creator Shigeru Mizuki, and Mount Daisen, known as the "Mount Fuji of Hoki."
85f44c71dc894f3254db.intro.1: Few tourists come here, and the pace is slow. It's a good choice for a second trip to Japan or for anyone who wants to see something different. Public transportation reaches the main sights, but services are infrequent, so check bus schedules before you leave. Winter is snow crab season, and many people come specifically to eat crab and spend a night at a hot-spring ryokan.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.name: Tottori
85f44c71dc894f3254db.seasons.note: Spring and fall are the most comfortable times to visit the dunes; snow crab is in season from November to March; the sand is scorching in summer, while Mount Daisen gets enough snow for skiing in winter.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.sources.0.title: Mitokusan Sanbutsuji Temple: Nageiredo visit information
85f44c71dc894f3254db.sources.1.title: Official website of the Tottori Sand Dunes Sand Museum
85f44c71dc894f3254db.sources.2.title: JR West: Tottori–Matsue Pass
85f44c71dc894f3254db.sources.3.title: Wikipedia: Inaba Limited Express
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.0.name: Tottori Sand Dunes
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.0.text: Japan's most famous dunes rise in rolling waves toward the Sea of Japan. Climb the highest slope, known as the Umanose, and many first-time visitors stop in surprise at the view. You can ride camels or go sandboarding. Nearby, the Sand Museum creates huge sculptures of world landmarks from sand, with a different country as its theme each year. About 20 minutes by bus from Tottori Station.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.0.tip: Sand gets into your shoes, so wear shoes that are easy to remove. The sand is very hot at midday in summer, so go in the morning or evening.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.1.name: Uradome Coast
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.1.text: This stretch of coast east of the dunes has caves and islands carved by the waves. The water is crystal clear, earning it the nickname "San'in's Matsushima." The easiest way to see it is on a sightseeing boat around the coast. In summer, you can also kayak or swim at the beach. Take a bus or JR train from Tottori Station to the Iwami area.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.1.tip: Sightseeing boats may stop running in rough weather, so check whether they are operating that day before you go.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.2.name: Mizuki Shigeru Road
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.2.text: This shopping street in manga artist Shigeru Mizuki's hometown of Sakaiminato is lined with more than 100 bronze statues of yokai from GeGeGe no Kitaro. The Mizuki Shigeru Museum stands at the end. From Yonago Station, take the JR Sakai Line for about 45 minutes. The trains themselves are covered in yokai artwork. At night, the streetlights cast yokai shadows on the ground.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.2.tip: Stop for seafood in Sakaiminato, one of Japan's best-known fishing ports. Crab is plentiful in winter.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.3.name: Mount Daisen and Daisenji Temple
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.3.text: The highest mountain in the Chugoku region, Mount Daisen looks like Mount Fuji when viewed from the west, earning it the nickname "Mount Fuji of Hoki." If you don't want to climb the mountain, walk from Daisenji Temple along the long stone-paved approach to the Okunomiya Shrine of Ogamiyama. The forest is quiet, and the fall colors are beautiful. In winter, the area becomes a ski resort. About 50 minutes by bus from Yonago Station.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.3.tip: It is much colder on the mountain than on the plains, so bring a jacket even in spring and fall.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.4.fee: About ¥1,600 for the mountain climb and temple visit
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.4.name: Mitokusan Nageiredo
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.4.text: This temple hall, a designated national treasure, is built into a hollow in a cliff. Its name means "thrown in," reflecting how it appears to have been placed there. Reaching it requires climbing over tree roots and rocks using both hands and feet. The one-way climb takes about 1 hour, and the rules are strict: you must go with at least one other person, and staff inspect your shoes at the entrance. If they are unsuitable, you must change into straw sandals. Snow closes the mountain from December to March.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.4.tip: Reception is open about 8:00–15:00. Wear hiking shoes, keep both hands free, and don't bring a large backpack.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.5.name: Misasa Onsen
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.5.text: This historic hot-spring town is known for its radon-rich waters and stretches along the Mitoku River. A row of lanterns along the river creates a lovely atmosphere at night. Beneath the bridge is Kawara-buro, a completely open-air bath with no privacy—whether you get in is up to you. The town also has regular public baths and foot baths. About 20 minutes by bus from Kurayoshi Station. It works well as a same-day visit with Mount Mitoku.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.6.name: Kurayoshi White-Walled Storehouses
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.6.text: White-walled, red-tile storehouses line the Tamagawa River in a row, linked by small stone bridges. Many now house cafes, soy sauce shops, and general stores. The area is compact and takes a little over an hour to explore at a relaxed pace. About 15 minutes by bus from Kurayoshi Station. Stop here on the way to Misasa Onsen.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.7.name: Tottori Hanakairo Flower Park
85f44c71dc894f3254db.spots.7.text: One of Japan's largest flower parks, Tottori Hanakairo has a circular walkway around broad flower fields, with Mount Daisen in the background. Tulips bloom in spring, lilies in early summer, and cosmos in fall. Winter brings a large-scale illumination show. Public transportation is limited, so plan it for the same day as Mount Daisen.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.stay: Stay near Tottori Station in the east for easy access to the dunes and Uradome Coast. In the west, stay in Yonago or Kaike Onsen for closer access to Sakaiminato and Mount Daisen. In central Tottori, consider Misasa Onsen.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.tagline: Dunes, yokai streets, and snow crab in winter
85f44c71dc894f3254db.tips.0: Eastern and western Tottori are about 100 kilometers apart. Cover them by region over 2 days instead of trying to go back and forth in a single day.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.tips.1: International visitors can buy the JR Tottori–Matsue Pass. It costs about ¥4,000 for 3 days and works well for a trip that also includes Shimane.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.tips.2: Bus services are infrequent. Check the last bus back before you leave each sight.
85f44c71dc894f3254db.tips.3: The Sea of Japan coast gets frequent rain and snow in winter. Bring a waterproof jacket and shoes with good traction.

86233203412306e28ccf.author.name: Lin Yu
86233203412306e28ccf.author.role: Rail & Coastal Photographer · Kanto Commuter Line Specialist
86233203412306e28ccf.cover.alt: Vintage green Enoden tram gliding along the Kamakura coast with Mount Fuji across the bay
86233203412306e28ccf.cover.caption: On crisp autumn and winter mornings, Sagami Bay gleams crystalline blue as the dark-green Enoden hugs the seawall beneath a painted silhouette of Mount Fuji.
86233203412306e28ccf.excerpt: Two classic snags ruin Tokyo-to-Kamakura day trips: watching three packed Enoden trains roll by on weekends, and overpaying for passes you don't need. Run this smooth clockwise loop—Ofuna Shonan Monorail → Enoshima → Kamakurakokomae → Great Buddha → Komachi-dori.

871ab42ef312875717cf.cost: Okinawa soba about ¥900; Naminoue Shrine free
871ab42ef312875717cf.location: Yui Rail Shuri Station / walk from Asahibashi to Naminoue Beach
871ab42ef312875717cf.paragraphs.0: Once the shuttle drops you back in Naha around 12:30, refuel at a neighborhood noodle shop near Asahibashi or Makishi with a piping-hot bowl of Okinawa soba: springy thick wheat noodles in a clear, savory bonito-and-pork broth topped with tender braised pork belly (rafute) or melt-in-your-mouth cartilage ribs. Add a couple of drops of koregusu—island chilies steeped in awamori spirit—to warm off the sea chill.
871ab42ef312875717cf.paragraphs.1: In the afternoon, ride the monorail toward its terminus at Shuri Castle Park to see master craftspeople restoring the main hall beam by beam with traditional Okinawan techniques and Taiwanese red cypress (Shureimon Gate and the sweeping stone ramparts remain majestic). Before sunset, head back near Asahibashi and walk 15 minutes to Naminoue Shrine perched atop a coral cliff, then linger on adjacent Naminoue Beach as the sun melts into the East China Sea.
871ab42ef312875717cf.phase: Step 03 · Day 2 Afternoon: Shuri Castle & cliffside Naminoue Shrine
871ab42ef312875717cf.photo.alt: Handmade pottery bowl of Okinawa soba topped with braised pork belly beside fresh green sea grapes
871ab42ef312875717cf.photo.caption: Back on dry land after whale watching, a bowl of tender pork-rib Okinawa soba in bonito-pork broth with crisp sea grapes is the quintessential Okinawan afternoon recharge.
871ab42ef312875717cf.tip: Tabletop koregusu chili oil packs both fiery heat and strong awamori alcohol—start with just 2–3 drops to lift the broth, because pouring half a spoonful will knock your socks off.
871ab42ef312875717cf.title: Warm up with steaming Okinawa soba, then ride the monorail to Shuri Castle and Naminoue Shrine

8763ae0759471c438468.cost: Elephant seal beach & harbor boardwalk free
8763ae0759471c438468.paragraphs.0: If you took the US-101 detour and still have daylight to spare, a 35-minute drive north from Morro Bay effortlessly scoops up the southern stretch's Elephant Seal Vista Point at San Simeon and the foothills beneath Hearst Castle without any backtracking stress. Hundreds of rotund elephant seals snore and slap their bellies along the shore—especially lively during winter pupping season.
8763ae0759471c438468.paragraphs.1: Return before twilight to quiet harbor town Morro Bay, where 176-meter volcanic plug Morro Rock rises like a sea pyramid at the mouth of the bay. Grab crispy fish tacos from a waterfront shack along the Embarcadero boardwalk, claim a bench as sunset washes the water purple and rose, and spot wild sea otters floating on their backs in the kelp beds.
8763ae0759471c438468.phase: Step 04 · Day 2 evening: Morro Rock sunset
8763ae0759471c438468.photo.alt: Santa Monica Pier boardwalk and Ferris wheel at sunset in Los Angeles
8763ae0759471c438468.photo.caption: Arrive at Los Angeles' Santa Monica Pier as sunset and the Ferris wheel lights bring your 750 km Highway 1 journey to a glowing finish.
8763ae0759471c438468.tip: Even in summer, California's coast plunges to 12–14°C the moment the sun drops—Morro Bay and Monterey are especially prone to chilly marine fog, so always keep a fleece or packable down jacket in the car for everyone.
8763ae0759471c438468.title: Watch dusk settle behind Morro Bay's volcanic sea stack, with an easy 40-minute side trip north to San Simeon's elephant seals

88b484e99ced4379b4ca.location: DUMBO Washington St → Brooklyn Bridge Park → Williamsburg → Katz's (Lower East Side)
88b484e99ced4379b4ca.paragraphs.0: Ride the F train at 08:30 to York St and briskly walk 5 minutes to Washington St & Water St in DUMBO—arriving half an hour early rewards you with that clean, crowd-free shot of the Manhattan Bridge framed between brick warehouses. Afterward, grab a hot coffee by Brooklyn Bridge Park and Time Out Market while gazing across the East River at the entire Lower Manhattan skyline.
88b484e99ced4379b4ca.paragraphs.1: At noon, hop the subway or breezy NYC Ferry ($4.50 one way) north to trendsetting Williamsburg to browse vinyl shops, vintage racks, and indie boutiques. Cross back to Manhattan's Lower East Side by evening for the legendary 1888 institution Katz's Delicatessen: take your paper ticket at the door (never lose it!), step up to a cutter for Pastrami on Rye, and savor the piping-hot, juicy smoked-beef samples they hand over the counter first. One brick-thick sandwich with crisp kosher pickles easily satisfies two—and grab a $4 crisp cheese slice at Joe's Pizza on the way back to complete your New York initiation.
88b484e99ced4379b4ca.phase: Step 04 · Day 4 Brooklyn slow wander + Lower East Side legendary deli
88b484e99ced4379b4ca.photo.alt: Towering hot pastrami on rye sandwich with pickles at a historic New York deli
88b484e99ced4379b4ca.photo.caption: Katz's hand-carved hot pastrami sandwich towers too tall for a single bite—smoky beef, cracked black pepper, and deli mustard that's just right split between two.
88b484e99ced4379b4ca.tip: The paper ticket handed to you at Katz's entrance is mandatory for checking out—even if you don't buy a thing. Losing it incurs a $50 penalty, so clutch it tight or tuck it straight into a shirt pocket.
88b484e99ced4379b4ca.title: Shoot crowd-free DUMBO at 08:30, vintage-shop Williamsburg, and split Katz's iconic pastrami back in Manhattan

8933b52b36979934f9c2.0: Once December cold snaps roll across East Asia, travelers start hunting for a warm island under three hours away by flight, hovering around 20°C without breaking the bank. Winter Okinawa is one of Asia's most underrated sweet spots: typhoon season is long gone, hotel rates drop to half of July–August peaks, and you catch the three-month window when wild humpback whales return to the Kerama Islands.
8933b52b36979934f9c2.1: Best of all, you do not need an International Driving Permit or left-side driving nerves. Anchor all your nights right beside Naha's Asahibashi Station (connected to Naha Bus Terminal) or Kenchomae Station, and a combination of the Yui Rail monorail, direct express buses north, and whale boats with free hotel pickup lets you cover 4 days and 3 nights effortlessly on a tight budget.

89876ceb0d3c8a956e2f.0: [Skip the physical Opal card] Adults can tap on and tap off directly with Apple Pay or a contactless credit card for the exact same adult Opal fares and daily/weekly caps—just stick to the same card and same device throughout your trip.
89876ceb0d3c8a956e2f.1: [The Sunday fare-cap hack] Friday through Sunday carry lower daily caps (around A$9.65 on Sundays for unlimited trains, buses, and ferries all day). Schedule the 2-hour-each-way Blue Mountains train and the Manly ferry on Sunday for maximum value.
89876ceb0d3c8a956e2f.2: [Airport train surcharge trap] Sydney Airport stations (Domestic and International) tack on an Airport Station Access Fee of about A$17 that does NOT count toward the daily cap. For 2–3 travelers or heavy suitcases, splitting an Uber into the CBD often costs less than taking the train.
89876ceb0d3c8a956e2f.3: [Sunscreen & Blue Mountains chill] Australia's UV index is fierce even under clouds—wear SPF50+. Up in the Blue Mountains, temperatures typically run 6–8°C cooler than downtown Sydney, so pack a light windbreaker even in summer.

8c79804cb2b1da0f229e.summary: Stay 3 nights in Perth and 2 nights in Margaret River, changing hotels only once. Use the first day to adjust to the time difference, then visit Kings Park in the evening. On day 2, take the ferry from Fremantle to Rottnest Island, cycle around and see quokkas. On day 3, drive north to the Pinnacles and stop for lobster along the way. Then head south to Margaret River for 2 days. On the last day, return to Perth via Fremantle for a late-night flight.

8ca0ac55acaeef7d3e5f.0: Skipping the 30-day advance Nohi Bus booking and walking up to Kanazawa Station hoping for tickets—there is a 90% chance winter buses are sold out, wiping out your Shirakawa-go stop.
8ca0ac55acaeef7d3e5f.1: Assuming a JR Takayama-Hokuriku Pass lets you line up and board all-reserved buses—you still must reserve seats ahead by phone or at a ticket counter to get a booking number.
8ca0ac55acaeef7d3e5f.2: Arriving on one of Shirakawa-go's rare winter illumination dates without an official event ticket—afternoon traffic controls lock down the village and un-ticketed visitors must leave before dusk.
8ca0ac55acaeef7d3e5f.3: Packing connections too tightly with zero snow-delay margin—winter expressways occasionally close for 1–2 hours of snow clearing, so never pair this leg directly with a same-day international flight.

8cd218d53c81306c2537.access.0.how: China Southern operates about 3 nonstop flights a week year-round from Guangzhou. China Eastern operates seasonal nonstop flights from Shanghai Pudong, usually around December–February and June–August. Both flights take about 10 hours.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.access.1.how: About 1 hour 15 minutes by air; about 2–3 days by car along the Great Ocean Road.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.access.2.how: About 2 hours by air. Sydney is 30 minutes ahead of Adelaide.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.access.3.how: About 3 hours by air. Adelaide and Perth have a time difference of 1.5–2.5 hours.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.0.name: King George Whiting
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.0.text: A favorite local fish in South Australia, with delicate white flesh and a slightly sweet flavor. It's commonly fried in a light batter or breadcrumbs and served with lemon and chips, making a more refined version of standard fish and chips. You'll often see it on the menus of seaside restaurants and fish-and-chip shops.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.0.where: Seafood restaurants and fish-and-chip shops around Glenelg, plus pubs in central Adelaide.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.1.name: Coffin Bay Oysters
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.1.text: Farmed oysters from Coffin Bay on South Australia's Eyre Peninsula. They're plump, clean-tasting, and famous throughout Australia. Seafood shops and restaurants in Adelaide often serve them freshly shucked by the dozen. Add a squeeze of lemon and eat them as they are.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.1.where: Seafood stalls at Adelaide Central Market and seafood restaurants in the city center.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.2.name: Barossa Shiraz
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.2.text: The Barossa Valley's signature red wine, with deep color, rich fruit, and full tannins. Many wineries have vines more than a century old. At cellar doors, you can taste before buying. When taking wine home, check your airline's limits on alcohol in baggage and the duty-free allowance for your destination.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.2.where: Cellar doors at wineries throughout the Barossa Valley.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.3.name: Pie Floater
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.3.text: An old-school Adelaide late-night snack: a meat pie turned upside down in thick green pea soup, with a ring of tomato sauce on top. It looks unusual but tastes hot, savory, and comforting. It's not available everywhere these days, so try it when you see it.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.foods.3.where: Some bakeries and old-school snack shops in central Adelaide.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.intro.0: South Australia's capital, Adelaide, is compact, with a neat street grid and a relaxed pace. It's also close to several of Australia's best-known wine regions: about 1 hour by car to the Barossa Valley, about 45 minutes to McLaren Vale, and just half an hour to the Adelaide Hills. Wine and food lovers can easily spend four or five days here.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.intro.1: For wildlife, head to Kangaroo Island. Australian sea lions lounge on the beach, while wild kangaroos, koalas, and echidnas are common. You can reach the island by car and ferry in half a day, but plan to stay at least two nights. Five hours north by car, the Flinders Ranges offer an easy introduction to the Outback, with red ridges circling Wilpena Pound.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.intro.2: South Australia gets far fewer visitors than Sydney or Melbourne. You'll need a car between sights, and public transportation mostly covers Adelaide. A common route is to spend two or three nights in Adelaide, visit the wine regions, then continue to Kangaroo Island. You can also drive from Melbourne along the Great Ocean Road.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.name: South Australia
8cd218d53c81306c2537.seasons.note: March–May is grape harvest season, and spring from September–November is the most comfortable time to visit. December–February often brings temperatures above 35°C and a bushfire risk. The Flinders Ranges are best from April–October.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.0.name: Adelaide Central Market
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.0.text: An indoor food market in the city center, open for more than a century. More than seventy stalls sell local fruit, cheese, cured meats, bread, and seafood, with Chinatown next door. Come in the morning for a stroll and breakfast. It's also a good place to buy fruit and cheese for a winery picnic.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.0.tip: Closed Sunday and Monday. Open until 9 p.m. on Friday and closes at 3 p.m. on Saturday.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.1.name: Glenelg
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.1.text: This seaside town is about 30 minutes from the city center by tram. A long wooden pier extends into Gulf St Vincent, with a broad beach and gentle waves. Come at sunset to watch the sun sink into the sea. Jetty Road is lined with restaurants and ice cream shops, making it a relaxing place to spend your first evening in Adelaide.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.1.tip: Swim only in areas patrolled by lifeguards and marked with red-and-yellow flags.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.2.name: Barossa Valley
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.2.text: One of Australia's best-known red wine regions, famous for Shiraz and many vines more than a century old. Stone farmhouses, churches, and butcher shops left by 19th-century German immigrants still stand. Vineyards fill the area between the towns of Tanunda and Nuriootpa. It's about 1 hour by car from Adelaide. Choose three or four wineries for a full day of tastings.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.2.tip: Don't drive after drinking. A wine-region day tour is the easiest option. Reserve winery lunches in advance.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.3.name: McLaren Vale
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.3.text: This wine region is about 45 minutes south of Adelaide. Vineyards stretch toward the coast, with olive and almond groves in between. Its best-known sight is d'Arenberg Cube, a glass winery shaped like a Rubik's Cube, with tastings and dining inside. Spend a day here with nearby beaches, or stop on the way to Kangaroo Island.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.3.tip: The ferry terminal for Kangaroo Island is to the south. You can stay in McLaren Vale the night before and catch a morning ferry.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.4.name: Hahndorf, Adelaide Hills
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.4.text: A German immigrant town in the Adelaide Hills, established in the late 1830s. Its main street is lined with old stone buildings, bakeries, and delicatessens serving German sausages and local beer. The plane trees are at their best when they turn yellow in April–May. The surrounding hills have cool-climate wineries and apple orchards, about 30 minutes by car from the city center.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.4.tip: It gets crowded and parking is difficult around noon on weekends. Go on a weekday morning for a more relaxed visit.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.5.name: Seal Bay Conservation Park, Kangaroo Island
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.5.text: A protected colony of Australian sea lions on Kangaroo Island's south coast. They are among the world's rarest sea lions. Follow the roughly 900-meter boardwalk through the dunes to viewpoints overlooking sea lions sleeping and nursing on the beach. Guided tours can take you down to the beach for a closer look from a required distance. From Adelaide, drive about 2 hours to Cape Jervis, then take a ferry for about 45 minutes.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.5.tip: If you plan to drive on the island, ask the rental company whether its vehicles can go on the ferry.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.6.fee: Per-person admission, or about A$95 for a Kangaroo Island pass
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.6.name: Remarkable Rocks, Flinders Chase National Park
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.6.text: A cluster of huge granite boulders on a headland at the western end of Kangaroo Island, sculpted by wind and sea into hollows and hooks. Their orange-red lichen makes a striking contrast with the Southern Ocean. Nearby Admirals Arch is home to a colony of long-nosed fur seals. Vegetation in Flinders Chase National Park is recovering after the 2019–2020 bushfires, and kangaroos and echidnas are often seen along the road.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.6.tip: There are no railings along the rock edges. Stay away from the cliffs in strong winds. The light is best in the late afternoon.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.7.fee: Per vehicle, about A$14 per vehicle
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.7.name: Wilpena Pound, Ikara-Flinders Ranges National Park
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.7.text: A natural basin enclosed by a ring of red ridges in the Flinders Ranges, shaped like a giant bowl. Hikes lead to an old homestead and viewpoints, while stronger hikers can climb St Mary Peak. For an easier view, take a scenic flight over the complete ring of ridges. The slopes turn red in the early morning and evening, and kangaroos and emus often appear in groups. It's about 450 kilometers from Adelaide. Stay at least two nights.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.spots.7.tip: Many roads have no mobile service. Download offline maps, fill up with fuel, and carry plenty of water before heading into the ranges.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.stay: In Adelaide, stay in the city center (CBD) or North Adelaide for easy access to the Central Market and tram stops. For the beach, stay in Glenelg. In the wine regions, spend a night in Tanunda in the Barossa Valley. On Kangaroo Island, stay in Kingscote or Penneshaw.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.tagline: Wine country, wildlife islands, and red ranges
8cd218d53c81306c2537.tips.0: South Australia is 30 minutes behind Sydney and Melbourne, on UTC+9:30. From early October to early April, daylight saving time moves it to UTC+10:30.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.tips.1: Driving in South Australia with a foreign licence may require an original NAATI-certified translation, including one issued by a consulate. Requirements depend on your licence, so check the South Australian government's official website before setting out. Drive on the left.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.tips.2: Ferries to Kangaroo Island fill up quickly during school holidays and on weekends. Reserve a spot for your car in advance.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.tips.3: During the bushfire season from December–February, check alerts from the CFS website and Alert SA. Don't enter the ranges on days of extreme fire danger.
8cd218d53c81306c2537.tips.4: Adelaide buses accept Visa, Mastercard, and Amex directly, so you don't need a separate transit card.

8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.access.0.how: There are nonstop flights to Seattle from Shanghai, Beijing, and Chongqing. The flight takes about 11–12 hours. There are few departures, so you may need to connect in Tokyo, Seoul, or San Francisco.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.access.1.how: The flight to Seattle takes about 2–3 hours, with frequent service.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.access.2.how: Driving takes about 3 hours, not including the border wait. Trains and buses are also available. Entry requirements depend on your passport; check whether you need a valid U.S. visa.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.0.name: Pacific Northwest oysters
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.0.text: Oysters raised in the cold waters of Puget Sound and Hood Canal are small to medium in size, with a briny flavor and a touch of sweetness. Oysters from different bays taste noticeably different. They are served raw with lemon and red onion mignonette, and many restaurants offer happy-hour specials in the afternoon.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.0.where: Oyster bars along Seattle’s waterfront and in Ballard and Capitol Hill.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.1.name: Cedar plank salmon
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.1.text: Wild salmon is roasted on a soaked cedar plank, giving the fish a smoky wood aroma. Sockeye and coho salmon are freshest in summer, and menus usually specify the variety. Fish stalls at Pike Place Market also sell smoked salmon, which can be vacuum-packed to take home.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.1.where: Seafood restaurants in Seattle and around Pike Place Market.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.2.name: Seattle coffee
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.2.text: Seattle was one of the first American cities where specialty coffee took off. With so many gray, rainy days, neighborhood coffee shops serve as living rooms for the city. Alongside the established chains, Capitol Hill and Ballard have many small independent roasters that take both pour-overs and espresso seriously.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.2.where: Independent coffee shops in Capitol Hill, Ballard, and downtown.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.3.name: Seattle-style teriyaki
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.3.text: This local fast-food staple consists of char-grilled chicken thigh cut into pieces, topped with sweet-savory teriyaki sauce and served with a large portion of white rice and cabbage salad in a takeout box. It is filling, inexpensive, and quick—a longtime local lunch favorite.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.foods.3.where: Small teriyaki shops throughout Seattle and its suburbs.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.intro.0: Washington is in the northwestern corner of the United States. It is not the same place as Washington, DC. Seattle is the gateway. You can cover Pike Place Market, the Space Needle, and its coffee shops in a day or two. The real highlights are outside the city: Mount Rainier, the temperate rain forests and coast of the Olympic Peninsula, the bright green lakes of the North Cascades, and orcas around the San Juan Islands.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.intro.1: This state is best for travelers who enjoy the outdoors and are comfortable driving. From Seattle, Mount Rainier and the North Cascades can each be visited in a day. The Olympic Peninsula is best explored with one or two nights on the road. July–September is the dry season, with the clearest skies and mountain roads fully open. The rest of the year is wetter, but Seattle is still easy to explore.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.intro.2: If you have extra time, you can drive about 3 hours north from Seattle to Vancouver, Canada. Entry requirements for Canada depend on your passport, so check the official rules and arrange any required visa in advance. You will also go through border inspection when returning to the United States.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.name: Washington
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.seasons.note: July–September is the driest period. Mount Rainier’s wildflowers bloom around late July–August. October is the best month for fall colors. November–March is rainy, with snow in the mountains.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.sources.0.title: NPS Mount Rainier: Fees & Passes (no timed entry in 2026)
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.sources.4.title: Washington DOL: Do I need to take a test? (foreign licenses valid for up to 1 year)
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.sources.5.title: FlightConnections: nonstop routes from SEA
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.0.name: Pike Place Market
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.0.text: This public market opened in 1907. Fishmongers tossing salmon across the counter is its signature scene. Several levels are filled with flower and fruit stalls, craft vendors, and snack shops. Across the street is the Starbucks location often called the “original,” where a long line is common. Behind the market, Post Alley is home to the Gum Wall, covered in chewing gum.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.0.tip: Go before 10 a.m. for smaller crowds. Follow the stairs down to the waterfront, where you can join the newly rebuilt waterfront trail.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.1.name: Space Needle
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.1.text: This observation tower was built for the 1962 World’s Fair and is an icon of Seattle’s skyline. The observation levels have glass railings and a rotating glass floor. On a clear day, you can see Mount Rainier and Puget Sound. Seattle Center below also has Chihuly Garden and Glass and the Museum of Pop Culture, which can be combined into a half-day visit.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.1.tip: Entry is timed in 15-minute slots. Clear-weather evenings are the most sought-after. If it is rainy and the mountain is hidden, skip it.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.2.fee: About $30 per vehicle, valid for 7 days
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.2.name: Mount Rainier National Park
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.2.text: This glacier-covered volcano rises about 4,392 meters and towers south of Seattle on clear days. The most popular area is Paradise on the south slope. From the visitor center, the Skyline Trail leads through summer wildflowers with views of glaciers overhead. Sunrise on the northeast side has wider views, but the road is open only around July–September. In 2026, timed entry is not required, but summer weekend parking lots fill before noon.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.2.tip: In winter, vehicles heading to Paradise must carry tire chains. Mountain weather changes quickly, so bring a windproof jacket.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.3.fee: About $30 per vehicle, valid for 7 days
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.3.name: Olympic National Park
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.3.text: One park offers three distinct landscapes: moss-draped trees in the Hoh Rain Forest, sea stacks and driftwood at Ruby Beach, and alpine meadows on Hurricane Ridge. Driving the loop around the peninsula on Highway 101 takes 2–3 days. The Hall of Mosses Trail in the Hoh Rain Forest is about 1.3 kilometers and easy to walk.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.3.tip: The Hoh Rain Forest entrance often has lines in summer. Arrive before 9 a.m. Check road conditions before heading to Hurricane Ridge.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.4.name: North Cascades and Diablo Lake
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.4.text: About 2.5–3 hours northeast of Seattle, Highway 20 cuts through sharp peaks and glaciers. Glacial flour gives Diablo Lake its vivid green color, and roadside viewpoints make it easy to stop for a look. The national park has no entrance fee and draws far fewer visitors than Mount Rainier, making it a good choice for a quieter mountain trip. Washington Pass Overlook farther east is also spectacular.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.4.tip: The mountain-pass section of Highway 20 is usually closed for winter from November through April–May. Check WSDOT road conditions before leaving.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.5.name: San Juan Islands
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.5.text: This chain of islands north of Seattle moves at a slower pace, with rocky shores, lighthouses, and lavender farms. The main draw is orca watching. In summer, you may spot orcas from shore at Lime Kiln Point State Park on the west side of San Juan Island, or take a whale-watching boat from Friday Harbor. The Washington State Ferry from Anacortes takes about 1–2 hours.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.5.tip: Reserve ahead if you are taking a car on the ferry in summer. Lodging is limited, so book at least one month ahead.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.6.name: Leavenworth
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.6.text: This town on the east side of the Cascades is built in a Bavarian style, with wooden balconies, painted facades, and German sausage and beer halls. Snowy mountains rise behind it. October brings Oktoberfest and fall colors in the valley. In December, the town is covered in lights and looks like a Christmas village. From Seattle, the drive takes about 2.5 hours via Highway 2 and Stevens Pass.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.spots.6.tip: Weekends in December are extremely crowded, and parking is difficult. Go on a weekday if possible. In winter, check whether tire chains are required over the pass.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.stay: In Seattle, stay downtown or in South Lake Union, within walking distance of Pike Place Market and the Space Needle. On the Olympic Peninsula, stay in Port Angeles or Forks. Near Mount Rainier, Ashford is a good base by the park’s southwest entrance.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.tagline: Two hours outside Seattle: snowcapped mountains, rain forests, and islands
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.tips.0: Seattle’s sales tax is about 10%. At restaurants, tip 18–22% of the pre-tax bill. Most food bought at supermarkets is exempt from sales tax.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.tips.1: Washington allows foreign visitors to drive with a foreign license for up to 1 year. Check the rules for your license and carry your passport and a certified English translation if required.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.tips.2: October–May is often rainy and chilly. A waterproof jacket is more useful than an umbrella. Tire chains may be required in the mountains and over mountain passes in winter.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.tips.3: You need a Discover Pass to park at state parks such as Lime Kiln Point. A national park annual pass is not valid there.
8d0d6bc92e9fffd22a6d.tips.4: Large parts of Mount Rainier and the Olympic Mountains have no cell service. Download offline maps in advance.
