8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.name: Narita Airport
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.0.name: Keisei Skyliner
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.0.note: Reserved seating throughout and the fastest option. Best for Ueno, Asakusa, and Nippori; Keisei has announced a fare increase starting March 2027, so check the current fare before buying.
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.1.name: Keisei Access Express
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.1.note: No limited express ticket required. Runs directly onto the Toei Asakusa Line, so you can reach Asakusa and the Ginza area without changing. Cheap and easy.
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.1.time: Slower than the Skyliner; depends on the service
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.2.name: JR Narita Express (N'EX)
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.2.note: Direct service to Shinjuku and Shibuya, with no transfer. Travelers with foreign passports can buy the N'EX Tokyo Round Trip Ticket for about ¥5,200, with one round trip within 14 days. It pays off if you use it both ways.
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.2.price: about ¥3,140 to Tokyo Station and ¥3,330 to Shinjuku
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.2.to: Tokyo Station / Shinagawa / Shibuya / Shinjuku / Yokohama
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.3.name: Limousine Bus / budget airport bus
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.3.note: The Limousine Bus stops directly at major hotels, making it easiest with lots of luggage. Budget buses are cheaper, but late-night and early-morning services have different fares. Traffic can add time.
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.3.price: About ¥3,600 on the Limousine Bus to Shinjuku; about ¥1,500 on the budget TYO-NRT bus to Tokyo Station
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.3.time: About 65 minutes at the fastest to Tokyo Station, or about 2 hours to Shinjuku, depending on traffic
8de38f5975ea6bddbf6a.options.3.to: Shinjuku hotel area / Tokyo Station / Ginza

8f535fffc45032c88187.s: Find Japan travel inspiration by season and interest: cherry blossoms, flower fields, autumn foliage, snow country, hot springs, islands, historic sites, mountains and countryside, and art. Each theme lists the top sights to visit.

9030b2d2a3e99753afda.access.0.how: Kyushu Shinkansen from Hakata to Kumamoto: about 33 minutes on Mizuho and about 40 minutes on Sakura
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.access.1.how: Kyushu Shinkansen from Kagoshima-Chuo to Kumamoto: from about 45 minutes
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.access.2.how: The airport bus takes about 1 hour to Kumamoto Station. You can also take the airport shuttle to Higo-Ozu Station and transfer to a JR train.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.access.3.how: The Kyushu Odan Bus connects Kumamoto, Aso, Yufuin, and Beppu. There are only a few departures a day, and reservations are required on some sections.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.0.name: Basashi
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.0.text: Kumamoto's best-known local dish: slices of raw horse meat served with sweet soy sauce, ginger, and garlic. Cuts range from lean red meat to marbled pieces. The meat is clean-tasting and not gamey. If you do not eat raw meat, try horse-meat sushi or grilled horse meat instead.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.0.where: Izakaya around Kumamoto Station and in the Shimotori area
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.1.name: Kumamoto ramen
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.1.text: Like Hakata ramen, it is made with a pork-bone broth, but the noodles are thicker. Fried garlic chips and garlic oil give the soup a strong garlic flavor. This bowl is best for people who like bold flavors.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.1.where: Ramen shops around Kumamoto Station, Shimotori, and Kamitori
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.2.name: Taipien
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.2.text: This Fujian dish brought by overseas Chinese became a Kumamoto comfort food. Glass noodles replace wheat noodles and come with shrimp, meat, and vegetables, topped with a fried egg. It is light and refreshing.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.2.where: Chinese restaurants and school cafeterias in central Kumamoto
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.3.name: Akaushi beef
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.3.text: Brown-haired wagyu raised on the Aso grasslands. It is lean, lightly marbled, and full of flavor. The most common preparation is akaushi beef rice bowls, with thinly sliced beef covering the rice.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.foods.3.where: Restaurants around Aso Station and throughout the Aso area
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.intro.0: Kumamoto is the birthplace of Kumamon. The city centers on Kumamoto Castle, which has been open in stages during restoration since the 2016 earthquake. You can see the repair work in progress. The trip from Hakata by Shinkansen takes about 30 minutes, making Kumamoto a good place to spend 1–2 nights between Fukuoka and Kagoshima.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.intro.1: To the east lies Aso, one of the world's largest volcanic caldera basins, with grasslands, volcanoes, and ranches stretching into the distance. Kurokawa Onsen is farther north. Southwest is Amakusa, home to fishing villages with a history of hidden Christians. Public transportation to Aso and Kurokawa is limited, so a day tour or private car is the best option.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.name: Kumamoto
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.seasons.note: See cherry blossoms at Kumamoto Castle in spring, the greenest grasslands in Aso in summer, and colorful foliage in Kikuchi Gorge in fall. Kurokawa Onsen may have snowy scenery in winter, but mountain roads can be icy.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.sources.0.title: Kumamoto Castle visitor guide (official)
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.sources.1.title: Aso Volcano Disaster Prevention Council crater restriction information
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.sources.2.title: Kyushu Sanko Bus Kyushu Odan Bus
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.0.name: Kumamoto Castle
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.0.text: One of Japan's three great castles, known for its steep Musha-gaeshi stone walls. The keep has reopened after earthquake repairs and now houses an exhibition. The top floor offers views across Kumamoto. An elevated viewing walkway brings you close to stone walls and turrets that are still being repaired.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.0.tip: Sakura-no-Baba Johsaien below the castle has a street of food stalls. You can buy a combo ticket that includes the exhibition hall. It gets very crowded during cherry blossom season.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.1.name: Suizenji Jojuen Garden
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.1.text: A strolling garden built by the Hosokawa family, lords of Kumamoto. It features a small hill modeled on Mount Fuji, and its pond is fed by Aso's underground water. The water is clear enough to see the carp. The garden is small and takes less than an hour to walk around. Stop at Kokin Denju-no-Ma by the pond for a cup of matcha.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.1.tip: The streetcar from Kumamoto Station to Suizenji Koen Station takes about half an hour.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.2.name: Mount Aso Nakadake Crater
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.2.text: This active volcanic crater offers dramatic views of a smoking, blue-green crater lake from the rim when access is open. However, entry is often restricted because of volcanic activity and gases. As of fall 2026, viewing from the crater rim has not resumed. The areas you can visit depend on the day's restrictions.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.2.tip: Check the Aso Volcano Disaster Prevention Council's restriction information before you go. People with asthma or heart disease should not approach the crater.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.3.name: Kusasenri
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.3.text: A broad, round grassland beside the crater, with a shallow pond in the middle. Mount Nakadake smokes in the distance, and horses often graze nearby. You can pay to ride around the grassland. When the crater is closed, this is the best alternative for views of Mount Aso.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.3.tip: Take a mountain bus from Aso Station. The grass is green in summer and brown in winter, and temperatures are much lower than in the city.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.4.name: Daikanbo
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.4.text: The highest point on Aso's outer rim. From here, you can see the entire volcanic basin, including villages, fields, and railways, with the Aso Five Peaks across the way. A sea of clouds often appears in the morning. The road to Kurokawa Onsen passes by here, and many day tours make a short stop.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.4.tip: The sea of clouds is most common on calm mornings in fall and winter. Stay nearby if you want to see it. The wind is strong, so bring a jacket.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.5.name: Kurokawa Onsen
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.5.text: A small hot spring town hidden in a mountain valley. About 30 ryokan line the stream, all built with wood and stone, with no high-rises or neon signs. Buy a Nyuto Tegata pass to choose three ryokan for open-air baths. After soaking in the evening, walking along the stream in a yukata is especially relaxing.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.5.tip: Buy the Nyuto Tegata at Kaze-no-Yu. It costs about ¥1,500 and is valid for 6 months. Direct buses run from Fukuoka and Kumamoto; reservations are required.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.6.name: Kamishikimi Kumanoimasu Shrine
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.6.text: Moss-covered stone lanterns climb through the forest to a huge boulder weathered into a large hole. The woods are thick, and the moss is at its greenest after rain. The mysterious atmosphere has made it a popular stop for anime fans.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.6.tip: The shrine is in Takamori, south of Aso. Public transportation is inconvenient, so a private car is recommended. The stone steps are slippery; wear shoes with good traction.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.7.name: Kikuchi Gorge
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.7.text: A gorge on the northern side of Aso's outer rim, with clear water and several small waterfalls along the trail. The water's edge is refreshingly cool in summer. November is the most popular time for fall colors, when sunlight filtering through the trees shines on the water.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.spots.7.tip: Part of the gorge closes for a period in winter, so check the opening dates before you go. There is no direct public transportation; a private car is recommended.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.stay: In the city, stay near Kumamoto Station or the Shimotori and Kamitori shopping arcades. Kumamoto Castle is a short streetcar ride away. In the Aso area, consider staying one night at a ryokan in Kurokawa Onsen. The hot spring town is especially atmospheric in the evening.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.tagline: One prefecture, three ways to travel: Kumamoto Castle, Mount Aso, and Kurokawa Onsen
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.tips.0: The Mount Aso crater is often closed. Plan around Kusasenri and Daikanbo, and treat an open crater as a bonus.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.tips.1: Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your licence and the required documents. For the Aso and Kurokawa areas, a day tour or private car is recommended.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.tips.2: Streetcars are enough for getting around central Kumamoto. Kumamoto Castle and Suizenji are both on the network.
9030b2d2a3e99753afda.tips.3: Ryokan in Kurokawa Onsen fill up quickly. Book 1–2 months ahead for weekends and fall foliage season.

919179670662d3693536.paragraphs.0: Board the vintage dark-green Enoden eastbound from Enoshima Station; the second it clears Koshigoe's street-running stretch, the right-hand windows burst open onto pure Pacific blue. Stop 2 is Kamakurakokomae Station, famed for the Slam Dunk opening credits.
919179670662d3693536.paragraphs.1: After years of tourists stepping into traffic for photos, guards and police now patrol the crossing daily. Stay strictly behind the white line on the ocean-side sidewalk—never step into the road or across rail warnings. Better yet, walk 100 meters east along the slope to the next seaside hill for the same tram-and-ocean framing with a fraction of the crowd. Once you have your shot, stroll along the seawall to Shichirigahama for a hot latte and sea breeze—that's Shonan at its most unhurried.
919179670662d3693536.tip: Run the Enoden fare math one more time: Enoshima → Kamakurakokomae (¥200) → Hase (¥220) → Kamakura (¥200) totals just ¥620—¥180 cheaper than the ¥800 Noriorikun 1-day pass! Only buy the pass if you plan to hop off at more than 4 stops.
919179670662d3693536.title: Grab a respectful quick snap at Kamakurakokomae crossing, then linger over coffee at Shichirigahama

96574c6b2704d746e247.location: Malibu → Santa Monica Pier → Griffith Observatory
96574c6b2704d746e247.paragraphs.0: Glide along PCH past Malibu's surfers and blufftop mansions, park by Santa Monica Beach before dusk, and stroll out onto the wooden Santa Monica Pier—also the historic western terminus of Route 66. As the vintage Ferris wheel sparks to life under pink sunset skies and buskers strum guitars, your full 750 km Pacific coastline drive comes to an unforgettable close.
96574c6b2704d746e247.paragraphs.1: Still have energy after dark? Drive up toward Griffith Observatory (hilltop lots fill fast at dusk; park near the base and hop the 50-cent DASH shuttle up) to gaze out over the glittering grid of the Los Angeles basin stretching to the horizon, then celebrate with sizzling charcoal-grilled short ribs in Koreatown.
96574c6b2704d746e247.phase: Step 06 · Day 3 evening: Santa Monica Pier finale & LA city lights
96574c6b2704d746e247.tip: Pairing this drive with Yosemite National Park? Double-check whether your travel month requires peak-hours entry reservations—and plan to arrive early, since entering Yosemite Valley after 08:30 on busy weekends can mean circling an hour for parking.
96574c6b2704d746e247.title: Roll down Malibu's sunset coast to close the road trip at Santa Monica Pier and Griffith Observatory

97ff56cad1e28a0c693f.cover.caption: After 6 PM, Ura-Namba's lanes glow with warm lanterns—none of Dotonbori's tour-group crush, just Osaka office workers unwinding over skewers and cold beer.
97ff56cad1e28a0c693f.excerpt: Kuromon Market is now mostly pricey tourist stalls. 995351418a8250a15a81.passes.0.name: JAPAN RAIL PASS
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.0.price: Ordinary class: about ¥50,000 for 7 days (official website price) / about ¥53,000 through overseas agents; about ¥80,000 starting price for 14 days; about ¥100,000 starting price for 21 days
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.0.text: Available only to foreign visitors staying short-term. Overseas agents will raise their prices in October 2026, while the official website will temporarily keep its current prices, making it cheaper to buy there. The pass covers most JR lines and Shinkansen trains, but the Nozomi and Mizuho require a separate special ticket (about ¥4,960 between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka). It usually isn't worthwhile for trips covering only one or two regions. Calculate the cost if you're making long round trips between Tokyo, Kansai, and Kyushu.
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.1.text: The price will rise from about ¥15,000 to about ¥16,000 starting in March 2026. The pass covers destinations around Tokyo, including Karuizawa, Nikko, and Lake Kawaguchi. It's suitable for travelers using Tokyo as a base for two or three day trips to the surrounding area. You don't need it for travel within Tokyo.
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.2.name: Kansai WIDE Area Pass
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.2.text: Ride JR trains throughout Kansai, including the HARUKA and reserved seats on the Sanyo Shinkansen between Shin-Osaka and Okayama. Destinations include Himeji, Okayama, Kinosaki Onsen, Amanohashidate, and Shirahama. It's ideal for trips based in Osaka or Kyoto with excursions farther afield. The former Kansai Area Pass stopped being sold on September 30, 2026. For travel only around Kyoto, Osaka, and Kobe, consider the Kansai Mini Pass at about ¥3,000 for 3 days (HARUKA not included).
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.3.name: Kansai-Hiroshima Area Pass
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.3.text: Take the Sanyo Shinkansen from Kansai to Hiroshima, including the Nozomi, and use the ferry to Miyajima. It generally pays for itself on routes combining Osaka and Kyoto with Hiroshima and Miyajima.
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.4.name: JR Kyushu Rail Pass (All Kyushu)
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.4.price: About ¥22,000 for 3 days, about ¥24,000 for 5 days, and about ¥26,000 for 7 days
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.4.text: Ride Kyushu Shinkansen and limited express trains as much as you like. There are also Northern Kyushu passes for about ¥15,000 for 3 days and Southern Kyushu passes for about ¥12,000 for 3 days. Online reservation prices may differ. Check the JR Kyushu official website.
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.5.name: Hokkaido Rail Pass
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.5.price: From about ¥22,000 for 5 days (overseas/online advance purchase price); about ¥1,000 more when purchased at a station
995351418a8250a15a81.passes.5.text: Ride all JR Hokkaido lines except the Hokkaido Shinkansen. The pass costs about ¥28,000 for 7 days and about ¥37,000 for 10 days. Two or three long round trips, such as Sapporo—Hakodate, Asahikawa, Furano, or Kushiro, can make it worthwhile. All limited express seats are reserved, so remember to pick up a seat ticket before boarding.

995351418a8250a15a81.tips.0.text: Transit IC cards such as Suica, PASMO, and ICOCA work on subways, JR trains, and most buses in major cities. You can also use them at convenience stores. On iPhone, you can add a Suica directly in Wallet. If you can't exit because your balance is too low, don't panic. Top up and pay the difference at the 「精算機」 (fare adjustment machine) beside the gates.
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.0.title: Transit IC cards: one card for the whole country
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.1.text: On the Tokaido, Sanyo, and Kyushu Shinkansen (Tokyo—Shin-Osaka—Hakata—Kagoshima-Chuo), luggage with total dimensions over 160 cm and up to 250 cm requires a seat with an oversized baggage area (same price) when you buy your ticket. If you board with an unreserved large bag, you'll have to pay a fee of about ¥1,000 and follow the crew's instructions. Bags over 250 cm are not allowed onboard.
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.1.title: Reserve a seat in advance for large bags on the Shinkansen
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.2.text: Kuroneko Yamato can ship your bags from a hotel front desk, convenience store, or service center to your next hotel. Most routes arrive the next day. To send luggage to an airport, ship it 2 days before your flight (3 days in some areas), then pick it up at the airport counter that day with your shipping receipt. Each item must weigh no more than 30 kg. Send your bags ahead before changing locations or going to the airport, and train rides will be much easier.
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.2.title: Luggage delivery: explore hands-free
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.3.text: In Tokyo's 23 wards, regular taxis start at about ¥500 (for about 1 km), then charge by distance. Fares rise by about 20% from 22:00 to 5:00, and highway tolls are extra. The doors open and close automatically, so don't pull them yourself. Taxi apps such as GO let you link a card and enter your destination directly, which is especially convenient when there's a language barrier.
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.3.title: Taxis: expensive but easy
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.4.text: In major cities such as Tokyo and Osaka, the last trains usually run around midnight. Suburban routes end earlier. Check the last train before going out at night. If you miss it, you'll have to take a taxi or wait for the first train. Plan your route into the city in advance, especially on holidays or when your flight arrives late at night.
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.4.title: The last train may be earlier than you expect
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.5.text: During holidays, cherry blossom and fall foliage seasons, and the year-end and New Year period, reserved seats are recommended. On regular weekdays in the off-season, nonreserved cars usually have seats available. JR Pass holders can also reserve seats at no extra charge. Reserve in advance at a ticket machine or online so you won't have to compete for a seat.
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.5.title: Reserved or nonreserved Shinkansen seats
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.6.text: Google Maps and apps such as 「乗換案内」 can show specific platforms, exits, fares, and last trains. In Japan, stations with the same name may belong to different companies, such as JR and the subway. Follow the app's instructions and confirm the operator and exit to avoid unnecessary detours.
995351418a8250a15a81.tips.6.title: Install a transit app

99f382a1234dff659023.location: Enoshima Benten Bridge → Enoshima Shrine → Sea Candle Lighthouse
99f382a1234dff659023.paragraphs.0: Stroll the 400-meter Benten Bridge onto the island to meet the weathered bronze torii and a lively approach lane fragrant with pressed octopus crackers and warm steamed manju. At the red wooden torii where stone staircases climb sharply uphill, save your energy for afternoon temple walks by picking up the 'Escar + Samuel Cocking Garden + Sea Candle' combo ticket on the left (escalators run up only; walking back down is breezy).
99f382a1234dff659023.paragraphs.1: Three escalator flights carry you effortlessly past Enoshima Shrine's Hetsumiya and Nakatsumiya halls straight to the summit's Sea Candle observation tower. Before 10:00 on crisp autumn and winter mornings, the air is crystal clear—step onto the outdoor deck facing west for an unobstructed sweep of Sagami Bay crowned by snow-capped Mount Fuji. With spare time, descend the southern steps to the sea-carved Enoshima Iwaya Caves to hear waves booming against black volcanic rock.
99f382a1234dff659023.photo.alt: Sunlit stone stairs overlooking turquoise Sagami Bay and volcanic cliffs on Enoshima Island
99f382a1234dff659023.photo.caption: Follow Enoshima's ridge toward the sea cliffs at 10:00, when clear morning sun turns Sagami Bay a luminous turquoise.
99f382a1234dff659023.tip: Watch the skies on the hilltop and shoreline—bold black kites love dive-bombing tourists for hot dogs, octopus crackers, and soft-serve ice cream. Shield food outdoors, or better yet finish snacks under cover.
99f382a1234dff659023.title: Walk under the bronze torii, ride the escalators to the lighthouse, and spot Mount Fuji across the bay

9aa8e6e1d6012c2bccc3.s: Plan each day with saved sights and food, view routes, estimate travel, and create a share link. No signup; saved in your browser.

9b45c896295393b06a91.access.0.how: Take the JR Marine Liner across the Seto Ohashi Bridge. The trip to Takamatsu Station takes about 55 minutes.
9b45c896295393b06a91.access.1.how: The airport bus takes about 45 minutes to Takamatsu Station and costs about ¥1,300. There are flights from Shanghai, Seoul, Taipei and other cities.
9b45c896295393b06a91.access.2.how: Take the Shinkansen to Okayama and transfer to the Marine Liner. The total trip takes about 2 hours. Highway buses also take about 3.5 hours.
9b45c896295393b06a91.foods.0.name: Sanuki udon
9b45c896295393b06a91.foods.0.text: Thick, square and chewy, with a springy texture. Many restaurants are self-service: take a bowl, choose hot or cold noodles, add tempura and toppings, then pay at the end. A bowl costs a few hundred yen. Popular styles include shoyu udon and kama-tama, udon mixed with a raw egg.
9b45c896295393b06a91.foods.0.where: Udon restaurants from central Takamatsu to Kotohira. Many are open only until noon or early afternoon.
9b45c896295393b06a91.foods.1.name: Honetsuki-dori
9b45c896295393b06a91.foods.1.text: This Marugame specialty is made by rubbing a whole chicken leg with salt and pepper, then grilling it over high heat. The skin is crisp, the meat is juicy and the flavor is garlicky. Choose oya-dori, a mature chicken with a firm bite, or hina-dori, a tender young chicken. It is usually served with beer and rice balls.
9b45c896295393b06a91.foods.1.where: Specialty restaurants and izakaya in Marugame and central Takamatsu
9b45c896295393b06a91.foods.2.name: Shodoshima olives
9b45c896295393b06a91.foods.2.text: Shodoshima was the first place in Japan to successfully grow olives. The island sells extra-virgin olive oil and pickled olives, along with olive-flavored ice cream and “olive beef” raised on olives. Olive oil makes a good souvenir.
9b45c896295393b06a91.foods.2.where: Shodoshima Olive Park, Tonosho Port and souvenir shops around the island
9b45c896295393b06a91.intro.0: Kagawa is Japan's smallest prefecture. It calls itself “Udon Prefecture,” and eating three bowls in one day is nothing unusual. Takamatsu, the prefectural capital, is the main port for the art islands of the Seto Inland Sea: Naoshima has Chichu Art Museum and Yayoi Kusama's pumpkins, Teshima has Teshima Art Museum, and Shodoshima has olive groves and Angel Road.
9b45c896295393b06a91.intro.1: On the mainland, the classics are Ritsurin Garden in Takamatsu, Kotohiragu Shrine in Kotohira, and Chichibugahama Beach in Mitoyo, where low tide can create photos of a “mirror of the sky.” Base yourself in Takamatsu for 2–3 nights: spend one day island-hopping and another eating udon and visiting gardens on the main island. The pace is just right.
9b45c896295393b06a91.name: Kagawa
9b45c896295393b06a91.seasons.note: Spring and fall are the most comfortable seasons for visiting the islands. Summer brings beautiful sea views but strong sun. From December–February, some island museums close or shorten their hours, so check their official websites first.
9b45c896295393b06a91.sources.0.title: Benesse Art Site Naoshima: Chichu Art Museum
9b45c896295393b06a91.sources.1.title: Benesse Art Site Naoshima: Art House Project
9b45c896295393b06a91.sources.2.title: Benesse Art Site Naoshima: Teshima Art Museum
9b45c896295393b06a91.sources.3.title: Kotohiragu Shrine official website
9b45c896295393b06a91.sources.4.title: Shikoku Kisen: Takamatsu–Naoshima (Miyanoura) route
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.0.name: Chichu Art Museum
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.0.text: Designed by Tadao Ando and built mostly underground, this museum shows works by just three artists: Claude Monet, James Turrell and Walter De Maria. Natural light changes how the exhibits look, so sunny and cloudy days feel completely different. Naoshima's top attraction requires an online reservation for a date and time slot. If tickets sell out online, none are sold at the museum that day.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.0.tip: Closed on Mondays, except when Monday is a holiday. Book several weeks ahead during peak season. Photography is not allowed inside.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.1.fee: Art House Project combination ticket from about ¥1,200
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.1.name: Naoshima Art House Project
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.1.text: Artists have transformed old houses, shrines and a dental clinic along Honmura's old streets into works of art. They are scattered through the narrow lanes, making it fun to explore on foot. Miyano-Ura Port has Yayoi Kusama's Red Pumpkin, while Yellow Pumpkin stands by the sea near Benesse House. Naoshima New Museum of Art, which opened in 2025, is also in Honmura and requires a reservation.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.1.tip: Minamidera requires a separate time-slot reservation. Most sites close on Mondays, so avoid planning Naoshima for Monday.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.2.name: Teshima Art Museum
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.2.text: This white concrete shell looks like a water droplet. Inside, there are no pillars or exhibits—only tiny drops of water that continuously emerge and roll across the floor, along with wind and light entering through the opening in the roof. Many visitors sit inside for a long time. From Ieura Port, it takes about 15 minutes by island bus or about 30 minutes by electric bike.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.2.tip: Closed on Tuesdays from March–November, and Tuesday–Thursday from December–February. Online reservations are also required.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.3.name: Ritsurin Garden
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.3.text: The lords of Takamatsu spent more than 100 years creating this strolling garden, backed by Mount Shiun. It has six ponds, more than a dozen landscaped hills and meticulously pruned pine trees. Take a small boat around South Lake or enjoy matcha at Kikugetsu-tei. From Takamatsu Station, take the JR or Kotoden train to the area around Ritsurin Garden Station.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.3.tip: The garden is quietest soon after opening, and the light is good for photos. Go early.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.4.name: Kotohiragu Shrine
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.4.text: Known affectionately as “Konpira-san,” this is the head shrine of the god of seafaring. From the entrance to the approach, it is 785 stone steps to the main shrine, taking about 1 hour one way. The climb continues to the inner shrine, for a total of 1,368 steps. Souvenir shops and udon restaurants line the steps, and the main shrine overlooks the Sanuki Plain. From Takamatsu, the trip to Kotohira takes about 1 hour by JR or Kotoden.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.4.tip: If your fitness level is average, the main shrine is far enough. Bamboo walking sticks are available at the entrance.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.5.name: Chichibugahama Beach
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.5.text: Low tide leaves shallow pools across the beach. On a still evening, they clearly reflect people and the sunset, earning the beach its nickname, the “mirror of the sky.” For the best photos, visit on a day when sunset overlaps with low tide, within a window of about 30 minutes. It takes about 10 minutes by taxi from JR Takuma Station.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.5.tip: Check the tide table before you go. Choose a day with low tide near sunset and little wind.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.6.name: Shodoshima
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.6.text: The second-largest island in the Seto Inland Sea is covered with olive trees and has a distinctly Mediterranean feel. Three main sights are Angel Road, a sandbar visible only at low tide; the Kankakei Ropeway, surrounded by fall foliage; and the white windmill at Olive Park. From Takamatsu Port, the high-speed ferry takes about 35 minutes to Tonosho Port.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.6.tip: Angel Road is walkable only around the two low tides each day. Check the tide table before planning your visit.
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.7.name: Yashima
9b45c896295393b06a91.spots.7.text: This flat-topped plateau east of Takamatsu was the site of a major battle between the Genji and Heike clans. Yashima-ji, one of the 88 temples on the Shikoku pilgrimage, stands at the summit. The observation deck overlooks Takamatsu and the islands of the Seto Inland Sea. It is scenic from evening through the night, and the newer observation facilities have a distinctive design. It takes about 30 minutes by car from central Takamatsu.
9b45c896295393b06a91.stay: Stay around Takamatsu Station or Takamatsu Port. Ferries to the islands and trains to Kotohira leave from here. To explore Naoshima at a slower pace, spend one night on the island.
9b45c896295393b06a91.tagline: Udon country and the gateway to the art islands of the Seto Inland Sea
9b45c896295393b06a91.tips.0: Nearly all museums on Naoshima and Teshima require online reservations. Closing days vary, so plan your visits before booking ferries.
9b45c896295393b06a91.tips.1: The ferry from Takamatsu to Naoshima takes about 50 minutes, while the high-speed ferry takes about 30 minutes. Services are limited, so do not miss the last ferry back.
9b45c896295393b06a91.tips.2: Many famous udon restaurants close by 2 or 3 p.m. Have udon for breakfast or lunch.
9b45c896295393b06a91.tips.3: The Setouchi Triennale takes place once every three years, and the islands get very crowded. Book accommodation and ferries earlier than usual.

9b94cbdd55b3a5ba5d80.s: Kyoto, Great Barrier Reef, Yellowstone, ramen…

9c01023d4d7b0932a23f.s: Days with 1 mm or more of precipitation

9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.access.0.how: JR Joban Line limited express trains run directly from Tokyo, Ueno, and Shinagawa stations to Mito in a little over 1 hour. For Hitachi Seaside Park, get off at Katsuta Station and transfer to a bus.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.access.1.how: The Tsukuba Express rapid service reaches Tsukuba Station in about 45 minutes and costs about ¥1,210. Transfer to a shuttle bus for Mount Tsukuba.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.access.2.how: The airport has a small number of international routes, including Shanghai. Services and schedules change frequently, so check the airport's official website before booking. Airport buses run to Mito and Tokyo Station.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.foods.0.name: Mito natto
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.foods.0.text: Mito is synonymous with natto. Small fermented soybeans mixed with sauce and mustard and served over white rice are an everyday local breakfast. Station gift shops sell traditional straw-wrapped natto as well as nonsticky dried natto snacks. The snacks are an easy introduction if you have never tried it.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.foods.0.where: Gift shops at Mito Station and restaurants nearby
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.foods.1.name: Anko nabe
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.foods.1.text: This monkfish hot pot is a signature Ibaraki winter dish. The flesh, skin, and liver cook together in a rich, savory miso broth made with sautéed monkfish liver. It is highly seasonal, at its best from about November through March of the following year. Many restaurants require reservations and a minimum order for 2 people.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.foods.1.where: Seafood restaurants and ryokan around Oarai and Kitaibaraki
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.foods.2.name: Hoshi imo
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.foods.2.text: Ibaraki produces the vast majority of Japan's dried sweet potatoes. Steamed sweet potatoes are sliced and sun-dried, giving them a soft, chewy texture and natural sweetness with no additives. Fresh batches are best in winter. Sold at convenience stores and stations, they keep well and make good gifts to take home.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.foods.2.where: Mito Station and gift shops near Hitachi Seaside Park
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.intro.0: Ibaraki lies northeast of Tokyo. It usually gets little attention, but 2 seasons make it worth a special trip: from late April to mid-May, blue nemophila blanket an entire hillside at Hitachi Seaside Park; from late February through March, more than 3,000 plum trees bloom in succession at Kairaku-en in Mito. In fall, the park's kochia turn red. Farther north, Fukuroda Falls is worth seeing for its fall foliage and winter ice.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.intro.1: Most visitors explore Ibaraki on a day trip from Tokyo. Take a JR Joban Line limited express to Mito, then transfer for Hitachi Seaside Park or Kairaku-en. To see more, stay overnight in Mito and visit the Oarai coast or Mount Tsukuba the next day. Sights are spread out and buses are infrequent, so choosing 1 or 2 highlights is more practical than trying to see everything.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.name: Ibaraki
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.seasons.note: Nemophila bloom from late April to mid-May, and plum blossoms from late February through March. Kochia turn red in October. Hitachi Seaside Park is busiest during Golden Week.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.sources.0.title: japan-guide: Hitachi Seaside Park
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.sources.1.title: japan-guide: Kairaku-en
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.sources.2.title: Hitachi Seaside Park official website
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.sources.3.title: Ibatoco: Fukuroda Falls fall foliage 2026
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.0.fee: About ¥450, plus a seasonal surcharge during flower season
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.0.name: Hitachi Seaside Park
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.0.text: Ibaraki's best-known sight. In spring, nemophila cover Miharashi Hill in blue that seems to stretch to the horizon. In October, rounded kochia bushes on the same hillside gradually turn from green to red. The park is large, with a sightseeing train and bicycle rentals. A bus from Katsuta Station's east exit takes about 15 minutes to the park's west entrance.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.0.tip: Bus stops and entrances have long lines on weekends during flower season. Aim to arrive before opening on a weekday. The park is usually closed on Tuesdays.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.1.name: Kairaku-en
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.1.text: One of Japan's 3 great gardens, built in the 19th century by the lord of Mito for the public to enjoy. It has about 3,000 plum trees in more than 100 varieties. The Mito Plum Blossom Festival runs from mid-February to late March. Kobuntei, a wooden pavilion in the garden, overlooks Lake Senba from its upper floor. Take a bus from Mito Station's north exit for about 15 minutes, or walk along Lake Senba for 30 minutes.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.1.tip: Outside the plum blossom festival, admission is free from opening until 9 a.m. Festival admission prices will rise starting in 2027.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.2.name: Fukuroda Falls
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.2.text: This waterfall drops about 120 meters over 4 tiers. Fall foliage covers the cliffs on either side, and in deep winter the falls can partially freeze. Walk through a viewing tunnel to a platform facing the falls, then take an elevator to a higher platform. Take the JR Suigun Line to Fukuroda Station, followed by a bus ride of about 10 minutes and a 10-minute walk.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.2.tip: Suigun Line trains are infrequent, so check your return schedule first. Evening illuminations are often held during the November foliage season.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.3.name: Mount Tsukuba
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.3.text: This twin-peaked mountain rises sharply from the Kanto Plain. The walk between its peaks, Nantai and Nyotai, takes a little over 10 minutes. Tsukubasan Shrine sits partway up the mountain. Reach the peaks by cable car or ropeway, or hike from beside the shrine in about 1.5 hours. On clear days, views stretch across the Kanto Plain. In the crisp winter air, you can see Mount Fuji to the west.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.3.tip: Take the Mount Tsukuba shuttle bus from Tsukuba Station. The cable car and ropeway serve different peaks, so choose based on which peak you want to visit.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.4.name: Ōarai Isosaki Shrine
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.4.text: The shrine itself stands on a small hill, but its best-known feature is Kamiiso no Torii, a torii gate on coastal rocks. Waves crash dramatically around it, and the rising sun silhouettes the gate at dawn. Nearby are Aqua World Ibaraki Prefectural Oarai Aquarium and a seafood market. You can combine a visit with Mito in the same day.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.4.tip: Stay in Oarai or Mito if you want to photograph the torii at sunrise. From Mito, take the Kashima Rinkai Railway to Oarai Station, then transfer to a loop bus.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.5.name: Kashima Jingu
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.5.text: One of the oldest shrines in Kanto, dedicated to a god of martial arts and long revered by samurai. Beyond the approach lies a quiet, ancient forest. At the far end is Mitarashi Pond, fed by a natural spring. Sacred deer are also kept on the grounds. A direct highway bus from Tokyo Station is simpler than making several train transfers.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.spots.5.tip: Combine it with Katori Jingu in Chiba. The shrines sit across the Tone River from each other, about 20 minutes apart by car.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.stay: Stay near Mito Station for convenient access to Kairaku-en, Hitachi Seaside Park, and Oarai. If you only want to see the flower fields, make it a day trip from Tokyo.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.tagline: Blue flowers in spring and plum blossoms in late winter, all within a day trip from Tokyo
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.tips.0: Hitachi Seaside Park and Kairaku-en post bloom updates on their official websites during flower season and the plum blossom festival. Check the day before your visit.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.tips.1: Extra buses run to Hitachi Seaside Park during flower season, but waits of 1 hour are still common on weekends.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.tips.2: Rural Ibaraki has few buses. If you plan to drive, the requirements depend on where your license was issued. Check official sources for the documents you need to drive legally in Japan.
9d9a06462b0bedf08c12.tips.3: Buy a reserved-seat ticket before boarding a Joban Line limited express. Booking through a mobile app is easier than using the ticket counter.

9eccb12e7b682ce94e88.location: Enoshima approach / harbor diners near Koshigoe Station
9eccb12e7b682ce94e88.paragraphs.0: Shonan's signature lunch is shirasu-don (baby whitebait over warm rice). If cliffside viral spots like Uomitei quote waits over 30 minutes, head off the island to a local fishermen's diner near Enoden's Koshigoe Station—honest prices and almost no line. Order the two-tone bowl (nishoku-don): half glistening, mildly sweet raw whitebait with grated ginger, half fluffy salted boiled whitebait, finished with two quick swirls of soy sauce.
9eccb12e7b682ce94e88.paragraphs.1: Visiting between January and mid-to-late March? If signs say no raw shirasu (nama shirasu), it isn't sold out—that's Shonan's mandatory winter conservation ban prohibiting raw catches region-wide. A steaming bowl of freshly boiled kama-age whitebait with seaweed miso soup still hits the spot.
9eccb12e7b682ce94e88.photo.alt: Ceramic bowl of raw and boiled whitebait over rice with nori, scallions, and ginger on a wooden counter
9eccb12e7b682ce94e88.photo.caption: Half raw, half boiled shirasu-don topped with grated ginger and shredded nori is the cleanest coastal recharge after Enoshima's stairs.
9eccb12e7b682ce94e88.tip: Plenty of old-school harbor diners and cracker stalls are cash-only—tuck a ¥5,000 bill and a handful of ¥100 coins in your wallet before heading down to Kamakura.
9eccb12e7b682ce94e88.title: Dig into a two-tone whitebait rice bowl on the island or at Koshigoe harbor—and know the off-season

9fe240e138343528b1f8.s: Travel Posts & Daily Updates: Every guide in the community cross-checks real public trip reports (including Xiaohongshu, Mafengwo, Qyer, Reddit, and official transit/tourism bulletins) before being rewritten from scratch as step-by-step walkthroughs covering connections, timing, costs, and pitfalls, with sources and check dates at the bottom. Columns use editorial traveler personas paired with an automated daily research pipeline.

a15998bbb260d89cb25a.cover.alt: Empty early-morning Kyoto temple garden with crimson autumn maples mirrored in a tranquil pond
a15998bbb260d89cb25a.cover.caption: Be first through Eikando's gates at 08:30 for the golden 20 minutes when morning sun ignites crimson maples over a glass-still Hojo Pond—well worth losing 1 hour of sleep.
a15998bbb260d89cb25a.excerpt: In late November, Eikando, Nanzen-ji, and Tofuku-ji are Kyoto's three most mobbed autumn icons. Setting your alarm 1 hour earlier and taking the Tozai Subway Line to Keage catches peaceful opening-hour reflections at Hojo Pond—plus a relaxed yudofu lunch before the rush.

a1caeac79a453e244779.0: Every December (12), social feeds fill up with winter Hokkaido rental cars sliding straight into snowbanks. Unless you have years of deep-winter ice driving under your belt, take this honest advice: Central Hokkaido's classic Sapporo + Otaru + Noboribetsu + Lake Toya loop has a superb rail network—riding heated JR trains and highway buses is ten times safer and lets you soak in snowy sea views.
a1caeac79a453e244779.1: Even by rail, winter Hokkaido takes smart pacing: daylight vanishes around 16:00, indoor heating blasts past 25°C, and snowstorms can pause trains on short notice. This 5-day, 4-night field guide nails train seats, smart layering, luggage tactics, and instant bus fallbacks.

a30e11e46edf36e288d5.0: [Essential pre-drive check] 1 week before, 1 day before, and the morning you set off, open Caltrans QuickMap (quickmap.dot.ca.gov), toggle on Road Closures, and check @CaltransD5 on X for Central Coast alerts.
a30e11e46edf36e288d5.1: [Golden Big Sur detour] If the middle stretch closes after you've driven south from Carmel to see Bixby Bridge, loop straight back to Carmel, take CA-68 east to inland US-101 south past Salinas and Paso Robles, then cut back west on CA-41 to Morro Bay. It adds roughly 2–2.5 hours while keeping both northern and southern coastal highlights intact.
a30e11e46edf36e288d5.2: [Bixby Bridge no-parking zone] Strict no-parking and enforcement zones now cover the bridge approaches and Old Coast Road—stopping on yellow lines or tight shoulders invites steep tickets. Use official paved turnouts or pull over slightly earlier at Hurricane Point for an even grander panorama.
a30e11e46edf36e288d5.3: [No cell service, pricey gas in Big Sur] Top off your tank and download offline maps in Monterey or Carmel before entering Big Sur—the handful of village pumps charge eye-watering prices, and cell coverage vanishes for miles.

a3412daac536a621f8be.s: Price out flights, stays, food and more on one page

a388a6efab556664cda5.location: San Francisco → Half Moon Bay → Pigeon Point → Monterey / Carmel
a388a6efab556664cda5.paragraphs.0: Pick up your rental car at eight-thirty in the morning and roll south out of San Francisco (dodging peak downtown rush hour—and never leave bags visible on the seats to deter break-ins). Joining Highway 1 quickly brings you into clearing fog at Half Moon Bay and the red-and-white Pigeon Point Lighthouse. Reach Monterey by lunch for a thick clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl on Old Fisherman's Wharf, and if time allows, pay $12 to loop 17-Mile Drive for the Lone Cypress and basking harbor seals.
a388a6efab556664cda5.paragraphs.1: Check in for the night at storybook Carmel-by-the-Sea, a village with no street numbers or neon chains—just cypress-shaded shingled cottages, art galleries, and flower-filled courtyards. Walk down to Carmel's white-sand beach for a Pacific sunset, grab dinner at a local trattoria or bistro, and be sure to fill your gas tank to the brim around Carmel tonight.
a388a6efab556664cda5.phase: Step 01 · Night before & Day 1 08:30 San Francisco departure
a388a6efab556664cda5.photo.alt: San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge and California bay as morning fog clears
a388a6efab556664cda5.photo.caption: Heading south past San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge, stop along Half Moon Bay and Monterey's Fisherman's Wharf—and top off your gas tank before entering Big Sur.
a388a6efab556664cda5.tip: Car break-ins remain a real threat across the San Francisco Bay Area. Whenever you stop to eat or see the ocean in Half Moon Bay or Monterey, stow all backpacks and suitcases out of sight in a covered trunk—and pack them away at your previous stop rather than loading a laptop bag in full view at the parking lot.
a388a6efab556664cda5.title: Verify live roads on Caltrans QuickMap, then cruise Half Moon Bay and Pigeon Point down to Monterey & Carmel

a3c9391ec51c39f54dae.cost: Kenrokuen admission ¥320; city loop bus ¥210 per ride
a3c9391ec51c39f54dae.location: Kanazawa Station → Kenrokuen Garden → Higashi Chaya District → Omicho Market
a3c9391ec51c39f54dae.paragraphs.0: Ride the Hokuriku Shinkansen from Tokyo (about 2.5 hours) or connect from Kyoto/Osaka via the Thunderbird Limited Express and Hokuriku Shinkansen (about 2 hours) straight into Kanazawa Station, where the soaring wooden Tsuzumi-mon Gate greets you outside. Kanazawa's sights cluster tightly together, so head straight to Kenrokuen Garden: every November, gardeners rig hundreds of conical hemp-rope canopies called yukitsuri over ancient pines to keep Hokuriku's wet, heavy snow from snapping their branches. On a snowy day, the ropes framing Kotoji Lantern and Kasumigaike Pond look lifted from a woodblock print.
a3c9391ec51c39f54dae.paragraphs.1: Walk 15 minutes for lunch at Omicho Market and order a winter seafood bowl piled high with sweet shrimp, seared nodoguro blackthroat seaperch, and kobako snow crab. Spend the afternoon wandering the Edo-era dark-wood lattice lanes of Higashi Chaya District for matcha in a century-old teahouse and a dazzling gold-leaf soft-serve cone, then wrap up with steaming Kanazawa oden and local sake.
a3c9391ec51c39f54dae.photo.alt: Ancient pine trees rigged with yukitsuri snow ropes beside the pond at Kenrokuen Garden in Kanazawa on a winter morning
a3c9391ec51c39f54dae.photo.caption: Visible only in late autumn and winter, Kenrokuen's yukitsuri rope umbrellas protect ancient pines from heavy wet snow while creating Hokuriku's signature geometric garden silhouette.
a3c9391ec51c39f54dae.tip: Kanazawa sees relentless winter rain and sleet—locals have an old saying: "Even if you forget your lunchbox, never forget your umbrella." Carry a sturdy windproof folding umbrella and wear waterproof, high-traction boots rather than relying on a hood.
a3c9391ec51c39f54dae.title: See Kenrokuen Garden's winter yukitsuri snow ropes, then stroll Higashi Chaya for gold-leaf sweets

a486336797f49756c607.days.0.items.0.note: Pick up your car at the airport. It takes about 20 minutes to reach the city; stay around the waterfront.
a486336797f49756c607.days.0.move: It takes about 30 minutes to drive from the city to the summit. The summit is windy, so bring a warm jacket.
a486336797f49756c607.days.0.title: Hobart · Mount Wellington
a486336797f49756c607.days.1.move: The MONA fast ferry takes about 30 minutes from Brooke Street Pier. The market is held only on Saturdays, so adjust your plans accordingly.
a486336797f49756c607.days.1.title: Salamanca and MONA
a486336797f49756c607.days.2.move: Hobart → Kettering takes about 40 minutes, followed by a 20-minute ferry ride. Drive slowly on the island's gravel roads.
a486336797f49756c607.days.2.title: Food on Bruny Island
a486336797f49756c607.days.3.items.2.note: Drive along the east coast to Coles Bay in the afternoon and arrive before dark.
a486336797f49756c607.days.3.move: Hobart → Port Arthur takes about 1.5 hours; Port Arthur → Coles Bay takes about 3 hours.
a486336797f49756c607.days.3.title: Port Arthur · Up the east coast
a486336797f49756c607.days.4.items.1.note: In the evening, join an optional tour to see little penguins return to shore in Bicheno.
a486336797f49756c607.days.4.move: Reach the parking lot before 9 a.m. Coles Bay → St Helens takes about 1.5–2 hours.
a486336797f49756c607.days.4.title: Hike to the Wineglass Bay lookout
a486336797f49756c607.days.5.items.1.note: Stop in Launceston around noon to restock, then drive west into the mountains.
a486336797f49756c607.days.5.move: St Helens → Cradle Mountain via Launceston takes about 4–4.5 hours. This is the longest driving day.
a486336797f49756c607.days.5.title: Bay of Fires · West to Cradle Mountain
a486336797f49756c607.days.6.items.1.note: Drive to Launceston in the afternoon to return the car and catch your flight.
a486336797f49756c607.days.6.move: The shuttle from the visitor center to Dove Lake takes about 20 minutes. Cradle Mountain → Launceston Airport takes about 2.5 hours.
a486336797f49756c607.days.6.title: Dove Lake circuit
a486336797f49756c607.for: For confident drivers who enjoy hiking, wildlife, and seafood
a486336797f49756c607.season: Warmest weather and longest days from December–April
a486336797f49756c607.summary: Fly into Hobart and out of Launceston, heading north without backtracking. Spend the first three days in Hobart: explore the market, MONA, Mount Wellington, Port Arthur, and Bruny Island. Then follow the east coast to Freycinet for the Wineglass Bay lookout, continue to the Bay of Fires, and finish with a night at Cradle Mountain to see wombats. Buy a national parks holiday vehicle pass before you leave.

a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.access.0.how: There are usually no nonstop flights. Enter the United States in Los Angeles, San Francisco, or Seattle, then connect through Denver or Salt Lake City to Jackson Hole Airport. The full trip takes about 18–24 hours.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.access.1.how: It is about 440 kilometers (275 miles) to Jackson by car, taking about 4.5–5 hours. West Yellowstone is about 5 hours away.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.access.2.how: Bozeman has many flights. It is about 130 kilometers and 1.5 hours to Yellowstone's North Entrance, or about 2 hours to West Yellowstone.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.access.3.how: It is about 90 kilometers and 1.5 hours through Grand Teton to Yellowstone's South Entrance, or about 2.5–3 hours to Old Faithful.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.cover.alt: Aerial view of Grand Prismatic Spring in Yellowstone
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.foods.0.name: Bison burger
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.foods.0.text: A staple on Wyoming restaurant menus. Bison is leaner and more flavorful than beef. It is most tender when cooked medium; overcooking makes it dry. You can find it at restaurants inside Yellowstone and casual spots in Jackson. Some places also serve elk burgers or elk sausage.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.foods.0.where: In Jackson and at restaurants inside Yellowstone
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.foods.1.name: Huckleberry ice cream
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.foods.1.text: Huckleberries are small purple berries that grow wild in the northern Rockies. They are tarter and more intensely flavored than blueberries and still cannot be grown on a large scale. Yellowstone and Jackson are full of huckleberry ice cream, milkshakes, jam, and pies. Getting a scoop after visiting the geysers is a classic move.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.foods.1.where: Stores inside Yellowstone and ice cream shops in Jackson
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.foods.2.name: Pan-fried trout
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.foods.2.text: Yellowstone and Grand Teton's rivers and lakes are home to native cutthroat trout, and the Snake River area is a renowned fly-fishing destination. The trout served in restaurants is usually farmed. It is coated and pan-fried until crisp, then served with lemon, butter, and potatoes. The mild flavor makes a welcome change after several days of burgers.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.foods.2.where: Restaurants in Jackson and the lake areas inside the parks
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.foods.3.name: Chuckwagon dinner
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.foods.3.text: An old ranch-style Western meal: stew beans, roast beef or chicken, cornbread, and biscuits served at outdoor communal tables, often with a country music performance. Several ranches near Jackson serve dinner every night in summer. It is geared toward visitors and makes a lively outing with children. Reservations are required in advance.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.intro.0: Wyoming is the least populous state in the United States. Almost every visitor heads to the northwest corner: Yellowstone was the world's first national park, with geothermal features, canyons, and wildlife spread across a volcanic plateau about 2,400 meters high. Grand Teton is just to the south, with jagged, snow-covered peaks rising from the plains. Jackson, at the foot of the mountains, is the main gateway town.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.intro.1: Yellowstone is huge. The main loop is about 229 kilometers, speed limits are low, and bison often cause traffic jams when they cross the road. Allow at least three days: one day for the geysers around Old Faithful and Grand Prismatic, one for the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone and Hayden Valley, and one early morning in Lamar Valley to look for wolves and bison. Allow another 1–2 days for Grand Teton. Lodging inside the parks should be booked about a year ahead. If you can't find a room, stay in West Yellowstone, Gardiner, or Jackson.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.intro.2: The season determines what you can see. From about early November to mid-April the roads in Yellowstone are closed to regular vehicles, except for the stretch between the North and Northeast entrances. In winter, you can enter only with snowcoach or snowmobile tours. Some roads begin reopening in May, but high-elevation Dunraven Pass often remains closed until late May. June–September offers the fullest access. September has fewer visitors, and wildlife is still active.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.name: Wyoming
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.seasons.note: All roads are open from June–September. July–August is the busiest period. September has fewer visitors and active wildlife, but temperatures near 0°C are possible in the morning and evening. Most roads in Yellowstone are closed from about early November to mid-April.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.sources.0.title: NPS: Yellowstone entrance fees

a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.sources.2.title: NPS: Yellowstone safety information (wildlife distances and geothermal areas)
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.sources.3.title: NPS: Grand Teton entrance fees
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.sources.4.title: NPS: International visitor fee
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.sources.5.title: NPS: America the Beautiful annual pass
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.0.fee: About $35 per vehicle, plus $100 per international visitor
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.0.name: Old Faithful & Upper Geyser Basin
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.0.text: Yellowstone's most famous geyser erupts about every 90 minutes on average, sending a column of water dozens of meters high. The visitor center and NPS App publish predicted eruption times. Don't leave right after the eruption: the Upper Geyser Basin has the world's highest concentration of geysers. Follow the boardwalk to Morning Glory Pool and back for about 4.5 kilometers, passing bubbling, colorful hot springs and small geysers that could erupt at any time.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.0.tip: The eruption can happen about 10 minutes before or after the predicted time. Across from the geyser, the Old Faithful Inn has a century-old timber lobby that is worth a look.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.1.name: Grand Prismatic Spring
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.1.text: The largest hot spring in the United States is about 110 meters across. Its center is deep blue, surrounded by bands of bacteria in green, yellow, orange, and red. From the boardwalk, you can see mostly steam and the edge. For a full view, go to the Fairy Falls trailhead and climb the slope to the overlook; the round trip is about 2 kilometers. On a sunny afternoon, there is less steam and the colors are clearest.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.1.tip: The parking lot is small. Go before 10 a.m. or in the evening during peak season. Strong winds can blow hats into the hot spring, so secure or stow them.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.2.name: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.2.text: The Yellowstone River cuts a canyon of yellow and pink rock here. The Lower Falls drop about 94 meters, with a powerful flow and thunderous roar. Artist Point on the South Rim is the classic viewpoint, just a short walk from the parking area. On the North Rim, a steep trail leads down to the top of the falls; the round trip is about 1.2 kilometers, and the climb back is tiring. Morning sunlight reaches into the canyon, and you may see a rainbow.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.2.tip: There is a scenic drive on each rim near Canyon Village. Drive between the viewpoints. Afterward, head south to Hayden Valley.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.3.name: Lamar Valley & Hayden Valley
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.3.text: These are Yellowstone's two main wildlife valleys. Open and flat Lamar Valley in the northeast is lined with bison grazing beside the road in summer. With luck, you may spot wolves through binoculars. Hayden Valley, between Canyon Village and the Lake area, has plenty of bison and elk, as well as the occasional grizzly bear. Animals are most active at dawn and dusk. A line of people with long lenses stopped along the road usually means someone has spotted something.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.3.tip: Stay at least about 91 meters (100 yards) from bears and wolves, and at least about 23 meters (25 yards) from bison and elk. Stop only in designated roadside pullouts.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.4.name: Mammoth Hot Springs
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.4.text: Mineral-rich hot springs have built up layer by layer into white, cream, and orange terraces of travertine. The formations change every year. Boardwalks and stairs cross the Lower Terraces, while the Upper Terraces can be explored by car on a short loop. Elk often lie on the lawns in the nearby town of Mammoth, and bulls are aggressive in fall. Near the North Entrance, this area is accessible by car even in winter.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.4.tip: Some terraces dry out and turn gray. Check the visitor center to see which areas are active. Do not walk between elk and vehicles.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.5.fee: About $35 per vehicle, plus $100 per international visitor
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.5.name: Jenny Lake, Grand Teton National Park
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.5.text: This glacial lake lies at the foot of the Teton Range, with Grand Teton, the highest peak, rising behind it at about 4,199 meters. Take the shuttle boat across the lake, then hike about 1.5 kilometers uphill to Hidden Falls and Inspiration Point, where you can look back over the lake and Jackson Hole. Without the boat, follow the lakeshore trail; the one-way distance is about 3 kilometers longer. Grand Teton charges admission separately from Yellowstone, and the international visitor fee is charged separately as well.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.5.tip: This is bear country. Carry bear spray on hikes. It cannot be taken on a plane, so buy or rent it locally. The shuttle boat costs extra.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.6.name: Mormon Row
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.6.text: Mormon settlers built farms on this prairie a century ago, leaving several wooden barns with the Teton Range lined up behind them. It is Grand Teton's classic sunrise location. Nearby, Oxbow Bend can offer reflections of Mount Moran in the early morning, along with moose and bald eagles. The cottonwoods along the river are most beautiful when they turn yellow in late September.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.6.tip: Arrive half an hour before sunrise. Bison often gather on the prairie, so do not approach them for photos.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.7.name: Jackson, Wyoming
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.7.text: This Western town lies south of Grand Teton. Each corner of the central square has an arch made from naturally shed elk antlers. Around it are wooden boardwalks, cowboy bars, and galleries. In summer, take a gondola up the mountain at Jackson Hole Mountain Resort in nearby Teton Village. In winter, it is a ski destination. From about mid-December to early April, horse-drawn sleigh rides at the National Elk Refuge north of town offer close views of thousands of elk spending the winter there.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.spots.7.tip: Prices and room rates are high here, so book early in summer. Stock up at a supermarket in town before entering Yellowstone.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.stay: Old Faithful, Canyon Village, and the Lake area have the best locations for staying inside Yellowstone, so book early. Outside the park, stay in West Yellowstone for easy access to the geysers or Gardiner for quick access to Mammoth and Lamar Valley. In Grand Teton, stay in Jackson or around Jackson Lake inside the park.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.tagline: Yellowstone's geysers and bison, Grand Teton's snowy peaks
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.tips.0: Yellowstone and Grand Teton each charge an entrance fee and a $100 international visitor fee per person. If there are two or more people in the same vehicle, buy the $250 international annual pass instead.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.tips.1: Stay at least about 91 meters from bears and wolves, and at least about 23 meters from bison and elk. Bison injure people every year, so do not approach them for photos.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.tips.2: Stay on boardwalks in geothermal areas. The ground may be a thin crust over scalding water. Touching hot springs and soaking in them are strictly prohibited.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.tips.3: Yellowstone is about 2,400 meters above sea level. Even in summer, hail and temperatures near 0°C are possible, so bring a fleece and a rain jacket. Cell service is very limited in the parks, so download offline maps first.
a5268aaefecb9fcfbd49.tips.4: You can drive in Wyoming with a foreign driver's license. An international driving permit is recommended. Check the rules for your license and rental company, and bring any required translation or supporting documents.

a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.access.0.how: The Hayabusa on the Tohoku Shinkansen takes as little as about 2 hours 13 minutes to Morioka. For Hiraizumi, get off at Ichinoseki Station.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.access.1.how: The Shinkansen takes a little over 30 minutes to Ichinoseki and about 40 minutes to Morioka.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.access.2.how: The JR Tohoku Main Line takes about 8 minutes to Hiraizumi Station.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.foods.0.name: Wanko soba
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.foods.0.text: A server stands beside you and adds another bite of soba to your bowl as soon as you finish the last one, calling out a chant each time. They keep going until you cover the bowl. Most people eat 30–50 bowls; the fun is in the spectacle.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.foods.0.where: Long-established soba restaurants in central Morioka
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.foods.1.name: Morioka reimen
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.foods.1.text: Inspired by Korean naengmyeon, these chewy, translucent noodles come in a cold broth with kimchi and fruit. You can choose the spice level. Almost every yakiniku restaurant in Morioka serves them, and a bowl makes a perfect finish after grilled meat.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.foods.1.where: Yakiniku restaurants and reimen specialty shops around Morioka Station
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.foods.2.name: Jajamen
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.foods.2.text: These thick, flat noodles are topped with meat miso, cucumber, and scallions, then mixed together. At the end, crack a raw egg into the bowl and ask the server to add hot broth. This turns it into a bowl of egg soup, the local way to finish.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.foods.3.name: Ichinoseki mochi cuisine
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.foods.3.text: Ichinoseki and Hiraizumi have a tradition of eating mochi. A set meal comes with several small dishes of mochi served with different toppings and sauces, including edamame paste, sesame, grated daikon, and natto, so you can try many varieties at once.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.foods.3.where: Around Ichinoseki Station and near Chuson-ji in Hiraizumi
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.intro.0: Iwate is the largest prefecture on Honshu, but most visitors focus on two areas: Hiraizumi and Ichinoseki in the south, and the prefectural capital, Morioka, in the north. Hiraizumi's Chuson-ji Konjikido is a World Heritage site, and with the two nearby gorges, it makes a full day out. Morioka's city center is compact and easy to explore on foot, with plenty of noodles to try.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.intro.1: Morioka is a major Shinkansen hub, with Aomori to the north and Kakunodate in Akita to the west along the way. Many travelers stay one night here while traveling through Tohoku. The Sanriku Coast to the east has beautiful scenery but slow transportation, so skip it if you're short on time.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.name: Iwate
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.seasons.note: Morioka's Ishiwarizakura blooms in mid-to-late April, while Hiraizumi's fall colors peak from late October to early November. In winter, gorge cruises have kotatsu tables.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.sources.0.title: Chuson-ji official website
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.sources.1.title: Motsu-ji · Visiting and access
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.sources.2.title: JR Group · Hayabusa stops and travel times
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.0.name: Chuson-ji Konjikido
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.0.text: Built by the Oshu Fujiwara clan more than 900 years ago, this Buddhist hall was covered inside and out with gold leaf. It is now viewed through glass inside a protective concrete shelter. From the entrance, a steep cedar-lined path leads uphill along Tsukimizaka. Part of the Hiraizumi World Heritage site, it is busiest during fall foliage season.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.0.tip: Tsukimizaka is steep, so wear comfortable shoes. Photography is not allowed inside Konjikido.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.1.name: Motsu-ji
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.1.text: The original temple buildings burned down long ago, leaving a peaceful Heian-period Pure Land garden with a large pond, curving stone banks, and foundation stones from the ruins. It is much quieter than Chuson-ji. About a 7-minute walk from Hiraizumi Station, it pairs well with Chuson-ji in a single day.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.1.tip: Iris bloom beside the pond in June–July, when the scenery is beautiful and crowds are light.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.2.name: Geibikei Gorge
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.2.text: Boatmen pole flat-bottomed wooden boats through a limestone gorge, singing local folk songs as they go. The round trip takes about 1.5 hours, with time to walk ashore midway. You can try tossing a small lucky stone into a cave on the opposite bank. In winter, boats have kotatsu tables, so you can watch the snowy scenery from under a blanket.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.2.tip: From Ichinoseki Station, take the JR Ofunato Line to Geibikei Station. Services are infrequent, so check the schedule ahead of time.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.3.name: Genbikei Gorge
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.3.text: This small gorge west of central Ichinoseki has water-worn potholes throughout the stream. The highlight is flying dango: a teahouse on the opposite bank hangs a basket from a cable. Put your money inside and knock on the board, and dango and tea slide over to you. A full walk around the gorge takes just 30–40 minutes.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.3.tip: The bus from Ichinoseki Station takes about 20 minutes. Genbikei can be combined with Hiraizumi in a single day.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.4.name: Ishiwarizakura
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.4.text: This cherry tree grows from a crack in a massive granite boulder and is said to be more than 300 years old. It stands in the grounds of the Morioka District Court. It blooms in mid-to-late April. Stop by Morioka Castle Ruins Park nearby, then explore the rest of downtown on foot.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.4.tip: It is in the city center, so just stop by during cherry blossom season rather than making a special trip.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.5.name: Koiwai Farm
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.5.text: This century-old farm west of Morioka has a visitor area where you can feed sheep and ride a horse-drawn carriage. Its own milk, ice cream, and cheese are well known. In late April, the farm's Ipponzakura cherry tree against the still-snowy Mount Iwate is a popular photo subject.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.5.tip: Some areas close in winter. Families with children will enjoy visiting most in spring or summer.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.6.name: Jodogahama Beach
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.6.text: White rhyolite islets line a shallow bay along the Sanriku Coast, where the water is clear and green. Take a sightseeing boat to watch gulls grab food, or board a small boat in the shallows to visit the Blue Cave. The bus from Morioka takes more than 2 hours, so this is better for a second visit or a slow trip along the coast.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.spots.6.tip: Swimming and Blue Cave boats are available only in summer. Many activities stop in winter.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.stay: Stay around Morioka Station for plenty of dining options and easy trips to Hiraizumi, Kakunodate, and Aomori. If you're only visiting Hiraizumi, staying near Ichinoseki Station also works.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.tagline: Chuson-ji Konjikido, gorge cruises, and endless bowls of wanko soba
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.tips.0: Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your licence and required documents. Check the official rules. A loop bus from in front of Hiraizumi Station connects the main sights.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.tips.1: The sights in Hiraizumi are fairly close together. To save money, rent a bicycle in front of the station.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.tips.2: Many wanko soba restaurants require reservations. Call or book online ahead of time on weekends and during peak seasons.
a551aedaf17eda9b8ec6.tips.3: Check the bus schedule carefully before heading to the Sanriku Coast. Some routes run only a few times a day.
