a80c50a21accff018fa0.access.0.how: The Joetsu Shinkansen takes about 1 hour 20 minutes to Echigo-Yuzawa and about 1 hour 40 minutes–2 hours to Niigata Station
a80c50a21accff018fa0.access.1.how: The airport bus takes about 25 minutes to Niigata Station and costs about ¥470; flights are available from Seoul and Taipei
a80c50a21accff018fa0.access.2.how: Sado Kisen to Ryotsu Port: about 67 minutes by high-speed ferry or 2 hours 30 minutes by car ferry
a80c50a21accff018fa0.foods.0.name: Hegi soba
a80c50a21accff018fa0.foods.0.text: This soba uses funori seaweed as a binder, giving it a smooth, springy texture. The noodles are served in small bundles on a square wooden tray called a hegi, usually for several people to share.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.foods.0.where: Traditional restaurants in Tokamachi and Ojiya; also available around Echigo-Yuzawa Station
a80c50a21accff018fa0.foods.1.name: Tare katsudon
a80c50a21accff018fa0.foods.1.text: Niigata's version of pork cutlet rice has no egg. Thin pork cutlets are fried, dipped in a sweet-and-savory soy sauce, and placed directly over rice. The result is crisp without being greasy.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.foods.2.name: Niigata sake
a80c50a21accff018fa0.foods.2.text: Niigata has more breweries than almost anywhere else in Japan. Its signature style is tanrei karakuchi: light, clean, and dry. If you're not sure what to choose, visit a tasting counter in a station and compare several varieties before buying a favorite.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.foods.2.where: Sake tasting shops inside Echigo-Yuzawa Station and Niigata Station
a80c50a21accff018fa0.foods.3.name: Sasa dango
a80c50a21accff018fa0.foods.3.text: These mugwort mochi dumplings are filled with sweet red bean paste and wrapped tightly in bamboo leaves. They're Niigata's most common souvenir. Freshly made ones are softest; if they harden, steam them briefly.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.foods.3.where: Souvenir shops at Niigata Station and Echigo-Yuzawa Station
a80c50a21accff018fa0.intro.0: Niigata lies on the Sea of Japan side of Honshu. It gets heavy snow in winter, and this is the area featured in Yasunari Kawabata's Snow Country. For most travelers, Echigo-Yuzawa is the easiest base: the Joetsu Shinkansen takes about 1 hour 20 minutes from Tokyo, and you can soak in hot springs or ski right after leaving the station. A winter day trip is also easy.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.intro.1: The other major draw is offshore: Sado Gold Mine was added to the World Heritage list in 2024. On the island's south side, Shukunegi is an old fishing village with boat-shaped wooden houses. The island is large, so plan to stay one night. In summer and fall, you can link Kiyotsu Gorge Tunnel, Hoshitoge Rice Terraces, and Yahiko Shrine, but buses between rural sights are infrequent, so check the schedules in advance.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.name: Niigata
a80c50a21accff018fa0.seasons.note: See snow and ski from December–March; Takada's illuminated cherry blossoms in early to mid-April; fall colors at Kiyotsu Gorge Tunnel from mid-October to early November. Weekend visits often require reservations.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.sources.0.title: Historic Site: Sado Gold Mine admission fees
a80c50a21accff018fa0.sources.1.title: Sado Kisen fare table
a80c50a21accff018fa0.sources.2.title: Niigata Kanko Navi: Kiyotsu Gorge
a80c50a21accff018fa0.sources.3.title: Niigata Airport bus transportation
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.0.name: Sado Gold Mine
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.0.text: Gold and silver were mined here for nearly 400 years beginning in the Edo period. In 2024, it was added to the World Heritage list as Sado Island Gold Mine. At the Sohdayu Mine, moving figures recreate the miners' work. The Doyu Mine shows Doyu no Warito, a mountain split open by mining. Buses on the island require transfers and run infrequently, so consider booking a local day-tour bus.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.0.tip: The tunnels stay around 10℃ year-round, so bring a jacket even in summer.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.1.name: Shukunegi
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.1.text: This small fishing village at the southern tip of Sado Island grew wealthy during the Edo period through the Kitamaebune trade. More than 100 wooden houses crowd its narrow lanes, including a distinctive triangular house known as the Boat House. Nearby Ogi Port offers rides in tarai bune, traditional washtub boats. The village is tiny and takes about 30 minutes to walk through, making it easy to combine with Sado Gold Mine for a 2-day island trip.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.1.tip: This is a residential village. Don't enter private yards to take photos, and keep your voice down.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.2.name: Kiyotsu Gorge Tunnel
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.2.text: One of Japan's three great gorges, this site was transformed into the Tunnel of Light in 2018 by a team led by Chinese architect Ma Yansong. Walk about 750 meters to the end, where a shallow pool reflects the gorge in a circular frame. The bus from Echigo-Yuzawa Station takes about 25 minutes, followed by a walk of about 30 minutes.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.2.tip: During fall foliage season and long holidays, it often operates by reservation only. You can't enter without a ticket, so buy one on the official website first.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.3.name: Echigo-Yuzawa Onsen
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.3.text: This is the snowy country at the beginning of Snow Country. The hot-spring district starts right outside the Shinkansen station. During ski season, some Shinkansen trains continue to GALA Yuzawa Station, where the ski resort is right outside and you can rent equipment. Ponshukan inside the station offers coin-operated tastings of sake from across Niigata. It's easy to visit as a day trip from Tokyo or stay overnight.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.3.tip: GALA Yuzawa operates only during ski season, so check the opening dates before you go.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.4.name: Hoshitoge Rice Terraces
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.4.text: More than 100 rice terraces cascade down the hillsides of Matsudai in Tokamachi. After the fields are flooded in spring and on fall mornings, the water reflects the sky, sometimes with a sea of clouds. It's a favorite scene among photographers. There is no direct bus, so you'll generally need to hire a car or join a local sightseeing tour.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.4.tip: The terraces are private farmland. Take photos only from the viewing area, don't walk on the ridges, and don't fly a drone without permission.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.5.name: Yahiko Shrine
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.5.text: Echigo's Ichi-no-miya, with a quiet approach lined by ancient trees. A ropeway behind the shrine goes up Mount Yahiko, which is 634 meters high—the same height as Tokyo Skytree. From the summit, you can look over the Echigo Plain and the Sea of Japan, and on clear days, see Sado Island. A chrysanthemum festival takes place in November, when the nearby Maple Valley also turns red.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.5.tip: It's about a 15-minute walk from JR Yahiko Station. The ropeway is weather-dependent, so check operations before you go.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.6.name: Takada Castle Site Park
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.6.text: This castle site park in Joetsu is home to about 4,000 cherry trees. In early to mid-April, the trees are illuminated at night, and the pink blossoms reflect in the moat. The display is considered one of Japan's three great nighttime cherry blossom views. From Hokuriku Shinkansen's Joetsu-Myoko Station, transfer to Takada Station, then walk about 20 minutes.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.spots.6.tip: Nights are still cold during cherry blossom season, so bring a warm jacket. Weekends are busiest in the evening.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.stay: If you're visiting for snow and hot springs, stay near Echigo-Yuzawa Station. The Shinkansen, ski resorts, and hot springs are all within walking distance. If you're going to Sado Island, stay near Niigata Station, which is close to the Sado Kisen ferry terminal, then spend one night on the island.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.tagline: Snow country 80 minutes from Tokyo, plus Sado Gold Mine and great rice and sake
a80c50a21accff018fa0.tips.0: Snow is deep in winter, so wear nonslip, waterproof shoes. Take short, slow steps when the roads are icy.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.tips.1: Whether your driver's licence and any required translation or permit are accepted for driving in Japan depends on your licence. For rural sights such as the rice terraces, consider a local sightseeing bus or private car.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.tips.2: Sado Island is large and has infrequent buses. A day trip is enough for only one sight, so plan to stay one night.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.tips.3: Skiers crowd the Joetsu Shinkansen toward Echigo-Yuzawa on winter weekends and around the year-end holidays. Reserve a reserved seat in advance.
a80c50a21accff018fa0.tips.4: Niigata rice and sake make the easiest souvenirs to take home. Station souvenir shops have the widest selection.

a8750c9a72f4973731c3.cost: Designated Odakyu/Fujikyu bus legs included in pass
a8750c9a72f4973731c3.location: Togendai Port → Moto-Hakone / Sengokuhara → Gotemba Station → Kawaguchiko Station
a8750c9a72f4973731c3.paragraphs.0: Board the Lake Ashi Sightseeing Pirate Ship at Togendai for a 35-minute volcanic-lake cruise to Moto-Hakone. From the top deck you'll spot Hakone Shrine's vermilion torii standing in the lake against ancient cedars—afternoon photo queues right under the gate often pass 40 minutes, so frame it cleanly from the lakeshore or enjoy hot soba nearby instead.
a8750c9a72f4973731c3.paragraphs.1: Next comes the one time-critical pivot of the trip: crossing from Hakone to Kawaguchiko via Gotemba Station (or Gotemba Outlets). Take the Odakyu Highway Bus from Togendai or Sengokuhara (~35 min to Gotemba), then switch to a Fujikyu local bus (~1h 15m) straight to Kawaguchiko Station. Aim to leave Hakone right around 15:00 so you check in by 17:30—after dark, mountain buses drop to hourly intervals!
a8750c9a72f4973731c3.phase: Step 03 · Day 1 13:00 Lake Ashi Pirate Ship & Mountain Transfer
a8750c9a72f4973731c3.photo.alt: Vermilion torii gate standing in Lake Ashi backed by cedar trees
a8750c9a72f4973731c3.photo.caption: Framed by towering ancient cedars, Hakone's red lakeshore torii looks most poetic from the boat deck or quiet afternoon piers.
a8750c9a72f4973731c3.tip: Bus schedules between Hakone and Kawaguchiko adjust seasonally—screenshot your exact 14:30–16:30 Navitime or Google Maps connections before heading up into spotty mountain reception.

a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.gateways.0.how: The JR Rapid Airport takes as little as 37 minutes to Sapporo, for about ¥1,230; Otaru takes about 1 hour 15 minutes
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.gateways.0.name: New Chitose Airport (CTS)
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.gateways.1.how: It is close to downtown. The airport bus takes about 20–30 minutes to Hakodate Station, making it convenient for trips focused on southern Hokkaido or travel north from Tohoku
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.gateways.1.name: Hakodate Airport (HKD)
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.gateways.2.how: The Hokkaido Shinkansen takes as little as 4 hours from Tokyo. The Hakodate Liner takes about 15–20 minutes to Hakodate Station
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.gateways.2.name: Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto Station
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.intro.0: Hokkaido is Japan’s northernmost and second-largest main island, treated as its own region. Most visitors arrive at New Chitose Airport and use Sapporo as their base, heading west to Otaru, northeast to Furano, Biei, and Asahikawa, and south to Noboribetsu Onsen and Hakodate. Cities are far apart, and limited express trains often take two or three hours. On your first visit, stick to two or three areas.
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.intro.1: Summer is cool and full of flowers, making it the most comfortable season. Winter brings excellent snow, snow festivals, skiing, and hot springs surrounded by snow, but weather can disrupt transportation. Shiretoko, Akan, and Kushiro Shitsugen in eastern Hokkaido have the wildest scenery and limited public transportation. They are better for a guided or private-car trip on a return visit.
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.name: Hokkaido
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.passes.0.name: Hokkaido Rail Pass
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.passes.0.text: Unlimited travel on all JR Hokkaido lines except the Shinkansen for 5/7/10 consecutive days. Purchase in advance for about ¥22,000 for 5 days. It pays off only if you plan to travel long distances to Hakodate or eastern Hokkaido
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.passes.1.name: Sapporo–Furano Area Pass
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.passes.1.text: 4 days, about ¥11,000, covering New Chitose Airport, Sapporo, Otaru, Asahikawa, Biei, and Furano. The best choice if you are visiting only these places
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.passes.2.name: Sapporo–Noboribetsu Area Pass
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.passes.2.text: 4 days, about ¥10,000, covering New Chitose Airport, Sapporo, Otaru, and Noboribetsu. Good for Sapporo plus one night at Noboribetsu Onsen
a9cc3da73f6eb4cce12b.season: See flowers and escape the heat in June–August; see snow and soak in hot springs in December–February. Fall foliage comes in September–October, when crowds and prices are lower.

ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.access.0.how: There are no direct flights. Most routes connect through Seattle, with the Seattle–Anchorage flight taking about 3.5 hours. You can also connect through Los Angeles, San Francisco or Tokyo.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.access.1.how: About 4 hours by car; the Alaska Railroad takes about 7.5–8 hours in summer and offers scenic views.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.access.2.how: About 2.5 hours by car. The Seward Highway along Turnagain Arm is very scenic, and trains also run in summer.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.access.3.how: There is no road access. Fly from Seattle or Anchorage in about 2 hours, or take a cruise ship or state ferry.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.0.name: Wild Alaska salmon
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.0.text: Almost all salmon in Alaska is wild. In summer, different species return to the rivers at different times: king salmon is the richest, sockeye is the reddest and most flavorful, and coho is lighter. Restaurants often serve it grilled or cedar-plank roasted, as well as in tacos and smoked. Menus usually list the species and origin.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.0.where: Seafood restaurants and harbor stalls in Anchorage, Seward and Juneau.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.1.name: Alaskan king crab legs
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.1.price: Priced by the pound, about $60–100 and up
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.1.text: Caught in the Bering Sea, king crab has long, thick legs with meat that pulls out in one piece. Dip it in warm butter for a sweet, springy bite. It is expensive and priced by the pound. Most crab is reheated after freezing, and freshly caught crab is rare. Before ordering, confirm whether the price is for one pound or a whole crab.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.1.where: Seafood restaurants and harbor food trucks in Juneau and Anchorage.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.2.name: Halibut fish and chips
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.2.text: Alaskan fish and chips often uses halibut, which has thick, white flesh that holds together well. It is fried in a light, crisp batter and served with fries and tartar sauce. Harbor stalls around Homer and Seward fry it to order, making it a popular meal after a cruise.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.2.where: Harbor seafood stalls in Seward and Homer, and seafood shops in Anchorage.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.3.name: Reindeer sausage
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.3.text: A popular Alaskan street food, reindeer meat is mixed with pork or beef to make a smoked sausage. It is grilled, placed in a bun and topped with sautéed onions and mustard. The flavor is richer and slightly gamier than a regular hot dog. Breakfast restaurants also serve it with eggs and potatoes.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.foods.3.where: Hot dog stands and breakfast restaurants in downtown Anchorage.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.intro.0: Alaska is the largest state in the United States. Much of it is wilderness, and towns are often connected by just one road. There are two main ways to visit: May–September is the travel season, with Denali, fjord glaciers, whales and brown bears; late August–April is aurora season, centered around Fairbanks in the north.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.intro.1: The most common summer route starts in Anchorage: head south to Seward for a glacier cruise, north to Denali National Park for a park bus, then continue to Fairbanks, taking 7–9 days. You can connect the route by car, Alaska Railroad or tour bus. Juneau and Glacier Bay in the southeast have no road access, so you must fly or take a ferry or cruise ship.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.intro.2: Prices here are higher than in the rest of the United States. Lodging is tight during the travel season, and popular dates sell out months in advance. Weather changes quickly in the wilderness, and there are plenty of mosquitoes. This is a place for patience and time, not a rushed checklist of sights.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.name: Alaska
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.seasons.note: June–August brings long days and full service on all routes; early September has fall colors and the first chance to see the aurora; aurora season runs roughly from late August to mid-April, while February–March offers long enough nights without the coldest temperatures.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.0.name: Anchorage
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.0.text: Alaska's largest city and the starting point for most trips. Downtown is compact. Allow half a day for the Alaska Native Heritage Center and Anchorage Museum. You can bike the Tony Knowles Coastal Trail along the water, with views of Cook Inlet and distant mountains. South of the city, the Seward Highway hugs Turnagain Arm, where Dall sheep and beluga whales are often visible from the road.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.0.tip: At 11 p.m. in summer, it can still be light. A sleep mask is useful. Moose sometimes wander through town, so keep your distance.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.1.fee: About $15 per person, valid for 7 days
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.1.name: Denali National Park and Preserve
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.1.text: Denali, North America's highest peak, is about 6,190 meters tall and is often hidden by clouds. Seeing the whole mountain is a matter of luck. Private cars can drive only as far as Mile 15 at Savage River; beyond that, take a park bus. The new bridge at the Pretty Rocks landslide is due for completion in September 2026, but buses will run only to around Mile 43 at East Fork that season. Full-route service is expected to resume in 2027. Brown bears, caribou and moose are common along the way.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.1.tip: Buses generally run from mid-May to mid-September. Book through the official website, and reserve well ahead if you are staying only briefly. Bring lunch and water.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.2.fee: The park is free; cruises cost extra
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.2.name: Kenai Fjords National Park and Seward
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.2.text: From Seward harbor, take a fjord cruise. The 6–9-hour routes reach tidewater glaciers, where you may see chunks of ice calving into the sea. Sea otters, sea lions, humpback whales and orcas are common along the way. The park has no entrance fee. On land, you can visit Exit Glacier, about a 30-minute walk from the parking lot to the glacier face. Signs along the trail show how far the glacier has retreated over the years.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.2.tip: Cruises may shorten their routes in rough seas. If you get seasick, take medication in advance. Book cruises and lodging ahead for July–August.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.3.name: Fairbanks aurora
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.3.text: Fairbanks is about 200 kilometers south of the Arctic Circle, directly beneath the auroral oval. Its dry inland climate brings many clear nights, making it one of the most reliable places in the United States to see the aurora. The official aurora season runs roughly from August 21 to April 21. Stay at least 3 nights and watch from outside town between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m. for a good chance of seeing it. At Chena Hot Springs north of the city, you can soak outdoors while waiting for the aurora.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.3.tip: Temperatures often drop to −30°C from December–February. Phones and batteries lose power quickly, so bring enough warm clothing and hand warmers.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.4.fee: About $5 per person for the visitor center in summer
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.4.name: Mendenhall Glacier
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.4.text: About a 20-minute drive from downtown Juneau, this glacier's blue-and-white tongue can be seen across the lake from the visitor center. The most popular trail leads to Nugget Falls. The round trip is about 3 kilometers, mostly flat and easy, and reaches the foot of the falls with side views of the glacier. From July–September, black bears are often seen fishing for salmon along the creekside viewing boardwalk.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.4.tip: The glacier is busiest during the day when cruise ships are in port. Go in the evening for a quieter visit. Keep your distance from bears and follow ranger instructions.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.5.name: Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.5.text: This glacier-carved fjord northwest of Juneau was covered by ice more than 200 years ago. There is no entrance fee, but no road access either. Most visitors see it from a cruise ship's deck, with a ranger providing commentary on board. Independent travelers can fly from Juneau to Gustavus, stay in a lodge at Bartlett Cove, and take the park's day boat to the glaciers.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.spots.5.tip: Day boats and lodges operate only in summer. Space is limited, so book several months ahead.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.stay: Stay in downtown Anchorage for easy access to the airport and train station; near the Denali park entrance around Glitter Gulch; at Seward harbor for glacier trips; or in a hillside cabin outside Fairbanks during winter, away from the city's light pollution.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.tagline: See glaciers and brown bears in summer, and the aurora in winter
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.tips.0: Visitors may be allowed to drive in Alaska with a valid license from their home country for up to about 90 days. If your license is not in English, carry an official translation. Bring your passport as well. Check the current rules for your license and nationality.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.tips.1: Outside Anchorage, many stretches of road have no gas stations or signal for dozens of kilometers. Refuel when the tank is half full, and download offline maps in advance.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.tips.2: If you encounter a bear while hiking, do not run. Speak loudly and back away slowly. You can buy bear spray in bear country, but it cannot be taken on a plane.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.tips.3: There is almost no darkness in June–July, so you will not see the aurora. To see it, wait until late August or later.
ad7214382c68afa6eb9a.tips.4: During the travel season, lodging and cruises around Denali and Seward sell out well in advance. Make your reservations before setting out.

af70f636e4e9e8d04cb2.cost: Lookouts free; optional 15-minute scenic helicopter flight about A$175 / person
af70f636e4e9e8d04cb2.duration: About 3 hours (arrive 1.5 hours before local sunset)
af70f636e4e9e8d04cb2.location: Gibson Steps → Twelve Apostles → Port Campbell
af70f636e4e9e8d04cb2.paragraphs.0: Rejoining the coast in the afternoon brings you straight into the trip's grand finale: the Shipwreck Coast. Do not drive past Gibson Steps just a 2-minute drive east of the Twelve Apostles—descend all 86 stone steps carved into the 70-meter sheer cliff straight onto golden sand. Looking straight up at two colossal limestone stacks from the surf line makes you feel ten times smaller than viewing them from above (note the beach closes during heavy swells or king tides; obey entrance signs).
af70f636e4e9e8d04cb2.paragraphs.1: Drive 3 minutes onward to the Twelve Apostles Visitor Centre. If your budget allows, spring for a 15-minute helicopter flight from the helipad next door—seeing the sculpted cliff line from the air is unforgettable. Claim a railing spot on the east and west viewing decks 45 minutes before sunset as the dying light ignites the limestone walls in glowing amber and sea spray turns the sky from gold to violet-pink. Head out before total darkness for the easy 10-minute drive into Port Campbell and a hot roast lamb dinner.
af70f636e4e9e8d04cb2.phase: Step 04 · Day 2 15:00 The climax: Gibson Steps & Twelve Apostles sunset
af70f636e4e9e8d04cb2.photo.alt: Untamed coastal reserves and lush green headlands along southwest Victoria
af70f636e4e9e8d04cb2.photo.caption: Southwest Victoria sweeps unbroken from forested hills down to wild coastal reserves—every mile outside the car window opens onto another vast southern landscape.
af70f636e4e9e8d04cb2.tip: In peak Southern Hemisphere summer (December–February), sunset stretches past 20:30, whereas in winter (June–August) the sun drops by 17:15—check the exact local sunset time the evening before so you don't miss the golden twenty minutes, and grip your phone tight in the fierce cliff winds.
af70f636e4e9e8d04cb2.title: Descend Gibson Steps to stand beneath towering sea stacks, then claim a spot for Twelve Apostles sunset

b00bbe280b3c8a518824.0: First-time Tokyo travelers almost always wrestle with the same dilemma: Hakone or Lake Kawaguchiko—and can you pull off both in two days? Yes, once you crack the logistics. Hakone runs on Odakyu lines while Kawaguchiko runs on Fujikyu, separated by Gotemba's mountain pass with no direct train—only infrequent mountain buses linking the two.
b00bbe280b3c8a518824.1: I ran this tested 2-day, 1-night clockwise loop staying overnight at Kawaguchiko: Day 1 rides the Romancecar from Shinjuku through Hakone's switchback train, Owakudani ropeway, and Lake Ashi pirate ship before catching an afternoon bus across Gotemba to Kawaguchiko; Day 2 opens curtains at 06:30 to Reverse Fuji, covers Oishi Park and Chureito Pagoda, and glides back to Shinjuku by evening.

b1ab5d06381062d9759d.budget.note: Estimated for the low season, for about 7–10 days per person; rental cars are split between two people. Flights and hotels are often more than 50% more expensive during Lunar New Year, the December–January summer holidays, and Christmas. Accommodation at Uluru is more expensive.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.numbers.0.label: Police / ambulance / fire
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.numbers.0.note: Free. After connecting, say Police, Ambulance, or Fire, then give your address.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.numbers.1.label: Mobile emergency number
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.numbers.1.note: An international emergency number on mobile phones that connects to 000.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.numbers.2.label: Police non-emergency assistance
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.numbers.2.note: For lost property and non-emergency incidents. Call 000 if there is an immediate danger.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.numbers.3.label: Poisons information
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.numbers.3.note: 24-hour advice for accidental ingestion, medication misuse, or bites from poisonous animals.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.numbers.4.label: Flood and storm assistance (SES)
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.numbers.4.note: For non-life-threatening assistance with heavy rain, floods, fallen trees, and similar incidents.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.0.items.0.text: Travelers visiting Australia must apply online in advance for a Visitor visa (subclass 600), Tourist stream, through ImmiAccount. Apply from outside Australia. Fees start at about A$ 250 (official price as of November 2026). Visas generally allow a 3-month stay and may permit single or multiple entry, depending on your passport and circumstances.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.0.items.0.title: Apply for a subclass 600 visitor visa
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.0.items.1.text: Processing times are not guaranteed, so apply at least 1–2 months before departure. You may be asked to provide fingerprints, a photo (biometrics), or additional documents. The official website advises against making travel plans until you receive written notice that your visa has been granted. Book refundable flights and hotels when possible.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.0.items.1.title: Allow plenty of processing time
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.0.items.2.text: Frequent visitors to Australia can apply for the Frequent Traveller stream of the Visitor visa. Eligibility depends on your passport and circumstances. It can be valid for up to 10 years, with stays of up to 3 months per visit. The fee is about A$ 1,845, and you must provide fingerprints at an Australian biometrics collection center.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.0.items.2.title: 10-year multiple-entry visa
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.0.items.3.text: The Electronic Travel Authority (ETA) is available only to holders of certain passports, including those from the United States, Japan, Singapore, and Hong Kong. The eVisitor is mainly for European passport holders. Check the official website to see which option, if any, is available for your passport. Online claims about visa-free entry or visas on arrival may not apply to your passport.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.0.items.3.title: ETA and eVisitor may not be available
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.0.items.4.text: Passport holders aged 7 or over and at least 1.1 meters tall can generally use the SmartGate automated border gates. If you cannot use one, join the staffed queue. Keep your return ticket and accommodation details with you, and be ready to explain your itinerary if asked.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.0.items.4.title: Automated border gates
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.0.title: Visas and entry
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.1.items.0.text: On arrival, complete the Incoming Passenger Card, which is usually handed out on the plane. Starting in 2026, Australia is gradually introducing the online Australia Travel Declaration. The web version currently applies only to flights arriving at Western Sydney International Airport and can be completed up to 72 hours in advance.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.1.items.0.title: The arrival card is still on paper
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.1.items.1.text: Australian biosecurity rules are strict. Declare fresh fruit, meat (including vacuum-packed jerky and sausages), eggs and egg products, raw nuts, seeds, Chinese herbal medicines, and homemade food on your arrival card. If you are unsure, answer “yes” and hand the items over for inspection. Declared items may be confiscated or disposed of at worst; failing to declare them can lead to fines and, in serious cases, visa cancellation.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.1.items.1.title: Declare all food
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.1.items.2.text: Travelers aged 18 or over can generally bring in about A$ 900 worth of general goods and 2.25 liters of alcohol duty-free. The duty-free tobacco allowance is very low. Declare anything over the limit and pay the applicable tax. Check the ABF website before departure. Travelers have had visas canceled, been deported, or detained for failing to declare large quantities of cigarettes.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.1.items.2.title: Duty-free allowances are limited
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.1.items.3.text: You must declare cash of A$ 10,000 or more, or the equivalent in foreign currency. Carry prescriptions or information in English for personal prescription medicines, and keep them in their original packaging. Some Chinese medicines contain controlled substances and may be confiscated, so check the rules before departure.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.1.items.3.title: Cash and medicine
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.1.title: Arrival declarations and quarantine
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.2.items.0.text: Cards and contactless payments work almost everywhere in Australia. Many cafes and parking lots no longer accept cash. Bring a Visa or Mastercard credit card as your main card and another as a backup. Some stores serving Chinese tourists accept Alipay or WeChat Pay, but this is not widespread. UnionPay is accepted in fewer places.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.2.items.0.title: Cards are the main way to pay
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.2.items.1.text: From October 1, 2026, businesses cannot add a surcharge to eftpos, Visa, or Mastercard payments. Many restaurants also add a 10–15% surcharge on Sundays and public holidays. The menu or entrance should state this.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.2.items.1.title: Card surcharges are being removed
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.2.items.2.text: Australia has no strong tipping culture, so you do not need to tip at restaurants, in taxis, or at hotels. For especially good service, you can round up or leave a small amount. Upscale restaurants may add a service fee for large groups, so check the bill before paying.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.2.items.2.title: Tipping is not expected
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.2.items.3.text: Within 60 days before departure, you can claim a refund of the GST included in the price (about one-eleventh of the tax-inclusive price) if you spend at least A$ 300, including GST, with the same business (the same ABN). Wine may also qualify for a refund of the wine equalisation tax. You need the original English-language paper tax invoice. Invoices over A$ 1,000 must show the name on your passport. Keep the goods with you for inspection.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.2.items.3.title: TRS tax refund rules
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.2.items.4.text: On departure day, go to the TRS counter after passport control. Bring your passport, boarding pass, goods, and invoices, and complete the claim at least 30 minutes before your flight departs. You can fill out the form at trs.border.gov.au in advance and generate a QR code to save time. Refunds go to a credit card, an Australian bank account, or by check—not in cash.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.2.items.4.title: How to claim the refund
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.2.title: Payments, tipping, and refunds
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.3.items.0.text: Australia is huge: Sydney to Perth takes about 4–5 hours by air, and Sydney to Uluru takes about 3 hours. Domestic flights are the usual way to travel between states. Book one or two months ahead for better prices. Low-cost airlines charge extra for checked baggage and meals.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.3.items.0.title: Fly between states
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.3.items.1.text: Driving requirements vary by state. Visitors generally need to carry their original driving licence and an original NAATI-certified translation; photocopies are not accepted. Some states, such as South Australia, may also accept a translation issued by an embassy or consulate. Rental companies may have additional requirements, so check the transport department website for each state you plan to visit.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.3.items.1.title: Bring a translation of your driving licence
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.3.items.2.text: Australia drives on the left, with the steering wheel on the right. Turns and roundabouts are the easiest places to make mistakes. Travel clockwise around roundabouts and give way to vehicles coming from the right. Rural speed limits are often 100–110 km/h, and speed cameras are common. Kangaroos often come onto roads at dusk and night, so drive long distances during the day when possible.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.3.items.2.title: Drive on the left
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.3.items.3.text: Buses and trains in Sydney (Opal), Melbourne (myki), Perth (SmartRider), and Adelaide (metroCARD) generally let you tap a Visa or Mastercard credit card or mobile wallet directly at the gates. Short-term visitors usually do not need a transit card. Tap on and off; failing to tap may result in the maximum fare being charged.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.3.items.3.title: Tap on and off for city transit
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.3.items.4.text: Fuel stations in the outback can be hundreds of kilometers apart, so fill up whenever you see one. Many rental contracts prohibit driving on unsealed roads or at night. In the north, roads are often flooded during the wet season (about November–April). Check local road conditions before setting out.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.3.items.4.title: Driving in the outback and north
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.3.title: Transport and driving
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.4.items.0.text: The three major carriers are Telstra, Optus, and Vodafone. You can buy prepaid SIM cards at airports, supermarkets, and convenience stores. Activation requires passport identification. Choose Telstra for the outback, islands, and national parks because it has the widest coverage. Any carrier is fine if you are staying only in major cities.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.4.items.0.title: Local SIM cards
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.4.items.1.text: Newer phones can use an eSIM. Buy and activate one online before departure, then use it as soon as you land. Roaming packages from your home carrier also work and are convenient for short trips, but data is usually more expensive than with a local SIM. Apps such as WeChat and Alipay generally work normally in Australia.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.4.items.1.title: eSIMs and roaming
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.4.items.2.text: Many roads outside cities have no mobile coverage at all. Download offline maps before entering a national park, and save screenshots of your accommodation address and booking details. For wilderness hikes or long road trips, consider renting satellite communication equipment or a personal locator beacon.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.4.items.2.title: Remote areas may have no signal
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.4.title: Internet and phones
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.5.items.0.text: Call 000 for police, fire, or ambulance services. The call is free. Once connected, say which service you need. You can also dial 112 from a mobile phone. Visitors must pay for ambulance services, which can be expensive, so make sure your insurance covers ambulances and hospitalization.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.5.items.0.title: Emergency number: 000
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.5.items.1.text: Many Australian beaches have rip currents. Swim only in areas with lifeguards and red-and-yellow flags. In northern waters—including northern Queensland, the Northern Territory, and northern Western Australia—box jellyfish season is about October–May. Estuaries and waterholes may contain saltwater crocodiles. Do not enter the water where warning signs are posted.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.5.items.1.title: Swim only between the red and yellow flags
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.5.items.2.text: Australia's UV levels are much higher than in many other countries, and you can get sunburned even on cloudy days. Wear a wide-brimmed hat and sunglasses, and reapply SPF50 sunscreen every two hours. Avoid extended sun exposure from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. when possible.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.5.items.2.title: UV levels are extremely high
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.5.items.3.text: The southern states have their highest bushfire risk around December–February. Monitor state fire department apps and alerts, and avoid entering bushland on days rated “extreme.” Inland summer temperatures often exceed 40°C. Start hikes early and drink about 1 liter of water per hour. If your vehicle breaks down, stay with it and wait for help.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.5.items.3.title: Bushfire season and heat
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.5.items.4.text: Most snakes and spiders do not attack unless provoked. Do not reach into rocks or tree hollows. After a bite, apply a pressure bandage with an elastic bandage, keep still, and call 000 immediately. Do not feed kangaroos, wallabies, or birds. Human food can make them sick, and feeding wildlife is punishable by fines in some places.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.5.items.4.title: Wildlife
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.5.title: Safety and weather
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.6.items.0.text: Australia uses 230V and 50Hz, with angled three-flat-pin plugs (Type I). Type I plugs fit directly; two parallel flat-pin plugs and round-pin plugs do not, so bring an adapter to be safe. Wall outlets have switches; press the switch after plugging in to turn them on.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.6.items.0.title: Plugs are mostly compatible
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.6.items.1.text: Western Australia uses UTC+8. The Northern Territory and South Australia use UTC+9:30. Queensland, New South Wales, the Australian Capital Territory, Victoria, and Tasmania use UTC+10.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.6.items.1.title: Three time zones
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.6.items.2.text: From the first Sunday in October to the first Sunday in April the following year, New South Wales, the Australian Capital Territory, Victoria, and Tasmania use UTC+11, while South Australia uses UTC+10:30. Queensland, the Northern Territory, and Western Australia do not change their clocks. Check which time zone applies when booking an interstate flight.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.6.items.2.title: Daylight saving time is not used everywhere
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.6.items.3.text: Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere: December–February is summer and June–August is winter. The tropical north has a dry season (about May–October) and a wet season (about November–April). The period around Lunar New Year is Australia's summer and a peak travel period for visitors from China, so flights and hotels are more expensive.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.6.items.3.title: The seasons are reversed
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.6.items.4.text: Tap water is safe to drink in cities. Stores generally close at 5–6 p.m. In major cities, one evening a week—often Thursday or Friday—has later opening hours. Shops have shorter hours on Sundays and public holidays, and finding a restaurant open after 8 p.m. can be difficult in smaller towns.
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.6.items.4.title: Tap water and opening hours
b1ab5d06381062d9759d.sections.6.title: Plugs, voltage, and time zones

b2beaaf6481e75385111.location: Kamakura Station East Exit · Komachi-dori → Tsurugaoka Hachimangu
b2beaaf6481e75385111.paragraphs.0: Ride the Enoden to its Kamakura terminus, exit east, and turn left under the bright red torii into bustling Komachi-dori. Sample tiered-intensity matcha gelato and hot curry bread along the way, and pick up a classic yellow tin of Hato Sabure dove-shaped butter cookies at historic Toshimaya.
b2beaaf6481e75385111.paragraphs.1: Turn right at the far end of Komachi-dori to visit Kamakura's grand guardian shrine, Tsurugaoka Hachimangu. On your walk back to the station, switch to Dankazura—the elevated, cherry-tree-lined central approach down Wakamiya-oji, far wider and calmer than Komachi-dori. Tap straight onto the JR Yokosuka Line at Kamakura Station for a direct 55-minute ride back to Tokyo Station or Shinagawa with zero transfers.
b2beaaf6481e75385111.tip: The post-sunset rush from 17:30 to 18:30 packs northbound trains tight. On weekends, slip over to Kamakura's quiet West Exit (Onari-dori) for ramen or izakaya dinner—board JR after 19:30 and you'll almost certainly score a seat back to Tokyo.
b2beaaf6481e75385111.title: Snack down Komachi-dori for dove cookies, stroll Dankazura to Tsurugaoka Hachimangu, and ride JR home direct

b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.access.0.how: The Tohoku Shinkansen takes about 1 hour 20 minutes or more to Koriyama and about 1.5 hours to Fukushima
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.access.1.how: The JR Ban'etsu West Line takes about 1–1.5 hours to Aizuwakamatsu
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.access.2.how: The Aizu Railway takes about 40–50 minutes to Yunokami Onsen Station, followed by a bus or taxi to Ouchi-juku
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.0.name: Kitakata ramen
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.0.text: One of Japan's three great ramen styles: thick, wide, curly noodles in a clear soy sauce and pork broth, topped with slices of chashu pork. People in Kitakata often eat ramen for breakfast, and many shops open at 7 or 8 a.m.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.0.where: Central Kitakata, about 20 minutes by JR train from Aizuwakamatsu
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.1.name: Negi soba
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.1.text: Ouchi-juku's signature way to eat soba: use a whole green onion instead of chopsticks to lift the noodles, taking a bite of the onion when you like. It is mainly for fun, and the onion is fairly spicy. If you do not want to bite it, use it only to pick up the noodles.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.1.where: Soba restaurants in Ouchi-juku's old houses
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.2.name: Aizu sauce katsudon
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.2.text: A breaded pork cutlet covered in a sweet-savory sauce and served over sliced cabbage and rice. In Aizu, the cutlet is often bigger than the bowl, leaving no room to put the lid on. Portions are generous.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.3.name: Kozuyu
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.3.text: A clear soup made with dried scallops and filled with taro, shiitake mushrooms, konjac, wheat gluten, and other small ingredients. It was traditionally served at festivals. The flavor is light, and it is often served in a special shallow lacquer bowl.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.3.where: Local restaurants in Aizuwakamatsu and ryokan in Higashiyama Onsen
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.4.name: Fukushima peaches
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.foods.4.text: Fukushima is one of Japan's major peach-growing regions. Peaches are in season from July–September and are very juicy and sweet. Orchards in the countryside around Fukushima offer fruit picking, and station fruit shops sell sliced peaches as well.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.intro.0: Fukushima is the Tohoku prefecture closest to Tokyo, with Shinkansen trains reaching Koriyama in about 1.5 hours. Most visitors head west to the Aizu region: Aizuwakamatsu has Tsuruga Castle and the story of the Byakkotai, while Ouchi-juku's thatched-roof houses lie to the south and Kitakata ramen and the Goshikinuma Ponds are to the north.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.intro.1: Fukushima is one of Tohoku's best cherry blossom destinations in spring. Miharu Takizakura and Hanamiyama Park usually bloom around mid-April. In fall and winter, you can ride the Tadami Line through valleys filled with autumn leaves or snow, but there are very few trains, so plan ahead. Restricted areas around the nuclear power plants are along the Pacific coast; regular attractions in Aizu and central Fukushima are open as usual.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.name: Fukushima
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.seasons.note: Miharu Takizakura and Hanamiyama Park bloom around mid-April; Aizu's fall foliage peaks in late October; the Ouchi-juku Snow Festival is in February, and January–February is best for snowy scenery.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.sources.0.title: Tsuruga Castle official website · castle keep
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.sources.1.title: Ouchi-juku Tourism Association
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.sources.2.title: Aizuwakamatsu tourism guide
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.0.name: Tsuruga Castle
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.0.text: Aizu forces held this castle for a month during the Boshin War. The current keep is a reconstruction, with an unusual red-tile roof. Inside is a history museum, and the top floor has views across the city. Around 1,000 cherry trees bloom around the castle in mid-to-late April, while snow on the red roof makes a beautiful winter scene.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.0.tip: Take the “Haikara” loop bus from the stop in front of Aizuwakamatsu Station to Tsurugajo Iriguchi.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.1.name: Ouchi-juku
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.1.text: This Edo-period post town has more than 30 old houses with thatched roofs lining a dirt road. Most now house soba restaurants and souvenir shops. Climb the small hill at the end of the village for a view down the entire street. The snow-covered roofs are especially beautiful in winter, and a lantern-lit Snow Festival is held every February.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.1.tip: Public transportation is inconvenient. A day bus tour or private taxi from Aizuwakamatsu is easier.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.2.name: Goshikinuma Ponds
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.2.text: This chain of small lakes formed after Mount Bandai erupted in 1888. Each pond has a different color, from emerald green to cobalt blue, depending on volcanic minerals in the water, the weather, and the light. The lakeside trail is about 3.6 kilometers and takes a little over an hour on mostly gentle terrain. Late October, when fall foliage contrasts with the blue water, is the best time to visit.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.2.tip: Take a bus from Inawashiro Station; the ride takes about 30 minutes. Snow covers the trail in winter, so wear snowshoes or join a tour.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.3.name: Tadami River First Bridge
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.3.text: This is the classic view of a Tadami Line train crossing a railway bridge over the valley. It is especially atmospheric when mist rises from the river in the morning. Fresh green leaves in spring, fall foliage, and winter snow each create a different scene. The viewpoint is on the opposite hillside and takes just a few minutes to reach. You can also ride the Tadami Line across the bridge.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.3.tip: Only a few Tadami Line trains run each day, so check the crossing times before you go.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.4.name: Iimoriyama & Sazaedo
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.4.text: Iimoriyama is where the young Byakkotai members took their own lives during the Boshin War, and their graves are on the mountain. Sazaedo, a wooden double-helix pagoda on the hillside, has two nonintersecting ramps for going up and down. It is one of a kind in Japan. You can reach it by loop bus from Tsuruga Castle.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.4.tip: The stone steps up the mountain are somewhat steep. A paid moving walkway is available beside them.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.5.name: Miharu Takizakura
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.5.text: This red weeping cherry tree is said to be more than 1,000 years old. Its branches cascade like a waterfall, and it is one of Japan's “Three Great Cherry Trees.” There is only one tree, but the view from beneath it is powerful. It usually blooms in mid-April. During the bloom period, admission is charged and temporary buses run from Miharu Station.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.5.tip: It gets extremely crowded during bloom. Arrive before 7 a.m. to avoid tour groups.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.6.name: Hanamiyama Park
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.6.text: A flower farmer opened this family-owned hillside to the public for free. In early to mid-April, cherry blossoms, forsythia, magnolias, and peach blossoms bloom together in shades of pink, yellow, and white, with the still-snowy Azuma Mountains in the distance. A full loop takes about 1 hour, and several routes of different lengths are available.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.6.tip: Temporary buses run from Fukushima Station during bloom. Private cars cannot drive close to the park.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.7.name: To-no-Hetsuri
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.7.text: River water and wind have carved the cliffs into a row of tower-like rock formations. Cross the suspension bridge to walk through hollows beneath the cliffs. The site is small; 30 minutes is enough, making it easy to combine with Ouchi-juku on the same day. The rocks are most beautiful during the fall foliage season.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.spots.7.tip: From To-no-Hetsuri Station on the Aizu Railway, it is about a 5-minute walk. The suspension bridge sways.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.stay: Stay near Aizuwakamatsu Station or Higashiyama Onsen for easy access to Tsuruga Castle, Ouchi-juku, and Kitakata. During cherry blossom season, stay near Koriyama or Fukushima Station.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.tagline: Samurai castle towns, thatched-roof Ouchi-juku, and snowy views from the Tadami Line
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.tips.0: Whether your licence is valid for driving in Japan depends on the licence and documents you hold; check the official rules. Ouchi-juku and the Goshikinuma Ponds can also be reached by seasonal buses or local day tours.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.tips.1: The Tadami Line and Aizu Railway have infrequent service. Check the schedules in advance; missing one train may mean waiting two or three hours.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.tips.2: Attractions in central Aizuwakamatsu are spread out, so a one-day loop-bus pass is cheaper than paying for individual rides.
b365a2eaf93c6a7ae453.tips.3: Miharu Takizakura and Hanamiyama Park have short bloom periods. Check the bloom forecast a week before your trip and then set your dates.

b3685d34c5f4e994b9e1.s: What to know about Japan in 2026: departure tax rises to ¥3,000, tax-free shopping changes to refunds on departure, and Kyoto and Hokkaido introduce accommodation taxes, with official sources.

b3ff5f6a95a8de505dcb.0: Board a Kyoto city bus toward Eikando or Tofuku-ji at 10:30 AM in late November and you'll mostly see two things: frozen red brake lights outside the window and a wall of heads on Tsutenkyo Bridge. Peak-season Kyoto isn't ruined—it's just that the vast majority of visitors pile into the exact same flagship temples during the five-hour window from 10:00 to 15:00.
b3ff5f6a95a8de505dcb.1: This eastern-to-southern Kyoto route synthesizes real traveler queue reports from recent foliage seasons with official Kyoto Municipal Transportation routing (all photos are AI-generated scene illustrations), built on two iron rules: skip cross-town buses in favor of the Tozai Subway Line, walking, and the JR Nara Line; schedule crowd-sensitive Eikando for its 08:30 opening, retreat to spacious Nanzen-ji for midday yudofu, and time Tofuku-ji or evening illuminations smartly.

b40c2ee48b81ade2a2fc.cost: Staten Island Ferry free; 9/11 outdoor Memorial free (Museum ~$33)
b40c2ee48b81ade2a2fc.location: Whitehall Ferry Terminal → Charging Bull → 9/11 Memorial → Brooklyn Bridge
b40c2ee48b81ade2a2fc.paragraphs.0: Take the 1 train at 09:00 down to South Ferry and board the free Staten Island Ferry, departing every 30 minutes. Claim the right-hand outer deck heading out: the boat glides cleanly past the face of the Statue of Liberty with Lower Manhattan's skyscrapers behind you. Once docked, simply follow the crowd right back to the boarding gates for the free return boat—a 1-hour round trip for zero dollars.
b40c2ee48b81ade2a2fc.paragraphs.1: Back in Lower Manhattan, loop past Trinity Church, the New York Stock Exchange, and Wall Street's Charging Bull (side shots skip the long photo line), then walk 8 minutes to the twin reflecting pools of the 9/11 Memorial Plaza and the dove-winged Oculus transit hub. Around 16:00, step onto the Brooklyn Bridge's wooden pedestrian boardwalk heading east for a 40-minute crossing (stay inside the pedestrian lane, clear of cyclists) as sunset turns Lower Manhattan into a gilded silhouette.
b40c2ee48b81ade2a2fc.phase: Step 03 · Day 3 Lower Manhattan: free Lady Liberty ferry + Wall Street + Brooklyn Bridge walk
b40c2ee48b81ade2a2fc.photo.alt: Empire State Building seen at twilight blue hour from an open-air Midtown observation deck
b40c2ee48b81ade2a2fc.photo.caption: Book an open-air deck slot 1 hour before sunset and watch Manhattan shift from golden daylight into glowing blue hour over 40 unforgettable minutes.
b40c2ee48b81ade2a2fc.tip: If you do want to set foot on Liberty Island or climb the crown, Statue City Cruises is the ONLY official seller, and crown tickets sell out 2–3 months ahead. Ignore sidewalk hawkers in bright vests pushing overpriced 'Statue of Liberty cruise' tickets.
b40c2ee48b81ade2a2fc.title: Catch the free orange ferry past the Statue of Liberty, visit the 9/11 Memorial and Wall Street, and walk the Brooklyn Bridge at dusk

b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.contacts.0.hours: Check the hours published by the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.contacts.0.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department General Consultation Center
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.contacts.0.note: For non-emergency safety and police inquiries, with multilingual support. For an incident or accident in progress, call 110 directly.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.numbers.0.label: Police
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.numbers.0.note: Call for robbery, theft, traffic accidents, or personal threats. The call is free. Give your location first. If you cannot describe it clearly, give the name of a nearby shop, intersection, or address plate on a utility pole.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.numbers.1.label: Fire / ambulance
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.numbers.1.note: Call this number for a fire or an ambulance. The call is free. When connected, first say 「火事です」 (fire) or 「救急です」 (medical emergency), then give the address.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.numbers.2.label: Maritime emergencies
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.numbers.2.note: Call for emergencies at sea or on the coast, or if you see someone drowning. Calls are handled by the Japan Coast Guard.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.numbers.3.label: JNTO Visitor Hotline
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.numbers.3.note: Open 24 hours a day, year-round, with multilingual support. Call if you are sick or injured, or do not know whom to contact during a disaster. From abroad, call +81-50-3816-2787.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.sources.1.title: JNTO Staying Safe in Japan (emergency numbers and Tokyo police multilingual hotline)
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.sources.2.title: Japan Tourism Agency emergency medical guide
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.sources.3.title: Japan Tourism Agency Safety tips app
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.sources.4.title: Japan Coast Guard: Call 118 for maritime incidents and accidents
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.sources.5.title: Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department consultation hotline guide
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.sources.6.title: Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department lost-property reporting process
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.0.items.0: Think back to the last place you used your passport. Ask at the station, shopping center, and hotel front desk. Lost passports are often turned in.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.0.items.1: If you cannot find it, report the loss at the nearest police station or koban and get a 「遺失届」 loss report receipt. You will need it to replace your travel document.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.0.items.2: Contact the embassy or consulate serving your area. Explain that you are a short-term visitor to Japan and need to return home as soon as possible.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.0.items.3: Short-term visitors generally do not receive a replacement passport in Japan. Instead, apply for an emergency travel document to return home. Prepare the application form, passport photos, the police report, and a copy of your identification or passport as required by the embassy or consulate.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.0.items.4: Once your travel document is ready, take it to the airline to change your booking. Before leaving Japan, ask the embassy or consulate whether you also need to complete procedures at an Immigration Services Agency office.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.0.items.5: Photograph your passport information and visa pages and save them on your phone and in the cloud. This can speed up the replacement process.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.0.title: If you lose your passport
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.1.items.0: For an emergency—loss of consciousness, chest pain, heavy bleeding, or difficulty breathing—call 119 for an ambulance, or show someone nearby 「救急車を呼んでください」.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.1.items.1: If you do not know whether you need a hospital or which department to visit, call the JNTO Visitor Hotline at 050-3816-2787 (24 hours, with multilingual support). They can help you find a hospital that treats patients in other languages.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.1.items.2: You can also search for hospitals by area and language on the Japan Tourism Agency's 「身体不適時的應急指南」 emergency medical guide website.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.1.items.3: Bring your passport when seeking medical care. Most clinics accept cash only; larger hospitals may accept cards. If you have travel insurance, call the insurer's assistance line first to ask whether direct billing is available.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.1.items.4: Visitors from abroad generally pay out of pocket for medical care in Japan, and costs can be high. People with unpaid medical bills may be denied entry in the future, so settle the bill before leaving.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.1.items.5: For minor problems, go to a drugstore and describe your symptoms to buy over-the-counter medicine. If you brought medication you regularly take, keep track of its name and dosage.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.1.title: If you get sick or injured
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.2.items.0: Before your trip, install the Japan Tourism Agency's Safety tips app, which offers language options. Earthquake alerts and tsunami warnings are sent directly to your phone.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.2.items.1: When you feel shaking, protect your head and take cover under a sturdy table. Do not rush outside. Watch for falling objects and broken glass.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.2.items.2: On the coast, if you feel strong shaking or receive a tsunami warning, do not wait. Move immediately to higher ground or the upper floors of a reinforced-concrete building. Do not return to the coast until the warning is lifted.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.2.items.3: When you check in, look at the evacuation map on the back of your room door. During a disaster, follow hotel staff and broadcast instructions and go to the designated shelter.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.2.items.4: Keep your phone charged and carry a portable charger. Trains may stop across large areas, so do not try to force your way through.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.2.items.5: Let your family know you are safe. If you need help, call the JNTO hotline or your embassy or consulate.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.2.title: Earthquakes, tsunamis, and typhoons
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.3.items.0: If you left it on a train, bus, or taxi, contact station staff or the operator immediately. Give the time, route, car number, and direction of travel. Japan has a high lost-and-found recovery rate.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.3.items.1: For debit or credit cards, immediately call the issuer to report the loss. Freeze or change the passwords for your mobile payment accounts as well.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.3.items.2: For a phone, contact your carrier to suspend service. On an iPhone, use Find My to lock it.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.3.items.3: Report the loss at any police station or koban, and leave contact information for your stay in Japan, such as your hotel number. Lost property in Tokyo can be searched on the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department website.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.3.items.4: If you need to file an insurance claim, ask the police for a loss or theft report receipt and note the receipt number.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.3.items.5: If it has not been found before you leave Japan, do not worry. Lost property in Tokyo can be collected by someone on your behalf or mailed to an address in Japan for a postage fee. Follow the police department's instructions on where to collect it and what to bring.
b470b20bcb2a7c63f355.steps.3.title: If you lose your wallet, phone, or luggage

b55a3e323989419624af.days.0.items.0.note: Take the Meitetsu train from Chubu Centrair International Airport to Nagoya and drop off your bags
b55a3e323989419624af.days.0.move: The airport to Meitetsu Nagoya takes about 29–38 minutes; Nagoya Castle's Hommaru Palace stops admitting visitors at 4 p.m.
b55a3e323989419624af.days.0.title: Arrive in Nagoya
b55a3e323989419624af.days.1.move: The JR Hida limited express from Nagoya to Takayama takes about 2 hours 30 minutes
b55a3e323989419624af.days.1.title: Take the limited express to Hida-Takayama
b55a3e323989419624af.days.2.items.2.note: Take a bus from Shirakawa-go to Kanazawa in the afternoon, then have dinner near Kanazawa Station
b55a3e323989419624af.days.2.move: The bus from Takayama to Shirakawa-go takes about 50 minutes; Shirakawa-go to Kanazawa takes about 1 hour 30 minutes
b55a3e323989419624af.days.2.title: Morning market, Shirakawa-go and Kanazawa
b55a3e323989419624af.days.3.move: Take buses around the city; Kenroku-en and the museums are about a 5-minute walk apart
b55a3e323989419624af.days.3.title: Kanazawa's famous garden and tea-house districts
b55a3e323989419624af.days.4.items.2.note: Take the train back to Nagoya around noon, then take the Meitetsu train to Chubu Centrair International Airport
b55a3e323989419624af.days.4.move: Take the Shinkansen from Kanazawa to Tsuruga, then transfer to the Shirasagi limited express to Nagoya; about 2.5–3 hours
b55a3e323989419624af.days.4.title: Samurai district, then back to Nagoya
b55a3e323989419624af.for: For a second trip to Japan, with old streets and a thatched-roof village on your list; fly in and out of Nagoya
b55a3e323989419624af.season: April–May and October–November are most comfortable; snowy scenery in January–February
b55a3e323989419624af.summary: Start in Nagoya and make a counterclockwise loop: take the limited express to Hida-Takayama for its old streets, then travel via Shirakawa-go by bus to Kanazawa on day 3. On the way back, transfer at Tsuruga before returning to Nagoya. The Takayama-Hokuriku Area Tourist Pass covers most of the route for eligible travelers; buy a separate ticket for the Tsuruga–Nagoya leg. All buses have reserved seating, so book ahead.
b55a3e323989419624af.title: Nagoya round trip: Takayama, Shirakawa-go and Kanazawa in 5 days

b7ef830b239e187c81c0.access.0.how: The Akita Shinkansen Komachi takes about 3 hours to Kakunodate and as little as 3 hours 40 minutes to Akita
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.access.1.how: The Komachi takes about 35 minutes to Tazawako and about 45 minutes to Kakunodate
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.access.2.how: Take a bus to Nyuto Onsen in about 50 minutes
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.0.name: Kiritanpo hot pot
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.0.text: Freshly harvested rice is mashed, wrapped around cedar skewers, and grilled into kiritanpo. The pieces are simmered in a broth made with Hinai chicken, burdock root, maitake mushrooms, and Japanese parsley. The kiritanpo soaks up the broth and is especially comforting in fall and winter.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.0.where: Local restaurants in Akita City and Kakunodate
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.1.name: Inaniwa udon
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.1.text: These handmade, hand-pulled noodles are much thinner than regular udon and have a smooth surface. They are best served cold, when their silky texture stands out. One of Japan's three great udon varieties, dried noodles make a good souvenir.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.1.where: Akita City and the Inaniwa area of Yuzawa
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.2.name: Hinai chicken
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.2.text: This local Akita breed has firm meat and a rich chicken flavor. It is most often served in oyakodon or as yakitori, and is also used for the broth in kiritanpo hot pot.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.2.where: Around Akita Station and in Odate
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.3.name: Iburigakko
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.3.text: Akita's damp winters make it ideal for hanging daikon above a stove to smoke before pickling it. The result has a smoky flavor and tastes good sliced with sake or cheese.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.foods.3.where: Supermarkets, souvenir shops, and izakaya around the region
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.intro.0: Akita lies on the Sea of Japan side of Tohoku, with heavy snow in winter and cool summers. Most visitors follow the route linking Kakunodate, Lake Tazawa, and Nyuto Onsen. All three are along or near the Akita Shinkansen Komachi line and can be covered in two days.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.intro.1: Kakunodate's samurai residences and weeping cherry trees, along with Nyuto Onsen's open-air baths surrounded by snow, are signature Tohoku scenes. Akita City, the prefectural capital, is known for the Kanto Festival in early August. The Oga Peninsula is home to the Namahage tradition. To see Akita dogs, visit an exhibit in Odate or near Akita Station.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.name: Akita
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.seasons.note: Kakunodate's cherry blossoms bloom in late April, fall colors peak in late October, and the best time for snowy hot springs is January–February. The Kanto Festival takes place August 3–6 every year.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.sources.0.title: Lake Tazawa and Kakunodate Tourism Association
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.sources.1.title: Akita Kanto Festival official website
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.sources.2.title: Wikipedia · Nyuto Onsen
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.0.name: Kakunodate Samurai District
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.0.text: Samurai residences with black wooden walls line this broad historic street. You can visit homes such as the Ishiguro and Aoyagi residences. In late April, weeping cherry trees spill over the walls, while a cherry-blossom tunnel stretches for about 2 km along the Hinokinai River nearby. The fall colors and winter snow scenes are also beautiful.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.0.tip: During cherry-blossom season, arrive before 8 a.m. for the fewest crowds. The walk from Kakunodate Station takes about 20 minutes.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.1.name: Nyuto Onsen
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.1.text: Seven ryokan, each with its own spring source, are scattered through a beech forest. The best known is Tsurunoyu, with thatched roofs and milky outdoor baths surrounded by snow in winter. You can bathe without staying overnight, and a pass lets you visit several baths. The bus from Tazawako Station takes about 50 minutes.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.1.tip: Rooms at Tsurunoyu fill quickly, so book several months ahead for winter. The mixed-gender bathing area has a women-only pool.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.2.name: Lake Tazawa
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.2.text: Japan's deepest lake is more than 400 meters deep. On clear days, its water is deep blue. The golden statue of Tatsuko is the signature photo spot. The loop around the lake is about 20 km. Take a sightseeing bus or boat, then continue into the mountains to Nyuto Onsen.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.2.tip: The bus from Tazawako Station takes about 15 minutes to the lakeshore. The loop bus does not run in winter.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.3.name: Dakigaeri Gorge
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.3.text: This gorge lies between Kakunodate and Lake Tazawa. The river is a milky blue, and the red suspension bridge framed by fall colors is one of the best photo scenes in autumn. The walk to Mikaeri Falls and back takes about 1–1.5 hours. The trail is level and follows the river. The best time to visit is from late October to early November.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.3.tip: Public transportation is inconvenient. Taking a taxi from Kakunodate and back is the most practical option.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.4.name: Senshu Park
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.4.text: The ruins of Kubota Castle are about a 10-minute walk from Akita Station. Cherry blossoms bloom beside the moat in spring, and lotus flowers fill it in summer. The gates and observation tower are reconstructions. If you're short on time, it's an easy walk while waiting for a train in Akita City.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.5.name: Namahage Museum
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.5.text: On New Year's Eve, people on the Oga Peninsula wear demon masks and go door to door frightening lazy people and children. This Namahage tradition is listed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. The museum displays more than 100 masks from different villages. The neighboring Folklore Museum holds live demonstrations, and plenty of visitors get a fright.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.spots.5.tip: Transportation on the Oga Peninsula is limited. From Akita Station, take the JR Oga Line, then transfer to a bus or taxi.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.stay: For a first visit, stay one night near Kakunodate or Tazawako Station, then spend one night at Nyuto Onsen. Akita City is a good base during the Kanto Festival.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.tagline: Home of Kakunodate's samurai district, Nyuto's hidden hot springs, and Namahage
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.tips.0: Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your licence and required documents, so check the official rules. Nyuto Onsen and Lake Tazawa rely on Ugo Kotsu buses; check the schedules in advance.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.tips.1: All Komachi seats are reserved. Book ahead during busy periods, especially in late April during Kakunodate's cherry-blossom season.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.tips.2: The Kanto Festival offers paid viewing seats. Reserve ahead if you want to watch from a seat.
b7ef830b239e187c81c0.tips.3: Snow can be deep around Nyuto Onsen in winter. Bring slip-resistant shoes and gloves.

b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.0.items.1.note: Take an evening stroll by the Esplanade Lagoon, then get an early night
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.0.move: Meet at the wharf around 7–8 a.m. The boat ride takes about 1.5 hours, with a return around 5 p.m.
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.0.title: Cruise to the outer Great Barrier Reef
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.1.move: Take the Skyrail Rainforest Cableway up for about 1.5 hours, including stops, then the Kuranda Scenic Railway down for about 2 hours
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.1.title: Kuranda rainforest
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.2.move: Cairns → Mossman Gorge takes about 75 minutes; cross by ferry, then continue about 45 minutes to Cape Tribulation
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.2.title: Daintree Rainforest drive
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.3.items.0.note: Fly to Gold Coast Airport in the morning, then take a bus or taxi to Surfers Paradise, about 30–40 minutes away
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.3.move: The Cairns → Gold Coast flight takes about 2.5 hours
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.3.title: Fly to the Gold Coast
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.4.items.1.note: Head to Burleigh Head in the evening to see the sunset light up the high-rises
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.4.move: From Surfers Paradise, take a theme park shuttle bus or drive about 20–25 minutes
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.4.title: A day at a theme park
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.5.items.1.note: Take a short ride along the river on a CityCat ferry, then head to the airport in the afternoon
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.5.move: Drive or take the train from the Gold Coast to Brisbane in about 1–1.5 hours
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.days.5.title: Brisbane’s South Bank
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.for: Travelers who want coral reefs, rainforest walks, beaches and theme parks with the kids
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.season: Best during the dry season, May–October
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.summary: Stay in Cairns for 3 nights: spend a day snorkeling on the outer reef, a day taking the cableway and scenic railway to Kuranda, and a day heading north to Mossman Gorge and the Daintree Rainforest. On day four, fly to the Gold Coast and stay in Surfers Paradise for 2 nights. Spend a day at a theme park, then explore Brisbane’s South Bank before flying out.
b7fd1451d6725d0352d1.title: Cairns, the Great Barrier Reef and the Gold Coast · 6 days

bb399a04743e05b03ab5.cover.caption: Morning sunlight floods the turquoise lanes of Bondi Icebergs Pool as Pacific waves spill over the white wall every few seconds—Sydney's most exhilarating wake-up call.
bb399a04743e05b03ab5.excerpt: Getting around Sydney without a car is effortless: tap your phone's Visa or Mastercard straight at the gates, then pack your farthest Blue Mountains train and harbor ferry into Sunday so the whole day caps out under ten Australian dollars. This field-tested 4-day, 3-night itinerary pairs transit hacks with the Bondi-to-Coogee cliff walk and Surry Hills' iconic hotcakes.
