bb96f8843443209232e3.access.0.how: Highway buses cross the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge and Awaji Island. Osaka takes about 2.5 hours and Kobe about 2 hours to Tokushima Station.
bb96f8843443209232e3.access.1.how: The JR Uzushio Limited Express takes a little over 1 hour to Tokushima Station.
bb96f8843443209232e3.access.2.how: Take the JR Nanpu Limited Express to Oboke Station. Okayama takes about 1.5 hours and Kochi about 1 hour.
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.0.name: Tokushima ramen
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.0.text: This ramen has a dark brown pork-bone and soy sauce broth topped with sweet-and-savory pork belly. Many shops let you crack a raw egg into the bowl yourself. The broth is rich and slightly sweet, and locals often eat it with white rice.
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.0.where: Ramen shops around Tokushima Station and throughout the city
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.1.name: Naruto Kintoki sweet potatoes
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.1.text: These sweet potatoes are grown in the sandy soil along the Naruto coast. They have reddish-purple skin, golden flesh, and a sweet, fluffy texture. Roasted sweet potatoes are the simplest way to enjoy them, but they are also used in tarts, fries, and other sweets. They make a popular souvenir.
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.1.where: The souvenir area at Tokushima Station and roadside stations around Naruto
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.2.name: Sudachi
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.2.text: This small green citrus fruit is grown mainly in Tokushima, which produces most of Japan's supply. Its bright acidity works well squeezed over grilled fish, soba, or shochu. Local specialties include sudachi ice cream and sudachi soda. It is freshest in summer and fall.
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.2.where: Tokushima Station, izakayas, and souvenir shops around Tokushima City
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.3.name: Iya soba
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.3.text: This mountain soba from Iya contains little or no wheat flour. The noodles are short, thick, and easy to break, with a strong buckwheat flavor. They are served in a light broth. A bowl at a small shop beside the gorge feels deeply rustic.
bb96f8843443209232e3.foods.3.where: Restaurants around Oboke and Iya Kazurabashi Vine Bridge
bb96f8843443209232e3.intro.0: Tokushima Prefecture lies in eastern Shikoku and is the closest part of Shikoku to Kansai. From Osaka or Kobe, it takes a little over 2 hours by highway bus via the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge and Awaji Island. Naruto in the east is home to world-famous whirlpools and the Otsuka Museum of Art, with its full-size ceramic replicas of famous paintings. Every August, Tokushima City hosts Awa Odori, Japan's largest bon dance festival.
bb96f8843443209232e3.intro.1: The west feels like another world. The Yoshino River carved the Oboke Gorge, while the mountain valleys of Iya have vine bridges and old villages clinging to steep slopes. Public transportation is limited, but the scenery here is some of the wildest in Shikoku. Consider stopping for a night while traveling on the JR Limited Express Nanpu.
bb96f8843443209232e3.name: Tokushima
bb96f8843443209232e3.seasons.note: The whirlpools are largest during the spring and fall spring tides. Hotels in Tokushima City fill up during Awa Odori on August 12–15. Iya is best for fall foliage.
bb96f8843443209232e3.sources.0.title: Uzu no Michi official website: tickets and closures
bb96f8843443209232e3.sources.1.title: Otsuka Museum of Art: visitor information
bb96f8843443209232e3.sources.2.title: Wikipedia: Iya Kazurabashi Vine Bridge
bb96f8843443209232e3.sources.3.title: Wikipedia: Awa Odori
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.0.name: Naruto Whirlpools
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.0.text: The Naruto Strait has a large tidal range and fast currents. At high and low tide, the water forms whirlpools up to 20 meters across. The most thrilling option is a sightseeing boat that takes you right beside them. You can also look down from the glass walkway under the Onaruto Bridge, about 45 meters above the water. Everything depends on the tide schedule.
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.0.tip: Check the official tide table for the listed best viewing times, and visit about 1 hour before or after. The whirlpools are largest during the spring and fall spring tides.
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.1.name: Otsuka Museum of Art
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.1.text: The museum displays more than 1,000 full-size ceramic replicas of Western masterpieces, from ancient frescoes to Picasso. The entire ceiling of the Sistine Chapel has also been reproduced. You can touch and photograph the ceramic panels, making this a good stop with children. The museum is huge, with about 4 kilometers of walking, so allow at least half a day.
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.1.tip: Closed Mondays (if Monday is a holiday, closed the following day). Online tickets are slightly cheaper than tickets bought at the museum.
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.2.name: Iya Kazurabashi Vine Bridge
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.2.text: This suspension bridge is woven from hardy kiwi vines gathered in the mountains. It is about 45 meters long and 14 meters above the water. The gaps between the wooden planks are wide, and the bridge sways as you cross. It is one of Japan's three unusual bridges. The vines are rewoven every three years, and the bridge is one-way. From JR Oboke Station, it takes about 20 minutes by bus.
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.2.tip: If you are afraid of heights, you can simply view it from the side. The planks are slippery in the rain, so wear shoes with good traction.
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.3.name: Oboke Gorge
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.3.text: The Yoshino River cut through the mountains of Shikoku to form this gorge. The banks are made of schist carved into patterns by the water, and the river is emerald green. The easiest way to see it is on a sightseeing boat ride of about 30 minutes, with the boatman providing commentary as he rows. For more excitement, try summer white-water rafting. This is one of Japan's best-known rafting stretches.
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.4.name: Ochiai Village
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.4.text: This mountain village in Higashi-Iya has old houses, stone walls, and rice terraces climbing steep slopes from the valley floor. With its dramatic elevation change, it has been designated a Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings. The best view is from the observation deck on the opposite slope. It is especially beautiful in the morning mist and during fall foliage season. Buses are infrequent, so most visitors drive or hire a car and driver.
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.5.name: Awa Odori Kaikan & Mt. Bizan
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.5.text: You can see Awa Odori even outside August. Professional dance groups perform daily at the hall and invite audience members onstage for the finale. It is lively and fun. You can also take the cable car from the same building up Mt. Bizan. The summit overlooks Tokushima City and the Kii Channel, with good sunset and night views in clear weather. It is about a 10-minute walk from Tokushima Station.
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.6.name: Wakimachi Udatsu Street
bb96f8843443209232e3.spots.6.text: This former merchant district grew wealthy through indigo dyeing. The old houses have firewalls called udatsu at both ends of their roofs. Only wealthy families could afford them, and the Japanese expression meaning “can't raise the udatsu” means “can't get ahead.” The street is short, making it a good 1-hour stop on the way to Iya. You can also see Awa indigo dyeing.
bb96f8843443209232e3.stay: Stay near Tokushima Station in the east for easy trips to Naruto and Awa Odori. In the west, choose a hot-spring inn in Oboke or Iya, where gorge views are right outside your window.
bb96f8843443209232e3.tagline: Naruto Whirlpools, Awa Odori, and vine bridges in the mountains
bb96f8843443209232e3.tips.0: The Naruto Whirlpools depend entirely on the tides. Without checking the tide table, you may see only calm water.
bb96f8843443209232e3.tips.1: Hotels in Tokushima City are nearly full during Awa Odori. You can stay in Takamatsu or Naruto instead, but book 2–3 months ahead.
bb96f8843443209232e3.tips.2: Buses around Iya are infrequent. Write down the departure times for both directions before you go. If that does not work, join a guided tour.
bb96f8843443209232e3.tips.3: The Shikoku Rail Pass covers JR Limited Express trains to Oboke, but not highway buses.

bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.access.0.how: About 45 minutes to Atami and 1 hour–1 hour 20 minutes to Shizuoka by Tokaido Shinkansen
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.access.1.how: About 1 hour to Shizuoka and 30 minutes to Hamamatsu by Tokaido Shinkansen
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.access.2.how: About 35 minutes to Shuzenji by the Izu-Hakone Railway
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.access.3.how: Buses run to Shizuoka Station. International flight schedules change often, so check the official website before departure.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.0.name: Shizuoka oden
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.0.text: The broth is a dark soy-based soup made with beef tendon. Ingredients are served on bamboo skewers and finished with aonori and dried fish powder. Be sure to try the black mackerel fish cake called kuro hanpen.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.0.where: Oden shops around Aoba Yokocho near Shizuoka Station
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.1.name: Hamamatsu eel rice
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.1.text: Lake Hamana is considered the birthplace of eel farming in Japan. The Kanto style steams the eel before grilling it, making the meat tender. The Kansai style grills it without steaming, giving the skin a crisper texture. Ask the restaurant which style it serves when ordering.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.1.where: Eel restaurants around Hamamatsu Station and Lake Hamana
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.2.name: Sakura shrimp
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.2.text: These tiny pink shrimp are commercially caught only in Suruga Bay, with fishing seasons in spring and autumn. They are sweet raw and even better fried into kakiage fritters. Dried shrimp also make a good souvenir.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.2.where: Fishermen's restaurants around Yui and Kanbara in Shimizu Ward, Shizuoka City
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.3.name: Shizuoka green tea
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.3.text: Shizuoka produces more tea than any other prefecture in Japan. The most common style is fukamushi-cha, steamed longer to produce a deep green color. New tea arrives in April–May, and you will find tea farm visits, matcha desserts, and tea souvenirs throughout the region.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.foods.3.where: Tea shops around Shizuoka Station, the Makinohara Plateau, and Nihondaira
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.intro.0: Shizuoka lies south of Mount Fuji, with Yamanashi on the other side of the mountain. This side offers wider views: Miho no Matsubara brings Mount Fuji, the sea, and pine trees into one scene, while Nihondaira overlooks Suruga Bay. Fujinomiya is home to the head shrine of Japan's Sengen shrines, and in summer you can climb Mount Fuji from the Fujinomiya Trail. The Tokaido Shinkansen runs through the prefecture, taking about 1 hour from either Tokyo or Nagoya.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.intro.1: The Izu Peninsula in the east is where Tokyo residents go for weekend hot-spring trips. Atami is the closest to Tokyo, Shuzenji has a bamboo grove, and Kawazu's early cherry blossoms open in February. Shizuoka is also Japan's largest tea-producing region. Its green tea, Shizuoka oden, and Hamamatsu eel are all worth trying. The prefecture stretches a long way from east to west, so plan the Mount Fuji area and Izu as separate trips.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.name: Shizuoka
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.seasons.note: Mount Fuji is clearest from November–February; Kawazu cherry blossoms bloom in February; new tea arrives in April–May; summers are often cloudy, but you can climb Mount Fuji from July–September.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.sources.0.title: Official Mt. Fuji Climbing Site: Regulations on the Shizuoka Prefecture side
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.sources.1.title: Official Mt. Fuji Climbing Site: Climbing season
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.sources.2.title: JR Mt. Fuji–Shizuoka Area Tourist Pass Mini
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.0.name: Miho no Matsubara
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.0.text: A seaside pine grove stretching about 7 km, with views of Mount Fuji across Suruga Bay. It has appeared in ukiyo-e prints and waka poetry since ancient times. In 2013, it was registered as a component of the Mount Fuji World Heritage Site. Walk from the pine grove's Kami no Michi wooden path to the shore, then visit the nearby museum to learn about the Hagoromo legend. About 25 minutes by bus from Shimizu Station.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.0.tip: Winter mornings offer the best chance of seeing Mount Fuji with a snow-covered summit. The coast is windy, so bring a windbreaker.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.1.name: Nihondaira Yume Terrace
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.1.text: An observation facility at the summit of Nihondaira in Shizuoka City, designed by Kengo Kuma. A wooden lattice wraps around the octagonal building and its surrounding gallery, with views of Mount Fuji, Suruga Bay, and Shimizu Port. You can take the ropeway down to Kunozan Toshogu, the original burial place of Tokugawa Ieyasu. About 40 minutes by bus from Shizuoka Station.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.1.tip: The views are beautiful at sunset and at night, but the last bus runs relatively early. Check the schedule before you go.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.2.name: Fujisan Hongu Sengen Taisha
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.2.text: The head shrine of more than 1,000 Sengen shrines across Japan, dedicated to the deity of Mount Fuji. Everything above the eighth station of Mount Fuji legally belongs to the shrine. The main hall is an unusual two-story structure. The Wakutama Pond on the grounds is fed by a spring of snowmelt from Mount Fuji, clear enough to see the bottom. About a 10-minute walk from JR Fujinomiya Station.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.2.tip: Omiya Yokocho in front of the shrine serves Fujinomiya yakisoba, making it a convenient lunch stop.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.3.name: Shiraito Falls
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.3.text: Snowmelt from Mount Fuji seeps through cracks in the rock to form a curved curtain of water about 150 meters wide, like countless white threads hanging over the moss. It is also part of the Mount Fuji World Heritage Site. Nearby Otodome Falls has a much heavier flow. About 30 minutes by bus from Fujinomiya Station. Pair it with Sengen Taisha for a half-day outing.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.3.tip: The trail has steps and is slippery after rain. It is considerably cooler here than in the city in summer.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.4.name: Mt. Fuji Fujinomiya Trail
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.4.text: Starting at the Fujinomiya 5th Station, about 2,400 meters above sea level, this is the highest and shortest of the four trails to the summit, but it is also steeper. In summer, buses run to the 5th Station from Mishima and Shin-Fuji stations on the Shinkansen. The 2026 climbing season runs from July 10 to September 10. A mountain hut reservation is required to enter between 2 p.m. and 3 a.m.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.4.tip: Register in the Shizuoka Prefecture FUJI NAVI app, complete the learning test, and pay the fee first. Private cars are restricted on the road to the 5th Station in summer.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.5.name: Shuzenji Onsen
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.5.text: One of Izu's oldest hot-spring resorts, said to have been founded by Kukai. The hot-spring town follows the Katsura River. Tokko no Yu, in the middle of the river, is its landmark, and the nearby bamboo grove is a popular photo spot. Shuzenji Temple stands at the center of town. The area is busiest when the maples turn red in late November. From Mishima, take the Izu-Hakone Railway to Shuzenji Station, then a bus for about 10 minutes.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.5.tip: The bamboo grove is lit up in the evening, when it is quiet and less crowded. The town has free foot baths.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.6.name: Kawazu Cherry Blossoms
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.6.text: Kawazu cherry trees bloom early and have deeper-colored flowers than Somei Yoshino trees. They usually bloom from early February to early March. From Izu-Kyuko Kawazu Station, follow the Kawazu River. Cherry trees line both banks for several kilometers, with fields of yellow rapeseed flowers below. You can see the blossoms more than a month earlier than in Tokyo, making this a good choice for a late-winter or early-spring trip.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.6.tip: Weekend traffic is severe during the cherry blossom festival, so take the train. The Izu-Kyuko Line and the Odoriko limited express run from Atami and Ito.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.7.name: Atami Onsen
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.7.text: A seaside hot-spring town less than 1 hour from Tokyo by Shinkansen. The shopping street in front of the station sells dried fish and onsen manju. Walk downhill to the beach and seaside promenade. Many hotels have rooms facing Sagami Bay. Fireworks are held over the water many times a year, with the most events in summer. It is ideal for a relaxing overnight trip from Tokyo.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.spots.7.tip: Atami is built on a slope. The route from the station to the coast is downhill, so take a bus or taxi back to save energy.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.stay: For Mount Fuji and Miho no Matsubara, stay near Shizuoka Station or Fujinomiya, both convenient for trains and buses. For hot springs, stay in Atami or Shuzenji. Atami is closest to Tokyo, while Shuzenji is quieter.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.tagline: South of Mount Fuji, with Izu hot springs and tea-covered hills
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.tips.0: The Nozomi on the Tokaido Shinkansen does not stop at stations in Shizuoka Prefecture. Take the Hikari or Kodama instead.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.tips.1: Visitors can buy the Mt. Fuji–Shizuoka Area Tourist Pass Mini. It is valid for 3 days and covers JR local trains and many buses in the prefecture, but not the Shinkansen.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.tips.2: Mount Fuji is often hidden by clouds. Winter mornings offer the best chance of seeing it, while clouds usually build in the evening.
bc04d4ceda5942abd09f.tips.3: Check whether your licence is valid for driving in Japan before renting a car. In Izu, you can rely on the Izu-Kyuko Line, Izu-Hakone Railway, and buses.

bc19f00673d16b7b6c93.0: [OMNY fare-cap trick] Tap Apple Pay or Google Pay straight at the turnstile at $3.00 per ride. Once the same card and device hit roughly $35 (12 rides) within 7 days, every additional subway and local bus ride in that cycle is automatically free. Never alternate between your phone and the physical card, or your count resets.
bc19f00673d16b7b6c93.1: [Pick two of the five decks at most] Want open-air glass-free views framing both the Empire State Building and Central Park? Choose Top of the Rock. Want futuristic mirrored art shots? Choose SUMMIT One Vanderbilt. Skip buying all five—it drains your wallet and triggers skyline fatigue.
bc19f00673d16b7b6c93.2: [See Lady Liberty for free] Unless climbing into the crown is a must, head to South Ferry for the free, 24-hour orange Staten Island Ferry. Stand on the right-hand outdoor deck for close-up views of the Statue of Liberty and Lower Manhattan skyline—saving dozens of dollars and half a day in queues.
bc19f00673d16b7b6c93.3: [Street-smart basics] Always wait for trains away from the yellow platform edge with your back to a pillar; in Times Square, walk briskly past costumed characters pushing photos or strangers handing out 'free CDs' without making eye contact.

bca70276a24c9ec6caab.s: Offline: Pages you open are saved on your phone and work without a signal. In your browser, choose “Add to Home Screen” to use it like an app.

bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.access.0.how: The Keisei Skyliner takes a little over 40 minutes to Nippori and Ueno and costs about ¥2,470. The Access Express goes directly to Asakusa for about ¥1,290. It's slower but cheaper.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.access.1.how: JR N'EX has reserved seats throughout. It takes about 1 hour to Tokyo Station and costs about ¥3,140, or about ¥3,330 to Shinjuku. Depending on your passport, you may be able to buy a round-trip ticket for about ¥5,200.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.access.2.how: The Keikyu Line takes about 15 minutes to Shinagawa and costs about ¥330. The Tokyo Monorail takes about 15 minutes to Hamamatsucho and costs about ¥520, where you can transfer to the JR Yamanote Line.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.access.3.how: The Tokaido Shinkansen Nozomi takes about 2 hours 15 minutes from Kyoto to Tokyo Station and about 2 and a half hours from Shin-Osaka. Reserve a seat with oversized-baggage space if you're carrying a large suitcase.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.foods.0.name: Edomae sushi
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.foods.0.text: Tokyo-style nigiri sushi, made with fish treated with salt, vinegar, or sauce before being placed on vinegared rice. Tsukiji and Ginza have everything from conveyor-belt sushi to high-end sushi counters. For a first taste, try a seafood rice bowl or sushi set in Tsukiji, then splurge on a meal in Ginza if your budget allows.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.foods.0.where: Tsukiji Outer Market, Ginza, Toyosu Market
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.foods.1.name: Monjayaki
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.foods.1.text: Chopped cabbage and other ingredients are arranged in a ring on a hot griddle, then covered with a thin batter. Use a small spatula to scrape up bites as they cook. The texture is soft and gooey with crisp, browned edges. It may not look fancy, but it's a classic downtown Tokyo comfort food, and staff usually demonstrate it for first-time diners.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.foods.1.where: Tsukishima Monjayaki Street (Tsukishima Station, close to Tsukiji)
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.foods.2.name: Tokyo-style shoyu ramen
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.foods.2.text: Tokyo ramen is built around a clear chicken-and-soy broth with thin, curly noodles, making it lighter than Kyushu tonkotsu ramen. You'll find it throughout station areas and underground malls. Most shops use ticket vending machines at the entrance. Just follow the pictures and press the buttons—even without Japanese, you can order easily.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.foods.2.where: Tokyo Ramen Street, Shinjuku, and around Ogikubo
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.foods.3.name: Tendon
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.foods.3.text: A signature dish at old Asakusa restaurants, with shrimp and vegetables over white rice and topped with a sweet, rich sauce. It's especially satisfying after visiting Sensō-ji. Lines outside long-established restaurants are common, but avoiding the noon rush makes things much easier.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.intro.0: Tokyo isn't one attraction but a huge city made up of dozens of neighborhoods: Asakusa and Ueno show off old Tokyo; Shinjuku and Shibuya handle shopping and nightlife; Ginza and Tsukiji are known for fine food; and Odaiba has waterfront views and city lights. The neighborhoods are linked by subways and JR lines, and most trips take just 20–30 minutes. Planning by neighborhood and focusing on one or two areas a day is much easier than crisscrossing the city.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.intro.1: Allow 4–5 days for a relaxed first visit: spend one day in Asakusa and at Tokyo Skytree, one day in Ueno, Tsukiji, and Ginza, one day in Harajuku, Shibuya, and Odaiba, and half a day at Mount Takao. Tokyo works for any budget. Convenience-store breakfasts, station ramen, and department-store food halls can all be good. The main challenge is navigating large, crowded stations, so install a transit app ahead of time and avoid dragging luggage onto trains during rush hour.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.name: Tokyo
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.seasons.note: Cherry blossoms are best from late March to early April, while ginkgo and fall foliage peak from late November to early December. July–August is hot and muggy, and crowds are heaviest during Golden Week and around New Year's.
