bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.0.name: Sensō-ji
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.0.text: Tokyo's oldest temple. Enter through Kaminarimon Gate and follow Nakamise Shopping Street, lined with ningyoyaki cakes, senbei, and souvenirs. The main hall and five-story pagoda are at the end. Admission is free. The old streets around Asakusa are perfect for a slow stroll, and Tokyo Skytree stands across the Sumida River, making the two sights a good half-day outing.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.0.tip: It's packed during the day. Go before 8 a.m. or after the lights come on at night for a quieter visit and shorter lines at Kaminarimon.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.1.name: Tokyo Skytree
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.1.text: This 634-meter broadcasting tower offers sweeping views of Tokyo from its 350-meter Tembo Deck. On a clear day, you may see Mount Fuji to the west. Ticket prices vary by date. The official website is the cheapest place to buy them, while the onsite counter charges about ¥500 more per ticket. The large shopping complex below has plenty of anime stores, so it's also a good rainy-day stop.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.1.tip: For views of Mount Fuji, choose a clear winter morning. For city lights, book a time slot 30 minutes before sunset.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.2.name: Ueno Park
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.2.text: One of Tokyo's liveliest cherry-blossom parks. In spring, rows of cherry trees line the main paths, with picnickers filling the ground beneath them. The park is also home to the Tokyo National Museum, the National Museum of Western Art, and Ueno Zoo, so there are places to go even when it rains. Ameyoko Shopping Street is a few minutes outside the park, with dried goods, snacks, and inexpensive seafood.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.2.tip: Most museums are closed on Mondays, so check before you go. During cherry-blossom season, people claim picnic spots early even on weekends.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.3.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.3.text: After the wholesale market moved to Toyosu, Tsukiji was left with an outer market made up of hundreds of small shops selling tamagoyaki, seafood rice bowls, grilled scallops, kitchen knives, and dried goods. It's busiest from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. After eating, walk along Harumi-dori for about 10 minutes to Ginza. Spend the afternoon at department stores and flagship shops for an easy one-way itinerary.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.3.tip: Many shops close on Sundays, public holidays, and some Wednesdays. Bring cash. Eat purchases in the shop or in designated areas rather than while walking.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.4.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.4.text: A large garden beside Shinjuku's shopping district, with Japanese, English, and French-style gardens. It has many cherry varieties and a long blossom season, while the ginkgo trees and fall foliage are beautiful in autumn. The broad lawns are ideal for taking a break with a bento. It's a good place to escape the crowds after exploring Shinjuku, and it's a few minutes' walk from Shinjuku-gyoemmae Station.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.4.tip: Closed on Mondays, with closures moved to the next day when Monday is a public holiday. Alcohol is prohibited, including during cherry-blossom season.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.5.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatory
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.5.text: This twin-tower government complex was designed by Kenzo Tange. The observatories on the 45th floor, about 202 meters up, are free and offer views of Shinjuku's skyscrapers and Tokyo Skytree in the distance. On clear days, Mount Fuji is visible to the west. No ticket or reservation is needed—just pass through security. It's a good choice for travelers on a tight budget who still want a night view.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.5.tip: The north and south observatories close on different schedules and take turns closing for maintenance, so check the official website before you go.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.6.name: Meiji Jingu
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.6.text: The approach starts just outside Harajuku Station. Once you enter, towering trees block out the city noise. The shrine is dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken, and traditional wedding processions are common on weekends. After paying your respects, browse Takeshita Street and Omotesando in Harajuku, both packed with streetwear brands and dessert shops. Shibuya is about a 20-minute walk farther south.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.6.tip: The shrine opens at sunrise and closes at sunset, so watch the time if you visit late in the day. The first three days of the new year are extremely crowded.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.7.fee: Free at the crossing; SHIBUYA SKY requires a separate ticket
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.7.name: Shibuya Scramble Crossing
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.7.text: Thousands of people cross at once when the light turns green, making this Tokyo's most famous street scene. The statue of Hachiko outside the station is a popular meeting point. For a view from above, head to SHIBUYA SKY on the roof of Shibuya Scramble Square. Its open-air observation deck has wide-ranging views. Shibuya is also great for clothes shopping, record stores, and late-night food.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.7.tip: SHIBUYA SKY uses timed tickets booked through its official website. Slots around sunset often sell out several days ahead. The rooftop closes in strong winds or heavy rain.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.8.name: Odaiba
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.8.text: An artificial island in Tokyo Bay, reached by the driverless Yurikamome Line across Rainbow Bridge. Odaiba Seaside Park faces Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Tower and has beautiful night views. Large shopping centers and a life-size Gundam statue are nearby. teamLab Planets is next door in Toyosu and can be visited the same day. Come in the late afternoon, see the lights, and then return to central Tokyo.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.8.tip: For the return trip, you can take the Rinkai Line. Some trains run directly to Shibuya and Shinjuku and are faster than the Yurikamome Line.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.9.fee: About ¥490 one way by cable car
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.9.name: Mount Takao
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.9.text: About 50 minutes from Shinjuku on the Keio Line and about ¥430 to the foot of the mountain, Mount Takao is a favorite weekend escape for Tokyo residents. Trail 1 takes about 1 and a half hours to reach the 599-meter summit. The cable car cuts the effort in half. On clear days, you can see Mount Fuji from the top. Fall colors are best from late November to early December, and the tororo soba along the trail is worth trying.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.spots.9.tip: Cable-car lines are very long on fall-color weekends, so try to go on a weekday or arrive before 8 a.m. Sneakers are enough.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.stay: For a first visit, stay in Shinjuku, Ueno, or Asakusa. Shinjuku has connections in every direction and stays lively at night; Ueno has direct Skyliner service to Narita; and Asakusa offers good-value hotels. If you're mainly using Haneda, stay around Shinagawa or Ginza.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.tagline: The easiest base for a first Japan trip—you won't run out of things to do in a week
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.tips.0: Suica and PASMO transit cards work on nearly all trains and buses. On an iPhone, you can add a Suica directly in Apple Wallet.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.tips.1: Tokyo Subway Tickets cost about ¥1,000/1,500/2,000 for 24/48/72 hours. They cover subways only, not the JR Yamanote Line.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.tips.2: The cheapest way into the city from Narita is the TYO-NRT bus to Tokyo Station, which costs about ¥1,500. Fares double on late-night services.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.tips.3: The morning commute peaks from 7:30 to 9:30. Avoid boarding with a rolling suitcase; take an airport bus instead or travel outside those hours.
bcd9d579478eddfe2bb5.tips.4: Public trash cans are scarce. Throw away convenience-store purchases outside the store or take them back to your hotel.

beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.0.move: Take the subway from the domestic terminal or the bus from the international terminal to Hakata; use the subway around the city
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.0.title: Arrive in Fukuoka and explore the city
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.1.move: Use the Nishitetsu lines all day; consider the Dazaifu–Yanagawa sightseeing pass
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.1.title: Dazaifu and Yanagawa
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.2.items.0.note: Take the Yufuin no Mori in the morning. The trip takes about 2 hours 15 minutes, so reserve seats in advance
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.2.items.3.note: Return to the inn in the evening for a hot-spring bath and a kaiseki dinner
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.2.move: Take the Yufuin no Mori limited express from Hakata to Yufuin
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.2.title: Take the Yufuin no Mori to Yufuin
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.3.items.0.note: Go to Kinrin Lake early to see the morning mist. It is most visible in fall and winter
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.3.move: Take a highway bus from Yufuin to Beppu, about 1 hour; use buses around the city
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.3.title: Beppu's Hells and hell-steamed food
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.4.items.3.note: If you have an extra day, join a day trip to Mount Aso
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.4.move: Take the Sonic limited express from Beppu to Hakata, then change to the Kyushu Shinkansen to Kumamoto. The trip takes about 3 hours
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.4.title: Take a sand bath, then head to Kumamoto
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.5.items.2.note: The Shinkansen takes about 35 minutes back to Hakata; take the subway to Fukuoka Airport
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.5.move: Take the Kyushu Shinkansen from Kumamoto to Hakata, then continue to the airport
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.days.5.title: See Kumamoto Castle, then head home
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.for: First-time visitors to Kyushu who want hot springs and city sightseeing
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.season: Fall and winter are best, but spring is also nice
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.summary: Fly in and out of Fukuoka. Spend the first two days eating in the city, then take a sightseeing train to Yufuin for one night at a traditional inn. The next day, see Beppu's Hells and try hell-steamed food. Finish with a limited express and the Shinkansen to Kumamoto Castle. No rental car is needed: trains connect all the cities, and a North Kyushu Rail Pass should cover most of the trip.
beb532cf5bad33c8e9d8.title: 6 days of Kyushu hot springs · Fukuoka, Yufuin, Beppu and Kumamoto

bf0b402daecec4a02236.audience: First-time NYC travelers / architecture & art enthusiasts
bf0b402daecec4a02236.budget: ~CNY 8,500 per person (excluding international flights; hotels take the biggest bite)

bf4a0532285052ca2cbe.location: JR Sapporo → Asari / Otaru Station → Otaru Canal & Sakaimachi Street
bf4a0532285052ca2cbe.paragraphs.0: Catch a 09:00 JR Hakodate Main Line train from Sapporo toward Otaru and sit on the right-hand side! Passing Zenibako and coastal Asari Station, the rails skim within ten meters of wintry white-capped waves and snowy bluffs. Get off one stop early at Minami-Otaru to walk gently downhill through the entire Sakaimachi shopping strip—Music Box Museum, Kitakaro cream puffs, Rokkatei, and LeTAO double fromage—without backtracking.
bf4a0532285052ca2cbe.paragraphs.1: Break for lunch at Sankaku Market or Sushi Street over sweet shrimp, scallops, and Hokkaido sea urchin. Time your arrival at Otaru Canal's Asakusabashi Bridge or quieter North Canal by 15:45: just past 16:00 the vintage gas lamps glow against deep twilight blue. Then walk 10 minutes to JR Otaru Station and ride back to Sapporo before deep-freeze night hits.
bf4a0532285052ca2cbe.phase: Step 02 · Day 2 Sapporo ⇄ Otaru Snow Day Trip
bf4a0532285052ca2cbe.photo.alt: Snow-covered Odori Park winter lights in Sapporo, Hokkaido
bf4a0532285052ca2cbe.photo.caption: Starting from snow-draped Odori Park in Sapporo, the 40-minute west-bound JR ride whisks you straight to Otaru Canal and the wintry Sea of Japan.
bf4a0532285052ca2cbe.tip: Otaru sidewalks thaw slightly at noon and refreeze into invisible 'black ice' by dusk! Walk like a local penguin: lean slightly forward, take short steps, land flat-footed, and keep your hands out of your pockets for balance.
bf4a0532285052ca2cbe.title: Take the Sea-Side JR to Otaru, Stroll Sakaimachi Sweets at 14:00 & Catch 16:00 Canal Lamps

c0c4e16a482f7dbee4f5.audience: Travelers without an IDP / budget-minded winter-sun seekers
c0c4e16a482f7dbee4f5.budget: About CNY 4,200 per person (lodging, whale tour, buses & food)

c0d895f3cce8cb1ff421.s: If you're traveling with kids, plan one main activity each day and take the rest as it comes.

c189b7520037918332b1.access.0.how: From Hakata, it's about 40 minutes by limited express to Saga Station and about 1 hour to Takeo Onsen. Karatsu is reached by a direct subway-to-JR Chikuhi Line train and takes a little over 1 hour.
c189b7520037918332b1.access.1.how: The Nishi Kyushu Shinkansen takes about 30 minutes to Ureshino Onsen and Takeo Onsen.
c189b7520037918332b1.access.2.how: The airport has domestic flights and some international flights. Take an airport bus to Saga Station, then transfer to JR trains for other destinations.
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.0.name: Yobuko live squid
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.0.text: Live squid is sliced into translucent sashimi to order, with the tentacles still moving when it's served. The texture is crisp and slightly sweet. Any leftovers can be prepared as tempura or grilled with salt.
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.0.where: Seafood restaurants around Yobuko Port; also available in central Karatsu
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.1.name: Saga beef
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.1.text: Premium wagyu from Saga Prefecture, known for its fine marbling. Common preparations include teppanyaki, sukiyaki, and steak. Lunch sets are much cheaper than dinner, so go at midday for a taste.
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.1.where: Wagyu restaurants in central Saga, Takeo, Ureshino, and Karatsu
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.2.name: Hot-spring tofu
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.2.text: Tofu simmered in Ureshino hot-spring water. As it cooks, the edges dissolve and the broth turns milky white. The texture is especially soft. It's delicious with sesame sauce or ponzu.
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.2.where: Restaurants and ryokan in the Ureshino Onsen district
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.3.name: Sicilian rice
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.3.text: A casual local dish from Saga City: white rice topped with stir-fried meat, lettuce, and tomatoes, then drizzled with mayonnaise. The name has nothing to do with Italy. It's home-style, inexpensive, and filling.
c189b7520037918332b1.foods.3.where: Cafes and casual eateries around Saga Station
c189b7520037918332b1.intro.0: Saga is often treated as a stop on the way from Fukuoka to Nagasaki, but it also makes an easy day trip from Fukuoka. Takeo and Ureshino in the west are known for their hot springs. Arita and Imari are the birthplace of Japanese porcelain. Along the northern coast, Karatsu and Yobuko serve transparent live squid.
c189b7520037918332b1.intro.1: Saga gets far fewer visitors than Fukuoka and moves at a slower pace. It's a good choice for a second Kyushu trip or anyone looking to avoid crowds. Sights are spread out, so choose one route: hot springs and ceramics in the west, castles and seafood in the north, or Yoshinogari Historical Park near Saga Station.
c189b7520037918332b1.name: Saga
c189b7520037918332b1.seasons.note: The Arita Ceramic Fair runs from late April to early May. Mifuneyama Rakuen is beautiful in spring for its azaleas and in fall for its leaves. The Karatsu Kunchi Festival takes place in early November.
c189b7520037918332b1.sources.0.title: Yoshinogari Historical Park visitor information
c189b7520037918332b1.sources.1.title: Yoshinogari Historical Park access
c189b7520037918332b1.sources.2.title: Mifuneyama Rakuen official website
c189b7520037918332b1.sources.3.title: JR Kyushu Rail Pass official information
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.0.name: Mifuneyama Rakuen
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.0.text: A large garden built against a steep mountain. In spring, azaleas and cherry blossoms cover the slopes. In fall, leaves are reflected in the ponds, and evening light displays take place. It's in the same small city as Takeo Onsen, making it easy to combine a soak with a garden visit in one day.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.0.tip: It's about 5 minutes by taxi from Takeo Onsen Station. The evening illumination draws crowds in fall, so enter before dusk for a more relaxed visit.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.1.name: Takeo Onsen Romon Gate
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.1.text: This vermilion gate was designed by Kingo Tatsuno, the architect of Tokyo Station. Behind it are public baths where you can soak in a thousand-year-old hot spring for a modest fee. Nearby Takeo City Library has a trendy bookstore-like design and is worth a look if you enjoy architecture.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.1.tip: It's about a 15-minute walk from Takeo Onsen Station. Bring your own towel for the public baths, or buy one at the front desk.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.2.name: Ureshino Onsen
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.2.text: This hot-spring town is known for leaving your skin feeling smooth. Its slightly viscous water is said to be a beauty treatment. The town has a public bath and free foot baths. You can also try tofu simmered in hot-spring water and locally grown Ureshino tea. It's ideal for staying one night and doing nothing at all.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.2.tip: Nishi Kyushu Shinkansen's Ureshino Onsen Station is some distance from the hot-spring district. Take a bus or taxi.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.3.name: Arita ceramic district
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.3.text: Arita is where Japan first produced porcelain. The main street is lined with ceramic shops and kiln studios, while back alleys reveal old walls built from discarded kiln bricks. It's quiet outside the festival season and a good place to take your time choosing tableware. The Ceramic Fair from late April to early May fills the streets with shoppers.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.3.tip: Ceramics break easily. Ask the shop to pack large items or ship them directly to your hotel. If checking them as luggage, wrap them in clothing.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.4.name: Yoshinogari Historical Park
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.4.text: Japan's largest Yayoi-period moated settlement site. Reconstructed watchtowers, raised-floor storehouses, and a ceremonial hall offer a look at what a village may have looked like 2,000 years ago. The grounds are extensive, making it a good choice for families and history buffs. Wheelchairs and strollers are available to borrow free of charge.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.4.tip: From Hakata, take a limited express to Yoshinogari-Koen Station in about 40 minutes, then walk about 15 minutes to the East Gate. There is almost no shade in summer.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.5.name: Yutoku Inari Shrine
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.5.text: One of Japan's three major Inari shrines. Its vermilion main hall stands on tall wooden supports against the mountainside and is striking from a distance. A path of red torii gates leads up the rear mountain to a viewpoint over the main hall. It's far less crowded than Kyoto's Fushimi Inari Taisha.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.5.tip: Take a bus for about 10 minutes from Hizen-Kashima Station. The mountain path is steep, so wear shoes with good traction.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.6.name: Karatsu Castle
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.6.text: A seaside castle built on a small hill. The keep houses a museum, and the top floor looks out over Karatsu Bay and the long stretch of Niji-no-Matsubara pine forest. The old streets below the castle have several pottery shops, and Karatsu ware is simple and durable. In early November, the Karatsu Kunchi Festival features a procession of huge lacquered floats.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.6.tip: There is a sloped elevator at the castle gate for visitors who prefer not to walk uphill. Accommodation is difficult to book during the Kunchi Festival.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.7.name: Yobuko Morning Market
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.7.text: A short harbor-side street where local vendors sell dried fish, sea urchin, and fruit. It's one of Japan's best-known morning markets. Afterward, visit a nearby restaurant for live squid sashimi. The squid is translucent, and the remaining pieces can be made into tempura.
c189b7520037918332b1.spots.7.tip: The market generally runs from morning until noon. Take a bus from Karatsu and try to arrive in the morning.
c189b7520037918332b1.stay: Stay in Takeo or Ureshino for hot springs. Both towns have stations on the Nishi Kyushu Shinkansen, with easy connections to Nagasaki and Fukuoka. If you're only visiting Karatsu and Yobuko, a day trip from Fukuoka is enough.
c189b7520037918332b1.tagline: Between Fukuoka and Nagasaki, with hot springs, ceramics, and squid
c189b7520037918332b1.tips.0: All of Saga's sights can be visited as day trips from Fukuoka, so you don't necessarily need to change hotels.
c189b7520037918332b1.tips.1: The JR Kyushu Rail Pass covers all of Saga. It's a better value when combined with a trip to Nagasaki.
c189b7520037918332b1.tips.2: Extra trains run during the Arita Ceramic Fair, but both the trains and streets get extremely crowded.
c189b7520037918332b1.tips.3: You'll need to transfer to a bus for Yobuko and Yutoku Inari Shrine, so check the last bus times in advance.

c2234265c3d52e44d079.cost: Solo train ~A$21; Uber split among 2–3 people ~A$40–55
c2234265c3d52e44d079.paragraphs.0: Sydney International Airport sits only 9 km from the CBD, yet riding the T8 Airport Line into International Station triggers a private-station concession fee of roughly A$17 per adult—pushing a one-way ticket past A$21 and outside the daily cap.
c2234265c3d52e44d079.paragraphs.1: The math is simple: traveling solo and light, the 15-minute train is punctual and traffic-proof; traveling with 2–3 people and large suitcases, calling an Uber or taxi straight to T1 Departures works out to barely a dozen Australian dollars per person while saving you platform lugging. If you've spent A$300 or more on eligible goods, preload your receipts in Australia's TRS app to breeze through the airport lane for your 10% GST refund.
c2234265c3d52e44d079.phase: Step 06 · Smart departure to the airport
c2234265c3d52e44d079.tip: Airport expressways crawl on Sunday afternoons and weekday morning peaks (07:30–09:00). If you're taking a rideshare or taxi, build in an extra 25-minute traffic buffer.
c2234265c3d52e44d079.title: How to dodge Sydney Airport's hefty station access fee: solo train vs. group Uber compared

c3ebe95a1561371887d1.s: Useful Japanese phrases: ordering and dietary restrictions, tax-free shopping, hotels, transportation, luggage delivery, pharmacies and medical care, and asking for help. Tap to enlarge and show staff.

c4242208bacc38e84988.location: Enoden Hase Station · Kotoku-in & Hasedera Temple
c4242208bacc38e84988.paragraphs.0: Step off the Enoden at Hase Station and walk 7 minutes north to Kotoku-in. Cast in the 13th century, this monumental bronze seated Amida Buddha originally sat inside a wooden hall until a Muromachi-period tsunami swept the temple away—leaving him serene beneath open skies and wooded hills ever since. For ¥50 extra, you can even duck inside the hollow bronze interior to inspect medieval casting seams.
c4242208bacc38e84988.paragraphs.1: Backtrack 5 minutes and turn into Hasedera Temple. Famous for June hydrangeas, it shines just as brightly in autumn and winter: stone stairways weave past koi ponds and smiling Jizo statues up to the Miharashidai viewing terrace overlooking Yuigahama's sweeping crescent bay—easy to lose half an hour on a sun-warmed bench.
c4242208bacc38e84988.photo.alt: Open-air bronze Great Buddha of Kamakura surrounded by pines and autumn foliage in warm afternoon light
c4242208bacc38e84988.photo.caption: Soft 15:30 sunlight warms the weathered green patina of Kamakura's Great Buddha, framed by pines and autumn leaves.
c4242208bacc38e84988.tip: Hasedera requires advance tickets for its hydrangea path during June peak; in autumn and winter, just buy at the gate vending machine—last entry is around 16:30, so don't cut it too close.
c4242208bacc38e84988.title: Walk 7 minutes from Hase Station to the open-air Great Buddha, then climb Hasedera's sea terrace

c48940b63e0f3d2b2b02.duration: About 1 hour for lunch + 1.5 hours strolling
c48940b63e0f3d2b2b02.location: Nanzen-ji approach · historic yudofu dining strip
c48940b63e0f3d2b2b02.paragraphs.0: Eating 30 minutes early at 11:30 is peak-season survival gold. Classics along Nanzen-ji's approach like Junsei and Okutan rack up hour-long waits past noon, yet walking in with the first seating between 11:15 and 11:30 often lands a garden-view window table immediately. Silky tofu simmering in kombu broth—dipped in soy sauce with yuzu kosho and scallions, alongside sesame tofu and crisp vegetable tempura—thaws out an early-morning chill in minutes.
c48940b63e0f3d2b2b02.paragraphs.1: From 12:30 to 14:30, Kyoto hits peak midday frenzy; don't waste it battling Kiyomizu-dera or Arashiyama. Amble north along the Philosopher's Path for 15 minutes and slip into Honen-in and Shinnyo-do. Honen-in's thatched gate and raked white sand mounds are free and whisper-quiet, while Shinnyo-do wraps a three-story pagoda in blazing maples with almost no tour groups—perfect for sitting on sun-warmed stone steps and doing nothing at all.
c48940b63e0f3d2b2b02.phase: Step 04 · 11:30 Early lunch to sit out the rush
c48940b63e0f3d2b2b02.photo.alt: Traditional Kyoto yudofu set meal in a steaming clay pot beside a window overlooking autumn maples
c48940b63e0f3d2b2b02.photo.caption: Snagging a window seat at 11:30 before the lunch rush lets a steaming clay pot of kombu yudofu melt away the morning cold.
c48940b63e0f3d2b2b02.tip: Not in the mood for a ¥4,000 kaiseki-style tofu lunch? Several beloved udon shops and yoshoku eateries sit near Keage Station, or duck into a quiet machiya cafe at the start of the Philosopher's Path for pour-over coffee and matcha sweets.
c48940b63e0f3d2b2b02.title: Beat the noon queue for Nanzen-ji yudofu, then slip away to quiet Honen-in

c50386ac46973c927191.access.0.how: From Shinagawa, take the JR Tokaido Line for about 15 minutes. From Shibuya, take an express train on the Tokyu Toyoko Line for about 25 minutes, costing about ¥310.
c50386ac46973c927191.access.1.how: The Odakyu Romancecar runs directly to Hakone-Yumoto in about 85 minutes and costs about ¥2,470. Without the limited express, change trains at Odawara; the trip takes about 2 hours and costs half as much.
c50386ac46973c927191.access.2.how: The JR Yokosuka Line runs directly from Tokyo Station to Kamakura in about 1 hour. From Shinjuku, take the Shonan-Shinjuku Line, or take Odakyu trains and change to the Enoden at Fujisawa.
c50386ac46973c927191.access.3.how: The Keikyu Line takes about 30 minutes from Haneda Terminals 1 and 2 to Yokohama Station, without going into central Tokyo.
c50386ac46973c927191.foods.0.name: Shirasu don
c50386ac46973c927191.foods.0.text: These tiny white fish are caught offshore around Kamakura and Enoshima and served over rice with grated ginger and soy sauce. They come cooked, called kama-age, or raw. The raw version is sweet and fresh, but is available only when the day's catch is fresh. Fishing is closed from winter to early spring, so only the cooked version is available then.
c50386ac46973c927191.foods.0.where: Enoshima's approach, Kamakura's Komachi Street, and the Koshigoe area
c50386ac46973c927191.foods.1.name: Owakudani black eggs
c50386ac46973c927191.foods.1.text: These eggs are boiled in Owakudani's hot-spring pools, which turn the shells black with sulfur and iron. Inside, they taste like ordinary hard-boiled eggs. Local lore says that eating one adds seven years to your life. They are usually sold in bags of several eggs and make a good snack during the loop.
c50386ac46973c927191.foods.1.where: The shop beside Owakudani Cable Car Station
c50386ac46973c927191.foods.2.name: Yokohama-style ie-kei ramen
c50386ac46973c927191.foods.2.text: This Yokohama-born ramen has a rich pork-bone and soy sauce broth, thick straight noodles, spinach, and large sheets of nori. When ordering, you can choose the noodle firmness, broth strength, and amount of oil. For a first order, regular is fine for everything. Dipping the nori in the broth and wrapping it around rice is a common way to eat it.
c50386ac46973c927191.foods.3.name: Hato Sabure cookies
c50386ac46973c927191.foods.3.text: These dove-shaped butter cookies are made by Toshimaya, a long-established Kamakura confectioner. They are crisp and not too sweet, and the individual wrapping makes them easy to share. They are one of Kamakura's most common souvenirs. The main shop on Wakamiya Oji is the most convenient, and they are also sold around Kamakura Station.
c50386ac46973c927191.foods.3.where: Toshimaya's main shop on Wakamiya Oji and around Kamakura Station
c50386ac46973c927191.intro.0: Kanagawa lies just south of Tokyo. Its three top destinations are Kamakura, a samurai capital more than 800 years ago, with the Great Buddha, ancient temples, and a small seaside train; Hakone, a hot-spring and volcanic area where a full loop requires mountain trains, cable cars, and a sightseeing boat; and Yokohama, a port city with easy waterfront walks, night views, and Chinatown.
c50386ac46973c927191.intro.1: Kamakura and Yokohama both make easy day trips from Tokyo. Hakone is best with one night at a hot-spring inn, followed by the loop the next day. If this is your second time in Tokyo and you want to add something beyond the city, Kanagawa is an easy place to start. All three destinations get crowded on weekends and holidays, so go on a weekday if you can. Kamakura and Hakone have many slopes and stairs, so wear comfortable shoes.
c50386ac46973c927191.name: Kanagawa
c50386ac46973c927191.seasons.note: Kamakura's cherry blossoms appear from late March to early April, and June is best for hydrangeas. Hakone's fall colors usually peak around November. The beaches are crowded in summer, while winter is the most comfortable time for hot springs.
c50386ac46973c927191.sources.0.title: Odakyu: Hakone Freepass
c50386ac46973c927191.sources.1.title: Odakyu: Enoshima-Kamakura Free Pass
c50386ac46973c927191.sources.2.title: Kōtoku-in official website (hours and admission)
c50386ac46973c927191.sources.3.title: japan-guide: Hakone Ropeway
c50386ac46973c927191.sources.4.title: japan-guide: Transportation from Tokyo to Hakone
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.0.name: Tsurugaoka Hachimangu
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.0.text: Kamakura's spiritual center, Tsurugaoka Hachimangu was moved to its current location when Minamoto no Yoritomo established his shogunate. From the east exit of Kamakura Station, walk about 10 minutes along Wakamiya Oji's raised central walkway, the Dankazura, lined with cherry trees in spring. Komachi Street, directly opposite, is packed with food and shops and is ideal for a stroll after visiting the shrine.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.0.tip: Komachi Street gets very crowded on weekends. Arrive before 10 a.m. for a more relaxed visit.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.1.name: Kōtoku-in (Great Buddha of Kamakura)
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.1.text: This bronze Amida Buddha stands about 11 meters tall and was cast in the 13th century. After the original hall was destroyed by a tsunami, the statue remained outdoors. It is a 5–10-minute walk from Hase Station on the Enoden. For about ¥50 extra, you can enter the statue and see the casting seams inside—a hit with children.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.1.tip: Hase-dera is only a few minutes away, so visit both together. Entry inside the Buddha ends at 4:30 p.m.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.2.name: Hase-dera
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.2.text: Built halfway up a hillside, this temple houses a more than 9-meter-tall Eleven-Headed Kannon in its Kannon Hall. The observation platform overlooks Kamakura Bay. Flowers bloom here year-round, with the hydrangeas on the hillside being the most famous in June. It is a 5-minute walk from Hase Station and lies along the same route as the Great Buddha of Kamakura.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.2.tip: During hydrangea season, you need a numbered ticket for the hillside path. Waits can be long on weekends, so go early on a weekday if possible.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.3.fee: Free to enter the island; about ¥500 each for the lighthouse and caves
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.3.name: Enoshima
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.3.text: This small island is connected to the mainland by a long bridge. It is home to Enoshima Shrine, the Sea Candle observation lighthouse, and seaside Iwaya Caves. On clear days, you can see Mount Fuji across the water. The ride from Kamakura on the Enoden takes about 25 minutes and passes the famous railroad crossing featured in Slam Dunk. The island has many slopes, but visitors with average fitness can take the paid escalators uphill.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.3.tip: For views of Mount Fuji, choose a clear winter evening. From Shinjuku, take Odakyu trains; the trip takes about 65–75 minutes.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.4.name: Hakone-Yumoto Onsen
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.4.text: The final stop of the Romancecar and Hakone's largest hot-spring town. The shopping street in front of the station sells fish cakes, onsen manju, and other snacks. Along the river, several day-use hot springs welcome visitors, so you can bathe without staying overnight. From here, transfer to the mountain railway toward Gora and Owakudani—the starting point of the Hakone loop.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.4.tip: Many public baths do not admit guests with tattoos. If this is a concern, choose an inn with a private bath.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.5.name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.5.text: More than 100 sculptures are displayed across grassy hills at this open-air museum, with Hakone's mountains as a backdrop. It is an easy place to explore while walking. The Picasso Pavilion holds many ceramics and paintings, and you can climb inside the colorful stained-glass tower, Symphonic Sculpture. There is also a free foot bath for tired feet.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.5.tip: The museum is next to Chokoku no Mori Station on the mountain railway. Online tickets from the official website are about ¥200 cheaper than tickets bought on-site.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.6.name: Owakudani
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.6.text: This valley was formed by a volcanic eruption about 3,000 years ago and still vents sulfurous smoke. On clear days, you can see Mount Fuji. Owakudani is the midpoint of the Hakone loop: take the cable car up, continue to Togendai, board the sightseeing boat across Lake Ashi, and get off at Moto-Hakone. The torii gate standing in the lake at Hakone Shrine is one of the area's signature photo spots.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.6.tip: The mountain may close temporarily when volcanic gases are concentrated. In winter, the cable car often stops in sections for maintenance, with replacement buses running instead. Check the official website before leaving.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.7.name: Minato Mirai 21
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.7.text: Yokohama's modern waterfront district is home to a Ferris wheel, Red Brick Warehouse, and seaside promenades. It looks best after the lights come on at dusk. Walk along the water to Yamashita Park and Chinatown in about half an hour, with sea views all the way. The Cup Noodles Museum is nearby, where you can design a cup of noodles to take home.
c50386ac46973c927191.spots.7.tip: From Shibuya, take a through service on the Toyoko Line onto the Minatomirai Line. Get off at Minatomirai or Bashamichi Station for the shortest walk.
c50386ac46973c927191.stay: In Yokohama, stay around Minato Mirai or Kannai for easy access to the night views. In Hakone, stay at a hot-spring inn in Hakone-Yumoto or Gora, so you can take the loop at a relaxed pace the next day. Kamakura is usually visited as a day trip from Tokyo.
c50386ac46973c927191.tagline: Kamakura temples, Hakone hot springs, and Yokohama harbor—all within an hour of Tokyo
c50386ac46973c927191.tips.0: From Shinjuku to Hakone, the Hakone Freepass (about ¥7,100 for 2 days) includes round-trip travel and transportation within the area. The Romancecar requires an additional surcharge of about ¥1,200 each way.
c50386ac46973c927191.tips.1: If you are visiting only Kamakura and Enoshima, the Enoshima-Kamakura Free Pass from Shinjuku costs about ¥1,640 and allows unlimited rides on the Enoden.
c50386ac46973c927191.tips.2: The Hakone loop involves several transfers. Leave large luggage at your Tokyo hotel or in storage rather than taking it on the mountain railway.
c50386ac46973c927191.tips.3: Enoden platforms can have long lines on weekends in Kamakura. The sights are not far apart, so walking is often faster.

c53e22c6250cfee550ac.s: Passports, payments, internet, plugs—your selections save automatically

c58cea670c37097a065a.duration: About 45 minutes on JR + 14 minutes on the monorail
c58cea670c37097a065a.location: JR Ofuna Station → Shonan Monorail Shonan-Enoshima Station
c58cea670c37097a065a.paragraphs.0: Catch a JR Tokaido or Yokosuka Line train from Tokyo or Shinagawa just after 08:00 for a 45-minute straight shot to Ofuna Station. Outside the fare gates, follow the bold overhead 'Shonan Monorail' signs for 3 minutes and tap your mobile Suica straight onto the platform.
c58cea670c37097a065a.paragraphs.1: Try to snag the front window spot right behind the driver's cab in car 1. Hanging beneath its steel beam, the train dives through tunnels, skims suburban rooftops, and banks around wooded hills across a thrilling 14-minute ride until Sagami Bay flashes into view—an amusement ride at commuter fare. From the Shonan-Enoshima terminus, a 3-minute walk over the footbridge lands you right at Benten Bridge leading onto the island.
c58cea670c37097a065a.photo.alt: Silver Shonan Monorail suspended beneath elevated tracks gliding above green hills and rooftops
c58cea670c37097a065a.photo.caption: Just 14 minutes from Ofuna to Shonan-Enoshima, watching steel tracks weave over hills toward the ocean from the front car is the loop's best opening act.
c58cea670c37097a065a.tip: Based in Shinjuku, Yoyogi, or Shimokitazawa? Odakyu's Enoshima-Kamakura Freepass (~¥1,640, covering Shinjuku round trip plus unlimited Enoden rides) wins on value—just change to the Enoden at Fujisawa or ride direct to Katase-Enoshima.
c58cea670c37097a065a.title: Ride JR straight to Ofuna, then switch to the 'upside-down roller coaster' Shonan Monorail

c6cce1257f124190b24c.cost: Takayama Jinya admission ¥440; street snacks about ¥1,500
c6cce1257f124190b24c.location: Miyagawa Morning Market → Takayama Jinya → Kami-Sannomachi old town
c6cce1257f124190b24c.paragraphs.0: Takayama is at its gentlest between 08:00 and 10:00. Follow the snow-lined Miyagawa River through the Miyagawa Morning Market, browsing stalls sizzling Hida beef skewers, crisp honey apples, rich espresso poured into edible cookie cups, and handmade sarubobo charms while chatting with cheerful local grandmothers through clouds of frost.
c6cce1257f124190b24c.paragraphs.1: From the market, walk 8 minutes to Takayama Jinya—Japan's only surviving Edo-period shogunate provincial governor's complex—to see snow-framed tatami halls and ancient rice-tax granaries. Loop back to Kami-Sannomachi for two pieces of blowtorched Hida beef nigiri served on a crispy rice cracker and a skewer of smoky-savory mitarashi dango.
c6cce1257f124190b24c.phase: Step 05 · Day 3 Morning Miyagawa Market & snow-dusted Sanmachi
c6cce1257f124190b24c.photo.alt: Snow-dusted Edo-era wooden merchant houses along Takayama's Sanmachi Suji street in crisp winter morning light
c6cce1257f124190b24c.photo.caption: Before 9 a.m., Takayama's Sanmachi old town is free of tour groups—fresh snow trims the dark cedar eaves while clear water runs past in the stone gutters.
c6cce1257f124190b24c.tip: Got an extra half-day? Hop on a 15-minute local train from JR Takayama Station to Hida-Furukawa, the quiet town that inspired the anime "Your Name," where white-walled storehouses line clear canals with a tenth of Takayama's crowds.
c6cce1257f124190b24c.title: Stroll the 08:00 riverside morning market for warm milk, torched Hida beef sushi, and Takayama Jinya

c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.access.0.how: China Southern operates about 3–4 direct flights a week from Guangzhou to Perth year-round. The flight takes about 8 hours. From other cities, connect through Singapore, Hong Kong, Sydney, or Melbourne.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.access.1.how: Domestic flights take about 4–5 hours (westbound flights take longer). During daylight saving time in the eastern states, Perth is 3 hours behind.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.access.2.how: The flight takes about 5 hours. There are plenty of flights, making Singapore a convenient connection from other cities in China.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.access.3.how: The flight takes about 3 hours. You can also take the Indian Pacific across the continent, with 2 nights on board.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.0.name: Western Rock Lobster
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.0.text: One of Western Australia's most important seafoods, usually grilled whole or halved and served with garlic butter or lemon. When heading north to the Pinnacles, the coastal town of Cervantes is the most convenient place to eat lobster. Prices follow the daily market rate.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.0.where: Coastal towns such as Cervantes and Lancelin, and around Fishing Boat Harbour in Fremantle.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.1.name: Fish and Chips
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.1.text: A staple on the Western Australian coast. Freshly fried white fish comes with crisp batter, thick-cut chips, lemon, and tartar sauce. Each shop uses different fish, so ask what is available that day. Watch out for seagulls trying to steal your food.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.1.where: Restaurants along Fishing Boat Harbour in Fremantle.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.2.name: Margaret River Wine
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.2.text: Margaret River is known for Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay. Production is small, but quality is consistently high. Most wineries have a cellar door where you can taste a few wines before deciding whether to buy. Many also have restaurants, and a long lunch with wine is a classic local experience.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.2.where: Wineries around Margaret River town and along Caves Road.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.3.name: Marron
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.3.text: A freshwater crayfish native to southwestern Western Australia. Much larger than a typical crayfish, it has a blue-black shell and sweet, delicate meat. Farms and restaurants around Margaret River and Pemberton commonly serve it grilled or boiled and chilled.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.foods.3.where: Restaurants and farms around Margaret River and Pemberton.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.intro.0: Western Australia covers one-third of Australia, but most people live in the capital, Perth. The highlights are the coast and the wilderness: quokkas on Rottnest Island, the limestone pillars of the Pinnacles, wineries and surf beaches around Margaret River, and Ningaloo Reef farther north, where you can swim with whale sharks.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.intro.1: The sights can be hundreds of kilometres apart. For a first visit, use Perth as your base: spend 1–2 days in the city and Fremantle, 1 day on Rottnest Island, 1 day heading north to the Pinnacles, and 2–3 days south in Margaret River. To visit Ningaloo or Esperance, it is best to fly there first and rent a car. This saves time compared with driving the whole way.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.intro.2: Perth is on UTC+8, and there are direct flights from Guangzhou. The pace is relaxed and crowds are light, so it suits travellers who enjoy road trips and the outdoors. If you mainly want a big-city break and sights such as the Opera House, Sydney and Melbourne are a better fit.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.name: Western Australia
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.seasons.note: Wildflowers bloom from September–November, when temperatures are mild. March–May is also pleasant. Perth often exceeds 35°C from December–February. Ningaloo is best for whale sharks around March–August.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.0.name: Kings Park and Botanic Garden
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.0.text: This huge park on a hill west of the city centre is larger than New York's Central Park, with native bushland covering half of it. From the lookout beside the war memorial, you can see the Swan River and Perth's skyline at once. It is especially beautiful at sunset. The botanic garden contains thousands of native Western Australian plants and is at its most colourful during wildflower season in September.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.0.tip: Reach the lookout half an hour before sunset. The botanic garden also has an elevated walkway through the treetops.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.1.name: Fremantle
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.1.text: Perth's old port has remarkably well-preserved 19th-century limestone buildings, along with more cafés and small bars than the city centre. Fremantle Prison, a World Heritage site, can be visited on a guided tour. The Fremantle Markets, open Friday–Sunday, are ideal for browsing and snacking. Head to Fishing Boat Harbour at sunset for fish and chips. The train from Perth takes about 30 minutes.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.1.tip: The markets are open only on Friday, Saturday, Sunday, and public holiday Mondays.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.2.fee: About A$88 return from Fremantle (including the island admission fee)
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.2.name: Rottnest Island (Wadjemup)
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.2.text: This island is about a 30-minute ferry ride from Fremantle. Private cars are not allowed, so rent a bicycle and follow the island loop past white-sand coves and clear, pale-green water. The main attraction is the quokka, which looks as if it is smiling with its upturned mouth. They are common around the settlement near the jetty.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.2.tip: Do not touch or feed the quokkas. You can be fined. Supplies are limited on the island, so bring plenty of water and sun protection.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.3.name: The Pinnacles, Nambung National Park
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.3.text: Thousands of yellow limestone pillars rise from the sand, some several metres high, creating an otherworldly landscape. Cars can follow the roughly 4-kilometre one-way loop, and there is also a roughly 1.2-kilometre walking trail. The drive north from Perth takes about 2.5 hours. On the way, you can sandboard the white dunes at Lancelin. The sunsets and starry skies after dark are both excellent.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.3.tip: There is no shade in the park, so avoid midday in summer. Watch for kangaroos on the road when driving back after sunset.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.4.name: Margaret River Region
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.4.text: About 3 hours south of Perth, this wine region is also known for surf beaches and tall forests. Spend the day having lunch and tasting wine at wineries, exploring limestone caves such as Mammoth Cave and Lake Cave, or visiting Cape Leeuwin Lighthouse, where the Indian and Southern oceans meet. The Busselton Jetty extends almost 2 kilometres into the sea. Stay at least 2 nights.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.4.tip: You need to drive between wineries. Choose a designated driver or join a winery day tour.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.5.fee: Free access to the marine park; boat tours cost extra
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.5.name: Ningaloo Reef & Coral Bay
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.5.text: World Heritage–listed Ningaloo Reef lies right off the coast. At Coral Bay, you can walk a few steps from the beach to snorkel among coral and fish. From around March–August, boat tours offer the chance to swim with whale sharks. Humpback whales visit from June–November. More than 1,000 kilometres from Perth, the area is usually reached by flying to Exmouth and renting a car. Coral Bay and Turquoise Bay in Cape Range National Park are nearby.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.5.tip: Turquoise Bay has a current along the shore. Read the signs before snorkelling, and do not swim too far if you are not a strong swimmer.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.6.name: Kalbarri National Park
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.6.text: The Murchison River cuts a long gorge through red sandstone. The rock arch known as Nature's Window frames the river bend below, while a cantilevered lookout extends over the cliff for views into the gorge. Along the coast, waves have carved tall cliffs and natural bridges. The drive from Perth takes about 6–7 hours. You can combine it with the Pinnacles and Pink Lake on a route north.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.6.tip: The gorge area often exceeds 40°C in summer. Start hikes in the morning. Wildflowers are most abundant from July–October.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.7.name: Lucky Bay, Cape Le Grand National Park
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.7.text: This bay near Esperance on Western Australia's south coast has brilliantly white sand and water that shifts from pale green to deep blue. It is best known for kangaroos that often sun themselves on the beach. About 700 kilometres from Perth, it is usually reached by flying to Esperance and driving for about 1 hour. Hellfire Bay and other beautiful beaches are nearby.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.spots.7.tip: Do not feed the kangaroos bread or snacks, as these can make them sick. Keep your distance when taking photos.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.stay: For a first visit, stay in central Perth or Northbridge for easy access to the airport, ferry terminals, and train station. Fremantle is a good choice if you prefer a slower pace. For a wine-country trip, stay in Margaret River town or Dunsborough.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.tagline: Indian Ocean shores, quokkas, and wine country roads
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.tips.0: Perth is in the UTC+8 time zone, and Western Australia does not observe daylight saving time, making jet lag relatively easy to manage.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.tips.1: If you plan to drive, licence and translation requirements depend on your licence and the rules in Western Australia. Check the official website of the Western Australian Department of Transport before setting out. Australia drives on the left.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.tips.2: Kangaroos are common in the countryside around dusk and at night, so do most long-distance driving during the day. Service stations can be far apart; fill up when you see one.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.tips.3: If you plan to visit several national parks, you can buy a Western Australian parks pass on the DBCA website. It costs less than paying entry fees each time.
c76ea7d1b74d334208b6.tips.4: Flies are numerous and UV levels are extremely high from December–February. Bring a fly net, a hat, and SPF50 sunscreen.

c7f5255aad86f15430b9.0: [Why sleep at Kawaguchiko] 06:30–08:30 offers the clearest skies and glassiest water for Mt. Fuji—clouds frequently wrap the peak by noon. Sleeping lakeside doubles your odds.
c7f5255aad86f15430b9.1: [Hakone luggage rule] Never drag a 28-inch suitcase onto Hakone mountain trains and ropeways! Store big trunks at your Tokyo hotel or forward them ahead via Yamato Takkyubin.
c7f5255aad86f15430b9.2: [Fuji-Hakone Pass fine print] The 3-day pass (~¥10,100) covers Shinjuku round-trip, Hakone's 8 transport modes, and designated Fujikyu buses, but Romancecar express supplements (~¥1,200) cost extra—and if you're continuing straight to Kyoto instead of returning to Shinjuku, skip the pass.
c7f5255aad86f15430b9.3: [Autumn-winter visibility bonus] Historically, November (11) through April (4) boasts far higher clear-Fuji odds than hazy humid summer.

c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.name: Kansai International Airport
c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.options.0.name: Nankai rapi:t Limited Express
c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.options.0.note: Most convenient for Namba, Shinsaibashi, and Dotonbori. If you are not in a hurry, the Nankai Airport Express costs only the fare, about ¥44 minutes. Buying a limited express ticket onboard costs about ¥300 extra.
c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.options.0.price: about ¥1,670 (about ¥970 for the fare + about ¥700 for the limited express ticket)
c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.options.1.name: JR HARUKA Limited Express
c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.options.1.note: No transfer is needed for Kyoto. The discounted ticket requires a foreign passport and short-term visitor status. It can only be booked on the JR West website or through overseas travel agencies, not in Japan.
c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.options.1.price: Visitors from abroad can buy a discounted one-way HARUKA ticket. Tickets sold from November 1, 2026, have revised fares; check the JR West website.
c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.options.1.time: Direct to Kyoto with no transfer; check the timetable for the travel time
c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.options.2.name: Airport Limousine Bus
c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.options.2.note: No reservation is needed; board in order of arrival. Luggage goes underneath the bus. The easiest option if you are staying near Umeda or Kyoto Station, especially with large bags.
c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.options.2.price: about ¥1,800 to Umeda and ¥2,800 to Kyoto Station
c8527faf1e2011e40ecb.options.2.time: About 60 minutes to Umeda and 85–90 minutes to Kyoto Station

c912aa7ae0f556441af1.s: Starting November 1, 2026, Japan’s tax-free system will switch to refunds at departure: pay the tax-included price first, then receive a consumption tax refund after customs confirms your departure. Rules, steps, FAQs, and quick calculations.

cad50f1c1579573554fd.access.0.how: Direct flights to Sydney from Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Chengdu, Haikou and other cities take about 9–12 hours. A Shenzhen route is scheduled to launch in December 2026.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.access.1.how: About 1.5 hours by air, with frequent flights, or about 9 hours by car.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.access.2.how: About 1.5 hours by air. For Byron Bay, fly into Gold Coast Airport, then drive about 1 hour.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.access.3.how: About 3 hours by car or 50 minutes by air.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.0.name: Sydney rock oysters
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.0.text: Farmed in New South Wales estuaries, these native oysters are smaller than Pacific oysters, with a stronger flavor, mineral notes and a sweet finish. Purists eat them raw with just a little lemon and a glass of local white wine. Flavors vary by estuary, and many restaurants list where their oysters come from.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.0.where: Sydney Fish Market and seafood restaurants in The Rocks and along the harbor
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.1.name: Sydney Fish Market seafood
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.1.text: One of the Southern Hemisphere's largest fish markets, Sydney Fish Market has moved into a new building on Blackwattle Bay. Stalls steam, fry and grill seafood to order. You can also buy sashimi, lobster or prawns and take them to a waterfront seat. Lunchtime is busiest; arrive early for the best selection.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.1.where: Sydney Fish Market in Pyrmont, open daily
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.2.name: Aussie meat pie
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.2.text: Australia's staple fast food wraps tender minced beef and gravy in flaky pastry. The old-school Sydney version comes topped with mashed potatoes, mushy peas and more gravy, eaten standing by the roadside. You will find pies in bakeries and at sports grounds. Freshly baked is best.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.2.where: Bakeries, sports grounds and old-school pie carts around Woolloomooloo Wharf
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.3.name: Hunter Valley Semillon
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.3.text: Hunter Valley's signature white wine is light, tart and relatively low in alcohol when young. After five to ten years, it turns golden and develops honey, nut and toast aromas. Taste young and aged wines side by side at a winery to see the striking difference.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.3.where: Winery cellar doors around Pokolbin in Hunter Valley
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.4.name: Smashed avo on toast
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.4.text: A Sydney cafe brunch staple: toasted sourdough topped with smashed avocado, feta, lemon and chili flakes, often with a poached egg. Lines are common on weekend mornings. Add a flat white for a typical local weekend breakfast.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.foods.4.where: Cafes in Bondi, Surry Hills and Newtown
cad50f1c1579573554fd.intro.0: New South Wales is the first stop for many visitors to Australia. In Sydney, you can fit the Opera House, Harbour Bridge, ferries and beaches into a day around the harbor. The Blue Mountains are two hours west. Head north for Hunter Valley wineries and the dunes of Port Stephens, then continue to Byron Bay for an East Coast road trip.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.intro.1: For a first visit, allow 3–4 days in Sydney: one for the harbor, one for the coastal walk and Manly, and one for the Blue Mountains. Use any remaining time for the zoo or Hunter Valley. For dolphins, whales or white-sand beaches, add 2–3 days driving north or south. Beyond Sydney, you will generally need a car or a tour.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.intro.2: Sydney has convenient public transit. Tap a contactless credit card to ride trains, ferries and buses. December to January is the summer vacation peak, and hotels are expensive and hard to book around the New Year's Eve fireworks. At beaches, swim only between the red and yellow flags.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.name: New South Wales
cad50f1c1579573554fd.seasons.note: September–November and March–May have the most comfortable weather. December–February is hot, with peak beach season and bushfire season. Whales can be seen along the coast from May–November.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.0.fee: Free to view from outside / Tours about A$50
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.0.name: Sydney Opera House
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.0.text: Up close, the white shell-shaped roofs reveal more than a million tiles, with colors that shift in the sunlight. To see inside, take an official tour lasting about 1 hour. Better still, buy a performance ticket and hear a concert in the Concert Hall. Afterward, walk through the Royal Botanic Garden Sydney to Mrs Macquarie's Chair for the classic view of the Opera House and bridge together.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.0.tip: Book tours online in advance for a lower price than same-day tickets. Visit Mrs Macquarie's Chair toward evening for sunset and the lights coming on.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.1.fee: Free to walk across / Book bridge climbs in advance
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.1.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.1.text: Locals call this steel arch bridge, opened in 1932, the “Coathanger.” For a free crossing, take the eastern pedestrian walkway from The Rocks to the north shore. The walk takes about 20–30 minutes, with views of the Opera House and harbor along the way. For more of a thrill, join BridgeClimb and climb to the top of the arch in a safety harness. Allow two to three hours; sunset climbs are the most popular.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.1.tip: Climbers must take a breath alcohol test. Phones and cameras are not allowed; official photographers take the pictures.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.2.name: Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.2.text: Start at the southern end of Bondi Beach and follow the sandstone cliffs south through Tamarama, Bronte and Clovelly to Coogee. The walk is about 6 kilometers and takes 2–3 hours. Along the way are ocean pools, a clifftop cemetery and several small bays where you can swim. From May–November, you may spot whale spouts. Take a bus back to the city from Coogee.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.2.tip: There is almost no shade along the route. Bring water, a hat and sunscreen. At Bondi, swim only between the red and yellow flags.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.3.name: Manly Ferry & Manly Beach
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.3.text: The ferry from Circular Quay to Manly takes about 30 minutes, passing the Opera House and bridge along the way. It is the cheapest way to see the harbor. Manly has the harbor on one side and a surf beach on the other. Follow the coastal path to Shelly Beach to snorkel among the fish, then catch an evening ferry back to the city at sunset.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.3.tip: The outside deck has the best views. Tap a contactless credit card or Opal card to board.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.4.name: Taronga Zoo Sydney
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.4.text: This zoo sits on a hillside on the harbor's north shore, a little over ten minutes by ferry from Circular Quay. See Australian animals such as koalas, kangaroos and platypuses. Its best-known view has giraffes with the Sydney skyline and Opera House behind them. The grounds are hilly; allow half a day to a full day with children.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.4.tip: Arrive at opening, when the animals are more active. Wear comfortable shoes for the hilly grounds.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.5.fee: Echo Point free / Scenic World from about A$64
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.5.name: Blue Mountains National Park
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.5.text: The World Heritage-listed Blue Mountains are about 2 hours from Sydney. Oil released by the eucalyptus forests gives the distant valleys their blue haze. Views of the Three Sisters from Echo Point in Katoomba are free. Nearby Scenic World has what it calls the world's steepest railway, along with cable cars high above the valley. If time allows, walk a section of a cliffside trail or visit Wentworth Falls.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.5.tip: Trains from Central Station to Katoomba take about 2 hours. From December–February, check for extreme heat and bushfire road closures before setting out.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.6.name: Hunter Valley
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.6.text: One of Australia's oldest wine regions lies about 2 hours by car from Sydney. More than a hundred wineries cluster around Pokolbin. The signature wines are Semillon, which develops honey and toast aromas with age, and Shiraz. Take an early-morning hot-air balloon ride over the vineyards, visit three or four wineries on a tasting tour, then spend the night at a vineyard estate.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.6.tip: Keep drinking to a minimum if you are driving; Australia has strict drink-driving limits. A tour or private driver is the easiest option.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.7.name: Port Stephens & Stockton Bight Dunes
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.7.text: About 2.5 hours north of Sydney, the dunes behind Anna Bay are the Southern Hemisphere's largest moving coastal dunes. Take a four-wheel-drive tour to try sandboarding. A resident pod of bottlenose dolphins lives in the waters around Nelson Bay, with plenty of dolphin-watching cruises available. From May–November, you can also see migrating humpback whales. Combine the area with Hunter Valley for a two- or three-day road trip.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.7.tip: Driving in the dunes requires a permit. Keep regular rental cars off the sand; a four-wheel-drive tour is the easiest option.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.8.name: Byron Bay & Cape Byron Lighthouse
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.8.text: At mainland Australia's easternmost point, a white lighthouse stands on the headland. Many visitors come specifically for sunrise. The loop walk around the lighthouse takes about 1.5–2 hours, with sweeping bay views. Humpback whales are common from May–November, and dolphins sometimes surface offshore. The town is known for surfing, cafes and markets, about 1 hour by car from Gold Coast Airport.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.8.tip: Parking beside the lighthouse is very limited. In peak season, walk up from town along the coastal path in the morning.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.9.name: Jervis Bay & Hyams Beach
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.9.text: About 3 hours south of Sydney, Jervis Bay has water clear enough to see the bottom and fine white sand at Hyams Beach. Take a dolphin-watching cruise, spot whales from May–November or walk the coastal trails in nearby Booderee National Park. An overnight detour here makes a relaxed two-day trip between Sydney and Canberra.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.spots.9.tip: Traffic is heavy and parking is difficult in December–January and on weekends. Arrive early in the morning if possible. The water is cool.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.stay: For a first visit, stay around Circular Quay, The Rocks or the city center for easy walks to the Opera House and access to ferries. For a beach stay, choose Bondi or Manly, about 30–40 minutes from the city by bus or ferry.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.tagline: Harbor city, Blue Mountains, wineries and East Coast beaches
cad50f1c1579573554fd.tips.0: Tap a contactless credit card or mobile wallet to ride trains, ferries and buses. Daily and weekly fare caps apply.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.tips.1: At beaches, swim only between the red and yellow flags, where lifeguards patrol. UV levels are extremely high from December–February; a hat and sunscreen are essential.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.tips.2: Drive on the left and give way to traffic from the right at roundabouts. License and translation requirements depend on your license; check official requirements, including whether you need a translation by a NAATI-certified translator.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.tips.3: Daylight saving time runs from the first Sunday in October to the first Sunday in April of the following year. Sydney uses UTC+11 during this period and UTC+10 otherwise.
cad50f1c1579573554fd.tips.4: December–February is bushfire season. Before visiting the Blue Mountains or other mountain areas, check the NSW Rural Fire Service (RFS) for fire and road closure information.

cb7c25064c43625a09b4.0: [The car-free hotel rule] Book all 3 nights within a 5-minute walk of Naha's Asahibashi or Kenchomae Station. You never change hotels with luggage, and every northbound highway bus and day-tour pickup departs right outside your door.
cb7c25064c43625a09b4.1: [Anti-seasickness rule for whale watching] Winter swells off the Kerama Islands can get choppy. Even if you never feel motion-sick on land, take a seasickness tablet 30 minutes before boarding and pack a windproof, water-resistant jacket—the ocean breeze feels 6°C colder than downtown Naha.
cb7c25064c43625a09b4.2: [Two smart ways to reach Churaumi Aquarium] Want a full 4 hours inside the aquarium for the Kuroshio Sea feeding show? Catch the Yanbaru Express or Okinawa Airport Shuttle straight from Asahibashi. Prefer bundling Cape Manzamo, Kouri Island, and the aquarium in one sweep? A northbound sightseeing bus with admission included beats piecing tickets together.
cb7c25064c43625a09b4.3: [Off-peak budget reality] During the January–February low season (outside Lunar New Year week), four-star monorail-side hotels in Naha run under CNY 300 per person per night—freeing up your rental-car savings for Agu pork shabu-shabu and ocean-view coffee.

cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.0.text: Tax-free shops will first charge the tax-included price. When you leave Japan within 90 days of the day after purchase, scan your passport at an airport terminal and have customs confirm the purchase before checking your luggage. The shop or refund agency will then refund the consumption tax. The same-day, pre-tax purchase total at one shop must be at least ¥5,000. Consumables will no longer need to be sealed, and the ¥500,000 limit is removed. However, you cannot get a refund for items you eat or use in Japan.
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.0.title: Tax-free shopping changes to “pay tax first, get a refund when you leave”
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.1.text: The International Tourist Tax will be ¥3,000 each time you leave Japan. Airlines will collect it with your ticket price, so you do not need to pay it separately. Tickets issued before July 1 for flights whose departure date was already set will generally still be charged at ¥1,000. Children under 2 and passengers who leave Japan in transit within 24 hours of arrival are exempt.
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.1.title: Departure tax rises from ¥1,000 to ¥3,000
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.2.text: Kyoto City has five tax bands based on the room rate per person per night: ¥200 for less than ¥6,000, ¥400 for ¥6,000–¥20,000, ¥1,000 for ¥20,000–¥50,000, ¥4,000 for ¥50,000–¥100,000, and ¥10,000 for more than ¥100,000. The tax is based on your check-in date. If you prepaid under the old rates, you will need to pay the difference at check-in.
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.2.title: Kyoto accommodation tax rises to as much as ¥10,000
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.3.text: Stays in Hokkaido will incur a prefectural tax of ¥100 per person per night for room rates under ¥20,000, ¥200 for ¥20,000–¥50,000, and ¥500 for more than ¥50,000. Sapporo, Otaru, Hakodate, Asahikawa, Furano, Niseko, Kutchan, and other areas also add municipal taxes, so the actual amount will be slightly higher.
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.3.title: Hokkaido introduces an accommodation tax
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.4.text: Osaka Prefecture lowers the accommodation-tax threshold from ¥7,000 to ¥5,000 per person per night: ¥200 for ¥5,000–¥15,000, ¥400 for ¥15,000–¥20,000, and ¥500 for more than ¥20,000. The tax is based on the room rate excluding meals. Check whether it is included in the price when you book.
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.4.title: Osaka lowers its accommodation-tax threshold and raises the rates
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.5.text: JR East is raising fares by an average of about 7.1%. The starting fare on the Yamanote Line and other lines rises from ¥150 to ¥160, and Tokyo's former low-fare zones will be merged into the regular fare zone. JR trips in Tokyo will cost a little more, so do not use fares from older guides when planning your budget.
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.5.title: JR East raises fares
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.6.text: Since 2025, both the Yamanashi and Shizuoka trailheads have charged ¥4,000 per person, and the fee will remain unchanged in 2026. The Yoshida Trail is limited to 4,000 people a day and closes at the gate from 14:00 to 3:00 the next day. On the Shizuoka side, you must register with FUJI NAVI and complete the required learning program first; nighttime climbs require a stay at a mountain hut. Do not climb during the closed season.
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.6.title: Climbing Mount Fuji costs ¥4,000, unchanged in 2026
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.7.text: Previously, you could mail tax-free purchases yourself via EMS or another service before leaving Japan and clear customs with the paperwork. This option has been discontinued. To receive the tax refund, you must bring the items with you to the airport. Alternatively, arrange direct overseas shipping at the shop, which will handle the tax-free procedure.
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.7.title: You can no longer mail tax-free purchases home yourself
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.8.text: The ferry to Miyajima costs an additional ¥100 per person per trip. The ferry company collects it as part of the fare, so you do not need to queue separately. If you plan to visit several times within one year, you can pay ¥500 once for an annual pass. Preschool children are exempt.
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.8.title: Miyajima introduces a ¥100 visitor tax
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.9.text: Japan plans to introduce JESTA, similar to the U.S. ESTA, in fiscal 2028. It will apply to short-term visitors from visa-exempt countries. Travelers without approval will not be allowed to board, but the exact date has not been set. Travelers whose passports require a visa for Japan are generally not affected; there is currently no official application portal, so beware of websites offering applications on your behalf.
cbdcc46bc82b2773c52f.items.9.title: The JESTA electronic travel authorization has not started yet

cc37a727200c738ad5a8.paragraphs.0: A 15-minute stroll (or short subway hop to Nipponbashi) brings you through Kuromon Market. Here is the honest take: skip full meals here and walk right past entrance stalls waving giant tourist signs for grilled crab legs or wagyu—many quote prices per 100 grams, easily pushing a casual snack over ¥10,000.
cc37a727200c738ad5a8.paragraphs.1: Treat Kuromon as a quick warm-up walk toward Dotonbori and spend on just two honest neighborhood staples: Takahashi Foods' fresh warm soy milk (thick almost like silken tofu, under ¥150 a cup) and Ishibashi Foods' Kansai dashi oden—translucent daikon, beef tendon, and konjac simmered deep with flavor.
cc37a727200c738ad5a8.phase: Step 03 · 11:00 The Smart Way to Walk Kuromon
cc37a727200c738ad5a8.photo.alt: Lively covered arcade of Kuromon Market in Osaka
cc37a727200c738ad5a8.photo.caption: Kuromon works best as a quick snack corridor—stick to local soy milk and oden veterans instead of chasing overpriced crab stalls.
cc37a727200c738ad5a8.tip: Detour two minutes over to Sennichimae Doguyasuji Arcade, packed with chef knives, cast-iron takoyaki pans, ceramics, and hyper-realistic plastic food displays—ten times better browsing than Kuromon souvenirs.
cc37a727200c738ad5a8.title: Still Curious About Kuromon on Your First Trip? Dodge Price Traps and Hit Only 2 True Classics

cd10b659b02b29241f1c.location: JR Hokkaido Operation Status / Donan & Chuo Highway Buses
cd10b659b02b29241f1c.paragraphs.0: Winter Hokkaido's real wildcard is sudden Sea of Japan snow squalls (fubuki). For track clearing and safety, JR Hokkaido suspends Hakodate and Muroran services decisively during heavy storms—leaving buffer time on your return day is non-negotiable.
cd10b659b02b29241f1c.paragraphs.1: Bookmark the English 'JR Hokkaido Train Operation Information' page. If the Hokuto Express shows red in the morning, ask your hotel front desk immediately about Donan Bus or Chuo Bus highway alternatives—many major Noboribetsu and Toya resorts even operate advance-booked direct shuttle buses to Sapporo and New Chitose Airport that you can lock in when booking your room.
cd10b659b02b29241f1c.tip: If your departure flight leaves before 14:00, always spend your final night back in Sapporo or at New Chitose Airport—never gamble on a same-morning snow-country rail transfer from Lake Toya.
cd10b659b02b29241f1c.title: Woke Up to Snow-Suspended JR Trains? Switch to Highway Buses in 10 Minutes Without Missing Flights

ceab422d7d7c7db0310f.0: Too many visitors give the Great Ocean Road a single day from Melbourne: boarding a 7 a.m. coach, white-knuckling endless bends, reaching the Twelve Apostles under harsh afternoon glare for a rushed 25-minute photo stop, and racing back in the dark. Spanning nearly three hundred kilometers of sheer cliffs, lighthouses, wild koala groves, temperate rainforest, and the Shipwreck Coast, this highway truly shines when you rent a car and take it at a 3-day, 2-night "coast out, inland back" pace.
ceab422d7d7c7db0310f.1: Below is my road-tested route broken into 6 clean stages, designed around the four hurdles that rattle first-time drivers in Australia: rewiring muscle memory for left-side, right-hand-drive roads; losing mobile reception for a solid hour through the Otway rainforest; avoiding deadly dusk collisions with wild kangaroos; and adapting to coastal towns where kitchens shut at half past seven.

cf2b19b4d09c761a4e30.options.0.note: Change to the JR Yamanote Line at Shinagawa for the fastest connections. Some trains run directly onto the Asakusa Line, so you can reach Asakusa and Higashi-Ginza without changing.
cf2b19b4d09c761a4e30.options.0.time: About 11–13 minutes from Terminal 3 to Shinagawa and 34 minutes to Asakusa
cf2b19b4d09c761a4e30.options.1.name: Tokyo Monorail
cf2b19b4d09c761a4e30.options.1.note: Change at Hamamatsucho for the JR Yamanote Line or Keihin-Tohoku Line. The platforms are spacious and luggage-friendly, with frequent service.
cf2b19b4d09c761a4e30.options.2.name: Limousine Bus
cf2b19b4d09c761a4e30.options.2.note: Services run even when trains have stopped after a late-night arrival, and can take you directly to your hotel. Morning and evening rush hours are prone to traffic.
cf2b19b4d09c761a4e30.options.2.price: about ¥1,400 to Shinjuku; late-night services about ¥2,800
cf2b19b4d09c761a4e30.options.2.time: About 40 minutes–1 hour to Shinjuku, depending on traffic

d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.gateways.0.how: The Meitetsu μ-SKY train takes about 29 minutes to Nagoya and costs about ¥1,430. From there, the Hida limited express takes about 2 hours 30 minutes to Takayama.
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.gateways.0.name: Chubu Centrair International Airport (NGO)
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.gateways.1.how: The closest airport to Kanazawa. The airport bus takes about 40–55 minutes to Kanazawa Station and costs about ¥1,400. A good gateway for a Hokuriku trip.
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.gateways.1.name: Komatsu Airport (KMQ)
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.gateways.2.how: The airport bus takes about 25 minutes to Niigata Station and costs about ¥470. From Niigata Station, the Shinkansen takes about 2 hours to Tokyo.
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.gateways.2.name: Niigata Airport (KIJ)
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.gateways.3.how: The Hokuriku Shinkansen takes about 2 hours 30 minutes to Kanazawa. A bus from Shinjuku takes about 1 hour 45 minutes to Lake Kawaguchi.
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.gateways.3.name: Entering from Tokyo
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.intro.0: Chubu is the broad region between Tokyo and Kansai. It has three parts: Tokai on the Pacific coast (Nagoya and Shizuoka), the central mountains (Yamanashi, Nagano, and northern Gifu's Hida), and Hokuriku on the Sea of Japan (Niigata, Toyama, Ishikawa, and Fukui). Mount Fuji, the Tateyama snow walls, Shirakawa-go, Kanazawa, and Takayama are all here. Many travelers return to Japan a second time just to see them.
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.intro.1: The classic route starts and ends in Nagoya: Nagoya → Takayama → Shirakawa-go → Kanazawa. If you only want to see Mount Fuji, leave from Tokyo and spend a night at Lake Kawaguchi. The mountains get heavy snow in winter, and some mountain routes close from December to mid-April. Choose your route by season.
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.name: Chubu
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.passes.0.name: Takayama-Hokuriku Area Tourist Pass
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.passes.0.text: About ¥19,800 for 5 days. It covers the limited express from Nagoya to Takayama, the bus from Takayama via Shirakawa-go to Kanazawa, and the Shinkansen from Toyama to Tsuruga. Best value for a Nagoya-to-Kanazawa or Nagoya-to-Osaka trip.
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.passes.1.name: Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.passes.1.text: About ¥24,500 for 5 days. It covers the entire Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route and JR trains between Nagoya, Toyama, and Matsumoto. Available only from mid-April to early November.
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.passes.2.name: Hokuriku Arch Pass
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.passes.2.text: About ¥35,000 for 7 days. It covers a one-way loop from Tokyo via Kanazawa to Osaka. Not worth it for a short trip in Chubu alone. Consider it for a Tokyo-to-Osaka itinerary.
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.passes.3.name: Mt. Fuji-Shizuoka Area Tourist Pass Mini
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.passes.3.text: About ¥6,500 for 3 days. It covers JR local trains and several bus companies in Shizuoka Prefecture, but not the Shinkansen. A good choice if you want to take your time exploring Shizuoka and Izu.
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.season: See the snow walls and cherry blossoms in April–June, fall colors in October–November, and Shirakawa-go's snowy scenery and ski slopes in winter. The mountains are a cool escape in summer.
d1a4a861e40f83e2eb15.sources.0.title: JR Passes for Overseas Visitors official website (JR Central · JR West)
