d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.access.0.how: Take the Tsubasa Yamagata Shinkansen to Yamagata in about 2.5–3 hours. No transfer is needed.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.access.1.how: The JR Senzan Line takes about 1 hour to Yamadera and about 1 hour 15 minutes to Yamagata.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.access.2.how: Take a bus to Zao Onsen in about 40 minutes.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.foods.0.name: Yonezawa beef
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.foods.0.text: One of Japan's best-known wagyu brands, with fine marbling and a tender texture. Around Yonezawa Station, you'll find sukiyaki, steak, and bento shops. For a more affordable option, try a Yonezawa beef bento.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.foods.0.where: Around Yonezawa Station and in central Yamagata City
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.foods.1.name: Imoni
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.foods.1.text: Taro, beef, konnyaku, and green onions simmered in a soy-based broth. In fall, people in Yamagata gather by the river to cook it in large pots. Restaurants serve it year-round, and it makes a warming winter soup.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.foods.1.where: Local cuisine restaurants in central Yamagata City
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.foods.2.name: Yamagata cherries
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.foods.2.text: Yamagata produces more than half of Japan's cherries. The popular Sato Nishiki variety is sweet and meaty. From mid-June to early July, you can visit farms for all-you-can-eat picking within a set time limit.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.foods.2.where: Fruit farms around Tendo and Higashine
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.foods.3.name: Cold ramen
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.foods.3.text: A Yamagata invention served in chilled broth, sometimes with ice cubes floating on top, but it still tastes like soy-sauce ramen. It's especially popular on hot summer days, though many shops serve it year-round.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.intro.0: Yamagata lies between Miyagi and the Sea of Japan. It has mountains, snow, and hot springs in abundance. Its two signature winter scenes are the snow monsters on Mount Zao, formed when ice and snow coat the trees, and the gas lamps glowing outside Ginzan Onsen's wooden inns on snowy nights. In other seasons, you can climb Yamadera or take a boat down the Mogami River.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.intro.1: The Yamagata Shinkansen runs directly from Tokyo to Yamagata City in about 2.5 hours. From Sendai, the JR Senzan Line takes about 1 hour to Yamadera, so many people visit on a day trip. To reach Ginzan Onsen, change to a bus at Oishida Station. Stay overnight for the best night views, but inns are hard to book.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.name: Yamagata
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.seasons.note: Zao's snow monsters are best from late January to February; Ginzan Onsen's snowy scenery is best from December–February; Yamadera's fall colors peak from late October to early November.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.sources.0.title: Risshaku-ji (Yamadera) official website
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.sources.1.title: Ginzan Onsen · Transportation
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.sources.2.title: Zao Onsen · Zao Mountain Resort
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.0.name: Yamadera (Risshaku-ji)
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.0.text: This ancient temple is built into a rocky mountain. From the temple gate to Okunoin, there are about 1,015 stone steps, taking about 1.5 hours round trip. Godaido offers sweeping valley views and the best photo spot. Basho wrote his famous cicada haiku here. The temple is beautiful among summer greenery and fall colors.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.0.tip: The stone steps can be icy in winter, so wear nonslip shoes. Cash only. The trail closes around 3 or 4 p.m.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.1.name: Ginzan Onsen
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.1.text: Three- and four-story wooden inns line both sides of a small river. When the gas lamps come on at dusk, the town looks like a movie set, especially in the snow. The hot-spring district is small; 30 minutes is enough to walk around. The bus from JR Oishida Station takes about 40 minutes. Winter weekends draw many day-trippers.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.1.tip: Traffic restrictions apply to private cars and day-trippers in winter. Check the official website for the latest information before you go.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.2.name: Zao Snow Monsters
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.2.text: In winter, strong winds blow snow and supercooled fog onto fir trees, freezing layer by layer and creating the famous snow monsters. From Zao Onsen, take the Zao Ropeway to Jizo Sancho Station and walk into the snow-monster grove. The monsters are most impressive from late January to February. Illumination is offered at night, and skiers can ski between them.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.2.tip: Temperatures at the summit often fall into the negative teens Celsius. Wear ski-level winter clothing. Strong winds can stop operations.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.3.name: Zao Onsen
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.3.text: At about 900 meters above sea level, Zao's strongly acidic sulfur springs are milky white and have a powerful smell. In winter, the area becomes a large ski resort. In summer, you can hike to see Okama Crater. The hot-spring town has several inexpensive public baths, plus a large outdoor bath in the mountains that closes in winter.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.3.tip: The sulfur can tarnish silver jewelry, so remove it before bathing.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.4.name: Mogami River Boat Ride
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.4.text: Ride a flat-bottomed wooden boat downstream through the Mogami Gorge for about 1 hour. Boatmen paddle while singing folk songs and telling stories. The gorge has steep walls and many waterfalls. Fall colors are beautiful, and in winter you can stay warm under a kotatsu. A bus from the endpoint returns to the departure point.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.4.tip: From Shinjo Station, take the JR Rikuu West Line to Furuguchi Station, then walk to the boarding area. Trains are infrequent.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.5.name: Mount Haguro
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.5.text: One of the Three Mountains of Dewa and a sacred mountain of Shugendo. From the base, climb about 2,446 stone steps through an old cedar forest. The National Treasure Five-Story Pagoda stands alone among the trees and has a striking atmosphere. The climb to the summit takes about 1 hour. If you prefer not to climb, take a bus directly to the summit.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.5.tip: The bus from Tsuruoka Station takes about 40 minutes to the base. Snow and ice can make the steps difficult in winter.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.6.name: Uesugi Shrine and Yonezawa
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.spots.6.text: This shrine, dedicated to the Warring States-period warlord Uesugi Kenshin, stands on the site of Yonezawa Castle. Cherry trees line the moat. Yonezawa is a stop on the Yamagata Shinkansen, making it a convenient place to stop for Yonezawa beef and a quick visit. In February, the Uesugi Snow Lantern Festival fills the area with snow lanterns.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.stay: Stay near Yamagata Station for convenient trips to Yamadera and Zao. Zao Onsen is a good base for winter skiing and seeing the snow monsters. Book Ginzan Onsen well in advance.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.tagline: Yamadera's thousand stone steps, Ginzan Onsen's snowy nights, and Zao's snow monsters
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.tips.0: Check whether your licence is valid for driving in Japan and what translation or permit is required. Winter mountain roads are also not recommended for self-driving; use the Shinkansen and buses.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.tips.1: Ginzan Onsen accommodations often sell out as soon as reservations open, so monitor booking dates well in advance in winter.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.tips.2: Yamadera has many steps, so pack light and bring water. Some sections may close when winter paths are covered in snow.
d1ce6fe8b848aa4f46ea.tips.3: The Zao Ropeway stops in strong winds. If you have 2 days, keep 1 day as a backup for seeing the snow monsters.

d251afebbd8362592365.s: Places in this step · Stamp directly into your trip

d2feb1f88e89291fa448.0: Relying on Kyoto city buses during foliage peak—a 20-minute ride easily stretches to 1 hour in traffic; always choose the Tozai Subway, Keihan Line, or JR when available.
d2feb1f88e89291fa448.1: Wearing hard-to-remove boots and thin socks to temples—Eikando and Tofuku-ji's Hojo require taking off shoes on frigid timber floors, and frozen feet ruin the mood.
d2feb1f88e89291fa448.2: Skipping reservation checks for booking-only temples—autumn hot spots like Ruriko-in and Enko-ji often require advance online reservations, and walk-ups get turned away.
d2feb1f88e89291fa448.3: Cramming Eikando and Tofuku-ji into the 11:00–14:00 crush—waking up just 1 hour earlier upgrades the whole day from a 60/100 slog to a 98/100 memory.

d40fea05c8991db13878.cost: All roadside lookouts and lighthouse grounds free
d40fea05c8991db13878.location: Split Point Lighthouse → Memorial Arch → Lorne → Kennett River → Apollo Bay
d40fea05c8991db13878.paragraphs.0: Past the surf hub of Torquay, detour to whitewashed, red-capped Split Point Lighthouse and walk the boardwalk overlooking Eagle Rock, then pull into the official parking bay at the iconic wooden Great Ocean Road Memorial Arch (honoring the WWI veterans who hand-carved the highway). Ahead lies the most photogenic stretch of cliff-hugging curves—every bend looks like a Southern Ocean postcard.
d40fea05c8991db13878.paragraphs.1: Pause in Lorne for a proper flat white and fish and chips, then reach Kennett River before 3 p.m. Turn off the highway onto Grey River Road beside Kafe Koala, creep in two hundred meters, park safely, and scan the forks of the tall eucalyptus trees overhead—you will likely spot three or four fluffy wild grey koalas dozing in the branches alongside vivid red-and-green king parrots. Never feed or startle them, and roll into Apollo Bay comfortably before 17:00.
d40fea05c8991db13878.phase: Step 02 · Day 1 11:30 Memorial Arch, Split Point Lighthouse & wild koalas
d40fea05c8991db13878.photo.alt: Great Ocean Road winding tightly along green coastal cliffs above the turquoise Southern Ocean in Victoria
d40fea05c8991db13878.photo.caption: Between Lorne and Apollo Bay, the road hugs sheer cliffs with the foaming Southern Ocean on your left and emerald slopes on your right—always pull into marked lookout bays before hopping out for photos.
d40fea05c8991db13878.tip: Apollo Bay's FoodWorks supermarket and seafront restaurants start shutting down around 19:30–20:00. If you want the town's famous scallop pie or a seafood dinner, drop your bags and head to eat by 18:00.
d40fea05c8991db13878.title: Stop at the Memorial Arch and Split Point Lighthouse, then spot wild koalas and parrots at Kennett River

d50363e7cefb3e6d585d.s: The Great Barrier Reef, Uluru, the Great Ocean Road—and an Aussie flat white.

d53f651679e2d7d89fe3.0: Mixing your physical credit card with the same card in Apple Pay at subway gates—OMNY treats them as two separate cards, costing you the $35 / 7-day fare cap.
d53f651679e2d7d89fe3.1: Staring down at your phone right along the yellow subway platform strip—always wait further back or with your back against a pillar and stay alert.
d53f651679e2d7d89fe3.2: Letting Times Square costumed characters pull you into a photo or accepting a stranger's 'free CD'—they'll surround you demanding a $20 cash tip seconds later. Wave off and keep moving.
d53f651679e2d7d89fe3.3: Booking The Met or observation decks without checking closure days and sunset slots—The Met closes Wednesdays, and last-minute observation tickets often leave only late-night times.

d54b8ff24cc60af4b0e2.cost: Maits Rest walk free; Cape Otway Lightstation entry about A$20
d54b8ff24cc60af4b0e2.paragraphs.0: Beyond Apollo Bay, the highway abruptly swings inland into the hills, trading sunlit surf for a towering canopy of Southern Hemisphere temperate rainforest. Cell reception vanishes completely here—your pre-downloaded offline maps immediately earn their keep.
d54b8ff24cc60af4b0e2.paragraphs.1: Spend 40 minutes walking the 800-meter wooden loop at Maits Rest Rainforest Walk: soaring mountain ash and giant three-meter tree ferns drip with velvety moss while morning mist and slanted shafts of sunlight make it feel prehistoric, with air crisp enough to bottle. Afterward, take the side spur down to mainland Australia's oldest surviving lighthouse at Cape Otway Lightstation—keep an eye on the eucalyptus lining the access road, another reliable wild koala hotspot.
d54b8ff24cc60af4b0e2.phase: Step 03 · Day 2 09:00 Into Great Otway temperate rainforest
d54b8ff24cc60af4b0e2.photo.alt: Lush Victorian hillside valleys and rugged inland landscapes near the Great Ocean Road
d54b8ff24cc60af4b0e2.photo.caption: Cutting inland from the ocean into Victoria's green hills and eucalyptus forest feels like stepping into a vast open-air oxygen bar.
d54b8ff24cc60af4b0e2.tip: The Otway side roads are narrow and twisty, with occasional fallen branches and wallabies darting out—cruise gently at 50–60 km/h, and pull into marked Slow Vehicle Turnouts whenever a line of locals builds behind you; they'll flash a friendly wave.
d54b8ff24cc60af4b0e2.title: Leave the coast for Jurassic fern forests: Maits Rest boardwalk & Cape Otway Lightstation

d6bb35ab96ca0232a3ad.0: [Golden overnight split] Spend Night 1 in the midpoint hub of Apollo Bay for groceries and fresh seafood, and Night 2 in Port Campbell—just 10 minutes from the Twelve Apostles, so you watch sunset without ever driving mountain curves in the dark.
d6bb35ab96ca0232a3ad.1: [Non-negotiable safety line] Never drive the Great Ocean Road or rural inland highways after 17:30. From dusk through late night, kangaroos and wombats frequently dart across the asphalt, totaling front ends and risking severe crashes.
d6bb35ab96ca0232a3ad.2: [Offline maps are mandatory] Mobile 4G/5G coverage drops to zero inside Great Otway National Park. Download the offline Google Maps area for southwest Victoria over Melbourne Wi-Fi before rolling out.
d6bb35ab96ca0232a3ad.3: [Four-seasons-in-a-day packing] Even in peak January summer, icy Southern Ocean gusts cut straight through a T-shirt. Keep a windproof shell jacket, high-SPF sunscreen, and sunglasses within reach in the car.

d7253a29367ff4553795.s: Click “Add to itinerary” next to a sight to add it here first.

d73a1e9210f7b6354b73.cost: About ¥6,200 (covered by the JR Takayama-Hokuriku Area Tourist Pass)
d73a1e9210f7b6354b73.duration: Limited Express Hida about 2 hours 25 minutes
d73a1e9210f7b6354b73.location: JR Takayama Station → Limited Express Hida → Nagoya Station (or Toyama for the Hokuriku Shinkansen)
d73a1e9210f7b6354b73.paragraphs.0: When leaving Takayama, board the sleek hybrid JR Limited Express Hida (HC85 series) southbound to Nagoya. Panoramic windows trace the winding Hida River gorge, framing snow-capped boulders against emerald rapids like an ink-wash scroll. From Nagoya Station, transferring to the Tokaido Shinkansen for Tokyo or Kyoto—or taking the Meitetsu train straight to Chubu Centrair International Airport for your flight home—is effortless.
d73a1e9210f7b6354b73.paragraphs.1: One final winter Hokuriku rule worth repeating: whether riding the Nohi Bus or the Limited Express Hida, whenever snow warnings are up, build at least a 1.5–2 hour buffer before onward Shinkansen or international flights. Never schedule snow-country transit on a summertime stopwatch.
d73a1e9210f7b6354b73.phase: Step 06 · Day 3 Afternoon exit: south to Nagoya or north to Kanazawa/Tokyo
d73a1e9210f7b6354b73.tip: Headed south toward Nagoya on the Limited Express Hida, seats on the left side (A/B) get the best views down the snowy Hida River gorge—just ask for a "window seat" on that side at the station ticket office.
d73a1e9210f7b6354b73.title: Ride the JR Limited Express Hida down snowy river gorges to Nagoya with a 1.5-hour buffer

d87158d56a4d34654923.access.0.how: Direct flights to Melbourne operate from Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Chengdu, Xiamen, Haikou, and other cities. The flight takes about 9.5–12 hours.
d87158d56a4d34654923.access.1.how: The flight takes about 1.5 hours, with frequent departures. Driving takes about 9 hours.
d87158d56a4d34654923.access.2.how: Flights to Hobart or Launceston take about 1–1.5 hours. You can also take the Spirit of Tasmania ferry from Geelong to Devonport, which takes about 10–11 hours.
d87158d56a4d34654923.access.3.how: The flight takes about 1 hour 15 minutes. Driving along the coast and the Great Ocean Road takes about 2–3 days.
d87158d56a4d34654923.cover.alt: The Twelve Apostles at golden sunset
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.0.name: Flat White
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.0.text: Melbourne's coffee culture is famous across Australia. A flat white is espresso topped with a thin layer of velvety microfoam. It has less milk and a stronger coffee flavor than a latte. Many independent cafes roast their own beans, and menus list the beans' origins and tasting notes. Order a single origin to taste beans from a specific estate.
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.0.where: Independent cafes in the city-center laneways, Fitzroy, and Collingwood
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.1.name: Hot Jam Doughnuts
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.1.text: This signature snack from the old food truck outside Queen Victoria Market has been sold for decades. The dough is fried to order, rolled in white sugar, and filled with scalding red jam. The jam can burn you, so wait half a minute before taking a bite. Joining the line on a market day is practically a Melbourne ritual.
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.1.where: The old food truck outside Queen Victoria Market, open on market days
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.2.name: Souvlaki
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.2.text: Melbourne has one of the largest Greek communities outside Greece, and Greek food is a local staple. Sliced grilled lamb or chicken with onion, tomato, and tzatziki is wrapped in pita for a full meal. Having one after a night of drinking is a long-standing local tradition.
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.2.where: Greek restaurants around Lonsdale Street in the city center and in Oakleigh
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.3.name: Chicken Parma
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.3.text: This classic Australian pub dish is a Melbourne favorite: a large breaded chicken breast is fried until crisp, then topped with tomato sauce, ham, and melted cheese. It comes with fries and salad. The portions are large, and one serving is often more than one person can finish. Many old pubs offer a weekly Parma night at a special price.
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.3.where: Traditional pubs in the city center and inner suburbs
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.4.name: Yarra Valley Pinot Noir
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.4.text: The Yarra Valley's cool climate produces light-colored Pinot Noir with delicate fruit, cherry notes, and hints of forest. Its Chardonnay and sparkling wines are also excellent. Winery tastings usually charge a small fee that can be credited toward a purchase. Add a cheese platter to a vineyard lunch for a classic Yarra Valley day.
d87158d56a4d34654923.foods.4.where: Tasting rooms and restaurants at Yarra Valley wineries
d87158d56a4d34654923.intro.0: Victoria is compact, but its highlights are close together. Melbourne is one of Australia's best cities for food and coffee. In 2–3 hours by car, you can reach the Twelve Apostles on the Great Ocean Road, the Penguin Parade on Phillip Island, and the mountains of Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park. It suits travelers who enjoy city life but also want to drive along the coast.
d87158d56a4d34654923.intro.1: Melbourne itself is worth 2–3 days. Spend the day exploring laneways in the city center, drinking coffee and admiring street art, then visit Queen Victoria Market and NGV International. In the evening, head to Phillip Island for the penguins. Allow 2 days for the Great Ocean Road. Stay overnight in Apollo Bay or Port Campbell, then visit the Twelve Apostles early the next morning for smaller crowds and better light.
d87158d56a4d34654923.intro.2: With another 2–3 days, visit wineries and wildlife sanctuaries in the Yarra Valley. Or head northwest to Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park to hike among the mountains and see kangaroos, or southeast to Wilsons Promontory National Park for wombats and white-sand beaches. Outside Melbourne, you will generally need to drive or join a tour. Public transportation only reaches the towns.
d87158d56a4d34654923.name: Victoria
d87158d56a4d34654923.seasons.note: Days are long from November–April, making this a good time for the Great Ocean Road. January is the busiest month because of the summer holidays. June–August is cool, cloudy, and rainy, while December–February is bushfire season.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.0.name: Melbourne Laneways & Hosier Lane
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.0.text: Some of Melbourne's best spots are hidden in the city's laneways. Across from Federation Square, Hosier Lane is covered in street art, with new work appearing almost every week. Degraves Street is packed with cafes and small restaurants, while the nearby arcades are 19th-century shopping galleries with glass roofs. Take your time with a coffee, then explore another laneway. Half a day goes quickly.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.0.tip: Trams are free within the free tram zone. Ride and hop off as you explore.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.1.name: Queen Victoria Market
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.1.text: This open-air market has been running for more than 140 years. The meat and seafood halls and deli section are housed in historic buildings, while long rows of stalls outside sell fruit, vegetables, groceries, and souvenirs. Come in the morning for a hot jam doughnut and coffee, then buy cheese and fruit for a picnic. Some Wednesday nights in summer and winter feature lively night markets with food stalls and live music.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.1.tip: The market is closed on Mondays and Wednesdays. Saturdays are the busiest, and fruit and vegetables are often discounted near closing time.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.2.name: NGV International
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.2.text: Australia's oldest and most visited art museum has free permanent exhibitions. The entrance features a glass wall of flowing water, while the main hall has a vast stained-glass ceiling that many visitors simply lie on the floor to admire. The collection ranges from European Old Masters to contemporary design. Australian and First Nations art is displayed at The Ian Potter Centre in Federation Square.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.2.tip: Open daily from 10:00–17:00. Large backpacks must be checked. Special exhibitions charge an additional fee.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.3.name: Great Ocean Road
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.3.text: Stretching about 240 kilometers from Torquay to near Warrnambool, this coastal road was built by World War I veterans. The first section follows cliffs and bays. Look for wild koalas in the eucalyptus trees around the Memorial Arch, Lorne, and Kennett River. Beyond Apollo Bay, the road turns through the Otway rainforest before reaching the sea stacks around the Twelve Apostles. Don't try to do it all in one day. An overnight stay makes the trip much more relaxed.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.3.tip: The road has many curves and narrow sections. Drive slowly on the left and park only at designated viewpoints. Watch for kangaroos crossing after dusk.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.4.name: Twelve Apostles & Loch Ard Gorge
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.4.text: These limestone sea stacks rise from the Southern Ocean. Fewer than twelve remain, and the waves continue to erode them. From the visitor center parking lot, take the underpass to the cliff-top viewing platforms. A few minutes west by car, Loch Ard Gorge marks the site where an immigrant ship sank in 1878. You can walk down to the small beach below the gorge, but do not enter the water. Helicopter flights also offer views from above.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.4.tip: Visit around sunrise or sunset for the best light and fewer tour groups. A new visitor center is under construction; follow the signs on site.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.5.name: Penguin Parade, Phillip Island
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.5.text: The world's smallest penguins come ashore in groups after sunset, waddling across the beach to their burrows in the dunes. The main viewing stands sit beside the beach, with closer underground viewing rooms and small-group tours also available. Phillip Island is about 2 hours by car from Melbourne. The Penguin Parade is often combined with the island's koala sanctuary and The Nobbies in a full-day trip.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.5.tip: Photography and filming are prohibited throughout the experience, including with phones. Book ahead for December–January and holidays. Bring a warm jacket because it can be cold and windy by the sea at night.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.6.name: Puffing Billy Railway
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.6.text: This century-old narrow-gauge steam railway departs from Belgrave at the foot of the Dandenong Ranges east of Melbourne. It passes through tall mountain ash forest and fern-filled valleys, crossing a wooden trestle bridge along the way. Children especially enjoy leaning out of the open-window carriages to feel the breeze and look at the forest. You can ride to Lakeside and back, then have afternoon tea in a Dandenong Ranges town.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.6.tip: The train from Flinders Street to Belgrave takes about 1 hour. Book ahead for weekends and holidays. On total fire ban days, services may switch to diesel trains or stop running.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.7.name: Yarra Valley
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.7.text: About 1 hour northeast of Melbourne, this cool-climate wine region is covered in rolling vineyards. It is best known for Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, and sparkling wine. Wine tastings and lunch at a winery are the classic way to visit, and hot-air balloon rides at dawn offer sunrise views. Nearby Healesville Sanctuary specializes in native Australian animals. Its platypuses and bird-of-prey flight shows are both worth seeing.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.7.tip: If you plan to drink, join a wine tour or hire a private car. The sanctuary is open daily from 9:00–17:00.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.8.name: Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.8.text: About 3 hours northwest of Melbourne, a line of sandstone ridges rises suddenly from the plains. Stay in Halls Gap at the foot of the ranges, where kangaroos often gather on the grass in the morning and evening. The classic hike climbs to the Pinnacle lookout for views across the valley. Boroka and Reed lookouts are accessible by car. Wildflowers are at their best in September–October, and Brambuk: The National Park & Cultural Centre shares stories of the area's First Nations people.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.8.tip: MacKenzie Falls is closed for construction from February 2026 through the end of the year. Some trails remain closed after the 2024–25 bushfires. Check park notices before setting out.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.9.name: Wilsons Promontory National Park
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.9.text: The southernmost point of mainland Australia is about 3 hours southeast of Melbourne. Granite boulders are scattered across white-sand beaches, and the fine sand at Squeaky Beach really does squeak underfoot. Wombats, kangaroos, and emus are often seen around Tidal River campground at dusk. If you're fit, climb Mount Oberon for panoramic views of the peninsula and its bays. The scenery is especially beautiful at sunset.
d87158d56a4d34654923.spots.9.tip: Campgrounds fill up early in December–January and on long weekends. There are no gas stations or large supermarkets on the peninsula, so stock up before entering.
d87158d56a4d34654923.stay: For a first visit, stay in Melbourne's city center or Southbank, where the free tram zone makes it easy to walk or take public transportation. On the Great Ocean Road, spend a night in Apollo Bay or Port Campbell. In Grampians (Gariwerd), stay in Halls Gap. The Yarra Valley is easy to visit as a day trip.
d87158d56a4d34654923.tagline: Coffee laneways, the Great Ocean Road, and little penguins
d87158d56a4d34654923.tips.0: Melbourne can have four seasons in one day. Even January temperatures can suddenly drop into the teens, so carry a jacket.
d87158d56a4d34654923.tips.1: Trams are free within the city-center free tram zone. Outside the zone, tap on with a myki. Check the stop sign before boarding.
d87158d56a4d34654923.tips.2: Drive on the left. Licence and translation requirements depend on where your licence was issued; check VicRoads for the current rules.
d87158d56a4d34654923.tips.3: The Great Ocean Road's beaches have strong currents. Swim only between the red and yellow flags where lifeguards are present, and never cross barriers at cliff-top viewpoints.
d87158d56a4d34654923.tips.4: Bushfire season runs from December–February. Check VicEmergency for fires and road closures before setting out. On total fire ban days, lighting fires is prohibited.

d9228921cd2ac12789ec.for: First-time visitors to Hokkaido who want to escape the heat and see flower fields in summer
d9228921cd2ac12789ec.season: Late June to early August; mid-July is best
d9228921cd2ac12789ec.summary: Use Sapporo as your base: take it easy in Sapporo and Otaru, then ride the JR to Furano and Biei to see the lavender fields and Blue Pond. Stop by Asahiyama Zoo along the way, then relax in a hot spring in Jozankei on the final night. The whole trip uses JR trains and buses, so you won't need to drive. The Sapporo–Furano Area Pass covers most of the fares.
d9228921cd2ac12789ec.title: Hokkaido summer · 6 days

d9cf295086a68f01dbac.cost: Point Lobos parking $10 / vehicle; roadside overlooks free
d9cf295086a68f01dbac.location: Carmel → Point Lobos → Hurricane Point → Bixby Creek Bridge
d9cf295086a68f01dbac.paragraphs.0: Leave Carmel at 09:00 and drive 10 minutes south to Point Lobos State Natural Reserve—its sea otters and emerald coves look almost unreal, and arriving early secures parking. Moments later, the highway rockets onto hundred-meter headlands and delivers you straight into the heart of Big Sur.
d9cf295086a68f01dbac.paragraphs.1: Two minutes before Bixby Bridge, pull into the generous turnout at Hurricane Point: looking back over the snaking cliffside road and exploding surf gives you the safest, widest vista on the north coast. When you reach iconic Bixby Creek Bridge, watch closely for red No Parking signs. Highway patrol strictly enforces the narrow bridge shoulders and Old Coast Road entrance to prevent gridlock and crashes—park only in the striped viewing turnout on the north side, or cross to a legal turnout south of the bridge to loop back rather than risking an angled stop on a yellow line.
d9cf295086a68f01dbac.phase: Step 02 · Day 2 09:00 northern Big Sur highlights
d9cf295086a68f01dbac.photo.alt: Steaming clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl by the ocean in Monterey
d9cf295086a68f01dbac.photo.caption: Don't pass Monterey's Fisherman's Wharf without a steaming sourdough bread bowl of clam chowder—it's pure comfort after hours in the ocean breeze.
d9cf295086a68f01dbac.tip: Even when Highway 1 is open end-to-end, Big Sur often keeps 1–2 slope-stabilization zones under timed traffic signals with alternating one-way flow. Expect 10–15 minute waits at each light—just relax, turn up your playlist, and watch the waves.
d9cf295086a68f01dbac.title: Take in the sweep from Hurricane Point and photograph Bixby Bridge legally without earning a ticket

dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.access.0.how: About 25 minutes to Fukui on the Hokuriku Shinkansen
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.access.1.how: About 3 hours direct to Fukui on the Hokuriku Shinkansen
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.access.2.how: Take the limited express Thunderbird to Tsuruga, then transfer to the Hokuriku Shinkansen; about 1 hour 50 minutes total to Fukui
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.access.3.how: The closest airport to Fukui. Take a bus to Komatsu Station, then transfer to the Hokuriku Shinkansen to Fukui
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.0.name: Echizen crab
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.0.price: Whole male crabs are often sold at market price; paying more than ¥10,000 for one is common
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.0.text: Male snow crab caught in Fukui, identified by a yellow tag attached to its leg. The season opens in early November. It is delicious boiled, grilled, or in a hot pot. Female crab, known as Seiko crab, is much cheaper but has a shorter season.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.0.where: Ryokan and restaurants around Awara Onsen, Mikuni Port, and Echizen Town
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.1.name: Echizen grated daikon soba
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.1.text: Cold soba topped with spicy grated daikon sauce, bonito flakes, and scallions. The daikon's sharp bite makes the noodles especially refreshing and is a staple of Fukui cuisine.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.1.where: Soba shops around Eiheiji, Maruoka, and central Fukui
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.2.name: Sauce katsudon
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.2.text: Fukui's version of katsudon: a thin pork cutlet coated in fine breadcrumbs and fried until crisp, then dipped in sweet Worcestershire-style sauce and served over rice without an egg.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.2.where: Long-established yoshoku restaurants around Fukui Station and downtown
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.3.name: Heshiko preserved mackerel
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.3.text: Mackerel from the Wakasa region cured in rice bran and salt for more than a year, with a rich, salty flavor. Slice it thin, grill it lightly, and serve it with white rice or ochazuke. It also goes well with drinks.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.foods.3.where: Diners and souvenir shops around Obama and the Mikata Five Lakes
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.intro.0: Fukui lies between Kanazawa and Kyoto and was once a place many travelers simply passed through by train. Since the Hokuriku Shinkansen extension to Tsuruga opened in 2024, Fukui is much easier to reach: about 25 minutes from Kanazawa and about 3 hours direct from Tokyo. Dinosaur statues fill the area around Fukui Station because most of Japan's dinosaur fossils have been found here.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.intro.1: The three best reasons to make a special trip are Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum in Katsuyama, Eiheiji Temple in the mountains, and the Tojinbo Cliffs on the Sea of Japan. They lie in different directions, so you can visit at most two in one day using the Echizen Railway and buses. In winter, save the evening for Echizen crab and stay in Awara Onsen.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.name: Fukui
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.seasons.note: Echizen crab season runs from the opening of the fishing season in early November through March; Eiheiji is best for fall colors in November and snowy scenery in January–February; Maruoka Castle's cherry blossoms bloom in early April.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.sources.0.title: Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum admission tickets
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.sources.1.title: Eiheiji Temple official website
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.sources.2.title: JR West Hokuriku Area Pass
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.0.name: Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.0.text: One of the world's three major dinosaur museums, housed in a silver, egg-shaped building filled with dozens of dinosaur skeletons. A Tyrannosaurus robot moves and roars at the entrance. Adults and children can easily spend 2–3 hours here. From Fukui Station, take the Echizen Railway Katsuyama Eiheiji Line to the last stop, Katsuyama, in about 1 hour, then take a bus for about 15 minutes.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.0.tip: Timed admission tickets should generally be bought in advance. Tickets go on sale 60 days ahead. Same-day tickets are sold at the museum only if spots remain.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.1.name: Eiheiji Temple
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.1.text: The head temple of the Soto school of Zen, founded by Dogen in 1244. More than 100 monks still train here. More than 70 buildings line the mountainside, linked by long wooden corridors. You may see monks moving between buildings during your visit. The ceiling in the Eihei-ji Temple's Eten-no-Ma room is painted with more than 200 bird-and-flower paintings.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.1.tip: You must remove your shoes and walk on wooden floors, so wear thick socks in winter. From Fukui Station, the Eiheiji Liner bus takes about 30 minutes.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.2.name: Tojinbo Cliffs
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.2.text: These columnar-rock cliffs stretch for about 1 kilometer along the Sea of Japan. The highest points are more than 20 meters above the waves below. Walk along the cliff tops or take a boat tour from the water. The cliffs are especially beautiful at sunset, when the sun sinks into the Sea of Japan. From Awaraonsen Station, take a bus for about 40 minutes, or take the Echizen Railway to Mikuni Minato and transfer.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.2.tip: There are no guardrails along the cliffs. Rocks are slippery in strong winds and after rain, so stay away from the edge.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.3.name: Ichijodani Asakura Clan Ruins
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.3.text: This castle town belonged to the Sengoku-period Asakura clan. After Oda Nobunaga burned it down in 1573, it lay buried beneath farmland for 400 years. Excavations uncovered a restored section of samurai residences and merchant streets that feels like a Sengoku film set. The museum next to Ichijodani Station displays excavated artifacts and a full-scale reconstruction of the Asakura residence. The restored streets are a little farther away. From Fukui Station, the JR Kuzuryu Line takes about 15 minutes.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.3.tip: The Kuzuryu Line may have only one train every 1–2 hours, so check the return schedule first.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.4.name: Maruoka Castle
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.4.text: One of Japan's 12 surviving original castle keeps. It is small, with a simple appearance and a roof covered in stone tiles. About 400 cherry trees bloom on the castle hill in early April, and the grounds are lit up at night. When the mist is heavy, the whole castle seems to float above the clouds, earning it the nickname “Kasumi Castle.” Take a bus from Fukui Station or Awaraonsen Station.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.4.tip: The stairs inside the keep are extremely steep, and you must climb while holding a rope. Wear comfortable walking shoes.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.5.name: Mikata Five Lakes
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.5.text: Five connected lakes beside Wakasa Bay, each with a different salt concentration and a different shade of blue. From the mountaintop park, you can see all five lakes and the Sea of Japan. Take a cable car or chairlift to the top. The lakes are in the Wakasa region of southwestern Fukui, far from central Fukui and more convenient to visit from Tsuruga or the Kansai area.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.5.tip: The lake views from the mountaintop park are best on a clear day. Public transportation is limited, so consider joining a local sightseeing tour.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.6.name: Awara Onsen
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.6.text: Fukui's largest hot-spring town, with more than 100 years of history and many large ryokan. In winter, many hotels offer Echizen crab meal plans. Close to both Tojinbo and Maruoka Castle, it makes a convenient base for seaside sightseeing and crab meals. The Hokuriku Shinkansen stops at Awaraonsen Station, while the hot-spring district is near Awara Yunomachi Station on the Echizen Railway.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.spots.6.tip: The Shinkansen station and hot-spring district are some distance apart. Take a bus, taxi, or the Echizen Railway.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.stay: Stay near Fukui Station, where the Shinkansen, Echizen Railway, and buses to Eiheiji depart. For hot springs and crab, stay in Awara Onsen, which is close to Tojinbo.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.tagline: Dinosaur fossils, a major Zen temple, and Echizen crab in winter
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.tips.0: The Echizen Railway is a private railway and is not covered by JR passes. You need it to reach the dinosaur museum and Eiheiji.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.tips.1: Tickets for the dinosaur museum often sell out early during peak season and on weekends. Buy them once your date is set.
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.tips.2: Echizen crab prices vary by size and grade. Ask the price before ordering, and do not order immediately just because the menu says “market price.”
dc2a6b08bd515fd86b65.tips.3: Your driver's license may not be valid for driving in Japan. Check the requirements for your license with an official source. Because Fukui's sights are spread out, a local sightseeing bus may be a better option.

e0fc18c60050d7b086eb.location: Kyoto Municipal Subway Tozai Line · Keage Station Exit 1
e0fc18c60050d7b086eb.paragraphs.0: During peak foliage, lines for Higashiyama-bound buses like Routes 5 and 100 outside Kyoto Station stretch three buses deep before 08:00, only to crawl along Gojo-zaka and Higashiyama-dori. From Kyoto Station or Shijo-Karasuma, ride the Karasuma Line to Karasuma Oike, switch to the Tozai Line to Keage Station, take Exit 1, and stroll through the historic Nejiri Manpo twisted brick tunnel straight to Nanzen-ji's edge.
e0fc18c60050d7b086eb.paragraphs.1: At 07:30, eastern Kyoto's tree-lined lanes belong almost entirely to local joggers and a handful of early-bird photographers. Grab a hot canned corn soup from a convenience store near your hotel or Keage Station to warm your hands, take a leisurely 12–15 minute walk north, and you'll claim a front-of-the-line spot at Eikando's ticket gate by 07:45.
e0fc18c60050d7b086eb.phase: Step 01 · 07:20 Subway past the morning gridlock
e0fc18c60050d7b086eb.tip: Late-November dawns in Kyoto sit around 5–7°C, and wooden temple corridors turn ice-cold once your shoes come off. Wear thick socks (or stick-on toe warmers) and slip-on shoes—save the tall lace-up boots for another day so you aren't holding up the line at the entrance.
e0fc18c60050d7b086eb.title: Ditch the city bus: take the Tozai Line to Keage Station and walk into crisp eastern Kyoto

e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.access.0.how: The JR Rapid Airport train takes as little as 37 minutes to Sapporo Station and costs about ¥1,230. A reserved seat in the u-seat car costs about ¥1,000 extra.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.access.1.how: Flying from Haneda to New Chitose takes about 1.5 hours and is the easiest option. You can also take the Shinkansen to Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto, which takes as little as about 4 hours.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.access.2.how: Otaru is about 35–45 minutes by JR; Asahikawa is about 1.5 hours by limited express; Hakodate is about 3.5–4 hours by limited express.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.0.name: Jingisukan grilled lamb
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.0.text: Hokkaido-style grilled lamb cooked on a domed iron pan. The rendered fat runs down and helps braise the vegetables. The lamb has little gamey flavor. Your clothes will smell afterward, and restaurants usually provide plastic bags for coats.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.0.where: Specialty restaurants around Susukino in Sapporo; Sapporo Beer Garden
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.1.name: Soup curry
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.1.text: A thin curry broth served with a whole chicken leg and large pieces of roasted vegetables. You can choose the spice level and broth. This Sapporo-born dish is served at many restaurants, each with its own style. Medium spice is a good starting point.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.1.where: Central Sapporo and around Hokkaido University
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.2.name: Seafood rice bowl
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.2.text: Uni, salmon roe, crab, and scallops piled over rice. Market restaurants tend to charge tourists more, so check the "market price" label before ordering. Uni is usually best in summer.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.2.where: Hakodate Morning Market, Nijo Market in Sapporo, and Otaru Sankaku Market
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.3.name: Sapporo miso ramen
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.3.text: A rich miso broth with thick, curly noodles. A layer of oil on top keeps it hot, making it especially filling in winter. Asahikawa is known for soy sauce ramen and Hakodate for lighter salt ramen, so try a bowl in each city for comparison.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.3.where: Sapporo Ramen Alley and neighborhoods across the city
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.4.name: Milk soft serve
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.4.text: Hokkaido has many dairy farms, and the soft serve sold at farms and flower fields is especially rich and milky. Furano also has lavender and melon flavors. People eat it while walking even in winter.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.foods.4.where: Farms and roadside rest areas in Furano and Biei
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.intro.0: Hokkaido covers more than one-fifth of Japan, and cities can be 200–300 km apart. Don't try to see it all in one trip. A common plan is to base yourself in Sapporo and add one or two of Otaru, Furano and Biei, or Hakodate. Save Shiretoko and Kushiro in eastern Hokkaido for a dedicated second trip.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.intro.1: Summer (June–August) is cool, with lavender and flower fields as the main draw. It's ideal for escaping the heat and taking photos. Winter (December–February) brings lots of dry snow, making the Snow Festival, skiing, and hot springs especially appealing. Days are short and roads get icy, so keep your schedule light. Spring and fall are less busy. Autumn colors begin in Daisetsuzan in late September.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.intro.2: Food is half the reason to visit Hokkaido: seafood rice bowls, crab, soup curry, jingisukan grilled lamb, miso ramen, and rich milk ice cream. The milk and cheese at supermarkets are also worth trying.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.name: Hokkaido
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.seasons.note: Lavender peaks in early to mid-July, and the Snow Festival takes place in early February. June and September are less crowded and cheaper. Don't overpack your winter itinerary.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.sources.0.title: JR Hokkaido · New Chitose Airport to Sapporo (Rapid Airport)
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.sources.2.title: Hakodate Tourism Information · Mount Hakodate transportation guide
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.sources.3.title: HOKKAIDO LOVE! · Shiretoko Five Lakes
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.sources.4.title: Asahiyama Zoo, Asahikawa · Opening periods and admission
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.0.name: Odori Park
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.0.text: A long east–west park in central Sapporo. It has flower beds and a beer festival in summer and hosts the main Snow Festival site in winter. You don't need to set aside much time for it; a walk through is enough. You can go up the TV Tower at the eastern end for city views. The 2027 Snow Festival runs from February 4–11, so book your hotel two or three months ahead.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.0.tip: The Snow Festival is prettiest at night when the lights are on, but it gets crowded. Watch for ice underfoot.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.1.name: Otaru Canal
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.1.text: The canal is lined with stone warehouses built more than 100 years ago, now converted into restaurants and shops. The canal itself is short; 20 minutes is enough for photos. The main attraction is browsing the glass shops, music box stores, and dessert shops along Sakaimachi Street. In February, the Snow Light Path fills the canal and streets with small candles.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.1.tip: Otaru makes an easy day trip from Sapporo. The canal looks best after the gas lamps come on at dusk.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.2.name: Farm Tomita
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.2.text: Furano's best-known lavender farm. The fields are at their most vivid in early to mid-July, with rows of colorful flowers nearby. Admission is free, and almost everyone gets a lavender ice cream. It's not far from JR Naka-Furano Station and is reachable on foot or by taxi. Outside flower season, there is little to see.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.2.tip: Weekends in July are very busy. Arrive before 9 a.m. for a more relaxed visit. The purple color fades noticeably after August.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.3.name: Shirogane Blue Pond
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.3.text: A small pond in the Biei mountains, dotted with dead trees. Minerals in the water give it a blue color, most visible around noon on a sunny day. It looks greener on cloudy days. The pond is small; 20 minutes is enough to walk around it. It is illuminated at night in winter and can be visited with nearby Shirahige Falls.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.3.tip: The Dohoku Bus takes a little over 20 minutes from Biei Station. Services are infrequent, so check the return schedule first.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.4.name: Asahiyama Zoo
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.4.text: A municipal zoo known for its animal behavior exhibits. Penguins swim through a waterway over your head, and polar bears plunge into the water right in front of the glass. After snow falls in winter, penguins take walks outside, drawing long lines. The zoo is built on a hillside with plenty of slopes, so wear comfortable shoes.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.4.tip: The zoo closes for a period in both spring and fall. Winter hours are short, so check the opening calendar before you go.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.5.name: Mount Hakodate night view
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.5.text: The sea squeezes Hakodate's city center into a narrow waist. From the summit, it looks like a glowing fan. The ropeway takes about 3 minutes to reach the top. Go up 30 minutes before sunset to get a spot, then watch the sky darken before the city lights come on. The summit is very windy in winter, so bring a hat and gloves.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.5.tip: Private cars cannot go up in the evening, and the mountain road closes completely in winter. The ropeway is the most reliable option.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.6.name: Goryokaku
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.6.text: A Western-style star-shaped fortress built at the end of the Edo period. Its shape is hard to see from the ground, so go up the nearby Goryokaku Tower for the full five-pointed star. Cherry trees line the moat and bloom from late April to early May. The reconstructed Hakodate Magistrate's Office inside the park is also worth visiting.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.6.tip: The tower requires a separate ticket. Visit early in the morning during cherry blossom season for the fewest people.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.7.name: Noboribetsu Jigokudani
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.7.text: This volcanic crater is filled with rising steam and a strong sulfur smell. A 15-minute walk on the boardwalk covers the main sights. Afterward, soak in the hot spring district. Noboribetsu has several types of mineral-rich water, and many hotels accept non-guests for bathing. Direct buses run from Sapporo and New Chitose Airport, making it a good place to add a night at a hot spring.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.7.tip: The trail from Jigokudani to Oyunuma takes about 30–40 minutes and passes a natural footbath.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.8.name: Shiretoko Five Lakes
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.8.text: Five pristine forest lakes on the Shiretoko Peninsula, a World Natural Heritage site. The free 800-meter elevated boardwalk is unaffected by brown bear activity. To take the ground trails around all five lakes, you need a paid guide from May 10 to July 31. At other times, attend a lecture lasting about 10 minutes first. The area closes in winter.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.8.tip: Eastern Hokkaido is hard to get around. From Memanbetsu Airport or Shiretoko-Shari Station, joining a tour is the easiest option.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.9.name: Jozankei Onsen
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.9.text: A hot spring valley within Sapporo. It's about 1 hour by road from the city center, making it a good choice if you want to stay at a hot spring ryokan without going far. The hills turn red in early to mid-October, and you can walk around the Futami Suspension Bridge area. In winter, soaking in an outdoor bath surrounded by snow is especially relaxing.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.spots.9.tip: The reservation-only Kappa Liner runs directly from Sapporo Station. Online bookings come with a discount.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.stay: For a first visit, stay near Sapporo Station, Odori, or Susukino for easy access to transport and food. Stay one night in Furano, Biei, or Asahikawa when visiting the Furano–Biei area. Give Hakodate 1–2 nights of its own.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.tagline: Flower fields in summer, snow-viewing hot springs in winter, and great food year-round
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.tips.0: Whether you can drive in Japan depends on your licence and the required documents. Check the official rules. Biei and eastern Hokkaido have limited bus service, so you can join a local day-tour bus.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.tips.1: Winter sidewalks can be dangerously slippery. Buy slip-on traction cleats for your shoes; convenience stores and drugstores often sell them.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.tips.2: The Furano–Biei Norokko train stopped operating in September 2026. Use regular trains or buses to reach the flower fields.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.tips.3: Cities are far apart. The limited express from Sapporo to Hakodate takes about 3.5–4 hours one way, so don't cross between two major cities in one day.
e111f1d8e0a0b2667f88.tips.4: If you're visiting only Sapporo, Otaru, and Furano–Biei, the Sapporo–Furano 4-day regional pass is better value than the nationwide Hokkaido pass.

e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.0.items.0.note: A taxi from Honolulu Airport to Waikiki takes about 30–40 minutes
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.0.move: Fly to Honolulu with a connection in Tokyo, Seoul, or the U.S. mainland
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.0.title: Arrive in Waikiki
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.1.move: The two sites are about a 15-minute drive apart. Rent a car for the day or take a taxi
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.1.title: Diamond Head and Hanauma Bay
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.2.move: Waikiki to Pearl Harbor takes about 30 minutes, and Pearl Harbor to the North Shore takes about 45 minutes. Renting a car is recommended
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.2.title: Pearl Harbor and the North Shore
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.3.items.0.note: Fly to Kahului on Maui in the morning, pick up your car, and drive to Kihei to check in
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.3.items.2.note: Go to bed early; leave around 3 a.m. the next morning to drive up the mountain
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.3.move: The flight from Honolulu to Maui takes about 40 minutes; Kahului to Kihei takes about 20 minutes
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.3.title: Fly to Maui
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.4.items.1.note: Stop in a highland town for brunch on the way down, then return to the hotel for an afternoon nap
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.4.move: Kihei to the summit takes about 2 hours. The road has many curves, so drive slowly at night
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.4.title: Haleakala sunrise
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.5.items.1.note: Return the same way and leave the mountain roads before dark

e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.5.title: Road to Hana
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.6.items.0.note: Spend the morning snorkeling or swimming at a beach in Kihei or Wailea
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.6.items.2.note: Fly home from Kahului Airport with a connection in Honolulu or on the U.S. mainland
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.6.move: Kihei to Kahului Airport takes about 20 minutes; allow plenty of time to return the car
e1b212d0921483366ca4.days.6.title: A half-day at the beach, then head home
e1b212d0921483366ca4.for: First-time visitors to Hawaii who want to experience beaches, volcanoes, and a road trip
e1b212d0921483366ca4.season: Year-round; best value in April–May and September–October
e1b212d0921483366ca4.summary: Stay in Waikiki for the first three days. Group Diamond Head, Hanauma Bay, and Pearl Harbor, which require reservations, into the itinerary. Spend the first day by the beach and recovering from jet lag. Fly to Maui and pick up a car on day four. Head up before midnight on day five to watch the Haleakala sunrise, then drive the Road to Hana on day six. Book the reservations based on Hawaii time, then set your dates; Hanauma Bay is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays, so don't schedule it for day two if it falls on either of those days.
e1b212d0921483366ca4.title: Oahu and Maui, Hawaii · 7 days

e2127e0c1d03556e6866.0: [Golden booking window] Japan Bus Online and Highwaybus.com open seats exactly 1 month before travel at 10:00 JST (09:00 UTC+8). Winter departures from Kanazawa at 08:40 and 09:40, and afternoon departures from Shirakawa-go at 14:30 and 15:30, vanish in minutes.
e2127e0c1d03556e6866.1: [JR Pass reservation catch] The JR Takayama-Hokuriku Area Tourist Pass covers the bus fare, but you still cannot skip reservations and line up to board. During peak winter, call the Nohi Bus reservation center on release day—or simply pay just over two thousand yen online to lock in your seat stress-free.
e2127e0c1d03556e6866.2: [Snow-delay rule of thumb] Heavy blizzards frequently trigger speed restrictions or temporary closures along the Hokuriku and Tokai-Hokuriku Expressways. Delays of 1–2 hours are common, so never schedule a tight Shinkansen transfer or dinner booking right after leaving Shirakawa-go.
e2127e0c1d03556e6866.3: [Illumination days play by different rules] On Shirakawa-go's handful of winter light-up nights, strict village-wide traffic controls shut down regular afternoon buses; only travelers who win official light-up tickets or lodging months in advance may stay after dark.

e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.access.0.how: There are no direct flights. Fly to Sydney or Melbourne first (about 9–12 hours), then take a domestic flight or drive from Sydney.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.access.1.how: About 3 hours by car; about 50 minutes by plane; long-distance buses also take about 3–3.5 hours.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.access.2.how: About 1 hour 10 minutes by plane; about 7–8 hours by car.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.cover.alt: Canberra's central axis from Mount Ainslie
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.foods.0.name: Canberra Region Black Truffles
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.foods.0.text: Cold winters and suitable soil make the Canberra region an important black truffle area in Australia. The harvest runs from June–August. Restaurants offer truffle menus, and nearby farms let you follow dogs into the woods to search for truffles. Anything you find can be sliced fresh over scrambled eggs or pasta.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.foods.0.where: Seasonal menus at city restaurants from June–August; nearby truffle farms
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.foods.1.name: Canberra District Wine
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.foods.1.text: The Canberra region's high elevation and large temperature swings produce crisp, lemony Riesling. Shiraz blended with a little Viognier is another local specialty. Most wineries are around Murrumbateman, north of the city, about a 30–40-minute drive away. The tasting rooms are small, and you may get to chat with the winemaker.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.foods.1.where: Winery tasting rooms around Murrumbateman north of the city
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.foods.2.name: Dickson Asian Eateries
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.foods.2.text: Woolley Street in Dickson, north of the city, is Canberra's Chinatown. Chinese, Vietnamese, Malaysian, and Korean restaurants sit side by side, with better prices than in the city center. It's the ideal place when you're tired of Western food, and many restaurants stay open relatively late.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.intro.0: The Australian Capital Territory is essentially Canberra: a capital built from scratch to a master plan in the last century, with Parliament, national museums, and galleries arranged around artificial Lake Burley Griffin. The city is quiet, with little traffic, and feels completely different from Sydney or Melbourne.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.intro.1: It suits anyone interested in history, politics, or art, as well as families visiting the science museum. Parliament House, the war memorial, and the National Gallery are all free, and you can see two or three in a day. Spend another half a day in a reserve outside the city to see kangaroos and koalas. Two days is enough. If you're driving from Sydney, you can add Jervis Bay on the South Coast along the way.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.intro.2: Canberra sits on an inland plateau, so the seasons are more pronounced than on the coast: deciduous trees turn yellow and red across the city in March–April, mornings often bring frost in June–August, and December–February is hot and dry. Public transport is limited, so taxis or a rental car are the fastest way to get between sights.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.name: Australian Capital Territory
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.seasons.note: March–April has the best fall colors; Floriade runs from mid-September to mid-October; early mornings and evenings are often around 0 °C in June–August.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.0.name: Australian Parliament House
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.0.text: Built into a hill, Australian Parliament House has a broad grass-covered roof topped by a huge stainless-steel flagpole. Entry is free. After security, you can explore the halls and art collection on your own or join a free short tour held daily. When Parliament is sitting, you can enter the public gallery to watch Question Time in the House of Representatives. It's even livelier than on TV.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.0.tip: Check the sitting calendar on the official website. Entry security is similar to airport security, so don't bring knives.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.1.name: Australian War Memorial
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.1.text: Part memorial and part museum, it covers Australia's military history from Gallipoli in World War I to peacekeeping missions, using aircraft, tanks, and full-scale models. The most moving experience is the Last Post Ceremony held before closing each day. It tells the story of one fallen service member and ends with a bugle call. Anzac Parade runs straight from the memorial toward Parliament House across the lake.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.1.tip: The ceremony takes place in the Commemorative Courtyard at 16:30 each day. Arrive 15 minutes early. Some galleries are being renovated.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.2.name: National Gallery of Australia
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.2.text: Australia's largest art museum is free to visit. At the entrance is the Aboriginal Memorial, made from 200 painted hollow logs. Indigenous art is the collection's main highlight, alongside Western modern works such as Pollock's Blue Poles. In the lakeside sculpture garden, James Turrell's Skyspace installation Within Without lets you sit inside and watch the sky.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.2.tip: Open daily from 10:00–17:00. Special exhibitions require separate tickets; the permanent collection is free.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.3.name: Mount Ainslie Lookout
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.3.text: This is the best place to understand Canberra's design. From the summit, Anzac Parade, Lake Burley Griffin, and Parliament House line up in a straight axis—the city center drawn by the planners. You can drive straight to the top. If you're fit, walk up from behind the war memorial on a trail that takes about 45 minutes to 1 hour one way.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.3.tip: Go before sunset for the best views. After dark, you can see the city lights. The summit is windy in winter, so bring a jacket.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.4.name: Lake Burley Griffin & Commonwealth Park
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.4.text: Canberra's artificial lake is lined with the National Library, Questacon, and the National Portrait Gallery. The most relaxing option is to rent a bike and ride around the central section of the lake, passing the Captain Cook Memorial Jet and the National Carillon. From mid-September to mid-October, Commonwealth Park on the lake's north shore hosts Floriade, with fields of tulips in bloom.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.4.tip: The Canberra Balloon Spectacular takes place in March. Dozens of hot-air balloons fly over the lake in the early morning, so check the dates in advance.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.5.name: Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.5.text: This valley reserve is about a 40-minute drive southwest of the city. Kangaroos and emus are common in the grasslands, and the koala trail through the eucalyptus forest offers close-up views. Platypuses and black swans live in the wetlands. Trails range from flat paths a few hundred meters long to half-day hikes. It feels more like the Australian bush than a city zoo and works well as a half-day drive.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.spots.5.tip: Animals are most active in the early morning and evening. The reserve charges admission per vehicle; check the official website for opening hours.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.stay: Stay in City or Braddon, north of the center, for easy dining. For quick access to Parliament and the museums, stay south of the lake in Barton or Kingston.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.tagline: A planned capital with mostly free museums
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.tips.0: Parliament House, the Australian War Memorial, and the National Gallery are all free, and they fit neatly into the same day.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.tips.1: City sights are spread out and buses run infrequently. For two or more people, a taxi or rental car saves time compared with taking the bus.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.tips.2: Australians drive on the left. Licence and translation requirements depend on your licence and circumstances, so check the latest requirements with Access Canberra before you leave.
e3efc269fccce3afcb8e.tips.3: Roads can be icy in the early mornings from June–August, so drive slowly. Kangaroos often cross roads around the city outskirts at dusk.

e459c01cde23bddc1403.access.0.how: Take the Tobu Tojo Line express to Kawagoe Station in about 30 minutes. At about ¥490, it is the fastest and cheapest way to get to Kawagoe.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.access.1.how: The Seibu limited express Laview runs directly to Seibu-Chichibu in about 80 minutes, with reserved seats for every passenger. If you skip the limited express, change trains at Hanno. The trip takes about 20 minutes longer and costs half as much.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.access.2.how: The JR Keihin-Tohoku Line or Shonan-Shinjuku Line takes about 30 minutes. The Shinkansen also stops at Omiya, making it a transfer point for trains to Tohoku and Hokuriku.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.foods.0.name: Kawagoe sweet potatoes and desserts
e459c01cde23bddc1403.foods.0.text: Kawagoe has been known for sweet potatoes since the Edo period. The old town has enough sweet potato treats to keep you snacking as you walk: roasted sweet potatoes, sweet potato ice cream, sweet potato fries, and sweet potato yokan. Prices are modest, and it is normal to try three or four items while walking. Finish them at the shop before moving on.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.foods.0.where: Kawagoe Warehouse District and Kashiya Yokocho
e459c01cde23bddc1403.foods.1.name: Kawagoe unagi
e459c01cde23bddc1403.foods.1.text: Kawagoe once relied on river transport, and the nearby rivers were rich in eel. Several century-old eel restaurants still operate around the old town. The Kanto style steams the eel before grilling it, giving the meat a tender texture and a slightly sweet sauce. Popular restaurants can have waits of one or two hours on weekends, so arrive before opening or take a number and explore the streets while you wait.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.foods.2.name: Chichibu waraji katsudon
e459c01cde23bddc1403.foods.2.text: This Chichibu specialty features a pork cutlet pounded thin and wide until it resembles a straw sandal. It is dipped in a sweet-and-savory sauce and placed over rice, usually with two cutlets per bowl. The portions are generous. Add a bowl of Chichibu soba for a complete meal, especially after a strenuous day of hiking.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.foods.2.where: Around Seibu-Chichibu Station and Chichibu Shrine
e459c01cde23bddc1403.intro.0: Saitama lies just north of Tokyo, and many Tokyo residents commute from here every day, so transportation is easy. Kawagoe is the best choice for most visitors: its Edo-period warehouse district is beautifully preserved, and it is just a 30-minute train ride from Ikebukuro. Farther west, Chichibu has moss phlox in spring and fall foliage in autumn. At Nagatoro, you can drift down a rocky river gorge in a wooden boat.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.intro.1: For a second trip to Tokyo or a half-day outing without an early start, Kawagoe is the best choice. Chichibu and Nagatoro are better as a full-day trip; the Seibu limited express takes about 80 minutes from Ikebukuro. Omiya has The Railway Museum and a bonsai village, so families and train enthusiasts can easily spend half a day there. Saitama has limited accommodation, so most people return to Tokyo the same day.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.name: Saitama
e459c01cde23bddc1403.seasons.note: In late March, Gongendo Sakura Embankment in Satte combines cherry blossoms with rapeseed flowers. Hitsujiyama Park's moss phlox blooms in late April, and Nagatoro's fall foliage peaks in mid- to late November. Chichibu is very crowded during Golden Week.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.sources.0.title: japan-guide: Getting from Tokyo to Kawagoe
e459c01cde23bddc1403.sources.1.title: japan-guide: Getting from Tokyo to Chichibu
e459c01cde23bddc1403.sources.2.title: japan-guide: Nagatoro river cruises
e459c01cde23bddc1403.sources.3.title: The Railway Museum: Visitor information
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.0.name: Kawagoe Warehouse District
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.0.text: During the Edo period, Kawagoe was a merchant town that supplied Edo. Wealthy merchants built fire-resistant storehouses with thick black-and-gray plaster walls, creating the distinctive warehouse district that survives today. The landmark Toki no Kane clock tower rings several times a day. Nearby Kashiya Yokocho is lined with old-fashioned candy shops, making it a fun place to snack as you walk.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.0.tip: The streets are crowded around noon on weekends. Arrive before 10 a.m. for better photos. The Kawagoe Festival takes place on the third weekend of October, with floats parading through the streets.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.1.name: Kawagoe Hikawa Shrine
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.1.text: This shrine is famous as a place to pray for love and marriage, and it is within walking distance of the old town. In summer, an arcade is filled with Edo-style wind chimes that tinkle in the breeze and are lit up at night. Visitors can also fish for fortunes written on small sea bream-shaped slips, a popular activity with younger visitors. Cherry blossoms line the Shingashi River behind the shrine in spring.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.1.tip: The wind-chime arcade is a summer event. It looks best after the evening lights come on; check the shrine's website for exact dates.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.2.name: Hitsujiyama Park
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.2.text: From mid-April to early May, pink, purple, and white moss phlox cover the hillsides in colorful carpets, with Mount Buko rising behind them. It is a 15–20-minute walk from Seibu-Chichibu Station. Outside the blooming season, the park is free and offers a hilltop view over Chichibu.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.2.tip: Limited express tickets sell out quickly during Golden Week, so book ahead in the Seibu app. Admission during the flower season is about ¥300.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.3.name: Nagatoro Iwadatami and river cruises
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.3.text: Broad stretches of flat, layered rock along the Arakawa River look like tatami mats laid out in steps, with emerald-green water flowing beside them. You can drift downstream in an unpowered wooden boat while the boatman steers with a long pole. The boat splashes through rapids, and the upper and lower sections can be taken separately. The foliage along both banks is best in mid- to late November, and rafting is also available in summer.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.3.tip: The Chichibu Railway takes about 20 minutes from Chichibu to Nagatoro Station. Cruises stop when water levels are too high or too low.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.4.name: Chichibu Shrine
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.4.text: Chichibu's main shrine is known for its finely detailed, colorful carvings. Some are by Hidari Jingoro, who is also credited with the sleeping cat at Nikko Toshogu. Held each year on December 2–3, the Chichibu Night Festival is one of Japan's three major float festivals. Huge floats are pulled uphill through the winter night, accompanied by fireworks. The shrine is about a 15-minute walk from Seibu-Chichibu Station.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.4.tip: The festival night draws enormous crowds. If you cannot find a place to stay, return to Tokyo before the last limited express. You can also watch the festival on large screens.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.5.name: Gongendo Sakura Embankment
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.5.text: Someiyoshino cherry trees line this roughly one-kilometer-long embankment. From late March to early April, the blossoms bloom alongside rapeseed flowers below, creating a classic Kanto scene of pink and yellow. Hydrangeas bloom in June, followed by red spider lilies in late September. From Satte Station on the Tobu Nikko Line, take a bus to the Gongendo-iriguchi stop, then walk 5 minutes.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.5.tip: Temporary shuttle buses and food stalls operate on weekends during cherry blossom season, when the area gets very crowded. Weekday mornings are more relaxed.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.6.name: The Railway Museum
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.6.text: JR East's railway museum is filled with retired steam locomotives, Shinkansen trains, and limited express cars on the first floor. Many can be entered, including the driver's cabs. The simulators are especially popular; the most sought-after ones require a lottery or a separate paid reservation. From Omiya Station, take the New Shuttle one stop to The Railway Museum Station. The museum is right outside the station.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.spots.6.tip: Closed Mondays. The museum recommends buying tickets online in advance; advance tickets are about ¥100 cheaper than same-day tickets.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.stay: Most people visit from Tokyo as a day trip. If you want to see the Chichibu Night Festival or visit Nagatoro early the next morning, stay near Seibu-Chichibu Station, close to both the hot springs and the station.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.tagline: Little Edo and the Chichibu mountains, just half a day from Tokyo
e459c01cde23bddc1403.tips.0: Tobu offers a discounted round-trip Kawagoe pass for international visitors. Buy it at Ikebukuro Station; it costs less than buying two one-way tickets.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.tips.1: Seibu offers a 1-day pass and a Nagatoro version that includes the Chichibu Railway. If you are visiting both Chichibu and Nagatoro, it costs less than buying separate tickets.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.tips.2: Two loop buses serve Kawagoe's old town, but most sights are just 10–15 minutes apart on foot. If you have the energy, walk.
e459c01cde23bddc1403.tips.3: Seibu limited express trains sell out quickly during the Chichibu Night Festival and moss phlox season. Reserve a seat at least one week ahead.

e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.days.4.items.0.note: Watch the sunrise from a viewpoint, then hike the Navajo Loop–Queen's Garden Trail
e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.days.4.move: Bryce Canyon→Page: about 240 kilometers and 2.5–3 hours; set your clock 1 hour back when entering Arizona from March–November

e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.days.6.items.2.note: In the evening, take the Hermit Road shuttle to Hopi Point for sunset
e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.days.6.move: Use the free shuttles in the park; private cars cannot use Hermit Road from March–November
