e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.days.7.move: Grand Canyon→Seligman: about 2 hours; →Hoover Dam: about 2.5 hours; →downtown: about 45 minutes
e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.days.7.title: Return to Las Vegas via Route 66
e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.days.8.items.2.note: Return the car in the afternoon and go to the airport; connect in Los Angeles or San Francisco for your flight home
e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.days.8.move: The Strip→Red Rock Canyon: about 30 minutes; timed-entry reservations are required on the scenic drive from October–May
e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.days.8.title: Red Rock Canyon, then depart
e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.for: First-time visitors to the American Southwest who can drive and want to see the major canyons in one trip
e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.summary: Pick up a car in Las Vegas and make a clockwise loop of about 1,700 kilometers. Head to Zion via Valley of Fire and stay two nights. Drive through the tunnel to Bryce Canyon to see its hoodoos, then continue south to Page for Horseshoe Bend and a guided tour of Antelope Canyon. Enter Grand Canyon National Park from the east and stay two nights. Finally, return to Las Vegas via historic Route 66 and Hoover Dam. Keep driving to about 3 hours a day; the final day is the longest.
e47c4a311bfe0a3b7433.title: The Southwest canyon loop · 9 days

e4816e24f70cd29ea1e8.s: Attractions total about {n} hours; may be too packed

e4ace16469afed1b72a9.access.0.how: Take the Relay Kamome limited express from Hakata, then transfer to the Nishi Kyushu Shinkansen on the same platform at Takeo Onsen. The fastest journey takes about 1 hour 20 minutes.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.access.1.how: The airport bus takes about 45–55 minutes to Nagasaki Station and costs about ¥1,400.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.access.2.how: Direct limited express trains run from Hakata to Sasebo and Huis Ten Bosch stations. From Nagasaki Station, take a JR train or highway bus to Sasebo.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.0.name: Nagasaki champon
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.0.text: This large bowl of noodles was created by overseas Chinese residents for students. Thick noodles simmer in a pork-and-chicken-bone broth with pork, seafood, and plenty of vegetables. The portions are generous enough for a full meal.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.0.where: Restaurants around Shinchi Chinatown and Chinese restaurants throughout central Nagasaki
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.1.name: Sara udon
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.1.text: A thickened seafood-and-vegetable sauce is poured over crisp fried noodles, which soften as they absorb the sauce. Spicy vinegar sauce is usually kept on the table; adding a little is the local way to eat it.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.1.where: Available at most of the same restaurants that serve champon
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.2.name: Castella
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.2.text: This sponge cake came from Portugal. It has coarse sugar crystals on the bottom and a moist, dense texture. A whole cake in a gift box from a long-established shop is a popular souvenir and is easy to take home at room temperature.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.2.where: Long-established shops and department stores around Nagasaki Station and Meganebashi Bridge
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.3.name: Turkish rice
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.3.text: A single plate combines a fried pork cutlet, curry or fried rice, and spaghetti. It is like a grown-up version of a children’s meal. Despite the name, it has nothing to do with Turkey. This classic Nagasaki yoshoku dish is ideal when you are hungry.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.3.where: Yoshoku restaurants and cafés around Shianbashi and Hamamachi
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.4.name: Sasebo burger
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.4.text: These freshly made, generously sized burgers were influenced by the U.S. military base. Recipes vary by shop, but many use thick patties, bacon, and a fried egg. They are noticeably larger than burgers from chain restaurants.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.foods.4.where: Burger shops around Sasebo Station and throughout Sasebo
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.intro.0: Nagasaki was Japan’s only port open to foreign trade during the country’s period of isolation. Traces of China, the Netherlands, and Portugal remain throughout the city: Chinatown, Dejima, churches, and Western-style homes on the hillsides. Nagasaki was also devastated by an atomic bomb. Peace Park and the Atomic Bomb Museum deserve a thoughtful half-day visit.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.intro.1: Nagasaki’s city center is hilly, with narrow roads, but its sights are close together and easy to connect by tram. Two days is enough for a good overview. If you have more time, head north to the Kujukushima Islands and Huis Ten Bosch near Sasebo, or east to Unzen for hot springs. Each makes a good extra day trip.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.name: Nagasaki
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.seasons.note: Spring and fall are the most comfortable. The Nagasaki Lantern Festival takes place around Lunar New Year, filling the city with Chinese lanterns. Summers are hot and humid, and the hills make sightseeing tiring.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.sources.0.title: Glover Garden visitor information
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.sources.1.title: Gunkanjima Concierge official website
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.sources.2.title: JR Kyushu Rail Pass official information
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.0.name: Glover Garden
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.0.text: Several Western-style homes from the Meiji period remain on the hillside. The Former Glover Residence is Japan’s oldest surviving Western-style wooden house and a World Heritage site. Walking downhill gives you views over Nagasaki Port. Oura Church is just below the entrance, and combo tickets are available.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.0.tip: An inclined electric walkway leads to the upper part of the garden. Start at the top and walk downhill to save energy. The garden has extended evening hours in fall.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.1.name: Peace Park and Atomic Bomb Museum
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.1.text: The Peace Statue in the park is one of Nagasaki’s symbols. A few minutes south are the hypocenter and the Atomic Bomb Museum. Exhibits include melted bottles, a clock stopped at 11:02, and victims’ belongings. The material is heavy but important, so allow plenty of time.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.1.tip: Take the tram to Peace Park or Atomic Bomb Museum Station. Written explanations are available, and audio guides can be rented.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.2.name: Mount Inasa night view
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.2.text: From the observation deck at the 333-meter summit, Nagasaki Port and the lights on both hillsides at night look like a bowl. Take the Nagasaki Ropeway up the mountain; the glass cabins offer views throughout the ride. Go up 30 minutes before sunset to see both the evening colors and the night view.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.2.tip: The ropeway station is some distance from Nagasaki Station, and many hotels offer free shuttle buses. The summit is windy, so bring a jacket.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.3.fee: Tour prices vary by operator; a facility-use fee is charged separately.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.3.name: Hashima (Gunkanjima) island tour
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.3.text: This abandoned undersea coal-mining island looks like a warship from a distance. Its dense cluster of crumbling concrete buildings forms part of a World Heritage site. You can land only as part of a boat tour. Boats leave from Nagasaki Port, and the trip takes about half a day including the cruise. Once ashore, visitors must stay on designated paths.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.3.tip: When the wind and waves are strong, boats circle the island without landing. Book online in advance and leave a spare day toward the end of your trip.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.4.name: Dejima
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.4.text: This fan-shaped artificial island once housed the Dutch trading post during Japan’s period of isolation. The residences, warehouses, and kitchen have been reconstructed and furnished in period style. You can see some of the earliest Western tableware, billiard tables, and coffee introduced to Japan. An hour is enough for a visit.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.4.tip: Get off at Dejima tram stop. Shinchi Chinatown is within walking distance, so the two sights are easy to visit together.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.5.name: Huis Ten Bosch
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.5.text: This large theme park recreates Dutch streets, with canals, windmills, and European-style buildings spread across a wide area. It is best known for spring tulips and winter illuminations. The nighttime lights are a major reason many people visit. Plan on a full day, especially for couples and families.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.5.tip: Ticket prices vary by season and time slot. Buy tickets in advance on the official website. Direct limited express trains run from Hakata to Huis Ten Bosch Station.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.6.name: Kujukushima Islands
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.6.text: More than 200 small islands lie off the coast of Sasebo. From the observatory at Tenkaiho, you can see the island chain spread across the sea. The view is especially beautiful at sunset. You can also take a sightseeing boat through the islands from the Pearl Sea Resort. It works well as a day trip combined with Huis Ten Bosch or scheduled before or after it.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.6.tip: From Sasebo Station, take a bus or taxi to Tenkaiho. Rapeseed flowers bloom in spring, and cosmos flowers bloom in fall.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.7.name: Unzen Onsen
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.7.text: This mountain hot-spring town is known for its sulfur springs. Unzen Hell, with its clouds of white steam, is right beside the town. Follow the wooden walkways to see the vents. Nearby Nita Pass has azaleas in spring, fall foliage, and occasional rime ice in winter. Stay overnight to relax after leaving Nagasaki.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.spots.7.tip: Direct buses run from Nagasaki Station. You can also take a JR train to Isahaya and transfer to a bus. It is colder in the mountains than in the city, so bring a jacket.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.stay: Stay near Nagasaki Station for easy access to the shinkansen and airport buses. For convenient evening dining and drinks, choose the Shianbashi or Shinchi Chinatown area. Stay in Sasebo for Huis Ten Bosch, or in Unzen for hot springs.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.tagline: A port city of slopes, Western-style homes, peace, and night views
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.tips.0: Nagasaki’s city center has many hills. Wear comfortable walking shoes, and if you have a lot of luggage, book a hotel near a tram stop.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.tips.1: Trams are the main way to get around the city. Fares are charged per ride, so buy a one-day pass if you plan to ride several times.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.tips.2: Hashima is highly dependent on the weather. Do not schedule it for the day before your departure.
e4ace16469afed1b72a9.tips.3: The Nagasaki Lantern Festival takes place around Lunar New Year, and the dates change each year. Book accommodation early.

e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.0.items.0.note: Arrive in the morning, travel into the city, and leave your bags at the hotel first
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.0.move: Take the Skyliner from Narita to Ueno in a little over 40 minutes, then transfer to the Ginza Line to Asakusa
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.0.title: Arrival · Asakusa and Tokyo Skytree
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.1.items.3.note: In the afternoon, walk along Harumi-dori to Ginza for department stores and flagship shops
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.1.move: Take the Hibiya Line from Ueno to Tsukiji in about 15 minutes. Tsukiji is closed on Sundays and some Wednesdays, so avoid those days
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.1.title: Ueno, Tsukiji and Ginza
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.2.items.1.note: Shop and enjoy sweets along Harajuku's Takeshita Street and Omotesando
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.2.move: Take the JR Yamanote Line to Harajuku Station. After exploring, walk along Omotesando to Shibuya in about 20 minutes
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.2.title: Meiji Jingu and Shibuya
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.3.move: Take the Keio Line from Shinjuku to Takaosanguchi in about 50 minutes. Return to Shinjuku in the afternoon; Shinjuku Gyoen closes at 4:30 p.m. in winter
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.3.title: Mount Takao and Shinjuku
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.4.items.2.note: Haneda is closer from Odaiba. Allow more time if you're flying from Narita
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.4.move: Take the Yurakucho Line from Tsukishima to Toyosu, then transfer to the Yurikamome Line to Odaiba
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.days.4.title: Tsukishima, Odaiba and departure
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.for: First-time visitors to Japan who want to explore Tokyo's main neighborhoods
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.season: March–May and October–December are the most comfortable
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.summary: Stay at one hotel in Tokyo and focus on one or two neighboring areas each day: old Tokyo's Asakusa and Ueno, Tsukiji and Ginza for food lovers, and Harajuku and Shibuya for a younger vibe. Spend half a day hiking Mount Takao for fall colors or views of Mount Fuji. On the last day, head to Tsukishima for monjayaki and Odaiba for ocean views, then go straight to the airport in the evening.
e5197f918c6275a5c26a.title: Your first time in Tokyo · 5 days

e6e198ec920f17b43e17.cost: Express bus round trip about ¥4,000 + ticket ¥2,180; or all-in day tour about ¥6,500–8,000
e6e198ec920f17b43e17.location: Naha Bus Terminal → Cape Manzamo → Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium (Ocean Expo Park) → Kouri Island
e6e198ec920f17b43e17.paragraphs.0: To reach Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium up in northern Motobu without a car, pick between two stellar routes. If you want an unhurried 4 hours exploring Ocean Expo Park—lingering at Ocean Blue Cafe beside the colossal Kuroshio Sea acrylic wall as whale sharks and manta rays glide overhead, plus catching the dolphin show—book the Okinawa Airport Shuttle or Yanbaru Express online the evening before, board at Asahibashi at 08:30, and hop off right at Kinen Koen-mae.
e6e198ec920f17b43e17.paragraphs.1: If you would rather sweep Cape Manzamo's dramatic cliffs, the ocean-spanning Kouri Bridge, and Chatan's American Village into the same day, book a northern sightseeing coach departing Kenchomae (most bundle the aquarium ticket). Nap between stops, skip transfer math, and often pay less per person than buying piecemeal long-distance fares.
e6e198ec920f17b43e17.phase: Step 04 · Day 3 Northern headliner: Churaumi Aquarium + Cape Manzamo
e6e198ec920f17b43e17.photo.alt: Whale shark gliding across the colossal deep-blue Kuroshio Sea tank at Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium
e6e198ec920f17b43e17.photo.caption: Standing before the giant Kuroshio Sea glass wall watching whale sharks cruise through deep-blue light still takes your breath away, even on a third visit to Okinawa.
e6e198ec920f17b43e17.tip: When riding public express buses independently, snap a photo of the return bus stop timetable the second you step off—the last express buses back to Naha generally depart around 17:30–18:30, and missing them means a cab ride costing well over ten thousand yen.
e6e198ec920f17b43e17.title: Two tested car-free ways north: direct express bus for deep aquarium time vs all-in sightseeing tour

e83d363d0319a434f171.cost: SUV rental with full insurance about A$95–130 / day
e83d363d0319a434f171.location: Melbourne CBD / airport rental depot → M1 Freeway → Geelong
e83d363d0319a434f171.paragraphs.0: To drive legally in Victoria as an overseas visitor, carry your valid home driver's license along with an International Driving Permit (IDP) or a NAATI-certified English translation if your license is not in English (confirm exact requirements for your license on VicRoads). Opt for Zero Excess full coverage—on coastal roads, a stray gravel chip in the windshield or a car-park scrape easily hits four figures in Australian dollars, and full cover keeps the whole trip relaxed.
e83d363d0319a434f171.paragraphs.1: Australia drives on the left from the right-hand seat. Drivers used to right-hand traffic almost always make two classic mistakes in their first twenty minutes: flipping the windshield wipers instead of the turn signal, and drifting onto the left edge line. Stick to two simple cues: keep the driver's seat hugged toward the center line, and at every roundabout yield to traffic coming from your right before looping clockwise. After 10 minutes on wide suburban lanes, take the M1 past Geelong's painted waterfront bollards, stock up on two cases of water and road snacks at Coles, and merge onto the B100 Great Ocean Road.
e83d363d0319a434f171.phase: Step 01 · Day 1 08:30 Melbourne car pickup & left-side drill
e83d363d0319a434f171.tip: Victoria's speed cameras are well hidden and fines are punishing—exceeding the limit by just 10 km/h can cost hundreds of Australian dollars. Limits along the Great Ocean Road jump constantly between 80, 60, and 50, so ease off the gas at every sign and never tailgate locals.
e83d363d0319a434f171.title: Check your license (plus IDP or NAATI translation if required) and take a 10-minute warm-up loop

e8d0e521d86950188845.location: Shinsekai JanJan Yokocho · Dobutsuen-mae or Ebisucho Station
e8d0e521d86950188845.paragraphs.0: Ride the subway two stops at twilight into Shinsekai. Neon flashes up Tsutenkaku Tower over oversized 3D signs and retro pachinko parlors straight out of Showa-era Osaka, with menu prices noticeably gentler than Shinsaibashi.
e8d0e521d86950188845.paragraphs.1: Duck south into narrow JanJan Yokocho toward old-school kushikatsu institutions like Yaekatsu or Tengu. Start with a frost-rimmed draft beer and order doteyaki (miso-braised beef tendon), whole prawns, lotus root, quail eggs, and cheese chikuwa. The ultra-thin panko crust stays miraculously crisp; crunch the free chilled raw cabbage between bites to reset your palate.
e8d0e521d86950188845.phase: Step 05 · 17:45 Dusk in Shinsekai for Kushikatsu

e8d0e521d86950188845.photo.caption: Old-school Shinsekai kushikatsu nails paper-thin crunch fried to order—pair with crisp chilled cabbage and cold draft for pure Osaka joy.
e8d0e521d86950188845.tip: Shinsekai's main strip and JanJan Yokocho are lively and safe at night, but avoid wandering deep south across the JR overpass into inner Nishinari—head back to Namba via Ebisucho or north of Tsutenkaku.

ea50c28f7cd3f23e875c.cost: Half-day whale tour about ¥6,000–7,000 / person (usually includes free Naha hotel pickup)
ea50c28f7cd3f23e875c.duration: About 3.5–4 hours including transfers and time at sea
ea50c28f7cd3f23e875c.location: Naha Miegusuku Port → Kerama Islands offshore waters
ea50c28f7cd3f23e875c.paragraphs.0: Winter Okinawa's irreplaceable signature moment is heading offshore to watch whales. From late December through early April, hundreds of 15-meter humpback whales migrate into the crystal-clear Kerama Islands to mate and raise calves. Book a Naha operator running large catamarans (far steadier in swell) that explicitly offers free Naha hotel pickup—at 08:15 a minibus collects you downstairs and whisks you straight to Miegusuku Port with zero transit guesswork.
ea50c28f7cd3f23e875c.paragraphs.1: About 40 minutes out in deep sapphire water, captains across the fleet radio spout sightings to one another in real time. The instant a four-meter plume of white spray shoots skyward—followed by a massive, uniquely patterned black-and-white tail fluke arching high and slapping the sea—the whole deck erupts in cheers. Top operators log sighting rates over 98% during peak February–March, and many offer a refund or free re-boarding guarantee if no whales appear.
ea50c28f7cd3f23e875c.phase: Step 02 · Day 2 Morning: winter-only Kerama whale watching
ea50c28f7cd3f23e875c.tip: Never gamble on skipping motion-sickness meds: take a tablet 30 minutes before departure, stay on the mid-to-rear open deck watching the horizon in fresh air instead of scrolling your phone inside the closed cabin, and note that large suitcases are not allowed on whale boats.
ea50c28f7cd3f23e875c.title: Free pickup right at your hotel door for 3 hours watching breaching humpback whales

eb7cab3d59876b5eaa89.days.0.move: Take the JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station to Kamakura in about 1 hour. Use the Enoden between sights; for the return, take the Odakyu Line to Shinjuku.
eb7cab3d59876b5eaa89.days.0.title: Kamakura temples and Enoshima
eb7cab3d59876b5eaa89.days.1.items.3.note: Take the pirate ship from Togendai to Moto-Hakone and see the torii gate standing in the water at Hakone Shrine.
eb7cab3d59876b5eaa89.days.1.move: Take the Romancecar from Shinjuku to Hakone-Yumoto in about 85 minutes. During winter cable-car maintenance, take the replacement bus instead.
eb7cab3d59876b5eaa89.days.1.title: Hakone loop
eb7cab3d59876b5eaa89.days.2.move: Take the Hakone Tozan Railway from Yumoto to Odawara, then transfer to the JR Tokaido Line for Yokohama. Return to Tokyo that evening.
eb7cab3d59876b5eaa89.days.2.title: Yumoto hot springs and Yokohama
eb7cab3d59876b5eaa89.for: Travelers who have explored central Tokyo and want a few days of temples, beaches, and hot springs
eb7cab3d59876b5eaa89.summary: On day 1, take a day trip from Tokyo to Kamakura and Enoshima to see the Great Buddha, historic temples, and the sea. On day 2, take the Romancecar to Hakone and follow the loop by mountain railway, cable car, and pirate ship. Stay at a hot-spring ryokan that night. On day 3, soak in the hot springs in the morning, then enjoy the waterfront and ramen in Yokohama's Minato Mirai before returning to Tokyo that evening.

ec32980db39805c5f60a.0: Scroll Xiaohongshu or Reddit for Osaka food advice and eight out of ten threads warn about Kuromon Market—three strawberries for ¥1,500, wagyu skewers priced like Ginza, and local Osaka shoppers haven't bought groceries there in a decade. Plenty of visitors blow a whole morning in Kuromon without ever tasting real everyday Osaka.
ec32980db39805c5f60a.1: Just one subway stop from Namba sits Kizu Wholesale Market, the real kitchen of Osaka: open from 6 AM with overflowing sea-urchin and tuna bowls at roughly half of Kuromon's tourist prices. Follow these 6 chronological stops from dawn Kizu Market through the only 2 Kuromon old-timers still worth visiting, all the way to Shinsekai skewers and late-night Ura-Namba standing bars.

ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.access.0.how: Take the Kintetsu line from Osaka-Namba to Kintetsu-Nara Station. The rapid express takes about 40 minutes, and the station is the closest to Nara Park.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.access.1.how: The Kintetsu line from Kyoto Station to Kintetsu-Nara takes about 35 minutes by limited express or 45 minutes by express. The JR Nara Line takes about 45–70 minutes.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.access.2.how: A limousine bus takes about 1.5 hours to Nara. You can also take JR and transfer at Tennoji.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.foods.0.name: Kakinoha-zushi
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.foods.0.text: Salt-cured mackerel or salmon is pressed onto vinegared rice and wrapped in a persimmon leaf. You don't eat the leaf, but it adds a faint fragrance and softens the fish's salty flavor. It is a good choice for lunch or a meal on the train.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.foods.0.where: Long-established shops and station bento stores near Kintetsu-Nara Station and Higashimuki Shopping Street.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.foods.1.name: Miwa somen
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.foods.1.text: The Miwa area of Nara is the birthplace of hand-pulled somen noodles. They are extremely thin but pleasantly chewy. Try cold somen in summer or hot nyumen in winter for a light, refreshing meal.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.foods.1.where: Noodle shops around Naramachi and Nara Park; there are more long-established shops near Miwa Station.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.foods.2.name: Kuzumochi and kuzukiri
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.foods.2.text: Yoshino kuzu starch is made into translucent sweets with a cool, slippery texture. They are served with brown sugar syrup or soybean flour. A serving is especially refreshing after walking in the summer heat.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.foods.2.where: Dessert shops and teahouses in Naramachi and on Mt. Yoshino.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.intro.0: Nara became a capital before Kyoto. Todai-ji's Great Buddha, Kasuga Taisha, and Horyu-ji are all 1,200–1,300-year-old treasures. Sights in the city center cluster around Nara Park, and you can connect them on foot over mostly flat ground. More than 1,000 deer roam freely through the park, making this one of the easiest days out in Japan for families and first-time visitors.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.intro.1: Most people make a day trip from Kyoto or Osaka: visit Todai-ji and Kasuga Taisha in the morning, then explore Naramachi in the afternoon. For a quieter day, head south to Asuka and cycle past ancient burial mounds, or visit Mt. Yoshino in spring for hills covered in cherry blossoms. Nara gets quiet early at night, so staying overnight lets you have the park mostly to yourself in the morning.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.name: Nara
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.seasons.note: Cherry blossoms bloom at Mt. Yoshino and Nara Park in early April, followed by fall foliage in November. Fawns are born in May–June, and the mothers can be irritable.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.sources.0.title: Todai-ji: Visiting hours and admission fee
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.sources.1.title: Wikipedia: Kintetsu limited express
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.0.name: Todai-ji Great Buddha Hall
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.0.text: One of the world's largest wooden buildings, it houses a bronze Great Buddha about 15 meters tall. You don't realize how enormous the hall is until you walk through the entrance. A hole at the base of one pillar is said to bring good luck to anyone who crawls through it, and most of those in line are children. Don't miss the two fierce guardian statues at the Great South Gate.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.0.tip: Arrive when it opens at 8. School groups usually don't arrive in large numbers until after 10.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.1.name: Nara Park and the deer
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.1.text: Todai-ji, Kasuga Taisha, and Kofuku-ji all stand in this large park, where more than 1,000 deer roam across the grass. Vendors sell shika senbei, crackers made for feeding the deer, which bow to ask for food. The park is flat and open, with cherry blossoms in spring and fall foliage in autumn. Take your time and spend a full day walking around.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.1.tip: The deer are wild animals and may bite or head-butt. After you finish the crackers, hold out both hands to show that you have none left.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.2.name: Kasuga Taisha
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.2.text: The vermilion shrine buildings sit beside an ancient forest. About 2,000 moss-covered stone lanterns line the approach, and more than 1,000 bronze lanterns hang inside the shrine. The atmosphere is quieter than at Todai-ji. The wisteria along the corridors is famous in early summer, and during the Mantoro festivals in early February and mid-August, all the lanterns are lit.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.2.tip: The approach outside is free, but the inner shrine corridors require a separate admission fee.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.3.name: Naramachi
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.3.text: This old neighborhood south of the park preserves the layout of an Edo-period merchant district. Narrow lanes are lined with traditional wooden houses with lattice windows, along with cafes, general stores, and sake shops. The World Heritage site Gango-ji is here too. Walk over after seeing the Great Buddha for a snack and a glass of Nara sake.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.3.tip: Many shops close around 5 in the afternoon, so don't arrive too late.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.4.name: Horyu-ji
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.4.text: The world's oldest surviving group of wooden buildings includes a 1,300-year-old five-story pagoda and main hall. It is Japan's first World Heritage site. Much quieter than Todai-ji, it is ideal for anyone interested in architecture and Buddhist statues. From Nara Station, take JR for about 15 minutes to Horyu-ji Station, then walk about 20 minutes or take a bus.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.4.tip: It is separate from Nara Park, so allow half a day. If you're coming from Osaka, you can visit here first.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.5.name: Mt. Yoshino
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.5.text: Japan's most famous cherry blossom mountain has about 30,000 mountain cherry trees that bloom in stages from the foot upward: Shimo-senbon, Naka-senbon, Kami-senbon, and Oku-senbon. The World Heritage site Kinpusen-ji stands midway up the mountain. From Osaka-Abenobashi, take the Kintetsu line for about 1 hour 15 minutes to Yoshino Station, then take the ropeway or a bus up the mountain.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.5.tip: The blossoms usually peak in early to mid-April, and weekends are crowded. Outside the peak season, it is quieter, but shops also close early.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.6.name: Asuka
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.6.text: This area was home to Japan's earliest capital and is now a rural landscape dotted with historic sites: the Ishibutai Tomb, built from huge stones; Asuka-dera's oldest surviving Buddhist statue in Japan; and terraced rice fields. Rent a bicycle at Asuka Station and spend half a day to a full day exploring at an easy pace. In autumn, the rice fields turn golden and red spider lilies bloom along the roads.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.spots.6.tip: There are some hills, so an electric-assist bike will make the ride much easier.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.stay: A day trip from Kyoto or Osaka is enough for most people. If you stay overnight, choose a place near Kintetsu-Nara Station. The park and Naramachi are both within easy walking distance, and the area is quieter at night and in the morning.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.tagline: See the Great Buddha and feed the deer—older than Kyoto
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.tips.0: The deer in the park may snatch paper bags and maps. Don't wave snacks or paper items around in your hands.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.tips.1: From Osaka, take the Kintetsu line to Kintetsu-Nara Station. It is about 15 minutes closer to the sights on foot than JR Nara Station.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.tips.2: Many temples and shrines in Nara close around 5. There is little to do at night, so check whether a lantern festival is taking place if you want to see the city after dark.
ef9cc0f52715d9a338ff.tips.3: The path between Todai-ji and Kasuga Taisha has some gentle slopes. Flat shoes are fine, and bring a bottle of water.

f0324333eaa0545d014f.access.0.how: The Hokuriku Shinkansen takes about 1 hour 20 minutes–1 hour 40 minutes to Nagano and about 1 hour 10 minutes to Karuizawa
f0324333eaa0545d014f.access.1.how: The JR Azusa limited express takes about 2 hours 40 minutes to Matsumoto
f0324333eaa0545d014f.access.2.how: The JR Shinano limited express takes about 2 hours to Matsumoto and about 3 hours to Nagano
f0324333eaa0545d014f.access.3.how: Cross the mountains via the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route to Ogizawa, then continue to Shinano-Omachi. Allow a full day (April–November only)
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.0.name: Shinshu soba
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.0.text: Nagano’s highlands have a large temperature difference between day and night, giving the buckwheat a strong aroma. The region is one of Japan’s leading soba producers. In summer, order cold zarusoba to enjoy the flavor of the noodles, with a little green onion and wasabi in the dipping sauce.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.0.where: Many long-established restaurants in Togakushi, Matsumoto, and front of Zenkoji Temple
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.1.name: Oyaki
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.1.text: These round buns are made with wheat dough filled with nozawana greens, eggplant, red bean paste, and other fillings, then steamed or grilled. Fresh oyaki have lightly browned skins and are easy to eat while walking.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.1.where: Along the approach to Zenkoji Temple, at Nagano Station, and at roadside rest areas
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.2.name: Sanzoku-yaki
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.2.text: A fried chicken dish from the Matsumoto and Shiojiri area. A whole chicken thigh is marinated in garlic soy sauce, coated in starch, and fried. The pieces are large, with a crisp outside and juicy interior. The name is a pun on words meaning “to steal” and “to fry.”
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.2.where: Set-meal restaurants and izakayas in Matsumoto
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.3.name: Shinshu apples
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.3.text: Nagano is Japan’s second-largest apple-producing region. The season runs from September–November, and apples from roadside farm stands are large and crisp. You can also find apple juice, apple pie, and dried apples.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.foods.3.where: Fruit stands and roadside rest areas around Nagano city and Matsumoto
f0324333eaa0545d014f.intro.0: Known as the “Roof of Japan,” Nagano is home to the Northern, Central, and Southern Alps. In winter, the powder snow in Hakuba and Nozawa Onsen draws skiers from around the world. The monkeys bathing in the hot springs at Jigokudani are a classic winter sight. In summer, Kamikochi is cool and ideal for escaping the heat and hiking.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.intro.1: In the cities, Matsumoto has Matsumoto Castle, with its original black keep, while Nagano city is home to the thousand-year-old Zenkoji Temple. To the south, Tsumago-juku and Narai-juku in the Kiso Valley preserve the look of Nakasendo post towns from the Edo period. Nagano is large, so plan the northern area around Nagano city and the central area around Matsumoto separately. Staying one or two nights in each saves time compared with traveling back and forth from one base.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.name: Nagano
f0324333eaa0545d014f.seasons.note: Skiing and snow monkeys from December–March; Kamikochi and Hakuba for cool weather in July–August; fall colors in the mountains from mid- to late October. Kamikochi closes in winter.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.sources.0.title: Matsumoto Castle visitor information
f0324333eaa0545d014f.sources.1.title: Jigokudani Monkey Park visitor information
f0324333eaa0545d014f.sources.2.title: Kamikochi official website: transportation
f0324333eaa0545d014f.sources.3.title: Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route: transportation
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.0.name: Matsumoto Castle
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.0.text: One of Japan’s 5 national treasure castle keeps, with black-lacquered exterior walls. It is often called “Crow Castle.” The keep has survived from the late 16th century, and its interior retains the original timber structure. Climb all the way to the sixth floor for views of Matsumoto and the Northern Alps. The best reflections are by the moat, which is lit up at night during cherry blossom season in early April.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.0.tip: You must remove your shoes inside the keep. The steepest stairs are about 61 degrees, so secure your backpack and use both hands on the railings. Lines are often long in the morning during peak season.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.1.name: Kamikochi
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.1.text: A high-altitude valley at about 1,500 meters, with the clear blue Azusa River and the Hotaka mountain range in the background. The round trip from Kappa Bridge toward Myojin Pond takes about 2 hours. The trail is flat and easy for beginners. Private cars are prohibited year-round, so change to a shuttle bus at Sawando or Hirayu. The ride takes about 30 minutes.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.1.tip: Open only from mid-April to mid-November (in 2026, April 17–November 15); mornings and evenings are cool, so bring a jacket and a bear bell.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.2.name: Jigokudani Monkey Park
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.2.text: The only place in the world where you can see wild monkeys bathing in hot springs. In winter, the monkeys doze in the steaming pool amid the snow. They are known overseas as “snow monkeys.” From Nagano Station, take the Nagano Dentetsu train to Yudanaka, change to a bus for the entrance, then walk along a forest road for about 30–40 minutes. You can combine the visit with nearby Shibu Onsen in one day.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.2.tip: The monkeys mainly bathe from December–March. Do not feed or touch them, and do not stare at or provoke them. Wear slip-resistant snow boots on snowy days.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.3.name: Zenkoji Temple
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.3.text: An ancient temple with about 1,400 years of history. It is open to all Buddhist sects and has long been associated with the saying, “You should visit Zenkoji once in your life.” The main hall is a national treasure. Its most unusual feature is the Kaidan Meguri, a pitch-dark passage beneath the main hall where you feel your way forward to find the legendary “key to paradise.” It is about a 30-minute walk or a bus ride from Nagano Station.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.3.tip: The morning service takes place early. Worshippers can kneel along the approach and receive a touch on the head from the head priest’s prayer beads. The inner sanctuary and Kaidan Meguri require a separate admission ticket.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.4.name: Tsumago-juku
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.4.text: One of the best-preserved post towns along the Nakasendo. Even the utility poles have been hidden, making the whole street feel like a return to the Edo period. The classic route is to hike from Magome-juku on the Gifu side to Tsumago. The full trail is about 8 kilometers and takes 2.5–3 hours, crossing Magome Pass and passing stone paths, waterfalls, and teahouses. Take a JR train to Nagiso Station, then walk or take a bus.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.4.tip: Luggage delivery services are available along the route, so you can send large bags ahead to the other end. Bears are active in the mountain areas, so carry a bear bell.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.5.name: Hakuba
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.5.text: The main alpine skiing venue for the 1998 Nagano Winter Olympics, with around a dozen resorts nearby. It has excellent snow, many international visitors, and relatively good access to English. In summer, take the gondola up Happo Ridge and hike to Happo Pond for reflections of the Hakuba Three Peaks. The round trip takes about 3 hours. Buses and the JR Oito Line run from Nagano Station and Matsumoto.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.5.tip: Snow-season lodging and lessons fill up early, so book as soon as your dates are set. Mountain weather changes quickly, so bring a windproof jacket.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.6.name: Karuizawa
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.6.text: A summer resort developed by foreign missionaries during the Meiji era, with villas, churches, and cafés scattered among the trees. A large outlet mall is just outside the south exit of the Shinkansen station, while Old Karuizawa Ginza to the north is a traditional shopping street. Just over an hour from Tokyo, it is ideal for a day trip combining shopping and a walk. The larch trees turn golden in late October.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.6.tip: The sights around Old Karuizawa are spread out, so consider renting a bicycle. Summer weekends are busy with both people and cars.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.7.name: Nozawa Onsen
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.7.text: The ski resort and hot spring village are connected. The village has more than a dozen free public baths, or sotoyu, maintained and cleaned by local residents. Enjoying them one by one in a yukata is part of the fun. Snow is deep in winter, and the Dosojin Fire Festival, one of Japan’s three major fire festivals, takes place on January 15. From Iiyama Station on the Hokuriku Shinkansen, the bus ride takes about 25 minutes.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.spots.7.tip: The sotoyu baths are very hot, so use a bucket to rinse yourself and adjust to the temperature first. Bring your own towel and leave a little change in the oil money box as a thank-you.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.stay: Stay near Nagano Station for easy access to Zenkoji Temple, Jigokudani, and Nozawa Onsen. Stay around Matsumoto Station for trips to Kamikochi and the Kiso Valley. For skiing, stay directly at a resort hotel in Hakuba or Nozawa Onsen.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.tagline: Snowy mountains, bathing monkeys, a national treasure castle, and old post towns along the Nakasendo
f0324333eaa0545d014f.tips.0: Snow is deep in northern Nagano in winter. Wear waterproof, slip-resistant shoes. Indoor heating is strong, so dress in layers that are easy to remove.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.tips.1: Driving rules in Japan depend on your licence and required documents. Check the official requirements before driving. Ski resorts and hot spring villages generally have bus service.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.tips.2: Mountain sights such as Kamikochi and the alpine routes close in winter. Check the opening period before you leave.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.tips.3: The northern area (Nagano, Yudanaka, and Nozawa) and central area (Matsumoto and Kamikochi) are far apart, so staying in separate locations saves time.
f0324333eaa0545d014f.tips.4: Black bears live in the mountains. Carry a bear bell when hiking and do not leave food on forest roads.

f2277be5f3d209e57c8f.s: Set aside time for lunch each day, and make long trips in the morning whenever possible.

f39e09a6391608b4dbbe.excerpt: Winter Hokkaido brings two real hazards: blizzards halting JR trains and slick black ice knocking unprepared walkers flat. This 5-day, 4-night car-free guide covers coastal train seats, layering for 25°C indoor heating, 16:00 sunsets, and blizzard bus fallbacks.

f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.access.0.how: About 45 minutes–1 hour from Shin-Osaka to Okayama Station on the Sanyo Shinkansen
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.access.1.how: About 35–40 minutes from Hiroshima Station to Okayama Station by Shinkansen
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.access.2.how: About 30 minutes by airport bus to Okayama Station, about ¥1,000; flights serve Shanghai, Hong Kong, Taipei, and other destinations
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.access.3.how: About 55 minutes to Okayama Station on the JR Marine Liner Rapid Service across the Seto Ohashi Bridge
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.0.name: White peaches
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.0.text: Okayama's white peaches are grown in bags, which keeps their skins white. They are juicy and highly fragrant, making them popular gifts. July–August is peak season. Buy one at a fruit shop or station and eat it fresh, or order a seasonal peach parfait at a café.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.0.where: The gift shops inside Okayama Station, fruit shops in the city, and fruit cafés
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.1.name: Muscat of Alexandria grapes
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.1.text: Okayama is Japan's leading producer of greenhouse-grown Muscat of Alexandria grapes. The grapes are large and intensely fragrant. They are at their best from August–October. If you do not want to buy a whole bunch, try a grape parfait or grape daifuku.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.1.where: Fruit shops near Okayama Station and dessert shops in the Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.2.name: Demikatsudon
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.2.text: Okayama's specialty katsudon replaces the egg with a rich demi-glace sauce poured over the cutlet. It comes with rice and green peas underneath and has a Western-style feel. Locals eat it as a home-style meal, and the portions are generous.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.2.where: Old-fashioned diners around Okayama Station and downtown
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.3.name: Bara-zushi
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.3.text: Vinegared rice is topped with more than a dozen ingredients, including Spanish mackerel, shrimp, lotus root, and shredded egg. The colorful dish was originally a home-style food served during festivals. Station shops sell bento versions that are convenient to eat on the Shinkansen.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.3.where: Bento shops at Okayama Station and Japanese restaurants in the city
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.4.name: Kibidango
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.4.text: In the Momotaro story, this is what he gives the dog, monkey, and pheasant. Today's kibidango are soft, chewy rice-flour dumplings with a mild sweetness. They are Okayama's most common souvenir.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.foods.4.where: Okayama Station and souvenir shops around Okayama Korakuen Garden
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.intro.0: Okayama Prefecture lies between Kansai and Hiroshima. Okayama Station is a major Shinkansen stop. Head south across the Seto Ohashi Bridge to Shikoku, north by limited express to Tottori and Matsue, or southeast by ferry to Naoshima. Many travelers use Okayama as a transfer point, but it is worth staying for 1–2 days. Okayama Korakuen Garden, one of Japan's three great gardens, Okayama Castle with its black exterior, and the whitewashed storehouses of the Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter are all within a 30-minute drive.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.intro.1: Okayama has many sunny days and few typhoons, earning it the nickname "Land of Sunshine." Its fruit is excellent. White peaches and Muscat of Alexandria grapes are expensive but delicious in summer. If you have time, head into the mountains to see Bitchu Matsuyama Castle above a sea of clouds. It is one of the few original castle keeps in Japan still standing today.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.name: Okayama
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.seasons.note: Spring and fall are the most comfortable seasons; July–September is white peach and grape season; on clear mornings in October–November, you may see Bitchu Matsuyama Castle surrounded by a sea of clouds.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.sources.0.title: Okayama Korakuen Garden official website: Admission and combination tickets
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.sources.1.title: Okayama City: Frequently asked questions about Okayama Castle and Korakuen Garden
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.sources.2.title: Ohara Museum of Art: Visitor information
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.sources.3.title: Okayama Tourism WEB: Kurashiki River boat tours
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.sources.4.title: Takahashi Tourism Association: Bitchu Matsuyama Castle
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.0.fee: About ¥500, or about ¥800 with Okayama Castle
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.0.name: Okayama Korakuen Garden
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.0.text: One of Japan's three great gardens, along with Kenrokuen in Kanazawa and Kairakuen in Mito. Broad lawns surround ponds and small hills, with open views and Okayama Castle visible in the distance. From Okayama Station, take the tram to "Shiroshita," then walk about 10 minutes. The cherry and plum blossoms are beautiful in spring, and the fall colors are lovely. There is also a nighttime illumination in late November.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.0.tip: Buy a combination ticket with Okayama Castle. It is cheaper than buying the tickets separately.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.1.name: Okayama Castle
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.1.text: Its black exterior has earned it the nickname "Crow Castle." It faces Okayama Korakuen Garden across the Asahi River, just over Tsukimi Bridge. The keep was rebuilt after the war. After renovations in 2022, the interior became a museum about Okayama's history, and the top floor offers panoramic views of the garden. The best photo angle is from the garden or the opposite riverbank, where the black keep is reflected in the water.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.2.name: Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.2.text: This Edo-period merchant district has whitewashed, black-tiled storehouses lining a willow-lined canal. It is about a 10-minute walk from JR Kurashiki Station. You can take a boat ride of about 20 minutes along the canal. Buy tickets at the Kurashikikan Tourist Information Center. The narrow lanes are filled with denim shops and cafés, and look their best after the evening lights come on.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.2.tip: Boat rides do not operate on the second Monday of each month. From January–February, they run only on weekends. If a boat is full, you have to wait for the next one.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.3.name: Ohara Museum of Art
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.3.text: Japan's first private museum devoted mainly to Western art stands beside the Kurashiki canal. Its collection includes works by Monet and El Greco. One ticket covers the Main Gallery, the Craft Museum, the Oriental Museum, and other exhibition spaces. Art lovers should allow 2 hours; if you are less interested, you can see just the Main Gallery.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.3.tip: Closed Mondays, except on holidays. From December–February, it closes at 3 p.m.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.4.name: Bitchu Matsuyama Castle
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.4.text: This historic castle sits atop a mountain at an elevation of about 430 meters. Its keep is an original from the Edo period. When surrounded by a sea of clouds on fall and winter mornings, it is known as a "castle in the sky." From Okayama Station, take the JR Hakubi Line for about 35–50 minutes to Bitchu-Takahashi Station, then take a vehicle to the middle of the mountain. The final approach requires about 20 minutes of uphill walking.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.4.tip: To see the sea of clouds, go to the viewpoint on the mountain opposite the castle. You will need to take a reservation-only taxi or drive yourself, and your chances depend on the weather forecast.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.5.name: Kibitsu Shrine
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.5.text: This shrine is dedicated to Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto, said to be the model for Momotaro. The main hall is a National Treasure, and a photogenic wooden corridor about 360 meters long extends along the hillside behind it. Hydrangeas bloom beautifully beside the corridor in June. From Okayama Station, take the JR Kibi Line for about 20 minutes. It makes an easy half-day trip from the city.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.6.name: Mount Washu
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.spots.6.text: This is one of the best places to see the Seto Ohashi Bridge and the many islands of the Seto Inland Sea. The mountain is not high, and the viewpoints are just a few minutes' walk from the parking lot. At sunset, the bridge and islands look beautiful in silhouette. Without a car, take a taxi from JR Kojima Station for about 15 minutes. You can also visit Kojima's denim street along the way.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.stay: Staying near Okayama Station is most convenient. Kurashiki, Okayama Korakuen Garden, and Uno Port, for Naoshima, are all one train ride away. For evening views of the old streets, stay a night in Kurashiki.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.tagline: A transport hub for gardens, whitewashed streets, and the Seto Inland Sea
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.tips.0: You can take the tram from Okayama Station to Okayama Korakuen Garden, and use a transit card to pay.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.tips.1: To reach Naoshima, take a JR train from Okayama Station to Uno Station, about 1 hour, then take the ferry. Check the sailing schedule in advance.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.tips.2: Most shops in the Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter close around 17–18. Evenings are mainly for walking and enjoying the lights.
f4c6aed8f71789d81f48.tips.3: The mountain path to Bitchu Matsuyama Castle is steep, and the stone steps are slippery when wet. Wear shoes with good traction.

f5a6cb53fcf953c4bc7d.duration: Set aside 20 minutes to sort receipts and layer bags
f5a6cb53fcf953c4bc7d.location: Your hotel room · the night before flying home
f5a6cb53fcf953c4bc7d.paragraphs.0: A huge share of traveler horror stories happen at the packing stage. People assume no sealed bag means they can stuff tax-free snacks and skincare deep beneath dirty laundry—or tear open two sheet masks back at the hotel. When the KIOSK flags a red light the next day, they end up excavating an entire suitcase at the customs desk, and one missing opened box of masks disqualifies the whole ¥20,000 skincare receipt.
f5a6cb53fcf953c4bc7d.paragraphs.1: The cleanest defense is to ring up anything you'll consume in Japan separately: drinks, snacks, or toiletries for the trip go on a regular receipt, never mixed with tax-free purchases. Group all tax-free items inside one zippered packing cube right on top of your checked bag, and keep high-ticket watches, bags, and non-liquid tax-free items under 100ml in your carry-on. Snap a photo of every receipt organized by store name as backup.
f5a6cb53fcf953c4bc7d.phase: Step 02 · Pack an inspection-ready top layer
f5a6cb53fcf953c4bc7d.tip: Liquid tax-free items (toners, sake, skincare over 100ml) have to go in checked luggage, which means you must clear the customs KIOSK BEFORE dropping your bag—don't remember after passing security.
f5a6cb53fcf953c4bc7d.title: Keep high-value tax-free items and small cosmetics on top of your suitcase to avoid terminal chaos

f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.access.0.how: Nonstop flights connect Los Angeles and San Francisco with Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou. Xiamen has nonstop flights to Los Angeles, and Wuhan has nonstop flights to San Francisco. Flights take about 11–13 hours. Routes change often, so check with the airline.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.access.1.how: The flight takes about 1.5 hours. Driving on Interstate 5 takes about 6 hours; Highway 1 takes at least 2 days.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.access.2.how: The flight to Los Angeles takes about 1 hour. Driving takes about 4–5 hours, with frequent traffic on Friday afternoons and on the return trip Sunday.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.cover.alt: Big Sur coast and Bixby Bridge
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.0.name: Clam chowder in a sourdough bowl
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.0.text: A hollowed-out sourdough loaf serves as a bowl for creamy clam chowder. After finishing the soup, tear into the bread. The sourdough has a mildly tangy flavor and is a longtime San Francisco specialty. Fisherman's Wharf has the most options, and a bowl is especially comforting in the sea breeze.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.0.where: Around Fisherman's Wharf, Pier 39, and the Ferry Building.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.1.name: Dungeness crab
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.1.price: Priced by weight at the market rate
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.1.text: This seasonal Bay Area seafood is large and sweet. It is often boiled whole and served with butter, or roasted with garlic. Chinese restaurants also serve it stir-fried with ginger and scallions. The season generally starts in winter, but the opening date is often delayed because of whales and water quality. Ask whether it is fresh and in season before ordering.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.1.where: Street stalls at Fisherman's Wharf, and Chinese restaurants in the Sunset and Richmond districts.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.2.name: Mission burrito
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.2.text: Developed in San Francisco's Mission District, this oversized Mexican burrito packs rice, beans, grilled meat, salsa, and guacamole into a steamed flour tortilla wrapped in foil. One is a full meal. The Mission has many small shops along the streets; order in line and watch it get rolled fresh.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.2.where: Around 24th Street and Valencia Street in the Mission District.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.3.name: Baja fish tacos
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.3.text: A San Diego staple originating in Mexico's Baja California: crispy battered white fish topped with shredded purple cabbage, sour cream sauce, and lime in a corn tortilla. They taste best by the water. Grilled fish versions are also available and lighter.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.3.where: Beach areas, La Jolla, and Old Town San Diego.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.4.name: Koreatown Korean BBQ
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.4.text: Los Angeles's Koreatown is one of the largest Korean communities outside Korea, with barbecue restaurants open late into the night. Beef belly and short ribs cook at the table alongside an array of complimentary refillable side dishes. Many restaurants offer fixed-price all-you-can-eat meals. It is liveliest with a group at dinner.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.foods.4.where: Around Wilshire Boulevard and Western Avenue in Koreatown.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.intro.0: California is the most popular choice for a first trip to the U.S. West Coast: San Francisco and the Bay Area in the north, Yosemite and the Big Sur coast along Highway 1 in the middle, and Los Angeles, San Diego, and several theme parks in the south. You can see cities, granite valleys, coastal cliffs, and desert in one trip. Just remember that the state is huge, and driving between places often takes four or five hours.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.intro.1: For a first trip, stick to one route: San Francisco and Yosemite, then south along Highway 1 to Los Angeles. 8–10 days is about right. Families with children can focus on Los Angeles and San Diego. Outside San Francisco, you will generally need a car in California; public transportation is mainly useful within cities.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.intro.2: Starting in 2026, non-U.S. residents entering Yosemite must pay an additional $100 per person (ages 16 and up), which can significantly affect your budget. If you plan to visit more than two national parks, or have two or more adults in the same car, the $250 nonresident annual pass is usually a better deal. One pass covers the entire car.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.name: California
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.seasons.note: April–June and September–October are the most comfortable. Yosemite's waterfalls are at their fullest in May–June. San Francisco is often foggy and cool in June–August, while Joshua Tree can exceed 40°C in summer.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.sources.0.title: NPS Yosemite: Fees & Passes (including the $100 nonresident surcharge)
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.sources.1.title: NPS Yosemite: No entry reservations required in 2026
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.sources.2.title: NPS: Entrance Passes ($80 resident / $250 nonresident annual pass)
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.sources.9.title: FlightConnections: nonstop routes from LAX / SFO
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.0.name: Golden Gate Bridge
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.0.text: This orange-red suspension bridge spans the entrance to San Francisco Bay and is about 2.7 kilometers long. You can walk or bike across on the east-side walkway. Three classic viewpoints are Fort Point beneath the southern end, Battery Spencer on the high ground at the northern end, and Baker Beach in the city. Summer afternoons are often swallowed by fog. Visibility is best in the morning and fall.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.0.tip: Driving south into the city incurs a toll. There are no toll booths; the rental car company charges your card by license plate and adds a processing fee.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.1.fee: About $48 for an adult day tour
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.1.name: Alcatraz Island
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.1.text: This former federal prison in the bay once held notorious gang leaders and is now managed by the National Park Service. The ferry takes about 15 minutes. The cellhouse audio tour is well worth taking, with stories about escape attempts and prison life, and is available in several languages. The views back toward San Francisco's skyline are excellent, too. Only officially authorized Alcatraz City Cruises can take you there, departing from Pier 33.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.1.tip: The earliest you can book is 90 days ahead, and tickets often sell out weeks in advance during peak season. Avoid expensive third-party tickets.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.2.fee: About $35 per vehicle, plus $100 per nonresident
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.2.name: Yosemite National Park
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.2.text: This glacier-carved granite valley is home to El Capitan, Half Dome, and several major waterfalls, most of which you can see on easy, level walks. A classic plan is to visit Tunnel View and Yosemite Falls in the valley, see the giant sequoias at Mariposa Grove in the south, and head up to Glacier Point for a view from above in summer and fall. In 2026, entry reservations will no longer be required, but parking is difficult during peak season. Try to enter the valley before 8 a.m.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.2.tip: Glacier Point Road and Tioga Road usually close for winter starting in November and reopen in May–June the following year. Check road conditions before you leave.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.3.name: Highway 1, Big Sur
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.3.text: The route from Carmel to Cambria is about 160 kilometers long, with the highway clinging to cliffs between the mountains and the Pacific. Bixby Bridge, McWay Falls, and Pfeiffer Beach are all easy to see from roadside parking. Farther south, Piedras Blancas has elephant seals. The full route reopened after repairs to the landslide section in January 2026, but heavy winter rain can still cause temporary closures.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.3.tip: Gas stations are few and expensive along the route, so fill up before leaving Monterey. Driving north to south puts you on the ocean side and makes parking easier.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.4.name: Griffith Observatory
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.4.text: This white observatory on the Hollywood Hills offers one of the easiest views of Los Angeles and the Hollywood Sign, and admission is free. Come in the evening: watch the sunset, then see the city lights stretch to the coast. On a clear night, you can also line up to use the public telescopes. The astronomy exhibits are worth a look, while planetarium shows cost extra.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.4.tip: Closed Mondays. Parking on the hill is difficult on weekends, so you can take the DASH Observatory shuttle up.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.5.name: Santa Monica Pier
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.5.text: This is Los Angeles's most iconic waterfront spot. The wooden pier has a Ferris wheel and small amusement park, and marks the western end of Route 66. Ride south on the coastal bike path for about 20 minutes to reach Venice Beach, with its skate park, Muscle Beach, and canals. Sunset over the Pacific is best in the evening.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.5.tip: The ocean is cool year-round, so choose July–September if you want to swim. Nearby parking lots fill up early on weekends.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.6.name: Disneyland Resort & Universal Studios Hollywood
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.6.text: Southern California's two major theme parks: Disneyland Resort in Anaheim has the first Disneyland, opened in 1955, and the neighboring Disney California Adventure Park. Universal Studios Hollywood sits north of the Hollywood Hills and has a studio tram tour and The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. The two are about 1 hour apart by car. Plan a full day for each, or at least two days with children.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.6.tip: Ticket prices vary by date and are cheaper on weekdays outside holiday periods. Buy only from the official website or an authorized seller.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.7.name: San Diego
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.7.text: This harbor city at California's southern tip has mild weather year-round and a slower pace than Los Angeles. Balboa Park is packed with museums and sits next to the San Diego Zoo. The USS Midway Museum is docked downtown on the waterfront. Sea lions and seals lounge on the rocks at La Jolla Cove, where you can see them up close. The Mexican border is only about a 30-minute drive away.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.7.tip: Do not approach or touch the sea lions and seals at La Jolla. Keep several meters away. Some beaches close during breeding season.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.8.fee: About $30 per vehicle, valid for 7 days
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.8.name: Joshua Tree National Park
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.8.text: Two deserts meet here, with strange-shaped Joshua trees and granite boulders piled into small hills. It is ideal for climbing, short hikes, and stargazing. The drive from Los Angeles takes about 2.5 hours, and you can combine it with Palm Springs. Hidden Valley, Skull Rock, and the Cholla Cactus Garden are all along the main road and can be sampled in a day.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.8.tip: There are no gas stations and almost no cell service in the park, so bring plenty of water. Avoid hiking at midday from May–September.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.9.name: Napa Valley
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.9.text: This wine region is about a 1.5-hour drive north of San Francisco. Wineries line both sides of Highway 29, and Cabernet Sauvignon is the specialty. Most wineries require advance reservations for tastings, usually 4–5 wines per visit. Tastings often cost more than $50 per person, and some can be paired with food. Harvest season in September–October is the liveliest and most expensive. Neighboring Sonoma has more small wineries and somewhat lower prices.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.spots.9.tip: Do not drive after wine tasting; DUI enforcement is strict in the U.S. Join a tour, hire a car and driver, or stay in town.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.stay: In San Francisco, stay near Union Square or Fisherman's Wharf for easy transportation. Lodging in Yosemite Valley is limited and expensive, so consider El Portal or Mariposa outside the park. In Los Angeles, choose Santa Monica or Hollywood based on your itinerary rather than saving money by staying far out.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.tagline: Cities, coastal highways, and national parks—all in one trip
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.tips.0: Nonresidents pay an additional $100 per person to enter Yosemite. If there are two or more adults in the same car, or you are also visiting other national parks, the $250 nonresident annual pass is usually a better deal.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.tips.1: Driving rules depend on your passport and driver's license. Check the official requirements before you go. If a translation is required, bring a certified English translation along with your passport, and confirm the rental company's requirements before booking.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.tips.2: Listed prices do not include sales tax (about 7–10%). Tip 18–22% of the pre-tax bill at restaurants. Some restaurants already add a service charge, so check the bill carefully.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.tips.3: Car break-ins and theft are common in San Francisco and Los Angeles. Do not leave anything visible in the car, including luggage.
f5c3f616fea00f32a3ad.tips.4: San Francisco is often only 15–20°C in summer, so bring a jacket for the coast. Inland areas and the desert can exceed 40°C on the same day.

f69dcb26212b21fa7e8f.cover.alt: Panoramic view of snow-blanketed Shirakawa-go village glowing with warm lights at dusk
f69dcb26212b21fa7e8f.cover.caption: Snow-laden gassho-zukuri farmhouses glow warm golden at dusk in Shirakawa-go—but reaching Shiroyama Viewpoint starts with locking in your Nohi Bus seats exactly 30 days ahead.
f69dcb26212b21fa7e8f.excerpt: Kanazawa's snow-roped Kenrokuen pines, Shirakawa-go's deep-snow thatched rooftops, and Hida beef in Takayama's old town form central Japan's dream winter route—yet all-reserved Nohi buses trip up countless travelers. Follow this step-by-step playbook starting 30 days out, including illumination-day closures and snow-delay buffers.
