f75ce27009dd527061db.access.0.how: Nonstop options to John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) include Air China from Beijing, China Eastern from Shanghai, China Southern from Guangzhou, and XiamenAir from Fuzhou. Flights are limited and take about 13–16 hours. Connections through the West Coast, Tokyo, or Seoul offer more options.
f75ce27009dd527061db.access.1.how: Take the AirTrain to Jamaica, then transfer to the E subway line or the Long Island Rail Road for Manhattan, about 50–70 minutes total. Taxis to Manhattan charge a flat fare, plus tolls and a tip.
f75ce27009dd527061db.access.2.how: Amtrak trains reach Moynihan Train Hall at Penn Station in about 3–3.5 hours from Washington, D.C., or 1–1.5 hours from Philadelphia.
f75ce27009dd527061db.access.3.how: Amtrak takes about 3.5–4.5 hours. Buses take about 4–5 hours and cost less, but travel time depends on traffic.
f75ce27009dd527061db.cover.alt: Manhattan skyline and Brooklyn Bridge at dusk
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.0.name: New York-style pizza slice
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.0.text: Large, thin, chewy pizzas are sold by the slice. Fold one in half and eat it as you walk, New York style. Plain cheese and pepperoni are the best tests of a pizzeria. Neighborhood shops bake and slice them fresh, making lunch for a few dollars.
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.0.where: Neighborhood pizza shops in Manhattan and Brooklyn, including late at night.
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.1.name: Bagel with lox and cream cheese
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.1.text: New York bagels are boiled before baking, giving them a shiny crust and a dense, chewy center. The classic breakfast is a split bagel spread with cream cheese and layered with smoked salmon, red onion, and capers.
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.1.where: Long-running delis and neighborhood bagel shops on the Upper West Side and Lower East Side. Freshest in the morning.
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.2.name: Pastrami on rye
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.2.text: A Jewish deli classic: beef brisket is cured, smoked, steamed, and hand-cut into thick slices, then piled onto rye bread with yellow mustard and pickles. Katz's on the Lower East Side has been serving it since 1888. One sandwich is enough for two.
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.2.where: Long-running Jewish delis around Houston Street on the Lower East Side.
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.3.name: Halal cart chicken over rice
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.3.text: An affordable street-cart meal of turmeric rice topped with chopped grilled chicken or lamb, white sauce, hot red sauce, and some lettuce. Generous portions are ready in minutes, making it a favorite quick meal for office workers and students. Go easy on the red sauce at first; it is very hot.
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.3.where: Halal carts around Midtown. The corner of 53rd Street and Sixth Avenue is the best known.
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.4.name: Buffalo wings
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.4.text: These fried chicken wings originated in Buffalo in western New York. Coated in a buttery hot sauce, they come with blue cheese dressing and celery sticks to cool the heat. Stop for some in Buffalo on a trip to Niagara Falls, or find them at almost any New York City sports bar.
f75ce27009dd527061db.foods.4.where: Long-running restaurants and bars in downtown Buffalo, and sports bars in New York City.
f75ce27009dd527061db.intro.0: New York is the first U.S. stop for many travelers. Museums, parks, Broadway, and skyline views are packed onto Manhattan, easy to explore by subway and on foot. Allow at least 4 days for a first visit, grouping sights by area: a day in Midtown, a day for Upper East Side museums and Central Park, and a day for Lower Manhattan, the Statue of Liberty, and Brooklyn Bridge.
f75ce27009dd527061db.intro.1: Hotels and meals make New York expensive. A midrange Manhattan hotel often costs $300–400 a night in peak season, even for a small room. Restaurant bills come with added tax and a tip of about 20%. The subway runs 24 hours a day. Tap a bank card or phone to enter; it is cheaper and often faster than a taxi.
f75ce27009dd527061db.intro.2: New York State has much more to offer beyond the city. The Hudson Valley is an hour or two north, with hills full of fall color in October. Niagara Falls, at the state's far western edge, calls for a flight and a separate day or two.
f75ce27009dd527061db.name: New York
f75ce27009dd527061db.seasons.note: April–June and September–November have the most comfortable weather. December is festive but cold and expensive, July–August is hot and humid, and January–February often brings snow.
f75ce27009dd527061db.sources.9.title: China–U.S. nonstop flight roundup (U.S. Credit Card Guide)
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.0.name: Central Park
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.0.text: Stretching about 4 kilometers north to south through the middle of Manhattan, this vast park is where New Yorkers run, picnic, and soak up the sun. For a first visit, enter at the southeast corner and follow the elm-lined Mall to Bethesda Fountain and Bow Bridge. Continue north to Belvedere Castle and the Reservoir. Half a day is enough for this route. Fall colors are best from late October to mid-November.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.0.tip: Pedicabs charge by the minute, so confirm the total price before getting in. Renting a bike is better value.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.1.fee: About $30 for out-of-state and international visitors
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.1.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.1.text: The largest art museum in the U.S. has everything from an Egyptian temple and European paintings to Chinese calligraphy and a classical garden. Even a full day is not enough to see it all. For a first visit, focus on 3 areas: the Egyptian galleries with the Temple of Dendur, European paintings on the second floor, and the Astor Court, modeled on a Suzhou garden. Your ticket also includes same-day admission to The Met Cloisters farther north.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.1.tip: Closed Wednesdays. Open until 9 pm on Fridays and Saturdays, with fewer visitors in the early evening.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.2.name: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.2.text: Statue City Cruises is the only authorized ferry operator to the islands. Boats leave from The Battery at Manhattan's southern tip, stopping first at Liberty Island and then at the Ellis Island immigration museum. One ticket covers both islands. For a distant view of the statue, take the free Staten Island Ferry. Pedestal and crown tickets are limited, so book well ahead in peak season.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.2.tip: People around The Battery sell “Statue of Liberty tickets,” often for sightseeing boats that do not stop at the islands. Book through the official website.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.3.name: Brooklyn Bridge & DUMBO
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.3.text: Opened in 1883, this bridge has stone towers, steel cables, and a raised pedestrian path about 1.8 kilometers long. Start by taking the subway to DUMBO in Brooklyn. From its cobbled streets, photograph the Manhattan Bridge framing the Empire State Building, then head to the waterfront park for skyline views and sunset. Walk back across Brooklyn Bridge toward Manhattan, with the skyline ahead of you.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.3.tip: The bridge gets packed during the day. Go before 8 am or in the early evening for a more pleasant walk.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.4.fee: Square free; show ticket prices vary by performance
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.4.name: Times Square & Broadway
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.4.text: Giant screens light the intersection as brightly as daylight. Come at night for the atmosphere; a quick look is enough. The real draw is a Broadway musical in the surrounding Theater District. Book popular shows ahead through official channels, or try the TKTS booth beneath the red steps for discounted same-day tickets. Many shows are dark on Mondays.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.4.tip: Costumed characters posing for photos and people pressing CDs into your hands will ask for money afterward. Keep walking.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.5.name: Empire State Building Observatory
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.5.text: Completed in 1931, this Art Deco skyscraper has an open-air observatory on the 86th floor, overlooking Central Park, the Hudson River, and Lower Manhattan. Go up about an hour before sunset to see both daytime and nighttime views. To photograph the Empire State Building itself, choose the observatory at Rockefeller Center. For a glass floor, try Edge at Hudson Yards.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.5.tip: Rain and fog can hide the views, so check the weather before buying tickets. Tickets that allow date changes cost more.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.6.name: The High Line
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.6.text: This former elevated freight railway is now a walking path stretching about 2.3 kilometers from the Meatpacking District to Hudson Yards, lined with old and new buildings, wildflowers, and grasses. Visit Chelsea Market near the southern end, then finish at Hudson Yards and the Edge observatory in the north. Little Island, a park on the Hudson River to the west, is also worth a stop.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.6.tip: Walk south to north for the best light around sunset. Winter opening hours are shorter.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.7.name: The Museum of Modern Art
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.7.text: A top choice for modern art, with Van Gogh's The Starry Night, Monet's Water Lilies, and works by Picasso and Warhol. The fifth floor has the greatest concentration of famous works. Smaller than The Met, it is manageable in half a day. Rest in the ground-floor sculpture garden afterward, then walk to Fifth Avenue or Rockefeller Center.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.7.tip: Arrive at opening and head straight to the fifth floor. After noon, expect a line to take photos of The Starry Night.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.8.fee: Park free; boat rides from about $30
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.8.name: Niagara Falls State Park
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.8.text: At the oldest state park in the U.S., viewpoints and Goat Island bring you close to the American Falls and Bridal Veil Falls. Horseshoe Falls lies mainly on the Canadian side. In summer, take the Maid of the Mist boat to the base of the falls, then get soaked on the wooden walkways at Cave of the Winds. Fly from New York to Buffalo in about 1.5 hours, then drive about 30 minutes.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.8.tip: Entry requirements for crossing Rainbow Bridge into Canada depend on your passport. Check official Canadian entry rules before planning to cross.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.9.name: Hudson Valley
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.9.text: North of New York City, the valley's hills turn red and gold around mid-October, making it one of the closest places to enjoy fall foliage. Without a car, take Metro-North Railroad from Grand Central Terminal to Beacon in about 1.5 hours for large-scale contemporary art at Dia Beacon. If driving, visit Storm King Art Center, where huge sculptures dot broad grassy slopes, then stop at a farm to pick apples.
f75ce27009dd527061db.spots.9.tip: For fall weekends, reserve admission and parking for Storm King and orchards ahead through their official websites.
f75ce27009dd527061db.stay: For a first visit, stay in Midtown between Times Square and the south end of Central Park, or near a subway station in Lower Manhattan. Both make getting around easy. For lower prices, try Long Island City in Queens or a spot near the subway in Brooklyn, about 15–20 minutes from Manhattan.
f75ce27009dd527061db.tagline: Museums, skylines, and Broadway—one island is more than enough
f75ce27009dd527061db.tips.0: Tap a bank card or phone to ride subways and buses. A single ride costs about $3; after spending about $35 on the same card within 7 days, further rides are free.
f75ce27009dd527061db.tips.1: New York City sales tax is about 8.875% and is not included in listed prices. At restaurants, add a tip of about 18–22%, unless a service charge is already included.
f75ce27009dd527061db.tips.2: The Met is closed Wednesdays. Other museums have different closing days, so check each one before planning your itinerary.
f75ce27009dd527061db.tips.3: Snowstorms are common from December–February and can lead to flight cancellations. Leave a spare day when visiting Niagara Falls or the Hudson Valley.
f75ce27009dd527061db.tips.4: Many people cross against the light. Check for traffic before following them; bicycles and e-bikes can move fast.

f855f8518efc58cdff93.cost: Cape Manzamo entry ¥100; Agu pork shabu-shabu about ¥4,500 per person
f855f8518efc58cdff93.location: Cape Manzamo / Kouri Beach → Naha Agu pork specialty restaurant
f855f8518efc58cdff93.paragraphs.0: Even when winter water is too cool for swimming, Okinawa's coastline loses none of its punch. Below Cape Manzamo's grassy elevated coral plateau, surf shifts from translucent mint to vivid cobalt—whenever the sun breaks through, every frame looks Hawaii-bright without a filter. Just hold onto your hat and scarf in the brisk cliffside wind.
f855f8518efc58cdff93.paragraphs.1: Back in Naha for dinner, treat yourself to Okinawa's crown jewel: Agu pork shabu-shabu. Swish thinly sliced heritage black pork in simmering kombu dashi for ten seconds, dip it in tangy shikuwasa citrus ponzu, and finish by cooking rice porridge in the sweet, pork-and-seaweed-infused broth—pure comfort in a pot.
f855f8518efc58cdff93.phase: Step 05 · Day 3 Scenic coast stop & feast
f855f8518efc58cdff93.photo.alt: Coral limestone sea cliff and turquoise bay of Cape Manzamo in Okinawa on a sunny winter afternoon
f855f8518efc58cdff93.photo.caption: Standing on Cape Manzamo's bluff on a 20°C winter afternoon means glassy coral waters with none of the scorching summer glare or crowds.
f855f8518efc58cdff93.tip: Naha's cult-favorite Agu pork restaurants (such as Matsumoto and Shimabutaya) book out fast even in low season—reserve 1–2 weeks ahead online or via your hotel concierge instead of trying to walk in.
f855f8518efc58cdff93.title: Take in winter glass-blue seas at Cape Manzamo, then celebrate in Naha with Agu pork shabu-shabu

f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.gateways.0.how: The Keisei Skyliner takes a little over 40 minutes to Ueno and costs about ¥2,470. The JR N'EX takes about 1 hour to Tokyo Station and costs about ¥3,140. Buses to Tokyo Station cost about ¥1,500.
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.gateways.0.name: Narita International Airport (NRT)
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.gateways.1.how: The Keikyu Line takes about 15 minutes to Shinagawa and costs about ¥330. The monorail takes about 15 minutes to Hamamatsucho and costs about ¥520; transfer to the JR Yamanote Line there.
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.gateways.1.name: Haneda Airport (HND)
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.gateways.2.how: The Tokaido Shinkansen Nozomi takes about 2 hours 15 minutes to 2 and a half hours from Kyoto or Osaka. The Tohoku, Hokuriku, and Joetsu Shinkansen lines also depart from here.
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.gateways.2.name: Tokyo Station (Shinkansen)
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.intro.0: Kanto is the region around Tokyo, made up of Tokyo and six prefectures. It is where most people first land in Japan. Tokyo itself can easily fill four or five days. South are Kamakura, Hakone, and Yokohama; north are Nikko's World Heritage sites and Gunma's hot springs; east are Narita, the Boso Peninsula, and Ibaraki's flower fields. Most make easy day trips from Tokyo.
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.intro.1: The easiest plan is to stay in Tokyo and head out in a different direction each day: one day for Kamakura and Enoshima, one day for Nikko, and half a day for Kawagoe. Hot-spring towns such as Hakone and Kusatsu are worth an overnight stay. On a second visit, focus on the outskirts. Tokyo's subways and private railways can get you around, so you may not need a nationwide rail pass.
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.name: Kanto
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.passes.0.text: Unlimited rides on the Tokyo Metro and Toei Subway for 24/48/72 hours cost about ¥1,000/1,500/2,000. JR is not included. It pays off after four or five subway rides in a day.
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.passes.1.name: JR Tokyo Wide Pass
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.passes.1.text: About ¥16,000 for 3 days, covering JR East trains to Nikko, Karuizawa, Lake Kawaguchi, and other destinations. It is worthwhile only if you take long trips out of Tokyo on two of the three days. Available for purchase only in Japan.
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.passes.2.name: Hakone Freepass
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.passes.2.text: Issued by Odakyu, this pass costs about ¥7,100 for 2 days from Shinjuku. It includes the round trip and Hakone's mountain railway, cable car, and sightseeing cruise. The Romancecar costs extra. It is generally worth buying for a trip to Hakone.
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.passes.3.text: Issued by Tobu, this pass costs about ¥3,000 for 2 days in the World Heritage area. It includes round-trip travel from Asakusa to Nikko and buses in the area. Limited express trains cost extra. Choose this one if you are only visiting the Toshogu area.
f8a8d58c7af5a60dc94a.season: Cherry blossoms are best from late March to early April, and fall colors in November. July–August is hot, humid, and rainy. Winters bring many clear days and better chances of seeing Mount Fuji from afar.

f947e6334b02c4201421.s: Temples, shrines, castles, and old streets are the least seasonal parts of a Japan trip. Go a little earlier for fewer people and better light.

fa2d305bfeeb3311c2aa.s: For trips over a week across several prefectures, compare JR Pass and regional pass prices.

faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.3.items.4.note: Look for the 「精算機」 next to the gate and top up your card.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.3.items.4.zh: I don’t have enough money on my IC card, so I can’t get through the gate.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.3.items.5.note: Give your ticket or IC card to a station attendant and pay the difference.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.3.items.5.zh: I missed my stop. Could you help me pay the fare difference?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.3.items.6.zh: I bought the wrong ticket. Can I get a refund?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.3.items.7.zh: What time is the last train toward X?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.3.items.8.note: When taking a taxi, show the driver the address or hotel name.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.3.items.8.zh: Please take me to this address.

faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.0.note: Yamato’s 「空港宅急便」 service usually requires sending it 2–3 days before your flight.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.0.zh: I’d like to send this piece of luggage to the airport.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.1.note: Staff will ask for your flight details when you send luggage to the airport.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.1.zh: I’m taking a flight on X month X day at X time, departing from X Airport.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.2.zh: I’d like to send this luggage to my next hotel. Here is the address.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.3.zh: Can it arrive by the Xth?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.4.zh: About how many days will delivery take?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.5.zh: How much is the shipping fee?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.7.note: Show the shipping receipt at the airport宅急便 counter.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.7.zh: I’m here to pick up the luggage sent to the airport. Here is the shipping receipt.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.8.note: Contact the next hotel before sending your luggage there.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.items.8.zh: I’ll check in on the Xth. If my luggage arrives before I do, could you store it for me?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.4.title: Sending luggage
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.items.0.zh: I’ve had a fever since yesterday.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.items.1.zh: I have a stomachache and diarrhea.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.items.3.zh: I need cold medicine. Do you have something that doesn’t cause drowsiness?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.items.4.note: You can add the symptom: かゆい (itchy).
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.items.4.zh: Do you have medicine for allergies?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.items.5.note: Write the medicine name in 〇〇. Its English generic name is also fine.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.items.5.zh: I’m allergic to this type of medicine, XX.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.items.6.zh: How many times a day should I take this medicine?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.items.7.zh: I’d like to go to a hospital. Is there one nearby with staff who speak my language or English?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.items.8.note: You can also call 119 yourself. Start by saying 「救急です」.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.items.9.note: Show your policy or insurance card at the same time.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.5.title: Pharmacies and medical care
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.6.items.0.zh: Excuse me, I don’t speak Japanese. Can we use a translation app?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.6.items.1.zh: Is there anyone here who speaks my language?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.6.items.2.note: Ask the other person to point it out on a map.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.6.items.3.zh: I lost my wallet. Where should I report it?
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.6.items.4.note: Ask a station attendant as soon as possible.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.6.items.4.zh: I left something on the train. It was the train traveling toward X at around X o’clock.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.6.items.5.note: Say this at a police box or police station. You’ll need the report to obtain an emergency travel document.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.6.items.5.zh: I lost my passport. I want to report it, and I need proof to get a replacement from my embassy.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.6.items.7.zh: Please help me contact the police.
faf2533e274d2189aca3.categories.6.items.9.zh: I’d like to contact my embassy.

fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.days.0.move: Take the Shinkansen from Shin-Osaka to Hiroshima in about 1.5 hours, then take the streetcar around the city
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.days.0.title: Hiroshima city and Peace Memorial Park
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.days.1.move: Take JR from Hiroshima Station to Miyajimaguchi in about 30 minutes, then take the ferry for about 10 minutes
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.days.1.title: Head to Miyajima and stay on the island
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.days.2.items.0.note: Before breakfast, head to the waterfront to see the Great Torii without the crowds
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.days.2.move: Take the ferry and JR back to Hiroshima Station, then the Shinkansen to Okayama in about 40 minutes
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.days.2.title: See the torii at dawn, then head to Okayama
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.days.3.items.3.note: In the evening, take the Shinkansen from Okayama back to Kansai, or head to Okayama Airport
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.days.3.move: Take JR from Okayama Station to Kurashiki Station in about 15–20 minutes
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.days.3.title: Half a day in Kurashiki's historic quarter
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.for: First- or second-time visitors who have been to Kansai and want to explore farther west
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.season: Best for cherry blossoms in spring and fall foliage in autumn; winter is perfect for oysters
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.summary: Take the Shinkansen west from Kansai. On day 1, visit Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park. On day 2, head to Miyajima and spend the night on the island. Avoid the day-trip crowds and see the Great Torii at dusk and dawn. On the last 2 days, return to Okayama to visit Korakuen Garden, Okayama Castle, and Kurashiki's historic quarter, then take the Shinkansen back to Kansai.
fb5b76e29a9d2ee52ab7.title: Hiroshima + Miyajima + Okayama · 4 days

fb7c6268879e369cd153.s: Cloudborne Travel is a guide by Cloudborne, covering Japan, Australia, and the United States. Find where to go, how to get there, what it costs, and what to do when you arrive—all in one place.

fbd6c805e528f39979cb.0: Transit hack: ride the Kyoto Subway Tozai Line to Keage Station (Exit 1) and walk 12 minutes past Nanzen-ji straight to Eikando, bypassing the Shijo and Higashiyama-dori gridlock altogether.
fbd6c805e528f39979cb.1: Eikando sprint: queue at 07:45 and skip the entrance rock garden when gates open at 08:30—walk briskly to Hojo Pond and Tahoto Pagoda for clean shots first, then circle back to Garyuro corridor.
fbd6c805e528f39979cb.2: Tofuku-ji workaround: either queue at 08:15 the next morning (or snag a JR Central early-morning private slot), or cross the free Gaunkyo Bridge in the afternoon for the classic Tsutenkyo panorama with zero ticket line.
fbd6c805e528f39979cb.3: 11:00–14:00 shelter plan: when tour buses flood the main temples at midday, duck into Nanzen-ji for yudofu and linger at quiet, uncrowded Honen-in and Shinnyo-do.

fc1151ec3460e476496e.location: International flight or ferry checkout pages
fc1151ec3460e476496e.paragraphs.0: Starting July 1, 2026, Japan raised its International Tourist Tax—commonly called the departure tax—from ¥1,000 to ¥3,000 (roughly CNY 140). Both international visitors and Japanese residents pay it whenever departing Japan by air or sea.
fc1151ec3460e476496e.paragraphs.1: Thankfully, there is no separate airport kiosk or cash counter to deal with: airlines collect it automatically in the ticket's tax breakdown (usually under code TK). If you hold a long-haul ticket issued before June 30, 2026, the old ¥1,000 rate still applies, though reissuing or changing dates can trigger the ¥2,000 difference.
fc1151ec3460e476496e.phase: Step 05 · Check the higher departure tax on your ticket
fc1151ec3460e476496e.tip: Redeeming airline miles for a return flight out of Japan? Taxes and fees will look noticeably steeper than last year—that extra ~¥2,000 per ticket is the new departure tax alongside airport facility fee tweaks, which adds up fast for a family.
fc1151ec3460e476496e.title: The departure tax tripled to ¥3,000—but you won't stand in line to pay it

fd1127ec22f453489638.s: A full season of flowers follows the cherry blossoms: wisteria and nemophila in late April, hydrangeas in June, and Hokkaido lavender in July. Bloom periods are more stable, and crowds are lighter.

fe0a54370005dbf98b31.s: Japan emergencies: police 110, fire/ambulance 119, at sea 118, Japan Visitor Hotline, and what to do if you lose your passport, need medical care, or experience an earthquake.

fe81342251c1b65e9c3c.s: From Chichu Art Museum on Naoshima to city architecture, Japan’s contemporary art and architecture deserve a dedicated day. Many museums require reservations and are often closed Mondays.

ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.0.detail: Visa applications may require a certain amount of remaining passport validity. Renew your passport first if it is close to expiring. If you lose it, a photo and photocopy can speed up replacement.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.0.text: Make sure your passport is valid for the entire trip, and save a photo of the photo page to your phone and cloud storage
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.1.detail: Apply through a channel designated by a Japanese embassy or consulate in your country. Visa types, documents, and permitted stays follow the latest official notices. Avoid unauthorized agencies.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.1.text: Check whether your passport requires a visa for Japan, and apply early
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.2.detail: Have your passport, flight details, and email address ready. Show the QR code at immigration and customs after landing. It must be displayed on your phone; if you complete it on a computer, open it on your phone too.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.2.text: Complete your entry and customs information in Visit Japan Web before departure
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.3.detail: After registering your passport information and landing permission sticker details, you can generate a tax-free shopping QR code. At 7 major airports, you can also use it to complete outbound customs confirmation online.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.3.text: Register the tax-free shopping QR code while you are at it
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.4.detail: Visitors pay medical expenses in Japan themselves, and hospitalization or surgery can cost millions of yen. Save the insurer's 24-hour assistance number.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.4.text: Buy overseas travel insurance with medical coverage and direct billing
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.5.detail: You may be asked for your address and itinerary at immigration. Without internet access, you can also show the hotel address to a taxi driver.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.items.5.text: Save offline copies of your flight and hotel bookings
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.0.title: Documents and visas
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.1.items.0.detail: Cards are increasingly convenient in cities, but small restaurants, shrines and temples, some buses, and some guesthouses still accept cash only.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.1.items.0.text: Carry some yen in cash; small shops, rural areas, and ryokan often accept cash only
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.1.items.1.detail: These are among the most widely accepted cards in Japan. You can use them at major malls, chain stores, convenience stores, and on the Shinkansen. It is best to carry a backup card too.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.1.items.1.text: Carry a Visa, Mastercard, or JCB credit card
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.1.items.2.detail: Seven Bank ATMs in 7-Eleven stores accept UnionPay, Visa, Mastercard, and other overseas cards. Airports have them too. Japan Post Bank ATMs also accept overseas cards. Fees depend on the card issuer.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.1.items.2.text: You can withdraw yen with bank cards, including UnionPay cards, at 7-Eleven ATMs
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.1.items.3.detail: Large drugstores, electronics stores, and department stores often accept them, but small shops may not. Check the signs at the register and ask before paying.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.1.items.3.text: Visa, Mastercard, contactless payments, and cash are more reliable; Alipay and WeChat Pay are accepted in some places, but do not rely on them alone
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.1.items.4.detail: If you lose a card, reporting it immediately is more urgent than filing a police report.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.1.items.4.text: Save each card's lost-card phone number separately from the card
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.1.title: Money and payments
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.0.detail: An eSIM is the easiest option. If you are traveling with several people or need to connect multiple devices, rent pocket Wi-Fi and pick it up and return it at the airport. Confirm that your phone supports eSIM first.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.0.text: Buy an eSIM, Japanese data SIM, or pocket Wi-Fi in advance
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.1.detail: Roaming data may use your home network. If you need Google Maps or Gmail, a local Japanese eSIM or data SIM is more reliable.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.1.text: Some services, including Google, may not work when you roam with your home-country SIM
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.2.detail: Google Maps is useful in Japan for public transit, walking directions, and business hours. Save your hotel and other destinations.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.2.text: Install a map app and download offline maps in advance
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.3.detail: Stations with the same name may belong to JR or different subway companies. Use the app to confirm the operator and exit.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.3.text: Install a transit app to check platforms, fares, and the last train
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.4.detail: Photo translation and conversation translation are useful. You can also use this site's large-print cards to show staff.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.4.text: Install a translation app and download the Japanese offline pack
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.5.detail: It sends earthquake early warnings, tsunami alerts, and weather alerts.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.5.text: Install the tourism agency's Safety tips app to receive earthquake and tsunami alerts
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.6.detail: Navigation and taking photos all day use a lot of power. In an emergency, your phone can be a lifeline.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.items.6.text: Bring a power bank and a cable long enough for comfortable use
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.2.title: Internet and phones
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.0.detail: Suica, PASMO, ICOCA, and other cards are interoperable nationwide. You can use them in different cities. Some rural routes may not accept them, so check before setting out.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.0.text: Transit IC cards work across Japan and can be used on city transport and at convenience stores
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.1.detail: Top up the card in Wallet after adding it. If the top-up fails, use cash at a station or convenience store. Android support varies by model.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.1.text: On iPhone, add Suica directly to Wallet and tap your phone to enter stations
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.2.detail: There is no deposit, but the cards have a validity period and unused balances are nonrefundable. Add only as much as you need. TOURIST PASMO is sold at Narita and Haneda airports.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.2.text: If you do not want to use your phone, buy a visitor card such as Welcome Suica or TOURIST PASMO
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.3.detail: This is limited to certain railway companies and lines. Before using it, confirm that the gate has a contactless symbol.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.3.text: Some lines let you tap a credit card directly at the gate
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.4.detail: A 7-day ordinary-car pass starts at about ¥50,000. It is usually not worthwhile if you are visiting only Tokyo or Kansai. Add up the regular one-way fares for your itinerary before deciding.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.4.text: The nationwide JR Pass may be worthwhile only for long-distance round trips across regions
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.5.detail: For bags with total dimensions over 160 cm (up to 250 cm), reserve a seat with an oversized baggage storage area. A fee applies if you do not reserve one.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.items.5.text: Reserve a luggage space when taking the Tokaido, Sanyo, or Kyushu Shinkansen with a large suitcase
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.3.title: Transit cards
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.0.detail: Two-flat-pin plugs used in many countries can be plugged in directly. Most phone and computer chargers support 100–240V. Do not bring hair dryers or curling irons marked for 220V only.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.0.text: Japan uses Type A two-flat-pin plugs and 100V; bring an adapter for three-prong plugs
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.1.detail: For flights departing Japan: each person may carry up to 2, each under 160Wh. Do not place them in the overhead bin, and do not use or charge them onboard. Airlines in your country may have separate rules; follow your airline's requirements.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.1.text: Power banks must be carried on and cannot be checked
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.2.detail: Most meat products are prohibited, including processed products. Violations can result in a fine of up to ¥3 million or imprisonment for up to 3 years.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.2.text: Do not bring meat products such as jerky, sausage, ham, or meat floss into Japan
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.3.detail: They cannot enter without a plant quarantine certificate issued by the exporting country's government. Declare them at the plant quarantine counter on arrival.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.3.text: Do not bring fresh fruit, vegetables, seeds, or plants with soil
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.4.detail: You must see a doctor before buying prescription medication in Japan. Bring the medication instructions or drug name so a pharmacist can help you find an alternative.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.4.text: Bring enough of your regular medication, and note the names and doses
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.5.detail: Walking 20,000–30,000 steps a day is common. Temples, ryokan, and some restaurants require you to remove your shoes at the entrance.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.items.5.text: Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a pair that is easy to take on and off
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.4.title: Packing
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.0.detail: At convenience stores, sort trash into burnable waste, plastic bottles, and cans before throwing it away. In hotels, follow the sorting instructions in your room.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.0.text: There are few trash cans on the street, so carry a bag for your own trash
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.1.detail: Put your phone on silent. Queue to board, and let people off before boarding. Keep your voice down near priority seats.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.1.text: Do not make phone calls on trains or buses, and keep your voice down
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.2.detail: Many hot springs, public baths, and pools restrict entry for people with tattoos. For small tattoos, ask whether you can cover them with a patch, or choose a private bath or a room with a private bath.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.2.text: If you have tattoos, check whether they are allowed before visiting a hot spring
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.3.detail: Do not wear a swimsuit in the bath unless otherwise specified. Tie back long hair, and do not wash your body in the bath.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.3.text: Wash before entering a hot spring, and keep your towel out of the water
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.4.detail: You do not need to tip at restaurants, hotels, or in taxis. Insisting on a tip may make the recipient uncomfortable.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.4.text: Japan has no tipping culture; just pay the bill
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.5.detail: Smoking while walking can result in a fine in many areas. Look for a place with an ashtray and a designated smoking sign.
ffc0179352f447baf31d.groups.5.items.5.text: Smoking is banned on the streets in many cities, so use designated smoking areas
